canonical_summary: Abat produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream transcript, Ppp6r1, and only in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Directly assayed GABA synthesis, vesicle-loading, reuptake, glutaminase, GABA_A, and GABA_B perturbations did not reproduce the Abat-Ppp6r1 response in Pvalb cells.
GABA_A receptor-subunit perturbations, especially Gabrb2 and Gabrg2, generated activity-regulated transcripts in glutamatergic groups where Abat was flat.
The data-driven Abat signature-neighbor search yielded no robust phenocopy.
Abca1 produced a single exploratory Atp2b3 upregulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and no other FDR<0.10 downstream gene anywhere.

Abca1 failed to move measured ApoE, Abcg, LXR/RXR, cholesterol-synthesis, and cholesterol-trafficking transcripts, whereas the Srebf2 comparator generated a recurrent sterol-biosynthesis knockdown module.
ABCA1 pathway and Alzheimer-related comparators did not phenocopy the one Abca1 response in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Abca1 had no robust whole-universe transcriptomic neighbor, and data-driven top neighbors did not reproduce its CNU-MGE Atp2b3 upregulation.
Acute Abca7 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across all 23 recovered NeuN-enriched neuronal groups.
Abca7 loss did not trigger the Srebf2/cholesterol-biosynthetic module that the same dataset could readily detect after Srebf2 perturbation.
Abca7 did not phenocopy a neuronal endolysosomal stress response despite a strong Rab7 lysosomal/v-ATPase/sterol compensation signature in the same analysis universe.
ABCA7-related Alzheimer's and phagocytic comparator targets were mostly flat in neurons, localizing their expected biology outside the healthy NeuN-enriched transcriptional axis.
Whole-profile neighbor analysis found no robust Abca7-like or anti-Abca7-like signature.
Abcb7 produced a pan-null downstream transcriptional surface in all 21 neuronal cell groups in which it was measured.
The expected Fe-S/OXPHOS, iron-heme, and secondary ISR/redox/proteostasis transcriptional programs were absent after Abcb7 perturbation.
Literature-nominated Fe-S and iron-homeostasis targets did not phenocopy Abcb7 in matched neuronal groups.
The unbiased Abcb7 signature-neighbor search yielded only tiny positive and negative cosines.
Abcc9 CRISPR targeting produced a complete neuronal transcriptomic null across the 22 recovered cell groups.
Abcc9 had no credible positive or negative transcriptional neighbor in the perturbation universe, and its canonical KATP partners were absent as perturbations.
Abcd3 loss produced a high-confidence pan-neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 measured cell groups.
The acute neuronal assay also failed to recover a shared peroxisome signature among directly testable relatives of ABCD3.
Abcd3 had no close data-driven cross-perturbation neighbor after gene-by-cell-group residualization.
Abcd3 did not induce peroxisomal paralog compensation or a detectable UPR/proteostasis stress state.
Abhd12 CRISPR lowered the Abhd12 transcript broadly but produced no robust downstream neuronal transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered cell groups.

The screen failed to recover an Abhd12 neuroinflammatory or phagocytic module because the canonical PHARC axis is a lyso-PS/oxidized-PS lipid and microglia/macrophage program, not an acute transcriptional program of postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.
Abhd12 did not transcriptionally couple to either the 2-AG/cannabinoid pathway or the AMPA-receptor complex in juvenile neurons.
The unbiased Abhd12 signature has no strong positive neighbor, and its weak anti-neighbor Psmb4 is a broad stress/proteostasis responder that is absent from Abhd12.
Neuron-enriched snRNA-seq is unlikely to supply a proximal pharmacodynamic biomarker for ABHD12 loss or inhibition.
Acute postmitotic Abhd2 loss produced no FDR-supported whole-transcriptome response in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
Abhd2 did not phenocopy the represented progesterone/endocannabinoid comparators Abhd12, Pgr, or Cnr1.
The unbiased Abhd2 signature did not have a convincing convergent or anti-convergent neighbor among 1,772 other target perturbations.
Abhd2's lipid-enzyme null contrasts with the Marchf6 sterol-homeostasis response detected in the same neuronal universe.
Acbd5 loss produced no robust downstream neuronal transcriptomic response in 22 recovered cell groups.
Expected peroxisomal, sterol, UPR/ISR, and autophagy/lysosomal transcripts remained FDR-flat after Acbd5 perturbation.
Measured peroxisome and lipid relatives failed to phenocopy Acbd5 in matched neuronal groups.
Data-driven Acbd5 signature neighbors had near-zero score-vector correlations across the whole model-visible universe.

Ache produced a pan-measured neuronal downstream null: every recovered group had 0 non-Ache genes at FDR<0.10, even though the Ache transcript was significantly reduced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The expected activity-regulated early-response genes were not recovered: Fos, Fosb, Jun/Junb/Jund, Egr1-4, Npas4, Nr4a1/2, Arc, Homer1, and Bdnf all had FDR≥1.0 across the Ache surface.

Represented cholinergic receptor neighbors also failed to define a transcriptomic module: fourteen nicotinic or muscarinic receptor perturbations produced only 7 total FDR<0.10 downstream hits across 294 Ache-matched target×group tests, with no receptor target exceeding 2 hits.

Whole-universe, feature-centered signature search placed Ache in a near-null residual neighborhood rather than near a mechanistic module: the strongest positive neighbor was Sec63 at r=0.064 and the strongest inverse neighbor was Maf at r=-0.069, and none of the six retained neighbors shared an FDR-gated gene with Ache.
Aco2 produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream hit, Sirt7 up-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, rather than a broad neuronal metabolic signature.
The Aco2 DE surface lacks the mitochondrial ISR, TCA/OXPHOS, and autophagy programs predicted for severe mitochondrial aconitase dysfunction.
CRISPR perturbations of represented TCA, pyruvate-dehydrogenase, and Fe-S neighbors did not phenocopy Aco2 and mostly remained as buffered as Aco2.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors of Aco2 were numerically tiny, with Ndufb9 the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top inverse neighbor but neither forming an interpretable Aco2 module.
Opa1, an optic-atrophy mitochondrial comparator, generated a broad ISR-like and mt-RNA-depletion signature that Aco2 lacked.

Acp1 knockout was a complete robust transcriptomic null across the recovered juvenile NeuN+ brain surface: every one of 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the missing 215 MB Dopa group was not tested.

The RTK outputs expected from LMW-PTP biology were not recovered: immediate-early, MAPK-feedback, insulin/PI3K/Foxo genes were FDR=1.000 throughout Acp1, and direct receptor/PTP comparators Pdgfrb, Epha2, Insr, Igf1r, Ptpn11, Fgfr1, and Ptpn1 failed to phenocopy Acp1 with a multi-gene downstream signature.

The strongest whole-profile Acp1 neighbors were effectively non-neighbors: the best positive score correlation was H2ac8 at r=0.0319 and the best anti-correlation was Abcb7 at r=-0.0159, with no shared Acp1 FDR genes.
Acsl4 loss produced its only BH-significant downstream response in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, where Srebf2 increased.
The Acsl4 restricted signature was inversely oriented to direct Srebf2 perturbation, which drove Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, and Ldlr downward.
Acsl4 did not phenocopy canonical ferroptosis-axis perturbations: Gpx4 and Nfe2l2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Tfrc had only five isolated hits.
The strongest full-coverage positive neighbors of the Acsl4 restricted signature, Inpp5k, Sucla2, and Ebf1, had zero robust downstream genes in the matched groups.
A neuronal ACSL4-inhibition program would not be well monitored by ferroptosis markers alone; Srebf2 and sterol genes are the only detected Acsl4-responsive transcripts.

Actg1 loss produced an extremely buffered postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups, even though the Actg1 transcript trended downward in every measured group.
The clearest FDR-supported downstream event was Flna induction in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut after Actg1 perturbation.
191 MB P MY GABA showed an isolated down-regulation of Fbh1, with no accompanying DNA-repair or replication-stress module.
Actg1 had no robust data-driven signature neighbor: the strongest feature-wise residual cosines were very small and the nearest non-safe targets were mostly flat perturbations themselves.
Represented actin-network targets, including Rho/WAVE, MRTF, myosin, tropomyosin, and filamin-family perturbations, did not phenocopy Actg1 in the two Actg1 responder classes.
Postnatal CRISPR loss of Actg1 did not recapitulate a broad ACTG1 actinopathy program in mouse neurons.
Postnatal Actn4 CRISPR loss of function was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Actn4 had no meaningful positive or negative whole-transcriptome neighbor in the screen.
Actn4 did not phenocopy NMDA receptor subunit loss in excitatory neurons.
Single perturbations of the mGluR/CaMKII and F-actin-regulatory neighborhood were also mostly buffered at the basal nuclear RNA level.
Acvr1 produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event: down-regulation of the PI3P phosphatase Mtmr3 in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
The Acvr1 result does not belong to a coherent BMP/TGF receptor-SMAD perturbation module in this postnatal neuronal assay.
Acvr1 loss failed to move the canonical BMP-SMAD Id/feedback transcriptional program in every measured neuronal group.
Data-driven signature neighbors of Acvr1 were mathematically real but biologically too weak to keep as convergent modules.
The neuronal Acvr1 LoF surface is opposite in design to ACVR1 disease mechanisms built from activating alleles in mesenchymal or oligodendroglial contexts.

Acvr2a loss of function was transcriptionally silent across all 21 recovered neuronal cell groups: no group had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10 and no expected SMAD or activity-response sentinel reached FDR<0.10.

The flat Acvr2a surface was mirrored by represented activin/BMP/TGF-beta receptor and SMAD targets: Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad3, Smad4, Smad6, Smad9, Tgfbr1, and Tgfbr3 had zero matched FDR<0.10 genes, while Acvr1, Bmpr2, Tgfbr2, Bmpr1b, and Smad2 showed only one or two isolated singleton genes.

Whole-profile Acvr2a signature neighbors were null-like or unrelated: the highest Pearson neighbors were Adam10, Xpr1, Safe_target_66, Unc13b, and Safe_target_23, whereas the lowest were unrelated Psmc1 and Psmb4 proteasome signatures despite still having positive correlations.
The screen models sparse single-cell Acvr2a LoF, not an extracellular ActRIIA-Fc ligand trap: neither Acvr2a nor its retained type-II partners generated a basal neuronal transcriptional signature.
Acvr2b perturbation produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
Acvr2b loss did not trigger or repress a sustained canonical SMAD transcriptional program in any measured group.
Represented ACVR/TGFβ/BMP receptor and SMAD relatives showed near-zero score correlations to Acvr2b and did not converge on an Acvr2b-like FDR signature.
The data-driven Acvr2b nearest neighbors were only weakly correlated, and the strongest broad responder among them, Qrich1, was weakly anticorrelated rather than convergent.
The postmitotic neuronal null separates Acvr2b's embryonic laterality/axis requirement from basal juvenile neuronal transcriptomic maintenance.
Acvrl1 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 neuronal cell groups in which it was recovered.
Represented ALK1 partners and TGF-beta/BMP receptor-family targets did not phenocopy Acvrl1 in neurons.
Acvrl1 loss did not trigger the canonical endothelial ALK1-SMAD-ID, arteriovenous-marker, or PI3K-axis transcripts in the neuronal nuclei.
Full-transcriptome comparison found no meaningful positive or negative Acvrl1 signature neighbor.
Adam10 produced no BH-supported downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 9 neuronal cell groups in which it was recovered.
Measurable APP, Notch, and synaptic-adhesion relatives failed to form a shared Adam10-like RNA module.
The Adam10 all-gene signature sat at the empirical noise floor while Wdr26 proved that comparable recovered cell numbers can produce hundreds to thousands of DE genes.
The Adam10 null should not be read as absence of Alzheimer-relevant α-secretase biology.

Adam22 loss produced a strongly buffered neuronal snRNA-seq surface: one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 21 recovered cell groups and 355046 tested Adam22 rows, despite recurrent mild decreases in Adam22 mRNA.
The only downstream Adam22 hit was Pum3 up-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Adam22 did not transcriptionally engage the canonical AMPAR, MAGUK, TARP, Kv1, immediate-early, or ISR/UPR modules expected if sparse deletion caused a cell-autonomous excitability or stress state.

Represented direct complex or receptor-subunit comparators did not phenocopy Adam22: Cacng2, Dlg4, and Kcna1 were downstream-null in all Adam22-matched groups, and Gria1/2/3/Kcna2 each produced only one isolated downstream row elsewhere.

The unbiased Adam22 signature neighbors were extremely weak: continuous score cosines peaked at Syn1 r=0.0367 and Stag2 r=0.0300, whereas the strongest negative non-safe neighbors were Ikzf3, Wdr26, and Il1rapl2 with |cosine|<0.018.
Sparse postnatal Adam22 loss failed to mimic the transcriptional footprint one might expect from biallelic ADAM22 epileptic encephalopathy or lethal mouse loss.
Adamts17 produced a pan-neuronal null DE surface: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 non-self genes at FDR<0.10, and the best downstream Adamts17 q value was 0.274.

The fibrillin/BMP-SMAD program predicted from Adamts17 growth-plate biology was not recovered in postmitotic neurons: Fbn1, Fbn2, BMP/TGF-beta markers all had Adamts17 FDR=1.0, and represented Fbn1, Bmpr, Tgfbr, and Smad perturbations were themselves flat or single-gene responders.
Genome-wide score-space neighbors of Adamts17 were noise-scale: the strongest positive neighbor was Nipa1 at r=0.0363 and the strongest negative neighbor was Wdr26 at r=-0.0251.
Adar produced one FDR-threshold downstream hit: Dync1li2 was selectively down-regulated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Adar did not phenocopy the ADAR-family comparator Adarb1; Adarb1 drove a recurrent Flnb-dominated module across 13 matched groups whereas Adar had no shared significant genes.
The literature-predicted MDA5/type-I-interferon response was absent after Adar perturbation in every measured neuronal group.
Unbiased cross-target neighbors were essentially zero-correlated and included safe-target controls, so no hidden Adar-like transcriptional module was nominated by the full perturbation universe.
Flnb is the dominant recurrent abundance biomarker of Adarb1 perturbation, down in 13 cell groups and ranked as the strongest Flnb-depleting perturbation in every matched responding group.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is the only cell group with a multi-gene Adarb1 response, combining Flnb down, Flna down, Zfp941 down, and Fam20c up.
Zfp941 down-regulation is confined to posterior Adarb1 responders and always appears with strong Flnb down-regulation.
Adarb1 loss did not change the abundance of the canonical edited ion-channel and receptor substrate mRNAs Gria2, Gria3, Gabra3, Htr2c, Kcna1, or Ryr2.
Adar and direct substrate perturbations failed to phenocopy Adarb1 in the model-visible DE universe.
Tpr, Ogt, Uba5, and Psmb4 were the strongest same-direction restricted neighbors of the sparse Adarb1 signature.
Rnpc3, Sin3a, and Wdr26 opposed Adarb1 on the same restricted Flnb, Flna, Zfp941, or Fam20c features.
Adarb1 produced a large number of cell-type zeros and one-gene effects rather than a broad transcriptional stress program.
Sparse P16 Adcy1 loss of function was barren at FDR<0.10 in all 20 recovered neuronal groups.
The expected activity-dependent cAMP/PKA/ERK/CREB immediate-early program was absent.
NMDAR subunit perturbations were detectable where Adcy1 was flat.
Some calcium/cAMP/CREB nodes responded, but the Adcy1 branch remained silent.
Single transmembrane adenylyl-cyclase perturbations were family-wide buffered in the matched brain groups.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbor search found no robust Adcy1-like transcriptional signature.
Wild-type Adcy1 LoF did not resemble the Fragile-X ADCY1 overexpression state.
Adcy3 loss was a pan-neuronal downstream null in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR assay.

The expected cAMP linear pathway did not phenocopy: Adcy1 and Adcy5 were also downstream-null, Gnas/Gnal and Pde4b/Pde4d were flat or singleton responders, and only the nuclear Creb1/Crebbp arm produced a restricted TH signature.
direction_pattern: Adcy-family null; CREB-axis restricted response after Creb1/Crebbp only

canonical_summary: ADCY3 was not an outlier among measured ciliary genes: Bbs5, Ttc8, Ift88, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l perturbations were also essentially flat in neuronal nuclear RNA.
Adcy3 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbors; the best score-vector correlations were |r|≤0.033.
A 3-4 week whole-neuronal RNA signature is a poor biomarker for ADCY3 engagement.
Adcy5 CRISPR perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across all recovered neuronal groups: 22 measured cell groups each had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The striatal-like CNU-LGE cAMP module was inducible by Pde10a loss but not by Adcy5 loss: Pde10a knockdown up-regulated Scg2 and Crem, whereas the same two genes were FDR-flat after Adcy5.
The represented membrane adenylyl-cyclase paralogs shared the absence of downstream DE: Adcy1, Adcy3, and Adcy5 each produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered cell groups.
Most represented upstream and downstream cAMP-pathway perturbations were also nearly silent in basal transcriptome, even when Prkaca showed strong own-transcript depletion.

A data-driven full-surface signature search yielded only trivial Adcy5 neighbors; the top positive score correlation was Smc1a at r=0.0329 and the strongest negative annotated target was Ndufb8 at r=-0.0180.
The null CRISPR-LoF surface does not phenocopy ADCY5 movement-disorder alleles, particularly dominant gain-of-function alleles that elevate cAMP.
P16 Add1 loss-of-function was pan-null at the single-nucleus transcriptional level: all 21 recovered neuronal classes had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Add1 did not transcriptionally compensate through the measured membrane-skeleton genes Add2, Add3, Sptan1, Sptbn1, Sptbn2, Ank2, Ank3, or Actg1.
The literature-obvious related perturbations Add2, Add3, and Ank2 phenocopied Add1 as complete transcriptional nulls, whereas Sptan1 produced only a sparse surface dominated by its own transcript.
Unbiased target-neighbor search also failed: the top positive and top inverse Add1 signature neighbors were only B9d1 and Wdr26 with |r|<0.03.
The absence of stress, synaptic-gene, or cytoskeletal transcription after juvenile Add1 perturbation narrows ADD1 disease biology away from acute nuclear collapse in surviving young neurons.
Acute sparse P16 Add2 loss-of-function produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The adducin paralog axis was RNA-buffered: Add1 and Add3 were unchanged downstream of Add2, and direct Add1/Add3 perturbations were themselves null in their recovered groups.
Measured spectrin-actin and PKC-neighbor perturbations did not converge with Add2 in score space.
Add2 had no meaningful unbiased signature neighbors: the largest positive and negative genome-wide correlations were near zero.
Add3 loss of function generated a pan-measured neuronal snRNA-seq null: 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The obvious α- and β-adducin paralog perturbations, Add1 and Add2, also lacked any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, so the Add3 null is shared by individual adducin-family targets rather than unique to the γ subunit.

A search of 1,772 other target labels found no meaningful Add3 signature neighbor: the largest absolute all-coordinate cosine was only 0.0285, and the top non-safe positive and top negative gene targets were Hspa5 and Wdr26 with no FDR-level Add3 overlap.
Adgra1 acute postmitotic CRISPR loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The PSD/synaptic, PI3K-AKT-GSK3B, MEK-ERK, and hypothalamic thermogenesis transcripts nominated by germline Adgra1 knockout studies were absent from the Adgra1 DE surface.
Genome-wide score-vector neighbors of Adgra1 had tiny correlations, with top real-gene Pearson r values from -0.016 to 0.029, and did not reveal a hidden convergent transcriptional module.
Represented PSD95, PI3K/AKT, MAPK, G-protein, Rac/Cdc42, and Wnt-receptor pathway targets did not phenocopy Adgra1 in matched neuronal DE.
Adgra1 loss did not induce Adgra2, Adgra3, or broader adhesion-GPCR transcriptional compensation, and broad adhesion-GPCR target perturbations were themselves flat.
This screen nominates no acute neuronal mRNA pharmacodynamic biomarker for ADGRA1 modulation.

Acute P16 Adgrb1 loss produced a pan-neuronally flat nuclear transcriptome: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the self-transcript was not detectably reduced after multiple-testing correction.

No represented BAI-family or BAI1 Rac-axis comparator phenocopied a transcriptional Adgrb1 signature: Adgrb3, Baiap2, and Tiam1 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes overall, and Rac1 had only one downstream gene across 22 tested groups.

Whole-surface signature search found no convincing Adgrb1-like perturbation; the strongest positive neighbors had correlations of only 0.035 or 0.031, whereas the strongest negative biological neighbor, Wdr26, robustly changed 3128 downstream genes while Adgrb1 remained flat.

The hippocampal-containing 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut group showed no Adgrb1 transcriptional responder despite literature in which much earlier and stronger BAI1 depletion changes hippocampal dendrite arbors and plasticity.
Adgrb3 produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: 22 of 23 cell groups were recovered, but no cell group contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

The C1QL/BAI3-GluD2/Rac1 cerebellar-synapse prior did not map onto a shared nuclear signature: Adgrb1 and Grid2 were fully null in matched groups, and Rtn4r and Rac1 had only 2 and 1 unrelated FDR<0.10 genes with near-zero score cosines to Adgrb3.

Data-driven neighbors placed Adgrb3 close to the random null floor rather than to a coherent positive or negative program: the strongest score cosine was only 0.0263 and the strongest anti-neighbor was -0.0145.
No C1QL/BAI expected gene, synaptic effector, stress, proteostasis, or autophagy transcript passed FDR<0.10 after Adgrb3 perturbation.
P16 Adgrg1 CRISPR loss of function was transcriptomically buffered in every measured NeuN+ neuronal class: 22 of 22 assayed groups contained zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The Adgrg1 zero is not embedded in a hidden adhesion-GPCR module: whole-surface score correlations to all other perturbations were tiny, and represented paralogs Adgrg2 and Adgrg6 plus ECM/Rho-family comparators Dag1, Itgb1, and Cdc42 were themselves FDR<0.10 nulls across their assayed neuronal surfaces.
Neither the cortical GPR56-Col3a1/RhoA migration program nor an OPC/myelin marker response appeared as a secondary neuronal nuclear program after Adgrg1 perturbation.

Adgrg2 loss of function was transcriptionally silent throughout the measured NeuN-enriched juvenile brain surface: 22 measured cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.
The efferent-duct ADGRG2/CFTR/Gq/beta-arrestin axis was absent from the Adgrg2 neuronal DE surface.
Represented adhesion-GPCR relatives, including same-ADGRG-family Adgrg1 and Adgrg6, did not phenocopy Adgrg2 in the matched brain groups.
Adgrg2 had no credible data-driven signature neighborhood: the strongest positive and negative score-vector cosines were only +0.03465 and -0.03047 and overlapped safe-target magnitudes.
Adgrg6 loss was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: all 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical GPR126-cAMP-PKA-Schwann-myelin effectors were expected but absent after Adgrg6 perturbation in neurons.
Neither the data-driven neighbors nor related adhesion-GPCR and cAMP/myelin targets converged with Adgrg6.
ADGRG6 disease and therapeutic biology is displaced away from the sampled postmitotic neuronal transcriptome.
Adgrl1 produced a self-transcript decrease without any downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The ADGRL1 synaptic disease program was not recovered as differential expression of synaptic or inhibitory/excitatory marker transcripts after sparse postnatal Adgrl1 loss.
Latrophilin paralogs, extracellular ligands, neurexins, and intracellular/signaling neighbors failed to form a shared transcriptional module in the cell groups where Adgrl1 was flat.
Restricted data-driven Adgrl1 neighbors were weak and could not be validated by FDR-level shared DE.
Adgrl2 loss of function was transcriptionally silent by FDR criteria in every measured neuronal group.
The post-literature synaptic-adhesion and activity-response query was completely unrecovered in the Adgrl2 DE surface.
Represented latrophilin-family and FLRT/Teneurin/UNC5 comparators did not form a shared transcriptional module with Adgrl2.
The nearest data-driven Adgrl2 neighbors were algorithmic weak-signature neighbors, not biologically convergent FDR modules.
The flat neuronal result refines, rather than contradicts, embryonic and endothelial ADGRL2 disease biology.
Adgrl3 produced no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups in this P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR snRNA-seq screen.
Four groups had significant Adgrl3 self-RNA reduction but still showed 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Latrophilin paralogs and represented FLRT/Tenm/Unc5 relatives did not converge with Adgrl3; most were completely downstream-flat in matched groups.
The unbiased cross-target search found no robust positive or negative Adgrl3 signature neighbor.
The Adgrl3 LoF transcriptomic null does not test ADGRL3 variant-specific GPCR coupling mechanisms.
Acute Adgrv1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal cell groups.

Adgrv1 lacked a meaningful cross-perturbation signature neighbor; the closest data-driven neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations below 0.05 and the measured adhesion-GPCR relatives were themselves null.
Adgrv1 loss failed to activate candidate MAG/myelin, GPCR immediate-early, autophagy, or unfolded-protein-response genes in the sampled nuclei.
Adipor2 loss produced a one-gene responder, Smim10l1 up-regulation, restricted to 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The CNU-MGE Smim10l1 hit was uncoupled from canonical AMPK/PPAR-alpha/fatty-acid-oxidation, ceramide, autophagy, ER-stress, ISR, and redox transcriptional programs.
Represented APPL1, AMPK-alpha2, PPAR, and PGC-1-axis perturbations did not phenocopy Adipor2 and did not induce Smim10l1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

A blind score-vector scan found no strong transcriptomic neighbor for Adipor2: Asxl3 and Eef2 were the closest positive and negative targets, but both similarities were near zero and neither shared the CNU-MGE Smim10l1 hit.
Smim10l1 is an exploratory candidate sentinel for Adipor2 loss in 054 CNU-MGE GABA because its FDR<0.10 induction was unique to Adipor2 among 1,731 perturbations in that cell group.
Acute Adk loss produced no BH-significant downstream neuronal transcriptome in any of the 23 recovered cell groups.
The computed Adk nearest neighbors did not define a biological module.
Represented cAMP, phosphodiesterase, purine, and methylation-node perturbations failed to phenocopy Adk.
The Adk null argues against using this NeuN-enriched P16 screen to down-rank ADK as an adenosine-augmentation or epileptogenesis target.

P16 Adnp loss produced a narrow corrected neuronal response: 5 of 21 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 45 genes, while two taxonomy groups were not recovered for this target.

Chd4 was the only high-confidence mechanistic neighbor of Adnp: it was the top positive signature neighbor and shared same-direction FDR hits including Pvalb Cacnb3 and the thalamic Cpne7/Xylt2/Srrm4/Cacng7/Aifm3/Uchl1/Echdc2 cluster.
Cacnb3 was the recurrent positive Adnp biomarker, induced in Pvalb, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons GABA groups and also induced by Chd4 perturbation in Pvalb neurons.
Adnp repression of Plppr3 and Atp9a marks a small membrane-lipid/endosomal module across midbrain and thalamic responders.
Sst interneurons showed an isolated but corrected presynaptic-vesicle hit, Rab3a down-regulation, rather than the Cacnb3 induction seen in Pvalb neurons.
The 151 thalamic response included a mostly down-regulated cell-surface glycan/proteoglycan component, led by Xylt2 and joined by B3glct, Sdc3, Ptpru, Pcdh1, and Cdh24.

The same thalamic signature carried a secondary RNA/protein-handling and metabolic/redox skew: Srrm4, Cpsf6, Uchl1, and Anapc7 were down, Eif4b was up, and Gsr/Aifm3 rose while Acsl3/Acat1/Eno2/Echdc2 fell.

The literature-obvious chromatin and NDD comparators did not substitute for Adnp: BAF-adjacent Smarca2/Smarca4/Smarcc1/Smarcc2/Arid1b, NuRD-associated Gatad2b, Auts2, and Chd8 showed weak, absent, or distinct overlap with Adnp.
Corrected Adnp loss did not recover Wnt/β-catenin, neural-induction, cell-cycle, or broad canonical synaptic-marker programs in the P16 NeuN+ assay.

Sparse postnatal Adra1a loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups, including 052 Pvalb Gaba where the Adra1a RNA row itself decreased significantly.

A model-visible residual signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Adra1a transcriptional neighbor; the largest centered Pearson correlation was only 0.043 and involved a safe-target control.

Represented adrenergic-family and Gq-linked GPCR perturbations did not form an Adra1a-like basal transcriptomic module; the few responding comparators had only one to three FDR<0.10 genes in matched groups, while Adra1a had none.

Adra1a loss did not down-regulate a maintained activity/CREB immediate-early program in any recovered neuronal class, despite direct Creb1 and Camk2a perturbations producing detectable small signatures elsewhere in the same dataset.
Adra2a produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 23 assayed neuronal cell groups: Ppp2r2b up in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Zdhhc21 down in 053 Sst Gaba.
direction_pattern: Ppp2r2b up in Pvalb; Zdhhc21 down in Sst

canonical_summary: Ppp2r2b was selectively up-regulated after Adra2a perturbation in Pvalb neurons, nominating a PP2A-B55 regulatory compensation.
Zdhhc21 was selectively down-regulated after Adra2a perturbation in Sst neurons, suggesting cell-type-specific adjustment of a palmitoyltransferase rather than a shared alpha2A program.
Adra2a perturbation did not induce a detectable immediate-early, CREB/cAMP-feedback, G-protein, HCN, KCNJ, or KCNQ transcript program in any assayed group.
Adrenergic receptor, G-protein/cAMP, PDE, HCN/KCNQ/KCNJ/Ca2+-channel, GABAB, and Ppp2r2b perturbations were directly queried and did not converge with Adra2a.
Data-driven Adra2a signature neighbors had near-zero correlations and did not share the Pvalb/Sst Adra2a marker genes.
The Adra2a basal snRNA null should not be read as evidence that alpha2A is an inert or poor CNS drug target.
Adra2b produced a one-gene, FDR<0.10 response in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, down-regulating the histone-variant gene Macroh2a1.
Adra2b loss did not activate a detectable cAMP/MAPK or immediate-early transcript program even in the one responsive group.
Unbiased cross-target signature neighbors were extremely weak: Aff2 was the top positive real-gene neighbor and Grm7 the strongest negative real-gene neighbor, but neither shared the Macroh2a1 hit.
The measured adrenergic receptors did not phenocopy Adra2b: Adra2a had a separate two-gene interneuron response, Adra1a/Adrb2/Adrb3 were FDR-flat, and Adra2c was not represented.
The weak mouse Adra2b loss-of-function surface should not be read as a direct negative model of the human ADRA2B del301-303 emotional-memory allele.
Adrb2 was a complete basal neuronal transcriptomic null: all 23 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and every Adrb2 self-transcript row had FDR 1.0.
The expected CREB and immediate-early sentinels downstream of β-adrenergic cAMP signaling were absent after Adrb2 perturbation.
β-adrenergic and proximal cAMP-pathway perturbations were flat like Adrb2, whereas direct Creb1 perturbation produced a small Crem-centered transcriptional response.
The model-visible, row-normalized genome-wide signature search found no nontrivial Adrb2-convergent or Adrb2-opposing perturbation.

Adrb3 is a pan-null perturbation in the recovered juvenile neuronal atlas: every one of the 23 measured glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, thalamic, midbrain and cerebellar groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The canonical beta-adrenergic cAMP/PKA/thermogenic transcriptional chain was not engaged by Adrb3 loss: Adrb2, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, Ppargc1a, Ppara and Pparg were also flat at FDR<0.10, while Creb1 produced only a small CREM-dominated response that Adrb3 did not share.
The reported amygdala Glut3/Slc2a3 correlate of germline Adrb3 loss was absent after acute P16 neuronal Adrb3 perturbation.
Aebp1 loss produced no FDR-resolved downstream genes in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.

Aebp1 perturbation did not recover collagen/ECM, PPAR-gamma, NF-kappaB, or TGF-beta/integrin programs, and represented comparator perturbations in those axes were also flat or singleton-only in matched neurons.
Whole-surface signature search found only near-zero positive and negative Aebp1 neighbors; none shared FDR<0.10 genes with Aebp1.
The neuronal null should not be used to deprioritize or de-risk extracellular ACLP inhibition for fibrosis or connective-tissue disease.
Aff2 produced a single robust total-mRNA hit, Susd4 down-regulation, and only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons.
The Aff2-responsive gene Susd4 links the Aff2 perturbation to a neuronal complement/AMPAR-plasticity molecule rather than to a full complement or multi-gene stress transcriptome.
Aff2 loss did not create a broad steady-state RNA-polymerase-II elongation or G-quadruplex splicing abundance signature in postmitotic neurons.
The represented AFF paralog Aff3 and the Fragile-X comparator Fmr1 did not converge with Aff2.
Aff2 has no robust data-driven signature neighbor: the strongest positive and negative score correlations were nearly zero.
Aff3 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal mRNA null rather than a maintenance transcriptional program in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR assay.
The embryonic Aff3-Laf4/Mdga2 cortical migration axis was not reactivated or maintained as a detectable postnatal cortical IT/ET/NP transcriptomic dependency.
The only measured AFF-family paralog, Aff2, was essentially orthogonal to Aff3.
An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Aff3-like or Aff3-opposing target in the full model-visible DE universe.
Afg3l2 produced a one-gene, L2/3 IT-restricted responder: Cdh7 was down-regulated in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut while every other measured group had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The expected AFG3L2 mitochondrial proteotoxicity/OMA1-ISR transcriptional program was absent after Afg3l2 perturbation, even though Opa1 perturbation in the same parquet robustly induced Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, amino-acid tRNA synthetases and mt-OXPHOS repression.

Represented mitochondrial-protease relatives were not interchangeable with Afg3l2: Yme1l1 and Clpx were transcriptomically flat, Clpp had a single GABA hit, and Lonp1 had only 8 FDR-significant genes outside the Afg3l2 Cdh7-positive cortical group.

The pre-literature, all-target neighbor search did not find a strong Afg3l2 signature neighbor: the top positive global score correlation was Opa1 at r=0.0328 and the top negative was Safe_target_28 at r=-0.0121.
Ager loss-of-function was transcriptomically inert across all 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every group and no corrected self-transcript change.
Ager had no meaningful signature convergence with either data-driven neighbors or represented RAGE/Aβ/TLR/NF-kappaB pathway comparators.

The screen provides no autonomous juvenile-neuronal RAGE biomarker signature, redirecting RAGE-target interpretation toward ligand-rich disease, vascular, microglial/astrocytic, macrophage, or lung assays.
Postnatal Agk loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
Agk perturbation did not induce the expected TIM22-carrier, sideroflexin/one-carbon, OXPHOS, or ATF4/UPR/ISR marker transcripts.
Measured mitochondrial and lipid comparators, including Slc25a4, Dgke, Tomm40, Dnajc19, Afg3l2, Yme1l1, Clpp, Lonp1, and Micu1, did not converge with Agk.
The neuronal flatness of CRISPR Agk loss should not be read as broad AGK-inhibition safety.
The pre-literature full-profile Agk neighbors were nearly uncorrelated and biologically non-diagnostic.
Ago1 loss-of-function produced an almost flat whole-transcriptome surface: only Kif13b in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut passed FDR<0.10 across 20 measured neuronal groups.
Kif13b up-regulation marks the only FDR-qualified transcriptomic consequence of Ago1 perturbation, and it is restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Represented core miRNA/RISC relatives did not phenocopy Ago1: Ago2 and Dicer1 each had zero FDR<0.10 genes in the 20 Ago1-matched groups, Tnrc6b had zero in 19 matched groups, and Tnrc6a had only two modest MB Glut genes.
The P16 sparse Ago1 CRISPR perturbation did not recreate a broad Argonaute-syndrome-like neuronal transcriptional disturbance.
Genome-wide score-vector comparison found no strong positive or negative Ago1 signature neighbor; the best correlations among 1,772 other targets were tiny, with |r| below 0.03.
Acute P16 Ago2 perturbation produced no robust single-nucleus mRNA program in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The all-target signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Ago2 neighbor.
Canonical miRNA/RISC perturbations represented in the same parquet also failed to converge on an Ago2-like response.
Ago2 syndrome biology is not reproduced as an acute, sparse, postmitotic mRNA-derepression or stress signature.

Agps produced FDR-supported downstream transcriptional signal only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Dhcr24, Lmtk3, and Cyp51 were up-regulated; the other 20 measured Agps groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
direction_pattern: 151-specific up-regulation of Dhcr24, Lmtk3, and Cyp51

canonical_summary: The Agps responder up-regulated two cholesterol-biosynthesis enzymes, Dhcr24 and Cyp51, consistent with a small sterol rebound after perturbing ether-lipid synthesis.
Marchf6 loss converged with Agps on Dhcr24 and Cyp51 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Srebf2 loss drove the same sterol genes in the opposite direction.
Mib1 was the top positive data-driven neighbor of the Agps three-gene 151 signature and itself induced a broad sterol program in the same cell group.
Far1, Pex1, Pex14, and Hmgcr did not reproduce the Agps Dhcr24/Cyp51/Lmtk3 signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Lmtk3 was the only non-sterol FDR-supported Agps downstream gene and was not part of the Srebf2/Marchf6 sterol core.
direction_pattern: up after Agps only among these restricted comparisons

canonical_summary: Agrp produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered cell groups.
The top data-driven neighbors of Agrp had near-zero score correlations and were rejected as biologically meaningful signature matches.
Measurable Agrp-related neuromodulator targets were flat or nearly flat in the same screen, despite belonging to feeding GPCR, NPY, GABA, or melanocortin-adjacent biology.
Known MC4R-pathway druggability is not mirrored by an Agrp nuclear-RNA biomarker panel in this assay.

Agtr1a loss was globally flat in the basal P16-to-P37/44 neuronal Perturb-seq assay: every recovered cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Agtr1a self-transcript was never significant.

Represented angiotensin and proximal Gq-pathway comparators did not converge with Agtr1a: Agtr2, Plcb1, and Itpr1 were also transcriptionally flat, Agtrap had only one singleton Elmo1 hit, and all four signatures correlated with Agtr1a at r≤0.0133.

Agtr1a loss did not induce the immediate-early, neuropeptide, inflammatory, ROS, or ER-stress markers expected from active AT1R signaling, although the same DE universe detected Gfpt1 UPR and Eef2 IEG/neuropeptide programs.
Acute P16 Agtr2 CRISPR loss of function produced no robust steady-state neuronal transcriptional response at P37-P44 in any measured cell group.
The in-parquet renin-angiotensin relatives did not reveal a hidden neuronal Ang II transcriptional module: Agtr1a was completely flat and Agtrap had only a single Elmo1 hit in one GABAergic group.
Canonical AT2R neurite-outgrowth, MAPK, phosphatase, NO/cGMP, and immediate-early readouts were absent from the Agtr2 DE surface.
Agtr2's nearest whole-vector signature neighbors sat at the global noise floor rather than defining a convergent module.
Agtrap loss produced one corrected downstream response, Elmo1 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Agtrap did not phenocopy represented renin-angiotensin or Rac pathway comparators.
Agtrap had only weak all-gene score neighbors, and the closest 054 CNU-MGE GABA neighbors did not share a corrected Elmo1 signature.
Sparse postmitotic Ahr loss produced no robust whole-transcriptome response in any measured neuronal group.
The basal AHR/ARNT/AHRR feedback and xenobiotic target program was absent from Ahr-perturbed NeuN+ neurons.
AHR-linked CNS inflammatory and neurogenic programs were not engaged by acute mature-neuron Ahr loss.
Ahr has no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Ahrr loss produced a pan-neuronal FDR null and did not de-repress the canonical AHR xenobiotic-response gene battery.
The AHR branch was jointly flat: Ahr and Arnt perturbations, not only Ahrr, lacked FDR-supported downstream responses in matched neuronal groups.
Active Bmal1/Clock circadian bHLH-PAS signatures contrasted with the flat Ahrr/Ahr/Arnt/Hif1a/Bmal2/Npas3 surfaces.
The top data-driven Ahrr signature neighbors were near-null and were rejected as a convergent biological module.
Aimp1 was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null after acute P16 CRISPR loss of function.
Aimp1 loss did not trigger a detectable amino-acid-starvation, ISR/UPR, or proteostasis transcriptional program.
Aimp1 did not converge with Nefl, Nefm, or Nefh perturbations despite AIMP1/p43's known neurofilament-light interaction.
Unsupervised Aimp1 signature neighbors were effectively uncorrelated, so Atxn10 and Paqr7 were rejected as meaningful biological phenocopies.
The screen could not test same-complex cytosolic MSC redundancy, and the represented mitochondrial aaRS disease-family targets did not converge with Aimp1.
Akap11-targeting CRISPR produced a pan-measured buffered nuclear transcriptome: 22 recovered neuronal groups all had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The expected PKA-RI, AKAP11-autophagy-partner, immediate-early, and synaptic marker mRNAs were explicitly present but unchanged in every Akap11 group.
Full-profile signature search did not find a biologically convincing Akap11 neighbor.
Literature-obvious AKAP/PKA/GSK3β comparators showed no Akap11-like transcriptional module; only Gsk3b made a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response where Akap11 was still flat.
The genetic risk gene Akap11 is not an acute driver of a large, cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA state in juvenile postmitotic brain.
Akap6 perturbation was a target-wide basal transcriptomic null: every one of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
BDNF/cAMP/calcineurin-NFAT and apoptosis/stress transcripts were measurable but never significant after Akap6 perturbation.
Direct AKAP6/cAMP/Ca2+ relatives were mostly flat like Akap6, whereas Mef2c and a few calcineurin/calmodulin relatives showed small, cell-restricted transcriptional responses.
Unbiased whole-signature neighbors of Akap6 had score-cosine magnitudes near zero and did not define a convergent module.
The Akap6 null should not be used to rule out AKAP6-directed neuroprotective interventions that act through stimulated protein-protein interactions.
Akap9 loss produced no robust downstream whole-transcriptome response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Biochemical linkage to NMDA receptors did not translate into a Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b-like transcriptional phenotype.
Akap9 joins represented AKAP-family and cAMP/PKA-pathway perturbations in a mostly buffered transcriptomic class.
The Golgi/centrosome AKAP450 microtubule function maps to architecture and developmental timing rather than to an Akap9-triggered adult-like stress transcriptome.
The transcriptome did not phenocopy the cardiac Yotiao-KCNQ disease axis in neurons.
Akap9 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Akt3 loss-of-function was transcriptionally all-null across the recovered postmitotic neuronal atlas: no measured cell group had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The Akt3-null surface is not a generic failure to detect PI3K/mTOR-axis transcription: Tsc2, Mtor and Gsk3b perturbations produced FDR<0.10 genes in the same analysis universe, whereas Akt3 had none.

Several directly represented PI3K-AKT relatives were flat alongside Akt3: Pik3cb, Pik3r1, Pik3r2 and Rptor each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and their score correlations with Akt3 were |r|≤0.019.
Postnatal CRISPR loss of Akt3 did not mirror the transcriptomic consequences expected from activating AKT3/PIK3R2/PIK3CA overgrowth alleles.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbor search nominated no robust Akt3 module: the top positive and negative correlations were only +0.0656 and -0.0308.
Acute Alk loss of function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic zero: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in each of the 21 measured cell groups, with only two subthreshold weak bins.
The expected RAS/MAPK, PI3K/STAT, and ERK-ETV5-RET ALK outputs were absent after Alk perturbation.
Generic RTK/RAS/MAPK perturbations did respond in this same analysis universe, whereas Alk did not.
A data-driven genome-scale neighbor search found no meaningful Alk phenocopy or anti-phenocopy.
The neuronal Alk loss-of-function surface separates wild-type receptor loss from ALK activating alleles in neural-crest cancer.
Acute P16 Alkbh8 loss was buffered at the basal mRNA level across the recovered neuronal panel: every measured cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and no on-target FDR signal.

Upstream Elongator loss and Alkbh8 loss are transcriptionally uncoupled: Elp1 and Elp2 converged on a shared ISR/amino-acid program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Alkbh8 had no FDR-significant gene in the same class.

The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not reveal a robust Alkbh8 module: the nearest score-vector neighbors had absolute cosine values of only 0.053 or less, and the top positive and negative neighbors produced their own FDR signatures where Alkbh8 was flat.

The absence of an Alkbh8 mRNA phenotype despite ALKBH8-linked intellectual disability and germline brain redox phenotypes refines the disease model toward developmental, challenged, or protein-level mechanisms rather than an acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptional program.

Acute postmitotic Alms1-targeting perturbation produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal RNA response: 22 measured cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite an assayed Alms1 self-transcript.

The data-driven Alms1 signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor after group-gene centering; the best non-safe positive neighbor was Lztfl1 and the best negative was Crebbp, but both were nearly uncorrelated.
Represented primary-cilium, BBSome, intraflagellar-transport, and ciliary-GPCR targets did not phenocopy Alms1 on the neuronal transcriptome.
Expected ciliary-GPCR, endosomal-recycling, α-actinin, Hedgehog, and TGF-beta sentinel transcripts were present but not regulated after Alms1 targeting in any measured neuronal group.
Alx1 loss of function was almost completely buffered in the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal assay, with only Lztr1 up-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA reaching FDR<0.10.
Lztr1 was the only FDR-supported Alx1 downstream gene, rising in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
The literature-obvious ALX paralogs Alx3 and Alx4 failed to phenocopy Alx1 in matched neuronal groups.
Whole-transcriptome data-driven neighbors of Alx1 were near-zero and did not validate as shared 059/Lztr1 responders.

Acute Alx3 loss in P16 postmitotic neurons was almost transcriptionally buffered: the assay found one robust downstream gene across 23 measured cell groups and 388023 downstream gene-by-cell-group tests.
The only robust Alx3 downstream event was decreased Serinc3 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Alx1 and Alx4 did not phenocopy the Alx3 Serinc3 hit in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and were themselves nearly silent in neuronal nuclei.

The pre-literature signature-neighbor scan rejected a meaningful whole-surface Alx3 neighbor: the largest non-safe positive score correlation was Pou3f3 at r=0.035 and the strongest non-safe anticorrelation was Npy1r at r=-0.010.
Alx4 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptional program in any of the 23 recovered postnatal neuronal cell groups.

Neither data-driven signature neighbors nor literature-obvious ALX4 relatives produced an ALX4-like robust signature; the strongest beta-catenin/TCF effector responses, Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, diverged by showing hundreds of DE genes where Alx4 had zero.

Acute postnatal Amfr loss was transcriptionally buffered across all 21 recovered neuronal groups: no non-Amfr gene reached FDR<0.10, even in the two groups with significant Amfr self-transcript depletion.

Amfr did not induce a UPR/ERAD bounce-back program: Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Dnajb9, Hyou1, Pdia6, Herpud1, Creld2, Sel1l, and Asns all stayed at FDR=1.0 after Amfr perturbation, whereas Manf and Hspa5 perturbations produced coherent UPR/ERAD signatures in the same DE universe.

The sterol/SREBP module was MARCHF6-responsive but AMFR-insensitive in midbrain/thalamic glutamatergic neurons: Marchf6 up-regulated Insig1, Hmgcr, Msmo1, Cyp51, Dhcr24, Fdps, Ldlr, Sqle, and Srebf2 in 151/155 groups, whereas the same genes were FDR=1.0 after Amfr.

A lymphocyte-defined GP78-UBAC2-LMBR1L Wnt-control mechanism did not manifest as a neuronal Wnt response after Amfr loss, even though direct Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 perturbations down-regulated the Wnt reporter Axin2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The lack of an early neuronal UPR, sterol, or Wnt transcriptome after mosaic Amfr loss suggests that AMFR-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia is unlikely to be reproduced by a 3-4 week autonomous nuclear stress program in juvenile brain neurons alone.
Acute postnatal Ammecr1 loss of function was transcriptomically silent across all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Ammecr1 CRISPR did not induce the paralogous AMMECR1L compensatory transcript in any measured neuronal group.
The proliferative cell-cycle and apoptosis programs expected from AMMECR1 knockdown in A549 cells were not recovered in postmitotic neurons.
Data-driven cross-perturbation search placed Ammecr1 in a near-zero, null-like neighborhood rather than in a coherent positive or negative module.
Acsl4, the only represented AMME/Xq22 disease-region comparator, did not phenocopy Ammecr1.
Ank1 produced only one downstream FDR<0.10 event across 22 recovered neuronal groups: B4galnt1 down in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
B4galnt1 down-regulation nominates ganglioside biosynthesis as a candidate Ank1-sensitive marker in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Canonical AnkR partners in Pvalb and cerebellar neurons were uncoupled from the Ank1 nuclear RNA response.
Measured Ank1 relatives and AnkR/Kv3 neighbors did not converge with Ank1 or with one another as a shared RNA module.
Ank1's empirical whole-surface neighbors were null-like and had near-zero score correlations.
The juvenile neuronal Ank1 LoF null is orthogonal to the Alzheimer's ANK1 signal in aged human microglia.
Ank2 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The Sema3A/L1CAM/Nrp1/cofilin pathway predicted by AnkB440 growth-cone work was absent at the transcript level under Ank2 perturbation.
Directly testable ankyrin/spectrin/adducin/L1CAM structural comparators were as flat as Ank2 or only minimally active.
Sodium-channel and KCNQ perturbations showed strong target engagement in several cases but little downstream RNA output, paralleling the Ank2 null.
Full-vector signature neighbors of Ank2 were extremely weak, with best broad cosine similarities near zero and no shared FDR gene set.
Ank2 disease biology is unlikely to be tracked by a juvenile mosaic RNA biomarker in this assay.
Ank mRNA was measurably depleted without any FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in several broad neuronal classes.
The canonical extracellular pyrophosphate/mineralization axis and generic neuronal stress markers were not induced or repressed after Ank perturbation.
Three represented brain-calcification/phosphate-homeostasis comparators, Slc20a2, Xpr1, and Pdgfrb, also failed to converge with Ank in the same neuronal Perturb-seq assay.
Ank had no meaningful transcriptome-wide positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Ankfy1 perturbation produced no FDR-qualified downstream transcriptional response in any of 22 recovered juvenile neuronal cell groups.
Ankfy1 did not phenocopy measurable endolysosomal, retromer, mTOR, or autophagy-adjacent responders in the same target universe.
Full-transcriptome signature-neighbor search placed Ankfy1 among extremely low-amplitude, mostly null-like perturbations.
The 308 CB GABA zero refines, but does not contradict, aged Ankfy1 Purkinje-cell degeneration.

P16 Ankrd11 loss was narrow rather than pan-neuronal: 6 of 23 measured groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the three multi-gene responses were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried the dominant Ankrd11 signature, with 25 downstream genes and a mostly up-regulated receptor, GPCR-modulator, potassium-channel, and RNA-regulatory program.
Midbrain glutamatergic and pontomedullary/midbrain GABAergic responders shared an electrogenic module centered on Atp1a3 and Atp1b1, with Kcnc1 recurring in 191 MB P MY GABA and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The expected BDNF/TrkB transcriptional module was absent: Bdnf, Ntrk2, Arc, Fos, Junb, and Egr1 had no FDR<0.10 hits in the Ankrd11 surface.
Brd4 and Setd5, not the ANCO paralog Nsd2-like noise, were the FDR-supported positive Ankrd11 signature neighbors.
Proteasome and spliceosome perturbations inverted the Ankrd11 electrogenic/synaptic signature rather than converging with it.
Ankrd12, Ncoa1, Ncoa3, Ep300, and Hdac8 failed to phenocopy Ankrd11, while Crebbp produced only a small opposite thalamic overlap.
Cohesin-axis targets did not simply reproduce the Ankrd11 signature despite the biochemical ANKRD11-cohesin interaction.
The Phactr1 and Tub singleton effects are real FDR<0.10 hits but not coherent recurrent Ankrd11 programs.
Ankrd12 loss produced a single corrected downstream event, U2surp down-regulation, restricted to 155 MB Glut.
At the only Ankrd12 downstream row, U2surp in 155 MB Glut, all FDR-qualified cross-target neighbors were inverse rather than same-direction.
The ANCO paralog Ankrd11 and the measured p160 coactivators Ncoa1 and Ncoa3 did not phenocopy the Ankrd12 U2surp decrease in 155 MB Glut.
Adult-cognitive-function genes that were represented in the parquet did not reproduce the Ankrd12 U2surp response in 155 MB Glut.
Antxr1 loss produced no FDR-controlled downstream transcriptional signature in any of the 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
The expected ANTXR1 ECM/VEGF/CTGF and Wnt/LRP6 transcriptional outputs were specifically absent after Antxr1 perturbation.
Neuronal Wnt signatures were detectable in the same analysis universe, but they were restricted to Wnt-core perturbations rather than to Antxr1.
The anthrax-toxin receptor paralog Antxr2 was also largely buffered in neuronal nuclei and did not reveal a hidden ANTXR-family neuronal ECM module.
Whole-universe signature search found no convincing positive or inverse Antxr1 perturbation neighbor.
Antxr2 produced an extremely restricted corrected response: a single CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic hit, Mga down-regulation, with no corrected DEGs in the rest of the neuronal surface.
The canonical ANTXR2 collagen/ECM program was not transcriptionally induced in any NeuN-enriched neuronal group.
Antxr2 did not converge with the Lrp6/Ctnnb1 Wnt-responsive neuronal axis, even though Lrp6 and Ctnnb1 perturbations produced clear thalamic transcriptional signatures.
The ANTXR paralog Antxr1 was also flat in all 23 neuronal groups and had a near-zero full-surface correlation with Antxr2.
Full-transcriptome data-driven neighbors were mathematically closest but biologically nonconvergent; Kcnq3 and Fbxo11 failed to reproduce the CA3 Mga hit.
Aopep loss of function was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null after P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation.
The AOPEP M1-peptidase lesion did not induce a detectable secondary proteostasis, ISR/UPR, autophagy, redox, or synaptic RNA program.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Aopep were essentially zero-correlation signatures rather than a coherent convergent module.
AOPEP-associated dystonia genes did not form a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic class with Aopep.
AOPEP enzymatic target engagement is unlikely to be monitored by an acute neuronal RNA signature alone.
Ap1b1 loss produced a single FDR-level downstream response, Napa down-regulation, restricted to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Ap1b1 is transcriptionally buffered across postnatal neuronal nuclei, including two groups with significant self-transcript depletion but no downstream FDR signal.
The same-complex Ap1s2 perturbation and AP-family comparators did not phenocopy Ap1b1.
Cltc generated a broad coated-vesicle secondary response in cell groups where Ap1b1 was largely flat.
direction_pattern: Cltc broad mixed response versus Ap1b1 nearly flat

canonical_summary: Whole-surface nearest-neighbor analysis did not identify a robust Ap1b1 convergent or anti-convergent perturbation.
Ap1s2 loss elicited a single robust response: Btbd8/APache up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Ap1s2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic neurons: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
Measurable AP-family comparators did not phenocopy the Ap1s2-Btbd8 response.
Btbd8 induction in 191 MB P MY GABA was the strongest and only robust Btbd8 event among 1750 perturbations in that group.
Cltc, but not Ap1s2, produced a Ddit3-containing stress/trafficking signature in the Ap1s2 responder group.

Ap3b1 loss was pan-transcriptionally buffered across the recovered NeuN+ neuronal atlas: every one of 18 measured groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the smallest downstream FDR in the whole surface was 0.428.

Ap3b1 did not phenocopy late endosome/lysosome-fusion perturbations: Rab7, Becn1, Vps41 and Atp6v1a all had nonzero FDR<0.10 surfaces in Ap3b1-matched cell groups, whereas Ap3b1 had none and a pre-specified Lamp/Cts/Dpp7/Mcoln1/Atp6 panel was completely absent.
Other AP-3/BLOC- or synaptic-vesicle-adjacent perturbations were also silent in the Ap3b1-matched neuronal groups: Dtnbp1 and Slc32a1 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The genome-wide Ap3b1 signature had no biologically meaningful positive or negative neighbor; the largest score-vector cosine was only 0.0328 and safe-target controls were intermingled with the nearest neighbors.
Acute P16 Ap4s1 CRISPR produced no downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
Canonical AP-4 cargo and autophagy transcripts did not change detectably after Ap4s1 perturbation.
The unbiased Ap4s1 signature neighbors were near-zero correlations and did not define a robust convergent module.
Represented AP-family, autophagy and AP-4-cargo-adjacent perturbations failed to phenocopy Ap4s1.
ATG9A relocalization is a better AP4S1 functional biomarker than an acute neuronal mRNA signature in this context.
Ap4s1 did not trigger a UPR or integrated-stress-like nuclear response, even though such a program was recoverable under Hspa5 perturbation.
Acute Apbb2 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The literature-obvious APP/FE65L1 neighborhood also lacked a convergent active module: App was flat in all Apbb2-matched groups and Dab1, Fyn, Lrp2, Psen1, and Mapt were essentially flat.
The unbiased Apbb2 signature neighborhood was nearly featureless rather than pathway-like; the strongest full-coverage positive and negative cosines were only 0.027 and -0.016.
APBB2-directed perturbation should not be assumed to generate a neuronal transcriptional proxy for APP cleavage or Aβ output.
App loss produced a broad App self-transcript decrease but no FDR-supported downstream DEG in any recovered neuronal class.
Canonical APP-processing and AICD-responsive transcripts were uncoupled from App depletion.
Represented APP-processing enzyme perturbations Psen1 and Adam10 were transcriptionally flat and did not converge with App.
App loss did not induce Aplp1 or Aplp2 mRNA, arguing that any APP-family buffering here was constitutive rather than a detectable paralog bounce-back.
An unbiased centered search found no meaningful App co-signature or anti-signature in the 1,773-target universe.
Appl1 single-gene loss of function generated a pan-measured neuronal null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 20 recovered cell groups.
Appl1's data-driven signature neighbors were silent targets, not pathway effectors.
Appl1 loss uncoupled from Netrin/Trk/NMDAR and PI3K-Akt-mTOR comparator perturbations in the same cell groups.
The activity-induced APPL1 chromatin gene panel was absent after basal Appl1 CRISPR.
Ar loss of function was FDR-null in every measured neuronal cell group: 22 groups had Ar rows, 35-179 perturbed nuclei each, and 0 non-Ar genes at FDR<0.10.

The Ar null was not a generic failure to detect nuclear-receptor perturbations: Rora and Nr1d1 had large corrected signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas steroid-receptor relatives and p160 coactivators were flat or singleton-level in Ar-matched groups.

Full-surface, data-driven Ar neighbors were numerically but not biologically close: the best non-safe positive score-vector correlation was Gfi1b at r=0.0288 and the strongest broadly measured negative was Dst at r=-0.0108.

Sparse Ar loss of function did not induce a proteotoxic or neurodegenerative transcriptional program in young sampled brain neurons, consistent with the main AR neurodegenerative disease, SBMA, being a polyglutamine expansion gain-of-function rather than a simple AR-null state.
Arhgap18 perturbation produced a single BH-supported downstream event: Myo6 up-regulation in the 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut class.
The postnatal neuronal Arhgap18 response is almost completely buffered: 1 downstream DEG across 22 recovered cell groups.
Arhgap18 has no strong empirical signature neighbor in the parquet.
Measured Rho-family and actin-motor relatives do not phenocopy Arhgap18.
The schizophrenia-linked ARHGAP18 locus is not recapitulated by broad acute Arhgap18 loss-of-function transcription in juvenile mouse neurons.
Arhgap32 loss did not produce a robust nuclear transcriptomic phenotype in any recovered neuronal class.
Arhgap32 did not phenocopy NMDAR, postsynaptic-density, beta-catenin, GABA_A receptor, Rho-GTPase, or dynein/dynactin perturbations that were directly represented in the same parquet.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Arhgap32 convergence or opposition.
The juvenile mosaic LoF result refines ARHGAP32 ASD/Jacobsen biology toward a synaptic-transport phenotype without a large cell-autonomous stress or receptor-subunit mRNA signature.

Arhgef9 is a pan-measured downstream-null perturbation: all 20 recovered neuronal groups had 0 non-Arhgef9 genes at FDR<0.10, even though the Arhgef9 transcript itself was significantly lower in L5 ET, CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, and midbrain glutamatergic nuclei.

Neither unbiased nor canonical comparators defined an Arhgef9-like module: the top non-safe neighbor was only Kcnb1 at score-cosine 0.0353, Gphn/Cdc42/Nlgn3/Gabra2/Mtor had score cosines between 0.006 and 0.021 to Arhgef9, and Arhgef9 supplied no FDR-significant downstream genes for shared-direction overlap.

GABAA-receptor and ion-channel perturbations could induce sparse activity-linked nuclear genes in this same analysis universe, whereas Arhgef9 did not: Kcnb1 and Gabrg2 up-regulated Bdnf/Vgf-like genes in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut or 155 MB Glut, and Gabrb2 up-regulated Nr4a1, Vgf, Npas4, and Fos in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The proposed collybistin-mTORC1 connection was not recovered as an Arhgef9 RNA module: no Arhgef9 group contained a downstream DEG, and Mtor itself produced only six matched-group FDR<0.10 genes with negligible similarity to Arhgef9.
Acute Arid1a loss produced a genome-wide response in only one of 23 measured neuronal groups, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 response is a mixed neuronal signaling and synaptic-scaffold signature, with Kcnq2, Begain, Lrrc7, L1cam, Prkcb, Ptprz1, and Lef1 down and Clstn2, Mpp2, Nexn, and Slc25a23 up.

The strongest Arid1a neighbors were mSWI/SNF core-related perturbations Smarcc2 and Smarce1, which converged in the same 151 cell group and in the same direction on Ptpn3, Begain, Lrrc7/Rasa4/Prkcb, and related genes.
Arid1b and several literature-obvious mSWI/SNF relatives did not broadly phenocopy Arid1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Postmitotic Arid1a loss did not recover the ARID1A-mutant cancer programs most associated with Wnt/AP-1, MET–PI3K, cell-cycle, UPR/stress, or EZH2 synthetic lethality.
Acute P16 Arid1b loss is transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons: only one non-self gene reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The only robust downstream response was Kbtbd8 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Represented mSWI/SNF relatives did not phenocopy Arid1b: Arid1a, Arid2, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 produced larger 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signatures, whereas Smarca4 and Bicra were flat.
Full-surface data-driven signature scanning found no meaningful positive or negative Arid1b neighbor.
Arid2 produced a robust 118-gene FDR<0.10 response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 20 measured groups were null, 155 MB Glut was only subthreshold, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
The Arid2 response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contains a mostly up-regulated cell-adhesion, axon-guidance, and extracellular cue module.
Arid2 loss shifted a mixed synaptic and excitability signature, with Kcnj9, Gabbr2, Grm5, Dagla, and Syt11 up but Prkcd, Gria2, and Kcnk4 down.
Extracellular-matrix glycosylation and proteoglycan genes were significantly remodeled in the Arid2 thalamic response.
The same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature included cytoskeletal and trafficking genes such as Flnb, Flna, Kifc2, Coro6, Trim67, Ctnnd1, Cdc42se2, and Actr3b.
The represented PBAF/core target Smarcc2 and, more weakly, Smarce1 converged with Arid2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Smarca4, Smarca2, Smarcc1, and Smarcd1 did not.

Alternative ARID and queried Bcl11 targets did not phenocopy Arid2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Arid1a had only two Arid2-overlapping genes with one opposite, Arid1b had one DE gene, and Bcl11a/Bcl11b were flat.
Data-driven signature neighbors placed Arid2 closest to broad Elp1, Tnpo3, Rab7, and Smarcc2 signatures and opposite to Yy1, Sin3a, and Psmb4 on the 118-gene Arid2 vector.
Arid2 did not significantly induce a canonical ISR, UPR, proteasome, or lysosome rebound in its responding thalamic group.

Arih1 loss produced a sparse, posteriorly biased transcriptional response: 3 of 22 measured neuronal groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried 12 of the 14 downstream hits, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA carried one each, and 215 MB Dopa was missing rather than null.

The only multi-gene Arih1 responder, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, combined increased ER/endolysosomal membrane genes Reep2, Tmem59, Rnf103, Acp2 and Serinc1 with reduced Ogt, Grid2ip, Tmem132a, Cit, and Snhg11.
MB Glut and MB P MY GABA were real but single-gene responders: Hnrnpc was up in 155 MB Glut and Trim23 was down in 191 MB P MY GABA, with no recurrent multi-gene Arih1 program.

The strongest data-driven overlaps with the Arih1 signature were Tpr, Uba5, and Tnpo3, not Ariadne-family ligases: Tpr had six same-direction and two opposite FDR-overlapping Arih1 features, Uba5 and Tnpo3 each had five same-direction overlaps, while Rnpc3, Sin3a, and Wac were the leading opposite-direction neighbors.

Arih1 partially intersected UFMylation, proteasome, and endolysosomal perturbations in the same 151 thalamic cells, sharing the down-regulation of Ogt/Snhg11/Grid2ip-like features but reversing the Reep2-, Tmem59-, and Rnf103-positive arm seen after Arih1 loss.

Represented E3-ligase-family comparators did not phenocopy Arih1: Rnf216, Trim2, and Trim37 had zero FDR<0.10 overlap with the 14 Arih1 signature features in 151/155/191 even when their own guide pools were recovered.
Arih1 LoF did not induce or repress canonical type-I-interferon/cGAS, 4EHP translation-arrest, or ISR/UPR marker transcripts anywhere in the measured surface.
Arl2bp perturbation was a pan-measured-neuron transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The represented ARL3/ciliopathy comparator set did not phenocopy Arl2bp; the direct biochemical partner Arl3 was itself downstream-null in all 23 groups.

The phenotype-first score-neighbor search found only near-zero Arl2bp correlations, with top non-safe positive neighbors Rax, Tcf4 and Msx2 and top negative neighbors Fbxo11, Atp6v1e1 and Kif2a all at |r|<0.036.
Acute Arl3 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups; the only FDR-significant event was the Arl3 transcript itself in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The genome-wide Arl3 Wilcoxon-score vector had no meaningful data-driven neighbors: the largest positive and negative Pearson correlations to other targets were only 0.028 and -0.026, and biological targets were all closer to zero.

Ciliopathy comparators represented in the parquet—Arl2bp, IFT components, BBSome components, Cep290, Rpgr/Rpgrip1l, Dync2h1, Cplane1, Ttc8, Ttc21b, and B9d1—did not phenocopy Arl3 in the postnatal neuronal snRNA readout.
Armc9 loss did not produce any robust downstream nuclear transcriptomic response in the recovered postmitotic neuronal survey.
The Shh/GLI transcriptional program expected in ciliated proliferative progenitors was absent after Armc9 perturbation in P37-P44 NeuN+ neurons.

Represented ciliopathy-pathway relatives did not phenocopy Armc9 as a shared neuronal RNA module; B9d1 was the only ciliary/Joubert comparator with a multi-gene response, and it was confined to 308 CB GABA.
The unbiased Armc9 signature-neighbor search found only tiny residual correlations, so no hidden non-ciliary convergence module was recovered.
Arnt loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null across all 22 recovered cell groups.
Canonical AHR and HIF target programs were not recovered after Arnt perturbation, and directly measured Ahr, Hif1a, Ahrr, and Npas3 perturbations were also flat.
Bmal1 and Clock, unlike Arnt, generated the expected circadian target-gene signature in matched neuronal groups.
The Arnt score vector had no strong positive or negative signature neighbors in the complete perturbation universe.
The P16 neuronal Arnt null does not reproduce the embryonic placental ARNT requirement or the ARNT2-SIM1 hypothalamic-development phenotypes.

P16 Arx loss produced a sparse but real inhibitory-neuron response: all 10 downstream FDR<0.10 genes occurred in CTX-CGE, Pvalb and CNU-HYa/HY GABA groups, with no robust calls in any measured glutamatergic group.

The Pvalb Arx response was a small mature-state signature, not a wholesale loss of GABAergic identity: Tle2 and Tgfbr2 decreased, Atp2b3, Dip2a, Fam20c and Cck increased, while Dlx1/2/5/6, Gad1/2, Lhx6, Nkx2-1, Pvalb and Sst stayed at FDR 1.00.
Tmsb4x was the strongest CTX-CGE GABA hit after Arx perturbation, increasing 0.82 logFC at FDR 1.07e-4, with only Nrip3 also passing FDR<0.10 in the same group.

The literature-neighbor perturbations that were measurable did not phenocopy Arx: Dlx6 had no FDR<0.10 genes anywhere, Nkx2-1 had only Med13 in Pvalb neurons, and neither generated the 10-gene Arx signature at FDR<0.10.

The strongest data-driven Arx neighbors were computed from the 10 robust feature triples but did not reveal a robust shared module: Depdc5, Il10ra and Tbx22 were the top positive restricted-signature neighbors, Ctnnbl1, Usp48 and Chd4 were the top negative neighbors, and matched-cell FDR overlap was absent.

The screen argues against treating juvenile mature-neuron Arx LoF as a transcriptomic surrogate for ARX developmental disease: a P16 mosaic perturbation left most mature neuronal groups flat and retained only a small GABA-cell signal.
Asah1 loss was buffered at the snRNA-seq level in every recovered neuronal class: 21 measured cell groups all had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Asah1 did not converge with represented sphingolipid or lysosomal relatives: Psap and Sphk1 were fully downstream-null, while Sptlc2, Scarb2, and Lamp2 produced only isolated single-gene hits.
The strongest data-driven Asah1 score-vector neighbors were extremely weak and resolved to other null perturbations rather than a hidden disease module.

Acute Ascc3 loss produced a real but sharply restricted neuronal transcriptomic effect: 268 FDR<0.10 group-gene rows were confined to 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA; 15 other measured groups stayed weak.
All Ascc3 responder classes shared a negative membrane-neuronal core headed by App, Atp1a3, Srrm2, Clstn1, Aplp2, Atp2a2, and Serinc1.

The largest Ascc3 responders extended the shared core into coordinated loss of lysosomal, secretory-granule, and synaptic-vesicle transcripts, most prominently in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.

The Ascc3 response had a limited adaptive up-arm, with Dnajb1, Manf, Slc38a2, and Npas4 induced in hypothalamic GABA and Chchd2, Selenok, Rer1, Ssr4, Stub1, Faf2, Dnajc5, and Dnaja1 induced in 155 MB Glut.

The Ascc3 neuronal signature uncoupled RQT loss from canonical ISR, interferon, p53/DNA-damage, and AP-1/NF-kappaB/SRF transcriptional programs: representative markers from all four programs had 0 FDR<0.10 rows.
Proteasome subunit perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1 were among the strongest Ascc3-positive neighbors and re-used roughly half of the Ascc3 significant vector in the same direction.
RNA-processing and nuclear-transport perturbations, especially Prpf6, U2af2, Tpr, and Matr3, were also top positive Ascc3 neighbors.
Represented collision/ISR/RQC-adjacent targets did not phenocopy Ascc3: Eif2ak4, Hbs1l, Rack1, and Vcp had almost no FDR-significant overlap in Ascc3 responder groups.
The top negative Ascc3 neighbors were only weak anticorrelations: Grid1, Ppargc1a, Ephb1, Bicra, and Chd2 did not create a robust opposite FDR-overlap signature.
Ash1l produced no adjusted downstream DEG in any of the 22 recovered P16-to-P37/44 neuronal groups despite a consistently negative self-transcript trend.
Known ASH1L-linked Eph, BDNF-TrkB, and synaptic marker genes were explicitly measured but did not recur as adjusted DE after Ash1l perturbation.
Kmt2a and Wdr48 were the top non-safe positive Ash1l score neighbors and Sin3a was the top anti-neighbor, but all correlations were tiny and Kmt2a/Sin3a had adjusted DE surfaces that Ash1l lacked.
The represented H3K36/PRC2-axis relatives Nsd1, Nsd2, Setd2, and Kdm6b were weak or null like Ash1l, whereas Setd1a and the data-driven anti-neighbor Sin3a gave broad chromatin-regulator DE surfaces.

Acute postmitotic Asxl3-directed CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic zero: all 22 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and all Asxl3 self-transcript FDR values were 1.0.

PR-DUB-related perturbations did not converge with Asxl3: Bap1 gave only 34 genes in three matched groups, Foxk2 was fully flat, Mbd5 had a single-gene hit, and Ogt gave a broad 2154-gene response yet remained uncorrelated with Asxl3.

Representative mRNAs reported in germline compound-Asxl3 mutant mouse cerebrum or cerebellum, including Plod3, Ezh2, Suv39h1, Socs3, Slc6a4, Fos and Dlg4, were absent from the acute Asxl3 DE surface across all 22 measured neuronal groups.
The top data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbors of Asxl3 were not biologically meaningful neighbors: the largest positive correlation was only r=0.0352 and the most negative was r=-0.0125.
Atad1 produced a single robust downstream hit, Smarcd1 up-regulation, only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The data-driven Smarcd1 convergence with Elp1, Gfpt1, and Uba5 was restricted and did not mean that Atad1 had entered their broad ISR/ER-stress state.
Direct AMPAR-pathway perturbations, Nsf and Gria1/Gria2/Gria3, did not phenocopy Atad1 transcriptionally.
Atad1 was not transcriptionally coupled to mitochondrial or peroxisomal protein-quality-control comparators.
Thorase-mTORC1 biochemistry did not appear as an mTORC1-like RNA signature after Atad1 CRISPR.
The Atad1 null surface argues against a large cell-autonomous ISR, UPR, autophagy, mitochondrial, or AMPAR-transcriptional response within 3-4 weeks of sparse postnatal neuronal loss of function.
Atcay produced a single FDR-level downstream response, Zfp382 up-regulation, restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; the remaining 22 measured groups had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Atcay loss did not transcriptionally regulate the mRNAs for glutaminase, kinesin-1 subunits, MEK1/2, ATP-citrate lyase, cholinergic transport components, or Dapk1 in any cell group.
Represented caytaxin pathway neighbors failed to phenocopy Atcay: Kif5a, Kif5c, and Klc2 were flat, while Gls, Klc1, and Map2k2 produced only isolated one-gene effects and no 066 Zfp382 induction.
