The strongest data-driven positive and negative Atcay neighbors were weak nominal-signature matches and did not validate as FDR-level matched-cell-type comparators.
Ogt was the only other target that raised Zfp382 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA at FDR<0.10, but the overlap was a single gene inside a broad 453-gene Ogt response.

The P16 Atcay surface supports an off-axis disease model: Cayman-ataxia phenotypes are more likely to arise from developmental and local presynaptic cargo/circuit defects than from a strong juvenile soma-transcriptional stress program.
Acute Atf6 loss of function produced a corrected-transcriptome null across every neuronal group in which it was recovered.
A matched Hspa5 perturbation, not Atf6, exposed a detectable ER quality-control module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The closest complete-surface neighbor of Atf6 was Uba5, but the relationship was numerical rather than phenotypic.
The brain-wide Atf6 null is consistent with ATF6 disease biology being displaced to cone photoreceptors rather than generic postnatal brain-neuron transcription.
Basal Atf6 inhibition is unlikely to be read out as a large neuron-wide ER transcriptome shift, but that should not be extrapolated to stressed tissue or chronic pharmacology.
Atg16l1 targeting produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
The Atg16l1 null excluded a detectable autophagy-lysosomal, UPR/ISR, or inflammasome mRNA aftershock.
Literature-obvious autophagy perturbations were sparse responders or flat, and none phenocopied Atg16l1.
Unbiased Atg16l1 neighbors nominated UFMylation genes only at vanishing correlation, and Uba5/Ufc1 strongly diverged from Atg16l1 by FDR.
Atg5 loss produced a two-gene, negative Calr/Rtn1 response confined to 155 MB Glut.
The assay did not recover a canonical autophagy, lysosome, p62, proteasome-rebound, or UPR-ISR transcript program after Atg5 perturbation.
Atg16l1, the measured same-complex partner of Atg5, did not phenocopy Atg5 in any matched cell group.
Becn1 and Rb1cc1 retained the Calr-down component of the Atg5 155 MB Glut response.
Tsc2 loss was strongly transcriptomic where Atg5 was nearly flat.
Proteasome perturbations exposed a broad protein-homeostasis and neuronal-downshift axis of which Atg5 captured only a tiny Calr/Rtn1 edge.
All-surface nearest-neighbor correlations for Atg5 were near zero.
Acute postnatal Atl1 CRISPR was a pan-measured transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a consistently negative Atl1 self-transcript.
Atl1 loss did not induce a UPR/ISR/ERAD, BMP, or ER-phagy/autophagy marker program, whereas Atp2a2 and Hspa5 perturbations in the same analysis universe produced clear ER-stress transcription.
The obvious ER-shaping/HSP comparators were also transcriptionally buffered or very small: Reep1 and Spast had zero downstream DE genes, Atl3 had one, and Vcp had six across their recovered groups.

Data-driven signature neighbors did not nominate a coherent Atl1 molecular module; the strongest real positive neighbor was only r=0.0346 in Wilcoxon-score space and the strongest real negative neighbor was r=-0.0210.
The dataset argues that postmitotic CRISPR loss of Atl1 is a poor transcriptional phenocopy of SPG3A disease alleles.
Atl3 loss produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event, Kif21b downregulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Atl3 perturbation did not induce a sustained ER-phagy, autophagy, UPR, or ISR transcriptional module in any measured cell group.
Atl1, Spast, and Reep1 failed to phenocopy Atl3 in the 15 matched central-neuron groups, and Atl2 was not available for direct testing.
Unbiased cross-target correlations did not place Atl3 in a robust recurrent transcriptomic module.
Postnatal central-neuron Atl3 LoF did not reproduce transcriptomic correlates of ATL3 hereditary sensory neuropathy models.
Atoh1 was a uniform transcriptomic non-responder in every recovered postnatal NeuN+ neuronal group: 0 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in 22 of 22 measured groups.

The postnatal Atoh1 null surface did not move the canonical Barhl1/Barhl2, Notch/Hes/Dll, SHH/Gli, Pax6, Neurod1, Gfi1 or Zic readouts, and related bHLH/E-protein/Notch/SHH perturbations did not expose a shared Atoh1-like signature.

A whole-universe signature-neighbor search nominated only near-zero Atoh1 neighbors; the best positive cosine was Wdr26 at 0.03970 and the best negative non-control cosine was Fbxo11 at -0.05001, and neither phenocopied Atoh1 after their DE surfaces were inspected.
Atp11c loss of function produced no corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 20 measured neuronal cell groups.
Represented P4-family targets Atp8a2 and Atp9a also failed to reveal a broad postnatal neuronal P4-flippase stress module.
Atp11c had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor across the full model-visible perturbation universe.
The neuronal null separates ATP11C's RBC, B-cell, and hepatobiliary LoF biology from acute healthy-brain transcriptional liability.

Atp13a2 perturbation produced no corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups, despite directionally negative self-transcript logFC in all groups and FDR<0.10 self-decrease in 7 groups.
The expected TFEB/SYT11, lysosomal, autophagy, proteostasis, UPR/ISR, alpha-synuclein-clearance, and redox marker panel was completely absent from the Atp13a2 FDR surface.
The full perturbation universe nominated no meaningful positive or inverse Atp13a2 signature neighbor; the strongest score correlations were Nrxn2 r=0.0328 and Npy1r r=-0.0282.
P5B, autophagy, lysosomal, and Parkinson-linked comparators did not converge with Atp13a2; the direct paralog Atp13a3 had 0 downstream FDR genes in 22 groups and r=0.0095 to Atp13a2.

Vps35 and Mef2c generated corrected DE in matched groups where Atp13a2 was flat, including 30 Vps35 downstream FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut versus 0 for Atp13a2 with more Atp13a2-perturbed cells.
Atp13a3 produced a screen-wide neuronal transcriptional null: every measured cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite Atp13a3 itself being in the tested gene universe.

The obvious ATP13/polyamine relatives that were testable did not uncover a hidden Atp13a3-like neuronal program. Atp13a2 was completely null, while Eif5a and Sms produced only isolated singleton hits.

Atp13a3 did not align with the PAH/BMP-SMAD disease neighborhood in postmitotic brain neurons: perturbations of Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Acvrl1, Eng, Sox17, Eif2ak4, Kdr, Tbx4, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, and Smad genes were null or singleton-only.
An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no robust Atp13a3 module: the top positive and negative whole-universe Wilcoxon-score correlations ranged only from r=0.037 to r=-0.018.

Sparse juvenile Atp1a1 loss produced an almost completely buffered downstream transcriptome: 22 recovered neuronal groups, all with negative Atp1a1 self logFC, but only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes total.
direction_pattern: Atp1a1 down; two isolated up-regulated downstream genes

canonical_summary: Atp1a1 perturbation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut selectively up-regulated the neuronal α3 paralog Atp1a3.
Atp1a1 perturbation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut produced a single Snx32 up-regulation signal.
The represented Na/K-ATPase α paralogs did not phenocopy Atp1a1: Atp1a2 was nearly flat in neuronal nuclei and Atp1a3 drove a distinct 107-gene thalamic response where Atp1a1 was null.
The top model-visible whole-surface neighbors of Atp1a1, Zic1 and Retreg1, were weak and non-overlapping with Atp1a1 responder groups.
direction_pattern: weak positive for Zic1, weak negative for Retreg1

canonical_summary: The mostly blank Atp1a1 CRISPR-LoF mRNA surface does not derisk human ATP1A1 missense disease mechanisms or pharmacologic Na/K-ATPase inhibition.
Atp1a2 is buffered across postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal groups: only 1 of 22 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the self-transcript never passed FDR.
The only accepted Atp1a2 responder was Ubr1 upregulation in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Atp1a2 shares the 191 MB P MY GABA Ubr1 node with proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1 but not their broad stress/synaptic-collapse signatures.
Atp1a2 does not phenocopy its Na,K-ATPase alpha paralogs or the astrocytic glutamate-transporter comparator in this neuron-enriched screen.
Familial-hemiplegic-migraine channel comparators Cacna1a and Scn1a were also nearly flat at the downstream snRNA-seq level.

The pre-literature full-score signature neighbors of Atp1a2 were Bcl2, Nr2e1, Cnnm2, Unc13b, Cfap69, and Eef2, but all correlations were near zero and the top candidates did not reproduce the 191 MB P MY GABA Ubr1 response.

Atp1a3 CRISPR produced a 107-gene transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while the other five responding cell groups carried only one FDR<0.10 gene each and 17 measured groups had no robust downstream genes.
The thalamic Atp1a3 response selectively lowered Atp2a2/SERCA2 and Atp2b1/PMCA1 mRNAs without inducing Atp1a1, Atp1a2, Atp1b1-3, Fxyd6, or Fxyd7 compensation.

Ion-channel and synaptic signaling genes were remodeled in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Grin2a and Slc17a6 increased, whereas Kcnj3, Kcnj9, Kcna4, Kcnk9, Cacna1d, Slc1a1, Prkcg, and Rgs16 decreased and Ptpn5 increased.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-regulated Ache, Pcsk1n, Vgf, Ptprn, Scg2, Resp18, and Sv2b while down-regulating Cck.
Atp1a3 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coupled Notum induction to Lef1, Ctnnd1, Ptprj, L1cam, and Dscam repression, placing a Wnt/adhesion axis inside the ion-pump phenotype.
Mtmr11 and Pi4ka increased while Lpcat4, Fads6, Sec62, Tlcd4, and Sh3bp4 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Srxn1 was one of the strongest up-regulated genes in the 151 response, accompanied by Prkab2 and Slc41a3 up-regulation and Ttc19 down-regulation.
The data-driven positive neighbors of Atp1a3 were not Na/K-ATPase paralogs: Psmb4, Ctnnb1, and Cic shared 47, 41, and 40 robust Atp1a3-signature genes, mostly in the same direction.
The expected ER-stress/UPR module was absent from Atp1a3 despite being readily inducible by direct Atp2a2/SERCA2 perturbation in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.

Five non-151 responder groups each had only a singleton FDR<0.10 hit: Psma3 down in CA3 CA2-FC DG, Camsap2 up in CTX-CGE GABA, Clgn up in CNU-MGE GABA, Sgcb down in MH-LH TH Glut, and R3hdm2 up in MB Glut.

Literature-obvious ion and disease-family targets did not reproduce Atp1a3: Atp1a1 and Atp1a2 had zero robust Atp1a3-locus overlaps, Grin2a moved oppositely at its own transcript, Scn1a/Scn2a/Scn8a/Cacna1a were flat in 151, whereas Grin1 was only partially convergent.

The negative data-driven side was much weaker than the positive side: Qrich1 was the only top negative neighbor with robust Atp1a3-locus overlaps, and all five were opposite in sign, whereas Stard7, Kcna1, Rasa2, and Trpm7 had zero FDR<0.10 overlaps at the 112 Atp1a3 features.

Atp2a2 produced a highly cell-type-restricted transcriptomic phenotype: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut dominated with 284 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, while the next largest responses had 12, 7, 2, or 1 downstream genes and 14 measured groups had none.
direction_pattern: cell_type_restricted; strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

canonical_summary: The expected ER-stress/UPR program was recovered where the phenotype was broad: Hspa5 and Creld2 were induced in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Asns, and Cars were induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Chac1/Ddit3 reappearing in 155 MB Glut and Chac1 in 191 MB P MY GABA.

The 151 response coupled CHOP/UPR to an ATF4-like metabolic salvage module, inducing amino-acid transporters and serine/one-carbon genes including Slc38a1, Slc38a2, Slc1a4, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Mthfd2, Psph, Aldh1l2, Trib3, Atf4, and Sesn2; part of this program, including Aldh1l2 and Slc3a2, was also present in 155 MB Glut.

Stress induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coincided with neuronal-state remodeling: Fos, Npas4, Bdnf, Crem, Dusp1, and Vgf increased, whereas Slc17a7, Gabrd, Adam11, Ptprn2, Grm1, Grm7, Gabbr1, Gabra1, Grin2d, Kcnc2, and Cacna1g decreased; Slc17a7 alone was also down in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and Scn1a was down in 191 MB P MY GABA.

Proteostasis perturbations were the strongest data-driven Atp2a2 neighbors: Psmb4 and Psmc1 ranked first and third by global signed-score correlation and shared large same-direction subsets of the Atp2a2 FDR signature, including 110 Psmb4-overlap genes and 67 Psmc1-overlap genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Gfpt1 and Dhdds, two ER glycosylation-supply perturbations, ranked just behind the proteasome hits and converged almost perfectly in direction with the 151 Atp2a2 significant genes that they shared: 129/129 same-direction for Gfpt1 and 72/72 same-direction for Dhdds.

The literature-obvious calcium/UPR comparators did not reproduce the Atp2a2 program: Atf6, Itpr1, Ryr3, Atp2b2, and Atp2c1 had zero downstream FDR genes, Ryr2 and Atp2b3 had one each across their entire surfaces, and Atp2b1 gave a small 151 signature without CHOP/HSPA5/XBP1 induction.

Two low-cell-count responder groups showed isolated metabolic or organelle-contact markers rather than a full UPR: Acadsb was the only downstream gene in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Miga2 was the only downstream gene in 308 CB GABA.

Neuronal Atp2a2 loss of function refined the Darier/brain SERCA2 literature by separating a penetrant ER-stress transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut from widespread flat neuronal surfaces.
Atp2b1 loss produced a robust downstream transcriptome only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 26 genes at FDR<0.10, while 21 other recovered cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The TH Prkcd/Grin2c Atp2b1 signature was dominated by up-regulated activity/neuropeptide genes and a smaller Ca2+/synaptic-remodeling component.
Atp2b1 and Atp2a2 converged on a 9-gene TH activity module, but only Atp2a2 induced the ER-stress/UPR genes Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, Asns, and Chac1.
The TH Atp2b1 phenotype did not generalize to the measured PMCA paralogs Atp2b2 and Atp2b3, both of which had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes despite significant self-transcript depletion.
Gabrb2 loss converged with Atp2b1 on the TH Fos/Nr4a1/Vgf/Opn3 module, whereas Grin1 and the data-driven anti-neighbor Tardbp drove overlapping neuropeptide/activity genes in the opposite direction.

Several high-scoring restricted neighbors or literature-obvious relatives were rejected by FDR overlap: Adarb1, Stxbp1, Eif2ak4, Cacna1a, Prkaca, Ndufa12, calmodulin targets, CaMKII targets, and Grin2a/Grin2b did not robustly phenocopy Atp2b1 in 151.
Atp2b2 perturbation produced a broad on-target transcript scar but no adjusted downstream single-nucleus RNA response in any recovered neuronal group.
The cerebellar GABA group did not reproduce the expected PMCA2-null Purkinje mGluR1-Homer-IP3R1/AMPAR/VGCC/nNOS program at the RNA level.

Atp2b2 did not phenocopy other assayed calcium-pump perturbations: SERCA2/Atp2a2 activated a strong ER-stress ISR/UPR state and Atp2b1 produced a small thalamic Fos/Nr4a1/Vgf response, but Atp2b2 and Atp2c1 were downstream-flat.
Full-transcriptome signature-neighbor analysis found no anti-correlated Atp2b2 counterpart and no robust convergent FDR gene set.
Represented glutamate-receptor and calcium-signaling components of PMCA2-associated synapses were mostly downstream-flat as perturbations themselves.
A flat P16 brain snRNA profile should not be used as negative evidence against ATP2B2 as a disease gene or calcium-pump therapeutic target.
Atp2b3 had a one-gene downstream response in 191 MB P MY GABA, where Svop was up-regulated while the assayed Atp2b3 transcript was down.
Atp2b3 perturbation did not activate a sustained calcium/activity/ER-stress transcriptional program in any measured cell group.
direction_pattern: expected calcium and ER-stress RNA programs absent after Atp2b3

canonical_summary: The represented PMCA paralogs did not phenocopy one another: Atp2b1 produced a thalamic downstream response, whereas Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 were target-only or nearly target-only across the 22 matched groups.
direction_pattern: Atp2b1 responsive; Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 buffered

canonical_summary: Atp2a2/SERCA2, not Atp2b3/PMCA3, was the calcium pump whose loss triggered UPR/ISR RNA in matched postmitotic neurons.
direction_pattern: ER stress genes up after Atp2a2; absent after Atp2b3

canonical_summary: The data-driven Atp2b3 signature-neighbor search produced only tiny residual correlations and no Svop-sharing neighbor.
Postnatal Atp2c1 loss did not elicit a detectable downstream transcriptional signature in recovered neurons.
The only clearly responsive Ca2+-ATPase family member in the matched neuronal surface was Atp2a2/SERCA2, not Atp2c1/SPCA1.
Keratinocyte SPCA1-TMEM165 and SPCA1-NOTCH1 mechanisms were not redeployed as neuronal transcriptional modules.
Full-vector neighbors of the Atp2c1 signature did not identify a robust convergent biology.
Atp6ap2 loss produced a nearly silent survivor transcriptome in postmitotic juvenile neurons.
The only recurrent robust downstream response was Atp6v0a1 mRNA down-regulation in two glutamatergic thalamic/midbrain groups.
Atp6ap2 did not activate a canonical lysosomal-autophagy or unfolded-protein stress transcriptome; the only ER chaperone hit, Hyou1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, decreased.
Core V-ATPase perturbations failed to phenocopy Atp6ap2 in the matched effect groups.
Rab7 perturbation drove an opposite V-ATPase/lysosome compensation program in the same broad regions where Atp6ap2 changed only Atp6v0a1.
Atp6ap2 uncoupled from the Wnt/β-catenin module that Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 perturbations still exposed in thalamic neurons.
The Atp6ap2 profile did not converge with canonical angiotensin receptor perturbations.
The data-driven Atp6ap2 neighbors were weak and noncanonical, centered on the two Atp6v0a1 coordinates rather than on the whole transcriptome.
Atp6v0a1 perturbation was self-detected in eight cell groups but produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
Atp6v0a1 loss did not activate the expected TFEB/CLEAR, lysosomal, autophagy, ISR/UPR, or proteasome transcripts.
Represented V-ATPase relatives and lysosomal disease comparators also failed to generate a robust neuronal snRNA signature.
The weak full-surface neighbors of Atp6v0a1 were statistical rather than biological neighbors.
The ATP6V0A1 disease prior is refined toward developmental, missense, and direct physiology mechanisms rather than a generic postmitotic loss-of-function transcriptional state.

Acute juvenile Atp6v1a perturbation produced only four downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell hits across 20 recovered neuronal groups, with several groups showing target RNA reduction but no downstream response.
Ddit3 was the only canonical ISR/UPR sentinel recovered at FDR<0.10 and was confined to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The Atp6v1a score vector was closest to proteostasis perturbations, with Psmb4 and Psmc1 ranking first and second among 1765 other targets and sharing same-direction Ddit3 or Golga4 hits.
V-ATPase subunits and regulators did not recapitulate the four Atp6v1a downstream genes in matched cell groups.
Golga4 was specifically up-regulated after Atp6v1a perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Lta4h was the strongest Atp6v1a downstream hit, up 1.174 logFC at FDR 0.000869 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Chd2 was up-regulated in 191 MB P MY GABA after Atp6v1a perturbation.

Atp6v1e1 loss produced a strongly buffered transcriptional surface: only 10 downstream FDR<0.10 genes appeared across 20 measured neuronal groups, and none belonged to a coordinated TFEB, autophagy, lysosomal cathepsin, UPR, or ISR module.
The only multi-gene Atp6v1e1 response was in 308 CB GABA, where Cacnb4, Tnik, Jmjd1c, Stmn4, Strip2 and Akain1 were up-regulated while Gpr162 and Pde4a were down-regulated.
The non-cerebellar significant Atp6v1e1 signal was limited to one down-regulated gene in each responding CNU-HYa group: Chp1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Snrpn in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.

The best data-driven convergence was not the V-ATPase family: Ranbp2 was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative neighbor across the three Atp6v1e1 responder groups, with the statistically supported same and opposite overlaps concentrated in 308 CB GABA.

Literature-obvious V-ATPase comparators did not phenocopy Atp6v1e1: Atp6v0a1 was completely flat downstream, Atp6v1a and Atp6ap2 produced only sparse singleton responses, and Atp6v1b2 produced a Pvalb-restricted signature absent from Atp6v1e1.
Atp6v1e1 LoF in postmitotic neurons is a poor transcriptional proxy for pan-V-ATPase inhibition: neither Atp6v1e1 nor the tested V-ATPase relatives produced a common lysosomal-collapse signature.
Atp8a2 produced its only robust downstream DE in 308 CB GABA, where Cnot7 and Ddx10 were both up-regulated at FDR 0.0724.
Canonical Atp8a2 stress, axon-injury, apoptosis, and P4-family compensation were absent from all 23 acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomes.
The P4-family targets represented in the parquet, Atp9a and Atp11c, did not converge with the Atp8a2 CB-GABA signature.
Atp8a2 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbors in the model-visible perturbation universe.

Atp9a loss was broadly buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level, with only Rnf41 up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Sc5d down in 053 Sst Gaba reaching downstream FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups.
The CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic response was limited to up-regulation of the ubiquitin-ligase gene Rnf41.
Sst interneurons showed a single lipid-metabolic response, down-regulating Sc5d after Atp9a perturbation.
Atp9a depletion did not transcriptionally regulate recovered Atp9b, Rab5/Rab11, transferrin/GLUT1 cargo, Wntless, USP8, or retromer-core transcripts.
The literature-obvious Vps35 retromer and Atp8a2 P4-ATPase comparators did not phenocopy Atp9a in either Atp9a responder group.
Unbiased whole-score neighbors of Atp9a were extremely weak, with top cosine values between -0.026 and 0.034 after excluding Safe_target controls.
Sparse postnatal Atr loss was transcriptionally buffered across every measured neuronal group.
Atr perturbation did not induce the p53, apoptosis, UPR/ISR, or autophagy transcripts predicted for a replicating-cell ATR catastrophe.
The neuronal null is compatible with an ATR role that is postmitotic but presynaptic and largely non-transcriptional.
Neither unbiased signature search nor DDR/PIKK-family comparators produced an Atr-like module.
Atrn perturbation produced a single robust downstream event: Cnnm2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
Atrn self-transcript depletion could be detected without downstream propagation.
The acute Atrn surface did not recover an MGRN1/TSG101-like endolysosomal or autophagy stress signature.
The Atrn screen did not expose a melanocortin/Agrp transcriptional module.
Atrn had no strong empirical signature neighbor in the model-visible universe.
Cnnm2 up-regulation after Atrn did not behave like a reciprocal Cnnm2-loss module in cerebellar GABA cells.
Atrx generated FDR<0.10 downstream genes in only 3 of 18 measured cell groups, led by a 9-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature.
Csf2ra was the only recurrent robust downstream gene, down in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
The main 151 TH response included down-regulation of membrane-lipid and surface-processing genes Cyp46a1, Pnpla6 and Pigk.
Atrx up-regulated a small structural arm: Begain, Ablim1 and Pxdn in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Limd2 alone in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
Chd4 was the #1 positive data-driven neighbor of Atrx and shared Begain up-regulation and Cyp46a1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Sin3a was the #1 negative Atrx neighbor and significantly reversed Begain, Cyp46a1, Pnpla6 and Resp18 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Literature-obvious H3.3/heterochromatin and MeCP2 comparators did not phenocopy Atrx: H3f3a was flat, while Setdb1 and Mecp2 shared 0 Atrx FDR genes.
Atrx did not induce a p53/DNA-damage apoptotic program in any measured cell group.
Atxn10 loss produced a restricted postnatal neuronal response: 7 of 22 recovered groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with 052 Pvalb Gaba dominating.
052 Pvalb Gaba mounted the main adaptive Atxn10 program, coupling ISR/amino-acid response genes with regulated-secretory/neuropeptide up-regulation.
Atp1a3 was the most recurrent same-direction downstream marker of Atxn10 perturbation, falling in four responder classes.
A cytoskeletal/tubulin component was present from the thinnest cortical effect to the Pvalb, thalamic, and midbrain signatures.
Eef2, Psmb4 and U2af2, not ATXN10 textbook relatives, were among the closest empirical Atxn10 neighbors.
Ogt, a literature ATXN10 interactor, only partially overlapped Atxn10 and had a different cell-type footprint.
Atxn1, Atxn2 and Atxn7 did not phenocopy Atxn10 despite sharing spinocerebellar-ataxia naming.
The 308 CB GABA null and global absence of caspase/hnRNP K/PKCdelta markers argue that coding Atxn10 CRISPR loss did not recapitulate SCA10 repeat-RNA toxicity.
The 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut response was a small up, not down, immediate-early/MAPK-feedback signature.

Acute Atxn1 loss-of-function produced a dominant thalamic response: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 256 FDR<0.10 downstream genes, whereas only 2 and 4 genes were detected in the two cortical IT responders and 20 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 genes.
Cic was the strongest positive full-profile neighbor of Atxn1 and sharply converged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 177 of 256 Atxn1 FDR genes were also significant under Cic with the same direction.

The recovered CIC-like module was selective rather than a blanket canonical Etv program: Bace1 and Dusp4 were induced in 151 TH, but Etv4, Etv5, Dusp6 and Ccnd1 were measured and were not FDR-significant.
Bace1 was a significant Atxn1-loss marker only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, not in the other 20 FDR-null groups.
The 151-TH Atxn1/Cic-like state paired down-regulation of postsynaptic and excitability genes with induction of Bdnf and regulated-secretory/neuropeptide genes.
Atxn1 loss in 151 TH induced a coupled neurite-cytoskeleton, glycosylation, lipid and extracellular-matrix remodeling program.
A smaller metabolic arm of the 151-TH response induced Aldh1l2, glycolytic/amino-acid transport genes, and mitochondrial redox components without a coherent UPR/ISR signature.
Atxn1 did not phenocopy the literature-obvious Rora or ataxia-gene comparators in the thalamic responder.
The screen revealed no strong mirror-image Atxn1 signature: Dstyk was the strongest broad gene anti-neighbor but had only a -0.020 full-profile cosine and no 151-TH FDR overlap.
Atxn1 produced a reproducible but very small cortical IT response involving Wnt/synaptic-terminal genes rather than a local copy of the thalamic CIC program.
Atxn2 loss produced a robust downstream transcriptional response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite recovery in 21 neuronal cell groups.
The negative arm of the 151 signature hit RNA-processing and nuclear-speckle factors, including Srsf11, Rsrp1 and Son.
Atxn2 perturbation up-regulated a small synaptic and neurite-structure module in 151, including Syt7, Sncb, Cspg5, Tln2, Crmp1, Stmn4, Ncdn and Gprasp1.
The screen did not recover a robust ATXN2 partner, TDP-43, stress-granule, UPR/ISR, autophagy or mTOR transcript program after Atxn2 loss.
Restricted-signature analysis placed Zbtb7a and Elp1, not a textbook ATXN2 partner, as the strongest same-direction neighbors of Atxn2 in 151.
Yy1 and Psmb4 were the top inverse restricted-signature neighbors of Atxn2 in 151.
ATXN2's ALS/stress-granule relatives did not phenocopy Atxn2 single-gene loss: Tardbp and Matr3 were broad, Tia1 was nearly flat, and their 151 overlap with Atxn2 was small or mixed.
Spinocerebellar ataxia-family targets represented in the parquet diverged from Atxn2: Atxn1 and Atxn10 responded but shared little of the 151 Atxn2 signature, whereas Atxn7 was flat.
Atxn7 gRNA targeting was transcriptomically buffered across the postmitotic neuronal panel: 20 measured groups and 1021 perturbed nuclei yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Atxn7 occupied a near-isolated point in the model-visible perturbation signature space: the strongest positive score-cosine was only 0.0320 and the strongest negative score-cosine was -0.0200.

Related ataxia and polyglutamine-family targets did not phenocopy Atxn7 loss: Atxn10, Atxn1, Htt, and Atxn2 produced FDR<0.10 genes in matched cell groups, but all had near-zero vector similarity to Atxn7.
The absence of an acute Atxn7 LoF transcriptional stress signature is weakly reassuring for ATXN7-lowering strategies but only outside the retina, glia, and long-term SCA7 disease setting.
Auh produced no BH-significant downstream neuronal transcriptional response in any of the 21 recovered cell groups.
The represented leucine/BCAA catabolic comparators Bckdhb, Dld, and Ivd were also downstream-null across the same 21 neuronal groups.
Whole-surface comparison found no robust positive or negative Auh signature neighbor.
Auts2 loss produced a single robust downstream hit: Dpysl4 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Auts2 was almost globally transcriptionally buffered after P16 mosaic CRISPR, with 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 22 measured cell groups.
Csnk2b and Crebbp were transcriptionally active where Auts2 was nearly flat, while Ep300 was flat; none shared the robust Auts2 Dpysl4 response.
Ctcf was the top positive pre-literature Auts2 neighbor and shared the same robust Dpysl4-up event in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Direct Rac1 and Cdc42 perturbations were flat or nearly flat and did not converge with Auts2.
Avpr1a loss produced a single robust transcriptomic event: Srsf6 up-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
The Srsf6-positive group did not carry a broader V1a Gq/PLC/PKC/MAPK or immediate-early-gene signature.
Directly represented nonapeptide and PLC/PKC pathway perturbations did not phenocopy the Avpr1a 110/Srsf6 response.
Nominal-surface signature neighbors were rejected as robust Avpr1a phenocopies.
Avpr1a behaved like a circuit- and state-dependent GPCR target rather than a target with a large basal cell-autonomous transcriptional footprint.
Avpr1b loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any measured neuronal group.
Canonical V1b immediate-early, PLC/PKC, NMDA-CaMKII, and Pomc/HPA marker transcripts were absent from the Avpr1b RNA response.
Represented vasopressin/oxytocin-family and PLC/PKC comparators did not phenocopy Avpr1b.
The represented NMDA/CaMKII arm diverged from Avpr1b: Grin1 had a clear thalamic/midbrain DE surface while Avpr1b did not.
Unbiased signature matching found no meaningful hidden Avpr1b neighbors.
The flat basal neuronal response argues that V1b-antagonist biomarkers should be sought in stressed HPA or defined CA2/PVN states, not in broad unstimulated neuron transcriptomes.
Acute postnatal Axl loss in NeuN+ neuronal nuclei produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any measured cell group.
The expected TAM paralog Mertk did not phenocopy with an active neuronal signature; it was as FDR-flat as Axl across the same 22 neuronal groups.
Axl perturbation failed to recover the innate-inflammatory, TAM-compensation, neurotrophin, ISR/UPR, autophagy, or apoptosis programs predicted from TAM biology in other systems.
A dataset-wide nominal-score neighbor search found no strong Axl-like perturbation signature.
B3gat3 produced a real but extremely restricted neuronal RNA response: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the only one of 23 measured groups with any downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
direction_pattern: Ndor1 and Herc1 up in 059; no FDR<0.10 downstream response in the other 22 measured groups

canonical_summary: The 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA response consisted of up-regulation of Ndor1 and Herc1, nominating a small redox/ubiquitin-ligase marker pair rather than a broad canonical GAG module.
Acute B3gat3 loss did not transcriptionally feed back onto the common linker, heparan-sulfate/chondroitin-sulfate enzyme set, proteoglycan core genes, or canonical stress modules.

Represented GAG/HS pathway perturbations did not phenocopy B3gat3 in the matched 059 responder, and the only robust downstream relatives-of-interest signal, Ext2, appeared in other glutamatergic groups on Epha5 and Slc6a17.
direction_pattern: nonconvergent; Ext2-specific effects outside the B3gat3 responding group

canonical_summary: The data-driven 059 B3gat3 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor among the 1742 other targets measured in that group.

The mostly null P16 neuronal transcriptome argues that B3GAT3-linked phenotypes are displaced from ongoing, cell-autonomous neuronal RNA regulation toward proteoglycan biochemistry, earlier wiring, and non-neuronal matrix-rich tissues.
B9d1 produced one FDR-supported response, a 25-gene signature restricted to 308 CB GABA, while 20 other recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The B9d1 CB-GABA responder signature upregulated synaptic and neuronal-signaling transcripts including Homer3, Doc2b, Scn4b, Nptx1, Dlg2, Grm7, Lrp8, Cdh2, Stac, and Plppr5.
Two extracellular-matrix genes, Col5a1 and Col18a1, were among the strongest B9d1-induced CB-GABA genes.
B9d1 upregulated several membrane/cytoskeletal regulatory transcripts in CB GABA, including Arhgap31, Arap1, Garnl3, Atl2, Strip2, Ptprr, Phc2, and Pogk.
The B9d1 CB-GABA signature did not recover a canonical Hedgehog, ciliary-GPCR, ciliary-assembly, or broad stress transcriptional program; Gas8 was the only cilium-adjacent FDR gene.
Ranbp2 was the strongest same-direction data-driven neighbor of the B9d1 CB-GABA signature, sharing 11 FDR-supported genes in the same direction.
Wdr26 opposed the B9d1 CB-GABA signature, reversing 22 of 25 B9d1 FDR genes at FDR<0.10.
Represented ciliary and Hedgehog comparators were flat in 308 CB GABA and did not share an FDR-supported B9d1 signature gene.
Bach2 produced a real but extremely narrow L4/5 IT cortical response: Dnajc5 and Yeats2 were up at FDR<0.10 only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, while every other measured group was null or weak.
Loss of Bach2 did not de-repress Hmox1 or a canonical ARE/cytoprotection program, even though the same parquet shows that Mafg loss can activate Hmox1 strongly in Pvalb neurons.
Represented sMaf/CNC/AP-1/Maf-family relatives did not phenocopy the Bach2 L4/5 signature.
Bach2 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the rest of the target universe.
Dnajc5 and Yeats2 are hypothesis-generating L4/5 readouts of Bach2 perturbation rather than generic responders.
Baiap2 was a pan-assay transcriptional null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 after P16 CRISPR loss of function.
The expected PSD, glutamate-receptor, Rho-actin, and immediate-early transcriptional candidates were not recovered as Baiap2 downstream genes in any cell group.
Direct NMDA receptor perturbations diverged from Baiap2: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced recurrent DE in matched neurons, whereas Baiap2 had none.

BAI1/PSD scaffold comparators did not phenocopy a hidden Baiap2-like module: Adgrb1, Shank2, Dlg4, and Syngap1 each had zero downstream DE across the matched groups, while Shank3 and Dlgap4 were sparse with two and ten genes.
Unbiased signature matching found no credible Baiap2 module: the best positive and negative z-score cosines were only 0.0305 and -0.0185.
Bap1 had a sparse, cell-state-restricted postmitotic neuronal response: 34 downstream FDR<0.10 genes confined to Pvalb, TH-Prkcd/Grin2c, and MB glutamatergic neurons.
Scg2 was the only recurrent Bap1 responder gene, down in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program combined up-regulation of Cnot9, Cstf2, Aifm3, Peg3, Ank2, Cdkl1, and Nlgn2 with down-regulation of Hdac1, Acly, Gsto1, Tpp1, Stt3b, Sema5a, Prkch, Klf6, and Rreb1.
The 155 MB Glut response consisted only of Ccdc39 and Hcn3 down-regulation.
The unbiased whole-profile scan placed Hnrnpc and Ankrd11 closest to Bap1, with Ankrd11 and Hnrnpc sharing down-regulation of Rreb1 and Ankrd11 also sharing Scg2 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Asxl3 and Foxk2 were flat and Ogt was broad but nonmatching, so the measurable PR-DUB relatives did not phenocopy acute Bap1 loss in any matched neuronal group.
Wdr26, Sin3a, Tpr, Psmb4, and Psmc1 were the strongest negative Bap1 neighbors and reversed more Bap1 significant features than they shared.
Bap1 did not induce canonical ISR, UPR, proteasome, autophagy-adaptor, or p53/cell-death marker transcripts in the three cell groups that had real DE.
The weak postnatal neuronal LoF signature aligns better with allele- and timing-specific BAP1 neurodevelopmental biology than with a simple mature-neuron tumor-suppressor LoF model.
Baz1b produced a two-gene, two-cell-group FDR response: Sfi1 down in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Atp1b2 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Four groups with FDR-level loss of the Baz1b self-transcript, and two groups with nearly single-gene downstream effects, did not show broad secondary cascades.
Baz1b loss after P16 did not recover the Wnt/neural-progenitor, neural-crest, p53/ISR or heat-shock programs expected from earlier-stage BAZ1B biology.

The represented Williams-region comparators Gtf2i, Gtf2ird1, Limk1 and Fzd9 did not phenocopy Baz1b; Gtf2i/Gtf2ird1 had small non-overlapping 151 TH Prkcd signatures, whereas Limk1 and Fzd9 were FDR-flat.

Data-driven Baz1b signature neighbors were non-obvious and mostly non-robust: Rala, Htr1b, Il12rb1 and Bicra had zero FDR<0.10 genes, while Wac was the strongest inverse neighbor but a much broader responder.
A single CTX-CGE GABA response, Sirt5 up-regulation, is the only FDR<0.10 downstream event after Bbs5 perturbation.
Bbs5 did not activate the expected Hedgehog, ciliary GPCR, hypothalamic satiety-receptor, UPR/ISR, or autophagy mRNA programs anywhere in the measured neuronal atlas.

The represented BBSome/ciliary relatives did not phenocopy Bbs5: Ttc8 was transcriptionally flat, and Lztfl1, Ift88, Cspp1, Gli1, Smo, Lepr, and Htr6 produced only isolated non-overlapping one-gene effects.
Unbiased full-vector signature neighbors of Bbs5 were essentially at r=0, so the Bbs5 surface lacks a hidden genome-wide convergence module.
Bbx loss produced a one-gene, layer-restricted response: Prrg3 decreased only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.

Postmitotic neuronal Bbx perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: 371,818 Bbx rows across 22 measured groups yielded only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, the Bbx self-transcript was never FDR-significant, and the Fgf23/phosphate genes from peripheral Bbx loss were absent.

Bbx did not phenocopy Cic, its literature-nominated HMG-box subfamily comparator: Cic produced 815 downstream events in the same 22 groups, including 51 in the Bbx-responder L4/5 IT group, while leaving Prrg3 unchanged there.

The embryonic NFIX→Bbx forebrain relationship was not reconstituted in postnatal neurons: Nfix, Nfia, and Nfib were essentially flat in Bbx-matched groups, and NFI/SOX/TCF HMG-family comparators had zero L4/5 IT CTX downstream hits where Bbx affected Prrg3.

Whole-surface Bbx signatures had no meaningful data-driven convergence neighbor after gene×cell-group centering; the strongest residual correlations were near zero and failed the matched L4/5 IT Prrg3 test.
Bcap31 loss did not launch a UPR, ISR, apoptosis, Golgi, or ER-translocation transcriptional state in any measured postmitotic neuronal class.
The Bcap31 null is pathway-selective rather than a generic inability of the assay to see ER stress.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search found no meaningful positive or negative Bcap31 signature neighbor.
The postnatal NeuN+ Bcap31 null should not be read as contradicting DDCH genetics; it specifies which disease axes this assay did not model.
Bcas3 produced one robust downstream event, an up-regulation of Trim23, and it was restricted to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The sole Bcas3 responder gene, Trim23, points toward an exploratory ubiquitin/selective-autophagy compensation rather than a broad stress response.
Bcas3 did not phenocopy measurable Cdc42, TGFβ/adhesion, or core-autophagy perturbations in the matched neuronal surfaces.
The whole Bcas3 signature is null-like: its strongest cross-perturbation score correlations were only |r|≤0.051 and included safe-target controls.
Bckdhb was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null: all 21 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and Bckdhb adjusted p values were uniformly 1.0.
The measured BCKDH-axis relatives Bckdk and Dld were also FDR-flat and essentially uncorrelated with Bckdhb, despite their direct connection to the same biochemical complex or regulatory node.
Bckdhb failed to induce an ISR, mitochondrial-stress, oxidative-stress, or immediate-early secondary program in any measured group.
An unbiased search over 1772 other perturbations found no meaningful positive or inverse whole-transcriptome neighbor for the Bckdhb Wilcoxon-score vector.
Acute postmitotic Bckdk loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null rather than a cell-type-selective DE response.
Bckdk perturbation did not create a detectable BCAA-catabolic, ATF4/ISR, or mTOR-complex transcriptional feedback program.
Neither unrestricted signature search nor BCAA/mTOR pathway comparators supplied a hidden Bckdk-like neuronal signature.
The neuronal snRNA null should not be read as evidence that BCKDK inhibition is developmentally inert.
Bcl11a loss after P16 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal class.
The expected Sema3c/Tbr1/Bcl6/Nr2f1 cortical-development readout was absent after Bcl11a perturbation.
Bcl11a, Bcl11b, and Satb2 form a developmentally important cortical-transcription-factor set that is jointly buffered in this P16 acute assay.
The Bcl11a null is gene-specific, because related transcriptional and chromatin regulators produced detectable signatures in the same matched neuronal groups.
A whole-universe neighbor search found no meaningful convergent or inverse Bcl11a signature.
The postnatal neuronal null should not be extrapolated to developmental or systemic BCL11A inhibition.
Bcl11b produced a global downstream-null response: 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in every one of the 23 measured neuronal groups.
The Bcl11b perturbation failed to reproduce the expected mature MSN identity and Huntington-like marker program in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Bcl11a and Satb2 were as flat as Bcl11b, whereas Tbr1 showed FDR-supported cortical responses in the same parquet.
The Bcl11b null did not phenocopy NuRD-associated targets: Chd4 produced 158 downstream DE genes while Bcl11b produced none.
Data-driven raw-score neighbors did not define a Bcl11b-like module.
The predicted dentate Dsp/granule-neuron program was absent from the two DG-containing Bcl11b DE surfaces.
Acute Bcl2 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across every recovered neuronal group: 23/23 measured groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Bcl2 did not phenocopy the Beclin-autophagy arm that literature would nominate: Becn1 and Atg5 produced a small 155 MB Glut response, sharing Calr down-regulation, whereas matched Bcl2 cells had no FDR<0.10 genes.

The unbiased cross-target search found no credible convergent or opposing Bcl2 module: the strongest centered correlations to Bcl2 were below |r|=0.10 and the nominated targets had either no DE or isolated small signatures.
Bdp1 produced a real transcriptional response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where 9 of 10 FDR genes were up-regulated stress or tRNA-charging genes and Kcnc2 was the sole down-regulated gene.
The Bdp1-positive program is centered on aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, with Mars1, Iars, Lars, Aars, Cars, and Yars all significantly induced in the same direction.
Elp1, Elp2, Gfpt1, and Atp2a2 perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut substantially converged on the Bdp1 10-gene signature.
Polr3b, the only available same-machinery Pol III comparator, was a weak full-surface positive neighbor but did not share any FDR<0.10 genes with Bdp1 in the Bdp1 responder class.
Bdp1 activated CHOP/aaRS genes without the broad ER-chaperone or synaptic-downregulation programs seen in stronger stress neighbors.
Becn1 yielded a very restricted snRNA response: only 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 155 MB Glut had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 155 MB Glut was the only multi-gene responder.
In 155 MB Glut, Becn1 loss coordinately decreased Psma5, Calr, Dnajb11, Ctsb, Dnm1, and Syt11.
Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the strongest broad same-cell comparators to Becn1 on the restricted signature, sharing several Becn1-down 110/155 markers while driving Psma5 in the opposite direction.

Canonical autophagy relatives did not generally phenocopy Becn1: Rb1cc1 and Atg5 had a small 155 MB Glut Calr/Ctsb overlap, but Atg16l1, Bcl2, and Rubcn were flat in matched measured groups and Mtor/Tsc2 were divergent.
Becn1 did not induce a robust Sqstm1/LC3-GABARAP/LAMP/UPR-ISR mRNA program in the strongest responder or the two single-gene responder groups.
The isolated Spen up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Atp1b1 down-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut are exploratory one-gene Becn1 sentinels.
Bicra loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal class: 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Bicra.
Bicra did not phenocopy Brd4, despite the ESC literature linking BRD4 to BRD9/GBAF chromatin recruitment: Brd4 had a 612-gene response across Bicra-measured groups while Bicra had none.
The thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group reported a BAF-sensitive module for Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, Smarce1, Smarcd1, and Brd4, yet Bicra stayed flat in the same cells.
Whole-transcriptome score-neighbor analysis found no meaningful Bicra signature neighbor: even the top real positive and negative cosines were only +0.0336 for Bcl2 and -0.0160 for Wdr26.
Postnatal Bin1 loss induced only two isolated downstream genes at FDR<0.10 across the whole 23-group neuronal surface.
Several null groups showed the on-target Bin1 transcript fall at FDR<0.10 without any downstream transcript passing FDR<0.10.
The calcium, activity-response and synaptic gene-expression program expected from human BIN1-null glutamatergic models was absent in the mouse P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen.
Bin1 did not sit in a shared clathrin/endosomal Alzheimer-risk transcriptional module, despite strong responses by Cltc and Rab7 in the same analysis universe.
A pre-literature all-target score-vector search found no meaningful convergent or anti-convergent Bin1 signature neighbor.
Acute Bmal1 loss recovered the expected BMAL1:CLOCK/NPAS2 E-box output: Nr1d2 was down in all eight responding groups, and Nr1d1 and Dbp were also down where the response broadened.
direction_pattern: canonical E-box outputs down; feedback genes partly up

canonical_summary: The clock response was strongly concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, which carried 153 of the 169 Bmal1 significant group-gene effects.

Bmal1 perturbation did not simply collapse the oscillator: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut paired down-regulation of Dbp/Nr1d1/Nr1d2/Per3 with up-regulation of Npas2 and Cry1, and 151 also up-regulated Clock, Nfil3, and Per2.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response contained a mixed synaptic, calcium, and ion-channel remodeling program rather than a pure clock-gene signature.
Bmal1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also remodeled neuronal adhesion and extracellular-matrix/PDGF genes, including down Adgrb1 and Timp3 and up Pdgfa, Col4a1, Col4a2, Lrp1b, and Cntnap1.

The only significant stress-adjacent signal was a small Uchl1/Deptor/Tmem41b/Fis1 quality-control module in 151; canonical Nrf2, UPR/ISR, heat-shock, astrocyte, and microglial transcripts were absent in 151 and 155.
direction_pattern: narrow quality-control response without broad stress induction

canonical_summary: Clock was the closest data-driven positive neighbor of Bmal1, but it was a sparse phenocopy: it shared the direction of 8 FDR<0.10 Bmal1 features, centered on Nr1d2 and Dbp, and had no significant genes in the Bmal1-responsive 005 or 008 groups.

Nr1d1, although a REV-ERB repressor and not a same-complex partner, produced a broad 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut state that overlapped Bmal1 much more than expected from a simple negative-feedback diagram.
Rora was broad but mostly opposed to Bmal1 in 151, and Rorb, Rorc, Ahr, Arnt, and Hif1a did not converge on the Bmal1 signature.

The noncanonical data-driven neighbors were useful mainly as rejects: Atxn10 ranked third on the restricted Bmal1 vector but split 3 same and 3 opposite FDR overlaps, and the top negative neighbors Magi2, Ywhae, Nfic, Creb1, and Pacs2 had no shared FDR<0.10 Bmal1 features.
Acute Bmal2 loss of function produced a complete pan-neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 recovered cell groups despite measuring the Arntl2 transcript in every group.
Bmal2 failed to engage the clock-output genes that were FDR-significant after Bmal1, Clock, Cry2, Nr1d1, and Rora perturbations, most clearly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The data-driven signature search also did not find a coherent non-clock Bmal2 module: the strongest Wilcoxon-score cosines to all other targets were only +0.0638 and -0.0512.
At FDR<0.10, acute Bmpr1a loss produced a pan-neuronal zero: 0 robust downstream genes across all 22 recovered cell groups and 371,796 downstream gene-by-cell-group tests.

The expected canonical BMP-SMAD transcriptional readout was absent after Bmpr1a perturbation: Id, Msx, Hes, Olig/Dlx, calbindin, Pvalb, and Sst rows were all tested but none approached FDR significance.

Bmpr1a did not phenocopy its measurable BMP receptor and SMAD neighbors; most single-node receptor/SMAD perturbations were flat, and the few FDR<0.10 calls in Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, Acvr1, Smad2, and Tgfbr2 were isolated single-gene events.
Unbiased feature-centered signature search placed Bmpr1a at the noise floor: even the strongest positive and negative neighbors had |r| less than 0.017.
The neuronal null fits BMPR1A disease biology being dominated by epithelial, progenitor, and developmental contexts rather than by an acute, cell-autonomous mature-neuron transcriptional liability.
Bmpr1b loss produced a single cortical L2/3 IT response, Mrgbp up-regulation, rather than a multi-gene BMP-SMAD program.
The cerebellar GABAergic Bmpr1b response was limited to up-regulation of Rnf157, a neuronal E3-ligase gene.
Canonical BMP receptor and SMAD perturbations did not phenocopy the two Bmpr1b responding groups.
Bmpr1b perturbation did not detectably depress canonical BMP-SMAD target or feedback genes in any measured neuronal class.
Bmpr1b had no strong data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor among the other 1,772 perturbation targets.
Bmpr2 loss produced a single robust downstream call, up-regulation of Eif4a1, and only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The CNU-MGE Eif4a1 hit was uncoupled from the expected canonical BMP-SMAD-ID transcriptional module.
Same-pathway BMP receptor/SMAD and BMPR2-LIMK/FMR1 perturbations did not phenocopy Bmpr2.
Pre-literature signature neighbors of Bmpr2 were statistically ranked but biologically negligible.
The BMPR2 pulmonary-hypertension gene family was transcriptionally silent in NeuN-enriched neurons.
Bpnt2 self-RNA was lower in every measured neuronal group, including FDR<0.10 self-loss in 10 groups, but no cell group contained even one non-Bpnt2 gene at FDR<0.10.
The Bpnt2 neuronal surface failed to recover the chondroitin / proteoglycan sulfation and chondrocyte transcripts predicted from its canonical disease biology.

Represented proteoglycan-pathway targets B3gat3, Ext1, Ext2, and Hs6st2 did not phenocopy Bpnt2: Ext1 and Hs6st2 were fully downstream-null, and B3gat3/Ext2 had only isolated one- or two-group hits with near-zero Bpnt2 cosines.
Unbiased cosine matching found no strong positive or negative Bpnt2 signature neighbor; all top absolute cosines were below 0.033.
The neuronal Bpnt2 null warns that BPNT2-dependent lithium or PAP/PAPS effects are unlikely to be captured by acute neuronal snRNA-seq alone.
P16 Bptf loss produced a caudal neuronal response rather than the broad cortical-fate collapse predicted from embryonic Bptf deletions.
Zcwpw2 induction and Grk4 induction are the clearest recurrent Bptf-dependent transcripts.
The main Bptf-positive neurons combine Grk4 up-regulation with down-regulation of GPCR, vesicle, and excitability-associated transcripts.
direction_pattern: Grk4 up; most vesicle/excitability transcripts down

canonical_summary: Bptf responders carry RNA-processing, lysosomal/glycoprotein, mitochondrial, and protein-quality-control changes rather than a single canonical chromatin output.
direction_pattern: mixed, with most RNA-processing hits down

canonical_summary: The assayed Bptf loss did not recover the embryonic Smad, primitive-streak, pluripotency, or cortical fate gene sets expected from germline and forebrain knockouts.
Ctcf is the strongest high-overlap positive signature neighbor of Bptf.
Most chromatin and neurodevelopmental-disease comparators did not phenocopy Bptf even when they were active in the same cell groups.
direction_pattern: partial, divergent, or flat across comparators

canonical_summary: The Bptf-Ctcf convergence was not reproduced by the measured cohesin subunits Smc1a, Stag1, or Stag2.
direction_pattern: Ctcf converges; cohesin subunits weakly overlap

canonical_summary: Braf produced a tiny all-down response restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with recurrent Vgf down-regulation and only five downstream FDR<0.10 target-cell-group events in total.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature combined Vgf, Ptpn5, Atp2a2, and Unc13a down-regulation, connecting neuropeptide output to STEP-mediated synaptic feedback, ER calcium handling, and synaptic-vesicle priming.
Map2k1, Ntrk2, and Shoc2 partially converged with Braf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Map2k1 shared Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a down-regulation, Ntrk2 shared Vgf and Atp2a2, and Shoc2 shared Vgf.
Raf1, Map2k2, Kras, Hras, Sos1, Ptpn11, and Mapk1 did not phenocopy Braf, despite direct measurement as pathway relatives in the same parquet.
Gabrb2 and Atp2b1 were data-driven anti-neighbors in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut because they induced Vgf, while Braf repressed Vgf in the same cell group.
Braf neuronal LoF after P16 failed to recover a broad CFC/RASopathy-like MAPK transcriptional activation program and instead lowered selected Vgf/synaptic transcripts.
Rnpc3 and Tpr were the top noncanonical positive neighbors of the five-entry Braf signature, but their overlap sat inside very broad perturbation responses.

Brd1 loss produced a very small but real two-site postmitotic signature: five FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one in 308 CB GABA, with 20 measured groups lacking any robust downstream gene.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Brd1 signature converged with the Yy1, Wac, Phf12, and Sin3a perturbations on a Gabbr2/Rgs11/Ptpn3/Ndufa13/Wdr26 subset; Yy1 and Wac each reproduced three of Brd1's five thalamic FDR hits in the same direction.
Brd1 downregulated the complex-I subunit Ndufa13 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but broad nuclear-encoded mitochondrial markers were not coordinately changed at FDR<0.10.
The entire 308 CB GABA Brd1 response was Dnajb2 upregulation, whereas Wdr26 perturbation in the same cell class downregulated Dnajb2 while producing a much broader signature.

Represented MYST/HAT comparators did not phenocopy Brd1: Kat6a and Kat6b were flat in every measured group, Ep300 was flat, and Crebbp responded only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without sharing Brd1 FDR genes.
Arid2, the strongest negative thalamic score neighbor, pushed Gabbr2 upward where Brd1 pushed it downward.
Brd4 loss produced a basal neuronal response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with thirteen recovered groups having 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Pabpn1 was induced in five Brd4 responder groups and co-occurred with smaller recurrent increases of Leng8, Rsrp1, and Pnisr.
Brd4 perturbation repressed neuronal process, adhesion, channel, and synaptic genes in the thalamic and midbrain responders.
Lysosomal, vacuolar ATPase, and endosomal transcripts were induced in posterior Brd4 responders.
Mat2a was the only L4/5 IT cortical Brd4 FDR hit and was also strongly down-regulated in the main thalamic responder.
Data-driven Brd4 neighbors converged with Slc7a6os, Tnpo3, Yy1, and Wac rather than with a robust opposite signature; the strongest anti-neighbors Pkd1 and Ank1 had no overlapping FDR response.
Psmc1 partially overlapped Brd4 but was far broader, producing 11090 FDR genes across 21 groups compared with 612 Brd4 FDR genes.
Represented bromodomain, p300/CBP, Mediator, and MYC-axis comparators did not phenocopy Brd4.
Canonical MYC and broad immediate-early genes were measured but not activated or repressed at FDR<0.10 after Brd4 perturbation.
Acute Brinp1 loss in P16-specified NeuN+ neurons was almost completely buffered at the mRNA level: 21 of 22 measured cell groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream DEG and the remaining group had only one.
The only Brinp1 downstream gene crossing FDR<0.10 was Tbc1d2b up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nuclei.
Brinp1 did not phenocopy the data-driven neighbors or the measurable BMP/SMAD and retinoic-acid receptor targets in the Brinp1-matched cell groups.

The screen places Brinp1 behavioral and neurodevelopmental phenotypes upstream of the assayed mature-neuron transcriptome, in developmental timing, neurogenic precursors, or circuit/cell-number phenotypes.
Brsk2 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.

Brsk2 did not converge with measured LKB1/SAD/MARK or BRSK2-associated metabolic pathway targets; the nearest canonical comparators had near-zero Brsk2 score-cosines, whereas Tsc2 had a large independent response.
The all-gene Brsk2 vector had only near-zero data-driven positive and negative signature neighbors.
BRSK2 neurodevelopmental-disease relevance was not recovered as an acute juvenile Brsk2 nuclear stress or synaptic-transcript program.
Brwd1 loss produced a single FDR-significant downstream response, Jund induction, restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA neurons.
BRWD1 did not phenocopy BAF-complex loss even though BRWD1 is BAF-associated in brain.
A pre-literature sparse-signature scan found no robust Brwd1 convergence module.
The dataset does not recover the broad synaptic or BAF-mistargeting program predicted from Down-syndrome BRWD1 gain in euploid Brwd1 LoF nuclei.
Acute postmitotic Bscl2 perturbation was broadly buffered: 21 of 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the one responder had only Hpf1.
Hpf1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only robust Bscl2 downstream hit.
Genome-wide data-driven signature neighbors of Bscl2 were numerically near zero and failed a matched DE-surface recheck.
Hereditary motor-neuropathy and spastic-paraplegia comparators did not phenocopy Bscl2.
Srebf2 and Tsc2 perturbations proved that sterol and metabolic transcriptional signatures were detectable where Bscl2 was flat.
Postnatal mosaic Bsg loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a cell-type-restricted DEG program.
Canonical MCT/lactate, glycolytic, hypoxia, ISR/UPR, PMCA, Bsg-family, cyclophilin, and neuronal MMP transcripts were not transcriptionally induced or repressed after Bsg perturbation.
The PMCA catalytic axis diverged from Bsg: Atp2b1 loss triggered an immediate-early/neuropeptide response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Bsg and Atp2b2 were flat.
The measurable cyclophilin-B and integrin relatives did not phenocopy Bsg.
Bsg had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbors in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The Bsg surface argues against using acute neuronal stress transcripts as a sensitive on-target biomarker for CD147 inhibition.
Bsn loss induced a solitary Mcts1 up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Bsn perturbation was broadly buffered at the nuclear transcriptome despite Bassoon's established presynaptic active-zone function.
Piccolo, Unc13, Cacna1a, and Syp did not reproduce the 008 Bsn-Mcts1 signature, whereas Stxbp1 was a broad responder elsewhere.
Unbiased Bsn signature neighbors had near-zero correlations and no shared formal 008 Mcts1 response.
Broad hypothalamic groups did not show a juvenile Bsn transcriptional response despite the human adult-onset BSN obesity association.
The reported Bassoon-Atg5 presynaptic autophagy axis did not become a nucleus-wide autophagy or proteostasis RNA program.
Acute P16 Btbd9 CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The empirical Btbd9 score-vector neighbors were all nearly uncorrelated with Btbd9, so there was no meaningful convergent or anti-convergent module to keep.
Btbd9 did not produce a basal ubiquitin, proteasome, autophagy, ISR or UPR transcriptome, and represented BTB-family perturbations did not phenocopy it.
Btbd9 is transcriptionally uncoupled from clock-gene programs that are readily detected after Bmal1, Clock and Nr1d1 perturbation.
Dopamine and iron marker transcripts were absent under Btbd9 perturbation, and RLS-family perturbations Meis1 and Ptprd did not converge with Btbd9.
The Mn/insulin-IGF oxidative-stress branch of BTBD9 biology was not active in basal juvenile neurons.
C3 loss produced a uniform pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor measured C3-linked innate comparators converged with C3.
The flat C3 neuronal CRISPR signature should not be interpreted as a negative result for extracellular C3 pharmacology.
Cacna1a produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of its 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The cerebellar GABAergic null does not recapitulate SCA6-like alpha1-ACT or Purkinje-degeneration transcription.
Represented voltage-gated calcium-channel alpha and auxiliary-subunit perturbations did not converge on a Cacna1a-like signature.
The full Cacna1a signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor across the model-visible target universe.
Migraine, epilepsy, and synaptic-release comparator targets did not define a recurrent channelopathy transcriptome shared with Cacna1a.

Cacna1d perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the measured postnatal neuronal surface, with only 2 downstream FDR<0.10 genes among 355025 downstream tests and no FDR-significant decrease of the target transcript itself.
The only Cacna1d FDR hits were Vps28 down in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Ddx24 up in 053 Sst Gaba, two isolated single-gene responses.

Represented voltage-gated calcium-channel comparators did not phenocopy the weak Cacna1d signature; Cacna1g and Cacna2d1 responded in different cell groups and Cacna1a, Cacna1e, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, and Cacnb4 were flat.

Data-driven signature neighbors were not biologically convergent: Cpt1c was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative neighbor, but their full-surface score correlations with Cacna1d were only +0.0336 and -0.0208 and they did not share the Vps28 or Ddx24 hits.
The postmitotic Cacna1d LoF surface lacks the immediate-early, UPR, autophagy, and dopaminergic Ca2+-stress programs expected from other CaV1.3 contexts.
Cacna1e LoF produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The LoF screen does not reproduce the gain-of-function CACNA1E encephalopathy mechanism.
Cacna1e diverged from Cacna1g and resembled the mostly buffered CaV pore/auxiliary perturbations.
Cdkl5 LoF, like Cacna1e LoF, was transcriptionally flat despite a biochemical CDKL5-Cav2.3 phosphorylation relationship.
NMDAR subunit loss generated robust RNA signatures where Cacna1e remained flat.
The substantia-nigra dopaminergic Cav2.3 stress-survival program is not tested by the recovered Cacna1e surface.
Acute Cacna1g loss produced a real but narrowly thalamic transcriptional footprint: 14 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every other measured group.
The thalamic Cacna1g response included down-regulation of Jun together with postsynaptic or dendritic genes Lrrc7, Begain, Stmn4, Cpne7, and Zdhhc22.
Ptprn was the strongest downstream gene induced by Cacna1g in 151 TH, accompanied by Notum, Serpine2, and Iyd up-regulation.

Cacna1g did not phenocopy other represented voltage-gated calcium-channel perturbations: Cacna1a, Cacna1d, Cacna1e, Cacna2d1, Cacna2d2, Cacnb2, Cacnb4, Cacng2, and Cacng3 all had zero downstream genes in the same 151 TH group.

The top positive FDR-overlap neighbors of the 151 Cacna1g signature were not Cacna genes but Rnpc3 and Atp1a3; Rnpc3 shared 10 signature genes and Atp1a3 shared eight, mostly or wholly in the Cacna1g direction.
The strongest negative FDR-overlap comparators were weak and chromatin/transporter-biased: Arid2 reversed three of four shared Cacna1g genes, and Slc6a17 drove Jun and Stmn4 opposite to Cacna1g.

Cacna1g loss did not produce a broad immediate-early, CREB/BDNF, UPR, or ISR program in its responding thalamic class; Jun was down, but Fos, Bdnf, Arc, Egr1, Npas4, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, and Xbp1 were not FDR-significant.

A robust Cacna1g self-transcript drop in cerebellar GABA neurons produced no downstream DE, arguing that acute mosaic LoF is a poor transcriptional proxy for human cerebellar CACNA1G missense channelopathies.

Acute postmitotic Cacna2d1 loss-of-function produced a nearly flat neuronal snRNA-seq surface: 20 of 21 measured cell groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene and the remaining group had a single FDR 0.091 Actr3 hit.
The only Cacna2d1 downstream hit was Actr3 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.

The same parquet rejected a simple calcium-channel-family phenocopy: Cacna2d2 and the represented CaV1/CaV2-associated Cacna1a, Cacna1e, Cacnb2 and Cacnb4 surfaces were flat, whereas Cacna1g produced a 14-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.

Mean-centered whole-surface signature search found no robust Cacna2d1 neighbor; the strongest gene-level residual correlations were only r=0.0257 with Wrn and r=-0.0353 with Maf, and a safe-target control was among the top positives.

The flat central-brain signature should not be read as devalidating α2δ-1 as a pain target; the best-established pregabalin and α2δ-1 knockout phenotypes live in ligand binding, channel trafficking and injured sensory-neuron physiology rather than in DRG-free brain snRNA-seq.
Cacna2d2 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups.
The α2δ-family comparator Cacna2d1 was almost as transcriptionally buffered as Cacna2d2, and Cacna2d3/4 were not represented as perturbation targets.
direction_pattern: Cacna2d2 flat; Cacna2d1 cerebellar singleton only

canonical_summary: Cacna1g triggered a 14-gene T-type calcium-channel response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Cacna2d2 was flat in the same cell group.
direction_pattern: Cacna1g mixed; Cacna2d2 no FDR DE

canonical_summary: Grin2b produced a cortical activity/synaptic down-program that Cacna2d2 did not reproduce in the same broad cortical glutamatergic groups.
direction_pattern: Grin2b mostly down in IT neurons; Cacna2d2 flat

canonical_summary: The unbiased Cacna2d2 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor in the represented perturbation universe.
A gabapentinoid-binding α2δ-2 loss-of-function perturbation lacked a nuclear RNA biomarker in this assay.
direction_pattern: transcriptionally silent despite druggable CaV auxiliary biology

canonical_summary: Cacnb2 produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 21 recovered Cacnb2 cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and both dopaminergic/pineal groups were missing rather than silent.

The β2/CaV1.2 excitation-to-transcription expectation was not recovered: activity-, CREB-, and MAPK-responsive genes including Fos, Jun, Egr1, Egr3, Npas4, Nr4a1, Arc, Bdnf, Dusp1, Dusp6, and Homer1 were all nonsignificant after Cacnb2 perturbation.

Represented CaV relatives mostly failed to phenocopy each other: Cacnb4, Cacna1a, Cacna1e, Cacna2d2, Cacng2, and Cacng3 had no downstream FDR<0.10 signature in matched groups, Cacna1d and Cacna2d1 gave only singleton responses, whereas the β-independent T-type channel Cacna1g produced a 14-gene response restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Whole-surface Cacnb2 neighbors were themselves essentially null and had only tiny residual correlations, whereas unrelated Psmb4 and Psmc1 perturbations produced the two broadest DE surfaces in the same Cacnb2-measured cell groups.
The Cacnb2 neuronal null argues that CACNB2 cardiac and neurodevelopmental disease alleles should not be modeled as a generic, basal postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome.
Cacnb4 was a genome-wide downstream null in every recovered neuronal group, with only the Cacnb4 transcript itself reaching FDR<0.10 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
The Cacnb4 signature had no substantive positive or negative neighbor and did not converge with the represented voltage-gated-calcium-channel relatives.
Cacnb4 loss did not recover the thalamic T-type or GABAergic-remodeling program expected from organismal absence-epilepsy models.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was not globally refractory to calcium perturbation: Cacna1g, Atp2b1, and Calm1 all produced FDR-detectable DE in the same group where Cacnb4 had none downstream.
The cerebellar GABA group showed no Cacnb4 self-depletion and no downstream DE, despite the known adult lethargic cerebellar phenotype.
Cacng2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.
The measured Cacng2 null did not include an AMPAR, TARP-paralog, BDNF, or immediate-early mRNA rebound.
NMDAR-subunit perturbations were transcriptionally active in the same analysis universe where Cacng2 was silent.
Represented AMPAR/TARP/PSD-95 relatives were flat or almost flat, paralleling Cacng2 rather than the NMDAR subunits.
Data-driven full-surface neighbors of Cacng2 were only noise-scale and did not expose a hidden module.
The assay separates Cacng2 disease biology from the postnatal cell-autonomous nuclear programs it can trigger.
Cacng3 was a pan-null transcriptional perturbation in this post-P16 neuronal CRISPR screen.
The expected AMPAR, TARP-paralog, postsynaptic-scaffold, and activity-regulated feedback transcripts were not induced or repressed after Cacng3 perturbation.
Cacng3 had no robust genome-wide signature neighbor, and the measurable AMPAR neighbors Cacng2 and Dlg4 were also transcriptionally flat.
The CACNG3 childhood-absence locus did not behave like an acute thalamic Cacng3 loss-of-function transcriptome, even in a thalamic group where Cacna1g produced a measurable response.

Cadm2 was a pan-neuronal downstream transcriptomic non-responder: all 22 recovered cell groups had zero non-Cadm2 genes at FDR<0.10, including the four groups where the Cadm2 transcript itself was significantly reduced.

Cadm2 had no robust data-driven signature neighbor across the full perturbation universe; its highest positive and negative Wilcoxon-z correlations were |r|<0.03 and could not be kept as FDR-supported convergence.

Cadm2 did not phenocopy measurable synaptic-adhesion perturbations such as Nrxn1/2/3, Nlgn3, Cntnap1/2, Lrrtm1/3/4, Ptprt, Grid1/2, or Nectin1; those targets were themselves mostly downstream-flat or restricted to isolated one-gene effects.

The screen did not recover the synapse, axon-guidance, astrocyte-interface, or behavioral circuitry programs that the Cadm2 literature would nominate; it therefore narrows the acute Cadm2 phenotype away from a large post-P16 cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA program.
Cadps2 loss was buffered to an almost flat snRNA-seq surface: 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 22 measured neuronal groups, confined to Gnl3 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
The only Cadps2 DEG, Gnl3, points to a solitary nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis marker and is uncoupled from BDNF/NT-3, Trk, immediate-early, Pvalb, and neuropeptide-cargo transcripts.

Measured neurotrophin-receptor and vesicle-release perturbations did not phenocopy Cadps2 in 009: Stxbp1 had an Ankrd13d-only response and Ntrk2/Ntrk3/Unc13/Cplx/Syt2/Stx1b/Dnm1/Rab3gap1 perturbations had no 009 FDR<0.10 signature.
The data-driven Gnl3 neighbors were rejected as true Cadps2 signature neighbors: the top same-direction and opposite-direction ranks for Gnl3 in 009 were all sub-FDR.
Acute Calm1 loss was not a pan-neuronal transcriptional perturbation; only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a multi-gene response, while 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba had singleton responses.
The principal 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response mixed Rasgrp2, Resp18, Vamp1, Tuba1a/Tuba1b, Coro6, Eno2, Fabp5, Tecr, Peg3, Mest, Maged1, and Aifm3 induction with Atp2b1 and Car4 repression.
Calm2 and Calm3 did not phenocopy Calm1: Calm2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Calm3 had three non-overlapping singleton genes.
CaM effector perturbations were mostly flat or divergent; Atp2b1 and Ppp3r1 responded in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but shared almost none of the Calm1 genes.
The top data-driven signature neighbors were Zbtb7a, Cic, and Huwe1, while Camta1, Tpr, and Prpf6 were the strongest inverse neighbors.
The weak transcriptional consequence of Calm1 LoF supports separating postnatal neuronal single-gene haploinsufficiency from dominant calmodulinopathy alleles.
Resp18 was the only recurrent downstream gene, up in both 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Calm1 loss did not activate a classical Fos/Junb/Arc/Npas4/Egr/Nr4a activity-dependent transcriptional module.
P16 mosaic Calm2 loss produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
Calm2 did not trigger the Ca2+/CaM-activity transcriptional genes that are recovered after NMDA-receptor perturbations in the same DE universe.
The identical calmodulin-coding loci do not form a shared FDR signature: Calm1 has a sparse thalamic response, Calm3 only three singleton downstream calls, and Calm2 has none.
A whole-universe signed-Wilcoxon neighbor search found no meaningful positive or inverse Calm2 signature neighbor.
The neuronal Calm2 LoF null is consistent with calmodulinopathy being mainly a dominant missense, lineage-biased disease model rather than simple Calm2 haploinsufficiency.
Postnatal Calm3 knockdown produced a detectable Calm3 mRNA decrease in most measured neuronal groups but only three robust downstream DE genes across the entire 22-group response surface.
Ncdn was selectively induced downstream of Calm3 in Pvalb interneurons.
Cacna1c was selectively reduced downstream of Calm3 in Sst interneurons.
Slc38a1 was selectively reduced downstream of Calm3 in the hypothalamic CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic group.
The identical-protein paralogs Calm1 and Calm2 did not phenocopy Calm3 on the Ncdn, Cacna1c, or Slc38a1 anchors.
CaMKII and calcineurin subunit perturbations represented in the screen failed to reproduce the Calm3 anchor genes in matched responder groups.
The strongest FDR-supported data-driven antineighbor was Psmb4, which reversed two Calm3 anchors instead of converging on them.
Camk2a loss generated a very sparse transcriptional response: 4 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, all confined to two cortical glutamatergic groups, with no FDR signal in 20 other measured groups.
L4/5 IT cortical neurons carried a three-gene mixed signature, with Pnisr and Fhl1 increased and the sodium-channel β1 subunit gene Scn1b decreased.
L5 extratelencephalic cortical neurons down-regulated Rasal1 after Camk2a perturbation.
Camk2a did not phenocopy upstream NMDA-receptor subunits even though Grin2a and Grin2b were among the strongest matched cortical comparators.
The Camk2a RNA signature did not converge with CaMKII paralogs, calmodulins, Dlg4, or AMPAR subunits.
Camk2a lacked a strong data-driven transcriptomic neighbor in the complete perturbation universe.
Camk2b loss produced a nearly flat basal snRNA-seq phenotype: across 22 recovered cell groups, 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only effect group and Tmem25 was its single downstream DEG at FDR<0.10.

The measured CaMKII paralogs did not phenocopy Camk2b: Camk2a had only four downstream FDR<0.10 genes, Camk2g had none, and their whole-transcriptome score correlations with Camk2b were only 0.014810 and 0.021282.

Perturbing calmodulins and NMDAR/PSD targets did not share Camk2b's sparse response; Grin2a, Grin2b, and Grin1 generated real transcriptional signatures in matched groups, whereas Calm1-3, Grin1/2a/2b/2d/3a, Dlg4, and Syngap1 shared no FDR<0.10 genes with Camk2b.

Unbiased whole-universe score-vector comparison found no strong positive or negative Camk2b neighbor: the best positive real targets were Kcnc1 and Taok1 at r≈0.031, and the strongest negative real targets, Fbxo11 and Ranbp2, were only r≈-0.02.

The flat CRISPR-LoF RNA phenotype does not contradict CAMK2B disease genetics; it says that sparse juvenile loss is a poor proxy for the activity-dependent, developmental, and allele-specific CaMKII mechanisms implicated by human missense variants.
Camk2g loss of function produced no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected activity-dependent CREB/immediate-early-gene axis was absent from the basal Camk2g snRNA signature.
CaMKII-family knockouts did not converge on a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module.
NMDAR, calmodulin, calcineurin, and CREB perturbations can produce FDR-detectable signatures in the same cell-group universe where Camk2g is flat.
The flat P16 Camk2g loss-of-function surface supports a specific-allele and timing warning for CAMK2G neurodevelopmental disease models.
A data-driven neighbor search did not identify a robust Camk2g transcriptional module.
Acute P16 Camkmt perturbation produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Camkmt loss failed to induce a mitochondrial respiratory-chain, ISR, or UPR transcriptional program after P16 neuronal perturbation.
Direct CaM substrate genes and CaM-dependent effector genes did not transcriptionally converge with Camkmt.
Whole-parquet signature matching found only trivial positive and negative Camkmt neighbors.

P16 sparse Caml perturbation produced FDR<0.10 downstream responses in 6 of 23 measured neuronal groups, with broad signatures restricted to Pvalb, hypothalamic GABA, thalamic Prkcd, midbrain glutamatergic, and MB/P/MY GABA groups and a singleton Pineal signal.
Caml responders down-regulated synaptic vesicle, inhibitory-receptor, and ion-homeostasis genes, including Gabra1, Gabrd, Gabrg2, Syp, Sv2a, Gabbr1, Glrb, Gria2, and Atp1a3.

The broad TH and MB Glut signatures contained a down-regulated neuronal adhesion and extracellular scaffold branch, with Lingo1, Pcdh1, Spock1, Spock2, L1cam, Nrcam, Cadm4, Agrn, Lamb1, Nlgn3, and Cntnap5a affected across responders.
Caml perturbation repeatedly activated a Stmn4-up, neuronal-tubulin-down cytoskeletal module.
Caml induced a partial AP-1/CREM/XBP1 stress branch but not a full UPR/ISR program.
