Proteasome subunit perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1 were the top two same-direction neighbors of the restricted Caml signature.
Direct Gabra1 and Gabrg2 perturbations did not phenocopy Caml, despite successful self-transcript knockdown of the receptor subunits.
The top restricted anti-neighbors, Zbtb7a and Dctn1, opposed only a subset of Caml features and did not phenocopy the CAML state.
Camsap1 produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any recovered cell group.
No other perturbation in the model-visible universe converged strongly with Camsap1.
Represented microtubule comparators did not phenocopy Camsap1, and the direct CAMSAP paralog test was unavailable.
The disease-relevant Camsap1 biology is not recovered as an acute P16 stress, proteostasis, apoptosis, or synaptic transcriptional program in surviving neurons.
Camta1 loss elicited a recurrent negative core, headed by Snhg11 and joined by Snrpn, Peg3, Tecr, Coro6, Aifm3, Haghl, Cntnap1, and Vamp1, in all 17 cell groups with any FDR<0.10 downstream signal.

The high-response Pvalb, thalamic, midbrain/hindbrain, pineal-related, hypothalamic and cerebellar GABA signatures down-regulated axonal, synaptic-vesicle, glutamate-receptor and ion-channel transcripts.
Camta1 responders also carried a largely negative extracellular-matrix and adhesion submodule containing Bcan, Hapln4, Sparcl1, Cntn2, Cntnap1, Lgi3, Omg and Gas6.
A metabolic and ion-homeostatic arm, including Nat8l, Eno2, Pygb, Ckmt1, Aldoc, Cds1, Sfxn5 and Slc4a2, was down-regulated in the same stronger Camta1 responders.

The strongest posterior groups retained a smaller positive arm, with Stmn1, Celf3, Fnbp1l, Grik5, Gpr162, Igsf8 and selected synaptic or transmitter genes increasing against the dominant negative background.

The nearest unbiased positive neighbors of the Camta1 signature were Wdr26, U2af2 and Prpf6, with proteasome perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1 converging on the same Camta1-significant genes even more broadly.
Calm1 was the strongest biological anti-neighbor of Camta1, and Mecp2 and Huwe1 also opposed Camta1 on recurrent posterior genes.
The expected Calm and Camta-family transcriptional targets were absent: Camta1 perturbation did not significantly alter Calm1, Calm2, Calm3 or Camta2 mRNA in any measured group.
Represented ataxia-family genes were not Camta1 phenocopies: Atxn1 was concentrated in 151 and mostly opposite on shared Camta1 genes, Atxn2 was weak, and Atxn7 was flat.
Caskin1 produced a single robust downstream response: Mccc2 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups buffered Caskin1 RNA depletion without a downstream transcriptome.
Known Caskin1 biochemical neighbors did not phenocopy the Caskin1 responder in the snRNA perturbation map.
Grin2a and Grin2b drove cortical IT transcriptional programs where Caskin1 was flat.
Acute postmitotic Caskin1 LoF did not recover the reported iPSC CASKIN1 D1204N developmental transcriptome.
Unbiased Caskin1 signature neighbors were near zero and unrelated to the sole responder gene.
P16 Casr loss of function produced an almost fully buffered neuronal nuclear transcriptome: only two of 22 recovered cell groups had any FDR<0.10 downstream gene, and each was a singleton.
The sole Casr response in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut was Ago3 down-regulation.
The sole Casr response in 054 CNU-MGE GABA was Srrm4 up-regulation.
Literature-obvious class-C GPCR and CaSR second-messenger perturbations did not phenocopy the Casr surface.
An unbiased whole-DE neighbor search found no strong convergent or anti-convergent Casr signature.
Expected CaSR-linked differentiation, myelin/glial, neurite, and immediate-early activity transcripts were absent from the Casr DE surface.
Acute P16 Casz1 loss did not induce a robust neuronal transcriptome in any measured group: 22 of 22 tested cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Casz1 did not phenocopy directly represented NuRD-related perturbations: Chd4 and, to a much lesser extent, Gatad2b/Mbd2 generated FDR<0.10 genes in matched cell groups while Casz1 remained zero everywhere.
Casz1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor: the strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations across the model-visible perturbation universe were only +0.0257 and -0.0175.
The screen localizes Casz1 sensitivity away from acute, cell-autonomous mature-neuron transcription and toward earlier or unsampled CASZ1 biology.
Cblb was a high-confidence pan-neuronal transcriptional null in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen: 22 recovered neuronal groups all had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical Cbl-b immune-checkpoint program was absent from NeuN+ neurons, and the represented proximal relatives Fyn, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Pik3cb, and Akt3 were also flat.
Cblb did not phenocopy tractable neuronal RTK-MAPK or mTOR-axis perturbations: Tsc2, Map2k1, Ntrk2, and Mtor produced FDR<0.10 outputs but shared no significant genes with Cblb.

The data-driven Cblb neighborhood was essentially empty: the strongest absolute Pearson score correlation to any other perturbation was only 0.0285, and most nearest non-Safe neighbors were themselves FDR-level nulls.
The neuronal flatness is weakly reassuring for CBL-B inhibitor programs only on the narrow question of basal autonomous neuronal transcription; it should not be read as a CNS-wide safety result.
Ccdc50 loss was a pan-measured neuronal null at the snRNA-seq level: every tested cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite Ccdc50 transcript measurements in 22 groups.
The brain-neuron CRISPR null is directionally consistent with DFNA44 being poorly explained by simple Ccdc50 haploinsufficiency.

The cultured-neuron CCDC50-V2–NGFR/JNK neurite-outgrowth axis was not recovered by late postnatal cortical and hippocampal Ccdc50 perturbation, and represented RTK/JNK neighbors were also transcriptionally flat.
Ccdc50 did not phenocopy core autophagy perturbations: Becn1, Atg5, and Sqstm1 produced only sparse but real DE in selected neuronal groups, whereas Ccdc50 had zero genes in the same response matrix.
Ccdc50 had no informative positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor in the model-visible target universe.
The basal neuronal null is favorable for acute on-target tolerability but does not de-risk CCDC50 inhibition under lysosomal damage or proteotoxic aging.
Cck self-transcript depletion did not propagate into a cell-autonomous FDR-scale transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
The canonical CCK ligand-receptor axis was co-flat: Cck, Cckar and Cckbr perturbations all lacked significant downstream transcriptional output in matched brain cell groups.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Cck transcriptional module.
Cck perturbation did not activate an immediate-early or neurotrophin transcriptional surrogate for altered network activity.
Cckar single-gene loss produced a pan-taxonomy zero-FDR neuronal signature: no downstream gene crossed FDR<0.10 in any of 23 measured cell groups, and Cckar itself had FDR=1.0 everywhere.

The represented CCK ligand/receptor/Gq-pathway relatives Cck, Cckbr, Plcb1, and Prkca also failed to produce a significant downstream transcriptional surface, each yielding zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 22 measured groups.
Acute postnatal Cckar loss did not recover the embryonic CCK-receptor midline/interneuron-migration transcriptome: Cxcl12, Bmp7, Nrp2, Grin2b, and Grin3a were all FDR=1.0 in every Cckar cell group.

Full-profile data-driven neighbors were numerically near zero: Wdr26, Dstyk, and Frrs1l were the strongest positive neighbors, whereas Zfp280d, Serpinb6a, and Dnajb4 were the strongest comparable negative neighbors, all with |cosine|≤0.064 and no FDR-supported overlap with Cckar.
A flat NeuN+ postnatal brain signature should redirect, not deprioritize, CCK1R biology toward vagal-afferent, peripheral, ependymal, developmental, or ligand-evoked physiology.
Cckbr loss was transcriptionally flat in every measured neuronal class: 22/22 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Cckbr self-transcript had FDR 1 in each group.
The CCK ligand/paralog axis was also flat: perturbing Cck or Cckar yielded 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, despite significant Cck self-knockdown in three Cck groups.

Expected downstream programs were absent after Cckbr perturbation: opioid-system genes, Fos/Jun/Egr/Nr4a/Arc/Npas4 immediate-early genes, and Bmp7/Cxcl12/Nrp2 developmental candidates all had 0 FDR<0.10 hits.
Unbiased restricted-score neighbors of Cckbr were noncanonical and extremely weak: Kif1b was the top positive neighbor and Ndufs4 the top negative neighbor, with cosines of only +0.155 and -0.0936.

Direct Cckbr pathway relatives represented in the parquet did not phenocopy a receptor-loss program: Plcb1, Itpr1, Prkca, Adcy1, and Mapk1 were completely flat, while Prkcg, Camk2a, and Creb1 had only 3, 4, and 21 downstream hits in total.
Ccr2 acute loss-of-function produced a pan-measured neuronal null: none of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

The Ccr2 score vector had no substantive positive or negative perturbation neighbor; its strongest Pearson correlations were only +0.027 with Safe_target_20, +0.026 with Robo4, and -0.014 with Cfap69.
Represented chemokine-receptor comparators did not phenocopy Ccr2: Cx3cr1 was flat across its 23 tested groups and Cxcr4 produced only two isolated single-gene hits, with r≈0 to Ccr2.
The expected CCL2/CCR2 inflammatory-neuronal readouts were absent: Ccl2, Ccl7, Ccl8, Ccl12, Il1b, Stat3, Nfkb1, Rela, Fos, Jun, Isg15, and Cxcl10 all had minimum FDR=1.0 across Ccr2-perturbed groups.

Ccser1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group, and the represented mitotic comparators Cit, Kif11, and Nin were likewise flat in matched postmitotic groups.
Unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Ccser1 phenocopy: the strongest biological-gene correlations were only r=0.043 to Fbxo11 and r=-0.0205 to Uqcrc2.
The human FAM190A/CCSER1 cerebellar ADHD candidate signal was not recapitulated by acute Ccser1 loss in the recovered mouse cerebellar GABA group or in cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Cd14 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
Cd14 perturbation did not move the expected NF-kB, cytokine, TLR-adaptor, or TRIF/IRF transcriptional readouts in neurons.
The represented CD14/TLR/NF-kB pathway comparators Tlr4, Tlr2, Itgb2, Chuk, Map3k7, and Nfkb1 were jointly FDR-null in Cd14-matched neuronal groups.
Unbiased cross-target comparison found no stable positive or negative Cd14 signature neighbor.
Cd14 brain and druggability biology are displaced to microglial or systemic inflammatory compartments rather than direct juvenile neuronal loss of function.
Cd247 acute loss-of-function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The obvious TCR-CD3 complex comparators were also nearly silent: Cd3d and Cd3e had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Cd3g had only one isolated Sart1 hit.
Cd247 was uncoupled from the EphA4 and NMDA/AMPA/PSD95/CaMKII axes that the neuronal literature would nominate.
Cd247 had no robust data-driven signature neighbors; the top whole-surface score cosine was only 0.032 and safe-target controls appeared among the nearest neighbors.
Cd27 generated a single FDR-supported downstream event: Dffa was up in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Cd27 loss did not recover the canonical CD27-CD70/TRAF/NF-kB/JNK/survival transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group.
The full-score Cd27 signature had only tiny data-driven neighbors, and the top positive and negative neighbors failed phenocopy tests.
Represented TNFRSF and NF-kB/survival comparators converged on the Cd27 flat surface rather than producing a neuronal TNFRSF response.
A flat neuronal Cd27 surface should not be used to deprioritize CD27 immunology or CD27/CD70 drug programs.
Acute juvenile Cd2ap loss did not elicit a robust cell-autonomous nuclear RNA signature in any measured neuronal class.
Cd2ap perturbation was uncoupled from APP-processing, endocytic, actin, lysosomal, PI3K/MAPK, and synaptic-proteostasis mRNA programs.
The CD2AP-adjacent adaptor/APP perturbations were mostly flat, whereas Cltc generated 173 downstream genes in matched neuronal groups.
A pre-literature neighbor search found no robust Cd2ap transcriptional module.
The Alzheimer-risk biology of CD2AP is not reproduced as an acute postmitotic NeuN+ transcriptional response.
Cd36 loss of function produced no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The expected CD36 beta-amyloid/sterile-inflammatory module was absent from Cd36-edited neurons.
Broad hypothalamic Cd36 perturbation did not recover the VMH fatty-acid-sensing transcriptional changes reported after targeted VMH CD36 depletion.
Cd36 has no robust data-driven signature neighbor; its strongest whole-surface neighbors were extremely weak and did not share FDR genes.
Measured CD36 pathway relatives and lipid regulators also failed to phenocopy a neuronal CD36 program.
The screen argues against using resting neuronal snRNA-seq as a target-engagement biomarker for CD36-directed AD or stroke mechanisms.
Cd3d loss-of-function was transcriptionally silent across all 21 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
Related TCR/CD3 perturbations also lacked a shared neuronal module.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis placed Cd3d at the origin of the perturbation space rather than in a robust convergent or antagonistic module.
Cd3d-linked immunodeficiency biology is displaced to lymphoid development, not to the postnatal neuronal transcriptome sampled here.
Cd3e loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured postnatal NeuN+ neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa had no Cd3e rows and was not tested.

Canonical CD3-complex members represented in the parquet did not reveal a latent neuronal TCR module: Cd3d and Cd247 were entirely downstream-flat, Cd3g had only a single Sart1 call, and Fyn had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
direction_pattern: flat CD3 module with one isolated Cd3g-up Sart1 hit

canonical_summary: A published Cd247/CD3ζ retinal developmental role did not generalize to a shared Cd247/Cd3e postnatal brain transcriptional phenotype in this screen.
direction_pattern: retinal Cd247 precedent absent from measured brain snRNA-seq

canonical_summary: Cd3e had no informative data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor across the 1,773-label perturbation universe; the largest gene-target correlations were only approximately +/-0.036.

Cd3g is almost completely transcriptionally inert in the NeuN-enriched postnatal neuronal screen: 21 of 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the exception, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, had only Sart1 up-regulation.
The same-complex targets Cd3d, Cd3e, and Cd247 were also null in Cd3g-matched neuronal groups and did not reproduce Cd3g→Sart1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

The only corrected Cd3g downstream gene, Sart1, is an isolated U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP splicing factor signal in 054 CNU-MGE GABA; an exact universe scan found only Psmc1 as a same-direction robust Sart1 neighbor and no robust opposite neighbor.
Cd40 loss of function did not produce a corrected transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The Cd40 null is shared by measured core CD40-to-NF-kappaB pathway neighbors rather than being a Cd40-only anomaly.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful convergent or anti-convergent Cd40 neighbor.
The neuronal Cd40 null should not be read as a negative test of anti-CD40L therapy for neuroinflammation.
Cd46 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across all 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups; 054 CNU-MGE GABA had only a weak Ppm1h subthreshold feature and no FDR<0.10 genes.

The measured brain-neuronal surface did not couple Cd46 to a complement-activation transcriptome: Cd46 and the represented direct complement target C3 were both null, and four represented innate immune receptor targets were also null across their neuronal tests.

The unbiased score-neighbor search found no strong Cd46-like transcriptomic neighbor: the best positive correlation was Zfhx2 at r=0.0296 and the strongest negative non-safe correlation was Htr1f at r=-0.0136.

Human CD46-linked immune metabolic outputs were not recovered in Cd46-perturbed mouse neurons: Ifng, Il10, Slc2a1, Slc7a5, C3, C4b, Ddit3, Hspa5, Map1lc3a and Sqstm1 never reached FDR<0.10 in any measured Cd46 group.
Cd47 perturbation was self-transcript negative in all 19 recovered neuronal groups and FDR-significant on Cd47 itself in six, but every group had 0 non-Cd47 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Unbiased whole-surface signature comparison found no meaningful Cd47 transcriptomic neighbors; the top positive Stat1 and top negative Pola1 cosines were near zero and both comparator perturbations were trans-null.

Measurable Cd47-related immune, complement, phagocytic, and THBS1/integrin-neighborhood perturbations did not generate neuronal transcriptome phenocopies: C3, Cd36, Csf1r, Cx3cr1, Axl, Mertk, Itgb1, and Fyn all had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The Cd47 trans-null surface is not evidence that CD47/SIRPα blockade is neurologically inert, because the canonical therapeutic and CNS effects act through phagocytic partner cells and synapse engulfment rather than the edited neuron's nuclear RNA.
Cd4 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal group recovered for this target.
Cd4 did not sit inside a cryptic neuronal TCR/MHC module: related perturbations Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd247, Ptprc, H2-Eb1, and Fyn were flat in matched groups, and Cd3g had only one isolated Sart1 hit.

Unbiased signature correlation found only negligible Cd4 neighbors: Trp63 was the top positive neighbor at r=0.0268, Safe_target_15 the top negative overall at r=-0.0159, and Atp1a3 the top negative non-safe at r=-0.0125.
Cd79a loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.

The BCR/immunoreceptor neighborhood represented in the screen was also disconnected from neuronal transcription: Cd79b, Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd247, Fyn, Pik3cb, Pik3r1, Nfkb1, and Ptprc had zero downstream genes in their measured groups, while Cd3g, Rac1, and Sos1 had only one FDR<0.10 singleton each.

Cd79a is signature-isolated: the strongest whole-transcriptome raw-score neighbors were unrelated neuronal or signaling perturbations with absolute cosine similarity below 0.027 and zero shared FDR<0.10 genes.
The null de-risks only acute cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional effects of Cd79a loss; it cannot model CD79A immunodeficiency, B-cell malignancy, or myeloid tumor programs.
Cd79b loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any measured NeuN+ neuronal cell group.
The directly testable BCR-related perturbations phenocopied the lineage null: Cd79a, Fyn, Nfkb1, and Pik3r1 also lacked robust Cd79b-like neuronal signatures.
The data-nominated Cd79b signature neighbors were at the score-correlation noise floor rather than true convergent or anti-convergent modules.
The neuronal Cd79b null separates B-cell lymphoma CD79B biology from neuron-autonomous loss of function.
Cd80 loss of function was transcriptionally inert across all 21 measured NeuN-enriched neuronal cell groups: every group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Cd80 self row was FDR=1.0.

A full-rank cross-perturbation search did not nominate any meaningful Cd80-like or anti-Cd80-like transcriptomic module; the largest full-coverage positive neighbors were Il17rd, Agtrap, and Gnb5 with r=0.0258-0.0279, and the top negative neighbor, Mbd5, had r=-0.0220.

Represented immune co-signaling comparators Icos, Cd40, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9 also failed to phenocopy anything in the Cd80-matched neuronal groups, with 84 of 84 target-by-cell-group tests returning 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Microglial-lineage comparators Csf1r and Cx3cr1 were also flat in the same 21 Cd80-matched groups.
The same low-n single-nucleus Wilcoxon workflow detected a very broad Psmb4 perturbation while Cd80 stayed fully flat.
The dataset argues against a mature-neuron-autonomous transcriptomic mechanism for CD80/CD86-directed therapeutic biology in basal brain.
Cd81 loss lowered its own RNA broadly but produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
Cd81 perturbation selectively up-regulated the neural adhesion gene L1cam in Pvalb interneurons.
Cd81 perturbation selectively up-regulated Grsf1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut neurons.
Neuronal tetraspanin and CD81-web relatives did not reproduce the Cd81 L1cam or Grsf1 signature.
Unbiased Cd81 signature neighbors were near-zero and failed validation on the two response genes.
Canonical vesicle/surface and stress-adaptation transcriptional programs were not recovered after Cd81 perturbation.
The broad neuronal null surface refines Cd81 germline brain data toward glial/immune and membrane-localization mechanisms rather than acute neuronal transcription.

Cdc40 loss produced a sharply restricted postmitotic response: only 5 of 21 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 signature, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut plus 155 MB Glut carried the dominant response.
The broad Cdc40 responders remodeled a second layer of splicing and RNA-processing genes, with SR-related and RNA-binding genes generally down and selected spliceosome-associated genes up.
Pde4a was up in every FDR-significant Cdc40 cell group, and the broad signatures also induced Pde4b, Atf1, and Phactr3.
Cdc40 broad responders up-regulated ubiquitin-proteasome, lysosomal, and mitochondrial-quality-control genes.
Nuclear-pore, nuclear-envelope, chromatin, and general transcriptional genes were induced in the 151 and 155 broad signatures.
The broad Cdc40 state included down-regulation of synaptic and neuron-enriched transcripts.
Cdc40 induced only a partial p53/CHOP-like stress response rather than a wholesale apoptotic or unfolded-protein response.
Prpf6, U2af2, and Snrnp70 converged on the Cdc40 signature, whereas the represented Sm target Snrpb was essentially flat.
The noncanonical positive neighbors of Cdc40 were Tpr and the proteasome subunits Psmb4 and Psmc1.
Cdc40 had no strong inverse perturbation neighbor in the searchable universe.

Cdc42 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal class, even though its own mRNA was measured in every recovered group and was significantly reduced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The canonical Cdc42-Rho actin/spine program was transcriptionally silent: 43 actin, Rho-effector, and synaptic transcripts had zero FDR<0.10 calls across 903 Cdc42 gene-by-cell-class tests.
Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor represented Rho/Rac/Cdc42-axis relatives formed a shared Cdc42-like transcriptomic module.

The Cdc42 null surface should not be read as evidence against CDC42 neurodevelopmental disease or against D2R-linked striatal spine biology; those literatures depend on missense biochemical dysregulation, earlier development, defined D2R MSNs, disease state, or direct spine/LTP assays that are displaced from this screen.
Cdin1 loss produced a single FDR-supported downstream event, Pcdh10 down-regulation, restricted to 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Pcdh10 is a candidate marker of the sparse L5 ET Cdin1 response because no other target perturbation in that cell group made Pcdh10 significant at FDR<0.10.
Global Cdin1 signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated; neither the top positive nor top negative Wilcoxon-score neighbors formed a robust shared module.
The canonical CDIN1-Codanin1/ASF1, DNA-replication, erythroid, and stress programs were absent from P16 postmitotic neuronal Cdin1 loss-of-function.
Acute Cdk13 loss produced a real but strongly regionalized postmitotic-neuron response rather than a pan-neuronal Pol II-collapse signature.
direction_pattern: mixed; sparse in cortex and strongest in thalamic/midbrain/subcortical groups

canonical_summary: The most reproducible abundance marker of the Cdk13 state was an Amy1-up/Bend6-down/Rnpc3-up/Inha-down axis, not loss of the Cdk13 transcript itself.
direction_pattern: Amy1 and Rnpc3 up; Bend6 and Inha down

canonical_summary: Cdk13 converged more with Wac and the U1-spliceosome perturbation Snrnp70 than with the represented CDK-family target Cdk8.
The larger subcortical signatures coupled RNA-processing changes to repression of mitochondrial, centrosomal, and ciliary maintenance genes.
Postmitotic neuronal Cdk13 loss did not recover the proliferative CDK12/13 DNA-damage, G2/M, or Cdk5-axon expression programs predicted from dividing-cell and differentiation models.
The strongest Cdk13 anti-neighbors were not CDK12/13 pathway members and were supported by restricted anti-correlation rather than exact shared FDR genes.
Cdk8 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered neuronal groups despite measurable target rows and 28 to 192 perturbed nuclei per group.
Cdk8 did not converge with the β-catenin/Tcf7l2 thalamic program: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 shared 59 DE genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Cdk8 had zero DE genes and no Wnt-sentinel recovery.
Med13 and Med13l failed to phenocopy the Cdk8 null: Med13 had only 15 DE genes and Med13l only 2 across their surfaces, compared with 0 for Cdk8.
Cdk8 loss did not activate or repress IFN/JAK-STAT, NFkB, HIF1A/glycolytic, p53, or Wnt sentinel genes, and perturbations of Hif1a, Stat1, Stat3, Nfkb1, and Trp53 were also FDR-flat.
Data-driven Cdk8 signature neighbors were near-zero correlations; Dctn1, Drd4, Arhgef9, Ppargc1a, Dscam, and Smc1a were kept as measured comparators but rejected as substantive Cdk8 phenocopies.
Other transcriptional or chromatin regulators, including Brd4, Phf12, Chd8, and Med23, produced clear postmitotic DE signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Cdk8 remained flat.
Cdkal1 loss-of-function was almost transcriptionally silent in the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen, with only two downstream FDR<0.10 gene-cell-group events among 22 recovered cell groups.
The only significant MH-LH/TH glutamatergic response was Ggps1 induction.
The sole MB Glut Cdkal1 hit, Eef1a2, converged with Uba5 induction of Eef1a2 but not with the larger Uba5 program.
direction_pattern: Eef1a2 up in Cdkal1 and Uba5

canonical_summary: The beta-cell-like ER/ISR response predicted from severe Cdkal1-dependent mistranslation was absent from every measured neuronal group.
direction_pattern: expected ISR/UPR absent in Cdkal1; present after Elp1

canonical_summary: Represented tRNA-modification disease relatives did not phenocopy Cdkal1 in matched cell groups.
Cdkal1 had no robust whole-transcriptome signature neighbor.
Acute Cdkl5 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional signature in any recovered neuronal aggregate.
The one cell group with a statistically significant Cdkl5 self-transcript decrease, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, still had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Cdkl5 did not phenocopy Rett/DEE-neighbor perturbations that were detectable in the same matched cell groups.
Cdkl5 was transcriptionally uncoupled from NMDAR/BDNF-TrkB and AKT/GSK3/mTOR pathway perturbations that were readily measurable in the same analysis universe.
Whole-surface signature matching found no high-amplitude Cdkl5 convergence module.
Cdkn2a loss produced an ultra-sparse, cell-group-restricted response: a single up-regulated Lst1 hit in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.

The Cdkn2a perturbation did not derepress RB/E2F cell-cycle genes, suppress p53-effectors, or generate a coherent SASP-like module, and the directly measurable E2f1 and Trp53 perturbations were themselves flat.

The unbiased whole-surface neighborhood of Cdkn2a had no strong attractor: Mef2d was the top positive neighbor but had no downstream FDR<0.10 response, whereas Sin3a was the top negative neighbor and drove thousands of DE genes without reciprocal Lst1 regulation.

Acute Cdon loss of function was almost completely buffered in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons: 20 of 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the two responding groups each contained only one downregulated gene.
The expected canonical Hedgehog transcript program was absent after Cdon targeting and after direct perturbation of represented Ptch–Smo–Gli pathway relatives.
The neuronal null localizes known CDON forebrain and dopaminergic phenotypes away from P16 postmitotic maintenance and toward embryonic patterning, progenitor, or environmental-modifier windows.
The only Wnt/tankyrase-adjacent adjusted hit was borderline Rnf146 down in cerebellar GABA neurons, with no Axin2/Lef1/Tcf/Myc/Ccnd1 induction.
The data-driven robust-overlap search found no positive Cdon neighbor and only Psmc1/Psmb4 as exact anti-neighbors through Hcfc1 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Cebpe loss of function is pan-null across the 22 neuronal cell groups recovered for this target: every group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 41-213 perturbed nuclei per group.

The expected CEBPE-dependent granulocyte output module was silent in neurons: Card10, Ltf, Mmp9, Ngp, Hlx, Csf3r, Mpo, Elane, Ctsg, Prtn3, Lcn2, S100a8, S100a9, Cybb, Ncf1, Gfi1, Spi1, and Irf8 never reached FDR<0.10 under Cebpe perturbation.

Queryable myeloid pathway perturbations shared the same neuronal flatness: Spi1, Gfi1, Irf8, Csf3r, Csf1r, and Gata1 produced no FDR<0.10 genes in matched Cebpe groups, while Gfi1b produced only one isolated hit.

Data-driven Cebpe signature neighbors were numerical, not biological: the strongest Pearson correlations were only +0.052889 for Fbxo11 and -0.023915 for Wdr26; Fbxo11 itself had only one downstream hit, whereas Wdr26 generated 3128 FDR<0.10 genes in many of the same groups where Cebpe had zero.
Celsr2 loss in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons down-regulated the lysosomal GPCR-family gene Gpr137 as the only non-self FDR<0.10 hit.
Celsr2 loss in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons up-regulated Gtf2f1 as the only non-self FDR<0.10 hit.
Celsr2 produced a real but minimal response restricted to two cortical projection-neuron groups.
Celsr2 did not transcriptionally regulate the expected core PCP or synaptic/NMDA marker transcripts in any measured group.
Neither exploratory data-driven neighbors nor represented Wnt/Ror pathway relatives phenocopied the Celsr2 cortical signature.

Cep112 loss-of-function is a complete postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq null across the measured surface: 21 recovered neuronal groups, 21 target-expression tests with FDR=1.0, and zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Cep112 does not phenocopy GABAA receptor-subunit perturbation in any neuronal group, even though Gabrb2 and Gabrg2 perturbations generated sparse immediate-early or neuropeptide responses in matched thalamic, cortical, and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
The Cep112 perturbation lacks the Pol III/translation-stress-like output that appears when the Pol III factor Bdp1, and more weakly Polr3b, are directly perturbed.

Cep112 is consistent with a broader ciliary/centrosomal quiet class rather than with an active stress module: Ttc8, Cep120, Cep290, and Cep85l were also downstream-null in their recovered neuronal groups, and Bbs5 produced only a single Sirt5 hit.

Cep112 has no meaningful whole-universe signature neighbor: the strongest Wilcoxon-score correlations were Adam10 at r=0.0418 and Wdr26 at r=-0.0343, and the negative neighbor Wdr26 is a broad responder absent from Cep112.
Acute Cep120 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null rather than a ciliation, Hedgehog, ISR, UPR, proteostasis, or synaptic program.

Represented ciliary relatives did not converge on Cep120; most structural IFT/BBS/transition-zone perturbations were flat, whereas Mib1 alone generated a recurrent sterol-biosynthesis response absent from Cep120.
The raw whole-transcriptome Cep120 signature had no meaningful nearest neighbor or anti-neighbor in the visible perturbation universe.
Cep120-linked Joubert/Jeune ciliopathy biology is displaced from acute autonomous transcriptional failure in mature neurons toward developmental progenitor and cilium-structure mechanisms.
Cep290 loss produced no robust nuclear differential-expression program in any of the 20 assayed postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
The literature-obvious CEP290 transition-zone relatives did not phenocopy Cep290 as a shared transcriptomic module.
Expected ciliary GPCR, BBSome/IFT, and Hedgehog effector transcription was absent after Cep290 and nearly absent when the pathway components themselves were perturbed.
The pre-literature neighbor search nominated no coherent Cep290-like transcriptional state and found strong data-driven responders on both sides of the tiny Cep290 correlation spectrum.
Cep85l loss-of-function produced a pan-measured transcriptomic null in postnatal neurons: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered cell groups.
The expected CEP85L-CDK5/dynein/tubulin/Reelin migration network did not appear downstream of Cep85l perturbation, and represented migration or centrosome relatives did not phenocopy it.
A phenotype-first nearest-neighbor search found no hidden cross-perturbation module for Cep85l; the strongest full-rank score correlations were all |r|<0.05.
The screen gives no evidence for a late, cell-autonomous toxic transcriptome after Cep85l loss; the actionable disease biology remains the earlier centrosome/CDK5 migration event.
Acute postnatal Cert1 loss of function produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups.
The ER-stress, ISR, and mitochondrial-stress transcriptional outputs expected from severe CERT disruption were absent after Cert1 perturbation.
Neither data-driven score neighbors nor represented lipid-transfer comparators converged with Cert1.
Postnatal CRISPR loss of Cert1 does not phenocopy the gain-of-function CERT1 disease mechanism described for CerTra syndrome.
Cfap69 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The Cfap69 full-vector signature had no meaningful convergent or opposing neighbor; the strongest positive cosine was only 0.033 and a Safe_target label ranked second.
Represented primary-cilium transport targets likewise failed to elicit a shared IFT/BBSome transcriptional module in the Cfap69-matched neuronal groups.
Cfl2 produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were not tested.
155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA showed significant Cfl2 self-transcript decreases without any FDR-significant downstream gene.
Represented RAC1/CDC42-PAK-LIMK-cofilin pathway targets were nearly orthogonal to Cfl2 and lacked a shared Cfl2-like DE module.
Cfl2's strongest positive and negative transcriptome-wide neighbors had very small cosine magnitudes, from +0.0409 for Safe_target_81 to -0.0268 for Dstyk.
The Cfl2 LoF disease program was absent from postmitotic neuronal nuclei, while represented thin-filament or actin comparators Tpm1 and Tpm3 were also flat in Cfl2-matched groups.
Champ1 loss produced a near-flat postnatal neuronal transcriptome: 21 of 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream DE genes at FDR<0.10 and the only responding group had one FDR<0.10 gene.
Eid2 is a selective exploratory marker of the lone Champ1 responder, induced only in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

Represented CHAMP1-complex relatives did not phenocopy Champ1: Pogz was flat, while Setdb1 responded in other cell groups with a separable Tasor/Atf7ip/protocadherin-biased surface and no 027 Eid2 induction.

Unbiased full-profile search found no real Champ1 signature neighbor: the strongest positive and negative score correlations were only +0.03155 and -0.02251, and both comparator surfaces were FDR-flat.
Acute Chchd2 loss produced a 23-cell-group transcriptional null: all measured neuronal groups had zero non-target genes at FDR<0.10 despite directionally negative Chchd2 self-mRNA in every group.

Chchd2 did not induce the OMA1-DELE1-eIF2alpha mitochondrial ISR that is often expected from cristae stress; Atf3, Atf4, Ddit3, Chac1, Asns, one-carbon, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase sentinels were all absent at FDR<0.10, whereas Opa1 perturbation induced the same class of genes in overlapping groups.

Among represented literature-obvious mitochondrial and Parkinson comparators, Opa1 was a clear responder but Micos13, Ndufs2, Uqcrq, Snca, Yme1l1, Cox4i1, Tomm40, and Park7 were weak or flat; Chchd2 matched the buffered subset rather than the Opa1 mtISR state.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of the full Chchd2 score vector were all extremely low-amplitude and failed FDR overlap validation.
The postnatal mouse-neuron result supports a model in which CHCHD2-linked Parkinson risk is not reproduced by an acute, isolated juvenile loss-of-function transcriptome.
Acute postnatal Chd2 loss produced a sparse but real neuronal response in only five of 23 measured cell groups, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Snhg11 was the only transcript repressed at FDR<0.10 in every Chd2 responder group.
The two largest signatures share down-regulation of RNA-processing and spliceosome-associated transcripts.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut selectively down-regulated ion-channel and second-messenger genes after Chd2 perturbation.
The 151 TH response included an up-regulated membrane-trafficking and endolysosomal branch.
Bptf was the only data-driven nearest neighbor with a coherent same-direction overlap to Chd2.
Represented CHD-family genes Chd4, Chd7, and Chd8 did not phenocopy Chd2 in the matched responder groups.
BAF/PBAF chromatin-remodeler subunits showed heterogeneous thalamic activity but no Chd2-like signature.
Postnatal Chd2 perturbation did not recover the expected progenitor cell-cycle, cortical interneuron fate, immediate-early, ISR/UPR, or p53/DNA-damage transcriptional programs.
Acute Chd4 loss produced one broad response, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where 149 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10; every other effect was one to three genes.
The sparse non-thalamic Chd4 responders mostly appeared as weak echoes of the thalamic program, with Begain, Stxbp2, and Cacnb3 each recurring in 151 plus one additional cell group.
Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Chd4 loss up-regulated a channel and calcium/excitability branch including Cacng7, Kcnab3, Cacnb3, Cacna2d2, Kcnt1, Kcna2, Slc8a2 and Ache.
The 151 thalamic signature coupled Bcan/Ndst1/Chst1/B3galnt1 induction with reduced protocadherin-cluster transcripts, indicating cell-surface and extracellular-matrix remodeling.
A smaller 151 branch shifted metabolic and redox genes, with Pygm, Msra, Acss2, Ddo and Etnk2 up while Gss and Hsd17b4 were down, but canonical UPR/ISR or autophagy markers were absent.
The broad thalamic Chd4 response did not activate a p53-apoptosis signature: Trp53, Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bax and Bbc3 all had FDR=1.0, and Phlda3 was nominal only.
The data-driven Chd4 signature neighbor was Adnp, and Adnp and Huwe1 shared same-direction subsets of the 151 thalamic Chd4 program.

Measured NuRD-related perturbations did not phenocopy Chd4: Gatad2b was a restricted-signature neighbor but had zero downstream FDR genes in 151 despite a significant Gatad2b self-transcript drop, and Mbd2 was nearly flat.
BAF/PBAF perturbations fired in the same thalamic neurons but often inverted Chd4 genes, especially after Arid2, Arid1a, Smarce1 and Smarcc2 loss.
Chd4 up-regulated its NuRD ATPase paralog Chd3 in 151, yet Chd2 and Chd8 perturbations produced distinct signatures and Chd7 was almost inert.
Acute postnatal Chd7 loss produced only two robust downstream transcript changes across 23 neuronal cell groups: Ano8 up in 155 MB Glut and Nfyb up in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The rank-space Chd7 signature had no convincing positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
CHD-family perturbations Chd8, Chd2 and Chd4 responded where Chd7 was flat, with recurrent Pnisr or Snhg11/Begain-centered signatures and essentially zero overlap with Chd7.
The PBAF/SOX2/neural-stem-cell programs that are most obvious from the CHD7 literature were not recovered in the Chd7 neuronal DE surface.
direction_pattern: expected programs absent after Chd7 perturbation

canonical_summary: The retinoic-acid/pro-neural rescue axis reported for Chd7-deficient SVZ and inner-ear development did not appear after P16 neuronal Chd7 knockout.
direction_pattern: no RA/pro-neural induction or repression at FDR<0.10

canonical_summary: Acute postmitotic Chd8 loss was a restricted, subcortical-biased perturbation rather than a pan-neuronal transcriptional shock.
A recurrent PNISR/USP11/DUS3L-down module links the strongest Chd8 responders to RNA-processing and cotranscriptional regulation rather than to a Wnt-only program.
The thalamic and midbrain Chd8 signatures also carried an organellar and chromatin-maintenance arm.
Yy1 was the top data-driven positive neighbor of Chd8 and re-used the USP11/DUS3L/PNISR axis in the same subcortical groups.
The next Chd8-positive neighbors were proteasome, RNA-processing, or chromatin-corepressor perturbations, nominating a maintenance-state signature downstream of Chd8.
Setd1a and Zbtb7a opposed Chd8 even though they are transcription/chromatin regulators with broad neuronal signatures.
CHD paralogs, Wnt/beta-catenin targets, BAF components, and other ASD chromatin genes did not phenocopy Chd8 in the P16 neuronal assay.
The expected Wnt/p53/cell-cycle CHD8 program was not recovered after P16 neuronal perturbation.
P16 acute Chl1 loss produced a pan-neuronal downstream transcriptional null in every recovered cell group.
The obvious L1-family, NCAM/ankyrin, and semaphorin-receptor comparators fail to define a Chl1-like transcriptional module.
An unbiased cross-perturbation search places Chl1 in near-zero signature space, not in a hidden stress or organelle module.
The Chl1 screen result argues against an acute pan-neuronal toxicity transcriptome as the proximal correlate of CHL1 dosage neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
Chmp4b produced one corrected downstream change: Pip5k1c was down-regulated in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Chmp4b did not form a robust recurrent ESCRT/autophagy/cargo signature with either data-driven or literature-obvious comparators.
The P16 NeuN+ brain assay is orthogonal to the best-established CHMP4B disease context, autosomal-dominant cataract in lens.
Acute Chn1 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional negative: all 23 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The local EphA/semaphorin/Rac neighborhood also failed to form a transcriptomic module in this screen.
The LOF transcriptional null should not be read as evidence against CHN1 disease relevance because CHN1-linked Duane syndrome is driven by hyperactivating variants.
The data-driven Chn1 signature neighbors were near-zero cosine matches and were rejected as robust biological convergence.

Chrm2 loss was transcriptionally silent in every recovered neuronal class: 22 measured groups and 1,467 perturbed nuclei yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa had no Chrm2 rows and was not tested.
Chrm2 perturbation did not recruit an activity/EGR/immediate-early transcriptional module: Fos, Egr1-Egr4, Arc, Jun, Junb, Nr4a1, and Dusp1 were FDR-negative in all 22 measured groups.

Related muscarinic and proximal effector perturbations were also largely flat: Chrm3, Adcy1, Adcy5, Kcnj6, and Ache had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in Chrm2-matched groups, and Gnao1 had only one downstream gene, Puf60, in L4/5 IT cortex.

The Chrm2 null bounds disease and therapeutic interpretation: common human CHRM2 associations and mouse germline M2 behavioral phenotypes are not reproduced as a coding-LoF, juvenile, mosaic, cell-autonomous transcriptome in the recovered NeuN+ groups.

The unbiased neighbor search hit the noise floor: the top Chrm2 positive and negative score-vector neighbors were Fbxo11 with cosine +0.037177 and Wdr26 with cosine -0.026196, and neither produced a matched shared-direction Chrm2 DEG set.
Chrm3 loss of function produced a class-wide basal neuronal-transcriptome null rather than a cell-type-restricted FDR signature.
Chrm3 did not converge with the measured cholinergic/Gq/excitability targets Chrm2, Ache, Plcb1, Itpr1, Grm1, Grm5, Kcnq2, or Kcnq3.
The most correlated Chrm3 whole-surface neighbors were effectively noise-scale, and some of them had their own signatures that Chrm3 lacked.
The neuronal null should not be used as a pharmacodynamic marker for M3R remyelination or evoked cognitive and sleep biology.
Chrna1 produced a one-gene, FDR-supported Fgf9 induction restricted to 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.

The Chrna1-Fgf9 response did not converge with data-driven signature neighbors, same-complex muscle AChR subunits, neuronal nicotinic subunits, muscarinic receptors, or NMJ-organizing Lrp4/Musk perturbations.
Chrna1 lacked a broad postnatal neuronal transcriptional program despite 22 measured NeuN+ brain groups.
Acute postnatal Chrna2 loss is almost completely buffered transcriptionally across the recovered neuronal atlas.
Acap3 in L5-6 IT glutamatergic neurons and Dennd6b in midbrain glutamatergic neurons are the only Chrna2 downstream FDR calls, both weakly up-regulated singletons.
Nicotinic receptor relatives represented in the parquet do not phenocopy Chrna2 and do not converge on its two singleton DE genes.
Chrna2 weakly up-regulates Dennd6b where CTCF, nuclear-transport, and proteasome perturbations strongly repress Dennd6b in broad, stress-rich signatures.
Whole-transcriptome residualized signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Chrna2 neighbor.
The screen does not recover a CHRNA2 sleep-related-hypermotor-epilepsy-like expression program from simple acute loss of Chrna2.
Chrna3 loss is a pan-surface basal-transcriptome null in recovered postnatal central neurons.

The Chrna3-null surface confines this assay's informative negative result to broad young-adult CNS neurons, not to the α3-rich autonomic or ventral-habenular compartments that dominate the literature.
Represented nicotinic-receptor-family perturbations and Ache do not converge on a Chrna3-like transcriptional response.
An unbiased whole-universe neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Chrna3 signature neighbor.
Chrna4 has a single robust downstream response, Cyp46a1 down-regulation, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The one Chrna4 responder lacked a cholinergic-subunit compensation or immediate-early activity program.
Chrnb2 and other represented nicotinic relatives did not phenocopy the Chrna4 thalamic Cyp46a1 response.
Cyp46a1 is a recurrent 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptomic sentinel across unrelated perturbations, with Chrna4 among weaker Cyp46a1-down regulators.
Chrna4 has no strong global DE-signature neighbor or anti-neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Chrna6 loss of function produced a pan-measured transcriptional null: 21 measured neuronal groups and 1,113 perturbed nuclei yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Chrna6 had no meaningful attractor in the model-visible perturbation space: the strongest signed-score correlations were only +0.0307 to -0.0208.

Represented nicotinic-receptor relatives did not phenocopy Chrna6: Chrnb2 and Chrnb3 were completely flat, Chrna3 and Chrna7 were completely flat, and Chrna4 produced only a different one-gene thalamic response.

The measured null should not be read as absence of CHRNA6 nicotine-addiction or Parkinsonian biology, because the canonical MB Dopa group was not tested and dopamine/synaptic marker genes were not perturbed in the off-canonical groups.
Chrna7 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
Postnatal Chrna7 loss did not recruit the transcript programs most expected from α7 Ca2+ signaling or hippocampal inhibitory-circuit literature.
The literature-obvious cholinergic receptor relatives represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Chrna7.
The unbiased Chrna7 full-score neighbors were essentially zero-correlation hits rather than a hidden convergent module.
The screen does not support a persistent post-P16, cell-autonomous neuronal RNA program as the proximal transcriptomic mechanism of CHRNA7-linked 15q13.3 disease.
Chrnb1 perturbation produced an almost fully buffered neuronal transcriptomic surface, with only Rnf227 up in 053 Sst Gaba and Nova1 up in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA at FDR<0.10.
direction_pattern: two isolated up-regulated genes against a flat background

canonical_summary: Chrnb1 did not phenocopy represented muscle AChR subunits, represented neuronal nicotinic subunits, or the represented NMJ-associated targets Musk, Lrp4, and Ache in any matched neuronal group.
direction_pattern: no shared-direction FDR overlap with Chrnb1

canonical_summary: The top pre-literature Chrnb1 signature neighbors were low-cosine and failed a return-to-data FDR-overlap check.
direction_pattern: weak positive and negative restricted-score cosines, rejected by FDR overlap

canonical_summary: Chrnb2 perturbation was a self-transcript event, not a downstream transcriptome event: even the three groups with FDR-significant Chrnb2 mRNA depletion had zero non-Chrnb2 genes at FDR<0.10, and the same zero held in every other measured group.

The literature-obvious nAChR relatives did not converge with Chrnb2 on the basal transcriptome: Chrna2 and Chrna4 produced only isolated one-gene hits, Chrna3, Chrna6, Chrna7, and Chrnb3 were flat, and every shared-direction overlap with Chrnb2 was zero.

The full perturbation universe did not nominate a meaningful Chrnb2 module: the strongest positive gene-target correlation was Klc1 at r=0.0279 and the strongest negative gene-target correlation was Ogt at r=-0.0138.

The silent LoF transcriptome does not contradict CHRNB2 epilepsy genetics because the human syndrome is a nicotinic-channel disorder caused by heterozygous receptor-subunit variants, not evidence that removing beta2 from P16 mouse neurons should launch a cell-autonomous mRNA program.

A druggable alpha4beta2 receptor can be transcriptionally invisible: Chrnb2 and its direct alpha4 partner lacked a shared DE signature even though alpha4beta2 pharmacology is sufficient for a smoking-cessation drug concept.
Chrnb3 had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 21 recovered cell groups, no FDR-supported on-target mRNA depletion, and no weak near-threshold group.
The α6β2β3 nicotinic-receptor relatives that were represented as perturbations did not phenocopy Chrnb3 at the mRNA level.
The addiction-linked Chrnb3 biology is displaced toward dopamine and habenular nicotine-response physiology rather than a broad resting transcriptional state.
A pre-literature full-universe search produced only near-zero Chrnb3 signature neighbors.
Chrnd loss produced a nearly silent juvenile mouse-brain neuronal transcriptome: 20 of 21 measured cell groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 and the only responder contained one FDR 0.085 gene.
The sole Chrnd FDR<0.10 downstream hit was Ghitm down-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
Represented muscle AChR/NMJ perturbations were flat or orthogonal to Chrnd rather than convergent.
Neuronal nicotinic-receptor alpha/beta subunit perturbations did not converge with Chrnd.
Unsupervised whole-transcriptome neighbors of Chrnd had cosine similarities below 0.03 in magnitude and no shared FDR<0.10 genes.
Chrne loss of function produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any of the 23 measured postmitotic brain-neuron groups.
The muscle AChR structural subunit genes Chrna1, Chrnb1, Chrnd, and Chrng did not phenocopy Chrne in matched brain-neuron groups.
Central neuronal nicotinic receptor subunit perturbations were also non-convergent with Chrne.
Data-driven signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Chrne neighbor.
AChR turnover and clustering-pathway neighbors Ache, Musk, and Lrp4 were essentially flat in the same neuronal screen.
Chrng loss-of-function produced a pan-measured neuronal null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered brain neuronal cell groups, while 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.

The expected nicotinic-receptor relatives also failed to form a shared Chrng-like module: represented Chrn subunits and the NMJ-associated targets Ache, Lrp4, and Musk had Chrng correlations between -0.0034 and 0.0250 and zero shared FDR<0.10 genes.

Unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbors of Chrng were background-like rather than a hidden biological module: the top positive score-vector correlation was Safe_target_39 at r=0.0313 and the strongest anticorrelation was Safe_target_80 at r=-0.0184.
Acute Chuk loss in the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic neuronal assay produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
A canonical NF-κB feedback/inflammatory/survival transcript panel was completely absent from the Chuk DE surface.
NF-κB relatives represented in the parquet—Nfkb1, Rel, Traf3, and Tnfrsf1a—also had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the Chuk-matched neuronal surface.
Genome-wide score correlations identified only noise-level Chuk neighbors; the strongest non-control positive neighbor had r=0.0329 and the strongest negative neighbor had r=-0.0168.
The zero neuronal surface separates CHUK developmental disease biology from basal juvenile neuronal maintenance.
Cic loss produced one dominant neuronal transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a secondary L4-5 IT cortical response, and only very sparse single-gene/two-gene responses elsewhere.
Atxn1 was the nearest measured signature neighbor of Cic and cleanly phenocopied the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c module.
The direct PEA3/MAPK-feedback output of CIC was present but not the dominant 151 signature.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c neurons, Cic loss depressed subtype and excitatory-synaptic machinery while inducing secretory and lipid/ER-associated transcripts.
The cortical IT response was a small, same-direction echo of the thalamic program rather than an independent ETV-only program.
Small midbrain and posterior responders reused individual genes from the 151/L4-5 response, especially Pafah1b3 and Hsd17b12.
The measured RTK/MAPK positive branch did not phenocopy Cic loss in 151.

Beyond Atxn1, the top Cic neighbors were lower-confidence mixed stress/transcriptional signatures, and the strongest anti-neighbors were mostly restricted-score anticorrelations rather than robust opposite programs.
Acute Cisd2 loss produced a single robust downstream change, Mcfd2 up-regulation, only in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA neurons.
Cisd2 knockdown did not trigger the UPR/ISR, Beclin-autophagy, lysosomal, Fe-S, or respiratory-chain transcriptional programs expected from complete chronic CISD2 loss.
Direct BCL2/IP3R/autophagy and mitochondrial-Fe-S comparator perturbations represented in the parquet did not phenocopy the Cisd2 Mcfd2 response.
Cisd2 had only very weak all-transcriptome signature neighbors, and the highest-ranked positive and negative neighbors failed to reproduce Mcfd2 induction in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Cit loss-of-function produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any recovered P37-P44 neuronal cell group after P16 sparse AAV-CRISPR delivery.
The expected cytokinesis-failure stress axis was absent: canonical p53/apoptosis, ISR/UPR, and cell-cycle marker genes all remained FDR=1.0 in every Cit cell group.
Represented Rho-family and actin/abscission relatives did not phenocopy Cit: Cdc42, Rac1, Limk1, Pak1-3, Diaph2, Chmp4b, and Mrtfa all had near-zero full-score cosine to Cit.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of the complete Cit signature were extremely weak: the top positive score cosine was only 0.034 and the strongest negative cosine was -0.024.
The postmitotic neuronal null should not be interpreted as developmental safety for partial CITK inhibition.
Clcn3 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal group: 19 of 19 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected lysosomal-autophagy, ISR/UPR, and synaptic-marker transcript programs were absent after Clcn3 perturbation.
Whole-universe signature matching found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptional neighbor for Clcn3.
The literature-obvious vesicular chloride/proton exchanger comparator Clcn4 also failed to generate a downstream signature, whereas Cltc produced 173 FDR<0.10 genes in matched groups.
The screen argues against using acute sparse Clcn3 LoF in healthy postmitotic neurons as a direct proxy for CLCN3 neurodevelopmental disease alleles.
Acute postmitotic Clcn4 CRISPR loss caused no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
Endosomal Cl-/H+ exchange and V-ATPase relatives fail to form a Clcn4-like transcriptomic module in the same screen.
The developmental synaptic/dendritic RNA program expected from Clcn4 KD/KO models was not recovered in mature perturbed neurons.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Clcn4 partner.
Acute Clcn4 snRNA-seq provides no robust transcriptomic reversal signature for ClC-4-directed phenotypic rescue.
The flat CRISPR-LoF surface is consistent with patient missense alleles acting through mechanisms not reproduced by simple Clcn4 nulls.
Clec16a produced a narrow two-gene response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Sod2 up and Lrrtm1 down.
The strongest data-driven Clec16a neighbors were proteasome subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4, and both shared the Lrrtm1-down component of the 151 thalamic signature.
Canonical autophagy, autophagosome, retromer/HOPS, and mTOR comparators did not phenocopy the Clec16a two-gene thalamic response.
Clec16a did not induce the ISG15/interferon or ER-stress transcriptional programs reported in whole-body neurodegenerative Clec16a knockout settings.

The closest neuronal transcriptional convergence with Clec16a came from proteasome perturbations, making broad ubiquitin/proteasome manipulation a liability rather than a clean substitute for restoring CLEC16A mitophagy.
Clock loss depressed a tiny canonical circadian-output module dominated by Nr1d2, Dbp, Tef, and Per3 in six subcortical or pineal-containing neuronal bins.

Clock was robust in only 6 of 22 measured cell groups, with the largest multi-gene responses in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut and no FDR response in cortical, hippocampal, or cerebellar bins.

Bmal1 was the strongest positive Clock signature neighbor and reproduced eight Clock FDR entries, but it was also broader, including Clock-flat L4/5 IT CTX, L2/3 ENT/PPP/RSP, CNU-HYa HY MM, and MH-LH TH groups.

Represented feedback-loop relatives did not phenocopy Clock: Cry1 was nearly flat, Cry2 gave only a small 151 TH response, Nr1d1/Nr1d2 and Rora were dominated by thalamic or accessory-loop programs, and Rorb/Rorc were flat.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 converged on the Clock-repressed Dbp/Nr1d2/Per3 subset, especially in 155 MB Glut, but on top of thousands of non-clock DE genes.
The strongest negative data-driven neighbors, Uba5 and Rnpc3, opposed Clock only through one Dbp edge or showed mixed Dbp/Tef behavior rather than a coherent inverse clock signature.
Hhatl was the only noncanonical Clock FDR gene, increasing in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and recurring with Bmal1 and Nr1d1 in the same bin.
Clpp produced a single robust transcriptional hit: Rbm45 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Clpp loss was globally buffered at the nuclear snRNA-seq level.
The lone Clpp response was not a generic ClpXP-complex signature.
Other mitochondrial proteostasis and Perrault-related perturbations were sparse and did not converge with Clpp.
Unbiased signature search found no strong positive or negative neighbor for Clpp.
The neuronal P16 Clpp null refines Perrault biology toward chronic, recessive, protein/mtDNA, or unsampled-lineage mechanisms rather than an acute pan-neuronal UPRmt transcriptome.
Clpx CRISPR produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.

The Clpx signature did not converge with represented mitochondrial protease targets: same-complex Clpp was almost flat, Yme1l1 was flat, Afg3l2 had only one Cdh7 hit, and Lonp1 alone produced a small Ddit3/Herpud1-positive stress response.
Expected CLPX-associated heme, UPRmt/ISR, and respiratory genes were not induced or repressed at FDR<0.10 after Clpx loss in juvenile neurons.
Postnatal Cltc loss of function was transcriptomically selective rather than universal: 8 measured neuronal groups responded and 10 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Several Cltc responders down-regulated synaptic-vesicle, receptor, and excitability genes, including Snap25/Rph3a/Gria3 in L4/5 IT neurons, Gabrd/Gabrb2/Slc6a1/Sv2a/Scn1a in Pvalb interneurons, Unc13a/Gria4/Scn8a in hypothalamic GABAergic neurons, and Rph3a/Vamp1/Snap25/Stxbp1/Scn8a in midbrain glutamate neurons.

Subcortical responders activated an AP-1/ISR-like stress axis together with ER and lysosomal genes: Jun or Jund was induced in Pvalb, hypothalamic GABA, thalamic, midbrain glutamate, and cerebellar GABA groups; Ddit3, Derl1, Srxn1, Ctsb, Psap, Hrk, or Bcl2l11 marked the stronger GABAergic and midbrain/cerebellar responses.
Stmn4 was the most recurrent positive Cltc marker, induced in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.

The Cltc response included endolysosomal and receptor-traffic compensation: Rab15 and Tfrc were induced in Pvalb cells, Ctsb/Psap in 066 hypothalamic GABA cells, and Gaa/Atp6ap2/Clcn3 in 155 MB Glut, alongside repeated Atp8b2 induction.

Cltc converged most strongly with proteasome perturbations: Psmb4 and Psmc1 were the top two score-cosine neighbors and shared 112/117 and 77/80 significant Cltc gene-by-cell hits in the same direction.

Canonical synaptic endocytosis and uncoating targets did not phenocopy Cltc: Hspa8 produced 14 FDR<0.10 genes with no overlap, while Dnm1 and Synj1 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the Cltc-matched surface; the stronger synaptic neighbor was Stxbp1, an exocytic vesicle-fusion gene, with 10 same-sign overlaps.

A postmitotic Cltc LoF signature couples synaptic down-regulation to Jun/Ddit3/Hrk/Bcl2l11 stress and only partially models human CLTC dosage disease, whose severe presentations may include dominant-negative missense or in-frame variants.
The only BH-significant Cnksr2 downstream event was a borderline Atp5b/Atp5f1b increase in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
Cnksr2 loss was broadly transcriptionally buffered across juvenile postmitotic neurons.
Cnksr2 did not phenocopy its postsynaptic-density scaffold neighbors Dlg4, Magi2, Lrrc7, Tnik, or Shank3.
RAF/MAPK/Rap-pathway targets represented in the screen were also nearly orthogonal to Cnksr2.
The empirical nearest neighbors of Cnksr2 were tiny-cosine, null-like signatures rather than a coherent biological module.
Cnnm2 produced exactly one robust downstream call, Clk1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with no multi-gene splicing or stress program.

Across the complete Cnnm2 surface, postnatal neuronal loss of Cnnm2 was transcriptionally buffered: all 23 groups retained weak, non-significant Cnnm2 mRNA changes and only one group had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The only represented canonical PACT/magnesium comparator, Trpm7, converged with Cnnm2 on an almost-null transcriptomic surface rather than on a shared Mg-stress response.

Neither the global nor the 151-restricted score vector nominated a meaningful Cnnm2 co-response module; even the rank-1 neighbors had tiny cosine similarities and did not reproduce the Cnnm2 Clk1 call.

Cnot1 produced a sparse, postnatal neuronal RNA phenotype: eight downstream DE genes in 155 MB Glut, one borderline gene in 308 CB GABA, and zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 15 other measured groups.
The robust MB Glut response was mostly down-regulatory and contained secretory, lysosomal, trans-Golgi, ER/neurite, and extracellular-remodeling transcripts rather than a broad accumulation of mRNAs.
Psmc1 and Psmb4, not CCR4-NOT subunits, were the strongest positive Cnot1 signature neighbors and recapitulated most of the MB Glut eight-gene signature in the same directions.

Measured miRISC/TNRC6 and 5-prime-to-3-prime decay comparators failed to phenocopy Cnot1: Ago1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b and Xrn1 made zero FDR<0.10 calls on the nine Cnot1 significant gene-by-cell pairs.
The strongest numerical inverse neighbors, Hivep3 and Dmbt1, were extremely weak and had no opposite-sign FDR<0.10 recurrence on the Cnot1 signature.
The 308 CB GABA response consisted only of Slc25a37 down-regulation at the FDR threshold.
Canonical CNOT1-loss stress outputs were absent: Atg7, Atg5, Bbc3, Ddit3, Atf4, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Xbp1, Eif2ak3, Casp4, Casp12 and Trp53 were tested in every measured group and never reached FDR<0.10.
Cnr1 loss of function produced a nearly completely buffered snRNA-seq surface, with only Srcap up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut surviving FDR<0.10.
The predicted activity-dependent, MAPK, cAMP/PKA, Ca2+-channel, and GIRK response genes were absent from the Cnr1 FDR-level surface.
Represented Gi/o, cAMP/PKA, Ca2+-channel, GIRK, and mGluR5 pathway-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Cnr1.

The data-driven Cnr1 neighbors were Acp1/Tcf20/Pah in the positive direction and Frrs1l/Dennd5a/Washc4 in the negative direction, but all alignments were tiny and almost completely lacked FDR-level overlap.
The flat neuronal nuclear surface is not evidence that central CB1 blockade is biologically safe or inert.
Cntnap1 loss produced a pan-surface transcriptionally buffered phenotype in postmitotic neuronal nuclei: every recovered group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected paranodal/juxtaparanodal neighborhood was measurable but did not phenocopy Cntnap1: Cntnap2, Kcna1, Kcna2, Kcnab2, Nrcam, Nrxn1 and Ank2 all had near-zero whole-surface correlations to Cntnap1 and only isolated or absent FDR-significant genes.
Cntnap1 had no strong data-driven transcriptional neighbor in the full perturbation universe: the best positive and negative score correlations were only +0.036 and -0.031.
Cntnap2 perturbation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut produced one strong downstream event, decreased Rbfox2.
Cntnap2 perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut weakly decreased the KATP regulatory subunit Abcc8.
Cntnap2 did not transcriptionally converge with Cntnap1, Kcna1, Kcna2, or Kcnab2 despite their structural relationship to the CASPR2/Kv1 juxtaparanodal complex.
Five null groups showed significant Cntnap2 self-transcript decreases but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The shape of the two-gene Cntnap2 signature was private across the visible perturbation universe.
Coa8 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured NeuN+ neuronal groups after P16 AAV-CRISPR perturbation.
The canonical mitochondrial ISR/OXPHOS stress signature was expected but absent after Coa8 targeting, even though the same dataset recovered it after Opa1 targeting.
The represented complex-IV assembly neighbor Cox11 matched Coa8 by being completely flat in the same 23 neuronal groups.
Mitochondrial annotations were not sufficient to predict a transcriptomic response: Opa1 was broad, Coa8, Mff, Lrpprc, Ndufs4, and Ndufb9 were flat, and Slc25a46 produced only one downstream hit.
A phenotype-first whole-signature search found no strong Coa8 convergent or anti-convergent module.
The flat Coa8 neuronal transcriptome should not be interpreted as evidence that COA8 inhibition is biologically safe.
Cog4 produced a pan-null steady-state snRNA profile across all 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Cog5 and Stx5a, the represented COG/SNARE relatives of Cog4, failed to converge with Cog4 and produced only singleton FDR<0.10 responses.
The unbiased model-visible perturbation universe contained no strong positive or negative Cog4 transcriptomic neighbor.
Cog4 did not induce a Golgi/ER stress or proteostasis transcriptional rebound, although the same assay detected ISR/proteostasis genes after proteasome perturbation.

Cog5 produced a two-cell-class DNA-maintenance-biased response: Smarcal1 was induced in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Helq was induced in 155 MB Glut, each as the only FDR<0.10 Cog5 downstream gene in its cell group.

Cog5 did not recover a PERK/UPR/ISR transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group, even though the same assay recovered strong Hspa5, Ddit3, Asns, Herpud1, Xbp1, Atf4, Pdia6 and Chac1 induction after Gfpt1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: UPR absent after Cog5; UPR up after Gfpt1

canonical_summary: The only represented same-complex target, Cog4, was flat, and represented Golgi/glycosylation neighbors split into distinct surfaces rather than phenocopying Cog5: Gfpt1 was broad, Vps54 and Vps35 were thalamus-biased, Dpm1/Vps53/Stx5a/Stx16 were sparse, and Tmem165 was flat.

Unbiased whole-surface neighbor search found no strong Cog5-like module: the best positive score cosine was Ryr3 at 0.0283 and the strongest inverse biological cosine was Pdgfrb at -0.0157; direct lookup failed to recover any same-direction Smarcal1/Helq overlap in those neighbors.
Col11a1 CRISPR loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any measured postnatal NeuN+ brain neuronal group.
The directly represented cartilage/ECM relatives of Col11a1 also failed to generate a recurring neuronal ECM signature.
The expected Col11a1→Mmp3/Pax1 chondrocyte remodeling response was absent from the neuronal DE surface.
Nominal top-rank neighbors of Col11a1 were rejected as real convergent perturbations by FDR-level retesting.

Postnatal Col2a1 loss was essentially flat in NeuN-enriched mouse neurons: only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 23 cell groups and the assayed UPR/chondrocyte-ECM marker sets were completely absent.
The entire FDR-level Col2a1 response reduced to two non-recurrent singleton genes: Gal3st3 was up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Abi1 was down in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.

The cartilage-collagen and chondrocyte-regulator comparators represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Col2a1: Col11a1 and Runx2 were flat, Sox9 and Sox5 produced only off-context singleton or doublet signatures, and none reproduced Gal3st3 or Abi1 at FDR<0.10.

Score-vector neighbors failed as biological convergers: the top positive cosine to Col2a1 was only 0.03497 and the top named negative cosine was -0.02013, with no FDR-level overlap or opposition on Gal3st3 and Abi1.

Acute Comt perturbation was buffered at the neuronal nuclear transcriptome: Comt was reduced in every measured group and significantly self-depleted in four groups, yet no measured group had even one non-Comt gene at FDR<0.10.
Comt had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor; the largest positive correlation in the universe was only Ehmt1 at r=0.029 and the strongest non-safe anticorrelation was Fbxo11 at r=-0.0107.

Dopamine and adrenergic receptor perturbations that were represented in the screen did not phenocopy Comt; Drd2, Drd4, Drd5, Adra1a, Adra2a, Adra2b, Adrb2 and Adrb3 had correlations of only 0.0044-0.0274 with Comt and only four total downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their matched receptor surfaces.
Copa perturbation produced a strict whole-transcriptome null in every recovered neuronal class.
The COPA-syndrome ER-stress and STING/type-I-IFN outputs were absent after neuronal Copa CRISPR, although ER-stress transcripts were detectable in the same screen.
The nearest data-driven Copa neighbors were weak rank-order correlations, not biological phenocopies.
The literature-obvious same-coatomer comparator Copg1 was also nearly flat and did not expose a hidden COPI-like transcriptional state.
The neuronal Copa null should not be read as a negative STING/JAK therapeutic result for COPA syndrome.
Copg1 loss exposed a single CNU-HYa/HY GABA response: Ndrg4 was induced while the Copg1 transcript was reduced.
Postnatal neuronal Copg1 perturbation did not recover canonical COPI failure programs: ER-stress/UPR/ISR genes and cGAS-STING/type-I-IFN genes were flat across the measured taxonomy.
The only measured same-coatomer comparator, Copa, did not converge with Copg1.
Multiple high-count groups had a significant Copg1 self-transcript decrease but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The whole-surface Copg1 signature had only tiny non-COPI neighbors, and both positive and negative data-driven comparators were rejected as robust Copg1 phenocopies.
Coq5 loss produced a pan-neuronal buffered transcriptomic surface: 22 measured neuronal groups all had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected mitochondrial ISR/UPR letters-of-fire did not appear after Coq5 perturbation even though the same pipeline detected Atf4/Ddit3/Herpud1/Shmt2-class stress genes after other perturbations.

Neither unbiased nor literature-obvious perturbations phenocopied Coq5: all score-space neighbors were essentially zero-correlation, and UQCRC/CYC1/NDUF/LONP1/CLPP comparators also had r≈0 against Coq5.
Coq5 did not yield an snRNA-seq pharmacodynamic marker for CoQ-biosynthesis failure.
Cox11 CRISPR targeting did not provoke a corrected neuronal transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured groups.
Represented complex-IV relatives did not phenocopy Cox11 with a shared cytochrome-c-oxidase transcriptomic signature.
Cox11 had no robust convergent or divergent neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Cox4i1 was a pan-neuronal downstream-null target: every one of the 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon hits at FDR<0.10.
Cox4i1 loss failed to induce either an OXPHOS-rewiring program or a Cox4i2 isoform-switch program.
Represented complex-IV subunits and a COX pathway neighbor converged with Cox4i1 mainly by being flat, not by sharing a positive downstream module.
Cox4i1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor anywhere in the model-visible target universe.
The P16 sparse-neuronal Cox4i1 null does not reproduce a recessive COX4I1 disease state at the nuclear-transcriptome level.
Cox5a mRNA fell in every measured neuronal group but no group produced a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Directly measured complex-IV and nearby respiratory-chain perturbations did not converge on a shared mitochondrial transcriptional module.
Cox5a loss did not induce the expected ATF4/ISR, UPRmt, redox, autophagy, mitophagy, or TPI-response transcripts.
The unbiased Cox5a signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor: residual correlations across the queryable universe were near zero.
Cox6a1 loss-of-function produced no corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Cox6a1 did not activate a detectable ATF4/ISR, UPRmt, mitokine, or redox transcriptional program.
Represented Complex-IV structural and assembly comparators were almost as downstream-null as Cox6a1, with no coherent same-complex signature overlap.
The unbiased score-space neighbor search found only negligible positive and negative neighbors for Cox6a1.
The Cox6a1 central-neuron null does not phenocopy the human COX6A1 peripheral neuropathy link.
Cox7b produced a single corrected downstream hit, Eepd1 up-regulation, restricted to 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
Eepd1 is an exploratory DNA-maintenance candidate downstream of Cox7b perturbation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
Represented Complex-IV comparators failed to phenocopy Cox7b.
Cox7b loss was uncoupled from the expected ISR, UPRmt, mitophagy, and OXPHOS-compensation mRNA programs.
Cox7b had no meaningful whole-signature neighbor in the target universe.
Cox8a loss nominated a single NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut marker, Smurf2, rather than a broad mitochondrial module.
Cox8a perturbation was uncoupled from canonical mitochondrial-stress transcription.
Measured Complex-IV relatives did not phenocopy Cox8a.
Cox8a belongs to a dataset-wide class of acutely buffered nuclear respiratory-chain perturbations.
No hidden genome-wide signature neighbor emerged for Cox8a.
Cpe produced a single corrected downstream transcriptomic response: Aff3 was up-regulated in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, while the other 21 measured groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Canonical CPE-proximal peptide-processing transcripts and candidate secondary UPR/ISR/autophagy markers were not transcriptionally mobilized by Cpe loss in any measured neuronal group.

Cpe did not sit in a recovered cross-perturbation module: the strongest data-driven score-cosines were only about ±0.03, and the literature-obvious represented comparators Pcsk2 and Pcsk5 did not share the Cpe/Aff3 response.
The obesity, endocrine, and cognitive phenotypes of lifelong CPE deficiency were not accompanied here by a broad postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq signature after sparse Cpe CRISPR perturbation.
Cplane1 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 DE in any of 22 measured neuronal cell groups, despite a negative self-transcript trend and one on-target FDR hit in 155 MB Glut.

Ciliary, Hedgehog, and PCP transcript sentinels stayed silent under Cplane1: Gli1, Gli2, Ptch1, Smo, IFT/transition-zone genes, and represented FZD/PCP genes all had FDR=1.0 wherever tested in the Cplane1 surface.

Represented structural-cilia, Joubert, Hedgehog, and PCP neighbors did not converge with Cplane1; all score correlations were near zero and FDR hits in those comparators were sparse or restricted signatures with zero Cplane1 overlap.
Whole-surface data-driven neighbors of Cplane1 had almost zero score-vector correlations and did not define a recoverable biological module.
Cplx1 perturbation produced a single downstream hit, Rbfox1 down-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Cplx1 targeting was broadly buffered at the nuclear transcriptome: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene despite negative Cplx1 self logFC in every measured group.
The measured paralog Cplx2 was as transcriptionally silent as Cplx1 and did not phenocopy via a shared downstream signature.
Stxbp1/Munc18-1, unlike Cplx1, produced a broad downstream response in the same assay and in several Cplx1-null groups.
Cplx1 loss did not trigger a canonical activity-dependent immediate-early gene response.
Cplx1 had no strong data-driven transcriptomic neighbor in the full model-visible perturbation universe.
Acute mosaic Cplx2 CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups despite Cplx2 being assayed in each group.

The measured Cplx1 paralog did not reveal a hidden complexin transcriptional module: Cplx1 and Cplx2 score profiles were essentially uncorrelated and Cplx1 yielded only one downstream FDR hit outside its own transcript.
Most measurable presynaptic vesicle or active-zone comparators also lacked broad secondary transcriptional phenotypes and did not converge with Cplx2.
The flat Cplx2 surface is target-position-specific, not a global inability to detect synaptic perturbations: Stxbp1 and Grin1 produced 140 and 131 matched-group downstream DE genes, respectively.
Unbiased score-vector neighbors did not nominate a Cplx2 biology: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were only +0.0287 and -0.0183.
Cpt1c loss produced only two isolated responder classes: Mfn2 up in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Cnnm2 down in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
