Cpt1c transcript reduction was often measurable but was transcriptionally buffered downstream in the postmitotic juvenile screen.
Mfn2 up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut is a single-gene cortical organelle-contact candidate after Cpt1c loss.
Cpt1c loss decreased Cnnm2 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, nominating Mg2+/divalent-cation handling as an unexpected hypothalamic singleton.
Cpt1c did not phenocopy represented AMPAR, sphingolipid/lipid, or HSP/axon-transport comparators.
Cpt1c did not trigger a detectable ISR/UPR or mitochondrial-stress module, whereas Opa1 did in the same analysis universe.
Cr2 loss produced a two-gene, two-cell-class response rather than a broad neuronal complement response.
Map1lc3a is a cell-restricted autophagosome marker decreased by Cr2 perturbation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Cnep1r1 is a single nuclear-envelope/lipid-homeostasis candidate decreased by Cr2 perturbation in 308 CB GABA.
Represented complement-pathway and CD21-coreceptor perturbations do not phenocopy Cr2 in neuronal nuclei.
The top restricted-signature Cr2 neighbors were only nominal and were rejected as robust convergent or opposing phenocopies.
Healthy postmitotic neuronal Cr2 loss does not recreate the inflammatory or progenitor Cr2 biology reported in adult neurogenesis and brain-injury settings.
Crbn loss was nearly inert on the postnatal neuronal nuclear transcriptome and did not elicit UPR, autophagy, proteasome, AMPK, BK-channel, or core excitatory-synaptic mRNA programs.
The only FDR<0.10 downstream Crbn DEG was Psip1 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Crbn had no strong positive or negative whole-surface neighbor in the measurable target universe.
CRL4/DCAF, IMiD-neosubstrate, BK, AMPK, CaMKII, and AMPA-receptor comparators represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Crbn in L5 ET neurons.
The neuronal LoF signature warns against treating simple Crbn deletion as a proxy for CRBN-engaging glues or PROTACs.
Creb1 loss induced the paralog Crem in five subcortical responder groups.
The quantitatively broadest Creb1 response was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and was mostly a down-regulated ER/lipid/lysosomal/heme/membrane module plus Crem induction.
155 MB Glut mounted a separate four-gene response with Crem and Mmab up and Camk2b and Pgk1 down.
052 Pvalb Gaba showed an isolated down-regulation of Slc22a17.
The strongest data-driven positive neighbors of Creb1 were the proteasome subunit perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1.
Huwe1 and Zbtb7a opposed the thalamic Creb1 landmark directions.
Represented PKA, CBP/p300, TrkB, CaMK and MAPK pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Creb1.
Creb1 loss did not recover a basal Bdnf/Fos/Arc/Npas4 immediate-early program.
Crebbp produced a real FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 16 downstream genes, versus 0 in the seven other recovered groups.

The down arm of the thalamic Crebbp response preferentially hit neuronal membrane, ion-channel, neurite, and neuronal-splicing state genes, including Kcnq2, Kcnc2, Scn1b, Dgkz, Rtn4rl1, Nrn1, Stmn4, Rbfox2, Kctd17, and Ccdc141.
Crebbp induced a small regulatory rebound in the thalamic responder, with Srcap, Ddx17, Srsf11, and Leng8 increased alongside isolated Stxbp2 and Cfap298 up-regulation.
Basal Crebbp loss did not recover canonical CREB or immediate-early genes: Fos, Arc, Bdnf, Npas4, Nr4a1, Egr1, Jun, and Junb all failed FDR correction across the recovered groups.
The literature-obvious KAT3 paralog Ep300 and the canonical CREB-pathway factor Creb1 did not phenocopy Crebbp in the matched thalamic signature.
Psmb4 and Uba5 were the top same-direction thalamic neighbors of Crebbp, each sharing 8 of the 16 Crebbp genes at FDR<0.10.
Cic and Zmynd8 formed the strongest reverse Crebbp neighbors in the thalamic signature, opposing Stxbp2 and selected channel-state genes.
Brd4 had a broad thalamic response but only a partial Crebbp-like submodule: Leng8, Dgkz, and Rbfox2 matched Crebbp, while Scn1b moved in the opposite direction.
Crhr1-targeting loss-of-function guides produced only one FDR<0.10 downstream RNA hit: Dnajc13 was up-regulated in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB glutamatergic neurons.
The ligand-evoked CRHR1 cAMP/PKA/CREB immediate-early program was absent after basal Crhr1 loss-of-function.
Measured cAMP/PKA/CREB perturbations did not phenocopy Crhr1 either in 027 neurons or across the Crhr1-matched surface.
Unbiased whole-surface signature search found no strong positive or negative Crhr1 module.
Crlf1 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal null: 22 of 22 recovered Crlf1 cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Crlf1 perturbation did not induce or repress canonical CLCF1/CNTFR-gp130/JAK-STAT, MAPK, PI3K-AKT, survival, or immediate-early sentinel transcripts in any measured neuronal group.
Represented same-network perturbations, Il6st, Stat3, Il6ra, Sorl1 and Sort1, were also null or single-gene weak responders and had near-zero score correlation with Crlf1.
Crlf1's top data-driven neighbors were not biologically coherent signatures: the strongest positive and negative whole-profile correlations were only r=0.0309 and r=-0.0147.

The Crisponi/cold-induced sweating and oxidative-stress-neuroprotection priors are displaced from the assayed state: postmitotic Crlf1 loss did not perturb surviving CNS neuronal nuclei, and the midbrain dopaminergic group was not recovered for Crlf1.
Crppa produced no downstream FDR<0.10 gene in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation.
Represented α-dystroglycan and dystrophin-glycoprotein relatives did not phenocopy Crppa or converge into a shared transcriptomic module in this neuronal screen.
The top data-driven Crppa signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated and biologically unrelated.
The P16 Crppa null should not be used to infer that postnatal therapies would reverse embryonic dystroglycanopathy brain malformations.
Crppa did not trigger an ATF4/ISR, UPR, or proteostasis rebound that would have been transcriptionally visible.
Crx loss of function was a complete FDR-level null across the 22 recovered brain cell groups: no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any measured group.
The expected CRX output genes for rod/cone phototransduction and pineal melatonin synthesis were measured but absent: 0/328 photoreceptor tests and 0/206 pineal-gene tests passed FDR<0.10.

Literature-obvious retinal comparators represented in the parquet did not reveal a hidden CRX-like module: Otx2, Neurod1, Nr2e3, Opn1sw, Pax6, Rxrg and Thrb were flat, while Rax, Rorb, Rho, Sox2 and Vsx2 produced only one- or two-gene outliers across all tested groups.
The data-driven Crx signature neighbors were mathematically nearest but biologically non-convergent: the strongest positive score cosine was only 0.0335 and the strongest negative was -0.0321.
Cry1 produced a single robust downstream response: Per2 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The Cry1 response uncoupled Per2 from the broader core-clock output program.
Clock-loop relatives were active in the Cry1 responder group but did not phenocopy Cry1.
FDR-level data-driven neighbors converged or diverged with Cry1 only through Per2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Per2 de-repression is a plausible reciprocal biomarker of CRY1 loss, but it is not a pan-neuronal CRY1 biomarker in this dataset.
Postnatal mosaic Cry1 loss was transcriptionally buffered in 21 of 22 measured neuronal groups.
Cry2 loss produced a compact circadian-output response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Nr1d1 and Dbp were both significantly down-regulated.
Cry2 down-regulated Rabggtb in 191 MB P MY GABA as a one-gene, noncanonical response.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cry2 loss moved Dbp and Nr1d1 in the same direction as Bmal1 and Clock loss rather than the opposite direction expected from simple CRY derepression.
Cry1 did not phenocopy Cry2: in the Cry2-responsive thalamic class Cry1 perturbation produced only Per2 up-regulation, and its whole-surface score-cosine to Cry2 was 0.00639.
Cry2 was effectively neighborless at the full-surface level: its nearest biological score-cosine neighbor was Nrg3 at 0.0368 and the strongest negative neighbor was Setd2 at -0.0265.
Across 20 measured non-effect or weak classes, Cry2 failed to drive a robust Per/Cry/Rev-erb/Dbp clock-gene program after P16 perturbation.
Sparse P16 Csf1r loss of function produced a pan-neuronal robust zero: every recovered neuronal class had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The represented microglial CSF1R-axis comparators were also flat in the same neuronal readout.
Csf1r did not phenocopy its represented type-III receptor tyrosine kinase relatives in neurons.
The model-visible ranked-signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Csf1r neighbor.
The neuronal null cannot be used to de-risk CSF1R inhibition in the CNS.
Csf3r loss of function produced an empty FDR<0.10 downstream signature in every recovered postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal group.
The expected CSF3R-to-JAK/STAT/SOCS transcriptional footprint was absent, not merely the Csf3r transcript itself.
Literature-obvious cytokine-receptor and myeloid comparators represented in the parquet did not reveal a hidden Csf3r-like module.
The screen does not support interpreting neuronal Csf3r loss as a model of CSF3R-mutant myeloid neoplasia or severe congenital neutropenia.
Acute postmitotic Csmd1 loss was transcriptionally silent in every tested neuronal group: 22/22 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Csmd1 perturbation did not recruit the expected complement, microglial-engulfment, core synaptic-marker, or CSMD-family compensation transcripts, and the directly testable C3 perturbation was itself flat.

Unbiased signature comparison failed to find a convincing Csmd1 transcriptional neighbor: the best positive and negative biological targets all had |r|<=0.0356 and were rejected on direct surface inspection.
The null separates acute P16 neuronal Csmd1 loss from the early neuroepithelial and extracellular synapse-pruning mechanisms implicated by human CSMD1 loss and mouse germline studies.
Csnk2b loss produced an adjusted snRNA response only in a caudal/diencephalic subset—110, 151, 155, 191, and 217—while 17 other recovered neuronal groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
A recurrent cytoskeletal/neurite-remodeling module appeared in caudal responders, led by Stmn4 down in four cell groups and Carmil3 up in three.
Csnk2b engaged an RNA-processing/minor-spliceosome program, especially Rnpc3/Zranb2/Pabpn1-family decreases, and the top positive data-driven neighbors were Rnpc3 and Thoc1 perturbations.
P/MY/pineal glutamatergic neurons mounted a mitochondrial and metabolic rebound with glycolytic, aminotransferase, oxidative-phosphorylation, proteasome, and redox genes up.
Synaptic vesicle and secretory-transcript remodeling was recovered in 217 and 191, including Dnm1 up in both and Snap25, Slc17a6, Stxbp1, Syt7, App, and Rtn3 in one of the two groups.

The MB/P/MY GABA response combined ER/sterol genes Insig1, Fdft1, Tecr, Tmx2, Rtn3, App, and Bag6 with the shared cytoskeletal module; Dctn1 perturbation was a weaker positive neighbor that shared several sterol-response genes.
Canonical Wnt/β-catenin transcription was expected from CSNK2B variant studies but was essentially absent after Csnk2b CRISPR LoF; Ctnnb1 did not phenocopy the caudal Csnk2b surface.
Col4a1 was the only adjusted gene in 110 and recurred with Col4a2 in 191, nominating a low-confidence collagen/basement-membrane-like readout at the edge of the Csnk2b response.
Wdr26, Tbcd, and Caml were the strongest negative restricted-signature neighbors, with Wdr26 inverting 11 Csnk2b FDR gene-cell entries in the same caudal modules.
All five responder groups had a flat Csnk2b self-transcript despite 1 to 55 adjusted downstream genes.

Cspg4 loss of function produced a panel-wide neuronal transcriptional null: 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.
Neither the unbiased score-neighbor search nor direct tests of represented NG2-lineage comparators uncovered a hidden Cspg4-like neuronal module.

The mouse neuronal null is more consistent with CSPG4 disease mechanisms that require OPC protein trafficking, myelination, or glia-to-neuron signaling than with an acute cell-autonomous transcriptional defect in postmitotic neurons.
Cspp1 produced one borderline, FDR-supported transcriptomic change: Usp49 was up-regulated only in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The canonical cilium/Hedgehog transcriptional module was absent after postnatal Cspp1 perturbation.
Represented ciliopathy-family perturbations did not phenocopy the Cspp1 Pvalb Usp49 signature.
No strong genome-wide transcriptomic neighbor was found for Cspp1 in the model-visible perturbation universe.
A classical CSPP1 ciliopathy did not manifest as a maintenance transcriptopathy in juvenile, postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.
Csrnp3 produced a one-gene FDR response: Rab3ip was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and no other measured group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Postnatal single-gene Csrnp3 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across nearly the entire recovered neuronal surface.
Csrnp3 did not phenocopy indirect Wnt/β-catenin or TGFβ/SMAD comparators in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
Whole-signature neighbor analysis rejected both positive and negative Csrnp3 neighbors as robust convergent modules.
Cst3 loss produced one focal downstream signature, restricted to 145 MH-LH TH Glut and consisting of down-regulated Atp10a and Tmed4.
Cst3 knockout did not induce a detectable cathepsin, lysosome, autophagy, UPR/ISR, or apoptosis transcriptome in any measured neuronal group.
Neither the empirical Cst3 rank-vector neighbors nor the represented literature neighbors phenocopied the Cst3 response.
The Cst3 LoF screen refines disease expectations by separating acute neuronal loss from chronic, extracellular, amyloidogenic CST3 protein biology.
Acute P16 Cstf2 loss of function produced no FDR-supported gene-abundance response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The P16 LoF screen did not recapitulate the Cstf2 D50A brain APA examples at total mRNA abundance: Rbm24, Copg1, Cbln1, Nrxn1, Cntnap2, Shank2, Fmr1, and Cacng4 all had minimum FDR 1.0.
Cstf2 perturbation did not trigger Cstf1, Cstf2t, or Cstf3 mRNA compensation across the 23 neuronal classes.

Cstf2's data-driven neighbor surface was near null: the top positive neighbors had score cosines near zero and 0-1 downstream hits, while negative neighbors Psmb4 and Psmc1 were broad proteasome responders with thousands of DE genes.

Ctbp1 loss evoked a narrow, all-up membrane-trafficking and polarity-like module in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, with 8 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only Stxbp2 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Zeb1 was the top same-direction neighbor of Ctbp1 and reproduced 7 of the 9 significant Ctbp1 group-gene entries in the two responder thalamic groups.
The related CtBP-binding transcription factor Zeb2 did not phenocopy Ctbp1 in the Ctbp1-responder groups.

Ctbp1 self-transcript knockdown was decoupled from downstream output: two groups had significant Ctbp1 mRNA reduction with zero downstream DE genes, whereas the strongest 151 response occurred with only subthreshold Ctbp1 self-FDR.
The Ctbp1 perturbation did not recover canonical CtBP-linked apoptosis, mitochondrial pyruvate-carrier, or neuronal activity immediate-early programs at FDR<0.10.
The top negative sparse neighbors, Phf12, Smarcc2, and Cic, inverted selected Ctbp1 thalamic signature genes, especially Stxbp2, F11r, Mal2, and Arap2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Ctcf produced a highly skewed postnatal neuronal RNA response, with 92.2% of all downstream FDR<0.10 rows concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
Ctcf loss repressed a clustered protocadherin program in thalamic and midbrain neurons: 48 Pcdh-cluster rows were significant and 47 were down.
A Zcwpw2-up / Dennd6b-down fingerprint, accompanied by down-regulation of endomembrane-associated genes such as Abhd14b and Rabggta, recurred across compact and broad Ctcf responders.
Cohesin-machinery perturbations represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Ctcf: Smc1a and Stag2 yielded small 151-only signatures, Stag1 only one gene, and Pds5a/Hdac8 none.
Bptf was the strongest compact positive signature neighbor of Ctcf, sharing 32 same-direction versus 3 opposite significant Ctcf-feature rows.
Yy1 was a broad chromatin-looping comparator that diverged from Ctcf, with 1663 significant rows in Ctcf-measured groups but only a 40 same-direction / 28 opposite overlap on Ctcf features.

Broad data-driven neighbors and anti-neighbors were rejected as Ctcf-specific mechanisms: Uba5, Tpr, and Cic had mixed overlaps, Rnpc3, Camta1, and Prpf6 skewed opposite, and Cox4i1 had no robust DE overlap.
Ctnna2 produced a single robust downstream hit, Cdk17 up-regulation, only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The expected cadherin-catenin, Arp2/3-actin, and Lef1/Wnt transcript set was absent after Ctnna2 loss.

Ctnna2 did not phenocopy represented catenin-family comparators: Ctnna3 was completely flat, Ctnnd2 had only Elfn2 in 155 MB Glut, and Ctnnb1 produced a large thalamic/hypothalamic signature where Ctnna2 was null.
Ctnna2 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in the directly queryable universe.
The two largest Ctnna2 self-transcript decreases were subthreshold and did not propagate to downstream DE.
Ctnna3 produced no cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional response in any measured cell group.
Ctnna3 loss did not activate a Wnt/β-catenin target program, whereas Ctnnb1 loss generated a strong thalamic Wnt-linked response.
The represented neuronal catenin relatives Ctnna2 and Ctnnd2 also failed to produce a broad transcriptional phenocopy.
Genome-wide rank-neighbor analysis found only near-zero Ctnna3 signature neighbors.
Acute Ctnnb1 loss was not pan-neuronal: robust downstream DE appeared only in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with the thalamic 151 class carrying almost all signal.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recovered a canonical Wnt feedback loss with Axin2, Lef1, Nkd1, Notum, Wnt9b, Vangl1 and Prickle1 reduced while selected receptor/ligand transcripts rose.
Ctnnb1 loss depressed a thalamic excitability and synaptic-identity module, including Gabra4, Gabrb2, Gabrd, Chrna4, Grin2b, Slc17a7, Kcnc2, Kcnj3, Atp2b1 and Atp2a2.
Ctnnb1 loss rewired adhesion, guidance and extracellular-matrix transcripts in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with L1cam, Cdh2, Epha4, Ptprm/Ptprj/Ptprz1, Slitrk6, Spock3 and Adamts19 mostly down.
The 151 response reweighted Ras/Rho/PKC/cAMP signaling rather than uniformly suppressing it: Plekhg1, Rasgrp1, Tiam1, Rgs4, Prkcd, Prkcg and Adcy1 were down, while Mapk9 and Rasgrp2 rose.
Secretory-granule, neuropeptide-processing and calcium-control transcripts were remodeled in 151, with Chgb and Scg2 up but Pcsk2, Cpe, Scg5, Vgf, Ramp3, Atp2b1 and Atp2a2 down.
Within represented Wnt/catenin relatives, Lrp6 and Tcf7l2 converged with Ctnnb1 but Lrp5, Gsk3b, Fzd2/Fzd4/Fzd6/Fzd9, Lgr4, Gpc6, Ctnna2, Ctnna3 and Ctnnd2 did not.
The strongest non-Wnt positive neighbors of the Ctnnb1 thalamic signature were Rab7, Gfpt1, Psmb4 and Dhdds, each sharing the downshift of many Ctnnb1 excitability/adhesion genes.
The strongest anti-neighbors were Sgce, Camta1, Dnajc13, Cacnb2 and Ptprm; among them, Camta1 robustly flipped nine Ctnnb1-signature genes in 151.
The CTNNB1-NDD-relevant postnatal neuronal liability exposed here is thalamic Wnt/excitability/adhesion loss, not broad cortical transcriptional collapse.

Ctnnbl1 produced a real but extremely sparse postnatal neuronal-response surface: Paxbp1 up in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Arhgef1 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Unc13a up in 155 MB Glut were the only downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected catastrophic spliceosome response was buffered or absent after P16 Ctnnbl1 perturbation.
Ctnnbl1 intersected a glutamatergic RNA-processing vulnerability module through same-direction Arhgef1 and Unc13a regulation shared with Tardbp, Rnpc3, and Hnrnpu.
Prpf6 moved the Ctnnbl1 midbrain marker in the opposite direction, down-regulating Unc13a where Ctnnbl1 up-regulated it.
Hspa8, the only other represented curated PRP19-CDC5L component, did not phenocopy Ctnnbl1.
Ctnnbl1 did not behave like beta-, alpha-, or delta-catenin perturbations despite its catenin-like name.
Unc13a up-regulation marks the Ctnnbl1 response in 155 MB Glut and points to a presynaptic vesicle-priming compensation hypothesis.
Arhgef1 up-regulation marks the most statistically robust Ctnnbl1 responder class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Paxbp1 up-regulation is a Ctnnbl1-specific marker in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

Ctnnd2 loss produced a strongly buffered juvenile neuronal nuclear-transcriptome phenotype: 22 of 23 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 155 MB Glut had a single downstream hit.
Elfn2 was the only FDR<0.10 downstream gene induced by Ctnnd2, rising in 155 MB Glut.
The Ctnnd2 autophagy/dendrite literature was not recapitulated as transcriptional induction of core autophagy-lysosome genes.

The classical catenin comparators did not phenocopy Ctnnd2: α-catenin targets were flat or one-gene weak, whereas Ctnnb1 elicited hundreds of DE genes in thalamic glutamatergic neurons where Ctnnd2 had zero downstream genes.
Represented Rho-family, PDZ-scaffold, and postsynaptic-disease targets failed to converge strongly with Ctnnd2.
All-universe signature search found no strong positive or negative Ctnnd2 transcriptomic neighbor.
The flat juvenile neuronal mRNA surface argues that CTNND2 neurodevelopmental genetics should not be interpreted as a simple persistent cell-wide transcriptional deficiency in postmitotic neurons.
Ctsb formed a target-only perturbation surface: every recovered neuronal group had zero non-self downstream genes at FDR<0.10 although Ctsb mRNA itself was reduced in 17 of 22 groups.
Loss of Ctsb failed to induce a canonical lysosomal/autophagy/CLEAR or generic stress response: none of 946 measured expected sentinel rows reached FDR<0.10.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not uncover a hidden Ctsb-like module; several sampled comparators responded where Ctsb was flat, while APP-adjacent comparators were co-null.
The basal neuronal Ctsb knockout signature does not reproduce amyloid-processing or inflammasome biology that motivates CTSB modulation in disease models.
Cux1 was transcriptionally buffered across all 22 measured neuronal groups: no group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The literature-predicted Cux1 dendrite and firing arms did not appear: Cdkn1b, Rhoa, and Kcna1/Kcna2/Kcna3 were all FDR=1.0 in the Cux1 surface.
The expected paralog Cux2 did not reveal a hidden Cux-family juvenile RNA module; Cux2 had only one significant downstream gene and a Cux1 score correlation of 0.0039.
Whole-universe score correlations found no robust positive or inverse Cux1 neighbor; the strongest biological correlations were Pou3f4 r=0.0314 and Epha4 r=-0.0190.
Cortical TF comparators separated from Cux1: Tbr1 produced 28 FDR-significant genes where Cux1 had none, whereas Satb2 and Bcl11b were flat.
PI3K and OGG1-linked CUX1 tumor/DNA-repair programs were absent from Cux1-perturbed neurons: Pik3ip1, Pik3r1, Akt1, Mtor, and Ogg1 were all FDR-negative.
Cux2 loss produced a single robust downstream event, Sun1 up-regulation, and it was restricted to 053 Sst Gaba.
Cux2 mRNA itself was significantly reduced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but the downstream signature was still completely buffered.
Cux2 was flat with Cux1, Satb2, Bcl11b, and Foxp2, but Tbr1 retained a cortical projection-neuron TF signature in the same analysis universe.
The data-driven Cux2 signature neighbors did not survive FDR retesting as a convergent module.
Sparse P16 Cux2 loss did not reproduce the entorhinal-hippocampal or upper-layer cortical programs implicated by CUX2 epilepsy literature.
Cx3cr1 loss produced a pan-neuronal zero: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the Cx3cr1 receptor transcript itself was not a tested expression feature.

The measured CX3CL1 processing axis did not converge with Cx3cr1: neuronal Cx3cl1 mRNA was unchanged after Cx3cr1 perturbation, and the represented sheddase target Adam10 had 0 FDR<0.10 genes in its 9 measured neuronal groups.

Other represented neuroimmune targets were also nearly flat in NeuN-positive neurons: Ccr2, Il10ra, Irf5, and P2ry14 had no FDR<0.10 genes, while P2ry12 and Cxcr4 produced only isolated one-gene effects.

All data-driven Cx3cr1 signature neighbors were noise-level, with Adam10 the top positive score neighbor at r=0.0323 and Wdr26 the top negative score neighbor at r=-0.0134 despite Wdr26 producing 3,130 FDR<0.10 genes.
The neuronal null should not be read as evidence that CX3CR1 antagonism is transcriptionally silent in the CNS, because the responsive receptor-positive microglial compartment was largely excluded.
Cxcr4 produced a sparse two-island neuronal response: Zgpat was down in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Pum1 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in each cell group.
The canonical CXCL12/CXCR4/ACKR3 neurodevelopmental marker axis was not transcriptionally recovered after postnatal Cxcr4 perturbation.
Across all model-visible perturbations, Cxcr4 sat near a global transcriptional null: its strongest signed-score neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations below 0.027.
Represented chemokine/Rac-arm comparators did not converge with Cxcr4: Ccr2 and Tiam1 were null in all matched groups, and Rac1 produced a Ranbp1-only Sst response where Cxcr4 was flat.

The sparse NeuN+ Cxcr4 signature is a poor negative predictor for systemic CXCR4 antagonism, because the major hematopoietic and stromal compartments that define plerixafor biology were not part of this neuron-enriched screen.
Cyc1 loss produced exactly one robust downstream transcript, Gnb1, and only in 155 MB Glut.
Cyc1 transcript depletion did not recruit a detectable ATF4/ISR, UPRmt/chaperone, redox, HIF-glycolytic, or OXPHOS-compensatory transcriptional program.
Represented complex-III relatives did not phenocopy Cyc1: Uqcrfs1, Uqcrb, Uqcrq, and Ttc19 had isolated private hits, while Uqcrc2 and Uqcrh were downstream-null.
Cyc1 had no strong positive or negative whole-transcriptome signature neighbor across the represented perturbation universe.

Cyfip1 loss was transcriptionally buffered in all 23 measured neuronal cell groups: every group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, even though Cyfip1 itself was measured in every group and reached a target-transcript FDR of 0.0948 in 155 MB Glut.
A Tsc2 mTORC1-adjacent transcriptional program was strongly detectable in this same analysis universe, but Cyfip1 did not trigger it in any matched group.
The literature-obvious FMRP/CYFIP relatives did not form a robust shared acute neuronal transcriptomic module: Cyfip2 and Fxr1 had zero downstream hits, and Fmr1 had one singleton Slc25a27 hit.

Cyfip1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor: the top whole-surface correlations were only r=0.0338 to H4c11, r=0.0334 to Il1rapl1, r=0.0329 to Smo, r=-0.0327 to Fbxo11, r=-0.0290 to Npy1r, and r=-0.0210 to Zfp949.
Cyfip2 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal nuclear-transcriptome null: every recovered group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected WRC-Arp2/3 and FMRP/eIF4E neighborhood was transcriptionally uncoupled from Cyfip2 loss.
Directly measured canonical relatives, especially Cyfip1 and Fmr1, were also near-null rather than hidden strong Cyfip2 phenocopies.
The full-surface data-driven neighborhood had no meaningful Cyfip2 signature neighbors.
A simple sparse LoF signature did not resemble the severe human CYFIP2 missense mechanism.
Cyfip2 loss did not trigger a detectable neuronal stress, UPR/ISR, autophagy-lysosome, proteasome, or redox bounce-back program.
Cyld loss produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Cyld did not phenocopy basal NF-κB/TNF/TLR/JNK or Wnt pathway comparators; direct Ctnnb1 loss was thalamically active where Cyld was flat.
Neuronal CYLD biology is likely post-translational or allele-specific in this window rather than a broad stress, UPR, NF-κB, or autophagy RNA program.
Across the full model-visible target universe, Cyld had only near-zero positive and negative score-space neighbors.
D630045J12Rik produced a one-gene, thalamus-restricted transcriptional response: Kcnf1 was down-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 TH D630045J12Rik response is uncoupled from the Braf/Map2k1/Ntrk2 ERK-output module measured in the same cell class.
No robust cross-perturbation signature neighbor exists for D630045J12Rik in the model-visible universe.
The neuronal loss-of-function surface separates wild-type D630045J12Rik from the two main human KIAA1549 disease contexts: photoreceptor cilia and KIAA1549::BRAF glioma fusions.
Dab1 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 sparse CRISPR.
The measured Reelin core, Reln-Vldlr-Lrp8-Fyn, converged with Dab1 on a flat juvenile snRNA phenotype.
Matched Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b and Tsc2 perturbations generated many FDR genes where Dab1 and core Reelin perturbations were flat.
De-novo Dab1 score-neighbor analysis yielded only noise-scale correlations and no canonical Reelin-pathway neighbors.
Dach1 loss produced a single robust downstream transcript, Ppdpf, confined to 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
Dach1 had no strong positive or negative whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in the complete parquet.
RDGN- and TGF/SMAD-adjacent perturbations did not phenocopy the Dach1 CA3 Ppdpf response.
The proliferative DACH1-loss program seen in cancer and kidney models was absent from juvenile postmitotic neurons.
Dag1 loss of function produced a global FDR-defined null across the recovered neuronal screen: 0 downstream genes in 22 measured cell groups.
Measured DGC, dystroglycan-glycosylation and neurexin relatives failed to phenocopy the Dag1 null surface.
Known CCK/CB1R forebrain and cerebellar inhibitory-synapse phenotypes did not reappear as nuclear marker-gene responses after P16 Dag1 editing.
De novo signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptional neighbor for Dag1.
Dap3 loss-of-function was recovered in every neuronal cell group but produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any group.
Dap3 did not activate the ISR-like mitochondrial-stress module that was readily detected after Opa1 perturbation.
The death-receptor arm of DAP3 biology was silent in unchallenged juvenile neurons.
A Perrault-spectrum mitoribosome disease phenotype was not phenocopied by acute sparse Dap3 editing in sampled brain neurons.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Dap3 transcriptional neighbor.
Acute Dcaf8 targeting produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal groups.
155 MB Glut showed the only significant fall in the Dcaf8 mRNA itself, yet still had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Whole-universe signature search did not identify a meaningful Dcaf8 transcriptomic neighbor; the top positive and negative biological cosines were only +0.034 to -0.021 and the nominated targets did not share FDR-significant genes with Dcaf8.
Directly measurable CRL4/chromatin comparators did not phenocopy Dcaf8: Ddb2 and Dnmt3a were flat, while Setdb1 had a narrow protocadherin/Atf7ip/Tasor response with essentially zero cosine to Dcaf8.
The DCAF8-linked giant-axonal-neuropathy axis left no robust CNS neurofilament, proteasome, heat-shock, ISR or autophagy transcript footprint after acute Dcaf8 targeting.

Acute sparse Dcc loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups; the only weak group, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, stopped at minimum downstream FDR 0.190674.

Dcc perturbation also failed to transcriptionally mobilize obvious netrin, Slit/Robo and Rho/PAK/Src pathway genes, and the measurable receptor-family comparators were themselves almost completely flat in the same cell groups.

The Dcc null surface in P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neurons points disease-relevant loss toward wiring anatomy, electrophysiology or unsampled dopamine axons rather than an acute pan-neuronal stress or fate program.

The data-driven signature-neighbor search nominated only weak, non-guidance neighbors: Itga2 and Rab27a on the positive side, and Tpm3 and Tpk1 on the negative side, all with absolute cosine <=0.211 and no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in matched groups.
Dctn1 perturbation recurrently upregulated an SREBF2-like cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake module across the responding neuronal groups.
In the broad caudal and hypothalamic responders, the core sterol program expanded into fatty-acid, desaturation, elongation, citrate-CoA, and phospholipid remodeling genes.
Dctn1 produced only a limited lysosome/autophagy/proteostasis transcriptional echo despite DCTN1's canonical role in axonal lysosome and autophagosome transport.
The strongest Dctn1 signatures included a neuronal downshift in cytoskeletal, immediate-early, synaptic, and receptor-channel transcripts.
Dctn1 responses were sharply restricted: 12 of 22 measured groups had any FDR<0.10 downstream gene, and the broad programs were concentrated in 066, 151, 155, 191, and 217.
Mib1 was the strongest Dctn1 positive signature neighbor, with 138 same-direction FDR overlaps and no opposite overlaps across the Dctn1 signature.
Srebf2 was the only robust inverse neighbor: Srebf2 CRISPR drove the same cholesterol genes down that Dctn1 drove up.
Htt, Marchf6, Rab7, and Tsc2 converged with Dctn1, tying the response to vesicle transport, ER sterol-protein degradation, Rab7 lysosomal cholesterol export, and mTORC1-sterol signaling.
Srebf1, Hmgcr, canonical kinesins, Kifbp, Rptor, Amfr, Eif5a, and Vps41 did not robustly phenocopy Dctn1 despite being expected or data-driven candidates.
Ddb2 loss produced a pan-neuronal basal transcriptomic null: every one of the 23 measured neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite recovery of the Ddb2 transcript itself.

Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor represented DNA-repair comparators gave Ddb2 a meaningful convergent partner: all Ddb2 score cosines were near zero, and the NER/TFIIH target Gtf2h5 had only a two-gene 191 MB P MY GABA response that Ddb2 lacked.
Ddhd1 has a one-gene FDR<0.10 signature restricted to 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Mcl1 is upregulated.
Mcl1 upregulation is a candidate anti-apoptotic compensation to Ddhd1 lipid-enzyme loss in CTX-CGE GABA neurons.
The Ddhd1 CTX-CGE Mcl1 response is not shared by Ddhd2 or by assayed HSP/phosphoinositide comparators.
P16 Ddhd1 loss did not elicit a canonical phosphoinositide, lipid-droplet, mitochondrial, UPR/ISR, proteasome, or recycling-endosome DEG program in neuronal nuclei.
Ddhd2 loss of function did not produce a robust whole-transcriptome response in any measured neuronal class.
The lipid-droplet, lipophagy, and ROS/apoptosis programs expected from DDHD2 biology were not transcriptionally induced.
Related lipid/lipophagy and hereditary-spastic-paraplegia perturbations failed to phenocopy Ddhd2 in the matched DE surface.
The data-driven Ddhd2 signature-neighbor search yielded only background-like positive neighbors and no inverted neighbor.

Ddx39b produced a highly restricted postmitotic neuronal abundance response: only 3 of 21 measured cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and the only multi-gene response was in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The 191 MB P MY GABA Ddx39b signature was dominated by up-regulated RNA-processing and chromatin/transcriptional regulators together with a smaller down-regulated RNA-processing set.

The data-driven positive neighbors of Ddx39b were not random developmental genes: Thoc1, Tpr, and U2af2 were the top three biological same-direction restricted-signature neighbors, while Cdc40, Snrnp70, and Prpf6 provided weaker but directionally consistent spliceosome convergence.
Ddx39b also converged with proteasome perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 and carried an autophagy/mitochondrial remodeling tail in 191 MB P MY GABA and 308 CB GABA.

Ddx39b was far flatter than several pathway-proximal perturbations in the same cell groups: for example, in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Tpr and Prpf6 produced 478 and 368 downstream DEGs whereas Ddx39b produced only Mllt11.
Ddx39b did not phenocopy the represented neurodevelopmental RNA-helicase targets Ddx3x or Eif4a2 in its responder groups.
The L4/5 IT cortical and cerebellar GABAergic Ddx39b effects were real but isolated: Mllt11 alone in 005, and Miga2/Lancl1 up with Ttc14 down in 308.
Ddx39b perturbation did not transcriptionally induce Ddx39a, Alyref, Nxf1, or the measured export/splicing factors across the 21 measured cell groups.

Ddx3x LoF was a narrow postnatal neuronal perturbation: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut crossed FDR<0.10, with 9 and 6 downstream genes, while 20 measured groups had none and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response preferentially lowered a small synaptic/neurite-remodeling set, led by Grin2b, Synpo2, Vangl1 and Plekhg1, while Tmsb10 and Ypel3 were induced.
Ddx3x and Ctnnb1 converged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: five of nine Ddx3x downstream genes were significant in the stronger Ctnnb1 signature and every overlap moved in the same direction.
155 MB Glut showed an RNA-processing-flavored rebound, with Ddx5 increased and Hnrnpl decreased alongside Inha, Ppp2r5b and Bicd2 induction and Thy1 repression.

Biochemical translation-initiation relatives did not phenocopy Ddx3x: Ddx39b, Eif4g1, Fmr1, Fxr1, Atf6, Eif2ak4 and Tia1 were flat in both responder groups, and Eif4a2, Eif4h and Eif5a produced only one downstream gene each with no Ddx3x-feature overlap.
Ddx3x LoF produced no FDR-supported ISR/UPR, heat-shock, stress-granule, Ddx3y-compensation, or canonical Axin2/Lef1 Wnt-target transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group.
Strong postnatal RNA-binding/NDD comparators, especially Hnrnpu and Hnrnpc, generated hundreds of DE genes in the same two glutamatergic groups but did not align with the 15-gene Ddx3x signature.

Acute Deaf1 loss in juvenile postmitotic neurons produced an extremely sparse, mostly down-regulatory signature: 11 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in 5 of 22 tested groups and no significant Deaf1 self-transcript depletion.
Eif4g3 was the clearest direct-target-like Deaf1 output, falling in L4/5 IT cortex, TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, and MB glutamatergic neurons.
Rac3, B4gat1, and Tmem80 define a midbrain/thalamic negative module under Deaf1 perturbation, while Pcdh7 is the lone up-regulated FDR hit in 191 MB P MY GABA.

The strongest retained FDR-overlap neighbors of Deaf1 were proteasome perturbations rather than DEAF1 pathway members: Psmc1 and Psmb4 shared recurrent Eif4g3/Rac3/B4gat1 decreases but had thousands of additional DEGs in the same groups.
The canonical Deaf1-Htr1a serotonergic program was absent: Htr1a did not pass FDR under Deaf1 in any sampled group, and Htr1a perturbation itself was transcriptionally flat.

Measurable literature-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Deaf1: Gsk3b produced only an 8-gene 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c signature with no Deaf1-gene overlap, and the SAND-domain target Sp110 was flat.
Wdr26 was the only FDR-level anti-neighbor with more opposite than same Deaf1-feature overlaps, whereas Prpf6 and Yy1 each converged only on Eif4g3 down-regulation.
Dennd5a loss did not trigger a reproducible autonomous nuclear response in any recovered juvenile postmitotic neuronal class.
Expected DENND5A trafficking partners were not transcriptionally engaged, and the closest measurable Rab-GEF-cycle perturbations were also flat.
Dennd5a had no interpretable transcriptomic nearest neighbor in the complete parquet.
Depdc5 produced one robust postnatal transcriptional response, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The strongest Depdc5-positive module in 151 was sterol synthesis plus LDL uptake.
Tsc2 was the dominant same-direction Depdc5 neighbor and shared the sterol/PI3K 151 signature.
Srebf2 and Phf12 perturbations opposed the Depdc5 sterol axis rather than converging with it.
Mtor, Rptor, Strada, Pik3r1, and Pik3cb did not phenocopy Depdc5 in 151, despite being obvious pathway comparators.
Rab7 loss converged with Depdc5 on the sterol/endolysosomal 151 state.
Depdc5 also contained a small down-regulated RNA-processing arm.
A modest microtubule/synaptic-adhesion arm accompanied mTOR-sterol activation in the thalamic responder.
Postnatal mosaic Dgke loss had no robust steady-state neuronal transcriptional output in any recovered cell group.
Dgke did not belong to a detectable transcriptomic convergence module in this screen.
Represented PI-cycle/DAG/PKC and endothelial-disease neighbors also failed to phenocopy Dgke in neuronal snRNA-seq.

Dhdds produced a strong postnatal neuronal transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a smaller coherent response in 155 MB Glut, and only single-gene echoes in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 215 MB Dopa.
Dhdds induced a reproducible ER chaperone and ER-quality-control module centered on Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Sdf2l1, Creld2, Herpud1, Manf, Pdia4, and Pdia6.
The 151 response included a PERK/ATF4-like ISR and amino-acid arm, with Chac1, Ddit3, Sesn2, Asns, Slc7a5, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Shmt2, Psph, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases induced.
Cyb5r1 was the strongest 151 hit and Aldh1l2 recurred in 151, 155, and the single-gene 215 MB Dopa response, nominating redox and one-carbon genes as sensitive readouts of Dhdds stress.
In the coherent Dhdds responders, neuronal function genes were repressed, including Kcnc2, Atp1a3, Nrxn2, Grin2b, Grin2c, Gabrb2, Slc17a6, Kcna2, Syt3, Scg5, Thy1, Stmn3, Kifc2, Tuba1a, and Lrrc7.
Gfpt1 was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor of Dhdds and shared 126 same-direction FDR overlaps across the Dhdds FDR gene-cell pairs.
Atp2a2 and Hspa5 strongly, and Sec63 partially, converged with the Dhdds ER-stress signature; Vcp had a high cosine but too little FDR overlap to keep as a robust phenocopy.
The obvious represented relatives Dpm1 and Atf6 did not phenocopy Dhdds: Dpm1 had only two FDR genes in matched 151 and Atf6 had zero FDR genes in all matched Dhdds responder groups.
The most anti-correlated Dhdds neighbors, Il6ra, Diaph2, and Tmem63c, had zero FDR-significant opposite-direction overlaps and were rejected as mechanistic antagonists.
Diaph2 loss did not elicit a robust nuclear RNA program in either recovered postnatal glutamatergic class.
Diaph2 did not enter a coherent cross-perturbation transcriptomic module; the closest genome-wide score-vector neighbors were near-zero correlations.
The measurable RHO/formin relatives Cdc42, Rac1, Fmn1, and Fmn2 were also flat in the Diaph2-matched cell classes.
Dicer1 loss did not generate a BH-corrected basal mRNA response in any recovered neuronal class 3-4 weeks after P16 AAV-CRISPR perturbation.

The pathway-neighbor tests point to a broader miRNA/RISC-axis buffering in this assay: Ago2 and Tnrc6b were completely FDR-flat, while Ago1 and Tnrc6a produced only one to two isolated FDR<0.10 downstream hits.
A full-universe signature-neighbor search found only noise-scale neighbors for Dicer1; the strongest biological Pearson correlations were +0.0346 with Hdac5 and -0.0468 with Wdr26.
The experiment does not falsify delayed Dicer-dependent survival programs in adult dopaminergic or Purkinje neurons.
Acute postnatal Dip2b loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Dip2b did not engage the tubulin-isoform compensation program that was readily visible after Tuba1a perturbation in matched Pvalb and thalamic neurons.
Literature-nominated Dnmt3a, Dpysl5, semaphorin, and plexin perturbations failed to converge with Dip2b as a coherent postnatal nuclear transcriptome.
An unbiased Dip2b signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The FRA12A/DIP2B neurodevelopmental association is not phenocopied as a pan-neuronal juvenile transcriptional collapse by acute coding loss of Dip2b.
P16 Dlat loss produced a sharply restricted neuronal transcriptome: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a robust downstream DEG, Jarid2.
Jarid2 down-regulation was the sole FDR<0.10 downstream Dlat marker in the responder.
The only Dlat responder lacked an ISR, UPR, mitochondrial-chaperone, autophagy, or lactate/pyruvate transcriptional program.
Literature-obvious PDC and adjacent mitochondrial-carbon comparators failed to phenocopy Dlat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The leading unbiased 151 signature neighbor was Uba5, not a PDC component, and only Uba5 shared Dlat's Jarid2-down feature at FDR<0.10.
Related mitochondrial enzymes produced singleton effects in several forebrain groups where Dlat was null or weak.

Dld loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal class: none of the 21 measured groups had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10, despite Dld mRNA being assayed in each group.

Canonical mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, ER-stress, and antioxidant transcripts were absent from the Dld surface: Atf4, Atf5, Ddit3, Trib3, Asns, Hspa9, Hspd1, Clpp, Lonp1, Hmox1, Nqo1, Gclc, Gclm, Txnrd1, and Prdx5 were all FDR=1 in every measured group.

Directly measured DLD-pathway perturbations were also sparse: Bckdhb, Bckdk, and Mpc1 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Dlat, Dlst, Ogdh, Pdha1, Aco2, Mdh2, Sdha, and Suclg1 produced only one or two downstream genes each across the brain-wide panel.

The data-driven full-transcriptome neighbor search found no robust Dld-like target: the strongest positive and negative signed-score correlations were only +0.025 and -0.022, and Safe_target-labeled perturbations appeared in both tails.
Dlg4 perturbation was globally flat at the downstream snRNA level: all 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 non-Dlg4 genes at FDR<0.10 despite uniformly negative Dlg4 self-transcript logFC.
Dlg4 loss did not transcriptionally induce MAGUK paralogs or rewrite mRNAs for represented receptor and PSD partners.
NMDAR-subunit perturbations can be transcriptomically active in the same assay, but Dlg4 is not their mRNA phenocopy.
Several represented PSD scaffold or adhesion perturbations converged with Dlg4 by remaining close to transcriptionally flat.
Unsupervised cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Dlg4 signature neighbor.
The DLG4-related synaptopathy LoF axis lacks a durable P16-to-young-adult neuronal RNA biomarker in this assay.
Dlgap4 produced robust downstream RNA responses in only 3 of 23 recovered cell groups: L5 ET corticofugal glutamatergic neurons, CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons, and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
Dlgap4 down-regulated a dense-core vesicle and neuropeptide module in the two glutamatergic responder classes, with Vgf recurring in both and Scg2 plus Ptprn down in L5 ET.
The CNU-LGE LSX GABA response consisted of Scn1b and Tacc1 down-regulation despite a flat-to-positive Dlgap4 self-transcript.
In TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, Dlgap4 caused a borderline membrane-adhesion and glycosylation response: Plekha7 and Xylt2 decreased while Igsf8 increased.
Ctnnb1 was the top exact shared-direction neighbor of Dlgap4, sharing Vgf down, Xylt2 down, and Igsf8 up in TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
Atp2b1, Eef2, and Atp2a2 were the top exact anti-neighbors of Dlgap4 and inverted the Vgf/Xylt2 or Scg2/Vgf portions of the Dlgap4 signature.
Dlgap4 loss did not drive a transcriptional PSD95-SAPAP-SHANK or AMPA/NMDA receptor program, and several represented same-scaffold or synaptic-disease perturbations were fully flat.
Grin1 and Grin2b partially phenocopied individual Dlgap4 features, whereas Grin2a was divergent and acted mainly in upper-layer IT neurons where Dlgap4 was null or weak.
Acute Dll1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally silent across all 23 recovered juvenile-to-young-adult neuronal cell groups.
Dll1 perturbation did not move the canonical Notch-effector or neural-precursor transcriptional program.
The Notch-ligand E3 ligase Mib1 did not phenocopy Dll1: Mib1 drove a recurrent sterol-biosynthetic response whereas Dll1 and core receptor/protease nodes were flat or nearly flat.
Full-universe signature search found no meaningful Dll1-like or anti-Dll1 module.
Dlst loss-of-function produced an almost flat neuronal snRNA-seq surface: only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 371818 tested Dlst group/gene rows.
The residual Dlst response consisted of Abi1 down-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Ankrd29 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Dlst did not converge with OGDH-complex or other TCA perturbations, and even its data-driven top neighbors had near-zero correlations.
Canonical KGDH consequences tied to congenital disease, PPGL variants, histone succinylation, and lipid peroxidation were expected but absent from the P16 neuronal Dlst transcriptome.
Dlx3 loss produced a screen-wide weak/null transcriptomic surface: none of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups contained even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The weak Dlx3 surface did not uncover a hidden forebrain GABAergic Dlx program.
The Dlx3 neuronal LoF surface lacked the hair/ectodermal and osteogenic modules implicated by Tricho-dento-osseous biology.
There was no meaningful Dlx3-like perturbation neighborhood in the global score space.

Dlx6-targeted CRISPR produced an all-null FDR surface across all 23 measured neuronal cell groups: 2645 Dlx6-perturbed nuclei yielded 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the Dlx6 transcript row itself had FDR=1.0 everywhere.

The forebrain GABAergic DLX-GAD/Vgat/Pvalb program was not transcriptionally engaged by Dlx6 alone: Dlx5, Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Pvalb, and Sst rows were nonsignificant in the measured forebrain GABA groups, and those groups had 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes.

Unbiased signature matching found no robust Dlx6 module: the strongest signed-Wilcoxon neighbors were Pde4b and Gucy2e positively and Unc13b and Klf9 negatively, but all correlations were near zero and Dlx6 had no FDR gene set to overlap.

Measured literature-adjacent comparators rejected a hidden Dlx-family phenocopy: Dlx3 was null in 22 tested groups, Gad2 had no downstream transcriptional response, Nkx2-1 and Six3 were near-null, whereas Arx and Mef2c demonstrated that some matched neurons can produce FDR-detectable signatures to related developmental transcription-factor perturbations.

The null Dlx6 coding perturbation cautions that DLX5/6 locus phenotypes driven by developmental enhancer dosage or paired Dlx5/6 loss are not modeled by sparse Dlx6-only loss after neuronal specification.
Dmbt1 produced a single corrected neuronal response: Epb41 down-regulation confined to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The Dmbt1 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Represented WNT comparators did not phenocopy Dmbt1: Ctnnb1, Lrp5, and Lrp6 responded in thalamic or midbrain cell groups but not in Dmbt1-positive NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
NOD2/TLR4/NF-kappaB and IL-27/STAT comparator perturbations were flat across the Dmbt1-matched neuronal surface.
Itgb1 loss did not copy Dmbt1 in any matched neuronal group.
Dmd produced no robust cell-autonomous nuclear DE response in any recovered neuronal class.
The Dmd perturbation did not transcriptionally remodel DGC, GABA_A, neurexin or NMDA-receptor mRNAs.
Represented DGC comparators were also flat or nearly flat, so Dmd is part of a postnatal DGC scaffold module that is transcriptionally buffered in this assay.
Synaptic receptor perturbations can generate small cortical or thalamic DE programs where Dmd and core DGC perturbations do not.
Unbiased signature search placed Dmd in a near-zero residual neighborhood rather than near a disease or synaptic program.
Cell-autonomous neuronal snRNA-seq is unlikely to be a sensitive short-window biomarker for brain Dmd rescue or loss.

Dmxl2 produced an extremely restricted postnatal neuronal transcriptional response: a Scn2b decrease in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and a Serpini1 increase in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, with 0 downstream FDR genes in 20 other measured groups.
Dmxl2 perturbation selectively lowered Scn2b in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Dmxl2 perturbation selectively increased Serpini1 in 046 CTX-CGE GABA interneurons.
The Dmxl2 FDR surface did not recover the expected Rabconnectin-3/V-ATPase, Notch, autophagy-lysosomal, ISR/UPR, Rab3, or core synaptic transcript programs.

Represented V-ATPase, Notch, Rab3, and synaptic-vesicle perturbations did not phenocopy the two Dmxl2 responder signatures; the most direct Rabconnectin-3 relatives Dmxl1, Wdr7, and Rogdi were absent from the target set.
Blind Wilcoxon-score signature matching found no robust positive or negative Dmxl2 neighbor; all top correlations were near zero and safe-target perturbations appeared among top neighbors.
Acute Dnajb4 loss produced a pan-neuronal statistical null: every recovered neuronal class had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Dnajb4 did not induce the heat-shock, ER-UPR/ISR, autophagy, redox, or proteasome-bounce-back transcripts that would be expected from an unfolded-client crisis.
Represented DNAJ-family relatives were also small-effect perturbations and did not uncover a shared Hsp40 neuronal transcriptomic module.
The proteasome targets Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the least Dnajb4-like perturbations by whole-logFC correlation and were broad responders where Dnajb4 was flat.
The top positive whole-transcriptome neighbors of Dnajb4 were themselves null or nearly null, so there is no convincing positive Dnajb4 convergence partner in this analysis universe.
Hsp90ab1 mRNA depletion was itself buffered, producing zero downstream DE genes despite strong on-target transcript loss in many neuronal groups.
Dnajb6 produced a single reproducible-looking chromatin hit, Pcgf3 up-regulation, restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The expected HSP40/HSP90/CHIP relatives did not phenocopy Dnajb6.
The assay could detect HSP70, HSF1, and ER-UPR transcription when those nodes were perturbed, but Dnajb6 loss did not engage that response.
Central proteasome subunits produced massive stress/neuronal down-regulation surfaces at similar cell counts, whereas Dnajb6 did not.
Unsupervised neighbors of the weak Dnajb6 nominal signature were themselves weak and biologically incoherent.
Acute Dnajb6 loss in healthy postmitotic neurons does not mimic dominant DNAJB6 myopathy or induced polyglutamine aggregation biology.
Dnajc13 produced a one-gene, MH-LH TH Glut-restricted Spred1 induction.
Dnajc13 did not phenocopy the Vps35/Rab7 endolysosomal transcriptional state in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Proximal RME-8 pathway comparators were heterogeneous and did not converge on the Dnajc13 surface.
The expected Dnajc13 autophagy, lysosomal and HSP secondary program was absent at FDR<0.10.
Whole-surface Dnajc13 signature neighbors were numerically tiny and failed an FDR-overlap check.
Dnajc19 loss-of-function was globally transcriptome-buffered: none of the 22 recovered neuronal groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

The Dnajc19 null cannot be explained by inability of this snRNA-seq screen to detect mitochondrial stress, because Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations in the same parquet induced the expected ATF4/ISR-like genes.
A model-universe search found no meaningful Dnajc19 signature neighbor: the largest real-gene score correlation was only r=0.041 and the strongest inverse real-gene correlation was r=-0.016.

Represented DNAJ-family and proximal mitochondrial comparators did not phenocopy Dnajc19; the only broad inner-membrane stress phenotype among the checked relatives came from Opa1, while core TIM23/PAM members were not targeted.
Dnajc5 generated a single downstream FDR<0.10 event: Fndc3a up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
The Dnajc5 perturbation did not recover the expected CSPα synaptic-maintenance, Hsp70/co-chaperone, ISR, or autophagy nuclear programs.
Hspa8, the Hsc70 partner in the CSPα chaperone system, showed a small heat-shock/co-chaperone replacement signature that Dnajc5 did not share.
Cltc, unlike Dnajc5, produced a broad response in eight neuronal groups, including immediate-early, synaptic, and membrane-trafficking genes.
Represented DnaJ/Hsp40-family perturbations did not phenocopy the one-gene Dnajc5 signature.
Acute Dnajc5 loss-of-function did not phenocopy DNAJC5/CLN4 adult neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis biology at the neuronal transcriptome level.
The top whole-signature neighbors of Dnajc5 were effectively uncorrelated, and the Fndc3a hit did not recur among other 008 perturbations.
Dnal1 loss produced a near-pan-neuronal negative surface in this P16 acute CRISPR screen: among 22 measured NeuN+ groups only one downstream gene, Nup205 in L5 ET neurons, passed FDR<0.10.
The sole robust downstream Dnal1 signal was an isolated Nup205 decrease in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons.
Represented primary-cilium and ciliary-trafficking perturbations did not phenocopy Dnal1; their restricted-signature cosines were near zero and no comparator shared the L5 ET Nup205 hit at FDR<0.10.
The closest data-driven transcriptomic neighbors of Dnal1 were weak and biologically non-obvious; the top cosine was only 0.1307 with Map1lc3a and the strongest anti-neighbor was -0.1125 with Zfp292.

P16 Dnm1 CRISPR produced a pervasive downstream-zero signature: 0 non-Dnm1 genes reached FDR<0.10 in every one of 22 measured neuronal groups, even though the Dnm1 transcript decreased in 21/22 groups and was FDR-significant in 10.

Dnm1 did not phenocopy represented clathrin/synaptic-vesicle neighbors: Cltc and Stxbp1 each generated multi-group FDR<0.10 signatures in matched groups, whereas Dnm1 had 0 downstream FDR genes in the same taxonomy.

The unsupervised Dnm1 signature had no strong convergent or anti-convergent neighbor in the complete visible target universe: the top positive whole-profile cosine was Nos1ap at 0.02982 and the strongest negative gene-target cosine was Grik5 at -0.01206.

The GABAergic Dnm1 surface was also downstream-null, including Pvalb, Sst, CNU-MGE, CNU-LGE, hypothalamic GABA, midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA and cerebellar GABA groups; no immediate-early, stress/proteostasis or synaptic sentinel reached FDR<0.10 anywhere.
Dnmt3a loss at P16 produced a transcriptome-wide zero rather than a neuronal mCH-writer signature: no measured neuronal group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

The mCH writer and its represented methylation readers uncouple in the P16 screen: Mecp2 had a reproducible DE surface while Dnmt3a, Mbd2 and Mbd5 had only zero or single-gene surfaces and no shared robust DE with Dnmt3a.
The unsupervised Dnmt3a vector has no meaningful positive or negative neighbor; the top positive cross-target Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.030 and the top negative was r=-0.012.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was weak for Dnmt3a but strongly responsive to other chromatin regulators such as Chd8, Kmt2a, Crebbp, Nsd1 and Ehmt1.

The screen does not phenocopy constitutional DNMT3A neurodevelopmental disease; P16 neuronal knockout leaves a flat RNA surface despite Dnmt3a being a monogenic overgrowth-intellectual-disability gene.
Dock3 produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
Canonical Rac/WAVE/GSK3β nodes did not converge with Dock3 in the matched cell groups.
The strongest data-driven Dock3 positive and negative neighbors were effectively zero-correlation null signatures.
Somatic nuclear RNA is a poor candidate pharmacodynamic axis for DOCK3 activation or inhibition in uninjured postnatal neurons.
The represented presenilin/APP/tau-axis comparators did not create a Dock3-like transcriptomic disease signature.
Dpm1 loss produced a detectable but very small response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Pdia6 up and Ttyh3 down at FDR<0.10.
Dhdds, an upstream dolichol-backbone enzyme, reproduced both Dpm1-significant directions in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and did so within a much broader 168-gene response.
Dpm1 exposed only a Pdia6 edge of the ER-folding/UPR program that Gfpt1 strongly activated in the same thalamic cell group.
The downstream O-mannosylation and GPI-anchor comparators Fktn and Pign did not phenocopy Dpm1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The unsupervised whole-surface neighbor search found no strong Dpm1-like or Dpm1-opposite perturbation signature.
P16 mosaic Dpp6 loss produced no FDR-defined downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
The only literature-obvious Kv4 pore comparator represented in the screen, Kcnd3/Kv4.3, was as transcriptionally flat as Dpp6.
The all-target signature-neighbor search put Dpp6 at the noise floor rather than in a coherent convergent or antagonistic module.
Dpp6 loss did not transcriptionally backfill the Kv4 complex or elicit an immediate-early activity program.

Dpyd loss was almost entirely buffered on the acute neuronal nuclear-transcriptome axis: 21 of 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Pvalb GABA neurons had a one-gene response.
Zkscan3 down-regulation is the sole Dpyd-induced FDR<0.10 transcript in the entire measured surface and is restricted to Pvalb GABA neurons.
The Pvalb Zkscan3 decrease was uncoupled from detectable induction of representative autophagy, lysosomal, ISR/UPR, or redox-stress genes.
Matr3 was the only other perturbation that changed Zkscan3 in Pvalb neurons at FDR<0.10, but it up-regulated Zkscan3 whereas Dpyd down-regulated it.
A complete matched Wilcoxon-score scan did not find a meaningful Dpyd transcriptomic phenocopy or anti-phenocopy: the most positive and negative global correlations were only r=0.0258 and r=-0.0214.

Dpyd perturbation did not transcriptionally engage other pyrimidine metabolism genes that were observable as DE genes, and the sequential catabolic enzymes Dpys and Upb1 were not represented as perturbation targets.
Dpysl5 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 neuronal cell groups in which the target was recovered.
The literature-obvious semaphorin/plexin/GSK3B/Fyn and microtubule comparators did not converge with Dpysl5.
Human DPYSL5 neurodevelopmental genetics are not phenocopied by juvenile sparse Dpysl5 loss in mature neurons.
The data-driven Dpysl5 signature has no strong positive or negative neighbor in the perturbation universe.
Drd2 loss produced a one-gene cortical response: Zfp326 was up-regulated only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The Drd2 Zfp326 response did not converge with represented dopamine-family receptors, D2 effector nodes, or serotonergic psychiatric co-targets.
Drd2 deletion failed to induce the literature-expected basal cAMP/immediate-early, indirect-pathway, or dopamine-autoreceptor marker panels anywhere in the 23-group surface.
A genome-scale signature-neighbor search found no strong transcriptomic convergence or anti-convergence with Drd2.
Drd4 loss of function after P16 produced a taxonomy-wide FDR-clean neuronal transcriptomic null, including no cAMP, immediate-early, NMDA/AMPA, or GABA mRNA program.
Drd4 did not transcriptionally converge with dopamine-receptor or cAMP effector perturbations represented in the same screen.
The all-target neighbor search placed Drd4 in background rather than in a reproducible co-signature module.
The result separates DRD4-linked behavior genetics from simple juvenile neuronal loss of D4-driven basal transcription.
Drd5 loss was transcriptionally silent in every recovered neuronal group: 22 measured groups and 2,165 perturbation-assigned nuclei yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected dopamine/cAMP/CREB, immediate-early, and hippocampal NMDA-receptor mRNA programs did not appear after Drd5 perturbation.
Represented dopamine-pathway relatives did not converge with Drd5, including Drd2/Drd4, Gnas/Gnal, Adcy1/3/5, Pde10a, and Creb1.
An unbiased whole-universe score search found no biologically strong positive or negative Drd5 neighbor.
P16 Dscam loss-of-function was globally buffered at the whole-transcriptome level: every one of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 non-Dscam genes at FDR<0.10.
The only cell group with a corrected Dscam self-transcript change was 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but even there the closest non-self gene, Ltbp3, stopped below the response threshold.
A 1772-target restricted-signature scan found no strong Dscam transcriptomic neighbor or antineighbor; the largest signed-Wilcoxon cosine was only 0.161.

Netrin and axon-guidance relatives did not uncover a Dscam-like response: Dcc, Slit2, Unc5c, Unc5d, Robo1, and Robo2 had no non-self hits in matched groups, and Neo1 produced only three isolated downstream genes.
The Down-syndrome DSCAM/PAK1 neurogenesis axis was not recapitulated by acute Dscam loss in normal P16 postmitotic neurons; Pak/Rac/Fyn comparators were also nearly flat.
Dst produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of 22 measured NeuN+ brain cell groups after acute P16 CRISPR perturbation.
Dst failed to phenocopy Dctn1 or Tuba1a, even though those cytoskeletal/transport comparators generated real secondary programs in matched cell groups.
The broader plakin/spectraplakin neighborhood was itself nearly transcriptionally silent: Macf1, Plec, and Map1b produced 0-1 significant genes across the 22 Dst-matched groups.
Full-universe score-space search found only near-zero Dst signature neighbors, with no hidden convergent module below the FDR threshold.

Postnatal Dstyk loss produced a two-gene, two-cell-group transcriptional surface: Coro1a decreased in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Dach1 decreased in 308 CB GABA, while 20 other measured groups had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Coro1a was the sole robust responder in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut after Dstyk perturbation.
Dach1 was the only FDR<0.10 gene in 308 CB GABA after Dstyk perturbation.
The Dach1 branch in 308 CB GABA converged with Wdr26 and diverged from Ranbp2, whereas whole-profile Dstyk neighbors were otherwise weak.
Expected FGF/ERK, Wnt/LDHA and mTORC1/TFEB transcriptional reporters were absent from the Dstyk neuronal DE surface.
The oncology-style DSTYK-autophagy/mitochondrial-fitness liability was not mirrored as a neuronal stress signature.
Dtnbp1 produced no BH-corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss-of-function.

The assayed mRNAs did not recapitulate the canonical dysbindin effector phenotypes: Grin/Gria receptor transcripts, Drd2, neurotransmitter synthetic markers, and vesicle genes all had minimum FDR=1.000 across Dtnbp1 groups.
Ap3b1, the only represented BLOC-1/AP-3 trafficking comparator, also failed to produce corrected DE in Dtnbp1-matched groups, and its Wilcoxon-score profile was uncorrelated with Dtnbp1.
The data-driven Dtnbp1 signature was not assigned to any robust perturbation neighborhood; the best positive and negative score correlations among biological targets were only +0.037 and -0.014.
Dym knockout after P16 is transcriptionally buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons rather than producing a Golgi/UPR crisis.
The only corrected Dym downstream signal was a small Aak1 decrease restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The data-driven neighbors of Dym were statistical near-neighbors only, not convergent biological signatures.
The literature-obvious Golgi disease comparator RAB33B was not directly tested, and represented broad trafficking comparators did not phenocopy Dym.
Dync2h1 is a complete measured transcriptional null after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation in NeuN-enriched neurons: 21 recovered cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical Sonic Hedgehog/Gli transcriptional program was not recovered: Gli1, Gli2, Gli3, Hhip, Ptch1, Ptch2, Shh, and Smo were assayed across the Dync2h1 surface but never reached FDR<0.10.

The broader ciliary transport/Hh target set also stayed flat in the same assay: the dynein-2 partner Dync2i1 and most IFT or Hh comparators had zero multi-gene FDR signatures in Dync2h1-matched cell groups.

Unbiased nearest-neighbor analysis found no credible Dync2h1 signature partner: the strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were only 0.0387 and -0.0224, and a safe-target perturbation appeared among the top positives.

The two recovered hypothalamic Dync2h1 populations were flat, arguing that reported DYNC2H1 links to hypothalamic hamartoma are unlikely to be maintained by a P16-onward autonomous Hh/Gli expression state in differentiated hypothalamic neurons.
Dync2i1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally silent across every recovered postnatal neuronal group.
The represented dynein-2/IFT/Hedgehog relatives were also nearly all flat, whereas broad proteasome perturbations responded in the same model-visible universe.
Postnatal Dync2i1 perturbation did not reopen WDR60's embryonic cortical-migration program.
Dyrk1a produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 19 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.

The measurable calcineurin/NFAT branch did not fire after Dyrk1a perturbation: Rcan1 and Nfatc1-4 were never significant, Nfatc3 knockout was flat, and Nfat5 produced only two Slc38a2 calls in matched groups.
The ribosomal-protein mRNA program reported after DYRK1A depletion could not be evaluated because canonical cytosolic Rpl/Rps genes were absent from the Dyrk1a DE universe.
The strongest nominal anti-neighbor of Dyrk1a was Tsc2, and Tsc2 produced 634 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in matched groups while Dyrk1a produced none.
Dyrk1a had no meaningful empirical whole-surface neighbor: the top positive and top negative Pearson correlations among 1,728 comparators were only +0.02974 and -0.02555.

Represented Hsa21 / Down-syndrome neuronal candidates App, Dscam, Kcnj6, Synj1, and Tiam1 did not converge with Dyrk1a; like Dyrk1a, each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the matched groups in which it was recovered.
Phenotypically overlapping neurodevelopmental genes were not uniformly flat: Mecp2 and Zeb2 produced small post-P16 signatures whereas Dyrk1a and Ube3a were flat in matched groups.

The P16 neuronal RNA null should not be treated as a safety proof for DYRK1A inhibition: known mature DYRK1A effects include phosphorylation of pre-existing synaptic and cytoskeletal substrates whose transcript levels stayed unchanged.
Dzip1 induced a single FDR<0.10 gene, Mlec, specifically in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Dzip1 had no robust same-direction or opposite-direction perturbation neighbor in the model-visible target universe.
Dzip1 failed to recover a Hedgehog or pan-ciliogenesis transcriptional program, and represented ciliary/Hh comparators were sparse and nonconvergent.
E2f1 is a pan-cell-group FDR-null perturbation across the healthy P16 to P37-44 NeuN+ screen.
Loss of E2f1 did not move the canonical E2F DNA-replication, mitotic, or apoptotic transcriptional program.
Measured E2F/DP and cell-cycle relatives did not converge on a hidden E2F module.
The assay separates basal E2f1 loss from the stressed-neuron E2F1 apoptosis and mature-neuron cell-cycle phenotypes reported in other systems.
E2f5 loss of function produced no corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured NeuN-enriched neuronal groups.

Canonical E2F/DREAM G1/S transcripts were not derepressed after E2f5 perturbation, and the directly measured E2f1, Tfdp1 and Tfdp2 perturbations were also essentially flat in the matched neuronal groups.
Genes representing choroid-plexus secretion and multiciliogenesis did not move in the neuronal E2f5 surface, and the choroid-plexus comparator Trp73 was likewise nearly null.
A full-vector search found only very weak E2f5 signature neighbors: the strongest genic correlations were |r|<=0.038 and had no shared FDR-significant E2f5 genes to overlap.
Ebf1 produced zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every measured P16-to-P37/44 neuronal cell group.
The CNU-LGE/LSX GABA group did not down-regulate a striatonigral medium-spiny-neuron program after Ebf1 perturbation.
Represented EBF-family comparators did not reveal an acute COE-family module: Ebf3 and Zfp521 were flat and Ebf2 had only one isolated CA3/DG hit.
The unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbor scan found no biologically strong Ebf1 signature neighbor.
Other represented striatal-development regulators also failed to induce a matched acute D1/MSN transcriptional program.
P16 Ebf2 loss-of-function was almost globally buffered in recovered NeuN+ postmitotic neurons: only one non-self gene reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The only resolved Ebf2 downstream gene was CA3/CA2-fasciola/dentate Tbc1d14 down-regulation.
The EBF paralogs Ebf1 and Ebf3 did not phenocopy Ebf2, including in the CA3 Tbc1d14 locus.
The cerebellar GABA test did not recapitulate the germline Purkinje Ebf2 program: Aldoc, Igf1, Plcb4, Pcp2, and Itpr1 all had FDR=1.0 after P16 perturbation.
Data-driven Ebf2 signature neighbors were at the noise floor and did not share a robust Tbc1d14 module.
Ebf3 loss produced a broad postmitotic neuronal transcriptional null: every measured group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected EBF3 developmental readout genes did not move after Ebf3 perturbation: Neurod1, Reln, Th, Slc6a3, and Cntnap4 were all FDR=1 across the measured groups.
The P16 assay buffered the EBF paralog family, not only Ebf3: Ebf1 had no downstream FDR hits and Ebf2 had only one hit across the same 21 groups.
Unbiased signature neighbors did not reveal a robust convergent module; the strongest positive and negative score correlations to Ebf3 were only |r|≤0.026 and mostly belonged to flat targets.
Arx, an embryonic basal-forebrain regulator that directly represses Ebf3, retained a small P16 GABA response whereas Ebf3 was completely flat in those same GABA classes.
Eda produced a pan-neuronal corrected-DE null: every one of the 23 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The closest whole-surface Eda signature neighbors were extremely weak and included safe-target controls, and their returned DE surfaces were null or nearly null.
The embryonic EDA/EDAR/NF-kappaB placode program was not recovered: Dkk4, Lrp4, Shh, Ccnd1, and Edar were all present in the ranked Eda gene universe and all had minimum FDR=1.0.

Postmitotic neuronal Wnt/beta-catenin signatures are detectable in this same parquet but diverge from Eda: Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and Lrp6 all had corrected DE in thalamic glutamatergic groups in which Eda had none.

Acute Edem3 loss did not induce a robust ER-stress, ERAD, proteasome, or EDEM-family transcriptional program in any of the 21 neuronal groups tested; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed only a sub-threshold Xbp1 nominal signal.

The ER proteostasis branch is detectable in this screen: Hspa5 perturbation, with fewer 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells than Edem3, up-regulated Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, Herpud1, Asns, and Nfe2l1, whereas Edem3 did not.

The unbiased Edem3 neighborhood search collapsed to noise: the strongest positive and negative score-vector neighbors had absolute correlations below 0.03, including the broad Wdr26 and Uba5 responders and the negative Safe_target_50/Gabra3/Tcf12/Gls set.

The neuronal transcriptome null does not contradict EDEM3-CDG genetics because reported pathogenic biology is a germline N-glycan-processing defect; the assayed P16 mosaic LoF would miss early, systemic, and primary glycan phenotypes.

The only canonical UPR-sensor perturbation represented as a target, Atf6, was itself flat, showing that basal loss of an ER-stress pathway gene need not create the Hspa5-like UPR output in these neurons.
Ednra loss yielded a single FDR-level Sst-neuron marker, Dhtkd1 up-regulation, rather than a broader endothelin pathway.
P16 Ednra loss was buffered across the assayed postmitotic neuronal surface: 19 of 20 measured groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the remaining group had only one.
Canonical EDNRA-induced transcriptional modules were absent from the Ednra DE surface.
Neither data-driven nor literature-obvious comparators converged on Ednra.
The neuronal null should not be generalized to EDNRA antagonist pharmacology in vascular, craniofacial, or injured-glial systems.

Postnatal Eef2 loss produced a sharply cell-type-skewed neuronal transcriptome: 845 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 86 in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 62 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 39 in 155 MB Glut, and only focal or absent effects elsewhere.
Eef2 own mRNA was never significantly depleted even in the broad responders; self FDR was 1.0 in every measured group while the downstream signature reached 1119 gene-by-cell entries at FDR<0.10.
The dominant 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut response was an up-regulated trophic/activity and secretory program, including Vgf, Bdnf, Nptx2, Inhba, Scg2, Ptgs2, Fosb, Egr3, and Dusp6.

Several Eef2 responders paired compensatory up-regulation with loss of mature synaptic, vesicle, cytoskeletal, and neuronal-metabolic transcripts such as Snap25, Syn2, Uchl1, Tuba1a, Dync1i2, Cadps, Cyp46a1, and Eno2.
Eef2 responders repeatedly induced ER, translocon, lysosomal, and sphingolipid genes, including Smpd1, Lamp1, Lgmn, Rpn1, Tmx1, Prkcsh, Ssr2, Ssr4, Sec62, and Laptm4b.
Ranbp2, Son, Prpf8, and Hnrnpu formed a recurrent nuclear-pore/RNA-processing arm of the response, with Ranbp2 up in six groups and Son up in five.

Atxn10 was the strongest positive data-driven neighbor of Eef2 and shared same-direction L2/3 activity genes and Pvalb metabolic/Syt4 genes, despite not being a translation-initiation or elongation factor.

Eef2 aligned with Grin2a loss but anti-aligned with Grin2b loss in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut: Eef2 and Grin2a shared 16 FDR genes in the same direction, whereas Eef2 and Grin2b shared 18 of 21 in the opposite direction.

The Eef2 response was not a generic feature of perturbing translation-factor or mTORC1-coupled targets: Eif5a, Eif2ak4, Eif4a2, Eif4g1, Eif4h, Mtor, and Rptor were flat or nearly flat, while Tsc2 was broad but nonconvergent.
Eef2 did not activate a canonical ATF4/CHOP integrated-stress response: Atf4, Ddit3, Atf3, Asns, and Trib3 were below FDR<0.10 in all 21 measured groups.
Vgf, Syt4, Smpd1, Son, and Ranbp2 were the best recurrent positive transcript markers of Eef2-sensitive neuronal states.
Efemp1 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptome in any recovered cell group: all 20 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Neither unbiased score-vector neighbors nor literature-obvious EFEMP1 partners/pathways converged with Efemp1.
The R345W fibulin-3 stress axis was absent after CRISPR Efemp1 loss: UPR, VEGF, Notch/NF-kB, and ECM-remodeling marker genes never reached FDR<0.10.
Egr2 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 21 measured juvenile NeuN+ central neuronal groups.
The measured Egr2 surface did not recover an EGR/NAB feedback, immediate-early-gene, or myelin transcript program.
The cross-target signature scan found only very weak Egr2 neighbors, with the best Pearson correlations below 0.033 in either direction.
The represented hindbrain and Schwann-cell comparators Mafb and Sox10 did not converge on the Egr2 surface in matched juvenile neurons.
Wdr26 and Huwe1 produced robust DE in the same broad cell classes where Egr2 remained flat.
