The Egr2 perturbation did not engage the peripheral myelin gene module most relevant to EGR2-linked CMT and congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy.
Ehmt1 loss was a very sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptomic perturbation: only thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells and midbrain glutamatergic cells had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The main Ehmt1-positive signature was a seven-gene thalamic module dominated by up-regulation of Abhd12b, Endou, Smtn, Stxbp2, Msra, and Atp2a1 with Vwc2 as the only down-regulated hit.
The 155 MB Glut response was a singleton Nrip3 up-regulation.
The Ehmt1 thalamic module converged most strongly with Chd4, Setdb1, and Sin3a, which re-induced Abhd12b/Smtn/Msra in the same direction.
Uba5, Cic, Elp1, Smarcc2, and Yy1 opposed the Ehmt1 TH module despite being strong responders in the same cell group.
Ehmt1 did not recover the expected protocadherin, BDNF, or NMDA-receptor transcriptional programs anywhere in the 22 measured groups.
The measurable G9a/GLP recruitment cofactor Zfp644 did not phenocopy Ehmt1 in the matched thalamic or midbrain responder groups, while Ehmt2 and Wiz were not represented as perturbation targets.
Postnatal Eif2ak4 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream DE in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
No canonical ATF4/amino-acid-starvation or compensatory eIF2α-kinase mRNA program was recovered after Eif2ak4 perturbation.
Eif2ak4 was isolated in the model-visible perturbation manifold: even its top score-vector neighbors were effectively uncorrelated.
The assayed Creb1 perturbation did not reveal an Eif2ak4-to-CREB nuclear signature in the hippocampal-like pools.
PVOD/PAH genetics did not map to a neuronal Eif2ak4 signature in this screen.

Acute Eif4a2 loss produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured neuronal groups, and the true transcriptional responders were restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
Cadm4 was the sole robust non-self gene in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
Dbn1 was the sole robust non-self gene in the 191 MB P MY GABA response.
The Eif4a2 surface did not recover an integrated-stress, unfolded-protein, proteostasis, ribosomal, or eIF4F transcriptional bounce-back program.
Represented Ccr4-Not/eIF4F/mTOR comparators did not phenocopy the two Eif4a2 responder signatures.
The top phenotype-first signature neighbor was Ufc1, not a canonical eIF4F or miRNA-pathway target, and the convergence was concentrated in a shared thalamic Cadm4 decrease.
The mouse P16 mosaic Eif4a2 LoF phenotype is compatible with EIF4A2 disease being a selective translation-timing problem rather than a pan-neuronal mRNA-collapse state.
Eif4g1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response in any of the 21 recovered postnatal neuronal cell groups.
An ATF4/amino-acid stress program that is readily observed after Opa1 and Elp1 perturbation was absent after Eif4g1.
direction_pattern: ISR genes up in Opa1/Elp1 but absent in Eif4g1

canonical_summary: The individually perturbed eIF4F/mTOR cap-initiation arm was flat or extremely weak, whereas Tsc2 loss generated hundreds of DEGs in matched neurons.
Parkinson-family targets represented in the parquet did not converge with the Eif4g1 acute loss-of-function surface.
A full-universe signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Eif4g1 neighbor.

Sparse P16 Eif4h loss did not recreate the broad cortical and growth phenotype expected from germline Eif4h deficiency; the assay recovered only two FDR<0.10 mRNA changes across 22 measured neuronal groups.
Hexim1 was the sole FDR<0.10 Eif4h hit in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and fell in a recurrent thalamo-hypothalamic module shared in the same direction by Uba5, Ufc1, and Tsc2.
Syt1 was the only FDR<0.10 gene in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and was uniquely up-regulated by Eif4h among all perturbations that significantly changed Syt1 there.
The global Eif4h signature had no strong whole-surface neighbor: the best positive cosine was only 0.0327 and the most negative was -0.0202 across 1772 other perturbations.
Eif4h did not phenocopy the literature-obvious cap-dependent initiation comparators Eif4a2 or Eif4g1, even though Eif4a2 was the top unbiased positive neighbor.
Eif4h was also separable from FMRP/mTOR translational-control targets: Tsc2 produced a broad multi-group response, whereas Mtor was small and Rptor, Fmr1, and Cyfip1 were nearly or completely flat.
Eif5a loss produced a two-gene, two-cell-class response rather than a pan-neuronal translation-failure signature.
Pvalb interneurons showed a solitary Nrg3 up-regulation after Eif5a perturbation.
The expected ISR, UPR, autophagy/lysosomal, and OXPHOS stress transcriptomes were absent.
Eif5a did not phenocopy the represented elongation-factor target Eef2.
The thalamic Dgkz-down call placed Eif5a on one pole of a recurrent cross-perturbation axis.
Elf2 loss produced an almost flat neuronal snRNA-seq surface: no cell group lost the Elf2 transcript at FDR<0.10 and only one non-self gene passed FDR<0.10 across all 23 recovered groups.
The only robust Elf2-dependent neuronal transcript was Stxbp2, up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Elf2 did not engage the literature-predicted BAP31–ELF2–VCP axis in juvenile neurons.
Measurable ETS and endothelial-receptor comparators failed to phenocopy Elf2.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors did not reveal a hidden Elf2 module.

Elp1 caused a sharply restricted neuronal response: six of 21 measured groups had downstream FDR<0.10 genes, with 830 of the signal calls concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and smaller same-program fragments in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The same-complex target Elp2 was the top non-safe Elp1 signature neighbor and shared 166 FDR<0.10 calls with Elp1, all in the same direction.
Acute loss of the represented tRNA-modification enzymes Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1 did not reproduce the Elp1/Elp2 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.

Elp1 up-regulated an ATF4-linked amino-acid, one-carbon, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase program: Asns, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Slc7a1, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Mthfd2, Aldh1l2, Cars, Mars1, Aars, Lars, and Eprs were induced in the thalamic response, with subsets recurring in 145, 155, and 191.
Elp1 activated an ER protein-quality-control branch marked by Herpud1 in 151, 145, and 155, plus Xbp1 in 151 and Stt3b in 191.
Srsf5 was down-regulated in five Elp1 responder groups and Ddx17 in three, nominating RNA-processing factor loss as a recurrent secondary marker of the Elp1 state.
Elp1 can drive a central postmitotic neuronal ISR/UPR within 3-4 weeks, outside the peripheral sensory and autonomic lineages classically emphasized in familial dysautonomia.
The dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response paired ATF4/UPR induction with down-regulation of neuronal synaptic, cytoskeletal, and RNA-processing genes.
Beyond Elp2, the strongest positive Elp1 neighbors were Gfpt1, Atp2a2, Dhdds, and Hspa5, all with same-direction raw cosine similarity and same-direction significant overlap on Elp1 coordinates.
The strongest raw non-safe anticorrelates to Elp1 failed a robust FDR-overlap test and should not be interpreted as inverse biology.
Elp2 caused a pathway-scale response almost only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; all other responders were single-gene, marginal surfaces.
Elp1, the only assayed alternative Elongator subunit, was the strongest positive Elp2 neighbor and reproduced the 151 ATF4/amino-acid signature in the same directions.
Elp2 did not phenocopy represented non-Elongator tRNA-modification targets in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 Elp2 signature contains a high-confidence ATF4/integrated-stress-response program.
Elp2-perturbed 151 cells up-regulated a tRNA-charging and amino-acid supply module.
Non-obvious ER and proteostasis perturbations, especially Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Dhdds, converged on the Elp2 151 signature, but Elp2 lacked a full BiP/Xbp1 chaperone UPR.
The stress-positive 151 population also down-regulated neuronal, synaptic-vesicle, calcium-channel, and cytoskeletal transcripts.
Srsf5 and a broader RNA-processing/RNP module decreased under Elp2 loss, with Srsf5 recurring as the single significant 155 MB Glut gene.
Restricted-signature anti-neighbors of Elp2 were vector artifacts rather than robust inverse perturbations.
En1 produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered P16 postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
The En1 perturbation surface is missing 215 MB Dopa, the cell class most directly predicted by adult Engrailed dopaminergic-maintenance literature.
En1 has no robust data-driven signature neighbor and does not converge with En2 or other assayed homeobox/Pbx relatives.
The assayed En1 loss did not elicit expected dopaminergic mitochondrial, oxidative-stress, UPR/ISR, or organizer-marker transcriptional proxies.
En2 produced a one-gene CTX-CGE GABA response, up-regulating Tmem191 and no other transcript at FDR<0.10.
The En1 paralog did not phenocopy En2: En1 had zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the 22 matched groups, no CTX-CGE Tmem191 effect, and only a weak global score correlation with En2.
En2 loss did not activate the expected Pvalb/Sst/GABA-receptor, Ndufs1/Ndufs3, or Snca programs in any recovered cell group.
The data-driven En2 nearest neighbors were correlations close to zero rather than strong convergent modules.
Eng loss of function produced a neuronal pan-null: 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the remaining 215 MB Dopa group was not recovered for Eng.

The ENG pathway did not silently reappear through related TGFβ/BMP receptors: Acvrl1 and Tgfbr3 were completely flat, Smad4 was flat, and 16 represented TGFβ/BMP comparator perturbations produced only seven isolated one-gene hits across 350 matched neuronal tests.
Whole-universe score-vector neighbors of Eng were near zero, including a safe-target neighbor, and their DE surfaces were absent or one-gene only.
Acute P16 Eno1 loss produced no corrected single-nucleus transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The Eno1 null is most consistent with pre-existing mature-neuronal enolase buffering rather than transcriptional induction of another enolase isoform.

ENO1's canonical glycolysis and cancer metabolic-reprogramming priors did not map onto an HIF/MYC, lactate, UPR/ISR, or oxidative-phosphorylation transcriptional program in healthy postmitotic neurons.
No other perturbation in the directly queried universe converged with or opposed Eno1 in a meaningful way.
Ep300 single-gene loss did not produce a robust steady-state transcriptional response in any of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
Canonical immediate-early and plasticity transcripts were absent from the Ep300 DE surface.
The measurable KAT3 paralog Crebbp did not broadly phenocopy Ep300 in the matched screen universe.
Other transcriptional and chromatin regulators were FDR-level responders in the same cell groups where Ep300 was silent.
Ep300's nearest whole-transcriptome neighbors were almost correlation-free flat responders.
Epha10 loss of function yielded a single FDR<0.10 downstream transcript: Trappc5 up-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
The Epha10 DE surface did not recover transcript-level MAPK/ERK, Rho-family, stress, autophagy, NANOG, MMP9 or E-cadherin outputs expected from Eph signaling or EPHA10 cancer literature.
Neither the weak data-driven neighbors nor the measured Eph-family relatives phenocopied the Epha10 CTX-CGE Trappc5 response.
Twenty-one of the 22 measured Epha10 cell groups had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a modest median negative Epha10 self-logFC.
Epha2 loss of function was pan-neuronally buffered at the steady-state mRNA level: every one of the 23 measured neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Programs predicted from Epha2 lens and glioblastoma biology were specifically absent in the neuronal data.
Epha2 did not phenocopy other Eph receptors or proximal EphA2 signaling neighbors represented in the same screen.
The nearest data-driven Epha2 neighbors were essentially correlation-of-noise hits, while unrelated neuronal stress and synaptic perturbations produced large signatures in the same parquet.
Acute Epha2 knockdown did not create an obvious normal-neuron transcriptional liability, but the result should not be extrapolated to the main EphA2 therapeutic compartments.
Epha3 produced a pan-measured transcriptional null: 0 non-self downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered cell groups.
Epha3 did not transcriptionally converge with represented Eph/ephrin receptors or ADAM10, Psen1, Src-family, Rho/Rac, MAPK, CHN1, and PAK pathway neighbors.
Unbiased target-neighbor search rejected substantive positive and negative Epha3 signature neighbors.
The postmitotic neuronal Epha3 null separates EPHA3 oncology and cardiac developmental biology from a normal-neuron loss-of-function stress program.

Five groups showed significant Epha4 mRNA depletion but no downstream genes, showing that postnatal Epha4 loss is usually transcriptionally buffered in this assay.
Full-transcriptome signature neighbors of Epha4 were extremely weak and did not reproduce the Tmsb10 Sst event.
Represented Eph receptors and Rho/Pak actin nodes did not phenocopy Epha4.
The juvenile brain-neuron Epha4 knockout did not elicit an ALS-like survival or proteostasis transcriptional program.
Epha5 produced exactly one robust downstream hit: Lnpep was down-regulated in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and no other measured Epha5 cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Loss of Epha5 after P16 did not recover the expected Eph/ephrin axon-guidance, Rho-cytoskeletal, or synaptic transcriptional programs; the whole Epha5 surface contained only Lnpep at FDR<0.10.

The Eph-family comparators represented in the parquet did not converge with Epha5: Epha2, Epha3, Ephb2 and Ephb4 were fully flat, Epha10/Epha4/Ephb1 each produced only one off-target-cell hit, and none reproduced the 012 Lnpep decrease.
The unbiased 440-feature Epha5 cosine search returned only low-amplitude neighbors and no robust shared FDR program.
Rare EPHA5 dosage links to ASD and mouse behavioral phenotypes are not accompanied here by an acute postmitotic neurodevelopmental transcriptional signature.
Ephb1 loss produced a single significant downstream transcript, Tmem135 down, restricted to 308 CB GABA.
Eph-family receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Ephb1: Ephb2 and Ephb4 were flat, while Epha4, Epha5, and Epha10 showed unrelated one-gene hits in other cell groups.
Direct Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbations generated multi-gene transcriptional signatures, but Ephb1 and Fyn did not, separating EphB1-NMDAR physical signaling from the Grin nuclear response.
The whole-surface Ephb1 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor; the best full-coverage signed-score correlations were near zero.
Ephb2 loss was a pan-recovered-neuron transcriptional null in the P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR screen.
Ephb2 did not phenocopy NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations at the transcriptional level.
Single Eph-family receptor perturbations converged in flatness rather than producing cell-type-specific transcriptomes.
The EphB2→Kalirin/Rac/PAK spine-morphogenesis branch was not represented as a recurrent transcriptomic signature.
Unbiased Ephb2 signature neighbors were near-zero and biologically unconvincing.
The juvenile healthy Ephb2 null should not be used as a negative test of EphB2 augmentation in Alzheimer models.
Ephb4 loss was flat across all recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 22 measured groups.

The measurable Eph/NMDAR neighborhood did not phenocopy Grin2b: Grin2b produced 78 matched-group DE genes, whereas Ephb4 and most EphB-adjacent receptor or cytoskeletal perturbations were flat or singleton-only.
Ephb4 had no meaningful full-transcriptome signature neighbor; the largest positive and negative Pearson correlations were only 0.027 and -0.016.
The Ephb4 neuronal null should not be read as lack of EphB4 druggability or lack of vascular risk.
Acute mosaic Epm2a loss produced no BH-corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The expected glycogen-quality-control and stress-marker transcripts remained BH-null after Epm2a perturbation.
Cortical GABAergic classes CTX-CGE, Pvalb, and Sst did not show a preferential early Epm2a response.
Data-driven Epm2a score neighbors were too weak to define a convergent or opposing perturbation module.
Direct Lafora/glycogen relatives were unavailable as perturbations, and indirect glycogen-energy targets Gaa, Gsk3b, and Prkag2 did not converge with Epm2a.
Acute neuronal snRNA markers are poor pharmacodynamic readouts for laforin biology in this perturbation window.
Epor loss produced a single FDR-level downstream hit, Ifitm10 down-regulation, and that hit was confined to 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Pvalb Ifitm10 response occurred without detectable induction or repression of the canonical EPOR/JAK-STAT survival-feedback transcript set.
Sin3a, not the represented EPOR pathway effectors or the very-low-cosine whole-signature neighbors, was the only measured target that converged with Epor on FDR-level Pvalb Ifitm10 down-regulation.
P16 Erbb3 loss caused no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured NeuN-enriched neuronal cell groups.
The measured NRG/ERBB relatives Erbb4, Nrg1, Nrg2, and Nrg3 did not reveal an Erbb3-like neuronal transcriptomic module.
Canonical ERBB3 effector targets in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR and RAS-MAPK transcriptional neighborhood did not phenocopy Erbb3.
The unbiased signature-neighbor scan found no robust positive or negative Erbb3 neighbor; all score-vector correlations were near zero.
Erbb4 RNA itself fell in the two measured inhibitory groups with FDR-level on-target evidence, but neither group produced a downstream transcriptome at FDR<0.10.
The receptor-family and neuregulin-ligand targets that were directly represented in the screen did not phenocopy Erbb4.
Erbb4 was flat in places where synaptic and PI3K/mTOR comparators were detectably transcriptional.
An unbiased search over all 1773 model-visible targets found no robust Erbb4 signature neighbor.
Erf perturbation yielded no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered juvenile postmitotic neuronal group.
Expected ETS/MAPK, retinoic-acid neurogenic, proliferation, EMT, and osteogenic sentinel transcripts were not derepressed by Erf loss.
Cic responded strongly in matched neuronal groups whereas Erf was flat, separating two RTK/RAS/MAPK-linked transcriptional repressors.
Represented FGFR-RAS-MAPK and ETS-family comparators did not converge with Erf.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no high-confidence Erf convergence partner.
Esr1 loss produced a single robust response, Nfic induction, restricted to 155 MB Glut.
The canonical ERα transcriptional surface was buffered: 21 of 22 measured Esr1 cell groups had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and Pgr/Tac/Kiss1-like hypothalamic markers were absent.
Represented estrogen-family and nuclear-receptor comparators did not phenocopy Esr1 in 155 MB Glut.
The data-driven Esr1 signature neighborhood was essentially flat, with top real positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations all |rho| ≤ 0.0334.
ESRRA, unlike Esr1, generated a broad thalamic transcriptional phenotype in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Esr2 loss caused a near-flat baseline transcriptome: 23 cell groups were tested, only Slc2a3 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Jmjd6 in 155 MB Glut passed downstream FDR<0.10, and whole-surface neighbors had near-zero cosine values.
Esr2 perturbation up-regulated the neuronal glucose transporter gene Slc2a3 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and no accompanying glycolytic or hypoxic transcriptional module reached FDR<0.10.
Esr2 up-regulated Jmjd6 in 155 MB Glut, and the same Jmjd6-up row recurred in that cell group after Psmb4, Psmc1, Prpf6, and Tpr perturbations.
The measured estrogen-receptor and p160-coactivator perturbations Esr1, Gper1, Ncoa1, and Ncoa3 did not converge with Esr2 and did not share the Slc2a3 or Jmjd6 responder genes.
Esrra loss generated a strong 86-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program while Esr2 had zero FDR genes in the same broad cell class.
Esrra loss produced a single robust downstream signature, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 signature recovered the expected ERRα/PGC-1 oxidative-metabolism arm.
Esrra coupled oxidative metabolism to ion-handling and synaptic genes in thalamic glutamatergic neurons rather than in the literature-obvious Pvalb interneuron group.
direction_pattern: mostly down in 151; absent in Pvalb Gaba

canonical_summary: A secondary extracellular-matrix, adhesion, and axonal module accompanied the metabolic response in 151 cells.
Textbook relatives did not phenocopy Esrra in the 151 responder group.
Nrf1 was a strong 151 mitochondrial perturbation but shared little of the Esrra FDR signature.
The strongest robust noncanonical convergence came from Psmb4 and Camta1, not from ESRR-family genes.
Cic loss opposed the signed Esrra 151 state.
Esrrb perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered P16 brain neuronal groups.
Among ERR-axis comparators, Esrra alone generated a resolved 86-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Esrrb, Esrrg, and Ppargc1a were flat in the matched surface.
The strongest unbiased Esrrb signature neighbors were near-zero correlations to other flat perturbations rather than a coherent positive or anticorrelated module.
Esrrg produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation.
The canonical ERRgamma mitochondrial/Tfam/OXPHOS readout was absent, including in the midbrain dopaminergic bin where adult conditional Esrrg loss is reported to depress mitochondrial transcripts.

The literature-obvious ERR/PGC-1 comparators did not phenocopy Esrrg: Esrra had a discrete 86-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Esrrb and Ppargc1a were FDR-flat and all score correlations to Esrrg were near zero.
Data-driven neighbors also collapsed to near-zero similarity: the strongest non-control positive neighbor was Kcnq3 with r=0.029, and the strongest negative neighbor was Ddhd1 with r=-0.023.
Etfa produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of its 21 measured neuronal cell groups despite Etfa itself being assayed in each group.

Etfa did not converge with represented ETF/FAO-adjacent perturbations: Ivd, PPAR/PGC1 regulators, and Cpt1c were flat or nearly flat, while the same-complex Etfb and Etfdh targets were absent from the screen.
Opa1, Nrf1, and Esrra produced robust mitochondrial or ISR-like signatures in groups where Etfa remained flat.
Etfa's full-surface data-driven neighbors were all near zero in score-correlation space, with Fbxo11 r=0.044 as the top positive and Erbb4 r=-0.017 as the top negative.
Ets1 loss was a pan-neuronal null in this P16-to-P37/P44 mosaic CRISPR snRNA-seq experiment: all 23 assayed neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The data-driven Ets1 signature neighborhood was indistinguishable from a null surface: the top non-safe positive neighbor was Cdkn2a at r=0.0260 and the strongest inverse neighbor was Atl3 at r=-0.0196.
Represented ETS-family targets and Ras-MAPK/BMP pathway nodes did not phenocopy Ets1 in matched neuronal groups.
Previously reported Ets1 effector transcripts from axon-growth and neural-crest programs were absent: Lcn2, Hdac1, Id3, Bmp2, Bmp4, Msx2, and Snai2 never reached FDR<0.10 after Ets1 perturbation.

The screen did not convert Ets1 into a neuronal autoimmune-risk program: robust B- and T-cell Ets1 biology is displaced to lineages that were absent or strongly depleted from the NeuN-enriched neuronal assay.
Postnatal Etv6 loss produced an extremely sparse neuronal transcriptomic surface: 2 of 23 tested cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responder contained only one such gene.
Etv6 loss up-regulated Adora1 as the single FDR-level hit in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Etv6 loss up-regulated the chromatin enzyme Kdm4c as the only FDR-level hit in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Prox1, a data-driven positive neighbor of the weak Etv6 signature, independently up-regulated Adora1 in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group.
Sin3a, a measurable corepressor-pathway comparator, down-regulated Adora1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut whereas Etv6 up-regulated Adora1 there.
Other ETS-family targets represented in the parquet, Elf2, Erf, Ets1, and Spi1, did not phenocopy the Etv6 Adora1 or Kdm4c outputs.
The screen did not recover ETV6-linked interferon, apoptosis, UPR/ISR, or megakaryocyte-marker programs after Etv6 loss in any neuronal cell group.
P16 acute mosaic Ext1 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal class.
Ext1 perturbation failed to induce the expected heparan-sulfate feedback, FGF/ERK, Hedgehog, WNT, Slit/Robo, or Eph transcriptional reporters.
The data-driven Ext1 neighborhood was null-like, and the closest non-safe neighbor, B3gat3, did not mark a coherent heparan-sulfate module.
The postnatal Ext1 phenotype most consistent with this dataset is a silent-to-snRNA synaptic glycan defect rather than an ISR, UPR, or morphogen-transcription phenotype.
Ext2 mRNA could be reduced without producing a corrected downstream neuronal transcriptome.
The corrected Ext2 signature is two down-regulated neuronal connectivity genes: Epha5 in L2/3 IT cortex and Slc6a17 in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons.
P16 Ext2 loss did not recover the embryonic FGF/Wnt morphogen-output program predicted from developmental Ext2 and HS work.
Ext1, the obligatory same-complex partner of Ext2, did not phenocopy even the sparse Ext2 transcriptional surface.
Other represented HS-linkage, HS-modifying, and HSPG-core perturbations were also decoupled from Ext2.
The unbiased Ext2 signature-neighbor search found no meaningful global convergence or antagonism.
F2 loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a coagulation, PAR, stress, or synaptic program in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
F2 had no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor; even the extremal whole-universe score correlations were approximately zero.
The expected thrombin/PAR receptor and AP-1/NF-kappaB injury readouts were measurable but absent after F2 perturbation.
The neuronal CRISPR null does not model systemic thrombin inhibition or the human F2 20210G>A thrombophilia allele.
Fam120a loss caused an almost fully buffered basal neuronal transcriptome: 23 cell groups were measured, but only Hgs in Pvalb GABA and Luc7l3 in MB glutamatergic neurons reached FDR<0.10.
Pvalb GABA neurons showed a single FDR<0.10 response, Hgs up-regulation, after Fam120a perturbation.
MB glutamatergic neurons showed a single FDR<0.10 response, Luc7l3 down-regulation, after Fam120a perturbation.
Fam120a did not engage the neuronal mTORC1/SREBP sterol module even though the same assay detected it after Tsc2 activation and Srebf2 loss in MB Glut.
Fyn, Pik3r1, Pik3cb, and Akt3 perturbations did not converge with Fam120a, and none reproduced the Hgs or Luc7l3 singletons.
Ago1, Ago2, and Tnrc6a produced flat or tiny DE surfaces and did not phenocopy Fam120a.
The top data-driven Wilcoxon-score neighbors of Fam120a were not strong: the best positive cosine was Nefl at 0.0337 and the best negative cosine was Atrn at -0.0179.
Fam120a is much flatter than several represented schizophrenia rare-variant comparators in the same assay, especially Setd1a.
Fam149b produced a single FDR-level downstream change, Sin3b down-regulation, confined to 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Fam149b loss did not recover the expected GLI/PTCH readout or a secondary IFT/cilium RNA module in any assayed neuronal group.
The represented same-pathway ciliary comparators were nearly flat and did not phenocopy the Fam149b Sin3b response.
A whole-transcriptome score-neighbor search gave only near-zero Fam149b neighbors and anti-neighbors.

Far1 loss-of-function produced an ultra-sparse neuronal transcriptional response: exactly two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 21 measured cell groups, Insig1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Tial1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

canonical_summary: The hypothalamic GABA Far1 hit lands on the INSIG/SREBP sterol-feedback node: Far1 and Tsc2 perturbations both increased Insig1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, whereas direct Srebf2 perturbation decreased Insig1.
Far1 induced the RNA-binding/stress-granule gene Tial1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without accompanying FDR<0.10 ISR, unfolded-protein, redox, synaptic-vesicle, or peroxisome sentinel genes.

Canonical ether-lipid and peroxisome perturbations did not phenocopy Far1: Agps had only three non-overlapping thalamic genes, Pex14 had zero downstream genes despite strong self-transcript drops in several groups, and Pex1/Hsd17b4/Abcd3/Acbd5 were essentially flat.
Far1 did not elicit a broad sterol, peroxisome, ISR/UPR-redox, or synaptic-vesicle mRNA program; only Insig1 passed FDR<0.10 among the queried sentinel genes.
direction_pattern: expected sentinel programs absent after Far1

canonical_summary: The sparse LoF profile should not be treated as a model of dominant FAR1 Arg480 disease, whose mechanism is feedback escape with elevated ether-lipid synthesis rather than Far1 loss.

canonical_summary: Fars2 CRISPR did not produce a robust downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal population measured for the target.

The expected ATF4/ISR, mitochondrial chaperone/protease, and mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS RNA programs were absent after Fars2 perturbation even though Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations show that such genes are detectable in this analysis universe.
The represented mitochondrial aaRS relatives Rars2 and Lars2 were also almost flat and did not converge with Fars2.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful transcriptional neighbor for Fars2.

Fas loss was globally buffered in recovered juvenile NeuN+ neurons, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 row across 22 measured cell groups and no detectable apoptosis, NFkappaB/JNK, or stress-gene program.
Pafah1b2 was the sole Fas-induced FDR<0.10 gene, up in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Measured TNFR/death/NFkappaB/MAPK neighbors failed to phenocopy Fas despite known pathway proximity.
Whole-universe signature neighbors of Fas were quantitatively negligible.
Fbn1 loss was nearly globally buffered in postnatal NeuN+ neurons, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 row across 371796 non-self tests in 22 measured cell groups.
Dym was the sole FDR<0.10 Fbn1-response gene and was upregulated in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Fbn1 did not phenocopy represented fibrillin/TGFβ comparators and did not induce a detectable TGFβ/ECM target-gene panel.
Unbiased Fbn1 signature neighbors computed from nominal p<0.001 rows did not yield an FDR-level convergent module on re-test.

Fbxo11 loss produced a highly buffered postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: among nine recovered cell groups, only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and that response was a single Ppib decrease.
direction_pattern: buffered; Ppib down only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

canonical_summary: Ppib is the sole robust Fbxo11-responsive transcript and is down-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; canonical UPR/ISR transcripts such as Hspa5, Ddit3, Atf4, and Xbp1 did not reach FDR<0.10.

The top empirical neighbors of the restricted Fbxo11 rank signature were Dscam, B9d1, and Nfib, while En1, Rack1, and Dcaf8 were the strongest anti-neighbors, but their actual FDR<0.10 surfaces did not share the Fbxo11 Ppib hit.
Represented literature-obvious comparators in the F-box, p53, TGF/SMAD, and Snail axes were nearly flat in the same nine cell groups and did not reproduce Fbxo11's Ppib response.

FBXO11 proteasome biology did not manifest as a persistent postnatal neuronal UPR/ISR transcriptome: Ppib alone changed, while Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, and Xbp1 were non-significant in the Fbxo11 DE surface.
Fbxo38 produced an extremely sparse neuronal response: 2 single-gene responder groups among 22 measured groups, with 20 measured groups lacking downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Fbxo38 loss uniquely up-regulated Hdac2 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Fbxo38 loss down-regulated the TRAPP-complex gene Trappc11 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Direct Klf7 loss was transcriptionally visible in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Fbxo38 loss in the same cell group did not recover a KLF7-like transcriptomic effect.
The top data-driven perturbation neighbors of Fbxo38 were tiny-amplitude similarities and did not reproduce its responder groups.
Trappc11 moved in the opposite direction under Fbxo38 than under broad Psmc1 and U2af2 perturbations in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Fbxw7 loss-of-function produced a single adjusted-significant downstream gene, Trp53inp2, and only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Acute postnatal Fbxw7 knockout did not recover canonical FBXW7 substrate-output transcriptional programs.
Fbxw7 does not phenocopy mTOR/SREBP-axis perturbations that are detectable in the same neuronal groups.
Fbxw7 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor in the full target universe.
Available Notch-pathway perturbations were themselves nearly silent in the Fbxw7-matched postnatal neuronal groups.
The FBXW7 neurodevelopmental signal is displaced from an acute juvenile pan-neuronal transcriptional phenotype.
Fcgr4 loss of function produced no robust cell-autonomous transcriptional response in any measured NeuN-enriched neuronal cell group.
Fcgr4 had no meaningful signed transcriptomic neighbor in the whole parquet universe.
The screen could not test FcγR-family redundancy around Fcgr4 because the closest receptor and ITAM-adaptor comparators were mostly absent as perturbation targets.
The pan-neuronal null should not be used to deprioritize FcγRIV biology in antibody effector or neuroinflammatory settings.
Fezf1 loss produced a single robust transcriptional response, Dtx3 up-regulation in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
The expected Fezf1/Fezf2-Hes5-Neurog2 neurogenic cascade, olfactory sensory markers, and Gnrh1 were absent from the P16 postmitotic Fezf1 DE surface.
Represented cortical-fate, Notch, and Kallmann-neighborhood perturbations failed to phenocopy the Fezf1 L5 ET Dtx3/Pde2a response.
A data-driven two-gene L5 ET comparison found Fezf1 itself at the top for Dtx3 induction, no robust positive phenocopy, and Ranbp2/Yy1 as opposite Dtx3 regulators.
Fgd4 loss produced a complete FDR-level null across the recovered NeuN+ mouse-brain cell groups.
The neuronal null fits a Schwann/PNS-centric CMT4H mechanism rather than a broad mature brain-neuron transcriptomic requirement for Fgd4.
The FRABIN-Cdc42/Rac/PAK actin axis did not become a shared neuronal DE module.
NRG1/ERBB/mTOR and endosomal-CMT comparators failed to define an Fgd4-like neuronal module.
The all-target signature search yielded only near-zero Fgd4 neighbors.
Fgf12 CRISPR loss was almost completely buffered at the snRNA-seq level, with a singleton Nmnat2 response confined to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
The sole robust Fgf12 downstream gene, Nmnat2, points to an axon-maintenance transcript rather than to altered Nav-subunit mRNA.
Hspa5 was the only same-direction FDR-level neighbor of the Fgf12 Nmnat2 coordinate, but its broader ER-stress signature did not accompany Fgf12 loss.
The measured FHF/Nav relatives did not phenocopy Fgf12 in the MH-LH TH group, so Nmnat2 is not a generic transcriptional consequence of reducing Nav-channel complex activity.
A sparse postnatal Fgf12 loss-of-function transcriptome should not be read as a negative test of FGF12 channelopathy mechanisms or sodium-channel-blocker logic.
Acute Fgf13 loss produced a single FDR-level downstream marker, Rell2 down-regulation, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Fgf13 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across nearly the entire juvenile neuronal atlas despite measurable self-transcript loss in several groups.

The pre-literature whole-surface signature-neighbor search produced only near-zero correlations, and the nearest non-control positive and negative targets failed to reproduce the Rell2-containing thalamic response.
Represented FHF, NaV, and receptor-FGF perturbations did not phenocopy Fgf13 in the matched snRNA-seq surface.
P16 sparse Fgf1 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptome in any recovered cell group.
Fgf1 LoF did not produce the canonical FGFR-RAS/MAPK immediate-early or ERK-feedback transcript program.
Directly measured FGFR/RAS/ERK-neighbor perturbations also failed to converge on a broad Fgf1-like state.
The represented Fgf-family paralogs were rejected as Fgf1 phenocopies.
The data-driven nearest-neighbor search did not nominate a robust Fgf1 module.
Hypothalamic Fgf1 LoF was not a transcriptional mirror of pharmacologic central FGF1 action.
Fgfr1 loss produced an exceptionally sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptomic surface: only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured cell groups.
CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic neurons carried the only negative Fgfr1 downstream call, Hnrnpm down-regulation.
Cerebellar GABA neurons carried the only positive Fgfr1 downstream call, Nipa1 up-regulation.
Fgfr1 perturbation did not lower canonical MAPK-feedback transcripts, and core MAPK-relay perturbations did not converge with the two Fgfr1 responder loci.
Fgfr2, Fgfr3, and the receptor-like Fgfrl1 were measurable but did not phenocopy Fgfr1 in the two Fgfr1 responder groups.
The represented FGF-family perturbations, Fgf1, Fgf12, and Fgf13, did not identify an autocrine FGF module feeding the Fgfr1 two-gene response.

The unbiased Fgfr1 signature-neighbor search yielded no robust biological neighbor: the best whole-vector correlations were near zero, and the two-gene restricted neighbors were only nominal at the matched loci.
Fgfr2 loss produced a single significant CA3-family hit, Ccsap up-regulation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, suggesting a narrow ciliary or centrosomal response rather than a broad FGF program.
Fgfr2 did not recover canonical FGF/ERK feedback genes even though Braf and Map2k1 perturbations elicited a MAPK-linked Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a/Etv5 program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Measured FGFR-family and nearby FGF-pathway perturbations were sparse singleton/null surfaces and did not phenocopy the Fgfr2 CA3 Ccsap response.

The broad postnatal neuronal null contrasts with FGFR2 gain-of-function craniosynostosis and cancer biology, refining those disease priors to stage, allele class, and lineage contexts not modeled here.
Fgfr2’s best restricted-signature neighbors were weak non-FGFR targets, Ghsr in the same direction and Oprk1 in the opposite direction, with low absolute cosines near 0.125.
Fgfr3 loss of function was almost completely buffered at the single-nucleus transcriptome level across P16-to-P37/44 neurons, with only one downstream gene in one measured cell group at FDR<0.10.
Hook3 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the single Fgfr3-selective downstream call.
The represented FGFR-family perturbations did not phenocopy each other in P16 neurons.
Fgfr3 was uncoupled from the detectable Braf/Map2k1 neuronal MAPK-output module.
Fgfr3 had no robust data-driven cross-perturbation neighbor.
This Fgfr3 loss-of-function screen is an acute neuron-intrinsic liability test, not a phenocopy of activating FGFR3 disease alleles or glial developmental FGFR3 biology.
Fgfrl1 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
The expected FGF/ERK feedback and published embryonic kidney Fgfrl1-output genes were assayed but absent after postnatal neuronal Fgfrl1 perturbation.
Classical Fgfr1-Fgfr3 receptor perturbations were directly measurable yet did not converge with Fgfrl1.
Unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbor analysis did not nominate a credible Fgfrl1-like module.
Acute neuronal Fgfrl1 loss should not be read out as canonical FGFR/RAF kinase inhibition.
Fhit loss was a pan-measured-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
Fhit had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the 1773-target universe; the largest genome-wide Wilcoxon-score correlations were only Cit r=0.0337 and Safe_target_23 r=-0.0208.

The literature-obvious FHIT comparators did not reveal a hidden fragile-site or checkpoint family signature: Wwox, Atr, Trp53, and Bcl2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in their matched Fhit groups, while stress and autophagy perturbations such as Hsf1, Hspa5, Rb1cc1, Mtor, and Nfe2l1 did generate detectable but cell-restricted signatures.
Acute Figla loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured postmitotic brain-neuron groups.
The expected Figla ovarian regulon was absent in neurons, and measurable oocyte-network perturbations, Nobox, Sohlh1, Pou5f1, Tcf3 and Tcf4, did not reveal a shared transcriptional module.

Figla had no meaningful DE-signature neighbor: its nearest Wilcoxon-score correlations were near zero, and unrelated neighbors Ranbp2 and Wdr26 generated hundreds to thousands of DE genes in the same assay where Figla was flat.
Fkbp1a loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal zero downstream transcriptome in the basal P16-to-P37/44 snRNA assay: 23 of 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at BH FDR<0.10.
Detectable Fkbp1a self-transcript reduction was still locally buffered: L5 ET CTX and TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons showed significant Fkbp1a mRNA depletion, yet each retained 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The FKBP12-to-mTORC1 expectation was not recovered: Fkbp1a was uncorrelated with Mtor, Rptor, and the mTORC1 disinhibitor Tsc2, while Tsc2 loss produced 636 downstream genes where Fkbp1a was flat.

No FKBP12-dependent TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD transcriptional program appeared; direct Tgfbr1, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad3, and Smad4 perturbations were also completely flat, and Tgfbr2, Acvr1, and Smad2 produced only one to two single-gene hits.

The calcium-channel/calcineurin branch also failed to leave a coordinated RNA footprint: Itpr1, Ryr3, Ppp3cc, and Nfatc3 were flat, Ppp3ca returned only six downstream genes, Ryr2 only one, and Fkbp1a returned none.

The data-driven nearest-neighbor search found no real Fkbp1a module: the strongest positive score neighbor was only r=0.032 and the strongest negative was r=-0.014 after excluding Safe_target controls.
The MB dopamine result is not a Parkinsonian FKBP12 test: only 20 Fkbp1a-targeted MB Dopa nuclei were recovered and no FDR<0.10 downstream RNA change accompanied Fkbp1a loss.
Fktn CRISPR produced a single robust downstream event: Plxdc2 induction in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
The Fktn Plxdc2 response was not phenocopied by measured α-dystroglycan/matriglycan or dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex perturbations.
P16 neuronal Fktn loss did not elicit a broad ECM, glycosylation, stress, proteostasis, autophagy, redox, or synaptic transcriptional program.
The data reinforce that postnatal NeuN+ neuronal snRNA-seq is a poor standalone pharmacodynamic readout for FKTN brain rescue.
Flnb produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The Flnb surface is uncoupled from represented FLNB actin, integrin, Rho-family, and BMP/TGF-beta/Smad pathway neighbors.
The unbiased Flnb nearest-neighbor signature is effectively random rather than a coherent module.
The screen refines FLNB disease biology away from an acute mature-neuron transcriptomic LoF mechanism.
P16 Flrt3 loss produced an ultra-sparse nuclear RNA response: only Dapk1 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Odc1 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The two Flrt3-regulated transcripts nominate Dapk1 and Odc1 as weak, cell-restricted sentinel genes rather than members of the canonical FLRT adhesion machinery.

Represented FLRT3-adjacent adhesion and guidance targets did not phenocopy Flrt3: Adgrl1/2/3, Unc5c/d, Tenm3/4, Lrrtm3, Robo1, and Dcc were completely flat in matched groups, while Lrrtm1, Lrrtm4, and Nrxn1 produced only unrelated singletons.
Global cross-perturbation search did not uncover a robust hidden Flrt3 neighbor: the strongest full-surface signed-score correlations were Pdx1 at r=0.02817 and Calm2 at r=-0.01588.
Flt3 loss produced a selective, one-gene Gak-up response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and nowhere else in the measured neuronal surface.
The Flt3 neuronal DE surface did not recover canonical FLT3 STAT5, PI3K, RAS-MAPK, survival, or inflammatory transcriptional output.
Neither the top score-vector neighbors nor represented RTK relatives phenocopied the Flt3 L5 ET Gak event.
Flt4 loss produced a single corrected cerebellar GABA response: down-regulation of the ERAD E3-ligase gene Tmem129.
The Flt4 transcriptional response was restricted to 308 CB GABA and consisted of one gene; all other 22 neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Canonical VEGFR3-pathway comparators did not phenocopy Flt4: Kdr, Nrp1, Nrp2, Prox1, Sox18, Notch1, Tek, and Flt3 all failed to regulate Tmem129 in 308 CB GABA, and Prox1 instead produced a separate 64-gene thalamic signature.
Flt4 loss did not induce VEGF receptor, lymphatic-endothelial identity, or neural progenitor marker programs in any measured postmitotic neuronal cell group.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Flt4 were essentially zero-correlation and were rejected as biological phenocopies.
Flvcr1 was a pan-null perturbation across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups, with zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
No strong data-driven signature neighbor emerged for Flvcr1; the best non-safe positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were only +0.0315 for Eef2 and -0.0155 for Auts2.
Expected ISR, UPR, heme-stress, Kennedy-pathway, and heme-biosynthesis markers were unchanged after Flvcr1 perturbation.
Represented literature-obvious comparators Itpr1, Mcph1, and Tfrc did not reveal a matched postnatal neuronal FLVCR1 module.
The P16 postmitotic neuronal screen supports a bounded disease model: FLVCR1-associated pathology is not reproduced as an acute pan-brain neuronal transcriptional injury state.
Fmn1 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered in every recovered neuronal class: 22 of 23 groups were tested and none contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

Fmn1 did not seed a formin/Rho transcriptional module: its best genome-scale signature neighbors had |r|<=0.036, and Fmn2, Diaph2, Cdc42, Rac1, and Rala were also absent or single-gene responders in the matched surface.

The Fmn1 limb-BMP signature was not redeployed in neurons: BMP sentinels Msx1, Grem1, Id1, Id2, Id3, Bmp2, Bmp4, and Bmp7 all remained FDR=1.0 after Fmn1 perturbation, and BMP receptor targets were flat or isolated single-gene responders.

The adherens-junction branch was separable from Fmn1: Ctnnb1 knockout produced a large thalamic glutamatergic signature, whereas Fmn1 was zero-hit in the same 145 and 151 groups and Ctnna2/Flnb gave at most isolated hits.

The embryonic Ngn3-Fmn1 dendritogenesis/synaptogenesis axis was absent at the RNA level: Fmn1 did not regulate synaptic or dendritic sentinel transcripts, and Neurog3, Notch1, and Notch2 perturbations were zero- or single-gene responders in the matched postnatal surface.
Acute P16 Fmn2 loss produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream calls across 22 recovered neuronal groups, with one singleton in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and one in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Ss18 was selectively up-regulated after Fmn2 perturbation in L4/5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Pign was up-regulated after Fmn2 perturbation in CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
The embryonic Fmn2/Wnt/β-catenin axis is uncoupled from the acute postmitotic Fmn2 signature.
Formin-family perturbations represented in the screen did not converge with Fmn2.
No strong data-driven signature neighbor or anti-neighbor of Fmn2 was present in the model-visible target universe.
Acute Fmr1 perturbation produced a singleton Slc25a27/UCP4 induction in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The whole Fmr1 response is nearly orthogonal to other perturbation signatures.
FXR, CYFIP, eIF4G, and group-I-mGluR single-gene perturbations do not phenocopy Fmr1 in this acute snRNA screen.
Tsc2 loss, not Fmr1 loss, is the mTOR-linked perturbation that generates a broad neuronal transcriptome in the same analysis universe.
Canonical FMRP target mRNAs and secondary stress programs are absent from the Fmr1 nuclear transcriptome.
Fntb produced a near-pan-neuronal buffered transcriptional surface: only Lhfpl4 and Nefl passed downstream FDR<0.10 across all 23 recovered cell groups, and Fntb itself was never FDR-significant.
Fntb up-regulated Lhfpl4 only in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, nominating a focal hippocampal inhibitory-synapse auxiliary response.
Fntb up-regulated Nefl in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, a low-count focal neurofilament response.
Represented FTase substrate and downstream Ras/Rheb pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Fntb in the Fntb responder cell groups.
Neither global nor restricted data-driven cross-perturbation rankings yielded a robust Fntb neighbor.
Folr1 produced a pan-measured neuronal null after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered cell groups.
Canonical folate transport, one-carbon, and neural-plate cadherin/endocytosis genes failed to appear as secondary transcriptomic programs after Folr1 perturbation.

Folr1 had no meaningful score-space neighbors; the strongest positive and negative full-surface cosines were close to zero, and the strong Wdr26 response diverged from Folr1 in the same matched groups.
Fosl2 loss-of-function was almost completely buffered in P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neurons, with one downstream gene at FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The only Fosl2-dependent downstream event was Rnf34 down-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
The measured AP-1/JUN comparator Jund and broader bZIP relatives did not converge on the Fosl2 MB Glut signature.
Fosl2 loss did not induce an AP-1/immediate-early, UPR/ISR, redox, or non-neuronal Fosl2 target program.
Basal neuronal Fosl2 CRISPR loss is not a transcriptional phenocopy of the human last-exon FOSL2 disorder.
Foxa2 produced a pan-measured null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in each of 22 recovered neuronal groups, with every Foxa2 self-row FDR=1.0.
The canonical dopamine-neuron branch was untested or off-lineage: 215 MB Dopa was missing for Foxa2, and measured MB Glut and MB P MY GABA groups had 0 downstream genes.
Foxa2 did not move the hypothalamic orexin/MCH program in recovered hypothalamic aggregates.
Neither data-driven neighbors nor canonical Foxa2 pathway comparators converged with Foxa2 into a robust shared DE module.
Acute Foxc2 loss of function was pan-null across the 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
Foxc2 did not induce the arterial VEGF-Dll4/Notch-Hey2, CXCR4, lymphatic NFATc1/ITGA9, or RhoA/ROCK cytoskeletal programs its literature predicts in endothelial cells.
Neither unbiased score-neighbors nor curated VEGF/Notch/BMP/TGF-beta/lymphatic comparators phenocopied Foxc2.
The neuronal null should not be used to discount FOXC2 as a lymphatic or vascular disease target.
Foxe3 produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Foxe3 knockout did not change a canonical lens epithelial proliferation, differentiation, crystallin, or Foxe3-linked growth-factor panel in any sampled neuronal group.
The whole-universe Foxe3 score vector had no credible convergent or divergent perturbation neighbor.
Represented upstream and disease-family lens factors did not phenocopy Foxe3 in the neuronal screen.
The Foxe3 screen result argues that FOXE3-linked ocular and aortic disease biology is not modeled by acute postnatal knockout in NeuN+ brain neurons.
Acute Foxi1 loss of function was transcriptionally inert across all measured postnatal neuronal groups.
The represented V-ATPase module did not connect Foxi1 to a neuronal acidification signature.
Foxi1 had no accepted positive or negative whole-surface signature neighbor.
Acute Foxj3 loss of function after P16 produced no robust whole-transcriptome response in any of the 21 Foxj3-measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.

The myogenic Foxj3-Mef2c regulatory axis did not fire in postnatal neurons: Foxj3 perturbation left Mef2a, Mef2c, and Mef2d at FDR=1.0 in every measured cell group, while Mef2c perturbation itself produced a cortical/Pvalb/thalamic signature that Foxj3 lacked.
Whole-surface Wilcoxon-score neighbors of Foxj3 were near zero-correlated and were rejected as biological convergence or anticonvergence.
Foxk2 produced no FDR-significant downstream response in any of 22 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 postmitotic CRISPR perturbation.
The FOXK-SIN3A autophagy/lysosome derepression program was absent after Foxk2 perturbation.
Sin3a deletion was broadly active where Foxk2 was flat, arguing that the measured SIN3A-dependent neuronal response is FOXK2-independent.
Represented mTOR, AP-1, PR-DUB/REST, Wnt, apoptosis, EP300, and E2F comparators did not converge with the Foxk2 surface.
A whole-universe phenotype-first correlation search found no meaningful Foxk2 signature neighbor.

Acute Foxl1 loss of function was transcriptomically inert across the sampled juvenile NeuN-positive neuronal groups: all 22 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.

Foxl1 did not phenocopy represented Wnt/beta-catenin or Hedgehog/Gli perturbations: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 generated hundreds of FDR<0.10 rows in Foxl1-matched neuronal groups, whereas Foxl1 had none, and Gli/Ptch/Smo correlations with Foxl1 were near zero.

The Foxl1 signature had no coherent nearest neighbor: the strongest all-gene score correlation was only r=0.034762 to Wdr26, a safe-target perturbation ranked second, and the represented Fox-family perturbations including Foxl2 and Foxj3 all had 0 FDR<0.10 rows in Foxl1-matched groups.
Foxl2 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every measured juvenile NeuN+ neuronal group.
The ovarian sex-maintenance, steroidogenic, FOXL2-SMAD/Fshb, and hypothalamic Ghrh programs expected from canonical FOXL2 biology were absent downstream of Foxl2 in brain neurons.
Foxl2 had no meaningful data-driven transcriptomic neighbor in the model-visible Perturb-seq universe.
Literature-obvious FOXL2 partners and FOX-family comparators also failed to expose a neuronal FOXL2-like state.
Foxn1 loss of function produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal class.
Canonical thymic-epithelial and hair-keratin Foxn1 effector genes were present in the neuronal DE tables but did not move after Foxn1 perturbation.
Represented forkhead-family perturbations and the available p63 epithelial regulator also failed to produce a Foxn1-like neuronal signature.
Whole-signature empirical neighbors of Foxn1 were nearly uncorrelated and had no shared FDR-supported module.
Foxp2 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of 22 measured neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.
The P16 Foxp2 perturbation did not recover CNTNAP2 or early FOXP target-gene regulation even though the nominated target genes were assayed.
The score-vector neighbors of Foxp2 were almost orthogonal, and their robust thalamic or sparse signatures did not phenocopy Foxp2.
Postnatal TF responsiveness is factor-specific: Tbr1 and Mef2c had real DE surfaces in Foxp2-matched groups, whereas Foxp2, Bcl11b, and Satb2 were flat.
The disease-linked FOXP2-CNTNAP2 axis was not engaged by juvenile mouse Foxp2 loss: Cntnap2 was measured in every Foxp2 group and never passed FDR correction.
Foxp3 produced a uniform neuronal null: all 23 recovered mouse-brain neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Foxp3 loss in NeuN+ brain nuclei did not activate or repress the expected Treg marker and cytokine program; Cd3e, Cd4, Ctla4, Il2ra, Il2rb, Il2rg, Ifng, Tnf, Tnfrsf18, and Ikzf2 were FDR=1.0 across the Foxp3 response surface.

The measured literature-obvious comparators did not converge with Foxp3: the neuronal FOXP paralog Foxp2 had zero DE genes in its 22 recovered groups, the represented IL-2R/STAT5 and NF-kappaB targets were flat, and Smad2 produced only two single-gene neuronal hits with Foxp3 correlation r=0.00396.
A genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no meaningful convergent or divergent Foxp3 neighbor; the strongest non-safe positive and negative targets had correlations of only 0.03296 and -0.01512.
Fras1 produced no robust single-nucleus transcriptional response in any measured juvenile neuronal class: all 21 tested groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected Fraser-complex and nephronectin-integrin axis was transcriptionally uncoupled from Fras1 editing: Frem1, Frem2, Frem3, Grip1, Npnt, Itga8, Itgb1, Gdnf, and Ret all had FDR=1.0 as Fras1 downstream genes in every measured group, and represented Itga8/Itgb1 perturbations were essentially uncorrelated with Fras1.

A feature-centered all-target scan found no meaningful Fras1 signature neighbor; the best positive and negative residual neighbors were Fbxo11 at r=0.028949 and Hnf4a at r=-0.020292, and each had only one matched downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Frmd5 acute mosaic loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.

The Frmd5 null in hippocampal, thalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar neuronal groups refines FRMD5 disease biology away from a broad autonomous juvenile mRNA program and toward synaptic scaffold, morphology, and electrophysiology axes.
Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 generated convergent thalamic glutamatergic signatures, but Frmd5 did not respond there and was not itself an FDR-supported Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 target in any neuronal group.
Agnostic score correlations and represented FERM/actin comparators did not uncover a Frmd5-like transcriptomic module.
Frmpd4 loss of function was a complete nuclear-transcriptome null across every recovered neuronal group: 22/22 tested groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Expected PSD and group-I-mGluR relatives did not reveal a hidden Frmpd4-like module: Dlg4, Homer2, Grm1, Grm5, Shank2 and Mapk1 were themselves flat in matched groups, while Dlgap4, Camk2a and Shank3 produced only isolated DE that could not overlap Frmpd4's empty FDR signature.

Unbiased Frmpd4 signature-neighbor analysis found no robust model-visible convergence: the top restricted-signature positive neighbors were Spi1, Prlr and Gaa; the strongest negative neighbors were Gphn, Nrp1 and Nefl; each had zero or one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in matched groups.
The expected FRMPD4 disease program was absent at the level of PSD, mGluR and activity-regulated mRNAs.
Frrs1l CRISPR produced negative self-transcript estimates in every measured group but almost no downstream nuclear transcriptional response.
308 CB GABA was the only recovered cell group with a downstream FDR<0.10 response to Frrs1l, represented by Med20 up-regulation.
The expected AMPAR structural and auxiliary genes remained transcriptionally flat after Frrs1l perturbation.
Frrs1l did not transcriptionally phenocopy the represented AMPAR partner Cpt1c or AMPAR receptor/auxiliary targets.
Fshr produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups, with only 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut approaching the threshold through a single Mlxip hit at FDR 0.1146.

The reported neuronal FSHR-to-C/EBPbeta/AEP Alzheimer axis was not transcriptionally engaged by Fshr LoF in matched forebrain glutamatergic groups; Cebpb, Lgmn, App, Mapt, Bace1, Psen1 and Psen2 were all FDR=1.0.

The obvious glycoprotein-hormone receptor relatives Lhcgr and Tshr did not converge with Fshr in neurons: Lhcgr was fully downstream-null and Tshr showed only three isolated singleton genes across its own surface.

Fshr's strongest whole-surface signature neighbors were nearly uncorrelated controls or weak genes, whereas the strongest negative neighbors Uba5 and Ufc1 generated large FDR-significant surfaces in several same assay groups.
Fshr LoF did not recover FSHR-cAMP/CREB immediate-early genes or granulosa/steroidogenic target genes in any recovered neuronal group.
Fto loss produced a sparse, cell-type-restricted abundance response: 5 of 22 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, led by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 15 genes.
Rsrp1 down-regulation was the recurrent Fto signature marker, significant in three independent neuronal groups.
Fto converged most strongly with RNA-processing and nuclear-transport perturbations nominated directly from the screen, especially Snrnp70, Rnpc3, Tnpo3, and Tpr on the restricted Fto signature.
Huwe1, Tardbp, and Tsc2 were the top clean opposing neighbors, and Rnpc3 loss reversed the Fto-up Rnpc3/Amy1 rows despite sharing other Rsrp1-centered effects.
The measured nuclear m6A reader relatives Hnrnpc and Hnrnpa2b1 did not phenocopy Fto in matched groups.
Fto perturbation did not induce transcript-level compensation of m6A machinery and did not move marker genes from adipocyte IRX, dopamine, adult neural-stem, or postnatal-growth programs.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried a small proteostasis/ER-phagy edge, with Ccpg1 up and Ppib, Ttc4, Wsb1 down.
Slirp was selectively up-regulated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
A small neuronal membrane/axon-excitability cluster appeared only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Camk2d and Trim46 increased while Kcnj3 decreased.
Acute Fxr1 perturbation was transcriptionally silent across every measured postmitotic neuronal class, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 13 of 13 recovered groups.
Fxr1 loss did not change the literature-nominated AMPAR/GluA2 or Cdkn1a transcript readouts in mature neurons.
The measurable Fragile-X and post-transcriptional comparator perturbations did not reveal a hidden Fxr1-like nuclear program.
The unbiased Fxr1 signature-neighbor search yielded only near-zero score correlations and did not identify a convergent transcriptional module.
Fyn loss was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered neuronal brain: every one of 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Fyn did not phenocopy NMDA-receptor subunit loss, even in cortical and subcortical glutamatergic groups where Grin1, Grin2a or Grin2b knockdown produced robust activity-gene programs.
The APP/tau/PrPC/mGluR5/Fyn Alzheimer axis was mostly silent as a normal juvenile loss-of-function module.
Fyn had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor in the 1,772-target model-visible universe.
Represented Reelin/Dab1 pathway members were largely transcriptionally buffered like Fyn after P16 perturbation.
Acute P16 Fzd2 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 assayed neuronal cell groups.
Fzd2 loss did not propagate to canonical Wnt/beta-catenin marker RNAs even though core Wnt-axis perturbations were transcriptionally detectable in matched neuronal groups.
The represented single Frizzled receptors shared Fzd2's lack of a downstream neuronal signature: Fzd4, Fzd6, and Fzd9 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found only near-zero Fzd2 correlations and did not nominate a coherent positive or negative phenocopy.
The postnatal neuronal Fzd2 null is displaced from the embryonic craniofacial and limb lineages in which FZD2 disease alleles produce canonical and PCP Wnt phenotypes.
Fzd4 loss was transcriptionally silent in every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class, separating this postnatal neuronal assay from FZD4's canonical Norrin-dependent endothelial barrier program.

Fzd4 did not converge with the Wnt pathway nodes that were actually detectable in this neuronal dataset: Ctnnb1 and, weakly, Lrp6 produced thalamic glutamatergic responses including Lef1 or Axin2, whereas Fzd4, Fzd2, Fzd6, and Fzd9 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 signature.

Full-transcriptome neighbor search failed to reveal a meaningful Fzd4-like module: the strongest non-safe positive and negative cosine neighbors, Dstyk and Fbxo11, had absolute cosine values below 0.05 and only singleton or two-gene FDR responses of their own.
Acute Fzd6 loss-of-function was transcriptomically silent in every recovered neuronal cell group.
Fzd6 was uncoupled from the postnatal thalamic beta-catenin/TCF module that was readily detected after Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2 and Lrp6 perturbation.
Represented Frizzled and PCP receptors did not phenocopy Fzd6 or form a hidden receptor module under single-gene P16 neuronal perturbation.
Genome-wide signature-neighbor analysis did not identify a credible Fzd6-like transcriptional module.
Fzd9 is a screen-wide postmitotic neuronal transcriptional null: all 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and no FDR-supported Fzd9 self-transcript change.
Fzd9 did not feed a detectable canonical Wnt gene-expression program even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 perturbations produced FDR-supported responses.
Measured Wnt receptor-level perturbations were mostly flat and did not phenocopy Fzd9; broader posterior responses were concentrated in downstream Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and Csnk2b nodes.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis rejected the Fzd9 nominal tail as a reproducible transcriptomic module.
Gaa was a pan-neuronal downstream-flat perturbation: all 23 recovered cell groups had 0 non-Gaa genes at FDR<0.10 even though Gaa itself was FDR-significantly lower in ten of them.
Canonical lysosomal, autophagy, UPR/ISR, and glycogen-metabolism transcripts were absent from the Gaa surface rather than merely shifted below a pathway threshold.

Gaa did not phenocopy represented autophagy, mTOR-lysosome, retromer, or lysosomal-sorting targets; Tsc2, Rb1cc1, Vps35, Mtor, Atg5, and Lamp2 all produced at least one FDR<0.10 downstream gene whereas Gaa produced none.

A whole-parquet signature search found no meaningful data-driven Gaa neighbor: the strongest positive secondary-score correlation was Fam149b at r=0.029 and the strongest negative was Dap3 at r=-0.011.
The flat signature is consistent with a cross-correctable enzyme in a mosaic tissue: edited Gaa-low neurons could still receive GAA protein from nearby wild-type cells.
Gabbr1 produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream hit: Eif4e up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Four groups with significant Gabbr1 transcript reduction had no FDR<0.10 downstream DEG.
Obligate GABAB-receptor partner and proximal effector perturbations did not phenocopy the Gabbr1 Eif4e response.
Gabbr1 loss did not produce a robust neuronal-activity, CREB, or ATF4/ISR transcriptional program.
The best data-driven Gabbr1 signature neighbors were not robust FDR-level neighbors.

The GABBR2 disease mechanism represented by human loss-of-function variants is not recoded as a juvenile single-cell basal-expression signature after mosaic CRISPR deletion.
Postnatal sparse Gabra1 loss failed to generate any robust cell-autonomous downstream transcriptome in all 22 measured neuronal groups.
The null persisted in five cell groups where the Gabra1 transcript itself was significantly depleted.
Gabra1 did not phenocopy alpha1 receptor partners or GABA-synapse neighbors that were directly represented as perturbations.
Postnatal Gabra1 perturbation did not induce compensatory transcription of other GABA-A receptor subunit genes.
The CRISPR loss-of-function context did not reproduce a GABRA1-variant ER-stress or unfolded-protein-response state.
An unbiased score-space search found no robust positive or negative Gabra1 signature neighbor.
Gabra2 produced 0 FDR<0.10 downstream DE genes in every recovered cell group.
β2, γ2, and δ GABA_A-family perturbations produced sparse FDR-supported responses where Gabra2 did not.
Gabra2 loss did not induce transcriptional compensation by other measured GABA_A receptor subunits.
Gabra2 had no robust data-driven transcriptomic neighbor across the target universe.
The flat postmitotic RNA surface shifts Gabra2 disease and pharmacology interpretation toward electrophysiology, receptor localization, and circuit mechanisms.

Acute Gabra3 loss-of-function was transcriptionally buffered across all 19 recovered neuronal cell groups: no group had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10 despite a nominal-to-FDR-significant self decrease in a subset of groups.

Gabra3 did not phenocopy the measurable GABA_A receptor or inhibitory-synapse relatives; the 14 represented Gabra/Gabrb/Gabrg/Gabrd/Gabrr2/Gphn/Arhgef9/Gad2/Slc6a1 comparator signatures were essentially orthogonal to Gabra3, and most were themselves flat.

Unbiased whole-universe signature matching found no credible positive or negative Gabra3 neighbor: the strongest Wilcoxon-score cosine was only +0.058 with Fbxo11 and the most negative was -0.048 with Wdr26.
Gabra5 perturbation was transcriptome-flat across the recovered P16-to-P37/44 neuronal atlas.
The Gabra5 null is alpha5-specific within a mostly transcriptionally quiet GABA_A/GABAergic target set.

Gabrb3 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any recovered neuronal class.

A flat CRISPR-loss transcriptome should not be extrapolated to all GABRB3 disease alleles, especially gain-of-function missense variants.

The high-dimensional residual Gabrd signature had no convincing positive or negative neighbor after direct testing.
Gabrg2 loss produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured neuronal groups despite a negative self-transcript in every group.

Human GABRG3 disease associations are not mimicked by a simple sparse postnatal coding LoF transcriptional program in the sampled mouse neurons.
Gabrr2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.

The whole-universe signature scan found no meaningful positive or negative Gabrr2 neighbor.

Gal loss-of-function produced a full-surface downstream transcriptional null across the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.

Hippocampal-associated Galr1 perturbation was flat in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut despite seizure and kainate literature implicating GalR1 in hippocampal protection.
Gata1 loss-of-function was a complete neuronal DE null across all 23 measured cell groups.

Unbiased signature-neighbor search found only near-zero Gata1 correlations in the 1773-target universe.

The only Gata3 downstream FDR<0.10 event is Hectd2 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Gata3 loss-of-function is almost completely buffered transcriptionally across the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal panel.
Directly measurable GATA-family and GATA-associated neural comparators do not phenocopy Gata3.
The full-universe signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Gata3 neighbor.

The neuronal Gata6 perturbation uncoupled completely from canonical GATA6 endodermal and neural-crest smooth-muscle targets.
The data-driven Gata6 signature had no meaningful positive or negative model-wide neighbor.
Literature-obvious GATA-family and endodermal neighbors did not phenocopy Gata6 in the mouse neuronal screen.
Gatad2b loss exposes a Rasgrp2-up thalamic glutamatergic signal rather than a broad NuRD release program.
Pvalb interneurons showed an isolated Ube2g1 induction after Gatad2b perturbation.
Across postmitotic juvenile neurons, Gatad2b loss was transcriptionally buffered and failed to recover the embryonic cortical-patterning program expected from GAND models.

The directly measured Mbd2 perturbation did not phenocopy Gatad2b, separating p66β loss from a simple MBD2/NuRD failure mode.
Zbtb7a was a nominal data-driven neighbor but was rejected as a Gatad2b phenocopy because its response was broad.

The high-dimensional Gcgr score vector had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor across the target universe.

The canonical oxidative-stress, glutathione-recycling, NRF2, ferritin/metallothionein, and ATF4/ISR transcriptome was absent after Gclm perturbation.
Acute mosaic Gdap1 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any of the 22 recovered central neuronal groups.
The Gdap1 null supports a peripheral/context-restricted interpretation rather than a cell-autonomous pan-CNS transcriptional stress model.
Opa1, but not Gdap1, triggers a recurrent ISR/amino-acid response in matched neuronal groups.
The represented fission and Caytaxin comparators, Mff and Atcay, did not form a GDAP1-like nuclear transcriptomic module.
A pre-literature restricted-signature nearest-neighbor search found no robust convergent perturbation module for the null Gdap1 profile.
Acute mosaic Gdi1 loss produced a nearly pan-neuronal transcriptional buffer: only one non-target transcript, Atrn, reached FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups.
The only downstream Gdi1 hit was an exploratory Atrn decrease in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The Gdi1 surface is uncoupled from a Rab7 endolysosomal response that is readily recovered in the same Wilcoxon universe.
Gdi1 did not converge with the measurable Rab3/Rab18/Rab27 relatives Rab3gap1, Rab3gap2, Rab18, and Rab27a.

Acute Gfap loss produced a strict pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.

The all-gene Gfap profile did not reveal a masked cross-perturbation module: the largest per-gene/per-cell-type-centered residual cosine was only 0.0618 and the nearest positive neighbors were Safe_target_30, Npy1r, and Atg16l1, each with no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The neuronal LoF surface is disconnected from Alexander-disease and reactive-astrocyte GFAP biology: the GFAP-associated transcripts Vim, Nes, Synm, Aldh1l1, Aqp4, and Gja1 were all FDR=1.0 after Gfap perturbation, and represented neurofilament relatives Nefl, Nefm, and Nefh did not phenocopy a robust Gfap module.
Gfi1 loss was transcriptionally silent in every sampled postnatal neuronal group.
The GFI1-ATOH1-POU4F3 hair-cell cassette was absent as a module rather than missed by one guide set.
The GFI1/GFI1B medulloblastoma axis did not map onto isolated loss of Gfi1 in normal juvenile neurons.
A genome-wide neighbor search found no substantive Gfi1-like or anti-Gfi1 signature.
Gfi1b loss was almost pan-neuronally buffered: across 371818 tested group-gene rows in 22 recovered cell groups, only one downstream row reached FDR<0.10.
Ankrd13a up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only robust downstream Gfi1b hit.
Gfi1b had no meaningful data-driven positive or negative transcriptional neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The represented GFI-family and sensory/hematopoietic TF comparators did not reveal a latent Gfi1b-like neuronal program.
Zbtb7a strongly diverged from Gfi1b despite both being connected to erythroid transcription-factor biology.
The flat normal-neuron LoF response does not test the known GFI1B medulloblastoma mechanism.
Postnatal Gfm2 perturbation produced no robust downstream single-nucleus RNA response in any measured neuronal class.
The ATF4/mitochondrial-stress program expected from severe mitochondrial translation impairment was absent after Gfm2 but recovered after Opa1 perturbation.
Within represented mitochondrial disease genes, Gfm2 resembled weak core OXPHOS/mitochondrial-translation perturbations more than the strong Opa1 stressor.
The basal neuronal null should not be interpreted as evidence that GFM2 is dispensable under respiratory or toxic stress.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Gfm2 were numerically near-zero and were rejected as meaningful phenocopies.
Gfpt1 loss produced a thresholded ER chaperone/ERAD response in 7 neuronal groups, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Gfpt1-responsive neurons co-induced an ISR/amino-acid module and a redox/one-carbon module rather than a pure chaperone-only UPR.
The broad responders down-shifted neuronal excitability, vesicle, and cytoskeletal transcripts while stress transcripts rose.
The top data-driven neighbors of Gfpt1 were ER/glycosylation and proteostasis perturbations, led by Dhdds and Atp2a2.
The represented obvious neighbors Ogt, Hk1, Gpi1, Atf6, and Eif2ak4 did not phenocopy Gfpt1.

The neuronal UPR/ISR signature did not extend to a robust autophagy or apoptosis transcriptome in surviving nuclei.

The expected GH/JAK-STAT feedback readout was absent after Ghr perturbation.
Represented GHR-pathway and class-I-cytokine comparators did not phenocopy Ghr.
A pre-literature whole-universe neighbor search found only noise-level Ghr neighbors.

The downstream Cplane1 singleton is not reciprocated by Cplane1 knockout.

Gigyf2 triggered a narrow ER quality-control response rather than a global proteotoxic-stress program.
The thalamic and MB Glut signatures contain a recurrent RNA-processing module that converges with spliceosome and nuclear-pore perturbations.

HS-linked FGF/Hedgehog/Wnt-axon-guidance transcriptional markers were not mobilized by postnatal Glce perturbation.

Gli2 generated 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.

The strongest data-driven Gli2 signature neighbors had score-vector correlations below 0.04 in absolute value.
Loss of Gli2 in P16 postmitotic NeuN+ cells did not reproduce embryonic ventral-patterning, cerebellar granule-precursor, or HPE-family transcriptional programs.

Literature-obvious GLIS/Hedgehog/ciliopathy comparators did not converge on Glis2 in neurons.

The Glra3 null is not evidence against alpha-3 GlyR analgesic biology.

The only FDR-level Glrb self-transcript drops were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and each remained downstream-null.

Glrb had no meaningful same-sign or opposite-sign target neighbor in the complete parquet signature search.
Gls produced one FDR<0.10 downstream event: Abcf3 induction in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Two subcortical glutamatergic groups had measurable Gls self-transcript depletion but still no downstream DE.

Glud1 loss produced no robust downstream neuronal transcriptional program in 22 measured cell groups despite a consistently negative self-transcript.
Represented glutamate/alpha-ketoglutarate neighbors did not converge on a shared transcriptomic module with Glud1.

Measurable Gbeta5/R7-adjacent perturbations were also nearly transcriptomically silent: Rgs6, Gpr158, Gnao1, Gpr179, and Kcnj6 generated at most one downstream FDR<0.10 gene apiece in matched groups.
The top data-driven Gnb5 signature neighbors were unrelated targets with absolute feature-centered correlations below 0.09 and zero shared FDR-supported genes.

The data refine known GNB5 loss-of-function disease toward electrophysiology, development, retina, heart, and dopaminergic systems rather than a persistent postmitotic cell-autonomous RNA state in sampled forebrain, midbrain, and cerebellar neurons.
Gnptab did not induce any downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 22 recovered neuronal groups, and canonical lysosomal, autophagy, and UPR/ISR genes were all FDR=1.0.
The direct GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase partner Gnptg was also flat in every Gnptab-matched group and had a near-zero score-Pearson correlation to Gnptab.
Perturbations of representative lysosomal hydrolase or cargo genes Ctsb, Gaa, Manba, Asah1, Ppt1, and Psap were flat across Gnptab-matched neuronal groups.
Vps35 and Rb1cc1 generated detectable signatures in Gnptab-matched neurons while Gnptab remained flat.
Genome-wide data-driven neighbors of Gnptab were all near zero and non-lysosomal.
Gnptg loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a lysosomal-storage-like secondary program.
