The expected lysosomal, TFEB/autophagy and cathepsin response was absent at FDR level.
The fibroblast GNPTAB-compensation motif was not reused by postmitotic neurons.
Gnptab, the represented same-complex partner, was also flat and did not converge with Gnptg by signed-score similarity.
Genome-scale signature comparison nominated no credible Gnptg responder neighbor or antagonist.
The Gnptg null is compatible with rescue by neighboring wild-type cells in a sparse M6P screen.

Gnrhr-targeting CRISPR produced a responder that was both cell-class restricted and one-gene restricted: Sbk1 was induced in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and no other cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

Full-surface cross-perturbation analysis did not find a robust convergent Gnrhr module; the strongest biological cosines were only 0.0265 to Camta1 and -0.0150 to Csf1r, and the data-driven neighbors did not reproduce Sbk1 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

The canonical pituitary GnRHR MAPK/immediate-early/gonadotropin transcriptional program was absent from neuronal Gnrhr perturbations, and represented HPG-axis receptors or GnRHR-linked signaling nodes were also essentially flat and non-convergent.
Got1 produced a real but very small DE response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 21 other measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
Mdh1, the cytosolic malate dehydrogenase partner of GOT1, was Got1's top positive six-gene neighbor and partially shared the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
Mitochondrial and carrier MAS comparators Got2, Mdh2, Slc25a12, and Slc25a13 did not phenocopy Got1 in the matched thalamic responder group.
Asns upregulation is compatible with a local amino-acid stress trace, but Got1 did not induce a broad ATF4/CHOP integrated-stress program.

Tpr and Setd1a were robust anti-neighbors that significantly reversed the Got1 Pcca/Zcchc7/Atp11b branch, whereas raw anti-neighbors Fbxo11, Son, and Brwd1 were rejected as subthreshold for the six Got1 genes.
The screen does not reproduce the strong GOT1-dependent redox liabilities reported in cancer cells or rods, so acute brain-neuron snRNA silence should not be read as systemic GOT1 safety.
Got2 produced a single weak downstream DEG: Snap25 was up-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Four neuronal groups showed significant Got2 RNA reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Core malate-aspartate-shuttle perturbations did not phenocopy Got2, even in the matched thalamic group where Got2 had its only downstream hit.
Got2 loss did not recover the amino-acid/ISR, redox, p53, or MAS-compensation programs predicted from severe GOT2-deficiency models.
The whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Got2 neighbor or anti-neighbor.

Gp1ba was almost completely transcriptionally silent in the postnatal NeuN+ brain assay: 21 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the only exception was one Sst GABA Auh call.
The one FDR<0.10 response to Gp1ba was a down-regulation of Auh in 053 Sst Gaba.
Measurable platelet and megakaryocyte relatives did not phenocopy Gp1ba in neurons: Gp6, Itga2b, Mpl, and Gata1 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered neuronal groups.
Whole-transcriptome signature neighbors of Gp1ba were numerical rather than biological: the largest positive and negative Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon-score profiles were only 0.031 and -0.020.
Gp6 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any measured NeuN-enriched postmitotic neuronal class.
GPVI-pathway and platelet-lineage comparators represented in the parquet did not form a coherent neuronal GPVI module.
The Gp6 rank signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor across all model-visible targets.
This neuronal CRISPR screen gives no support for a neuron-autonomous transcriptional liability of GPVI inhibition.
Gpc6 has a pan-tested postnatal neuronal null surface: every one of 22 measured NeuN+ cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Measurable heparan-sulfate biosynthesis and Slit/Robo relatives did not uncover a latent Gpc6-like guidance module.

Wnt/Hedgehog/BMP/FGF receptor and effector perturbations did not phenocopy Gpc6, while beta-catenin perturbation demonstrated that this assay could detect a Wnt-linked thalamic transcriptome when it exists.
The GPC6-NMDAR prior is not recovered as a Grin2b-like cortical DEG signature.
The apparently closest data-driven neighbors are statistical non-neighbors, not a hidden module.
The omodysplasia/Hedgehog disease axis is not phenocopied by acute mosaic Gpc6 loss in juvenile neurons.
Gper1 loss produced no FDR-supported basal transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The pre-literature nearest-neighbor search found no meaningful Gper1 expression module.
Classical estrogen receptors and represented GPER effector genes did not phenocopy Gper1 in the basal neuronal screen.
Hippocampal Gper1 knockout did not recover the Arc/BDNF/CaMKII/glutamate-receptor program expected from acute GPER1 synaptic-plasticity work.
The neuronal Gper1 null did not engage the astrocyte or microglial injury programs often used to explain GPER neuroprotection.
Gphn loss produced a single robust transcriptomic output: Cbarp up-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The FDR-level Gphn surface uncoupled gephyrin perturbation from transcription of GABA(A), glycine-receptor, and inhibitory-synapse genes.
Neither data-driven neighbors nor direct inhibitory-synapse relatives phenocopied the Gphn L4-5 Cbarp response.
Gphn did not trigger a molybdenum-cofactor or canonical ISR/UPR stress RNA response in the recovered neuronal nuclei.
Sparse postnatal Gpi1 loss yielded an almost origin-centered neuronal transcriptional phenotype: only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 over 22 measured groups.
Gpi1 exposed a small Ogt-down signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without the Ddit3/Hspa5/Asns/Herpud1/Sdf2l1/Chac1/Pdia6 HBP-UPR program that Gfpt1 loss robustly triggered in the same group.
The data-driven Gpi1 neighbors were numerically near zero and failed matched-cell validation.
The sparse juvenile neuronal Gpi1 perturbation did not recapitulate the high-penetrance erythroid, embryonic, or rare neurological manifestations of GPI deficiency.
Neither sparse Gpi1 loss nor direct Amfr perturbation revealed a mature-neuronal AMF/neuroleukin transcriptional axis.

Gpr156 loss produced an almost completely buffered postnatal neuronal transcriptome: only Zer1 and Kmt5a passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured neuronal cell groups, while canonical immediate-early, stress, autophagy/lysosomal and synaptic markers were uniformly FDR-negative.
The only corrected Gpr156 downstream hits were split between two limbic glutamatergic groups: Zer1 was down in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Kmt5a was up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.

Represented GABA(B), mGluR/CaSR, Gi/o, and PCP/Wnt comparator perturbations did not phenocopy Gpr156: none reproduced Zer1 suppression in 012 or Kmt5a induction in 017, and each had zero FDR<0.10 genes in those two matched Gpr156 responder groups.

Gpr156 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor: the best positive score-vector neighbor was Rxrb at r=0.029, while the strongest negative correlations were only about -0.011 and included safe-target controls.
The 145 MH-LH TH Glut group was flat for Gpr156 despite curated and humanized-allele evidence that GPR156 can control medial-habenula excitability and stress-related behavior.
The only robust downstream event after postnatal Gpr158 perturbation was Cnot3 up-regulation in the CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic group.
Gpr158 loss was transcriptionally buffered across the juvenile NeuN+ brain: 22 of 23 measured groups had zero downstream DEGs at FDR<0.10 despite negative Gpr158 self-logFC in every group.
The strongest unbiased positive and negative Gpr158 signature neighbors were essentially zero-correlation signatures rather than a hidden genome-wide module.
Represented RGS7-complex, GPR158-paralog, class-C GPCR, and cAMP-pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Gpr158.
Cnot3 induction was isolated from other measured CCR4-NOT subunit transcripts and from direct Cnot1 loss.
Resting snRNA-seq did not yield a cortical Bdnf, AMPAR/NMDAR, or immediate-early biomarker of Gpr158 inhibition.

Gpr161 was a pan-measured non-responder in juvenile NeuN-enriched neurons: 22 cell groups produced no downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and the one remaining taxonomy group, 215 MB Dopa, was not recovered for Gpr161.
The canonical Gpr161-loss Hedgehog/Gli program was uncoupled from Gpr161 perturbation in this postnatal neuronal assay.
The flat Gpr161 surface was mirrored by a mostly flat literature-obvious Hedgehog/ciliary/cAMP comparator set, rather than by a strong related-target responder.
No data-driven Gpr161 signature neighbor formed a meaningful transcriptional module.

The Gpr161 SHH-medulloblastoma and neural-tube-risk literature maps to proliferative embryonic or granule-progenitor contexts, not to the cerebellar or other mature neuronal clusters that were recovered here.
Gpr179 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured juvenile brain neuronal groups, while 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.
The canonical ON-bipolar mGluR6/TRPM1/RGS-GNB5 signalplex did not move at the transcript level after Gpr179 perturbation.

Represented relatives of the retinal cascade did not reveal a substitute Gpr179-like brain module: Gpr158, Gnb5 and Grm6 were flat or nearly flat, and Gnao1 had only one downstream hit in the 22 matched groups.
The data-driven signature-neighbor search returned only near-zero Gpr179 neighbors and anti-neighbors, with no FDR-level shared module to keep.
Gpr45 is an all-null perturbation at broad neuronal cell-class resolution in the P16-to-P37/44 screen.
The expected POMC/JAK-STAT/melanocortin and cAMP/CRE transcriptional readouts were absent under Gpr45 loss.
Neither the empirical Gpr45 signature neighbors nor the literature-obvious pathway comparators produced a convincing Gpr45 phenocopy.
Gprasp2 loss had no downstream FDR<0.10 nuclear transcriptomic effect in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The two cell groups with significant Gprasp2 self-transcript reduction, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, still had zero downstream DE genes.
Literature-obvious mGluR and postsynaptic scaffold comparators were also largely flat, whereas Tsc2 and Mecp2 produced measurable signatures in the same cell groups.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of Gprasp2 were essentially zero-correlation restricted-score matches: Fbxo11 was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative neighbor.

Gprasp2 perturbation did not induce an mGluR, immediate-early, autophagy/UPR, or Hedgehog transcript panel, so snRNA-seq provides no pharmacodynamic RNA marker for mGluR5- or Hedgehog-directed rescue in this setting.
Gprc5b produced a sharply restricted nuclear-RNA response: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was the only one of 22 measured groups with downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
direction_pattern: Pde1a and Sez6 down; Kctd16 and Tmem178b up

canonical_summary: The only robust L4/5 IT responders point to a small receptor/excitability module rather than to a generic stress or Wnt program.
direction_pattern: Pde1a and Sez6 down; Kctd16 and Tmem178b up

canonical_summary: The Gprc5b L4/5 IT response did not phenocopy represented Wnt/Frizzled/LRP, retinoid-receptor, or Fyn/NF-kappaB perturbations.
direction_pattern: expected Wnt/retinoid/NF-kappaB programs absent from Gprc5b

canonical_summary: Data-driven nearest neighbors did not identify a robust phenocopy or anti-phenocopy for Gprc5b.
direction_pattern: weak positive and weak inverse restricted-signature neighbors

canonical_summary: Pvalb and P/MY Pineal groups buffered Gprc5b self-transcript depletion without downstream FDR genes.
direction_pattern: Gprc5b RNA down, downstream signature absent

canonical_summary: Gpx4 produced zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.
Recovered Gpx4-perturbed nuclei did not induce measured ferroptosis, NRF2/glutathione, iron-handling, or ATF4-CHOP/ISR sentinels.
Represented ferroptosis/redox relatives did not phenocopy Gpx4 or form a shared significant module: Gclc, Gclm, Acsl4, Nfe2l2, Prdx1, and Sod2 were flat or single-gene responders.
The unbiased cross-target map found no meaningful positive or negative Gpx4 signature neighbor; the largest non-control matched Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.062.
The flat snRNA-seq surface should not be interpreted as neuronal safety of GPX4 blockade.
Postnatal sparse Greb1l loss produced no robust transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
Represented retinoid-pathway perturbations did not reveal a Greb1l-like module in the matched neuronal surface.
Blind signature-neighbor analysis found only near-zero Greb1l neighbors, and the strongest gene anti-neighbor, Wdr26, is a broad responder where Greb1l is flat.
Grhl2 loss-of-function produced a single FDR-level neuronal transcriptomic response: Klhdc4 up-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The canonical GRHL2 apical-junction, epithelial-barrier and EMT-suppression program was absent from every measured neuronal group.

Grhl2 is transcriptionally isolated in this neuronal perturbation universe: its nearest all-gene neighbors have near-zero cosine similarity, and represented GRHL2-adjacent regulators do not phenocopy it.
Acute Gria1 loss was broadly buffered on the nuclear transcriptome: 21 of 22 recovered neuronal groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene and the only responder was a one-gene cerebellar GABA signal.
The only conventional downstream Gria1 hit was Ndufs3 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
The AMPAR paralogs Gria2 and Gria3 did not converge with Gria1: each produced only a distinct singleton and neither reproduced CB-GABA Ndufs3.
NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations were transcriptionally visible in several cell groups where Gria1 was flat, most strongly Grin1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Grin2b in superficial IT cortex.
A residualized whole-transcriptome search across all targets found no robust data-driven Gria1 signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
The postnatal Gria1 LoF state lacks a GRIA1 disease-like stress or activity-transcription signature.

Gria2 CRISPR produced a measurable but strongly buffered RNA phenotype: the Gria2 transcript itself was significantly lower in four excitatory groups, yet the entire 22-group surface contained only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The sole downstream FDR hit was Ddx17 down-regulation in 053 Sst Gaba neurons after Gria2 perturbation.
NMDA-receptor subunits, but not Gria2, produced activity/synaptic transcriptional programs in matched cortical and thalamic glutamatergic groups.
Represented AMPAR-core and TARP/scaffold comparators were rejected as strong Gria2 phenocopies because Gria1, Gria3, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Dlg4 were all nearly downstream-null.
The full-universe Gria2 signature had no meaningful model-wide positive or negative neighbor.
Sparse postnatal Gria2 loss did not recapitulate the transcriptional footprint one would expect from GRIA2 neurodevelopmental alleles or from Q/R-editing-driven Ca2+-permeable AMPAR toxicity.
Gria3 loss produced a one-gene Jmjd1c-positive response restricted to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
The full Gria3 transcriptional signature lies at the perturbational noise floor and has no strong positive or negative neighbor.
AMPAR-core and AMPAR-trafficking relatives are buffered like Gria3, whereas NMDAR subunits Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produce detectable DE in the same universe.
Acute Gria3 loss does not activate a detectable immediate-early, CREB/BDNF, ISR/UPR, or autophagy transcriptional program.
The flat LoF surface refines GRIA3 disease biology toward variant- and physiology-specific channel dysfunction rather than a generic postmitotic transcriptional injury state.
Grid1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Delta/neurexin comparators were transcriptionally flat like Grid1, whereas NMDA receptor subunits Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced detectable cell-type-restricted signatures.
Unbiased Grid1 signature neighbors had negligible whole-surface correlations and no reproducible significant signatures.
Grid2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The 19 non-cerebellar recovered Grid2 groups are strong transcriptional negatives, matching the concentration of the canonical GluD2 program in cerebellar Purkinje-cell parallel-fiber synapses.
Even in 308 CB GABA, Grid2 loss did not induce a detectable GluD2/Cbln1/neurexin or AMPA-receptor transcript program.
Literature-obvious GluD2 relatives and synaptic neighbors did not phenocopy Grid2 as convergent downstream signatures in the matched cell groups.
The all-target signature search found no noncanonical Grid2 neighbor; the strongest whole-vector neighbor was Lonp1 with cosine 0.042 and the strongest anti-neighbor was Kcnh1 with cosine -0.030.
Grik1 loss produced a pan-measured null surface: zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered cell group.
Grik1 had no substantive data-driven transcriptomic neighbor; the largest whole-surface score correlation was only r=0.030.
Represented kainate subunits also failed to yield a coherent shared transcriptome: Grik4 and Grik5 were fully flat and Grik3 had only three isolated FDR<0.10 genes.

The screen could detect glutamate-receptor biology where it was transcriptional: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced FDR-significant activity/synaptic programs in Grik1-matched groups, whereas Grik1 did not.
A Grik1 CRISPR LoF allele gives no robust basal snRNA biomarker for the GluK1 programs pursued in epilepsy, pain, anxiety, or PV-interneuron biology.
Grik3 loss produced only a three-gene, cortex-restricted thresholded transcriptomic response: Amy1 down in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Gdpd5/Kcng3 up in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The Grik3 response was uncoupled from canonical receptor compensation and from activity-regulated immediate-early/plasticity transcription.

Measured kainate-family relatives did not phenocopy Grik3. Grik1, Grik4, and Grik5 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered groups and no Amy1/Gdpd5/Kcng3 overlap in the Grik3 responder groups.

The same dataset detects ionotropic-glutamate-receptor transcriptional output for NMDA subunits: Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations induced Bdnf/Nptx2/Scg2/Vgf/Npas4/Egr3/Kcnv1-rich cortical programs that Grik3 did not induce.
A whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no strong Grik3 module: the best responder-group cosine was only 0.133 for Spata7, and the strongest coding anti-neighbor was Tfcp2 at -0.0966.
Sst GABA nuclei showed a significant Grik3 self-transcript decrease but no downstream FDR<0.10 response.
Acute postnatal Grik4 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.

The expected kainate receptor relatives did not expose a hidden Grik4-like transcriptome: Grik1 and Grik5 were completely flat, and Grik3 produced only three idiosyncratic FDR hits outside the hippocampal groups.
Data-driven Grik4 neighbors were numerical only: the best restricted positive cosine was Kit at 0.183 and the best biological negative was Kcna1 at -0.116, with no shared Grik4 FDR genes.
The postmitotic LoF surface provides no transcriptomic biomarker for GRIK4-linked mood or neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
Acute P16 Grik5 loss was globally transcriptionally buffered: every one of the 22 recovered neuronal groups had zero non-on-target genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.

The represented kainate-receptor paralogs did not form a shared Grik5-like transcriptional module: Grik1 and Grik4 were fully flat, Grik3 produced only three isolated FDR<0.10 genes, and all three had near-zero score correlations with Grik5.

Grik5 was flat in cell groups where NMDA-receptor subunit loss produced robust activity/synaptic transcriptional signatures, including Grin1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Grin2a/Grin2b in upper-layer cortical IT neurons.

A blind nearest-neighbor search found only vanishingly small Grik5 correlations: the best positive neighbors were Drd4 and Notch2 with r≈0.04 and the strongest negative neighbors were Fbxo11 and Atp6v1e1 with r≈-0.04.
The Grik5 snRNA-seq null should not be read as a negative pharmacology result for GluK5/KAR antagonism.

Acute postmitotic Grin1 loss produced an FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in only 5 of 23 measured neuronal groups, and 126 of the 131 significant downstream group-gene entries occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The midbrain glutamatergic Grin1 response was a two-gene activity module, Bdnf and Egr1, both down-regulated.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Grin1 loss suppressed a presynaptic, postsynaptic-scaffold, and ion-channel program while also decreasing the clade-associated Prkcd transcript.
The same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature up-regulated growth/plasticity and stress-linked genes, including Stmn4, Gpm6a, Tspan7, Scg2, Jun, Igf1, Deptor, and Eif2ak3.
Pvalb GABA neurons showed a single robust downstream effect, down-regulation of the synaptic-vesicle amino-acid transporter Slc6a17.
008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut each had only one non-target hit, Mfsd4a up and Bbx up, respectively.

NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations did not phenocopy Grin1: Grin2a and Grin2b were mainly upper-layer cortical responders, whereas Grin1 was dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and had no exact FDR overlap with Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2d, or Grin3a.

Cross-perturbation ranking linked the 151 Grin1 signature to a data-driven trafficking/stress axis: Vps54 was strongly same-direction, Rab7 had the largest exact shared FDR overlap, and Wdfy3 was the strongest opposite-direction neighbor.
The sparse Grin1 LoF transcriptome and the Grin-subunit non-phenocopy caution against collapsing GRIN disorders into one basal transcriptional signature.
Grin2a loss produced a real transcriptional response only in upper cortical IT excitatory neurons, strongest in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and weaker in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The L2-3/L4-5 responder program was dominated by up-regulated activity-dependent secreted and peptide genes, especially Nptx2 and Scg2 in both responders and Bdnf, Ptgs2, Penk and Inhba in L2-3.
Grin2a loss in L2-3 IT cells coupled the activity gene increase to a smaller synaptic-organization and membrane-remodeling signature.
direction_pattern: mixed; mostly up with Plch2/Ptprd/Nyap2/Osbpl1a down

canonical_summary: The top positive neighbors of the Grin2a signature were not NMDAR subunits: Eef2 shared 16 same-direction L2-3 coordinates, Mef2c shared 6 coordinates across 005/007, and Kcnb1 shared Nptx2/Scg2 in 005.

The same-complex benchmark rejected a simple NMDAR-subunit phenocopy: Grin1 was flat in both Grin2a responder groups, Grin2b responded but was an inverse neighbor in L2-3, and other ionotropic glutamate/PSD comparators were flat or discordant.
Nptx2 was the strongest recurrent downstream marker of Grin2a loss, independently significant in both cortical IT responder groups.

Grin2b loss generated a real but sharply restricted response: 78 downstream FDR<0.10 group-gene calls across the 22 recovered Grin2b cell groups, with 76/78 in neocortical excitatory projection groups and only two singleton noncortical hits.

The main neocortical Grin2b signature was a down-regulated activity/excitability module: Vgf decreased in L4/5 IT, L2/3 IT and L5 ET neurons; Kcnv1, Rph3a and Diras2 decreased in both IT cortical groups; and Npas4/Nr4a1/Egr3 decreased in L4/5 IT cells.

In L2/3 IT CTX neurons, Grin2b loss repressed a synaptic release, active-zone and postsynaptic organization module containing Unc13a, Unc13b, Rims1, Erc2, Ppfia2, Rph3a, Dlgap2, Cttnbp2, Adgrb1, Igsf9b, Cabp1, Cacnb3, Nptxr and Sorcs3.

The up-regulated arm of the Grin2b response was sparse and led by recurrent Adamts2 induction in L2/3 IT and L5 ET neurons, with smaller cell-type-limited increases in Brd9, Arpp21, Sfpq, Mast1, Echdc2, Tbkbp1 and Gpr137c.

A restricted 78-feature all-target search nominated Psmb4 as the top same-direction neighbor of Grin2b; it shared seven significant same-direction Grin2b signature genes, including Kcnv1/Rph3a/Egr3/Tyro3 in L4/5 IT cells and Cbarp/Pianp in the singleton noncortical responses.

Eef2 was the top opposite-direction Grin2b neighbor: it significantly reversed 18 Grin2b signature features, including induction of Vgf, Igsf9b, Sorcs3, Diras2, Rph3a, Slc9a5, Kcnv1 and Unc13a where Grin2b repressed them in L2/3 IT cortex.

Loss of the represented NMDA-receptor relatives did not recapitulate the Grin2b cortical state: Grin1 had no significant overlap with the 78-feature Grin2b signature and concentrated its own hits in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Grin2a had a smaller L2/3 signature with two opposite shared genes and Grin2d/Grin3a were flat.
Represented PSD/CaMKII-pathway targets, including Dlg4, Shank2, Shank3, Syngap1 and Camk2a/b/g, did not produce significant overlap on the Grin2b 78-feature signature.
The measured LoF-like Grin2b state was cortical, activity-gene-decreasing and synapse-gene-decreasing rather than a pan-neuronal toxicity program.
Pianp in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Cbarp in 155 MB Glut were the only FDR<0.10 noncortical downstream responses to Grin2b loss.
Grin2d produced no downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal group in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function assay.
Grin2d did not phenocopy the responsive NMDA-receptor subunits Grin1, Grin2a, or Grin2b, even where those targets produced thalamic or upper-layer cortical signatures.
The Pvalb group did not recover the published PVI GluN2D-to-GABAergic/schizophrenia molecular program after Grin2d perturbation.
The screen gives little support for a simple juvenile sparse Grin2d loss-of-function transcriptome as a model of GRIN2D developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Grin3a CRISPR loss of function was a pan-measured-class transcriptional null: none of the 22 recovered cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The pre-literature signature-neighbor search found no convincing Grin3a module: the best positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were near zero.
Grin3a did not phenocopy classical NMDAR subunit loss: Grin1, Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations produced FDR-level signatures in matched neuronal groups whereas Grin3a produced none.
The expected GluN3A/GIT1/mTORC1 and activity-regulated IEG biology did not appear as a durable nuclear RNA program after P16 Grin3a editing.
The flat normal-brain phenotype warns that basal neuronal snRNA-seq will be a poor pharmacodynamic biomarker for Grin3a lowering.

Grm1 produced no downstream DEGs at FDR<0.10 in any of its 20 recovered neuronal cell groups; even the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group, where the Grm1 self-transcript was significantly reduced, had zero downstream genes.

Grm1 loss did not alter activity-regulated group-I mGluR transcriptional targets or mGluR1-effector transcripts: Arc, Fos, Egr1, Bdnf, Fmr1, Homer1-3, Itpr1, Trpc3, Prkcg, and Grm5 all had adjusted P=1.0 across the 20 measured groups.

Most represented mGluR1 pathway relatives and postsynaptic-scaffold targets were also flat in the Grm1-matched groups; Prkcg and Shank3 showed only isolated single-gene effects rather than a shared mGluR1-like module.

The strongest data-driven positive and negative Grm1 signature neighbors had near-zero cosine similarity and did not produce a shared FDR module; Wdr26, the only strong responder among them, responded in seven groups while remaining weakly anti-correlated with Grm1.
Sparse postnatal Grm1 LoF did not trigger a persistent cerebellar nuclear transcriptome resembling mGluR1 pathway failure.
Grm5 loss was pan-null at the basal nuclear transcriptome: 22 measured neuronal groups each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.

Grm5 loss did not reduce an mGluR5-induced immediate-early or synaptic-plasticity mRNA program; Arc, Fos, Jun, Egr1, Npas4, Nr4a1, Bdnf, Dusp6, Homer, Shank, PLC/IP3, and mTOR/FMRP-axis transcripts were all FDR=1.0.

Most measured metabotropic glutamate receptor, PLC/IP3, PKC/CaMK, and postsynaptic scaffold perturbations were also basal-snRNA buffered, with Grm1, Grm6, Grm7, Grm8, Homer2, Itpr1, Plcb1, Prkca, Dlg4, and Shank2 each producing zero downstream hits.
Tsc2, an mTOR-axis disease comparator, produced 636 downstream DEGs in nine groups where Grm5 remained flat; Fmr1 and Mtor themselves were close to flat.
The top data-driven Grm5 signature neighbors were all weak: the largest positive restricted cosine was 0.155 and the largest negative non-control cosine was -0.091.
Basal neuronal snRNA DE is unlikely to be a sensitive standalone readout for mGluR5 negative allosteric modulation.

Grm6 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptional response in any recovered non-retinal neuronal class; 21 groups were null and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was only weak because Mbd2 stopped at FDR 0.119.
The represented mGluR-family and ON-bipolar signalplex comparators failed to phenocopy Grm6: Grm1, Grm5, Grm7, Grm8, Gnb5, and Gpr179 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Gnao1 had only one.
Whole-surface signature search placed Grm6 at the dataset noise floor: even the top positive neighbor, Gnb5, had cosine 0.0313, and the strongest inverse neighbor, Fbxo11, had cosine -0.0203.
Canonical ON-bipolar cascade readouts did not move at the RNA level after Grm6 perturbation: 217 tests spanning Gnao1, Gnb3, Gnb5, Gng13, Gpr179, Lrit3, Nyx, Rgs7, Rgs11, and Trpm1 all had FDR 1.0.
Grm7 had no FDR-resolved downstream nuclear RNA response in any recovered neuronal group after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.
The expected sustained excitability/cAMP immediate-early readout was absent.
The only measured group-III paralog, Grm8, did not phenocopy Grm7, and neither Grm1, Grm5, nor Grm6 exposed a hidden metabotropic-glutamate transcriptional module.
The broader Gi/o-adenylyl-cyclase receptor branch was also largely transcriptionally buffered.
The data-driven signature neighbors of Grm7 were weak, noncanonical, and not FDR-overlap neighbors.
The P16 mosaic LoF null separates GRM7 developmental/synaptic disease biology from a broad postmitotic stress or identity RNA program.
Grm8 loss of function was a measured pan-surface transcriptomic null: 0 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.

Flatness was shared across represented metabotropic glutamate receptor paralogs: Grm1, Grm5, Grm6, Grm7, and Grm8 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and their score correlations with Grm8 were all |r|<0.009.
Grm8 perturbation did not leave a sustained activity-dependent immediate-early footprint: Fos/Fosl2/Jun/Junb/Jund/Egr/Arc/Npas4/Nr4a/Bdnf/Homer1 family rows were all FDR=1.0.

The unbiased Grm8 signature had no interpretable positive or negative neighbor: the strongest correlations over matched score vectors were Safe_target-labeled perturbations or tiny biological-target correlations of +0.033 to -0.018.
Grn produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 hits: Zbtb21 was up in 053 Sst Gaba and Ehmt2 was down in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
direction_pattern: Zbtb21 up in Sst; Ehmt2 down in CNU-LGE LSX

canonical_summary: The canonical PGRN lysosomal, autophagy, TDP-43, and innate-immune sentinel program was absent from all Grn-measured neuronal groups.
Full-transcriptome score-neighbor search found no coherent Grn-like perturbation; the top correlations were all near zero and included a safe-target control among the highest positive raw scores.
SORT1/PSAP/LRP1/TMEM106B and broader lysosome-autophagy perturbations did not phenocopy Grn or share its Zbtb21/Ehmt2 singleton features.
Tardbp was a broad neuronal responder where Grn was mostly flat, producing 696 downstream genes across Grn-matched groups with no overlap to the two Grn hit features.
Young sparse neuron-only RNA signatures greatly under-call progranulin biology that depends on secreted PGRN exchange and microglial lysosomes.
Postnatal CRISPR loss of Gsdme produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal group.
Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor directly queryable apoptosis-axis comparators converged with Gsdme on a robust module.
The DFNA5 hearing-loss biology is displaced from this brain-neuron loss-of-function assay.
Gsk3b produced a robust transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 8 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the other 20 measured groups.
The 151 Gsk3b response was a small mixed marker set, with Nrbp2, Rock2, Cck, Rsrp1, Nap1l5, and Faah down and Bhlhe40 plus Abca2 up.
Tsc2 was the leading robust positive cross-perturbation neighbor of Gsk3b in the 151 restricted signature.
The Gsk3b 151 trace opposed several robust 151 signatures, including Grin1, Caml, and Arid2, and weakly opposed Mtor.
Canonical Wnt/β-catenin transcription was absent after Gsk3b perturbation even though Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations were strongly detectable in 151.
Gsk3b loss did not change App, Mapt, Psen1, or Bace1 mRNAs in the responding group.
Tsc2 was much broader than Gsk3b across matched cell groups despite their 151 convergence.
Gstm5 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered in every measured neuronal group: 22 groups had Gstm5 rows and all had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Gstm5 perturbation did not activate the expected NRF2/glutathione, GST-paralog, oxidative-stress, ER-stress, or integrated-stress transcripts.

Gstm5 did not enter a reproducible cross-perturbation module: the strongest positive and negative whole-universe neighbors had signed-score cosines of only +0.029 and -0.023, and literature-obvious redox comparators were near-zero as well.
Gtf2h5 perturbation produced a narrowly significant Clu and Polr2a up-regulation only in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The complete Gtf2h5 191 MB P MY GABA signature was the top shared-direction subset of Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations.
Gtf2h5 loss was largely uncoupled from a canonical TFIIH or NER transcriptional stress program in basal juvenile neurons.
Gtf2i produced a compact response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only one downstream hit each in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Gtf2i signature is a small membrane/lipid/electrical-state gene set rather than a broad neuronal injury program.
Notum is an up-regulated, single-gene Wnt-antagonist marker of the main Gtf2i response.
Gtf2ird1 and other Williams-region comparators fail to phenocopy Gtf2i in the matched DE surface.
Empirical neighbors, not textbook Williams genes, share or invert the sparse Gtf2i thalamic signature.
The recovered Gtf2i responders lack a coordinated apoptosis, mitophagy/autophagy, mitochondrial-dynamics, or synaptic-transcript collapse.
Gas2l1 and Erlin2 define two posterior single-gene Gtf2i responses.
Significant Gtf2i self-transcript reduction can coexist with a downstream zero.

Postnatal mosaic Gtf2ird1 loss produced an almost flat neuronal transcriptome: only 9 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 3 of 22 measured cell groups, and no cell group showed FDR-significant reduction of the Gtf2ird1 transcript itself.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only multi-gene Gtf2ird1 responder, with 6 up-regulated genes, F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, Abca3, St3gal5, and Gkap1, and one down-regulated gene, Cit.
Two additional Gtf2ird1 responder groups consisted of one up-regulated marker each: Cckbr in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Smarcc2 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

The represented TFII-I/Williams-Beuren comparators did not phenocopy Gtf2ird1: Gtf2i had a distinct 151 TH signature with no overlap among the seven Gtf2ird1 TH genes, Baz1b was nearly flat, and Limk1 was flat in every matched group.

The small thalamic F11r/Sparcl1/Cit sub-signature was reused but with different signs by unrelated perturbations: Zeb1 and Zmym2 also up-regulated F11r, whereas Brd4 and Rnpc3 inverted key Gtf2ird1 TH genes.
Gucy2c loss produced a single FDR-controlled downstream hit: Cacng3 was down in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, while every other recovered group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Represented guanylyl-cyclase and cyclic-nucleotide comparators did not phenocopy Gucy2c in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Gucy2c had no high-confidence global convergent module; its nearest whole-universe neighbors had cosine magnitudes near zero and included safe-target controls.
Postmitotic Gucy2c perturbation did not recover hypothalamic Pomc/Lepr or nigral mitochondrial-stress marker programs in the measured broad hypothalamic and non-dopaminergic midbrain groups.
Direct perturbation of the data-nominated Cacng3 target, and of its TARP paralog Cacng2, was transcriptionally flat and did not reproduce the Gucy2c-linked 012 signature.
Gucy2e produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured neuronal brain cell groups.
Canonical phototransduction and photoreceptor-identity sentinel genes remained unchanged downstream of Gucy2e.
Represented guanylyl-cyclase or retinal comparators did not uncover a Gucy2e-like brain signature.
The unbiased centered-logFC search found no strong positive or negative Gucy2e signature neighbor.
H2-Eb1 loss produced a pan-neuronal null: all 23 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and no adjusted self-transcript depletion.
The IFNgamma-STAT1/MHC-II induction axis was not active in the measured neuronal perturbation universe.
The strongest unbiased H2-Eb1 signature neighbors were all effectively zero-correlation profiles and were rejected as phenocopies.
H2ac8 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 measured neuronal cell groups, and the H2ac8 self-transcript was FDR=1.0 in every group.

A data-driven neighbor search rejected the idea that H2ac8 carries a weak version of another target's signature: the best positive and negative Pearson correlations were only 0.0386 for Msx2 and -0.0335 for Fbxo11.

The only directly tested histone comparators, H3f3a and H4c11, did not produce a broad H2ac8-like response: H3f3a had zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes over 22 matched groups, and H4c11 had only one isolated Ryr2 hit.
H3f3a CRISPR was transcriptionally flat across all 22 measured neuronal classes: no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 anywhere, and the H3f3a transcript itself had FDR=1.0 in every group.
The flat downstream surface did not conceal an H3.3 paralog/chaperone mRNA bounce-back: H3f3b, Hira, Daxx and Atrx transcripts all stayed below FDR<0.10 in every measured H3f3a group.
Atrx, the only represented H3.3-deposition comparator, created a small FDR-level signature but did not phenocopy H3f3a.

Data-driven signature search found no meaningful H3f3a neighbor: the strongest positive score correlation was Ndufb9 at r=0.033 and the strongest overall negative was a four-group Safe_target_58 at r=-0.017.
Loss of H3f3a in postmitotic neurons did not model H3F3A oncohistone biology.
H4c11 generated a single significant downstream response, Ryr2 up-regulation, restricted to 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
A single H4c11 locus is broadly buffered in postmitotic juvenile neurons.
The represented single core-histone comparators H2ac8 and H3f3a were also FDR-flat and did not phenocopy the H4c11 Ryr2 response.
H4c11 had no strong data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor in the parquet.
The postnatal H4c11 LoF null does not phenocopy human H4C11 missense neurodevelopmental disease.
Hap1 loss was a pan-neuronal downstream transcriptomic null: 22 of 22 measured cell groups had zero non-Hap1 genes at FDR<0.10, despite a significant self-transcript decrease in 155 MB Glut.

Hap1 did not phenocopy Htt or Dctn1, even though each is an HAP1 trafficking partner: Htt generated 16 downstream DE genes and Dctn1 generated 450, dominated by SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthetic genes, in groups where Hap1 had none.
direction_pattern: Hap1 flat; Htt/Dctn1 up-regulate lipid genes

canonical_summary: The literature-prominent HAP1-KIF5-GABA_A and HAP1-BDNF/TrkB arms were not recovered as Hap1 mRNA programs; Kif5a and Kif5c themselves were flat, direct Ntrk2 produced only 3 downstream genes, and most GABA_A receptor/gephyrin perturbations were flat or very weak.

No strong data-driven transcriptional neighbor was found for Hap1: the best signed-score neighbor was Zkscan16 at r=0.033854, and the strongest negative neighbor was a safe-target control at r=-0.017822.

Postnatal Hbs1l loss was almost completely buffered at the nuclear-RNA level: only two single-gene FDR<0.10 calls were recovered across 22 measured neuronal groups, while every Hbs1l self-transcript test had FDR=1.0.
The only significant Hbs1l-induced transcripts were Babam1 up-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Usp48 down-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Uba5 and Ufc1 were the top two positive score-neighbors of Hbs1l, yet bona fide UFMylation perturbation was much broader than Hbs1l and did not share either Hbs1l FDR gene.

ASCC3 and EEF2 perturbations triggered detectable translation-quality-control or elongation-associated signatures in the same neuronal screen, whereas Hbs1l, Eif2ak4, and Upf3b did not produce comparable broad stress programs.
Hcn1 loss was almost transcriptionally silent after sparse postnatal CRISPR: 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 371,796 measured downstream tests and no Hcn1 self-transcript row below FDR 0.10.
The only Hcn1 downstream hit was Ctnnd2 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA neurons.
Hcn1 perturbation did not recover an activity-dependent immediate-early program or compensatory regulation of Hcn2, Kv, NaV, CaV, or Na/K-ATPase genes.
Hcn2, the only represented HCN paralog, was also downstream-silent despite significant Hcn2 mRNA depletion in 9 matched groups.
The data-driven Hcn1 neighbors were all near zero and non-HCN: Smad1, Adrb2, and Htr2b topped the positive list with cosines of only about 0.027-0.028, and none reproduced the Ctnnd2 CNU-MGE event.
Direct Ctnnd2 perturbation did not feed forward in the Hcn1-responsive CNU-MGE GABA group: it had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes there, while its only dataset-wide hit was Elfn2 in MB Glut.
Eef2 was a weak negative Hcn1 signature neighbor but a broad transcriptional responder, with 1,119 downstream genes across 14 matched groups versus one Hcn1 downstream gene.
Hcn2 mRNA was lower in every recovered cell group, significantly in 9 of 22, yet no non-Hcn2 transcript reached FDR<0.10 anywhere.
The only measured HCN pore-family comparator, Hcn1, had essentially zero whole-transcriptome similarity to Hcn2 and only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene in matched groups.
Hcn2 has no strong data-driven signature neighbor: the top positive neighbors have r=0.030-0.033 and the top negative neighbors have r=-0.011 to -0.015.
The flat Hcn2 LoF transcriptome should not be read as testing all HCN2 channelopathy alleles, because human HCN2 epilepsies include gain-of-function and dominant-negative channel mechanisms.
Hcrtr2 was a pan-null basal snRNA-seq perturbation: none of the 371,796 downstream tests in its 22 measured neuronal groups reached FDR<0.10.
The expected OX2R-to-ERK/CREB immediate-early transcriptional readout was absent across the Hcrtr2 surface.
Unbiased cross-target matching found no meaningful positive or negative Hcrtr2 signature neighbor.
Available OX2R signal-transduction perturbations did not phenocopy Hcrtr2: Gnao1, Gnas, Plcb1, Mapk1, Creb1, Camk2a, Camk2b and Adcy5 all had near-zero cosine to Hcrtr2.
The flat P16 mosaic transcriptional profile should not be used to de-prioritize OX2R pharmacology for sleep/wake disorders.
Hdac5 loss produced a single-gene, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut-restricted transcriptomic response: Chd5 upregulation.
Chd5 was a selective candidate marker of Hdac5 engagement in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Hdac5 did not activate the canonical activity/MEF2 target program after loss of function.
Represented MEF2, CaMK, and PKA pathway perturbations did not phenocopy the Hdac5 Chd5 signature.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Hdac5 convergent or inverse target.
The 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA null refines nucleus-accumbens cocaine literature to a stimulus-gated model.
Hdac8 had no FDR<0.10 downstream DE genes in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups, despite each group containing a measured Hdac8 self row.

Hdac8 did not phenocopy directly measured cohesin or chromatin-loop perturbations: Smc1a and Stag2 generated overlapping 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signatures, and Ctcf was a broad responder, while Hdac8 was null.
The only represented HDAC-family comparator, Hdac5, showed just one significant downstream gene and no shared module with Hdac8.
A flat sparse postnatal neuronal Hdac8 signature should not be used to de-risk HDAC8 inhibition in developmental lineages.
Hdgf loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups, despite the Hdgf transcript being quantified in all 22.

Residual whole-surface signature matching did not nominate a credible Hdgf phenocopy or anti-phenocopy: the strongest coverage-matched neighbors, Pax6 and Myod1, had near-zero correlations and flat matched DE surfaces.
Hdx loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a cell-type-restricted responder: every one of the 22 recovered Hdx cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The only direct HDX target program in the literature, EPAS1/HIF-2alpha release from repression in hypoxic neuroblastoma, was not reproduced in Hdx-perturbed mouse neurons.
A model-visible neighbor scan placed Hdx in the correlation noise floor rather than in a recurrent perturbation module.
Measured POU-class homeobox relatives were also almost entirely flat, so Hdx did not hide a shared acute postmitotic POU-like neuronal state change.
Hectd4 perturbation produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Hectd4 loss did not transcriptionally activate the GluN2B-MALT1-STEP61 injury axis in healthy juvenile neurons.
Huwe1, but not Hectd4 or most other represented HECT-family targets, generated a multi-cell-group transcriptomic response.
Full-rank Hectd4 signature neighbors were extremely weak and biologically unconvincing.
The P16 Hectd4 null shifts the missing disease-relevant mechanism toward developmental wiring and protein-level ubiquitination rather than mature-neuron transcriptional maintenance.
Hecw2 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups, and a 12-gene p53/p73 stress-apoptosis panel was completely unrecovered.

The Hecw2 null was not a generic failure of HECT E3-ligase perturbations: Huwe1 generated a reproducible splicing/RNA-processing-rich signature, whereas Hectd4 and Ube3a were flat and Herc1/Herc2 had only isolated DE genes.

The disease-relevant HECW2 biology is displaced from this screen's main axis: patient alleles and animal knockdown point to germline or early developmental effects, whereas P16 mosaic loss in surviving NeuN+ neurons left no large mRNA scar.
A whole-universe signed-rank neighbor scan found no meaningful Hecw2 convergence or antagonism: the top positive and negative Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon scores were only +0.0348 and -0.0223.
Acute P16 Herc1 loss of function was almost completely buffered at the single-nucleus transcriptional level, with only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across the whole recovered surface.
The only robust Herc1-dependent transcript was Dnm1 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA neurons.
Herc1 did not phenocopy Tsc2 or Mtor perturbation in any matched group, uncoupling the postnatal neuronal signature from canonical TSC/mTOR transcriptional responses.
The Herc1 Dnm1 singleton is not a Cltc or Dnm1 loss-of-function signature.
Herc2, the other large HERC-family E3 ligase in the screen, did not converge with Herc1.
A genome-wide restricted-nearest-neighbor search found no strong positive or inverse Herc1 phenocopy.

Herc2 loss produced an extremely sparse but real P16-to-P37/44 neuronal transcriptome: Rack1 was induced in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Dlat was induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 20 other measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Rack1 up-regulation was a private L5 ET marker of Herc2 perturbation: in that group Rack1 reached logFC 0.866 and FDR 0.0247, and no other tested perturbation made Rack1 significant at FDR<0.10.
Dlat up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nominated a mitochondrial pyruvate-dehydrogenase node as the thalamic Herc2 readout.
Herc1 and Ube3a failed to phenocopy the two Herc2 endpoint genes in matched responder groups.
Acute Herc2 knockout did not activate the canonical DNA-damage, p53, UBE3A/HERC-compensation, FBXL5/iron, UPR/ISR, proteasome, or autophagy marker set at transcriptional FDR<0.10.

Herc2 did not have a strong transcriptome-scale neighbor: the top same- and opposite-direction whole-rank neighbors were Tsc2 and Wdr26, but their cosines were only 0.0376 and -0.0266 and neither reproduced Rack1 or Dlat at FDR<0.10.

Hesx1 loss at P16 was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null across the recovered cell groups: zero downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in 22 measured groups spanning cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, hypothalamus, midbrain/pineal-labeled groups, and cerebellar GABA neurons.

The embryonic HESX1→Wnt/β-catenin repression program was not reactivated by postnatal Hesx1 loss: Axin2 and Lef1 were not significant under Hesx1, yet direct Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations produced thalamic signatures in the same matched analysis universe.

Hesx1 did not phenocopy the measured forebrain/pituitary transcription-factor network: Prop1, Lhx3, Lhx4, Otx2, Pax6, Pitx2, Pou1f1, and Gli2 were also FDR-null across the 22 matched groups, while Pax2, Six3, Rax, and Sox2 had only isolated one- or two-gene effects.

The pre-literature full-logFC nearest-neighbor calculation returned Six5 and Clpx as the top positive raw neighbors but both were themselves null; the most distant eligible profiles were broad proteasome perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1, which still had positive raw correlations.
Acute P16 Hic1 loss was transcriptomically buffered across every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class.
The canonical HIC1-SIRT1-p53 DNA-damage loop did not fire in the young neuronal screen.
The Hic1-Ptch1-Atoh1 medulloblastoma axis is absent from the sampled postmitotic neuronal compartment.
Wnt/chromatin perturbations were detectable where Hic1 was flat, rejecting a simple phenocopy with Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Chd4, Arid1a, or Ctbp1.
Hic1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbors beyond other null-like perturbations.
Acute Hif1a loss-of-function was pan-null across the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
Canonical HIF target transcripts were absent from the Hif1a-null surface.
The only same-complex HIF comparator available, Arnt, phenocopied Hif1a by being FDR-null; Ahr, another ARNT-dependent axis, was also flat.
Unbiased signature-neighbor search rejected both convergence and antagonism for Hif1a.
The quiet normoxic neuronal surface should not be extrapolated to injured or HIF-drugged brain.
Acute Hivep1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected NF-κB, cytokine, complement/MHC, and glial-inflammatory readouts were absent after Hivep1 perturbation.
The two measured HIVEP paralogs did not phenocopy Hivep1 in matched neurons: Hivep2 was fully flat and Hivep3 yielded only two isolated singleton DE genes.
Perturbing represented TLR/NF-κB neighbors also failed to reveal a Hivep1-like response.
The unbiased cross-perturbation search found no meaningful positive or negative Hivep1 signature neighbor.
Hivep2 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups despite one significant on-target mRNA decrease in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
The NF-κB, complement, MHC, and astrocyte-response program expected from germline Schnurri-2 deficiency was absent from Hivep2-perturbed neuronal nuclei.
Sstr2, Myc, Arc, dentate granule-cell maturation markers, and inhibitory markers were all flat after Hivep2 perturbation.

Hivep1, Hivep3, Nfkb1, and Chuk did not converge with Hivep2: the two paralogs and two NF-κB-side perturbations were flat or nearly flat with score correlations from 0.0005 to 0.0066 for the main flat comparators.
Ogt and immature-dentate comparators such as Camk2a, Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, and Ntrk2 did not phenocopy Hivep2; Ogt was a broad responder with 2154 FDR<0.10 genes whereas Hivep2 remained flat.

The data-driven top Hivep2 neighbors were near-zero full-vector correlations; the positive neighbors Unc5c, Erbb4, and Mbd5 and the negative neighbors Safe_target_81, Fbxo11, and Eef2 did not share any FDR genes with Hivep2.
Hivep3 loss produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 23 measured neuronal groups: Sorbs2 was up in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and R3hdm2 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The R3hdm2-up coordinate in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recurred in Tm2d1, Huwe1, Lrrtm1 and Gabrb2 perturbations; Tm2d1, Huwe1 and Lrrtm1 were the top three positive neighbors of the restricted Hivep3 two-gene signature.

The restricted Hivep3 signature is opposed by Sin3a, Wdr26 and Ogt: Sin3a and Wdr26 significantly down-regulate R3hdm2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Ogt significantly down-regulates Sorbs2 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Hivep1, Hivep2, the recovered NF-κB perturbations Nfkb1, Rel and Chuk, and the BMP/Runx2 perturbations Runx2, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad4 and Smad9 did not reproduce the Hivep3 Sorbs2/R3hdm2 response.
Hivep3 loss did not induce or repress the expected NF-κB/TNF, Runx2/Alg2/BMP, Id or chondrogenic ER-response genes at FDR<0.10 anywhere in the neuronal surface.
Sorbs2 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA nominates a hypothalamic GABAergic actin-synaptic scaffold marker after Hivep3 loss.
direction_pattern: up with Hivep3, down with Ogt at the same coordinate

canonical_summary: Acute Hjv loss of function was nearly transcriptionally silent across juvenile postmitotic NeuN+ brain neurons, producing one corrected downstream gene across all 23 measured cell groups and no corrected BMP/hepcidin/iron-homeostasis program.
The only robust Hjv downstream hit was a Sst-interneuron up-regulation of Rxylt1.
Measured RGM-neogenin/BMP pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Hjv.
The Hjv null was not a generic failure to detect iron-linked perturbations: Tfrc and Ireb2 produced small corrected signatures, but in other cell groups and genes.
The whole-universe Hjv transcriptomic-neighbor search found no convincing same-sign or opposite-sign partner.
Hk1 loss-of-function was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null in the assayed postmitotic brain: no measured cell group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The Hk1 LoF surface does not support simple haploinsufficiency as a strong postnatal neuronal transcriptional mechanism for dominant HK1 neurodevelopmental disease.
Hk1 failed to converge with represented glucose-entry and glycolytic comparators, whereas direct Ogt perturbation was broadly active in the very same cell groups.
The unbiased Hk1 signature-neighbor scan found no material positive or negative module.
A quiet neuronal snRNA-seq surface does not de-risk HK1 inhibition.
Hlcs perturbation is pan-null across the 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no FDR-significant induction of monitored carboxylase, ISR, or UPR transcripts.
Pcca, the represented direct propionyl-CoA-carboxylase substrate gene, did not phenocopy a hidden Hlcs program; both perturbations were flat and their DE-score vectors correlated only weakly.

All-universe signature ranking found no convergent Hlcs module: top positive and negative Pearson correlations were below 0.05 in absolute value, and the strongest anti-neighbor Wdr26 had thousands of FDR-significant genes where Hlcs had none.
Acute Hmgcr loss produced an almost flat neuronal transcriptional surface rather than a sterol-feedback signature.
The only real Hmgcr downstream hits were two isolated up-regulated transcripts: Hdac11 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Hnrnpul1 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Srebf2, but not Hmgcr, recovered a cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional module in the same parquet.
The other queryable Hmgcr relatives, Srebf1 and Fntb, did not phenocopy Hmgcr.
The strongest data-driven neighbors of Hmgcr were very weak proteasome/ER-associated signatures, not sterol-pathway perturbations.
Hmgcr did not induce the UPR/ISR-like stress program that the same assay recovered after Atp2a2 perturbation.
The screen separates Hmgcr muscle/liver essentiality from buffered postmitotic neuronal RNA phenotypes.
Hnf1a loss of function had no FDR-level whole-transcriptome response in any of the 23 recovered postnatal neuronal cell groups.
The neuronal Hnf1a null was shared by its directly represented HNF/MODY transcription-network comparators rather than selectively rescued or phenocopied by one paralog.
Whole-universe signature search did not reveal a robust Hnf1a-associated neuronal module.
Hnf1b produced no corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured juvenile neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.
Canonical HNF1B target programs were absent from the Hnf1b signature even when their genes were present in the Wilcoxon tables.
Literature-obvious neighbors of HNF1B were also weak or null in the same neuronal atlas, and none shared an FDR<0.10 signature with Hnf1b.
Data-driven score neighbors did not reveal a biologically large Hnf1b-like module.
The 17q12/HNF1B neurodevelopmental association is not phenocopied by acute Hnf1b loss in sampled P16 postmitotic neurons.
Hnf4a perturbation produced a single robust downstream change, Cacybp down-regulation, in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Postnatal Hnf4a loss does not recover the canonical HNF4A hepatocyte, visceral-endoderm, intestinal, or pancreatic transcriptional program in any sampled neuronal class.
HNF4/endoderm relatives represented in the parquet largely co-null with Hnf4a instead of uncovering a hidden neuronal HNF module.
direction_pattern: Hnf4g/Hnf1a/Hnf1b/Foxa2/Sox17 flat; Prox1 active in one thalamic class

canonical_summary: Unbiased whole-surface signature comparison did not find a convincing positive or negative Hnf4a neighbor.
Hnf4g loss yielded a clean FDR-level neuronal transcriptional negative across every recovered cell group.
The HNF comparison set was also nearly flat in the same brain groups: Hnf1a and Hnf1b had no FDR hits, and Hnf4a had only a single Cacybp decrease.

Unbiased score-space neighbors were rejected: the best Hnf4g cosine similarities were only +0.026 and -0.024, and the strongest apparent responder, Tsc2, had hundreds of FDR hits while Hnf4g had none.
Hnrnpa2b1 produced only 25 downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 6 of 21 measured cell groups, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

The strongest Hnrnpa2b1-responsive RNA/RNP genes point to compensatory RNP-family rebalancing: Hnrnpa1 was up in both main glutamatergic responders, Hnrnpu was down in two responders, and Rbm25, Tcerg1, and Drosha were up in the thalamic responder.

The expected m6A/pri-miRNA and antiviral IFN outputs were largely uncoupled from the measured neuronal response: Drosha was significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Dgcr8, Dicer1, and assayed IFN/TBK1 markers were never FDR-significant.
Hnrnpa2b1 was far weaker than related nuclear RBP perturbations: Hnrnpu, Tardbp, Matr3, and Hnrnpc generated 2096, 670, 555, and 260 matched downstream FDR calls, respectively.

Hnrnpa2b1 had no robust whole-transcriptome signature neighbor: the top positive and negative cosine similarities were only +0.0358 and -0.0226, and the nominated neighbors shared no same-group FDR hits with Hnrnpa2b1.
Acute Hnrnpa2b1 loss did not induce a broad stress, interferon, or proteinopathy-like gene-abundance program despite HNRNPA2B1 being an ALS/MSP protein.

Outside the RNA/RNP genes, recurrent FDR hits were limited to empirical markers such as Hmgn3 up in 005 and 155, Atp11b up in 066 and 151, and Fam193b down in 151 and 155, with singletons such as Mapk1ip1, Abhd8, Cep131, Ppcdc, Peg3, and Col4a2.

Hnrnpc loss of function generated a gene-level response in only 8 of 22 measured cell groups, concentrated in thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, hindbrain/pineal, and Pvalb GABA neurons rather than broadly across telencephalic projection neurons.

The strongest Hnrnpc responders rewired RNA-processing genes: Ddx39b, Ddx17, Pabpn1, Son, Prpf39 and Cpsf7 rose in selected groups, whereas Luc7l2, Rbm25, Srsf2, Tia1 or Hnrnpu fell in major thalamic/midbrain responders.
Hnrnpc-responsive groups induced a proteostasis/stress-granule-clearance flank marked by recurrent Txnl1 and by Zfand1, Anapc5, Ube2f, Rbx1, Josd1 and ubiquitin-pathway genes.
A mitochondrial nucleotide/mtRNA module accompanied Hnrnpc loss: Mterf3 was up in six responders, Slc25a36 in five, and Slc25a3, Atp5d, Ppm1k or Mff in selected major responders.

Major responders also changed neuronal effector genes, including Cacna1a up in 151/191/217, vesicle or endomembrane genes Scamp5, Stx3 and Stx1b, and down-regulation of Dst, Syne1, L1cam, Syt7, Shank3 or Gpm6a in selected groups.

Prpf6, a U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP spliceosome perturbation, was the top robust Hnrnpc signature neighbor; Snrnp70, Rnpc3 and Cdc40 produced broader spliceosome-related signatures that only partly overlapped Hnrnpc.

The expected U2AF2 antagonist did not form a clean opposite Hnrnpc gene-expression mirror: U2af2 was broad in the same neuronal groups but its Hnrnpc-overlapping calls were nearly balanced in direction.
Measured hnRNP-family members were not interchangeable with Hnrnpc: Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnph2 and Hnrnpdl were almost flat, whereas Hnrnpu was broad but directionally mixed relative to Hnrnpc.
Hnrnpc loss did not activate a detectable interferon/dsRNA response in the 22 measured neuronal groups.
The 217 P MY Pineal Glut responder carried a low-count, exploratory tail with Gclc and Rubcnl induction plus Jund, Tle2 and Gtf3c5 down-regulation.

Hnrnpdl loss in P16 sparse postmitotic neurons produced an almost fully buffered gene-abundance surface: only Hnrnpu in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Sh3bp5 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured classes.
The strongest Hnrnpdl-dependent transcript was Hnrnpu up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the same Hnrnpu row moved in the opposite direction after Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnpc or Wdr26 perturbation.
Hnrnpdl perturbation selectively increased Sh3bp5 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

Measurable hnRNP-family perturbations did not phenocopy Hnrnpdl: Hnrnpu and Hnrnpc altered 2140 and 294 downstream genes in matched groups, whereas Hnrnpdl altered 2, and their whole-surface correlations with Hnrnpdl were near zero.
The top model-visible neighbors of Hnrnpdl were not convincing biological convergers: the best positive non-safe correlation was Wdr26 at r=0.0446 and the best negative was Fbxo11 at r=-0.0469.

The P16 neuronal CRISPR perturbation did not recover broad muscle-dystrophy, phase-separation/proteostasis, endothelial-sprouting, or proliferative cell-cycle programs described for HNRNPDL in other systems.
Hnrnph2 loss produced only seven downstream whole-gene FDR<0.10 calls, concentrated in four caudal neuronal groups and absent from the other 18 measured groups.
Rsrp1 down-regulation was the recurrent RNA-processing readout of Hnrnph2 perturbation, appearing in 145, 151, and 155, while no other downstream gene recurred in more than two groups.
Idh3g, Ogdh, and Timm44 were induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Idh3g also induced in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Hnrnpu was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor, matching five of seven Hnrnph2 downstream coordinates including Rsrp1 down in three groups and Idh3g up in two.
U2af2, Cdc40, Prpf6, Snrnp70, and Matr3 converged with Hnrnph2 on Rsrp1 down-regulation but did not consistently share the Idh3g/Ogdh/Timm44 branch.
Proteasome/autophagy/translation-adjacent neighbors such as Psmb4, Huwe1, Gigyf2, and Rab7 opposed the Hnrnph2 Rsrp1 or Idh3g directions.
Hnrnpu-targeted nuclei up-regulated Hnrnpu RNA across all measured groups rather than showing a simple knockdown signature.

The acute Hnrnpu transcriptome was broad but concentrated in thalamic and midbrain groups, with 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA carrying 80.8% of all downstream FDR<0.10 events.
Hnrnpu induced a compensatory RNA-processing module and converged with spliceosome/RNA-processing perturbations.
Amino-acid starvation and ISR-like genes were induced in the largest Hnrnpu responders.
Hnrnpu triggered ubiquitin, lysosome, autophagy, and proteasome-quality-control genes and converged with direct proteasome-subunit perturbations.
Hnrnpu loss paired compensatory transport/cytoskeletal up-regulation with down-regulation of synaptic, axonal, and ciliary/neurite genes.
Chromatin and transcriptional regulators headed by Dmtf1 and Hdac3 were induced across the Hnrnpu surface.
An ECM/secretory-matrix module, including Col4a1, Col4a2, Colgalt1, Adam15, and Vldlr, rose in several neuronal Hnrnpu responders.
Measured hnRNP-family perturbations did not phenocopy Hnrnpu even though RNA-processing perturbations did.
Depdc5 was an Hnrnpu-induced gene, but the mTOR/DEE comparator landscape split: Tsc2 converged while Depdc5, Mtor, Scn2a, and Grin1 were rejected as phenocopies.
Setd1a and Zbtb7a were robust opposite-overlap comparators for the Hnrnpu signature.
The acute P16 Hnrnpu signature is a survivor stress signature, not a clean embryonic HNRNPU-NDD disease signature for direct transcriptomic reversal.
Dmtf1, Atxn2l, Gpr180, Ahi1, Rsrp1, Macf1, Depdc5, and Hdac3 form recurrent marker genes for acute neuronal Hnrnpu perturbation.
Homer2 loss produced a pan-measured, FDR-level null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Direct Homer-complex perturbations did not reveal a shared transcriptomic module that Homer2 failed to match.
The all-target, data-driven nearest neighbors of Homer2 were too weak to support a hidden convergent signature.
The addiction-linked mGluR5-Homer2-PI3K axis is not reproduced as a basal juvenile neuronal RNA state.
Hoxa13 produced a narrowly cell-class-restricted 217 P MY Pineal Glut response consisting only of Acp6 and Slc49a4 up-regulation at FDR<0.10.
The 217 Acp6/Slc49a4 signature was not shared by represented Hox-family targets or by assayed Pbx, Meis, and Pknox2 Hox cofactors.
Embryonic Bmp/Fgf/Eph/Gata3/vascular Hoxa13 effectors were absent from the postnatal neuronal DE surface.
Hoxa13 was transcriptionally buffered across 22 of 23 measured neuronal cell groups, with only one sub-threshold weak group.
The strongest data-driven anti-neighbor was Thap11, which robustly down-regulated Acp6 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut rather than reproducing the Hoxa13 up-signature.
P16 Hoxa1 loss was pan-cell-type flat at the robust DE threshold: all 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The embryonic Hoxa1 retinoic-acid and rhombomere program was not re-induced or derepressed after P16 Hoxa1 loss.
Represented HOX-family and Hox-cofactor/retinoic-acid comparators also failed to produce a broad postnatal neuronal Hoxa1-like signature.

Phenotype-first global neighbors of Hoxa1 were at noise-scale correlations, so Msx2, Wwox and Mbd5 were rejected as convergent positives and Lgals3, Wnk3 and Or51e2 were rejected as meaningful anti-neighbors.
The screen refines HOXA1-related disease biology toward congenital patterning in embryonic and non-neuronal derivatives, not ongoing Hoxa1 dependence of broad sampled juvenile neurons.
Hoxa3 is a pan-measured neuronal null in this P16-to-P37/P44 brain CRISPR screen.
Canonical third-pharyngeal-pouch and thymus/parathyroid marker genes were not mobilized by Hoxa3 loss in any measured neuronal group.
Perturbations of represented Hox/TALE/pharyngeal relatives did not phenocopy Hoxa3; most were as flat as Hoxa3.
The de novo Hoxa3 signature neighbors are random-like rather than a hidden convergent pathway.
Acute P16 Hoxb8 perturbation produced no robust neuronal transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered brain cell groups.
The Hoxb8 score vector had no meaningful transcriptomic neighbor: even the most positive and most negative genome-wide comparators had |r| ≤ 0.032.
Represented Hox genes and the Pbx/Meis TALE cofactors did not converge with Hoxb8 in this postnatal neuronal screen.

The neuronal all-null surface is most consistent with Hoxb8-linked grooming and anxiety phenotypes being microglial or developmental-circuit phenomena, not acute transcriptional defects of the sampled neurons.
The only reproducible Hoxd10 call was Tut1 up-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with no broader FDR<0.10 cascade.
Represented Hox-family targets and Pbx/Meis Hox cofactors did not phenocopy Hoxd10 in the matched P16 brain groups.
Unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no strong Hoxd10 signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
The perturbation did not ectopically reveal the embryonic lumbar motor-neuron program expected from Hoxd10 biology.
Hoxd13 targeting produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
Expected HOX13 embryonic limb and skeletal-patterning readouts were not induced or repressed by Hoxd13 in the brain screen.
Hoxd13 had no strong data-driven signature neighbors; top unbiased cosine similarities were near zero.
Represented HOX paralogs and PBX/MEIS cofactors did not converge with Hoxd13 in matched postnatal brain groups.
Single Hras perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
Hras failed to phenocopy represented Ras/MAPK neighbors, even in the thalamic cell class where Braf and Map2k1 both down-regulated Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a.
The expected basal Ras/ERK feedback and immediate-early module was not recovered after Hras loss.
A whole-universe score-cosine search found no strong positive or negative Hras signature neighbor.
Hs6st2 had no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured cell group.
The published hippocampal dendrite/synapse-down and ribosome/translation-up programs were absent from the two hippocampal excitatory groups.
Measurable HS-chain and FGF-receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Hs6st2, and Hs6st1/Hs6st3 were absent as targets.
Hs6st2 sits near the origin of cross-perturbation signature space.
The screen separates HS6ST2-linked disease biology from an acutely reversible postnatal neuronal DE cascade.
Hsd17b4 loss of function produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 21 recovered cell groups.
Directly measured peroxisomal relatives did not phenocopy Hsd17b4; Abcd3, Acbd5, and Pex14 were flat and Pex1 had only two isolated singleton FDR hits.
The Hsd17b4 raw full-transcriptome surface had no robust data-driven signature neighbor; the top positive and negative Pearson correlations were only 0.029 and -0.020.
Expected lipid-feedback and injury marker panels were absent from the Hsd17b4 DE surface; all queried peroxisomal, PPAR/SREBP, UPR/ISR, and cerebellar neuronal marker genes had FDR=1.0.
Postnatal Hsf1 loss reproducibly depresses a small HSP90/HSP110 co-chaperone module rather than activating a large mixed stress program.
Basal HSF1 dependence is sharply cell-type restricted in this P16-P44 neuronal screen.
Hsf1 loss did not itself produce a proteotoxic-stress, UPR/ISR, proteasome-bounce-back, redox, apoptosis, or mitochondrial stress transcriptome.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations run the Hsf1 HSP signature in the opposite direction.
Chaperone loss is not equivalent to Hsf1 loss: Hspa8 partially anti-phenocopies Hsf1, and Hsp90ab1 knockdown is almost exclusively on-target.
The leading non-Hsp same-direction neighbors were Sin3a, Prpf6, and U2af2, not other heat-shock factors.
Nrf1, Atf6, Nfe2l2, and Vcp were measured stress-branch comparators but did not phenocopy Hsf1.
Rsrp1 is the most recurrent non-classical transcript in the Hsf1 neuronal signature.
Acute Hsp90ab1 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every assayed neuronal class: all 23 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a negative Hsp90ab1 snRNA logFC in every group.
The canonical HSF1 heat-shock output expected after strong Hsp90 blockade, and broader ISR/UPR/autophagy stress reporters, were absent after Hsp90ab1 CRISPR.

The same assay readily detected proteotoxic remodeling when the 26S proteasome was hit: Psmb4 and Psmc1 generated 14008 and 11089 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, respectively, and in 155 MB Glut they shared 1823 same-direction DE genes while Hsp90ab1 had none.

Measured Hsp90-neighborhood perturbations did not phenocopy Hsp90ab1 or the core proteasome program: Hsf1, Hspa5, Hspa8 and Vcp produced only 6-24 downstream DE genes in total, and represented DnaJ perturbations were essentially flat.

Hsp90ab1 had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor: full signed-score cosines were only +0.0275 for the top positive gene Psmb4 and -0.0126 for the top negative gene Npy1r, with safe-target signatures among the extreme negative and positive ranks.

A single Hsp90β hypomorph in normal postmitotic neurons did not reproduce the biology usually sought with Hsp90-directed drugs—HSF1/Hsp70 induction and proteotoxic client triage—so this negative result should not be read as a negative pan-Hsp90-inhibitor test.

Hspa5 loss was not pan-neuronal: 16 of 19 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene, whereas 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried a 20-gene ER-stress signature and 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 308 CB GABA carried only 3- and 1-gene tails.
The main 151 response was induction of an ER folding and ER-associated degradation module, with Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, and Herpud1 among the corrected up-regulated genes.

Hspa5 perturbation also recruited a partial integrated-stress/amino-acid arm in 151, marked by corrected up-regulation of Asns, Slc38a2, and Vars, while Ddit3 and Chac1 trended but did not reach FDR<0.10.
Outside 151, the only corrected Hspa5 genes were a 145 MH-LH TH Glut trio, Zfr up with Nmnat2 and Gnao1 down, and a single 308 CB GABA Ptprs decrease.

The Hspa5 151 signature converged with glycosylation and ER-calcium perturbations rather than with arbitrary anti-neighbors: Gfpt1, Dhdds, and Atp2a2 shared 11, 9, and 7 same-direction corrected Hspa5-feature overlaps, respectively.

Among represented textbook relatives, Sec63 partially phenocopied the 151 ER-chaperone arm, but Atf6, Edem3, Hspa8, Nfe2l1, Nfe2l2, Sil1, and Vcp did not recapitulate the Hspa5 signature in matched cells.

Hspa8 loss produced a small but real neuronal transcriptomic response restricted to 4 of 21 measured cell groups, with 14 downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell events and a maximum 9-gene signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: mostly up-regulated chaperone genes with a sparse down-regulated tail

canonical_summary: The recurrent positive Hspa8 program was an HSP counterinduction module, led by Dnaja1, Hsp90aa1, Hspa4l, and Cct6a and recurring across 009, 066, and 151.
direction_pattern: up in Hspa8 and down in Hsf1 for Hsp90aa1-class targets

canonical_summary: The highest positive Hspa8 signature neighbors were not Hsp70 relatives but Uba5, Psmb4, and Ufc1, which converged on Dnaja1/Hsp90aa1/Cct6a induction and selected negative genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Thoc1 was retained as the strongest negative restricted-signature neighbor of Hspa8, opposing Dnaja1 and Syt4 in 151, while Rxra and Snca were rejected after matched-cell FDR checks.
direction_pattern: Thoc1 opposing; Rxra and Snca rejected

canonical_summary: The represented chaperone relatives Hspa5 and Hsp90ab1 did not phenocopy Hspa8: Hspa5 induced ER-UPR genes absent from Hspa8, whereas Hsp90ab1 autoreduced in 15 groups with zero downstream FDR genes.
Syt4 was the only FDR-significant neuronal vesicle/activity gene recurring after Hspa8 loss, rising in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
Canonical CMA/lysosome or macroautophagy compensation was absent from the Hspa8 FDR surface, even in Hspa8-responsive groups.
Htr1a perturbation produced a pan-measured weak/flat response with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
A de novo full-universe similarity search did not identify a meaningful Htr1a transcriptional neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Represented serotonin-receptor perturbations were flat or singleton responders rather than robust Htr1a phenocopies.
Proximal 5-HT1A effector perturbations did not converge with Htr1a.
Htr1a loss did not induce immediate-early, cAMP/CREB, Bdnf, Gad, GIRK, or adenylyl-cyclase mRNAs in any measured group.
Sparse CRISPR loss of Htr1a should not be treated as a surrogate for adult 5-HT1A pharmacology.
P16 Htr1b loss of function produced no robust downstream nuclear DE signature in any measured neuronal cell group.
Serotonin-receptor and cAMP-pathway relatives did not phenocopy Htr1b in the same cell groups.

The Htr1b null redirects known behavioral and druggable biology away from steady-state neuronal soma transcription toward terminals, circuits, early axons, and unsampled peripheral or vascular compartments.
No cAMP/CREB, immediate-early, or core synaptic-transcript rebound was detected after Htr1b perturbation.
Unbiased signature neighbors were effectively absent: the largest real-gene Htr1b score correlations were |r|<0.03.
The only FDR<0.10 downstream response to Htr1f loss was Zfp513 up-regulation in 053 Sst Gaba.
Htr1f perturbation did not produce a sustained cAMP/ERK/CREB immediate-early transcriptional program in any measured neuronal class.
Measured serotonin-receptor relatives did not phenocopy Htr1f in the matched Htr1f cell groups.
The flat Htr1f CRISPR LoF surface should not be read as evidence against 5-HT1F agonism for migraine.
The genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no robust convergent or divergent Htr1f module.
Basal Htr2a loss caused a very small but FDR-supported response only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, up-regulating Kcnma1 and Cbx4.
The canonical 5-HT2A agonist immediate-early/plasticity module was absent after unstimulated Htr2a CRISPR loss of function.
Htr2b, Htr2c, and Plcb1 did not phenocopy the Htr2a Kcnma1/Cbx4 response.
Whole-transcriptome signature neighbors of Htr2a were near-zero and failed to share the responder-gene pair.
Other represented serotonin-receptor perturbations were sparse and non-overlapping with Htr2a.
The only robust Htr2b downstream event was Tor1aip2 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Htr2b loss was buffered through almost the entire sampled postmitotic neuronal panel.
Htr2b did not phenocopy Htr2a, Htr2c, other serotonin receptors, Plcb1, Gnao1, or Gnas in matched cell groups.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Htr2b convergence or anti-convergence elsewhere in the perturbation universe.
The neuronal Htr2b CRISPR null should not be used to derisk 5-HT2B pharmacology in astrocytes or heart valves.
Htr2c produced no corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered broad neuronal class.
Neither the 5-HT receptor family nor proximal second-messenger comparators converged on Htr2c.
