The Htr2c perturbation did not recover a sustained activity-response or melanocortin-neuropeptide program.
The flat Htr2c DE surface should not be read as a loss-of-function phenocopy of HTR2C obesity biology failing to exist.
A data-driven search found no meaningful positive or negative Htr2c signature neighbor.
P16 Htr3a loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The same-complex Htr3b perturbation and the broader serotonin-receptor target set were also nearly flat, rather than revealing a hidden 5-HT receptor transcriptional module.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors of Htr3a were essentially noise-scale, with signed-score cosines of only 0.0276 at the positive extreme and -0.0102 at the negative extreme.
The Htr3a null should not be used as an anti-5-HT3 pharmacodynamic negative for setron-like antagonism.
P16 mosaic Htr3b loss produced an almost completely buffered neuronal transcriptome, with only Myadm in 012 and Rab34 in 017 reaching FDR<0.10 among 22 measured groups.
Myadm was selectively down-regulated by Htr3b perturbation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Rab34 was up-regulated by Htr3b perturbation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut at the lenient FDR<0.10 threshold.
Myadm-down and Rab34-up were Htr3b-specific in their matched cell groups rather than recurrent products of other perturbations.
The same-complex comparator Htr3a and other represented serotonin receptors did not phenocopy Htr3b.
Htr3b perturbation did not recover an activity-dependent immediate-early or transmitter-identity transcriptional program.
Postnatal mosaic Htr4 loss did not produce a robust cell-autonomous steady-state RNA signature in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The canonical Htr4→Gs/cAMP/CREB expectation was not recovered as Fos/Jun/Egr/Arc/Nr4a/Crem/Bdnf transcriptional feedback.
Htr4 did not phenocopy other measured serotonin receptors; the Gs relatives Htr6 and Htr7 were also essentially flat as single-gene perturbations.
The dataset did not show the nucleus-accumbens CART or muscarinic compensatory programs previously linked to Htr4 perturbation in circuit and germline models.
The top data-driven Htr4 score-cosine neighbors were near zero, and explicit querying of Wdr26, Rax, Fxr1, Cckar, Adam10, Fbxo11 and Neo1 rejected a robust shared FDR signature.
Htr6 produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event, Ndufs1 down-regulation in 308 CB GABA, while all other measured groups were FDR-flat.
The Htr6 signature had no substantial positive or negative whole-transcriptome neighbor across the model-visible perturbation universe.
Gs-coupled serotonin and cAMP comparator perturbations did not reproduce the Htr6 CB GABA response.
Known Htr6 Cdk5/GPRIN1/Cdc42 and mTOR/CREB axes were not recovered as an Htr6 loss-of-function RNA program.

Htr7 was a pan-tested basal transcriptomic null: none of 371,818 downstream tests across 22 recovered neuronal cell groups passed FDR<0.10, and the dopaminergic midbrain group was not recovered for this target.

The expected 5-HT7R-adjacent effector and readout genes were assayed but absent at RNA level: cAMP/CREB/immediate-early, HCN-channel, and Cdc42-Cdk5-mTOR structural-plasticity genes had 0 of 572 Htr7 gene×cell tests at FDR<0.10.

Other represented serotonin receptors also failed to generate a robust basal neuronal DE module: ten Htr-family perturbations produced only 0-2 downstream FDR<0.10 genes per target in Htr7-matched groups.

Gs/cAMP pathway neighbors likewise lacked a broad transcriptional phenocopy of Htr7: represented adenylyl cyclases, G proteins, Pde4 phosphodiesterases, and PKA subunits had only 0-2 downstream FDR<0.10 genes per target in Htr7-matched groups.

An unbiased whole-universe neighbor search found no credible Htr7 convergence: the top positive and negative target correlations were all near zero, and follow-up DE surfaces either were flat or, for Eef2, reflected an unrelated strong response.

Do not treat the Htr7 snRNA null as evidence against 5-HT7 therapeutic or behavioral biology; the same receptor has knockout and antagonist phenotypes in hypothermia, circadian phase shifting, sleep, and depression-like assays that live at ligand-, circuit-, and organism-level readouts.
Htt loss induced a compact SREBP/sterol feedback module in 155 MB Glut, with Srebf2 itself and eight cholesterol uptake or biosynthesis genes upregulated.
The Htt sterol response was restricted to hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain-enriched neuronal groups and was absent from cortical, hippocampal, striatal-enriched, and cerebellar groups.
Sterol-positive Htt responders did not co-induce autophagy, lysosome, UPR/ISR, apoptosis, REST, or BDNF sentinel transcripts at FDR<0.10.
The top positive Htt signature neighbors were Dctn1, Mib1, Tsc2, Marchf6, and Rab7, and all recovered the Htt sterol module in matched responder groups.
Srebf2 loss was the strongest opposing Htt-locus signature, repressing the sterol targets that Htt loss induced.
Literature-obvious Htt comparators Hap1, Rest, Becn1, Atg5, Sqstm1, and Srebf1 did not reproduce the Htt sterol signature at its 16 significant loci.
The thalamic 151 Htt response contained a small non-sterol downregulated arm, Nalf1 and Adgrb1, that did not recur in the other Htt responders.

A wild-type Htt-lowering perturbation can activate cholesterol-feedback transcription in selected young neuronal populations without reproducing the reduced sterol transcription usually associated with mutant-HTT HD models.
Huwe1 loss produced a sharply subcortical postmitotic response rather than a pan-neuronal or cortex-dominant response.
A positive RNA-processing/SR-factor module, led by Rsrp1 and Srrm-family genes, was the most recurrent transcriptional response to Huwe1 loss.
The Huwe1 signature coupled RNA-processing induction to a mitochondrial/redox and membrane-trafficking upshift in midbrain, hypothalamic, and brainstem responders.
Postnatal Huwe1 perturbation did not recover the expected N-Myc-DLL3/Notch, p53-apoptosis, proteasome-bounce-back, or UPR/ISR transcriptional programs.
Vps35 and Dctn1 were unexpected positive signature neighbors of Huwe1 and converged on selected axon/endomembrane genes.
Ogt, Tnpo3, and Camta1 landed on the negative side of the Huwe1 signature rather than phenocopying it.
The Huwe1 postmitotic signature was not a generic HECT/E3-ligase neurodevelopmental phenotype.

Ica1 CRISPR loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal resting-transcriptome null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups were measured, all 388,023 downstream tests stayed at FDR>=0.250, and the Ica1 feature itself was never BH-significant.
The expected PICK1/AMPAR axis was transcriptionally silent after Ica1 perturbation: Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Gria4, Pick1 and Prkca mRNAs had 0/138 FDR<0.10 rows in the Ica1 surface.
Ica1 loss did not elicit a detectable ER-stress, integrated-stress, lysosomal or autophagy bounce-back program in neuronal nuclei.

Measured AMPAR/PICK1-axis targets failed to form an Ica1-like transcriptional family: Gria1, Gria2, Gria3 and Prkca had near-zero full-surface cosines to Ica1 and only 0-1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene per target except for singleton Gria hits.

Whole-surface similarity did not nominate a credible alternative Ica1 RNA module: the strongest positive target, Tcf7l2, had cosine 0.026, and the strongest biological negative, Tmem126a, had cosine -0.015.

The Ica1 snRNA-seq null should not be interpreted as CNS functional safety: knockout literature places the disease-relevant neuronal phenotype in PICK1 stability, subcellular localization and activity-dependent LTP rather than in basal mRNA abundance.
Icos loss of function was a complete cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional non-responder: every measured group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Global signature comparison placed Icos at the noise floor: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon-score vectors were only +0.033 and -0.018.
The expected activated-T-cell ICOS program--Tfh regulators, cytokines, homing genes, CD3/T-cell receptor neighbors, and ICOS-linked PI3K nodes--was absent from the Icos neuronal DE surface.
Ide perturbation produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of 21 measured neuronal cell groups, even though Ide itself was significantly reduced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

The juvenile neuronal snRNA surface offers no RNA biomarker for IDE inactivation despite IDE being a druggable protease linked to diabetes and Alzheimer’s disease biology.

The closest data-driven Idh3a signature neighbors were essentially non-neighbors, with absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations no larger than 0.050.

Core measured IFNAR-axis perturbations did not phenocopy Ifnar1, showing that the pathway as a whole was quiescent in the matched neuronal DE space.
Unbiased full-surface neighbors of Ifnar1 were shallow and failed restricted-signature validation.
The flat neuronal surface should be read as a basal-context null, not as evidence that IFNAR1 blockade is intrinsically silent in the CNS.
Basal postmitotic neuronal Ifnar2 loss produced no corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any measured cell group.
The canonical IFNAR-JAK/STAT-ISGF3 program and the measured IFNAR-pathway comparators were absent or singleton-flat in matched neurons.
Whole-vector cross-perturbation search found no robust positive or negative Ifnar2 signature neighbor.
The Ifnar2 null refines viral-susceptibility biology to IFN-rich challenge contexts rather than basal juvenile neurons.
Ifngr1 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The represented IFN receptor and IFN transcription-factor relatives also lacked a coherent IFN-stimulated response in the same neuronal groups.
Continuous score-space neighbors of Ifngr1 were extremely weak and failed to define a robust convergent module.
Basal postmitotic Ifngr1 loss did not recapitulate the IFN-gamma-exposure neuronal MHCI/IFN program described in developmental or circuit-stimulation contexts.
Ifngr2 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The related interferon receptor/JAK-STAT perturbations represented in the parquet also failed to generate a shared ISG module.
The pre-literature nearest neighbors of the Ifngr2 nominal vector were weak, unrelated signatures rather than IFN-pathway perturbations.
Juvenile postmitotic Ifngr2 LoF did not reverse or expose the MHC-I program reported after developmental IFN-γ exposure.

The Ift43 disease axis is displaced from a broad juvenile NeuN+ neuronal transcriptome toward ciliary protein trafficking in other stages or lineages.

Cilium-related perturbations represented in the screen converge with Ift88 mainly by being transcriptionally buffered rather than by inducing a shared IFT-B knockout transcriptome.
Canonical Sonic Hedgehog/Gli transcription was not recovered after Ift88 perturbation.
Pre-literature restricted-signature neighbors of Ift88 were all low-cosine and failed to reveal a hidden robust module.

Sparse juvenile neuronal Igf1r transcriptomic silence should not be used as a CNS-safety claim for systemic IGF1R inhibition or for developmental IGF1R dosage disorders.

The neuronal Igsf1 signature did not recover the pituitary TRH/TSH, GH/PRL/FSH, or activin/TGFβ programs expected from organismal IGSF1 deficiency.

Neither the full-universe signature search nor represented cytokine/STAT relatives yielded a convincing Il10ra phenocopy.
The Il10ra surface places IL-10RA disease biology outside healthy postnatal NeuN+ neurons.

The 022 L5 ET CTX Glut response is an isolated Lpcat1 up-regulation event rather than a canonical ERK immediate-early module.

Il1rap produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group.

Represented IL-1R/TIR/NF-kB/MAPK relatives did not reveal an Il1rap-like response.

The basal neuronal null should not be extrapolated to ligand-stimulated anti-IL1RAP pharmacology.

Other immune cytokine receptor targets were likewise mostly inert, indicating a broad receptor-context mismatch rather than an Il21r-specific outlier.

Unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Il2ra neighbor; the largest non-control correlation to Il2ra was only r=0.0408.
The screen refines IL2RA disease and drug biology away from acute neuron-autonomous transcription and toward immune or non-neuronal compartments that were depleted by NeuN+ sorting.
Il2rb CRISPR loss-of-function produced no robust neuronal nuclear transcriptome in any of the 21 recovered cell groups.
The Il2rb null is part of a broader cytokine-receptor/JAK-STAT null module among represented IL-2-family, interferon-receptor, and STAT perturbations.
Il2rb perturbation did not recover the expected STAT/SOCS cytokine-feedback or IL-15/GABA-transmission transcript panels.
The strongest all-universe Il2rb signature neighbors were effectively background correlations rather than biological phenocopies.
Acute Il2rg CRISPR in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered cell groups.
Represented γc-family receptor targets and STAT targets were almost as flat as Il2rg in the same neuronal cell groups.
The full-universe data-driven neighbors of Il2rg were effectively orthogonal and noncanonical, with maximum signed-Wilcoxon cosine only +0.029 and minimum -0.021.

The only Il4ra FDR<0.10 event was Sf3b1 down-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
The measurable IL-4 receptor relative Il2rg and downstream branch gene Irs1 failed to phenocopy Il4ra.
Canonical IL-4/IL-13 STAT6 and alternatively activated macrophage markers were completely absent from the Il4ra neuronal DE surface.
The screen argues against a broad tonic neuron-intrinsic transcriptional liability from IL4RA blockade, but not against activity-, injury-, age-, or immune-compartment IL4RA biology.
Il6ra loss produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic event, Rtn4 down-regulation, confined to 308 CB GABA.
The Rtn4 event was uncoupled from the canonical IL-6R/gp130/JAK-STAT axis in this basal neuronal assay.
Represented Nogo receptor-complex perturbations did not phenocopy Il6ra in 308 CB GABA.
Il6ra had no robust data-driven signature neighbor; even the formal full-score nearest neighbors were nearly orthogonal.
A sparse neuronal Il6ra CRISPR loss should not be read as pharmacologic pan-IL-6R blockade.

The homeostatic neuronal flatness of Il6st does not de-risk systemic or inflammatory GP130 inhibition.

Insr loss of function was transcriptionally silent at FDR<0.10 in every recovered neuronal group: 0 downstream genes in 23 of 23 measured groups despite 2016 perturbed nuclei in aggregate.

The basal postnatal Insr snRNA null should not be read as evidence that brain insulin signaling is irrelevant or that insulin/IGF interventions would be inert.

The NPHP5/CEP290/RPGR/BBSome/IFT comparator panel did not collapse onto a shared Iqcb1-like neuronal module.
B9d1, not Iqcb1, was the only ciliary comparator with a multi-gene FDR signal, and that signal was confined to cerebellar GABA neurons.
Iqcb1 lacked a meaningful empirical score-vector neighbor.
The neuronal null should not be extrapolated to the retina-directed NPHP5 disease mechanism.
Iqsec1 depletion produced a detectable target-transcript hit but no downstream program in the best-engaged neuronal classes.
The screen did not reveal a shared IQSEC-family transcriptional module.
Iqsec1 uncoupled from glutamate-receptor transcriptional responses detected in the same neuronal atlas.
The strongest data-driven Iqsec1 signature neighbors were extremely weak and non-specific.
A flat P16 neuronal snRNA signature should not be read as evidence that IQSEC1 inhibition is synaptically safe.

The only significant CNU-HYa HY MM Glut response was Arfgap1 down-regulation, nominating an Arf-family vesicle-trafficking gene rather than a postsynaptic receptor transcript.
Iqsec2 down-regulated Cux1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the same thalamic Cux1 decrease recurred only after Yy1 and Uba5 among all other perturbations.

The dataset places Isca2 in the buffered branch of mammalian A-type Fe-S biology seen previously in standard mouse neurons, rather than in the severe HeLa-cell ISCA2-depletion state.

Directly measured Fe-S-related targets did not uncover a hidden Isca2-like module: Nfs1 and Abcb7 were flat, Aco2 and Cisd2 had only one isolated downstream hit each, and all four had near-zero correlations to Isca2.

The same screen recovered a mitochondrial ATF4/ISR-like program after Opa1 perturbation, but Isca2 had essentially zero similarity to Opa1 and lacked the Opa1-induced Asns/Ddit3/Chac1/Slc7a5 amino-acid stress signature.

Data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Isca2 were extremely weak: the top overall positive label was Safe_target_81 at r=0.0485, the top positive protein-coding neighbors were P2ry14, Cox4i1 and Map1lc3a with r≈0.032-0.034, and the top negative neighbors Ifngr2, Cckar and Zic3 had r≈-0.019 to -0.021.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the only FDR-significant Isca2 self-transcript decrease, yet still had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
P16 Isl1 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected embryonic forebrain cholinergic and striatonigral programs were uncoupled from acute P16 Isl1 perturbation in broad CNU-MGE and CNU-LGE/LSX GABA groups.
Hypothalamic arcuate neuropeptide markers predicted from Isl1 developmental biology were absent after P16 Isl1 perturbation in both HYa/HY groups.
Neither empirical signature neighbors nor literature-obvious Isl1 pathway comparators produced a robust convergent postnatal signature.
Itga2 loss was transcriptomically silent at FDR<0.10 in every sampled neuronal group.
The expected β1-integrin/focal-adhesion transcriptional module was absent not only for Itga2 but also for represented β1-integrin relatives.
Data-driven Itga2 signature neighbors were effectively orthogonal, with safe targets among the closest positives and Wdr26 the broadest weak inverse.
Normal postmitotic neuronal nuclei did not show broad ITGA2-loss transcriptional toxicity, but this cannot be extrapolated to platelets, vasculature, stroma, or glioblastoma cells.
Itga2b loss of function is globally transcriptionally silent across the recovered P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal atlas.
The null is shared by platelet-lineage and most integrin-family comparators represented in the screen, while Itgb3 and Itgav were absent as β3-complex comparator targets.
The data-driven Itga2b score signature has no meaningful positive or negative neighbor.
This neuronal CRISPR null should not be read as a CNS transcriptional efficacy or safety signal for αIIbβ3 antagonism.
Acute Itga4 LoF produced no FDR-level downstream response in any of 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal groups.
The canonical α4β1/α4β7 adhesion and focal-adhesion transcriptional panel did not move downstream of Itga4 CRISPR.
All-target signature comparison rejected a hidden Itga4-like transcriptional module.
The screen’s negative neuron-autonomous result is consistent with α4-integrin therapies acting through immune-cell trafficking rather than mature-neuron transcription.
Itga6 produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream calls, Pcmt1 up in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Spopl up in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The Itga6 Pcmt1/Spopl hits were not shared by measured integrin or laminin-receptor relatives.
Itga6 lacked a robust unbiased signature neighbor in the model-visible universe.
The postmitotic NeuN+ Itga6 null should not be used as a counterexample to α6-integrin dependence in SVZ or glioblastoma stem-cell niches.
Itga7 loss produced no FDR<0.10 neuronal downstream transcriptome in the 22 cell groups in which it was recovered; the 215 MB Dopa stratum was not tested.

The represented laminin-receptor and adhesion-complex relatives did not reveal a hidden neuronal α7β1-like module: Itgb1, Dag1, Dmd and Actn4 were also FDR-null, while Itga6 gave only two isolated genes.
A data-first all-gene search found no meaningful positive or negative Itga7 signature neighbor; the strongest absolute Pearson score was only 0.0497.
The neuronal flatness should not be used as evidence against Itga7 in BBB, vascular, skeletal-muscle, Schwann-cell or sensory-injury biology.
Itga8 perturbation yielded one corrected downstream event, Gnaz up-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba, with no broader FDR<0.10 program.
Canonical alpha8beta1 ECM, nephronectin-Gdnf, focal-adhesion, and MAPK transcripts were all FDR=1.0 across the 21 Itga8-tested groups.
The direct beta1 partner and represented integrin-family targets were almost completely flat in the same screen, and Itga6's two isolated hits did not overlap Itga8.
Genome-wide score-neighbor correlations for Itga8 were near zero; Wwox was the top positive neighbor and Sec63 the strongest broad negative neighbor, but neither shared the Pvalb Gnaz effect.
Itga9 loss gave a pan-null neuronal snRNA-seq surface: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered cell groups.
The flat Itga9 surface is shared by its direct β1 partner Itgb1 and α4 subfamily comparator Itga4; Itga6 and Itga8 produced only three isolated single-gene effects across all tested groups.
Whole-transcriptome, cross-target signature search found no strong Itga9 neighbor: the best non-safe Pearson correlations were only +0.031 and -0.032.

The Itga9 disease axis is displaced away from NeuN+ neuronal transcription: lymphatic-valve, VCAM/neutrophil, and injury-tenascin programs predicted from the literature were absent after postnatal neuronal LoF.

Itgb1 loss produced a pan-measured FDR-null nuclear transcriptome: 21 recovered neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while the targeted focal-adhesion, immediate-early, NMDAR/PSD, and Rho-family panel was FDR=1.0 throughout.

Represented integrin subunit perturbations mostly phenocopied the Itgb1 null rather than exposing a β1-like transcriptomic module: Itga2, Itga2b, Itga4, Itga7, Itga9, and Itgb2 had no FDR-supported downstream genes, while Itga6 and Itga8 produced only isolated one-gene effects.

The data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Itgb1 collapsed to near-zero residual correlations; top positive residual neighbors reached only r=0.0226 and top negative neighbors only r=-0.0193, and re-querying those targets showed no FDR-level shared module.

Itgb1 did not induce a detectable ER-stress, UPR, or survivor-stress program even though the same analysis detects Hspa5/Hyou1/Chac1-positive ER stress after Sec63 perturbation in matched thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
Itgb2 knockout produced a pan-measured-neuronal null: 22 recovered cell groups each had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.
Represented immune and microglial comparator perturbations C3, Cd14, Cd36, Csf1r, Cx3cr1, Tlr2, and Tlr4 were also FDR-flat in the Itgb2-matched neuronal groups.
The neuronal safety-looking Itgb2 signature should not be interpreted as evidence that CD18/Mac-1 or complement-phagocytosis modulation is silent in the brain.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Itgb2 transcriptional neighbor: the closest positive cosine was Fbxo11 at 0.0456 and the closest negative cosine was Npy5r at -0.0230.
Acute Itm2b loss produced only two isolated downstream FDR hits across 23 neuronal cell groups: P4htm up in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Lrrc24 up in 052 Pvalb Gaba.

The APP/secretase branch of BRI2 biology is uncoupled from nuclear RNA output in this perturbation: Itm2b loss did not change App, secretase, or furin-family transcripts, and App, Psen1, and Adam10 perturbations had near-zero score correlations to Itm2b.

The synaptic-prior genes Dlg4, Syp, Grin1, Grin2b, Gria1, and Gria2 did not phenocopy Itm2b; NMDAR perturbations generated their own cell-type-specific transcriptional signatures, whereas Itm2b remained almost flat in the same snRNA readout.

Genome-wide data-driven neighbor analysis found no meaningful convergent Itm2b module: the best positive non-control neighbor was Fbxo11 at r=0.047 and the best negative neighbor was Wdr26 at r=-0.013.
The postnatal neuronal LoF screen does not model the two axes most likely to matter for ITM2B dementia biology: C-terminal amyloidogenic alleles and microglial BRI2-TREM2 processing.
P16 mosaic Itpr1 loss produced a pan-neuronal downstream-null snRNA-seq surface: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 non-Itpr1 genes at FDR<0.10.

The cerebellar GABA group, the screen's closest Purkinje-containing readout, was also only weakly perturbed transcriptionally: Itpr1 logFC was -0.699 with FDR 0.136 and the strongest downstream gene stopped at FDR 0.103.

A phenotype-first search found no meaningful positive or negative Itpr1 transcriptomic neighbor in the 1772-target score universe; the best cosine was only +0.0321 and the most anti-correlated target was -0.0222.

Itpr1 loss did not phenocopy Atp2a2/SERCA2 loss: Atp2a2 generated a 284-gene UPR/ISR-like response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with Ddit3, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Chac1 and Atf4 up, while matched Itpr1 perturbation had 0 downstream genes there.

Represented mGluR/IP3R pathway comparators were also flat or nearly flat: Grm1, Plcb1, Homer2, Grid2, Grm5, Cacna1a and Ryr3 had no downstream FDR genes, whereas Prkcg, Ppp3ca, Camk2a and Ryr2 each produced only isolated one- to few-gene responses.
Acute postmitotic Ivd loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional zero rather than a mitochondrial, integrated-stress, autophagy, redox, or proteostasis program.

The Ivd null was shared by every represented BCAA/leucine-catabolic or ETF-adjacent comparator tested: Auh, Bckdhb, Bckdk, Dld, and Etfa each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the matched neuronal groups.

The pre-literature whole-surface neighbors of Ivd were noise-level rather than mechanistic: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was Adrb2 at r=0.028678 and the strongest negative was Atp6ap2 at r=-0.013138.

Acute P16 Jakmip1 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq program in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups; only 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut had a near-threshold single-gene hint, Ablim1 at FDR 0.138.
The expected JAKMIP1 RNP, PSD/NMDAR, and GABAB-receptor genes were assayed but did not move as nuclear transcripts after Jakmip1 perturbation.
Jakmip1 was not a transcriptional phenocopy of either empirical neighbors or literature-obvious translation/NMDAR regulators in this assay.
Jund loss was buffered across basal postnatal neurons: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the only responder had one gene.
The residual Jund signature was a single Zkscan2 up-regulation restricted to 308 CB GABA.
Represented AP-1/bZIP relatives and MAPK neighbors did not phenocopy Jund.
Jund had no robust data-driven signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Acute P16 Kalrn loss produced a completely FDR-flat nuclear transcriptome in 22 neuronal cell groups.
Kalrn did not induce transcriptional feedback in the Rac1/PAK/LIMK actin branch or in measured PSD/NMDAR pathway genes.
Kalrn did not phenocopy NMDAR-subunit perturbations: Grin1, Grin2a and Grin2b generated FDR-level signatures in Kalrn-matched groups where Kalrn remained silent.
Kalrn had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor; the strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations were only +0.028 and -0.021.

The absence of ISR, proteostasis, autophagy, redox or synaptic mRNA collapse constrains Kalrn-linked synaptopathy mechanisms toward structural and circuit phenotypes rather than acute cell-autonomous nuclear stress.
Sparse P16 Kat6a loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The literature-nominated Hox and CDKN2A/p16 axes were not recovered after Kat6a perturbation in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.
Kat6a and Kat6b were flat, whereas Brd1 and Crebbp produced small FDR-supported signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Brd1 also responded in 308 CB GABA.
A full-parquet score-neighbor search found only noise-scale Kat6a neighbors and no coherent positive or negative module.
The neuronal Kat6a-only null should not be used as a proxy for the pharmacology or safety of dual catalytic KAT6A/B inhibition.
Kat6b had no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of 22 measured postmitotic neuronal groups; 215 MB Dopa had no Kat6b rows and was not tested.
The represented KAT6 paralog Kat6a converged with Kat6b on a single-perturbation null rather than producing a paralog-specific neuronal DE program.
The unbiased whole-surface neighbor scan found no meaningful Kat6b-like or anti-Kat6b-like perturbation.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was able to report acute chromatin-factor signatures from Crebbp and Kmt2a while remaining completely flat for Kat6b.

The Kat6b null does not falsify KAT6B neurodevelopmental disease genetics because the CRISPR perturbation tests postnatal loss-of-function, not the dominant C-terminal truncation alleles that often underlie human GPS/SBBYSS.
The Kat6a/Kat6b single-gene neuronal flatness should not be read as a safety surrogate for dual KAT6A/B inhibitors.
Katnip loss produced a pan-measured transcriptional null in postnatal NeuN+ neuronal nuclei: 0 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups.
The Dictyostelium Katnip lysosome-delivery/autophagy expectation was not recovered as a neuronal FDR-level stress program.
Represented ciliary or KIAA0556-associated comparators Adgrg1, Cep290, and Cplane1 were also downstream-null, whereas Ift88 had only a one-gene MB Glut response not shared by Katnip.
A full-universe signed-Wilcoxon search found no informative Katnip signature neighbor.

Hippocampal-containing glutamatergic groups remained Katnip-null or only weak, consistent with the germline mouse report that CA1 and dentate-gyrus primary-cilium number and distribution looked grossly normal.
Kbtbd7 CRISPR targeting produced a pan-measured neuronal null: none of the 21 recovered cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The canonical KBTBD6/7-TIAM1-RAC1 branch was orthogonal to Kbtbd7 at the snRNA level.
The p97/VCP-KBTBD7-VANGL ERAD/Wnt-PCP axis was not recovered as a Kbtbd7-dependent neuronal transcriptome.
Unbiased score-vector neighbors were rejected: even the strongest Kbtbd7 signature neighbors had correlations near zero and did not share an FDR-significant Kbtbd7 gene set.
Cancer, pituitary, and microglial KBTBD7 substrate programs did not appear as neuron-intrinsic mRNA toxicity programs.
Acute Kcna1 loss did not produce a robust cell-autonomous snRNA-seq signature in any recovered neuronal group.

Represented Kv1/LGI1-complex comparators were also transcriptomically quiet: Kcna2, Kcnab2, Adam22, and Dlg4 produced zero or one downstream FDR gene per entire surface rather than a shared Kv1-like expression module.
The Kcna1 null is not a generic inability of the screen to detect stress or proteostasis biology: the least-similar neighbors Psmc1 and Psmb4 were broad multi-thousand-gene responders.

Other excitability genes produced only small, sharply cell-type-restricted transcriptional signatures, with Kcnb1 in L4-5 IT neurons as the clearest activity-gene responder, while Kcna1 remained flat in the same groups.
No durable Kcna1 snRNA-seq biomarker accompanied postnatal CRISPR loss of function.
Kcna2 produced exactly one robust downstream gene in the whole measured surface: Man1a2 was up in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
The expected chronic hyperexcitability and stress-transcription readouts were absent after Kcna2 loss-of-function.
Direct Kv1 relatives Kcna1 and Kcnab2 did not phenocopy Kcna2 at the transcriptome level.
Other epilepsy ion-channel perturbations were sparse and idiosyncratic rather than a common Kcna2-like channelopathy module.
Unbiased signature matching found no meaningful convergent neighbor for Kcna2.

Kcnab2 perturbation produced no downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups despite uniformly negative self-transcript shifts and significant Kcnab2 RNA depletion in five groups.
Kcnab2 loss did not induce an activity-regulated Bdnf/Vgf/Scg2 or Fos/Junb/Egr/Npas4/Arc program in any recovered group.
No data-driven gene perturbation converged strongly with Kcnab2; the largest non-control signed-score correlation was only 0.038 and the largest anticorrelation was -0.028.

Kv1 alpha-subunit perturbations Kcna1 and Kcna2 were as transcriptionally flat as Kcnab2, whereas broader potassium-channelopathy genes Kcnb1 and Kcnq2 produced only sparse, non-overlapping downstream hits.
Kcnb1 loss of function elicited a compact, all-up activity/neuropeptide module only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The L4-5 Kcnb1 response was chronic and buffered rather than a broad acute-IEG, UPR/ISR, autophagy, or proteasome response.
The Kv2 paralog Kcnb2 did not phenocopy Kcnb1 anywhere in the matched measured surface.
Kcnq2 and Gabrg2, but not Scn2a or Gabra1, converged on the Kcnb1 Bdnf output in L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
NMDA receptor subunits split by polarity: Grin2a converged with Kcnb1 on Nptx2/Scg2 up-regulation, whereas Grin2b opposed the Kcnb1 module.
Acute Kcnb2 CRISPR loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Kcnb2 did not phenocopy Kcnb1 in L4-5 intratelencephalic neurons: Kcnb1 induced Bdnf/Vgf/Scg2/Nptx2, whereas matched Kcnb2 did not move those genes.
The Kv2 structural module was not transcriptionally remodeled: Amigo1 and Kcnb1 transcripts stayed FDR-flat in every Kcnb2-measured group.
A full-universe search found no meaningful positive or negative Kcnb2 signature neighbor.
The postmitotic LoF signature does not provide a cell-autonomous transcriptomic model of human monoallelic KCNB2 disease.

Acute Kcnc1 CRISPR produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups, including Pvalb Gaba and MB/P/MY GABA groups with significant self-transcript decreases.

The flat Kcnc1 surface is shared by its Kv3 paralogs in this screen: Kcnc3 had zero downstream DE genes and Kcnc2 had only one isolated DE gene despite strong Pvalb self-transcript depletion for both comparators.
Kcnc1 loss did not induce an activity-dependent, GABAergic, compensatory ion-channel, ISR, or ER-stress transcriptional module at FDR<0.10.
Kcnc1 did not belong to a robust data-driven transcriptional module: its top signed-score neighbors across all targets had absolute correlations below 0.05.
The juvenile mosaic LoF assay is a poor phenocopy of the dominant-negative and allele-specific KCNC1 channelopathies despite targeting the same gene.
Kcnc1 did not phenocopy other represented epilepsy-channel perturbations, which were either similarly sparse or cell-type-restricted rather than convergent with Kcnc1.
Acute postnatal Kcnc2 CRISPR LoF generated a near-pan-null downstream snRNA-seq surface, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 22 measured cell groups.
Zyx was the only FDR<0.10 downstream Kcnc2 hit, up-regulated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Represented Kv3 paralogs Kcnc1 and Kcnc3 converged with Kcnc2 on absence of downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic responses.
All-gene Kcnc2 signature neighbors were mathematically closest at correlations near zero, with Fbxo11 as the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 as the top negative neighbor.
The LoF screen is allele-direction limited for KCNC2 channelopathy.

Kcnc3 loss was pan-transcriptomically buffered: every recovered neuronal group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 even though the Kcnc3 row was depleted in 22 of 23 groups and significantly depleted in 8 groups.
The SCA13 TBK1-Hax1-Cd63/multivesicular-body axis was not transcriptionally induced by wild-type Kcnc3 loss in juvenile neurons.

The flat Kcnc3 profile is part of a broader voltage-gated potassium-channel pattern, because Kcnc1, Kcnc2, Kcnd3, Kcna1, Kcna2, Kcnab2, Kcnb1, and Kcnb2 perturbations were themselves null or nearly null in the same snRNA-seq universe.
Kcnc3 had no meaningful score-signature neighbor in the model-visible universe, and the nominal nearest non-Safe targets did not share any robust downstream gene with it.
Postnatal sparse Kcnd3 loss produced a high-confidence pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 23 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Kcnd3 perturbation did not recruit either an activity-dependent immediate-early program or transcriptional feedback on canonical Kv4 subunits.
Dpp6, the only canonical Kv4 auxiliary target represented in the parquet, phenocopied Kcnd3 at the level of transcriptional silence, not a shared DE module.

The Kcnd3 null is not a generic failure to detect ion-channel perturbations: Cacna1g and Kcnb1 produced small, cell-type-restricted DE signatures in matched thalamic and L4/5 IT cells where Kcnd3 stayed flat.
Genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Kcnd3 convergence or opposition: the strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were only +0.0338 and -0.0220.
Kcnh1 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal zero: 22 recovered cell groups and 371796 non-self DE tests yielded no downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The Kcnh1 CRISPR phenotype is a loss-of-function depletion model, not a Temple-Baraitser/Zimmermann-Laband gain-of-function allele model.
The embryo/cycling-cell Kcnh1 cilium and cell-cycle program was not recovered in NeuN-positive postmitotic neurons.
Kcnh1 did not converge with the measured Kcnh5 paralog, shared calmodulin regulators, or KCNH1-adjacent dysmorphology genes by FDR-level overlap.
Nominal Kcnh1 nearest-neighbor structure was weak and non-reproducible at the FDR level.
The screen could recover transcription from other excitability genes in Kcnh1-matched cell groups, arguing against a blanket ion-channel blind spot.
Sparse postnatal Kcnh5 CRISPR produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
The CRISPR LoF did not recover a sustained immediate-early/activity program, arguing that KCNH5 clinical missense disease is not well modeled by basal, acute mosaic postmitotic knockout alone.
Kcnh1, the only other assayed Kcnh-family paralog, shared the Kcnh5 null rather than revealing an EAG-family transcriptional module.
Ion-channel transcriptional secondary responses were detectable in the same parquet: Kcnb1 and Kcnq2 induced a small Bdnf/Vgf-like L4/5 IT program where Kcnh5 stayed flat.
Kcnh5 had no interpretable whole-transcriptome neighbor: the strongest data-driven Pearson score correlations were only about four percent.
Kcnj6 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
Directly measured Gi/o receptor inputs to GIRK signaling were also transcriptomically flat or limited to one isolated FDR<0.10 gene.
Postnatal CRISPR loss of Kcnj6 did not phenocopy the gain-of-function, pore-selectivity, or trisomy mechanisms that dominate KCNJ6 disease literature.
The data-driven Kcnj6 signature neighbors were numerically near zero and did not define a reproducible shared DE module.
The screen does not de-risk GIRK2 channel modulation; it shows only that sparse Kcnj6 loss failed to launch a cell-autonomous RNA program.
Kcnma1 loss was a pan-measured downstream transcriptional null in this P16 sparse neuronal loss-of-function assay.
The disease-relevant cerebellar GABA compartment was also transcriptionally quiet after Kcnma1 perturbation.
Kcnma1 loss did not secondarily engage detectable immediate-early, activity-regulated, or generic stress genes.
Represented KCa, Slo-family, and M-current channel relatives did not phenocopy a Kcnma1 transcriptional module.
Kcnma1 had no meaningful data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbor despite direct comparison against every represented target.
Kcnma1 loss lacks a stable snRNA biomarker in this assay, warning against using baseline transcript rescue as the main potency readout for BK-channel therapies.
Kcnn2 had exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream hit, Kctd5 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
Kctd5 is an exploratory candidate reporter of a GPCR/Gbeta-gamma feedback state downstream of Kcnn2 loss in cerebellar GABAergic neurons.
The pre-literature data-driven Kcnn2 neighbor search yielded only nominal Kctd5 neighbors that were rejected as FDR-level convergences.
Kcnn3 and the three calmodulin perturbations did not phenocopy the Kcnn2 cerebellar Kctd5 response.
NMDAR and CK2-beta perturbations produced robust signatures in matched cell groups where Kcnn2 stayed weak.
Basal snRNA-seq is a poor primary biomarker for postnatal Kcnn2 loss despite strong electrophysiological and movement-disorder priors.
Kcnn3 was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional non-responder: all 23 assayed cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Kcnn3 loss did not secondarily recruit a nuclear activity-response program.
NMDAR and Ca2+-channel perturbations were transcriptionally stronger than Kcnn3 despite functional coupling of SK channels to Ca2+ sources.
The expected SK-family and calmodulin comparators did not phenocopy Kcnn3.
A model-wide, phenotype-first signature search found no meaningful Kcnn3 neighbor or anti-neighbor.
The Kcnn3 snRNA null should not be used to deprioritize KCa2/SK3 pharmacology.
Acute Kcnq1 loss of function was a pan-neuronal FDR-level null: every one of the 23 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Kcnq1 had no informative transcriptomic neighbor in the model-visible universe; the maximum positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.035 and the strongest negative correlation was only r=-0.021.

The represented Kv7 paralogs Kcnq2 and Kcnq3 did not phenocopy Kcnq1: Kcnq1-Kcnq2 and Kcnq1-Kcnq3 score correlations were r=0.003 and r=0.002, while Kcnq2/Kcnq3 produced only five total downstream FDR<0.10 genes in restricted cell groups.
Kcnq1 loss did not induce a detectable excitability-coupled immediate-early or Kv7/KCNE compensatory transcriptional program.

Kcnq2 produced an extremely sparse glutamatergic-only downstream surface: three non-self genes at FDR<0.10 across three of 23 measured classes, contrasted with Kcnq2 self-transcript reduction at FDR<0.10 in 14 classes.
Layer 4/5 IT cortical neurons mounted a single Bdnf-up response to Kcnq2 loss, and Bdnf was the only shared FDR<0.10 Kcnq2 feature recovered after Kcnb1 and Gabrg2 perturbation in the same class.
In L2/3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic neurons Kcnq2 uniquely down-regulated Rogdi across the model-visible perturbation universe.
The TH Prkcd/Grin2c response was a single Agap2 increase that converged with Atp1a3, Rnpc3, Sin3a, Zbtb7a and Ctnnb1 but was inverted after Psmb4, Psmc1, Tpr, Elp1 and Elp2 perturbation.
The expected Kv7 paralog Kcnq3 did not phenocopy Kcnq2 in the three Kcnq2-responding classes and produced only two isolated downstream genes across 22 recovered classes.
Psmb4 was a mixed data-driven neighbor, sharing Bdnf up-regulation with Kcnq2 in L4/5 IT cells but driving Agap2 down in TH Prkcd/Grin2c while Kcnq2 drove Agap2 up.

Kcnq3 loss produced almost no resting transcriptional response across the measured neuronal surface: only two downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-group calls, no robust immediate-early genes, no ISR/UPR or heat-shock module, and no voltage-gated channel compensation.
direction_pattern: two isolated up-regulated outliers with otherwise absent activity, stress, and channel-compensation signatures

Kv7.3 engagement is unlikely to yield a convenient resting snRNA pharmacodynamic signature in sparse postmitotic neurons.

Closest Na+/Ca2+-activated K+ channel relatives were also almost completely transcriptome-flat in the Kcnt1-matched groups.
Slack-associated FMRP, Cyfip, and Phactr1 biology did not become a shared nuclear RNA signature.
The Kcnt1 CRISPR null did not reproduce a KCNT1 gain-of-function epilepsy-like transcriptional state.
The flat wild-type Kcnt1 LoF signature argues that Kcnt1-reduction therapy is a network modifier, not a constitutive WT cell-state program.
Residualized whole-transcriptome neighbor analysis found no meaningful positive or negative Kcnt1 signature neighbor.
Kcnt2 is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null: all 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Kcnt2 loss did not recover a chronic neuronal activity or channel-compensation mRNA program.
A whole-universe score-vector search found no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor of Kcnt2.
The expected Slack/Kcnt1 paralog also sits in the KNa transcriptomic null class rather than exposing a shared Kcnt2-like program.
Kcnt2 is flatter than several represented intrinsic-excitability channel perturbations that did produce FDR<0.10 signatures in the same Wilcoxon universe.
A juvenile CRISPR loss-of-function null does not negate KCNT2 developmental epileptic encephalopathy genetics.
Kctd16 had no robust downstream nuclear transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal class.
The Kctd16 null extends across matched GABAB/Kir3 pathway perturbations rather than selectively sparing Kctd16.
Kctd16 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the 1,773-target analysis universe.
An snRNA transcriptional marker is unlikely to be a sensitive readout of partial KCTD16/GABAB auxiliary modulation.
Kctd1 generated a tiny, cell-type-restricted neuronal DE surface: three groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene and twenty groups were null or weak.
Resp18 was up-regulated after Kctd1 perturbation in two independent responder groups, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Cluap1 was selectively down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Kctd1 did not induce a Gli/Ptch Hedgehog response.
The L2/3 IT cortical response consisted of isolated Tnnc1 up-regulation.
Kctd1 did not phenocopy strong core Wnt perturbations, especially Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Represented KCTD-family perturbations Kctd8 and Kctd16 did not phenocopy Kctd1; the literature-obvious partner Kctd15 was not represented.
Phenotype-first nearest-neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Kctd1 phenocopy across the model-visible perturbation universe.
The only Kctd8 FDR-level downstream response was Rpgr up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Postnatal sparse Kctd8 loss was broadly buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level.
Kctd8 did not transcriptionally phenocopy the measured GABAB-complex relatives Kctd16, Gabbr1, Gabbr2, or Kcnj6.
The unbiased whole-transcriptome Kctd8 signature had no interpretable positive or negative neighbor in the 1773-target screen universe.
Kctd8 transcriptomic flatness should not be read as pharmacological inertness of KCTD/GABAB interfaces.
Kdm4b loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The two hippocampal glutamatergic groups also lacked FDR-level Kdm4b responses, refining the published CA1 spine and developmental-delay phenotype away from an acute P16 cell-autonomous mRNA program.
The represented KDM4 paralog Kdm4c was as flat as Kdm4b, with zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes across 21 measured cell groups.
Kdm4b lacked a strong cross-perturbation neighbor: the best all-gene positive and negative score correlations were only +0.0307 and -0.0300.
Acute postnatal Kdm4c loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of the 21 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The neural-stem-cell gliogenic and proliferative outputs previously linked to KDM4C were absent from Kdm4c-perturbed NeuN+ neurons.
The represented KDM4 paralog Kdm4b also lacked an FDR-level neuronal output and did not form a signed score-vector neighbor of Kdm4c.
The Kdm4c null is selective: other chromatin perturbations, including Setdb1, Ehmt1, Kdm5c, and Sin3a, generated FDR-level neuronal signatures in the same analysis universe.
Unsupervised comparison across 1,772 other perturbations found no meaningful Kdm4c signature neighbor.
Acute postnatal Kdm5b loss was FDR-null across every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class.
Kdm5c, not Kdm5b, produced a small thalamic/hypothalamic KDM5-family signature.
H3K4 writer perturbations were readily detectable where the Kdm5b eraser perturbation was silent.
Kdm5b had no convincing data-driven transcriptomic neighbor.
The neuronal null should not be read as evidence that KDM5B inhibition is globally inert in the brain.

Kdm5c produced a narrowly restricted response: 18 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a single Prrt1 call in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, while 20 measured groups had 0 robust downstream genes and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.

The Kdm5c 151 signature was dominated by up-regulated, lineage-atypical or cryptic-like genes such as Ptgds, Capn3, Col9a3, Catsperz, Spag5, Hexim2, Usp11, and Zmynd8, rather than Bdnf/Scn2a/Syn1 or WNT targets.

Zmynd8 was the top positive Kdm5c signature neighbor and recapitulated 13 same-direction Kdm5c downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Ptgds, Capn3, Msra, Spag5, Dusp27, Kcnk4, Zfp532, Medag, Hexim2, Man2a2, Usp11, Ank1, and Catsperz.

Kdm5b, Rest, Kmt2a, and Kmt2c failed to phenocopy the Kdm5c response: Kdm5b and Rest were flat, Kmt2c was nearly flat, and Kmt2a produced a different 151 signature with no exact Kdm5c FDR<0.10 overlap.
Bdnf, Scn2a, Syn1, WNT effectors, and ribosomal/mitochondrial modules were absent from the Kdm5c FDR<0.10 surface across all 22 measured neuronal groups.
Setd1a and Sin3a produced broad chromatin-regulator responses in the same analysis universe, whereas Kdm5c was sparse and non-convergent.
Acute postnatal Kdm6b loss was FDR-null in every recovered neuronal group.
The Kdm6b null is selective relative to other chromatin regulators that responded in the same thalamic group.
Known KDM6B-responsive inflammatory, activity-regulated, SVZ-neurogenic, and cerebellar-granule maturation marker sets were not recovered.
Kdm6b has no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Kdr loss produced an almost completely flat postnatal neuronal DE surface: 1 downstream FDR<0.10 event in 22 recovered neuronal cell groups and no canonical VEGF/endothelial transcriptional program.
The only bona fide Kdr downstream transcript was Clasp1 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Measured VEGF/Sema3E relatives and downstream nodes did not phenocopy Kdr in matched neuronal groups.
The pre-literature all-target neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Kdr signature neighbor.
The Kdr neuronal null should not be read as evidence that VEGFR blockade lacks brain-relevant vascular consequences.

Kif11 loss of function at P16 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered NeuN-positive brain neuron class, shifting the screen-compatible liability away from specified postmitotic neurons and toward earlier mitotic progenitors or unsampled KIF11-dependent lineages.
The screen did not convert known postmitotic KIF11 axon, growth-cone, dendrite, or synaptic microtubule phenotypes into a chronic cell-body snRNA-seq program.
Kif11 had no meaningful positive or negative global signature neighbor in the screen-wide target space.
Screened kinesin-superfamily relatives and Kifbp failed to phenocopy Kif11, and several showed significant self-transcript depletion where Kif11 did not.

The flat Kif11 neuron surface is reassuring only for postmitotic neuronal transcriptional toxicity and does not de-risk developmental, retinal, lymphatic, or proliferative-cell liabilities of KIF11 inhibition.
Kif1a loss induced a small but coherent sterol/cholesterol-biosynthesis rebound in three responder classes.

Exact corrected Kif1a coordinates recur after Dctn1, Tsc2, Rab7, Mib1 and Ufc1 perturbation, putting the Kif1a response closer to organelle-trafficking and lysosome/mTOR stress than to other kinesin motors.
Srebf2 loss inverted the MB P MY GABA Kif1a sterol pair, whereas represented Srebf1 and Hmgcr perturbations did not reproduce Kif1a.
Acute postnatal Kif1a LoF did not cause a pan-neuronal synaptic-vesicle or stress transcriptome despite reproducible self-transcript depletion in several null classes.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut responder was a distinct mixed Dusp1/Tanc2/Aifm3/Snhg11 state rather than the sterol rebound seen in 110 and 191.
Literature-obvious kinesin, Rab3 and exocytosis perturbations were measured but rejected as Kif1a phenocopies.
Kif1b produced a single robust downstream RNA response, Snap25 down-regulation, selectively in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Pvalb Kif1b response was Snap25-restricted rather than a pan-synaptic-vesicle or pan-SNARE transcriptional collapse.
Atxn10 and Sin3a, but not measured kinesin relatives, converged with Kif1b on Pvalb Snap25 down-regulation.
Kif1b lacks a strong whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in this perturbation universe.
Kif1b loss did not elicit a robust central-neuron apoptosis, mitochondrial-stress, ISR/UPR, lysosomal, or proteostasis RNA program.
Kif21a had a single downstream FDR<0.10 event, Cc2d1b up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The Kif21a RNA response did not contain the expected KANK, NCKX2, tubulin, end-binding, or guidance transcriptional program.
Dctn1 and Tuba1a made strong cytoskeletal-associated transcriptional signatures where Kif21a stayed nearly flat.
Represented kinesin, end-binding, dynactin, tubulin, and guidance comparators did not phenocopy Kif21a.
The top data-driven Kif21a neighbors were only tiny full-rank correlations.
Cc2d1b is an exploratory marker of the isolated 066 Kif21a response and was not accompanied by Htr1a derepression.
Kif2a was a pan-null nuclear-RNA perturbation in the measured P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen: none of 15 recovered cell groups contained a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Kif2a did not phenocopy the Tuba1a tubulin-paralog response even though both sit in the neuronal microtubule disease space.
The unbiased Kif2a neighbor search returned safe-target-like, nearly zero cosine scores rather than a coherent kinesin or tubulin neighbor.
The hippocampal/DG-containing Kif2a groups were transcriptionally flat despite the established postnatal dentate requirement for KIF2A.
Kif3b CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 21 recovered cell groups.
Represented IFT, dynein-2, BBSome, and transition-zone perturbations were also transcriptionally buffered in Kif3b-matched groups, with each comparator yielding zero or one FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
The unbiased Kif3b signature neighbors were all near-zero cosine matches, and the nearest positive and negative hits did not define a ciliary or neuronal-transport module.

The Kif3b null does not phenocopy photoreceptor KIF3B ciliopathy or NMDAR-transport phenotypes because those phenotypes are retinal, allelic, developmental, or protein-localization endpoints displaced from NeuN+ brain snRNA.
Hedgehog, neuronal ciliary GPCR/cAMP, and synaptic cargo candidate mRNAs were all uncoupled from Kif3b CRISPR at FDR<0.10.
Acute Kif5a CRISPR produced a self-transcript drop in four subcortical neuronal groups but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes anywhere.
Expected neurofilament, SFPQ, ISR, mitochondrial-stress, and lysosomal/autophagy transcripts were not induced or repressed after Kif5a perturbation.
A whole-universe residual signature search found no meaningful Kif5a neighbor.
Represented kinesin-pathway targets, including the neuronal paralog Kif5c and Kif5-associated genes Klc1, Klc2, Kif1a, Kif1b, Kifbp, Rhot1, and Trak1, did not phenocopy a hidden Kif5a-like module.
The flat Kif5a surface is not a universal limitation of sparse neuronal CRISPR: Dctn1 and Tardbp produced hundreds of downstream genes in overlapping groups.
The loss-of-function screen should not be read as a model of ALS-associated KIF5A ΔExon27 motor toxicity.
Kif5c produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 recovered neuronal cell groups despite measurable Kif5c self-transcript changes.
Measured kinesin-1 heavy-chain, light-chain, and MIRO/TRAK adaptor perturbations were null or sparse and did not form a Kif5c-like snRNA-seq module.
The absence of DE in cortical excitatory neurons indicates that P16 Kif5c LoF does not recreate an early cortical-malformation transcriptional program.
The top data-driven Kif5c neighbors had only near-zero signed-score cosines and no meaningful shared FDR module.
Kifbp perturbation after P16 produced a very small snRNA-seq response: only 4 non-target genes were significant across 23 neuronal cell groups despite negative Kifbp self-logFCs in every group.
L5-6 IT glutamatergic neurons selectively up-regulated Exosc10 and Plekhm2 after Kifbp perturbation.
CTX-CGE GABA neurons showed a single significant RNA-binding/splicing marker, Dazap1, up after Kifbp perturbation.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells down-regulated Srebf2 after Kifbp loss, whereas Dctn1 perturbation up-regulated Srebf2 in the same group.
direction_pattern: Srebf2 down with Kifbp, up with Dctn1

canonical_summary: Represented direct or pathway-adjacent Kifbp comparators did not phenocopy the Kifbp responder genes.

All-transcriptome neighbor ranking put Ncoa1 and Six5 nearest to Kifbp but they were rejected by the FDR signature, while Psmb4 and Psmc1 occupied the least-similar full-coverage tail and produced thousands of DE genes absent from Kifbp.
direction_pattern: positive-neighbor signatures rejected; negative-tail signatures broad

canonical_summary: Kiss1r loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream differential expression in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Kiss1r were essentially uncorrelated, with top Pearson score correlations of +0.028 for Oprm1 and -0.016 for Fbxo11.
Kiss1r did not phenocopy represented PLC/Ca2+/PKC/MAPK pathway perturbations: Plcb1, Itpr1, Prkca, and Mapk1 were flat and Camk2a was only sparsely active.

HPG and hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism comparators also failed to form a shared neuronal DE module with Kiss1r; Tacr3, Gnrhr, Fgfr1, and Chd7 each had only 1-2 significant genes in the 22 matched groups.

The absence of Fos/Egr/Dusp/Gnrh1/Kiss1/Tac2/Pdyn or gonadotropin-marker RNA shifts warns that KISS1R drug responses need ligand, electrophysiological, calcium, or hormone endpoints rather than broad resting snRNA-seq biomarkers.
Kit loss of function was buffered at the whole-transcriptome level: all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
CTX-CGE GABA showed a clear Kit self-transcript decrease but still no corrected downstream gene, separating target-RNA perturbation from a downstream neuronal state change.
Class III receptor relatives and canonical KIT effector perturbations did not converge with Kit in matched neuronal groups.
The data-driven Kit signature had no strong positive or inverse neighbor over the model-visible DE universe.
Kiz loss of function after P16 was transcriptomically silent across the recovered NeuN+ neuronal brain surface.
Kiz did not converge with retinal-dystrophy, ciliary, basal-body, intraflagellar-transport, or Hedgehog pathway targets that were directly represented in the screen.
A data-driven whole-parquet neighbor search found no strong Kiz signature neighbor in either direction.
Klc1 loss produced a very sparse nuclear transcriptomic response: only Pvalb GABAergic neurons and MB/Pons/Medulla GABAergic neurons had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
direction_pattern: Agtpbp1 down in Pvalb; Anapc4 up in MB/Pons/Medulla GABA

canonical_summary: In Pvalb GABAergic neurons, Klc1 loss selectively down-regulated Agtpbp1/CCP1, a tubulin deglutamylase that controls the polyglutamylated microtubule tracks used by neuronal motors.
In MB/Pons/Medulla GABAergic neurons, Klc1 loss selectively up-regulated Anapc4, a core APC/C subunit, without a broader cell-cycle or proteostasis transcriptome.
Klc2, Kif5a, and Kif5c did not phenocopy Klc1 in the two Klc1 responder groups, and robust Klc2 knockdown was downstream-silent.
direction_pattern: Klc1-specific; no shared FDR response in paralog/heavy-chain perturbations

canonical_summary: The acute wild-type Klc1 loss-of-function signature did not recover App, Mapt, or Mapk9/JNK transcriptional programs, and App, Mapt, and Mapk9 perturbations did not converge on Klc1 responders.

An unbiased whole-surface search found no strong transcriptomic neighbor for Klc1; even the top positive and negative score-vector neighbors failed to share Agtpbp1 or Anapc4 in matched responder groups.
Klc2 produced a dataset-wide null downstream transcriptional surface across all 22 recovered neuronal groups.
The Klc2 CRISPR-loss surface does not phenocopy KLC2-overexpression SPOAN biology.
Kinesin-1 complex relatives Klc1, Kif5a, and Kif5c also lacked a broad matched-cell transcriptional response.
The top global Klc2 signature neighbors were statistically near zero and were rejected as biological convergence or divergence.
Long-axon and HSP-pathway comparators were not more Klc2-like than other flat targets.
Postnatal Klf11 loss produced a pan-neuronal FDR-level zero: every one of the 23 assayed neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical KLF11-linked MAO, TGF-beta/Smad, dopamine-receptor, apoptosis, and glucocorticoid transcripts were all FDR-flat after Klf11 perturbation.
Klf11 did not reproduce the broad Sin3a chromatin-corepressor phenotype even though KLF11 can recruit mSin3A biochemically.
Represented KLF-family targets did not phenocopy Klf11.
The unbiased Klf11 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Klf12 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal group.
Canonical and context-linked KLF12 output genes were not de-repressed.
Ctbp1, Klf7, Klf9, and Klf13 could generate small FDR-supported thalamic signatures where Klf12 remained flat.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Klf12 module.
Klf13 produced exactly one robust downstream edge, Nrbp2 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 21 groups were strict nulls and one was weak.
Klf13 loss did not recover the expected cAMP/axon-growth transcriptome in any measured neuronal class.
Measured group-3 KLF paralogs did not phenocopy Klf13: Klf9 had a small thalamic-biased response, whereas Klf11 had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
Sin3a and Phf12 perturbations shared Klf13's Nrbp2-up edge in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Ctnnb1 and Tnpo3 were the strongest opposite-sign data-driven neighbors of the Klf13 Nrbp2 edge in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons.
Acute single Klf13 loss is insufficient to induce a durable pro-cAMP axon-growth transcriptional state in uninjured P16-perturbed neurons.
Acute Klf1 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected KLF1 erythroid effector cassette was absent, including no changes in globin, heme, membrane, BCL11A, Zbtb7a/LRF, Gata1, Tal1, or Epor-pathway readouts under Klf1 perturbation.
Neuronal KLF-family activity is paralog-specific: Klf7 and Klf9 gave small thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c signatures, whereas Klf1, Klf11, and Klf12 were FDR-flat and Klf13 had only one hit.

Brain Zbtb7a was strongly active without Klf1: Zbtb7a perturbation generated 2646 FDR<0.10 downstream genes, while Klf1 did not regulate Zbtb7a or Bcl11a and Bcl11a/Gata1/Epor perturbations did not converge with Klf1.
The data-driven Klf1 signature had no robust convergent module: its strongest global score-vector neighbors had absolute cosine below 0.046 and included safe-target controls.
Klf7 loss produced a real downstream transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 8 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and 21 other measured cell groups at zero.
The Klf7 thalamic signature is dominated by down-regulation of cytoskeletal and membrane-scaffold genes.
The responding Klf7 thalamic group did not activate or repress the expected Cdkn1a/Rac3/Trk/Gap43 regeneration and migration program.
Uba5, Elp1, Gfpt1, and Atp2a2 converged with the Klf7 eight-gene thalamic signature, whereas Zbtb7a reversed most of it.
Klf9 and Klf13, represented KLF-family axon-growth repressors, did not phenocopy Klf7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Postmitotic P16 Klf7 loss did not recreate KLF7 autism or cortical-migration biology in sampled cortical glutamatergic neurons.

Klf9 loss produced a robust downstream transcriptomic response in only 2 of 22 measured neuronal groups: a 19-gene mostly upregulated signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a single L1cam hit in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response is dominated by de-repression of a sparse neuronal morphogenesis/cyclic-nucleotide-adjacent module, not by the core cAMP genes nominated from KLF9/KLF13 in vitro work.
L1cam is a lone cortical FDR hit, increased in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut after Klf9 perturbation.
Klf9 converges with Sin3a, Zbtb7a, and Smarcc2 on the 151 module, with Sin3a sharing 13 exact Klf9 coordinates in the same direction at FDR<0.10 and Zbtb7a ranking first by restricted cosine.
Klf13 and the other represented KLF-family perturbations do not phenocopy Klf9 despite KLF9/KLF13 paralogy and published functional overlap.
Acute loss of Thra, Thrb, Nr3c1, or Nfe2l2 did not reproduce the Klf9 005/151 response, and Klf9 loss did not move the predicted cAMP, redox, or myelin target genes at FDR<0.10.
U2af2, Gfpt1, and Tnpo3 are robust anti-neighbors that invert multiple Klf9-induced genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Klhl20 produced a single FDR<0.10 actin-associated hit, Nebl down-regulation, only in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Klhl20 up-regulated the GARP/EARP subunit Vps52 as the sole robust hit in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The canonical KLHL20 Rho/neurite, Coro7/trafficking, DAPK-PML/interferon, and ULK1-VPS34-BECN1 autophagy-termination programs were transcriptionally absent.
Measurable autophagy/Rho/BTB relatives did not phenocopy Klhl20 in the two responder groups.
Whole-surface data-driven neighbors of Klhl20 were essentially flat, with no non-safe target exceeding |r|=0.040 by all-gene Wilcoxon-score correlation.
The quiet sparse CRISPR-LoF surface supports a distinction between postnatal Klhl20 loss of function and human Kelch-domain KLHL20 missense neurodevelopmental disease.

Acute Klhl7 loss of function produced no reproducible downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups. The Klhl7 transcript moved downward in every recovered group, but never below FDR<0.10, matching the expected weak mRNA self-drop behavior of this CRISPR-indel assay rather than proving failed perturbation.
The only KLHL-family comparator represented as a target, Klhl20, was also almost flat in the matched panel and did not share a downstream FDR<0.10 gene with Klhl7.

An unbiased residual-logFC neighbor search found no strong positive or negative signature partner for Klhl7; the top residual cosines lay between -0.022 and +0.022 and involved only subthreshold or nearly flat signatures.

Postnatal mosaic Kmt2a loss produced a sparse, glutamatergic-biased response: only 6 of 22 measured cell groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and 25 of 30 downstream genes were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kmt2a perturbation preferentially down-regulated a neuronal identity and connectivity program including Nr2f1, Pcdh7, Lhx9, Pcdh10, Grik2, Camk2d, Map1b, Sox2, and Elavl2.

The Kmt2a thalamic signature included an induced counter-module of extracellular, growth-factor, RNA-processing, ER-redox, and inhibitory-receptor genes: Igfbp5, Tnr, Cx3cl1, Atxn2l, Luc7l, Txndc5, Gabrd, Acsl3, Cry2, Car4, and Slitrk5.

Outside 151, Kmt2a produced only singleton downstream hits: Tcf4 down in L4-5 IT cortex, Ptprk down in L2-3 IT cortex, Aff4 up in MEA/LA/CA1/DG, Nap1l2 up in NP-CT-L6b-OB glutamatergic neurons, and Fnbp1l down in MB Glut.
Kmt2a did not phenocopy the represented H3K4 writer relatives: Setd1a was broad and largely non-overlapping, whereas Kmt2c was almost flat.
The top raw 30-locus Kmt2a signature neighbors and anti-neighbors were rejected because they did not share FDR-significant Kmt2a loci.
Kmt2c has a one-gene cortical responder: Prnp is down-regulated in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and no other downstream gene reaches FDR<0.10 anywhere in the Kmt2c surface.
Acute P16 Kmt2c loss is broadly buffered at the mature-neuron transcriptome: 15 of 16 measured groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the remaining group had only Prnp.
Kmt2c lacks a meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the model-visible universe.
Available H3K4/enhancer and chromatin-NDD relatives do not phenocopy Kmt2c in matched neurons.
The Kmt2c P16 snRNA-seq null does not recover the LSD1-inhibitor-normalizable disease transcriptome described in constitutive Kmt2c haploinsufficiency.

Acute Kpna3 loss produced a near-null neuronal transcriptome: 20 of 21 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the only corrected event was a single Txnl4a up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The only corrected Kpna3-responsive transcript, Txnl4a, was up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, nominating an isolated spliceosomal U5 snRNP marker rather than a full splicing program.

Kpna3 did not phenocopy represented nuclear-transport perturbations: Ranbp2 and Tnpo3 generated tens to hundreds of DE genes in matched neuronal groups, whereas Kpna3 was flat in the same groups and shared no Txnl4a response.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful recurrent Kpna3 module: the strongest global positive cosine neighbor was Reg1 at 0.0279 and the strongest negative neighbor was Fbxo11 at -0.0180.
The Kpna3 screen did not recover the expected NPAT/replication-dependent histone, NF-kappaB inflammatory, or reward-immediate-early transcriptional programs in any measured neuronal group.
Acute P16 Kras loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any of the 20 recovered neuronal groups.
Kras did not reproduce a RAF/MEK thalamic module that was detectable after Braf or Map2k1 perturbation.
Expected ERK-feedback, immediate-early and oncogenic-neuronal S100 programs were not recovered after Kras loss.
All-target signature searches found only near-zero Kras neighbors.
Acute Kremen1 loss of function was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Kremen1 did not phenocopy Wnt core perturbations: Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and weakly Lrp6/Gsk3b drove thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signatures, whereas Kremen1 had zero FDR<0.10 genes in the same high-recovery class.
A genome-wide signed-score neighbor search did not nominate any meaningful convergent or divergent Kremen1 program.
The ectodermal-dysplasia/tooth-agenesis axis did not project onto juvenile NeuN+ neurons: both Kremen1 and the represented disease-family target Eda were pan-neuronal nulls.
Healthy P16-to-P44 neurons did not show a baseline Kremen1-dependent transcriptomic liability, despite culture evidence that Kremen1 silencing can be protective under amyloid-beta/Dkk1 stress.
Krit1 loss after P16 produced no FDR-supported neuronal DE and did not induce the canonical endothelial KLF2/4, Rho-family, Nrf2-redox, or autophagy readouts of CCM loss.

The represented CCM-complex or CCM-adjacent perturbations did not define a shared neuronal module with Krit1: Pdcd10 was flat in all 21 Krit1-matched groups, and Cdc42, Tlr4, Itgb1, and Rac1 were null or single-gene responders.

Unbiased Krit1 score-vector neighbors were near zero rather than a hidden convergent class; the largest positive cosine was Itga7 at 0.0267, and the strongest negative gene neighbor, Wdr26, was only -0.0239 despite thousands of DE genes of its own.
L1cam perturbation produced a target-transcript-only signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: L1cam mRNA fell strongly, but no non-self transcript reached FDR<0.10.
Across every recovered L1cam cell group, the perturbation failed to elicit an axon-guidance, Ig-CAM, growth-cone, or cytoskeletal transcriptomic program at FDR<0.10.

The L1/NCAM comparator return-to-data step rejected a broad paralog phenocopy: Chl1, Ncam1, and Ank2 had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Nrcam had only two isolated one-gene downstream hits despite frequent Nrcam self-decreases.
Lamp2 produced only two corrected downstream hits, both in thalamic glutamatergic classes: Rgs11 up in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and Ppm1g down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Lamp2 loss did not induce a corrected lysosome, macroautophagy, chaperone-mediated-autophagy, proteasome, UPR/ISR, or redox transcript program in any measured neuronal group.
Neither literature-obvious autophagy/lysosomal comparators nor the top data-driven cosine neighbors phenocopied Lamp2's Rgs11/Ppm1g signature.
052 Pvalb Gaba and 191 MB P MY GABA showed significant Lamp2 mRNA depletion but zero corrected downstream genes.
Large1 produced a narrowly L5 ET-centered corrected response: Wwox was induced in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and every other measured cell group had zero corrected downstream genes.
Large1 did not phenocopy other directly assayed matriglycan/DAG1-glycosylation or dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex targets.
Large1 mRNA was significantly lower in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, yet no downstream transcript passed FDR<0.10 there.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of the Large1 full signature were extremely weak and failed corrected-overlap validation.
Lars2 produced a single FDR<0.10 transcriptome hit, Ttbk2 induction, confined to 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
Lars2 perturbation did not activate the expected mitochondrial translation, OXPHOS, or ATF4/ISR transcriptional program.
The phenotype-first global signature search left Lars2 essentially neighborless.
Mitochondrial protein-synthesis relatives Fars2, Gfm2, and Rars2 were also flat or nearly flat and did not phenocopy Lars2.
Acute Las1l loss of function was FDR-null in every recovered P16-to-P37/P44 neuronal group: 22 measured groups and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Las1l did not activate a secondary p53, ATF4/integrated-stress, or UPR-like transcriptional program: 24 sentinel genes across all 22 measured Las1l groups all had FDR=1.

Whole-surface Las1l signature neighbors did not yield a robust phenocopy: the strongest real positive and negative signed-score cosines were only 0.0315 for Zkscan1 and -0.0312 for Fbxo11, and all top real neighbors had 0 shared FDR-significant genes with Las1l.

The postnatal LoF null refines, rather than validates, the LAS1L neurodevelopmental-disease model: this screen found no acute transcriptional signature despite a literature link to syndromic ID that was classified as Limited in the cited ClinGen ID/Autism assessment.
Lbx1 produced exactly one robust downstream DEG across 22 measured neuronal cell groups, Vps35l down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Vps35l down-regulation is the isolated Lbx1 hit, but the rest of the Commander/WASH/CCC machinery and the represented Vps35l and Washc4 perturbations were flat.

The one-gene Lbx1 signature converged with Yy1 and opposed Thoc1 and U2af2 on Vps35l, while represented developmental partners Ptf1a, Pax2, Pax8, and Phox2b did not respond in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The P16 neuronal Lbx1 LoF surface did not recover AIS-associated or congenital-hypoventilation-associated programs.
Lemd3 loss produced a very sparse neuronal signature: only 053 Sst Gaba and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, totaling three genes across 371818 target rows.

Insig1 was upregulated in Lemd3-perturbed 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA neurons and recurred in the same cell group under Mib1, Rab7, Tsc2, Dctn1, and Far1 perturbations, while Srebf2 perturbation drove Insig1 down.
Ache increased in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA after Lemd3 perturbation and was recurrently altered, but with mixed direction, across other perturbations in the same cell group.
Vps35 was the sole FDR-significant Sst GABA downstream gene and was FDR-significantly up in the same Sst feature only under Psmb4 among other perturbations.

The expected BMP/TGF-beta/SMAD axis was not recovered: canonical SMAD-responsive transcripts stayed at FDR 1.0 after Lemd3 perturbation, and Acvr/Bmpr/Tgfbr/Smad/Ski perturbations were weak and did not share the Lemd3 responder genes.
Lemd3 was isolated in full perturbation-signature space: the top positive whole-profile neighbor was Mib1 with cosine 0.0338 and the top negative neighbor was Ywhae with cosine -0.0146.
Lepr loss produced a real but very narrow transcriptional response: only 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut crossed the FDR<0.10 downstream threshold, and its sole significant gene was Ankrd24 up-regulation.
The screen did not recover the textbook leptin-neuropeptide/JAK-STAT transcriptional program after Lepr perturbation.
Represented leptin-pathway and energy-balance comparators did not phenocopy the 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut Lepr singleton signature.
Unbiased score-vector comparison found no strong positive or negative Lepr signature neighbor in the 1,773-target visible universe.
Ankrd24 is a low-confidence candidate marker of the sparse Lepr response in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Lgals3 loss of function was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: none of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups carried even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The Galectin-3/TLR4/TREM2/NF-kB inflammatory axis was not recovered in any sampled neuronal group, and measured Tlr4, Cd14, and Nfkb1 perturbations were themselves flat.
Lgals3 perturbation did not elicit a lysosomal, ESCRT-autophagy, integrated-stress, or ER-stress bounce-back program in juvenile neurons.
Cross-perturbation search found no meaningful transcriptional neighbor for Lgals3.
The screen is reassuring only about broad neuronal transcriptomic liabilities of Galectin-3 loss, not about the microglial efficacy axis that motivates Galectin-3 inhibition in neurodegeneration.
Lgr4 loss-of-function was FDR-empty across all 21 recovered neuronal cell groups in the P16-to-P37/44 whole-brain snRNA perturbation assay.

The expected R-spondin/LGR4-to-β-catenin transcriptional program was absent after Lgr4 perturbation, despite detectable β-catenin/TCF biology from Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations in the same analysis universe.

Upstream Wnt receptor perturbations were individually buffered in these postnatal neuronal groups: Lgr4 and four Frizzled targets were flat, while Lrp5 and Lrp6 each produced only singleton-to-small effects.
The model-visible, literature-free neighbor search found no meaningful Lgr4 convergence or opposition: the strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations were only +0.027 and -0.018.
P16 Lhcgr loss of function produced a genome-scale basal transcriptomic null across every recovered neuronal cell group.
The data-driven Lhcgr signature has no stable positive or negative neighbor.
The glycoprotein-hormone receptor family is coordinately silent rather than selectively Lhcgr-silent in sampled postnatal neurons.
The assay can detect a nuclear cAMP-response perturbation, but Lhcgr loss does not reach it.
Lhcgr loss did not recover either gonadal steroidogenic or reported hippocampal neurosteroidogenic target genes.
Lhx3 perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 tested mouse brain neuronal groups.
The canonical Isl1-Lhx3 motor-neuron module was not reactivated or depleted downstream of Lhx3 loss in the juvenile brain neuronal panel.
Represented Lhx3 relatives, including Lhx4, Isl1, Mnx1, Pou1f1 and Prop1, did not converge with Lhx3 in the same cell-group DE universe.
The whole-signature neighbor search found only noise-scale Lhx3 similarities and anticorrelations.
