The LHX3 combined-pituitary-hormone-deficiency axis was absent from the neuronal Lhx3 loss-of-function surface.
Lhx4 loss-of-function produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured P16-to-P37/44 neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.

The Lhx3/Lhx4 pituitary and LIM-homeodomain neighborhood also failed to respond postnatally: Lhx3, Isl1, Prop1, Pou1f1, and Pitx2 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the Lhx4-matched neuronal cell groups.
The expected LHX4 loss programs were specifically absent: pituitary hormone/survival genes and retinal bipolar-cell markers showed zero FDR<0.10 changes after Lhx4 perturbation.
Unbiased whole-surface cosine analysis assigned only near-zero neighbors to Lhx4; even the strongest positive and negative neighbors had absolute cosine below 0.04.

The screen supports a developmental, lineage-displaced interpretation of LHX4-linked congenital hypopituitarism rather than a requirement for ongoing Lhx4-dependent transcription in the assayed juvenile brain neurons.
P16 sparse CRISPR loss of Limk1 produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 neuronal cell groups in which the target was recovered.
The canonical LIMK1 cofilin/actin pathway did not convert into a detectable nuclear actin-remodeling, proteostasis, UPR/ISR, redox, autophagy, or synaptic-stress program.
Represented Rac/Cdc42-PAK/LIMK pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Limk1 and did not reveal a shared actin transcriptomic module.
Limk1 had no robust data-driven signature neighbors after cell-group/gene feature centering.
The neuronal snRNA null should not be read as evidence that LIMK1 inhibition is inert or spine-safe.

Lingo1 loss produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic hit across 22 measured neuronal groups: Becn1 was up-regulated only in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, whereas 21 matched groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
direction_pattern: Becn1 up in one L2/3 IT cortical class; no FDR<0.10 downstream signal elsewhere

canonical_summary: The sole FDR-significant Lingo1-responsive downstream gene was Becn1, increased in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
The L2/3 IT Becn1 response and the global Lingo1 score vector were not reproduced by Lingo2, Rtn4r, Ngfr, Ntrk1, Ntrk2, or Ntrk3 perturbations.
Unbiased whole-parquet neighbors of Lingo1 were essentially flat: the strongest positive neighbor had r=0.033 and the strongest negative neighbor had r=-0.031.
direction_pattern: no robust positive or inverse neighbor

canonical_summary: The mostly null neuronal surface is not a test of the oligodendrocyte remyelination axis that motivated LINGO-1 antagonists.
direction_pattern: neuronal downstream null outside 007 does not assay oligodendrocyte remyelination biology

canonical_summary: Lingo2 had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups; 053 Sst Gaba was only a weak near-miss with Opcml at FDR=0.132.
The measurable Lingo/Nogo-axis perturbations Lingo1, Ngfr, and Rtn4r did not phenocopy Lingo2 or reveal a shared receptor-subunit transcriptional module.
The top unrestricted biological score neighbors of Lingo2 were only near-zero correlates, with absolute whole-surface cosine <0.025.
Litaf loss of function is transcriptomically flat across every recovered postmitotic neuronal class in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen.
Litaf does not phenocopy neuronal endosome/lysosome perturbations that were active in the same measurable universe.
The P16 CNS-neuronal Litaf null is consistent with CMT1C biology being displaced to peripheral, dominant-allele contexts rather than broad neuronal Litaf haploinsufficiency.
Litaf perturbation did not activate or suppress the TNF/LPS cytokine module in neurons.
No secondary ISR, UPR, autophagy, lysosomal, or immunoproteasome rebound accompanied Litaf loss.
Acute postnatal Lman2l loss of function was transcriptomically silent in every recovered neuronal group: no gene reached FDR<0.10 in 388046 tests across all 23 groups.
Lman2l did not induce an Hspa5-like UPR/ERAD program in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
The literature-obvious ER-export comparator Sec23a did not phenocopy Lman2l, and Lman2l had near-zero global correlation with both Sec23a and Hspa5.
Data-driven neighbors place Lman2l in a null-signature neighborhood rather than in a coherent biological module.
Lmbrd1 loss was a pan-measured neuronal downstream null: every recovered cell group had 0 genes at FDR<0.10 despite mostly negative Lmbrd1 self-logFC and significant self-depletion in two groups.
The expected cobalamin-processing transcripts did not form a feedback module after Lmbrd1 perturbation.
The measurable cobalamin-disease regulator Thap11 produced a broad neuronal signature and repressed Mmachc where Lmbrd1 did not.
The Lmbrd1 score surface had no non-random transcriptomic neighbor in the full perturbation universe.
Mmaa, the only represented intracellular AdoCbl-pathway target, converged with Lmbrd1 only by being flat.
Acute Lmx1b CRISPR produced a pan-taxonomy transcriptional null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Neither the data-driven nearest signatures nor the represented midbrain-dopamine network perturbations converged with Lmx1b.
The expected mDA mitochondrial-autophagy maintenance program was absent in the only recovered dopaminergic group.
Lonp1 loss produced a very narrow postmitotic neuronal transcriptional response: only 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut crossed downstream FDR<0.10.

The two multi-gene Lonp1 responders activate a CHOP/ISR-like mitochondrial metabolic module: Ddit3 is recurrent and is accompanied by Aldh1l2/Shmt2 in 155 MB Glut and Slc7a1/Herpud1 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
Lonp1 engaged an ER-proteostasis edge: Herpud1 rose in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, Emc3 rose as the only 110 hit, and Rtn3 fell in 155 MB Glut.
Lonp1 induced CHOP without a full canonical chaperone/protease UPRmt cassette: Atf5, Hspd1, Hspe1, Hspa9, and Clpp were all FDR=1 in the responder groups.

Opa1 was the closest positive data-driven Lonp1 neighbor and shared the Ddit3/Aldh1l2/Shmt2/Slc7a1 direction, while Atp2a2 and Psmb4 shared smaller or broader pieces of the same organelle-stress module.

Mitochondrial protease relatives Clpp, Clpx, Afg3l2, and Yme1l1 did not phenocopy Lonp1; Clpx and Yme1l1 had no FDR<0.10 downstream hits anywhere, and Clpp/Afg3l2 each had only one isolated hit in non-Lonp1-responder groups.
The data do not recover a broad CODAS-like neuronal developmental program after P16 Lonp1 loss; instead they recover late focal stress responses.
A LonP1-inhibition strategy should expect buffered neurons in most postmitotic groups but should monitor Ddit3/Herpud1/Slc7a1/Aldh1l2 as focal neuronal stress markers.
Lpar6 loss-of-function produced a uniformly empty FDR-level basal neuronal transcriptomic surface.
Lpar6 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Canonical LPA6 second-messenger and LIPH-LPA6 hair-axis expectations did not turn into a shared basal RNA program in juvenile neurons.
Lrba loss produced a pan-measured central-neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 tested cell groups.
Literature-obvious BEACH/autophagy relatives did not phenocopy Lrba: Lrba-Wdfy3, Lrba-Nbea, Lrba-Becn1, Lrba-Atg5, Lrba-Atg16l1, and Lrba-Map1lc3a score-cosines were all between -0.0049 and 0.0216.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of Lrba were effectively null: the strongest positive score-cosine was Igf1r at 0.0317 and the strongest negative was Dstyk at -0.0160.
The LRBA-CTLA4 immune checkpoint axis was completely absent from the neuronal response surface.
Lrba did not trigger a detectable autophagy, UPR, or integrated-stress transcriptional bounce-back in central neurons.
Acute Lrch1 perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal cell group.
Full-vector cross-perturbation neighbors of Lrch1 were only nominal and did not define a shared robust DEG module.
Represented LRCH1 pathway nodes and expected immune effector genes were absent as neuronal signatures.
Lrfn2 loss induced the chloride transporter transcript Slc12a5 as the only robust downstream DEG in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The Lrfn2 transcriptomic response was restricted to one of 22 measured neuronal groups.
Hippocampal Lrfn2 perturbation did not change PSD-95, AMPAR, NMDAR, or inhibitory-marker transcripts at FDR<0.10.
NMDAR-subunit perturbations produced broad signatures in matched groups that were flat after Lrfn2 perturbation.
Several represented PSD and synaptic-adhesion genes were themselves buffered, resembling Lrfn2 more than the NMDAR subunits did.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Lrfn2 had near-zero correlations and no shared Slc12a5 hit.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations drove Slc12a5 down, not up, in the same 066 class.
Acute postmitotic Lrif1 loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Lrif1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The represented SMCHD1/LRIF1 and nuclear-receptor comparators were flat in the matched neuronal assay.
Setdb1 responded where Lrif1 did not, separating the Lrif1 null from a generic flat-self-transcript or chromatin-target failure mode.
P16 mosaic Lrig2 loss of function was transcriptomically silent across every recovered postnatal neuronal group.
The Neogenin/RGMa/ADAM neighborhood did not expose a hidden Lrig2 transcriptional module.
LRIG2 disease and tumor mechanisms are displaced away from the sampled central postmitotic neuronal axis.
Proteasome perturbations show that the same low-cell matched surfaces could detect broad secondary transcription when the biology generated it.
The top positive whole-signature neighbors of Lrig2 were a shared flat-signature manifold rather than a biological convergence module.
Lrmda produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
A literature-predicted pigmentation and melanosome marker panel was absent after Lrmda perturbation in neurons.
The old 10q22 C10orf11 neurodevelopmental hypothesis was not phenocopied by acute Lrmda loss in postmitotic neurons.
Represented melanosome/LRO/endolysosomal comparator perturbations did not converge with Lrmda.
The dataset-wide similarity search found no meaningful positive or negative Lrmda signature neighbor.
Lrp1 loss-of-function produced a highly restricted juvenile neuronal transcriptome: only 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, both through Vgf up-regulation.

The 191 MB P MY GABA response coupled Vgf induction to an Unc13a increase, suggesting a secretory/active-zone adjustment in an inhibitory hindbrain-like class rather than loss of glutamate-receptor transcripts.
Vgf up-regulation after Lrp1 perturbation was uncoupled from an ER-stress/UPR program that the assay could detect in the same cell groups after Manf perturbation.

Acute neuronal Lrp1 loss did not induce a detectable APP/Aβ, tau, cholesterol, or apoptosis transcript module, despite LRP1's strong literature links to Aβ trafficking, apoE, tau and α-synuclein uptake, and age-dependent synapse loss.
LDLR-family relatives and sorting receptors represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Lrp1; Lrp6 instead produced a small thalamic Wnt-flavored signature including Axin2 down-regulation.

Canonical synaptic/endocytic perturbations were detectable but diverged from Lrp1: Cltc, Grin1, and Grin2b generated broader signatures, and Grin2b decreased Vgf in cortical IT neurons whereas Lrp1 increased Vgf in midbrain and pontine/myelencephalic cells.
The all-target, all-transcriptome search found no strong global Lrp1 neighbor; the largest non-safe cosine was only 0.0325 and failed to validate beyond Gabrg2 sharing Vgf up in 155 MB Glut.

The neuronal Lrp1 signature gives no support for a simple cell-autonomous transcriptomic toxicity after short juvenile loss, even though LRP1 blockade would be expected to alter uptake or spread of Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein at the protein-trafficking level.
Acute P16 Lrp2 loss produced no BH-corrected neuronal transcriptional response in any recovered cell group.
The absence of Gli/Ptch/Hhip, BMP-response, and Axin2/Lef1 remodeling places the DBS/FOAR-relevant LRP2 axis outside the assayed postmitotic neurons.
LRP2 did not phenocopy represented LDL-receptor-family, Reelin, SHH, or Wnt pathway targets; Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 responses show that at least a Wnt effector arm was detectable where Lrp2 was flat.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Lrp2 were numerically tiny and were rejected as biological convergence.
The data give no support for a P16 NeuN+ cell-autonomous neuronal LRP2 disease mechanism.
Lrp4 produced a singleton Arglu1 induction in 191 MB P MY GABA, with Arglu1 the only downstream transcript passing FDR<0.10 anywhere in the screen.
The all-cell Lrp4 perturbation is globally buffered: only 1 of 371,796 downstream Lrp4 tests reached FDR<0.10, and the strongest data-driven score-vector neighbors had |r|≤0.0417.
The LDL-receptor-family relative Lrp5 did not phenocopy Lrp4 in the only Lrp4 responder, 191 MB P MY GABA.
Lrp4 did not engage the thalamic Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional module that was readily detected after Lrp6 and Ctnnb1 perturbation.
The NMJ partner Musk was a measurable target but did not converge with Lrp4.
Ror2, the LRP4-associated kinase described for adult hippocampal neurogenesis, had no matched transcriptional convergence with Lrp4.
Lrp5 produced a single robust downstream change, Ercc1 down-regulation, specifically in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Canonical β-catenin/TCF feedback genes were absent from the Lrp5 DE surface.
Lrp6, not Lrp5, converged with Ctnnb1 on a six-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut module.
Most single Wnt/LDLR-family receptor perturbations represented in the parquet were flat or idiosyncratic and did not phenocopy Lrp5.
Lrp6 had a sharply restricted single-cell-group response: 6 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero in every other measured group.
The Lrp6 response includes down-regulation of the canonical Wnt feedback target Axin2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Ctnnb1 was the rank-1 positive data-driven neighbor of Lrp6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and changed all six Lrp6 FDR genes in the same direction.
Represented receptor-level Wnt relatives did not phenocopy Lrp6: Lrp5, Fzd2, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, Ror1, Ror2, and Ryk were flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Ctnnb1 was strongly convergent.
Tcf7l2 produced a broad 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature but only partially overlapped Lrp6 and did not significantly lower Axin2.
The non-Wnt data-driven neighbors after Ctnnb1 and the strongest negative neighbors were rejected as meaningful Lrp6 comparators.
Lrp8 produced one robust downstream RNA response: Gnai1 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
The full signed-rank Lrp8 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor in the 1,773-target model-visible universe.
Canonical Reelin-pathway perturbations did not reproduce the Lrp8::Gnai1 response.
NMDA-receptor perturbations generated detectable activity/synaptic RNA programs, whereas Lrp8 did not.
Juvenile neuronal Lrp8 loss did not converge with App, Psen1, Sorl1, Sort1, or Lrp1 perturbations.
Acute post-P16 Lrpprc CRISPR produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 21 recovered cell groups, spanning 1,209 perturbed nuclei.
The expected LRPPRC-proximal mtDNA mRNA and secondary ISR/UPR-mt programs were absent: 0/273 mtDNA protein-coding transcript tests and 0/336 stress-marker tests were FDR<0.10.

Lrpprc lacked a meaningful cross-perturbation neighbor: its top data-driven neighbors had absolute cosine <=0.0484, and represented mitochondrial comparators had cosines between -0.0218 and 0.0255; Opa1 was a clear divergent mitochondrial responder with 215 FDR genes in matched groups where Lrpprc had none.
Lrrc3b perturbation produced a single-gene Ndrg3 induction that was restricted to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The full Lrrc3b signature had no meaningful convergent or divergent global neighbor.
The OSN activity-gene comparator Kcnn2 did not phenocopy Lrrc3b in central neurons.
The epithelial tumor-suppressor program associated with LRRC3B was absent after acute Lrrc3b loss in postmitotic neurons.
Acute Lrrc7 CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any measured neuronal class.
The canonical PSD partners and readouts did not move as transcripts downstream of Lrrc7.
NMDAR subunit perturbations produced robust, cell-restricted RNA signatures where Lrrc7 did not.
Several PSD scaffold-neighborhood perturbations phenocopied Lrrc7 at the RNA level by remaining flat, despite detectable Dlg4 and Shank2 self-transcript loss.
Ctnnb1 loss down-regulated Lrrc7 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons, but Lrrc7 loss did not reciprocally perturb Ctnnb1.
The mGluR5 therapeutic axis in Lrrc7 mutant mice is not accompanied by a Grm5/Homer/Camk2 RNA biomarker in this postnatal mosaic assay.
Acute Lrrfip1 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream nuclear transcriptomic response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Lrrfip1 did not phenocopy the beta-catenin/Wnt perturbation surface: Ctnnb1, and weakly Lrp6, induced thalamic glutamatergic transcriptional signatures that were absent after Lrrfip1 perturbation.
The expected LRRFIP1 nucleic-acid/TLR/type-I-interferon axis was absent from the Lrrfip1 neuronal surface, and basal perturbation of measured TLR/IRF/NF-kappaB neighbors was nearly flat as well.
Homeostatic Lrrfip1 knockout did not elicit the oxidative-stress or excitotoxicity-linked programs that would be expected from LRRFIP1's DAPK1/OGD literature.

Lrrfip1 had no meaningful data-driven transcriptional neighbor: after feature-wise residualization its strongest positive or inverse correlations were only about plus or minus 0.02 and their own FDR-supported DE surfaces did not converge.
Acute P16 Lrrn2 loss produced no robust downstream nuclear transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
Lrrn3, the only same-NLRR paralog tested as a perturbation target, was as transcriptionally flat as Lrrn2 and did not reveal a shared postnatal NLRR loss-of-function module.
Unbiased whole-universe signature comparison found no meaningful positive or negative neighbor for Lrrn2.
The cerebellar 308 CB GABA population did not show a robust Lrrn2 loss-of-function signature despite human essential-tremor fine-mapping having nominated LRRN2 in cerebellar disease-relevant tissue.
Acute Lrrn3 loss did not generate an FDR-level nuclear transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
The unbiased signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Lrrn3 neighbor.
Lrrn3 was nearly orthogonal to the assayed Lrrn paralog, MAPK, MYCN, and clathrin comparators.
Neither the neuroblastoma differentiation literature nor the LRRN3 autism-candidate literature was phenocopied by simple postmitotic Lrrn3 loss.
Postnatal Lrrtm1 loss produced an almost entirely buffered nuclear response: one downstream DEG across 371,796 downstream tests in 22 measured neuronal groups.
The only Lrrtm1 DEG, R3hdm2, was confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Literature-obvious synaptic relatives did not phenocopy the Lrrtm1 R3hdm2 signature and were themselves mostly one-gene or zero-gene responders.
Lrrtm1 perturbation failed to induce immediate-early, AMPA/NMDA, neurexin or Cadm1/SynCAM-like compensatory mRNA modules.
Acute P16 Lrrtm3 loss was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null at P37-44.
The measured LRRTM-neurexin synaptic-adhesion neighborhood did not contain a hidden transcriptomic phenocopy of Lrrtm3.
Lrrtm3 loss did not lower App, Bace1, Ctnna3, or presenilin mRNAs in any tested neuronal class.
A universe-wide signed-score search placed Lrrtm3 in null-signature space, not next to a robust responder module.
Lrrtm4 produced a single FDR-resolved downstream transcript in L2/3 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons: Stag1 was up-regulated, while all other measured groups were FDR-flat.
Lrrtm4 loss did not transcriptionally recruit the LRRTM/neurexin/HSPG/AMPAR synaptic-adhesion program that its protein biology would nominate.
Represented LRRTM4 relatives and partner-pathway targets failed to phenocopy the Lrrtm4 Stag1-positive L2/3 IT signature.
Data-driven whole-surface matching found no meaningful Lrrtm4 signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Lyrm4 perturbation was almost completely buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level: 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene in 22 measured neuronal groups, 21 null groups, and one not-tested dopaminergic group.
Gmpr up-regulation in 155 MB Glut was the only FDR-supported Lyrm4 downstream event.
Nfs1 and other represented Fe-S/OXPHOS comparators did not converge on the Lyrm4 signature.
The data-driven neighbor analysis found no robust positive or negative Lyrm4 signature partner.
Lztfl1 loss produced a single robust downstream marker, Cyld up-regulation, confined to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
The lone Cyld response is interpretable as ciliary ubiquitin feedback, not as a generic stress or immediate-early gene burst.
Core BBSome, IFT, and transition-zone relatives did not phenocopy Lztfl1 in the LGE-GABA Cyld cell state.
Ciliopathy-family perturbations were not globally inert, but their transcriptomic effects occurred in different neuronal classes from Lztfl1.
The data-driven Lztfl1 signature neighborhood was noise-level and lacked a recurrent downstream module.
Canonical Hedgehog, hypothalamic leptin, and epithelial EMT readouts were absent after neuronal Lztfl1 loss.
Acute P16 Lztr1 loss-of-function produced a singleton, highly buffered neuronal transcriptome: only 2 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
Cacna1b was selectively down-regulated in Lztr1-perturbed 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons.
Vgf was selectively up-regulated in Lztr1-perturbed 191 MB P MY GABA neurons.
Canonical ERK-output mRNAs were absent from the Lztr1 surface.
RAS/MAPK-pathway perturbations represented in the parquet did not phenocopy the two Lztr1 singleton effects.
The strongest data-driven positive neighbors of Lztr1 converged on Vgf up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Wac was the data-driven opposite neighbor on the cortical Cacna1b axis.
Macf1 loss produced a single downstream FDR<0.10 gene, down-regulation of Atp1a3, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Macf1 was buffered in the postnatal snRNA readout: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, including a self-transcript-only weak result in 155 MB Glut.
Macf1 did not recover the Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional program expected from its Axin–β-catenin–GSK3β–LRP6 literature.
The cytolinker candidates Dst, Plec, and Map1b did not phenocopy Macf1 in the postnatal neuronal DE surface.
Macf1-induced Atp1a3 repression was not sufficient to induce the direct Atp1a3-loss program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Top data-driven Macf1 signature neighbors were all very weak and were rejected as mechanistic convergences.
Madd selectively up-regulated the OTU deubiquitinase gene Otud6b in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, the only FDR<0.10 downstream event in the entire Madd surface.
Madd loss of function was broadly buffered at the snRNA level: 22 tested cell groups yielded only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

The TNFR1-MAPK arm of MADD was uncoupled from basal P16-to-P37/44 neurons: AP-1, ERK-feedback, NF-kappaB, and UPR/ISR marker genes were all FDR=1.0, and represented TNF/MAPK pathway perturbations were flat or sparse.
Madd and the represented Rab3/Rab27-cycle targets converged on a buffered transcriptional outcome rather than a shared DE gene module.
Stxbp1, but not Madd or most other vesicle-release targets, produced a large snRNA response in the same screen.
The data-driven global signature-neighbor search did not identify a robust Madd-like or Madd-opposing transcriptomic perturbation.
Maf loss produced a four-gene, all-downregulated signature in 052 Pvalb Gaba and no FDR<0.10 downstream signal in the other 22 recovered cell groups.
Cacnb3, Lifr, Tmem108, and Entpd7 form a compact Pvalb membrane/excitability-receptor readout of acute Maf loss.
The neonatal Maf/Mafb -> Mef2c/Snap25/Cxcr4/Sst/Nrp1/Pnoc interneuron program was expected but absent after P16 single-Maf perturbation.
Mafb, Mafa, Mafg, and Bach2 did not robustly phenocopy the Maf Pvalb quartet.
The strongest FDR-retained restricted-signature comparators split the Maf quartet: Psmb4 shared Lifr/Tmem108 downregulation, while Adnp and Chd4 inverted Cacnb3.
Acute postmitotic Maf loss gives a narrow Pvalb transcriptomic state rather than a broad model of MAF-variant Aymé-Gripp syndrome.
Mafa had a single robust downstream hit, Pithd1 up, restricted to 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
Acute postnatal Mafa loss was transcriptionally buffered across sampled neurons.
Mafa did not phenocopy represented Maf-family perturbations in Pvalb GABA neurons.
The data-driven Mafa neighborhood was weak and non-repeatable at the FDR-gene level.
The Mafa apnea/GAD program was not recovered by P16 CRISPR loss of function in the sampled GABA classes.
The pancreatic β-cell/nicotinic Mafa program was absent from the neuronal Mafa surface.
P16 Mafb loss produced one robust downstream transcriptomic event: Ccdc88a down-regulation in Pvalb GABAergic neurons.
The expected neonatal Maf/Mafb MGE-interneuron program did not reappear after sparse single-gene Mafb perturbation at P16.
c-Maf, Mafg, and Mef2c responded in Pvalb neurons but did not share the Mafb Ccdc88a signature.
Mafb had no strong whole-surface positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor.
Ccdc88a down-regulation in Pvalb neurons recurred with Atxn10 but not with the obvious Maf/Mef2c comparators.
Mafg loss produced a Pvalb-interneuron redox/ubiquitin signature: Hmox1 was the dominant induced transcript and Uchl1 was repressed, while 21 other neuronal classes had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Mafg loss induced a small lysosomal/autophagy-leaning response centered on Lamp2, with Wdr70 as the only other FDR<0.10 transcript.
The Mafg signature did not phenocopy the represented canonical relatives Nfe2l2, Nfe2l1, Bach2, Maf, Mafa, or Mafb in the matched Pvalb and thalamic groups.
Mafg's thalamic Lamp2-up signal converged with Rab7, Dctn1, Yy1, and Tsc2 perturbations and was opposed by Uba5 and Qrich1, whereas Wdr70 was not recurrent at FDR<0.10.

Mafg self-transcript knockdown and downstream response were decoupled: L5-6 IT and midbrain glutamatergic neurons had significant Mafg mRNA reduction but no downstream genes, while the two responder groups had downstream FDR genes despite Mafg self FDR=1.
Acute Magel2 perturbation produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event: Kalrn was decreased in 155 MB Glut.
The Magel2 signature did not converge with the measured retromer/WASH surface.
Core-clock transcription was detectable after Bmal1 or Clock perturbation but absent after Magel2 perturbation.
Represented Prader-Willi/imprinted comparators did not phenocopy the Magel2 Kalrn response or generate a shared downstream module.
The screen did not reconstruct the neonatal oxytocin, arcuate POMC/leptin, or orexin/neuropeptide axes expected from Magel2 mouse-null disease biology.
Magel2 had no strong whole-surface neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.

Magi2-targeting postnatal CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal groups; only 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut reached near-threshold minima at FDR 0.108249 and 0.109857.

The Magi2 null did not recover AMPAR, NMDAR, TARP, neuroligin/neurexin, β-dystroglycan, or inhibitory-synapse transcriptional programs: 49 tested canonical synaptic or PTEN-mTOR transcripts had zero FDR<0.10 rows in the Magi2 surface.

NMDAR, β-catenin, and mTOR-pathway perturbations were measurable in the same cell groups but did not converge with Magi2: Grin1, Grin2b, Tsc2, and Ctnnb1 produced 131, 78, 636, and 489 downstream FDR<0.10 genes respectively, whereas Magi2 produced zero.
Magi2 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor: the largest Wilcoxon-score cosine across 1769 comparators was 0.050880, and the most negative was -0.030428.

P16 mosaic Manba loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and queried lysosomal, autophagy, unfolded-protein, and integrated-stress markers also had no FDR signal.

The flat Manba phenotype was shared by represented lysosomal hydrolase and M6P-trafficking targets: Gaa, Ppt1, Ctsb, Gnptab, and Gnptg each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in Manba-matched groups, despite strong self-transcript depletion for several of them.

The genome-scale signed-score search found no meaningful Manba signature neighbor: the best positive cosine was Kif1a at 0.02460 and the strongest negative was Fbxo11 at -0.01694, and these top neighbors failed to share an FDR-supported Manba program on re-query.

V-ATPase perturbations did not phenocopy Manba: Atp6v0a1 was flat across all 22 matched groups, while Atp6v1e1 produced only 10 FDR<0.10 downstream genes concentrated in 308 CB GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Manf loss elicited a recurrent, adaptive ER-chaperone/ER-protein-processing module rather than a broad neuronal identity program.

The Manf UPR was strongly cell-group restricted: 10 of 23 measured groups had any corrected downstream hit and only CNU-MGE GABA, CNU-HYa/HY GABA, MB Glut, and MB/Pons/My GABA carried multi-gene chaperone signatures.
The most robust positive signature neighbors were ER-load perturbations, especially Gfpt1 and Dhdds, not the textbook MANF paralog CDNF or the measured upstream branch target Atf6.
Manf activated chaperone genes without the severe ATF4/CHOP-like ISR module that appeared after Gfpt1 and Atp2a2 perturbation.

Manf loss did not recover an autophagy-lysosome transcriptional program and did not phenocopy core autophagy knockouts; Rb1cc1 instead induced the opposite chaperone direction in a subset of Manf feature genes.
Atf6 and Hspa5 perturbations were rejected as Manf phenocopies in matched neuronal groups.
Several corrected Manf hits were cell-specific singletons outside the core Hspa5 module.

Map1b produced a transcript-self-only response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: the Map1b transcript was significantly lower, but no non-Map1b transcript reached FDR<0.10 in either group or anywhere else.
Map1b loss failed to regulate the literature-nominated tubulin-tyrosination, axon-growth, neuronal-migration, and GSK3/MAP1B marker set at RNA level in all 22 measured groups.
The full-universe signature search found no meaningful Map1b neighborhood: the largest named-gene Pearson correlations were only +0.0308 to Syn1 and -0.0154 to Sipa1l3.
Mapt, Map6, Map1lc3a, and Mapre2 did not phenocopy Map1b, each producing 0 downstream DE genes at FDR<0.10 across the 22 Map1b-matched groups and Pearson r values from -0.0037 to 0.0173.

Dctn1, unlike Map1b, triggered a broad sterol/SREBP-like response in the same analysis universe, with 450 downstream DE genes across 12 Map1b-matched groups and strong up-regulation of Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Fdft1, and Sqle.
The Map1b null refines MAP1B disease biology toward developmental wiring, white-matter integrity, and subcellular cytoskeletal mechanisms rather than a stable postnatal neuronal transcriptomic state.
Map1lc3a loss produced a pan-panel downstream null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered neuronal groups, despite measurable negative self-transcript shifts in many groups.

The represented autophagy/lysosome/mTOR comparators did not phenocopy Map1lc3a: their score-profile correlations with Map1lc3a were approximately zero, and Tsc2 was strongly divergent with 636 downstream genes where Map1lc3a had none.
A target-agnostic signature-neighbor search found no hidden convergent module for Map1lc3a; even the largest Pearson correlation was only 0.061 and the strongest negative neighbor was only -0.039.

The Map1lc3a null did not contain transcriptional replacement of LC3A by alternative ATG8s or a TFEB/SQSTM1 autophagy-lysosome bounce-back: 22 expected transcripts were all FDR=1.0 in all 22 measured groups.
Map2k1 loss produced a sparse neuronal steady-state RNA response, with FDR<0.10 downstream genes in only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA among 22 measured groups.
direction_pattern: downstream response restricted to 2 of 22 measured groups

canonical_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c response is a down-regulated ERK-linked neuropeptide and synaptic program anchored by Vgf, Etv5, Ptpn5, and Unc13a.
Braf perturbation validates the 151 Map2k1 module by down-regulating Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a in the same group; Shoc2 shares the Vgf arm more weakly.

Most expected Ras/MAPK neighbors did not phenocopy Map2k1 in its responder groups: Map2k2, Mapk1, Ptpn11, Raf1, Hras, Kras, and Rasa2 were flat in 151 and 191, Sos1 produced only Cul7, and Lztr1 changed Vgf in 191 without matching the Las1l/Uso1 pair.
The 191 MB P MY GABA response was a two-gene, mixed-direction Las1l/Uso1 signature rather than a recovered Vgf/Etv5 ERK-feedback module.
155 MB Glut showed robust Map2k1 transcript depletion without any downstream DE genes.
The postnatal CRISPR-loss signature should not be read as a direct model of MAP2K1 developmental RASopathy alleles.
Map2k2 loss induced a single FDR<0.10 hit, Usp9x, specifically in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Single Map2k2 loss produced no persistent basal ERK-feedback or immediate-early transcriptional program across the 23 neuronal groups.
Map2k1 and Braf, but not Map2k2, converged on a small all-down thalamic module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The top whole-transcriptome Map2k2 neighbors had near-zero correlations and sparse, non-overlapping DE surfaces.
The flat single-Map2k2 CRISPR surface should not be read as a neuronal MEK-inhibitor safety result or as a cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome phenocopy.
Map2k6 loss was buffered across the basal postnatal neuronal transcriptome: every measured cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical p38/AP-1 and stress-response transcripts were absent from the Map2k6 surface.
Map2k6 did not phenocopy the p38-linked transcription factor Mef2c.
The represented stress-MAPK/TLR comparators were also flat, arguing against a latent basal MAPK transcriptomic module in this neuronal screen.
The numerical Map2k6 signature neighbors were too weak and too null to support a new network edge.
Map3k7 loss produced no FDR-resolved cell-autonomous transcriptional program in 22 measured juvenile NeuN+ neuronal groups.
Map3k7 had no meaningful positive or negative whole-screen signature neighbor.
The TLR/IL-1/TNF-to-TAK1-to-NF-kappaB/JNK/p38 axis was transcriptionally silent as a perturbation module in the same neurons.
Map3k7 did not phenocopy the represented TGF-beta/BMP/SMAD network in postnatal neuronal nuclei.
The neuronal Map3k7 null argues against reading this screen as a disease-variant or anti-inflammatory efficacy model for TAK1 inhibition.
Map6 was a complete downstream transcriptomic null across all 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Map6 did not phenocopy microtubule-track or motor perturbations: Dctn1 induced a large sterol/lipid program and Tuba1a induced reciprocal tubulin genes where Map6 induced none.
Unbiased Map6 signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated with Map6, with the strongest biological positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations all within |r|<0.03.
The synaptic, lysosomal, calcium-channel, and tubulin transcripts most expected from STOP/MAP6 literature were all present in the Map6 DE tests but absent at FDR<0.10.
The flat Map6 nuclear transcriptome should not be used as a negative biomarker for microtubule-stabilizing or synaptic rescue of MAP6-deficient circuits.

Mapk1 loss was transcriptomically buffered across the neuronal screen: all 21 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, even though the self-transcript trended down in every group and reached FDR 1.11e-05 in 155 MB Glut.

The canonical upstream nodes Map2k1 and Braf, but not Mapk1, resolved a small thalamic ERK-output module: Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a were significantly decreased by both Map2k1 and Braf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Mapk1 perturbation did not recover an ERK immediate-early, ETS-feedback, or plasticity response: Fos, Egr-family members, Jun/Junb, Arc, Npas4, Dusp1/4/5/6, Etv1/4/5, Bdnf, Vgf, and Ptpn5 were all FDR=1.0 across the 21 Mapk1 surfaces.
The flat Mapk1 loss-of-function surface separates postnatal ERK2 depletion from RASopathy-like MAPK1 enhanced function.

Mapk1 was essentially isolated in global perturbation-signature space: even the strongest data-driven non-safe positive and negative neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations of only 0.032 or less.
Mapk9 loss was FDR-silent in every measured neuronal class: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 across 21 recovered cell groups, despite weakly negative Mapk9 RNA in 20 of 21 groups.
Canonical AP-1/IEG, apoptosis, and FoxO/autophagy transcripts were all absent from the corrected Mapk9 surface.
Represented MAPK/JNK-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Mapk9. ERK/p38/JNK-adjacent targets were either flat, nearly flat, or cell-type restricted with near-zero Mapk9 cosines.
The leading data-driven neighbors of Mapk9 were extremely weak: the best restricted-signature positive cosine was 0.0749 and the best negative cosine was -0.0408.
Basal snRNA biomarkers are likely to be insensitive readouts of isolated neuronal JNK2 inhibition.

Mapkbp1 loss produced a two-gene, L4/5 IT CTX Glut-restricted downstream response: Tbc1d19 and Plppr4 were both decreased, while the other 20 measured Mapkbp1 groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The Mapkbp1 L4/5 IT signature did not converge with data-driven or canonical JNK/NOD2 comparators: Map3k7, Mapk9, and Nod2 were flat in L4/5 IT and globally, while the top data-driven Adam10, Maf, Xpr1, and Tbx22 relationships were extremely weak or non-significant.
Mapkbp1 perturbation did not induce a chronic AP-1, NFκB, autophagy, or DNA-damage transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group.
Mapkbp1 did not form a shared neuronal transcriptomic module with represented ciliary or nephronophthisis-family perturbations Cep290, Glis2, Bbs5, or Ift88.
Mapre2 loss did not create an FDR-supported nuclear transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
Measured reduction of the Mapre2 transcript in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut uncoupled on-target mRNA depletion from downstream transcriptional remodeling.
Mapre2 did not phenocopy represented microtubule, tubulin, or dynactin perturbations.
The full-universe signature search found no meaningful Mapre2 convergence partner.
The postnatal Mapre2 null does not model the embryonic, allele-specific MAPRE2 disease mechanisms reported for CSC-KT.
Mapt loss produced no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
The expected MAP-family/tubulin compensation was not an mRNA program after Mapt perturbation.
A MAPT-APP-Fyn/tauopathy transcript axis was absent from young wild-type neurons after Mapt loss.
Full-universe rank-neighbor analysis found no robust positive or negative Mapt signature neighbor.
The screen is compatible with neuronal tolerance of tau lowering but is not an efficacy model for tau-lowering ASOs.
Marchf6 loss induced a compact SREBP2/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptome in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with one-gene Fdps or Insig1 outposts in 066, 110, and 308.
Srebf2 perturbation was the matched pathway inverse of Marchf6: it was the second strongest negative neighbor and drove 12 downstream Marchf6 sterol genes in the opposite direction at FDR<0.10.
The obvious sterol relatives Hmgcr and Srebf1 were measured but did not phenocopy Marchf6 in its responder groups.
Mib1, Dctn1, Tsc2, and Htt unexpectedly converged on the same sterol coordinates as Marchf6, whereas Far1 fell out after FDR-level overlap testing.
Phf12 was the strongest data-driven antineighbor after returning to the parquet, opposing 11 downstream Marchf6 sterol coordinates at FDR<0.10; Kifbp, Pi4kb, and Opa1 did not pass that overlap gate.
The POMC-neuron ER-stress/ferroptosis expectation did not generalize: Marchf6 induced Acsl4 in 151, but not a coordinated Hspa5, Ddit3, Herpud1, Asns, Chac1, or Trp53 stress program.

Simple postnatal Marchf6 loss-of-function did not create a broad cortical, cerebellar, or pan-neuronal disease-like transcriptome, consistent with FAME3 being a specific intronic repeat-expansion mechanism rather than ordinary MARCHF6 haploinsufficiency.
Marcks loss was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered postmitotic neuronal atlas: none of 22 measured cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The embryonic MARCKS requirement for forebrain construction did not reappear as a postmitotic cortical or hippocampal snRNA program.
Marcks had no convincing data-driven signature neighbor: the strongest positive and negative gene-target correlations were all near zero.
Acute Marcks knockdown did not phenocopy represented PKC, calmodulin, or small-GTPase cytoskeletal perturbations.
Mark3 loss produced a restricted Rai1-down response in MH-LH TH Glut and no broader Rai1 effector module.
The Mark3 response was uncoupled from the canonical MARK tau/MAP and ARHGEF2-Hippo polarity axes at the mRNA level.
Genome-scale score-neighbor analysis did not reveal a robust Mark3 transcriptional phenocopy.
Mast1 loss produced a single lysosomal trafficking hit, Vps41 up-regulation, specifically in CTX-CGE GABA neurons.
Mast1 loss induced the Hsp40 co-chaperone Dnaja2 in CNU-MGE GABA neurons.
The Mast1 transcriptional response was almost completely buffered and confined to two inhibitory populations.
Mast1 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce MAST-family paralogs or the PTEN/syntrophin/nNOS axis.
Neither the data-driven nearest neighbors nor testable literature-neighbor perturbations converged with Mast1 in the responder groups.
The acute LoF null refines, rather than contradicts, MAST1 disease genetics.
Matr3 loss was broad but not uniform: 18 of 21 measured neuronal groups had FDR<0.10 downstream signal, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The most target-proximal-looking abundance change was an RNA-processing rebound: Sugp2 was up in 12 groups while Rsrp1 and several splicing factors were recurrently down.
Matr3 perturbation repeatedly induced ER quality-control and stress-adaptation genes, including Uggt2 and Sec11a, together with Zkscan3 and redox or mitochondrial quality-control markers.

A membrane/lipid-trafficking module headed by Ddhd1 and Atp9b was the most recurrent positive component of the Matr3 signature and coupled to synaptic or ion-channel changes such as Kcnq2 upregulation.
Gpt2 defined a subcortical metabolic branch of the response, rising in Pvalb/MGE/HY GABA and in thalamic or midbrain neurons but not in cortical IT neurons.

The unbiased nearest positive neighbors of Matr3 were U2af2, Tpr and Ascc3; U2af2, Prpf6 and Cdc40 splicing-factor perturbations shared a significant subset of the Matr3 module but were far broader than Matr3.
Among measurable ALS-family perturbations, Tardbp was the only partial Matr3 phenocopy; Hnrnpa2b1, Atxn2, Tia1, Kif5a, Sqstm1 and Vcp were essentially divergent or flat.

Because acute neuronal Matr3 depletion itself triggered broad RNA-processing, proteostasis and metabolic signatures, pan-Matr3 lowering is unlikely to be neutral even if allele-specific suppression of toxic MATR3 variants remains conceptually attractive.
Mbd2 produced a real FDR-level signature only in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where the entire response was Uhrf1bp1l down-regulation.
The screen did not recover the textbook MBD2 loss-of-repression program: no Mbd2 cell group contained an FDR<0.10 up-regulated downstream gene.
Mbd2 did not phenocopy MBD-family or NuRD-family perturbations represented in the parquet.
The unbiased Mbd2 signature had no strong recurrent neighbor; its largest all-vector cosine was only 0.031598 and the top six positive or negative neighbors did not share the CTX-CGE Uhrf1bp1l hit.
The germline hippocampal Mbd2-deficiency program reported in mice was not recovered by acute P16 mosaic Mbd2 loss in hippocampal-like glutamatergic groups.
Acute postmitotic Mbd5 loss produced a near-flat snRNA-seq response across 21 neuronal groups, with only one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Map2k4 was selectively increased in 001 L5-6 IT Glut and was the only Mbd5 downstream transcript passing the FDR<0.10 threshold.
Represented BAP1/PR-DUB-associated perturbations did not phenocopy Mbd5: Bap1 and Ogt were far broader, whereas Asxl3 and Foxk2 were flat, and none shared the L5-6 Map2k4 hit.
Mbd5 was not interchangeable with represented MBD-family, NuRD, or chromatin-NDD controls in the matched groups.
The Mbd5 perturbation did not recover the ciliary, synaptic-plasticity, or ASD/NDD-enriched programs reported from stronger or developmental MBD5 models.
Mbl2 loss produced a pan-neuronal FDR-null response: all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Mbl2 perturbation did not move the measured complement or inflammatory transcripts that would have reported a secondary neuronal response.

The data-driven Mbl2 neighbors were rejected as robust biology: Sox11, Nfkb1, and Tbx5 showed zero or one DE gene in matched groups, while the unrelated broad responder Wdr26 showed that matched groups were not globally incapable of producing DE.
Neuron-directed Mbl2 loss is a poor surrogate for protective MBL inhibition in brain injury models.
P16 mosaic Mc1r loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The MC1R melanogenic target program was absent from the neuronal Mc1r response surface.
Mc1r loss did not trigger a neuronal cytokine, NF-κB, redox, ISR, or UPR secondary program under basal conditions.
The represented melanocortin-system targets Mc2r and Agrp converged with Mc1r on a zero-downstream phenotype.
Represented adenylyl cyclase and PKA perturbations were flat despite some target-RNA drops, whereas direct Creb1 perturbation produced only a small, Crem-centered response.
Mc1r had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the full visible target universe.
Mc2r loss was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic negative in all 22 measured cell groups.
Mc2r had no robust global signature neighbor; its nearest positive neighbors were null-like safe-target controls and every absolute Pearson correlation was below 0.08.
The only measured melanocortin-receptor paralog, Mc1r, also remained flat and did not phenocopy Mc2r.
The neuronal null should not be used to model MC2R antagonist efficacy, but it is consistent with an adrenal-focused on-target mechanism.
The only FDR<0.10 downstream response after Mchr1 targeting was Pnrc1 induction in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Mchr1 perturbation did not produce a multi-gene cAMP/ERK immediate-early response or a stress/proteostasis rebound in any measured neuronal group.
The data-driven positive and negative neighbors of the weak Mchr1 signature were nominal-score neighbors only, not robust convergent perturbations.
Represented proximal GPCR/cAMP and dopamine-receptor comparators did not phenocopy Mchr1 in the matched basal snRNA assay.
MCHR1 antagonist biology should not be triaged with basal cell-autonomous snRNA alone.
Mcph1 loss was transcriptionally silent across every recovered postmitotic neuronal class, despite 1201 perturbed nuclei distributed over 22 tested groups.

The empty Mcph1 signature did not converge with its measurable condensin, checkpoint, or microcephaly-disease comparators: Ncapd3 showed only one weak DEG, Atr/Trp53/Prkdc/Cit/Kif11 were flat, whereas Smc1a and tubulin perturbations produced narrow non-overlapping responses.
Mcts1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across juvenile postmitotic neurons, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene among 355,025 tested cell-group gene rows.
Lpgat1 was the only significant Mcts1-responsive downstream transcript and was restricted to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Whole-signature neighbor analysis yielded no robust positive or negative phenocopy for the nearly null Mcts1 surface.
Mcts1 did not activate or repress an Opa1-like ATF4/ISR transcriptional program.
The neuronal Mcts1 RNA surface did not recover the JAK2/IFN-γ, Insr/Igf1r, or Klhdc8a/Asb8 axes expected from immune, Drosophila, and fibroblast ribosome-profiling studies.
Mdh1 loss produced a reproducible downstream transcriptome only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 42 genes at FDR<0.10, while the other 21 recovered neuronal groups had 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
The 151 response carried a small amino-acid and ISR-like metabolic edge, led by Cars, Gls, and Ddit3, but it did not recruit the full ASNS/CHAC1/SLC7A5/SHMT2 stress program.
Mdh1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coordinately reduced synaptic, adhesion, and excitability transcripts including Nrxn1, Cadm3, Grin2b, Lrrtm1, Epha4, Gabbr2, Kcnc2, Atp1a1, Pcsk2, and Cdh2.
Got1, the cytosolic aminotransferase paired with Mdh1 in the malate-aspartate shuttle, was the rank-1 positive 151 signature neighbor of Mdh1.
The mitochondrial MAS half did not phenocopy Mdh1 in 151: Mdh2 and Slc25a12 had strong self-transcript decreases but no downstream FDR genes, and Got2 produced only Snap25.
Gls was one of the strongest Mdh1-induced genes, but direct Gls perturbation did not phenocopy Mdh1 in 151.

Mdh1's stress response was far smaller than same-cell perturbations that strongly activate ISR/UPR genes: Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Opa1 produced 284, 416, and 44 DEGs in 151, respectively, whereas Mdh1 produced 42 and left Asns, Chac1, Slc7a5, and Shmt2 below FDR<0.10.
The 151 Mdh1 signature up-regulated a compact RNA-processing, ubiquitin, and ESCRT/endosomal-trafficking cluster: U2surp, Luc7l2, Hnrnpu, Ddx46, Snf8, Ube2b, and Ubr3.
The strongest FDR-backed inverse neighbor of the Mdh1 restricted 151 signature was Arid2, not another metabolic enzyme.
Mdh2 CRISPR perturbation elicited a single robust downstream transcript, Tcaf1, selectively in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
A canonical mitochondrial stress, ISR, or glycolytic-compensation program is absent across the entire measured Mdh2 neuronal surface.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Mdh2 is flat where the related Mdh1 and Got1 malate-aspartate-shuttle perturbations respond.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors of Mdh2 were near-zero signatures rather than a coherent metabolic module.
Acute P16 Mecp2 loss produced a sparse neuronal basal response restricted to 4 of 22 measured cell groups, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature was a mixed ion-channel, transmitter, extracellular-matrix, and adhesion-remodeling state.
direction_pattern: mixed; neuronal excitability genes mostly down with selected adhesion and matrix genes up

canonical_summary: Cacna1g was down in both thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons and MB glutamatergic neurons, the only recurrent Mecp2 FDR gene across cell groups.
The Pvalb response consisted of Auts2 up-regulation rather than Gad1/Gad2 loss.
Mecp2 perturbation in 191 MB P MY GABA down-regulated the CELF-family RNA-binding genes Celf3 and Celf5.
The screen did not recover the expected broad Bdnf/immediate-early, long-gene, or Gad1/Gad2 programs after Mecp2 loss.
Methyl-CpG / NCoR-complex relatives were largely uncoupled from the Mecp2 phenotype, while Sin3a was broad and only partially overlapping.
Wac, Yy1, and Psmb4 converged on portions of the Mecp2 signature but with far broader perturbation surfaces.
Atxn1, Brd4, and Camta1 inverted several 151 Mecp2 coordinates.
Clinically adjacent neurodevelopmental perturbations Cdkl5, Ube3a, Tcf4, and Rai1 did not phenocopy Mecp2.

Mecr loss produced a buffered neuronal transcriptome: only two singleton downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across all 23 recovered cell-group tests, and none of the measured mtFAS, lipoate, OXPHOS, Fe-S, ISR, iron, or ceramide marker genes were significant.
Pvalb interneurons carried the clearest noncanonical Mecr RNA hit, with the Pol III/TFIIIC gene Gtf3c2 up-regulated as a singleton FDR<0.10 event.
The dopaminergic Mecr response consisted of Scg3 down-regulation as one large-effect singleton hit.

The phenotype-first signature-neighbor search returned extremely small score cosines; the top positive non-Safe neighbors Cadps2, Uchl1, and Zfp536 and the top negative neighbors Slf2, Zfx, and Btbd9 did not define a coherent Mecr-like module.

Represented lipoate, OXPHOS, and Fe-S effector perturbations failed to phenocopy Mecr; even Ogdh, Dlat, Dlst, Sdha, Lyrm4, Nfs1, Ndufa6, Ndufb9, Ndufs4, and Isca2 had few or no singleton FDR events and no shared Pvalb or dopaminergic Gtf3c2/Scg3 response.

Med13 loss produced a 14-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut dominated by down-regulation of thalamic excitability, glutamatergic receptor, calcium-handling and synaptic genes, with Scnm1 as the lone up-regulated hit.
Med13 perturbation induced Fam168b as the only FDR<0.10 gene in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

Med13 was transcriptionally buffered in most recovered juvenile neurons: only 2 of 21 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the Med13 transcript itself had FDR=1 in all measured groups.

Cdk8 was an exploratory anti-neighbor of Med13 rather than a phenocopy: it was the second strongest negative 15-feature neighbor and flipped all Med13 responder-feature signs, but had no FDR<0.10 genes in either responder group.
Med13l did not phenocopy Med13 in the responder groups; only Grm1 reached FDR<0.10 under Med13l in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was flat.
Mediator subunits Med15 and Med23 converged on the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut down-regulated module more strongly than Med13l.

Med13 recovered only a small Wnt/β-catenin-sensitive thalamic subset: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 shared Med13 down-regulated genes, whereas canonical Wnt-feedback genes were not significant after Med13 perturbation.

Acute P16 Med13l loss produced a nearly flat postmitotic neuronal DE surface: only two downstream gene-by-cell-group rows, Arpp21 in L4/5 IT cortex and Grm1 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, crossed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured groups.
The two reproducible Med13l outputs were both neuronal signaling or morphogenesis-linked transcripts, Arpp21 down in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and Grm1 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Grm1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut converged across Med13l, its paralog Med13, and the broader Mediator subunit targets Med15 and Med23, and it also appeared in the data-driven neighbor Cic; the CKM kinase Cdk8 did not share it.
Arpp21 down-regulation in L4/5 IT cortical neurons was Med13l-selective: Med13, Cdk8, Med15 and Med23 were all measured in the same 005 group and none reduced Arpp21 at FDR<0.10.

Whole-surface signature neighbors did not become strong phenocopies: Wdr26, Cic and Sp7 were the top positive ranked neighbors and B9d1, Alkbh8 and Atxn10 the top negative ranked neighbors, but absolute score correlations were only 0.02-0.04 and only Cic shared either Med13l FDR hit.

The expected embryonic cortical neurogenesis and Wnt/FGF-associated MED13L program was absent after P16 neuronal CRISPR: Neurod2, Sox5, Auts2, Nfib and Wnt/developmental sentinels were all measured but never FDR-significant.
Med15 produced FDR-level downstream responses in only two measured cell groups, dominated by 26 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a single Usp48 hit in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Med15 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells downregulated a neuronal synaptic, calcium/ion-handling, and subtype-identity module.
A single ubiquitin-system gene, Usp48, was induced in the otherwise sparse 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut response.

The Med15 151 signature converged with Med13 and Med23 perturbations by shared-direction repression of neuronal genes including Prkcd, Plekhg1, Pcp4, Atp2a2, Grm1, Ildr2, Kcnc2, Adgrb1, Atp2b1, Lef1, and Ptpn3.
Med13l and Cdk8 failed to phenocopy Med15 where Med13 and Med23 converged.
Med15 perturbation did not recover the canonical SREBP cholesterol-biosynthesis program, whereas Srebf2 LoF downregulated Dhcr24, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Cyp51, and Sqle in 151 cells.
TGFβ/Smad-pathway perturbations did not converge with Med15 in either Med15 responder group.
Proteasome perturbations, especially Psmb4 and Psmc1, were top positive neighbors and significantly contained much of the Med15 151 downregulated module.
Setd5 opposed the Med15 151 signature at FDR level for Prkcd, Lrrc7, Ntng1, and Plekhg1.
Med23 loss produced a selective 20-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, dominated by downregulation of synaptic, receptor, adhesion, and calcium/ion-handling transcripts.
Kcnc1 was the sole robust Pvalb-interneuron response to Med23 perturbation.
Within directly measured Mediator perturbations, Med15 and Med13 converged with the Med23 151-thalamic module, whereas Med13l barely overlapped and Cdk8 was flat.
Med23 loss did not activate a broad canonical WNT program; its thalamic signature instead overlapped beta-catenin and Tcf7l2 loss-of-function signatures.
The sparse Med23 thalamic/Pvalb signature is a recurrent module shared with broad perturbations including Psmb4, Rnpc3, U2af2, Wac, Cic, Rab7, and Psmc1.
Ankrd11 and Setd5 were the strongest FDR-supported inverse neighbors of Med23 on the same 151-thalamic/Pvalb coordinates.
Acute Mef2a loss produced a real but tiny transcriptional response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Mef2c, not Mef2d, is the closest MEF2-family comparator and has cortical/Pvalb effects where Mef2a is flat.
The six-gene thalamic Mef2a signature is most cleanly embedded within the Ctnnb1 response.
Canonical activity-dependent MEF2 synaptic targets did not move after basal P16 Mef2a CRISPR.
Representative calcineurin and HDAC perturbations did not phenocopy Mef2a.

Acute postnatal Mef2c loss produced a real but sharply cortical IT-skewed transcriptional response: 49 and 50 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in L4/5 and L2/3 CTX IT neurons versus only 7 in Pvalb and 3 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons.

The two cortical IT responders shared a same-direction neurosecretory, AMPAR/pentraxin, and membrane-remodeling signature with Chgb, Stac2, Serinc2, Rasal1, Rasgrf1, Gria2, and Nptx1 up and Slit2, Rasgrf2, Enpp2, Sun1, and Zdhhc8 down.

Mef2c loss did not simply drop every synaptic transcript: L2/3 CTX neurons coupled an AMPAR/pentraxin increase to calcium-channel and guidance changes, including Ptk2b and Jam3 up but Kcnh5, Cacna2d1, Cacnb3, Grm3, Frzb, and Camk2n1 down.

The acute postnatal signature did not recover the classic Arc/Pcdh10/Syngap1 MEF2-FMRP synapse-elimination arm, the bulk Emx1-cKO ASD/synaptome markers Cdkl5, Shank2/3, Nrxn1, and Nlgn1, or the EphA/Efna5 and Rorb/Bcl11b laminar programs at FDR<0.10.

Mef2a, Mef2d, and Hdac5 did not phenocopy Mef2c: Mef2d had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes anywhere, Mef2a had only six thalamic genes and none in cortical IT, and Hdac5 had one hippocampal/amygdalar gene.

Within the literature NMDAR/calcium neighborhood, Grin2a was the only represented perturbation with repeated same-direction overlap to Mef2c, whereas Grin1, Grin2b, Camk2a, Camk2b, Ppp3ca, and Syngap1 were divergent or flat on the Mef2c feature set.

The largest real data-driven overlaps came from broad perturbations, not a clean MEF2C module: Eef2, Psmb4, Ogt, Cic, Prpf6, Ski, and Sin3a each overlapped the 109-gene Mef2c signature in mixed or sparse directions while top negative cosine neighbors had no FDR-level overlap.
Pvalb interneurons showed a real but very small Mef2c response, with Rph3a and Gria2 up and Kcnip2, Dock4, Cemip, and Abtb3 down; Pvalb itself, Gad1, and Gad2 were not significant.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response was limited to Edil3 up and Gpr4/Madd down; Gpr4 was also the one same-direction Mef2a overlap, but no broader cortical Mef2c module appeared there.

Human MEF2C disease is loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency, yet P16 sparse neuronal LoF produced a narrow cortical IT/Pvalb/thalamic RNA surface and left most embryonic laminar, PV-maturation, and canonical MEF2-FMRP outputs absent.
Mef2d loss produced a pan-recovered-neuron basal transcriptional null: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 measured cell groups despite a weak negative self-transcript trend.
Mef2c, not Mef2d, was the MEF2-family perturbation with a robust cortical response in this universe.
The unbiased Mef2d signature-neighbor search found no robust convergent or inverse module.
The basal 215 MB Dopa Mef2d null did not recover the MEF2D-ND6 Parkinson-related mitochondrial program.
P16 mosaic loss of Meis1 did not elicit a corrected whole-transcriptome program in any measured neuronal class.
The literature-obvious TALE relatives did not form a shared postnatal Meis1/PBX response module.
A restless-legs-syndrome-like dopamine/iron/cholinergic signature was not recovered from sparse juvenile neuronal Meis1 loss.
Pre-literature signature neighbors were only numerically ranked noise-level matches.
Meis2 perturbation produced a single corrected downstream transcript, Actr1b, up-regulated in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
A P16-to-P37/44 Meis2 perturbation did not recover the expected embryonic LGE/MSN gene-regulatory response in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Represented MEIS/PBX/DLX/SIX/TGIF relatives did not phenocopy the one-gene Meis2 signature or reveal a shared postnatal TALE-fate module.
The full-parquet data-driven neighbor search found only noise-level positive and negative Meis2 neighbors.

The flat P16 postmitotic neuronal screen supports interpreting MEIS2 haploinsufficiency biology as primarily developmental and lineage-specific rather than as broad acute neuronal transcriptome maintenance.
Postnatal Meox1 loss produced a focal Mecp2 transcriptional increase in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
The Meox1 response was restricted to 001 L5-6 IT Glut; every other measured neuronal group was FDR-flat.
The data-driven Mecp2 neighbors were rejected after matched FDR inspection.
The canonical Meox sclerotome/myogenic hierarchy was absent from the neuronal Meox1 DE surface.
Represented Meox-lineage comparator perturbations did not phenocopy the L5-6 IT Mecp2 edge.
Mertk produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.
The directly queryable TAM paralog Axl and other represented phagocytic or microglial relatives did not converge with Mertk in matched neuronal groups.
Mertk's data-driven signature neighbors were noise-scale: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was r=0.03055 and the strongest negative correlation was r=-0.01849.
Sparse postmitotic neuronal Mertk loss should not be used to de-risk systemic TAM or MERTK inhibition in glial, macrophage, or retinal pigment epithelial compartments.
Mesp2 loss produced a real but almost exhausted response in only two glutamatergic groups: Gtf3c1 was lower in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Arih2/Wdfy3 were lower in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut hit pair, Wdfy3 and Arih2, points to a very small ubiquitin-autophagy/proteostasis-adjacent decrease.
The single 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut hit, Gtf3c1, nominates TFIIIC/Pol III transcription as a one-gene candidate readout of Mesp2 perturbation in this group.
Mesp2 perturbation failed to move the expected somitogenesis/Notch output genes despite those transcripts being queried.
Mesp2 did not phenocopy represented segmentation-pathway perturbations in the neuronal atlas.
A data-driven whole-surface neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Mesp2 signature neighbor.
The screen should not be interpreted as a postnatal neuronal model of MESP2-linked vertebral segmentation disease.
P16 mosaic Mest loss produced no genome-wide downstream response in any recovered NeuN+ neuronal group.
The LRP6/Wnt-Akt/cadherin program expected from embryonic and adipogenic literature was not relayed by Mest in postnatal neurons, although Wnt comparators were transcriptionally detectable.
The assay did not directly sample the Mest-sensitive SNc dopaminergic subset implicated in progressive Mest knockout phenotypes.
Paternally expressed and imprinting-related neurobehavioral comparators did not form a shared postmitotic neuronal module with Mest.
A full-universe signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Mest neighbor.
Met loss of function was FDR-null in every measured neuronal class: 21 of 21 tested groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the target transcript itself had FDR=1.00 everywhere.
Directly perturbing several represented MET-adjacent pathway nodes produced detectable signatures, especially Ctnnb1, Gsk3b, Map2k1, Mtor, and Braf, but their score vectors did not converge with Met.
Met had no strong data-driven convergent or opposing neighbor: the best non-safe positive score-cosines were only about 0.027 and the best non-safe negative cosines only about -0.013.
Mff loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
Mff was uncoupled from the Opa1-like mitochondrial integrated-stress program that was readily detected in the same DE universe.
Empirical Mff signature neighbors were weak, control-like surfaces rather than a strong mitochondrial co-response module.
The P16 acute neuronal Mff perturbation did not phenocopy the stress component of severe MFF deficiency diseases.
Mfsd6 loss was buffered across the postnatal neuronal atlas: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the whole target yielded only one downstream hit.
The only significant downstream response was Tmtc1 down-regulation in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Mfsd6 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce related MFSD transporter genes, and MFSD8/MFSD10/MFSD11 were not available as reciprocal perturbation targets.
The macrophage MHC-I receptor annotation of Mfsd6 did not translate into a neuronal H2-K1/B2m/Tap/Psmb or interferon transcriptional module.
Cross-perturbation matching found no robust Mfsd6 phenocopy: the strongest non-safe positive and negative neighbors had score-vector correlations between −0.011 and 0.031.
Mga perturbation generated a tiny up-only response restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
Stag3 was the repeated MGA-loss marker, rising in both thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic responder groups.
Tasor connected the Mga and Setdb1 signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Mga loss did not derepress the expected broad germline, EMT, or E2F/cell-cycle programs in postnatal neurons.
Represented MAX/MYC and E2F-side perturbations failed to phenocopy Mga in the responding groups.
The top unbiased positive and negative signature neighbors of the near-null Mga surface were rejected by overlap.
Mib1 loss activates a recurrent SREBF2-like sterol/cholesterol-synthesis module in 8 strong neuronal groups, with an additional Hmgcs1-positive branch in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
The Mib1 sterol response is uncoupled from canonical Notch transcription in this postmitotic neuronal screen.
direction_pattern: Notch comparators flat; Mib1 sterol genes up

canonical_summary: Dctn1 was the strongest positive signature neighbor of Mib1, and Rab7, Htt, Marchf6 and Tsc2 also aligned in the same sterol genes.
Direct Srebf2 perturbation is the top inverse signature neighbor of Mib1.
007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut carries a small cortical Mib1 response enriched for Pde4a, Ptprf, Rfx3, Gde1 and Fst rather than the broad subcortical sterol battery.
Mib1-responsive cells did not mount a broad nuclear UPR, ISR, autophagy, lysosomal or proteasome-bounce-back program.
direction_pattern: absent except isolated Nfe2l1 in 155 MB Glut

canonical_summary: Micos13 produced a two-hit, GABA-restricted nuclear response: Zfp687 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Ppm1f down in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with no other FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 21 measured groups.

The postnatal Micos13 transcriptome did not recover a canonical mitochondrial ISR, OXPHOS, or lipid-stress program in the responder cells; Opa1 and Dctn1 induced those programs in the same 054/066 groups, but Micos13 did not.

Represented cristae and mitochondrial-dynamics relatives were not interchangeable with Micos13: Opa1 gave a broad amino-acid/ISR signature, Yme1l1 and Mff were flat, and the direct MICOS subunits were not perturbation targets.
The full-signature data-driven neighbors of Micos13 were numerically weak and did not reproduce the two Micos13 singleton markers in matched cells.
Zfp687 and Ppm1f are exploratory, cell-group-specific sentinels of Micos13 perturbation because no other target in the parquet changed the exact same gene/cell-group feature at FDR<0.10.
Micu1 was transcriptionally silent by the study threshold: every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.

The Micu1 null was not hiding a canonical stress module: ISR, UPR, redox, heat-shock, mitophagy, and proteostasis markers were all absent at FDR<0.10, whereas Opa1 perturbation in the same analysis produced a recurrent ISR/amino-acid response.

Data-driven Micu1 signature neighbors were numerically near zero and were rejected as biological convergence: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score cosine was 0.037 and the strongest negative was -0.024.

The screen could not test true MICU1 same-complex or paralog epistasis because Mcu, Mcub, Micu2, Micu3, Smdt1, Ccdc90a, Slc8b1, and Letm1 were absent as targets; a broader mitochondrial panel was mixed, with Opa1 strong but Ndufs4, Ppargc1a, Park7, and Yme1l1 flat.
Mif is downstream-silent across the entire recovered neuronal surface: no cell group had a non-Mif FDR<0.10 gene despite recurrent negative self-transcript shifts.
The only corrected Mif event was a self-decrease in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, not a downstream module or Ddt-family compensation.
Represented receptor and effector perturbations from the MIF literature failed to form a robust neuronal Mif-like module.
The pre-literature signature-neighbor search nominated only restricted, sub-FDR alignments with mostly flat targets.
Minar2 has a single robust downstream response: Pgbd5 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Pre-literature whole-signature neighbors were almost orthogonal to Minar2 and failed to reproduce the L5 ET Pgbd5 event.
Minar2 loss in postnatal neurons did not generate a Tsc2-like mTORC1 transcriptional response.
Notch receptor perturbations did not converge with Minar2.
Minar2 did not activate or suppress an Srebf2-like sterol-biosynthetic transcriptome.
Young midbrain and cerebellar neuronal groups did not recover the adult Minar2 knockout Parkinson-like phenotype, and 215 MB Dopa was missing.
Mkx loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal null: 21 measured cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were not tested for Mkx.
Canonical Mkx-regulated tenogenic ECM, tendon, TGFβ, and PDL/osteogenic readouts were present in the DE gene universe but were uncoupled from Mkx perturbation in neurons.
Mkx had no meaningful data-driven or curated cross-perturbation neighbor in the matched neuronal universe.
Mlxip perturbation was transcriptomically silent across every recovered juvenile neuronal group.
The canonical MondoA glucose/TXNIP and nutrient-storage transcriptional programs were absent after Mlxip perturbation.
Measurable relatives of the Mondo/Myc/mTOR metabolic neighborhood did not phenocopy Mlxip, and some activated programs that Mlxip did not touch.
Metabolic secondary programs were assay-detectable but not triggered by Mlxip perturbation.
The purely data-driven nearest neighbors of Mlxip were near-zero signatures, not robust convergent perturbations.
Acute postnatal Mmaa loss of function was pan-neuronal FDR-null: 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the missing dopamine group was not tested.
The expected secondary mitochondrial-stress classes were absent: ISR/UPR, mitochondrial chaperone/protease, redox, and autophagy/lysosome genes all had FDR 1.0 in Mmaa cells.
Represented organic-acid catabolic comparators, Pcca, Bckdk, Ivd, Bckdhb, and Dld, were also downstream-null across their matched neuronal groups.

Data-driven Mmaa signature neighbors were near zero and were rejected as biological convergence: two of the top three positive neighbors were safe targets, and the strongest negative cosines were only about -0.02.
Mnt loss failed to derepress a detectable MYC-like growth, ribosome, cell-cycle, or apoptosis program in juvenile postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.
The only upper-layer responder was Trim2 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
The only hippocampal responder was Preb up-regulation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
Sin3a perturbation was broad where Mnt was flat, so the sparse Mnt phenotype does not phenocopy loss of the corepressor scaffold that MNT-family repressors recruit.
Measured MYC, MYCN, MGA, MLXIP, E2F and TRP53-axis perturbations either stayed flat or responded in different cell groups, not the two Mnt responder groups.
The data-driven cross-perturbation neighborhood of Mnt was essentially uncorrelated.

P16 Mnx1 loss-of-function produced a nearly flat neuronal transcriptional surface: only Ell2 in Sst GABA and Nalf1 in midbrain glutamatergic neurons reached FDR<0.10 among 371,807 downstream Mnx1 gene-group tests.
Ell2 up-regulation was a Sst-GABA-specific, Mnx1-unique singleton rather than a recurrent target-wide state marker.

The MB Glut Nalf1 decrease is recurrent across several perturbations rather than Mnx1-specific; Prpf6, Tpr, U2af2, Psmc1 and Cdc40 also down-regulated Nalf1 at FDR<0.10 in the same cell group, whereas Wac up-regulated it.
The unbiased full-surface neighbor scan rejected any strong model-visible phenocopy or anti-phenocopy of Mnx1; the best biological positive and negative correlations were only r=0.033 and r=-0.018.
Neither Mnx1 nor its literature-obvious motor-neuron homeobox and guidance comparators recovered a motor-neuron identity program in the sampled P16 neurons.
Mpc1 is a BH-supported transcriptomic null across the recovered juvenile NeuN+ brain surface.
The postmitotic nuclear transcriptome is also buffered across the mitochondrial pyruvate-entry/PDC neighborhood.
The data-driven Mpc1 neighbors are effectively rejected: the largest full-rank cosines were below 0.03 in absolute value.
The screen separates MPC deficiency from a cell-autonomous basal nuclear disease signature.
Mphosph9-targeting CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal FDR-level transcriptional zero across the sampled juvenile-to-young-adult brain.
Cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Mphosph9 transcriptional neighbor.
Represented ciliary perturbations failed to phenocopy Mphosph9, and the exact KIF24-MPP9-CP110-CEP97 axis was mostly absent as perturbation targets.
The neuronal transcriptomic null does not contradict organismal Mphosph9 phenotypes; it places them outside an acute P16 neuronal RNA mechanism.
Mpl loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 recovered Mpl cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected MPL cytokine-feedback and apoptosis/MAPK transcripts were not induced or repressed in the Mpl surface.
The whole-universe Mpl signature has no meaningful positive or negative neighbor.
Represented hematopoietic-cytokine and MPL-effector comparators also failed to produce a recurrent Mpl-like response in Mpl-matched neuronal groups.
The neuronal null narrows how MPL loss-of-function disease should be mapped onto brain phenotypes.
Mrtfa produced a single thresholded Dnajb5 decrease in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and no other FDR<0.10 downstream genes across 23 groups.
Canonical SRF/MRTF cytoskeletal, immediate-early, and Cdk5/Cdk16-axis genes were tested but absent from the Mrtfa FDR<0.10 surface.
Mrtfa had no convincing convergent or anticorrelated perturbation neighbor, and represented Rho-actin or MAPK/SRF-adjacent targets did not phenocopy Dnajb5 down-regulation in class 008.
Flat Mrtfa responses in NeuN-enriched juvenile neurons should not be read as broad MRTF/SRF safety or dispensability.
Acute Msi1 loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical Msi1-Numb-Notch-Hes transcriptional output was absent from the Msi1 surface and direct Notch1/Notch2 perturbations were themselves nearly flat.
The Msi paralog axis remains the most plausible unresolved buffer: Msi2 was not available as a perturbation target and Msi2 mRNA was not transcriptionally induced after Msi1 perturbation.
A data-driven neighbor search did not recover a meaningful Msi1-like perturbation module.
The medulloblastoma/glioblastoma Msi1 cell-cycle program was not elicited in healthy postmitotic neurons.
Msl2 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 20 measured neuronal cell groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss-of-function.
The all-target Wilcoxon-score neighbor search around Msl2 was flat: the best non-control positive and negative cosines were only 0.056 and -0.0266.
Ogt, the only represented MOF/KAT8-network comparator nominated from the MSL/NSL literature, responded broadly whereas Msl2 was completely downstream-flat.
The sole FDR-controlled Msx2 downstream event was Sbf2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
Msx2 loss did not activate the expected embryonic BMP-MSX, Atoh1, cell-cycle/apoptosis, or osteogenic transcriptional outputs in postmitotic neuronal nuclei.
BMP-receptor and Smad perturbations represented in the screen did not phenocopy the Msx2-to-Sbf2 cerebellar GABA event.
Restricted-signature neighbors of Msx2 were computational but not FDR-convergent; Wdr26 and Ranbp2 showed large opposing CB GABA signatures without sharing the single Sbf2 hit at FDR<0.10.
The postnatal neuronal LoF surface does not model human MSX2 skull phenotypes or Boston-type gain-of-function craniosynostosis.

Mt3 perturbation showed a pan-measured buffered basal phenotype: the Mt3 self-row shifted negative in every recovered cell group, with FDR-significant self-depletion in 3 groups, but no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of 22 measured groups.
Mt3 loss did not activate metallothionein compensation, Nrf2/glutathione redox genes, heat-shock/ISR genes, or lysosomal/autophagy sentinels in any measured neuronal group.
Hippocampal Mt3 perturbation was flat in both recovered hippocampal glutamatergic groups, including the CA3/CA2-FC/DG group.
Neither phenotype-first nor literature-obvious cross-perturbation queries found a convergent Mt3 module in the parquet.
Mtnr1b loss produced a single robust downstream event, Kif21a up-regulation, and it was restricted to 308 CB GABA.
The FDR surface uncoupled Mtnr1b from the expected MT2 Gi/cAMP/CREB and circadian-clock transcriptional programs.
Data-driven signature neighbors did not validate a recurrent Mtnr1b-like program.
The screen argues against treating unstimulated juvenile neuronal MT2 loss as a proxy for MTNR1B diabetes alleles or melatonergic drug exposure.
Mtor loss-of-function produced an FDR-supported RNA response in only 2 of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
