The TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Mtor signature is a five-gene mixed module, with Rims3, Comt, and Pink1 up and Tmed8 and Kndc1 down.

The top positive Mtor neighbors were enriched for UFMylation factors: Uba5 was the #1 global neighbor and Ufc1 was #2, with Uba5 reproducing four of the six Mtor responder genes at FDR<0.10 in the same directions.
Tsc2, an upstream mTORC1 brake, was the strongest anti-neighbor of Mtor and reversed the MB Glut Stmn4 effect.
Canonical same-pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Mtor loss: Rptor and Fkbp1a were FDR-flat across all 23 groups, and Akt3/Pik3cb/Pik3r1/Pik3r2 were flat wherever measured.
Mtor loss did not recover the expected mTORC1 secondary RNA programs: selected translation-initiation, sterol/SREBP, lysosome-autophagy, and UPR/ISR genes never reached FDR<0.10.

The cortical Mtor LoF null refines, rather than contradicts, mTORopathy biology because the human epilepsy genetics are dominated by MTOR gain-of-function or loss of MTOR repressors, not postmitotic partial loss of the kinase.
Acute postmitotic Mttp loss was transcriptionally silent in every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class: all 22 measured groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and no measured Mttp self-transcript.

Mttp did not engage a neuronal sterol-response program, while the represented Srebf2 comparator caused coherent down-regulation of cholesterol-biosynthetic targets including Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Sqle, and Ldlr.
direction_pattern: Mttp absent; Srebf2 sterol genes down

canonical_summary: Mttp did not trigger an ER-stress or ERAD transcriptional signature, whereas Hspa5 perturbation in the same dataset induced Hsp90b1, Nfe2l1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, Herpud1, and Asns in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: Mttp absent; Hspa5 ER-stress genes up

canonical_summary: Whole-profile neighbor search found no meaningful Mttp convergence or opposition: the best full-coverage positive neighbors were Litaf and Ror1 at cosines 0.029 and 0.028, and the strongest full-coverage negative was Las1l at -0.013.
The neuronal null separates MTTP-associated neurologic disease from acute cell-autonomous Mttp action in P16-specified neurons.
Musk produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream hit, Vps4a up-regulation, restricted to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The sampled neuronal Musk response uncoupled from the canonical agrin-LRP4-MuSK-Dok7-AChR and Wnt-AChR modules, and measurable relatives did not phenocopy the 027 Vps4a hit.
Hippocampal-containing Musk nulls did not recover the reported MuSK-dependent cholinergic/learning CREB-C/EBPbeta program under basal postnatal snRNA-seq conditions.
Broad brain-neuronal flatness after Musk CRISPR should not be used to de-risk systemic MuSK inhibition because the major loss-of-function liability is displaced to unsampled skeletal-muscle NMJs.
Acute Myc loss of function is a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null in the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ screen: zero downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in the 22 recovered cell groups.
The expected MYC growth, ribosome-biogenesis, translation, and cell-cycle transcript panel was completely absent from the Myc DE surface.
The represented MYC/MAX-network relatives Mycn, Mnt, and Mga did not phenocopy Myc.
A blind search across all other perturbations found no strong positive or negative Myc signature neighbor.
Acute Mycn loss produced a small but FDR-supported signature only in 053 Sst Gaba neurons.
Sstr1 was the largest Mycn-responsive transcript in Sst neurons and nominates somatostatin-receptor remodeling as the clearest marker of this response.
The screen did not recover the canonical Myc/MYCN proliferative growth program after Mycn perturbation.
Measured MYC-family, MYC-regulator, SHH-GNP, and neuronal developmental comparators did not phenocopy the Sst Mycn signature.
A target-agnostic genome-wide neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Mycn signature neighbor.
Myef2 loss produced a tiny, spatially biased neuronal response: only 8 of 22 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with 17 significant gene-by-cell entries total.
Dzip3, Vbp1, and Ist1 form the recurrent Myef2 module, with Dzip3 significant in six groups, Vbp1 in five, and Ist1 in four.
Myef2 converged with proteasome-subunit perturbations on Dzip3/Ist1 but did not activate a full NRF1 proteasome bounce-back or ER-stress program.
Setd1a, Cdk13, and Uba5 perturbations inverted the Myef2 Dzip3/Ist1/Vbp1 signature in the same matched cell groups.
Myef2 perturbation did not de-repress an MBP/myelin or RUNX1/erythroid program in any measured neuronal group.
Bhlhb9 was selectively down-regulated in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and was the only negative FDR<0.10 gene in the Myef2 response surface.
217 P MY Pineal Glut showed a distinct two-gene up-response of Vbp1 plus Tada1 rather than the Dzip3/Ist1 module.
Myo5a loss was transcriptomically buffered: all 22 measured neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes below FDR 0.10 despite 868 total perturbed nuclei and a median Myo5a self logFC of -0.470.

The strongest self-transcript decreases, in Pvalb Gaba and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, remained self-only and did not induce UPR/ISR, lysosomal-autophagy, or synaptic receptor/scaffold marker transcription.

The represented Griscelli-pathway GTPase Rab27a did not phenocopy Myo5a in neuronal nuclei; Rab27a had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 21 matched groups and an almost-zero Myo5a cosine of -0.003431738.
No meaningful unbiased signature neighbor emerged for Myo5a: the top positive and negative neighbors were Gpx4 and Lrp6, but their global cosines were only 0.035350972 and -0.018517429.
Myo6 did not produce a robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 neuronal cell groups in which it was recovered.
Cltc perturbation triggered endocytic/stress transcriptional signatures in matched neurons whereas Myo6 was flat.

A whole-surface score-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Myo6 transcriptomic neighbor.

Myod1 produced only two permissive-FDR, single-gene signals: Ptprs down in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Atp13a3 down in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Canonical MyoD/MRF skeletal-muscle differentiation genes were not induced or repressed in any measured neuronal group.
Native neuronal MEF2 perturbations, especially Mef2c, responded in the same analysis universe whereas Myod1 remained essentially flat.
Whole-surface nearest-neighbor analysis did not identify a recurrent Myod1-like neuronal module.
The neuronal Myod1 LoF null should not be extrapolated to MYOD1-mutant rhabdomyosarcoma biology.
Myrf produced a singleton robust response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, where Mapk8 was up and no second downstream gene reached FDR<0.10.

Tcf7l2 and Srebf2 were robustly detectable neuronal transcription-factor perturbations where Myrf was flat.
The top data-driven Myrf nominal-signature neighbors were low-cosine and failed robust FDR validation.
The juvenile NeuN+ Myrf perturbation is non-informative for MYRF cardiac-urogenital and diaphragm developmental syndromes.

Postmitotic P16 Naa10 perturbation was a pan-neuronal FDR-level transcriptomic null: 22 measured neuronal groups, 2,123 total matched perturbed nuclei, mixed on-target Naa10 logFC, and zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Data-driven full-vector neighbors classified Naa10 with other flat signatures, not with a mechanistic NatA module: Mpc1, Rorb, and Gli2 were the top real-gene positive neighbors, while the lowest broad real neighbors were the responsive proteasome/translation targets Psmb4, Psmc1, and Eef2.
Acute postnatal Napb CRISPR produced no downstream transcriptomic response in any measured neuronal group.
The synaptic, neurite-guidance, and neurodevelopmental RNA program reported after complete human NAPB loss was absent from the postnatal mouse snRNA response.
Perturbations of represented vesicle/SNARE-neighbor targets did not uncover a shared Napb-like transcriptional module.
A whole-universe signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Napb neighbors.
Napa and Napg were not transcriptionally induced by Napb perturbation.
Nbea was a pan-null nuclear-transcriptome perturbation in every recovered cell group.
The canonical NBEA AMPA/GABAA receptor-trafficking phenotype is uncoupled from detectable receptor, activity, or stress mRNA changes after P16 mosaic loss.
Nbea did not converge with data-driven, BEACH-family, AKAP/PKA, or receptor-subunit comparators in the same cell groups.
NBEA-related LoF biology is unlikely to yield a simple postnatal neuronal snRNA biomarker panel in this assay format.
Ncam1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups despite negative Ncam1 self-transcript movement in every measured group.
The top positive and negative data-driven Ncam1 neighbors have signed-score correlations near zero, with the largest absolute neighbor r only 0.0295.

Ncam1-linked olfactory, plasticity, and neuropsychiatric biology is not accompanied by a stable post-P16 cell-autonomous mRNA signature in this assay.
Ncapd3 perturbation produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream transcript, Amigo1, and only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The dominant Ncapd3 phenotype in P16-edited postmitotic neurons was transcriptomic buffering, not a DNA-damage, p53, ISR/UPR, interferon, or cell-cycle response.
Related SMC/cohesin perturbations did not phenocopy Ncapd3: Smc1a and Stag2 converged on a 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program where Ncapd3 was flat.
Whole-surface data-driven neighbors of the nearly flat Ncapd3 signature were very weak and failed a driver-gene check.
Ncoa1 loss produced a single corrected downstream event, Supt6 up-regulation, restricted to 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rora, Thra, and Crebbp were detectable nuclear-receptor/chromatin perturbations, but Ncoa1 was exactly flat.
The represented p160 paralog Ncoa3 did not phenocopy Ncoa1, and the more plausible SRC-2/Ncoa2 redundancy test was unavailable.

Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Ncoa1 module: the strongest positive and negative score-vector neighbors had absolute correlations below 0.025.
Acute Ncoa3 perturbation produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event, Anapc4 down-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
The expected Ncoa3-Ago2 and NMDAR-subunit transcript readouts were absent from hippocampal-containing glutamatergic groups.
Ncoa3 had no strong positive or negative transcriptome-wide signature neighbor among 1,772 other targets.
Measured p160, nuclear-receptor, Ago, and CBP/p300 comparators did not phenocopy Ncoa3.
The juvenile snRNA null does not rule out adult hippocampal or synaptic liabilities of pharmacologic SRC3 inhibition.
Ndn had no FDR-level downstream transcriptional consequence in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups.

The PWS/MAGE-family comparator Magel2 and imprinted-region comparators Snrpn and Ube3a did not converge with Ndn.
The unbiased cross-perturbation search failed to identify a robust Ndn-like module.
The flat P16 Ndn surface warns that broad correction of Ndn in mature neurons is unlikely to recreate the developmental biology missing in PWS models.

Represented NDUF/NDUFAF complex-I relatives did not converge with the Ndufa10 signature.
Ndufa10 had no meaningful genome-wide positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.

Ndufa11 loss did not induce the expected mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, redox, or mitophagy transcripts in any measured cell group.
The unbiased cross-target neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbors for Ndufa11.
Ndufa12 produced a single formal downstream hit, Dip2b down-regulation, restricted to 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.

Whole-transcriptome distance search found no substantive Ndufa12 signature neighbor.

Measured Complex IV structural or assembly-factor perturbations converged with Ndufa4 on a mostly flat transcriptional surface.
The reported Ndufa4-Homer1/Ccnd2 neuronal proliferation-apoptosis axis was not recovered after P16 perturbation in NeuN+ postmitotic neurons.
Nominal data-driven Ndufa4 signature neighbors had very small cosine scores and failed follow-up as FDR-level convergent modules.
Ndufa6 produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 23 recovered neuronal groups and did not activate a mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, redox, autophagy, or OXPHOS sentinel program.
The only positive downstream Ndufa6 calls were singletons: Inpp4a down in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Cdc40 up in 308 CB GABA.
Respiratory-chain comparators were also sparse and did not phenocopy Ndufa6: 34 Nduf*/Cox*/Sdha/Uqcr* targets yielded only 23 total downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 772 target-cell tests.
Whole-surface data-driven Ndufa6 neighbors were extremely weak and non-phenocopying.
The Ndufa6 null surface should not be read as evidence that neuronal NDUFA6 inhibition is benign.
Acute Ndufa8 loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite uniformly negative Ndufa8 self-logFC values.

Ndufa8's flat surface matches a broader near-null behavior of represented complex-I structural and assembly perturbations: 22 Nduf comparators produced only 18 total downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the Ndufa8-matched groups, and same-family cosines to Ndufa8 were all between -0.005504 and 0.022506.

The P16 mosaic CRISPR result does not phenocopy germline human NDUFA8 complex-I disease at the snRNA level.
Ndufa9 loss produced no FDR-level nuclear transcriptome in any of the 21 measured neuronal groups.
The Ndufa9 null sits within a broader flat landscape for represented complex-I subunits and NDUFAF assembly factors rather than within a hidden complex-I transcriptional module.
A whole-universe Ndufa9 signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptional neighbor.
The screen provides a transcriptomic false-negative warning for NDUFA9 complex-I disease biology.
Ndufaf2 is almost completely transcriptionally buffered in the acute P16 neuronal LoF screen: 22 groups were measured but only 001 L5-6 IT Glut had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The sole Ndufaf2 FDR<0.10 downstream event was Clta down-regulation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
Canonical mitochondrial-stress, antioxidant, ISR, and primary-cilium marker transcripts were not induced after Ndufaf2 perturbation in any measured cell group.
Ndufaf2 did not transcriptionally converge with 21 represented Ndu* complex-I structural or assembly perturbations, including Ndufa12, Ndufaf4, Ndufaf5, Ndufs4, Ndufs2, and Ndufb9.
Unbiased all-gene signature neighbors of Ndufaf2 were extremely weak and failed return-to-data validation by FDR-gene overlap.
Ndufaf4 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Ndufaf4 did not induce the expected mitochondrial retrograde-stress, redox, proteostasis, or OXPHOS-rewiring transcripts.
Represented Complex-I neighbors generally failed to produce off-target transcriptomes, even when Ndufs2 and Ndufs8 achieved significant self-transcript depletion.
The top positive and negative whole-universe signature neighbors of the weak Ndufaf4 surface were all near zero.
Acute Ndufaf5 perturbation was a pan-measured neuronal null: none of 22 recovered neuronal groups had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Directly represented NDUFAF assembly factors and NDUF complex-I subunits were collectively sparse transcriptional responders and did not reveal a shared Ndufaf5-like complex-I stress state.
Ndufaf5 loss did not activate a detectable mitochondrial ISR/UPRmt, mitophagy, or mitochondrial-biogenesis transcript program.
Mitochondrial-context targets Nrf1 and Opa1 produced broad signatures in the same analysis universe, whereas Ndufaf5 and most NDUF targets did not.
Data-driven signature neighbors of Ndufaf5 were only weak nominal correlations and were rejected as biological phenocopies.

Ndufb10 knockdown produced a strongly buffered nuclear transcriptome: all 23 neuron groups were recovered and many groups showed a lower Ndufb10 transcript, yet only one non-target gene reached FDR<0.10 across the entire response surface.
The only robust Ndufb10 downstream transcript was Tbrg4 down-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Literature-obvious complex-I relatives did not converge with Ndufb10 in this postnatal neuronal assay.

The Ndufb10 null surface is specific to respiratory-chain structural subunits and not a failure of this dataset to detect mitochondrial stress, because Opa1 produced a broad ATF4/ISR-rich signature in the same Wilcoxon universe.
The unbiased full-transcriptome neighbors of Ndufb10 were only numerical nearest neighbors, not convergent biology.
Ndufb11 editing in juvenile neurons produced a nearly flat downstream transcriptome: only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups and 371,818 DE rows.
The only real downstream Ndufb11 hit was Clasp1 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA, with no accompanying mitochondrial stress module.
Canonical mitochondrial ISR and retrograde-stress marker transcripts were absent after Ndufb11 perturbation despite being testable in every measured cell group.
Represented complex-I subunits and assembly factors shared the same broad buffering rather than converging on the one Ndufb11 CB GABA Clasp1 hit.
A genome-wide neighbor search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Ndufb11.
Ndufb3 produced an FDR-qualified downstream response only in 191 MB P MY GABA, where Ogdh decreased and Pcbp3 increased.
The stronger 191 MB P MY GABA hit, Ogdh, links the Ndufb3 response to the alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase/TCA node immediately upstream of NADH production for the respiratory chain.
Ndufb3 loss did not activate an ATF4/DDIT3 mitochondrial integrated-stress, UPRmt, antioxidant, or Nduf-subunit compensation program in any recovered cell group.
Ndufb3 did not phenocopy the represented Nduf complex-I subunits or assembly factors in matched cell groups.
A full-universe signature search found no robust Ndufb3 transcriptional neighbor.

Ndufb7 was recovered in every neuronal group but produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 groups, including 0/414 significant tests among selected ISR, mitochondrial chaperone, mitophagy, redox, and mitochondrial-biogenesis markers.
The only FDR<0.10 events in the Ndufb7 target surface were depletion of Ndufb7 itself in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA; both groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Represented NDUF structural and assembly-factor comparators did not form a shared complex-I stress module with Ndufb7: 21 related targets produced only 18 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 16 target-by-cell-group tests, and all full-surface correlations to Ndufb7 were near zero.

Data-driven signature comparison found no robust positive or negative neighbor for Ndufb7; full-surface Pearson correlations among densely measured targets were all between -0.0155 and +0.0362, and top-500 nominal-feature cosines were exploratory.

Ndufb8 transcript depletion was recovered without a recurrent downstream transcriptome: all 22 self rows were negative and six reached self-FDR<0.10, but 20 of 22 measured groups had no downstream DEG and the other two had one DEG each.
The only Ndufb8 downstream DEGs were Prkag2 up in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Puf60 up in 308 CB GABA.
Represented Complex-I subunits and assembly factors did not phenocopy Ndufb8 or one another in this postnatal neuronal CRISPR surface.
Ndufb8 was uncoupled from the Opa1/Lonp1 mitochondrial ATF4-like amino-acid stress program that is readily visible elsewhere in the parquet.
Whole-surface unbiased Ndufb8 signature neighbors were near-zero, unrelated targets and did not reproduce the two FDR-significant singleton genes.
Ndufb9 loss-of-function was a pan-measured neuronal downstream null in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen.

The expected secondary mitochondrial ISR, chaperone/protease, redox, and autophagy transcripts were absent from every Ndufb9 cell group even though the same analysis detects those genes for other perturbations.
Other assayed Nduf/Ndufaf complex-I perturbations also yielded sparse signatures and did not converge with Ndufb9.
An unbiased similarity search placed Ndufb9 in near-zero signature space rather than next to a coherent mitochondrial responder.

Ndufc2 loss produced an almost completely buffered nuclear program: all 23 neuronal cell groups were recovered, but only the 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut class had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and seven other groups showed significant Ndufc2 self-depletion with no downstream response.
The sole robust downstream response was Pdcd6ip/Alix induction in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut nuclei.
Complex-I structural neighbors and disease subunits did not phenocopy the Ndufc2 009 response.
The 009 Pdcd6ip responder did not show the canonical transcriptional consequences expected after strong complex-I dysfunction.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no meaningful Ndufc2 convergence module.

P16 mosaic Ndufs2 CRISPR was almost completely buffered at the transcriptome: only 3 downstream genes crossed FDR<0.10 in 2 of 22 measured neuronal groups, even though the Ndufs2 self transcript was significantly lower in 6 groups.
The only real Ndufs2 downstream calls were cell-type restricted and non-recurrent: Nptx1 was up in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, while Mllt10 and Ppil4 were up in 052 Pvalb Gaba.

Ndufs2 loss did not activate the expected mammalian mitochondrial ATF4/ISR program: Asns, Chac1, Ddit3, Shmt2, Slc7a5, Aldh1l2, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, Herpud1, Lonp1, Mthfd2, mt-Co2, and mt-Cytb stayed below FDR<0.10, while Opa1 perturbation in the same parquet strongly induced many of these genes.

Ndufs2 failed to converge with represented complex-I subunits and assembly factors; 21 Ndufa/Ndufb/Ndufc/Ndufs/Ndufv/Ndufaf comparators had near-zero whole-signature correlations and no FDR overlap with the three Ndufs2 responder genes.
The dataset and Ndufs2+/− mouse literature point to a sharp Ndufs2 dosage threshold: modest Ndufs2 mRNA loss is transcriptionally buffered, but complete brain or dopaminergic deletion is severe.

The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no convincing transcriptomic partner for Ndufs2: Wdr26, Rest, and Copg1 were the top positive neighbors and Safe_target_81, Npy1r, and Cspp1 were the top negative neighbors, but all correlations were |r|≤0.035 and the Ndufs2 responder genes did not reproduce in those targets.
Ndufs4 loss was transcriptionally silent across all 20 recovered neuronal groups: no group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Ndufs4 belongs to a broader Complex I perturbation class that is dominated by on-target mRNA decreases but little downstream transcription.
Canonical ATF4/ISR, mitochondrial chaperone, redox, and mitophagy sentinel genes were absent from the Ndufs4 surface even though the assay could detect an ISR-like signature in another perturbation.
A target-agnostic all-feature neighbor search placed Ndufs4 at the origin of the signature space rather than near a robust convergent or anti-correlated module.

The P16 Ndufs7 perturbation was almost completely transcriptionally buffered: only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 across 23 neuronal groups, and the expected ATF4/mitochondrial-stress marker set was FDR=1.0 in every group.
Ndufs7 produced a CA3-restricted Capn2 induction and no other FDR<0.10 downstream hit.

Expected complex-I relatives did not phenocopy Ndufs7: 21 represented NDUF subunit or assembly perturbations were also sparse, Ndufs4 and Ndufaf5 were fully flat, and the CA3 Capn2 hit was unique to Ndufs7.

The absent Ndufs7 stress program passed a readout gate: Opa1 perturbation induced Asns, Chac1 and Ddit3 in the same screen, while Ndufs7 did not induce any of six mitochondrial-stress markers at FDR<0.10.

Whole-surface signature-neighbor analysis found no strong Ndufs7 neighbor: residual Pearson correlations were only +0.0698 for the top positive and -0.0635 for the top negative comparator with broad group coverage.
Ndufs8 perturbation produced a nearly flat downstream surface: 23 of 23 neuronal groups were measured, the target transcript was lower in every group, but only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10.
The only Ndufs8 downstream hit was Rbm39 up-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Canonical mitochondrial stress, ISR, proteostasis, redox, and compensatory OXPHOS transcripts were not induced by Ndufs8 perturbation in any measured group.
Measured Complex-I relatives failed to converge with Ndufs8, including closest tested Ndufs2, Ndufs7, Ndufs4, Ndufv1, Ndufv2, and Ndufa9 perturbations.
Unbiased all-target score correlations did not nominate a meaningful Ndufs8-like or Ndufs8-opposed module.
Ndufv1 targeting produced a pan-measured downstream transcriptional null: 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in all 22 recovered neuronal groups.

Represented Complex-I N/Q subunits and Nduf accessory or assembly factors also failed to phenocopy one another, with only isolated single-gene hits across their DE surfaces.
The unbiased all-target search yielded no meaningful positive or negative Ndufv1 transcriptional neighbor.
Ndufv2 produced a single robust downstream event: Cdc40 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Postnatal mosaic Ndufv2 perturbation did not induce the expected ISR, mitochondrial proteostasis, redox, mitophagy, or OXPHOS-compensation transcriptome.
Ndufv2 does not phenocopy measured complex-I relatives; Ndufv1, Ndufs2, Ndufs4, Ndufb8, and 17 additional Ndu* complex-I subunit or assembly-factor perturbations were all sparse and non-overlapping.
The top unbiased positive and negative signature neighbors of Ndufv2 had near-zero full-transcriptome cosine similarity.
Nectin1 produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
Nectin1 loss failed to transcriptionally rewire Nectin/Necl, cadherin/catenin, Cdc42/Rac, or synaptic marker transcripts.
Ctnnb1, but not Nectin1, produced a large thalamic transcriptional response in matched cell groups.
Nectin1 had no high-amplitude unbiased positive or negative signature neighbor across the 1772 other measured target perturbations.
The PVRL1 cleft/ectodermal disease axis is displaced from sparse P16 NeuN+ brain perturbation.
Nefh perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of 22 measured cell groups, including three groups with FDR-supported Nefh self-transcript decreases.

Nefl loss produced a near-pan-neuronal buffered nuclear transcriptome: one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in 22 measured groups, despite recurrent negative Nefl self-transcript shifts.
The only downstream FDR<0.10 event was Dync2i1 down-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
Neurofilament subunit perturbations Nefl, Nefm, and Nefh were jointly uncoupled from a robust nuclear DE program in the matched neuronal panel.

Full-vector data-driven Nefm neighbors had near-zero correlations, and the broad negative neighbor Psmb4 diverged strongly from Nefm.
Nek1 produced a single robust downstream hit: Mdm4 was down-regulated only in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, while the other measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The 027 Mdm4 response did not phenocopy measured NEK-family, ciliary, DDR, or ALS-family perturbations.

Acute Nek9 loss of function produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
Measured NEK-family and Eg5/KIF11-axis comparators did not uncover a hidden NEK mitotic module in juvenile neurons.
The strongest data-driven Nek9 signature neighbors were null-like rather than convergent biological responders.

Acute Nfatc3 loss produced no durable downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured juvenile neuronal groups.
Calcineurin-subunit perturbations scored where Nfatc3 was flat, especially Ppp3r1 and Ppp3ca in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The assayed NFAT-family outlier Nfat5 did not phenocopy Nfatc3; it produced only Slc38a2 down-regulation in two groups.
Whole-profile signature-neighbor analysis found no robust convergent or opposing Nfatc3 module.
Basal juvenile neuronal Nfatc3 loss does not recapitulate the glial, injury, aged, or pharmacological calcineurin/NFAT programs emphasized in disease literature.
Nfe2l1 produced a very narrow neuronal response: 5 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 1 in 191 MB P MY GABA, with no downstream FDR signal in the other 19 measured groups.
The canonical NFE2L1 proteasome-bounce-back and aggrephagy transcriptional programs were not recovered after Nfe2l1 loss in the two FDR-positive groups.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature combined Ubc up-regulation with Ogt and Mettl17 down-regulation plus Tspan7 and Plppr4 induction.
The 191 MB P MY GABA response was restricted to Snhg11 down-regulation and did not carry a recognizable NFE2L1 proteostasis, redox, chaperone, or aggrephagy module.
The strongest positive signature neighbors were Uba5 and Ufc1, UFMylation E1/E2 targets that partially shared the Nfe2l1 thalamic Ubc-up and Ogt-down pattern.
Direct proteasome hits Psmb4 and Psmc1 induced hundreds to thousands of DE genes in the same matched groups where Nfe2l1 produced only 5 and 1 downstream genes.
Nfe2l2, Mafg, Vcp, and Hsf1 failed to phenocopy Nfe2l1 in the matched responder groups.
The Nfe2l1 LoF transcriptome in unchallenged postmitotic neurons lacked the biomarkers expected for pharmacologic blockade of NFE2L1 during proteasome inhibition.
Acute postnatal CRISPR loss of Nfe2l2 was transcriptionally silent across the 22 neuronal cell groups in which it was measured.
Canonical NRF2 antioxidant, glutathione, thioredoxin, ferritin, SQSTM1, UPR, and ISR transcripts were all absent from the corrected Nfe2l2 surface.
Full-vector signature search placed Nfe2l2 next to only near-zero neighbors, including flat Safe_target labels, and opposite to Wdr26 only weakly.
The measured NRF2-network perturbations, including Nfe2l1 and Mafg, did not phenocopy Nfe2l2.
The screen argues against a cell-autonomous basal neuronal NRF2 requirement, not against astrocytic or injury-induced NRF2 therapy.

Acute Nfia loss was transcriptionally silent across the recovered postmitotic neuronal taxonomy: all 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the missing 215 MB Dopa group was simply not tested.

The Nfia signature was isolated rather than part of a detectable neuronal NFI/Sox9 module: Nfib and Sox9 were also flat in Nfia-matched groups, while Nfic and Nfix produced only 3 and 1 adjusted genes, respectively, and raw-score cosines to Nfia were all <=0.01750.

The NFIA haploinsufficiency program is not reproduced by deleting Nfia after neurons are born: no adjusted DE was detected for Nfia genome-wide or for astroglial targets Apcdd1, Mmd2, Zcchc24, and Gfap.
Data-driven signature search did not nominate a credible positive or negative Nfia neighbor: the best raw-score cosine was only 0.02370 and the strongest negative cosine only -0.01173.
Nfib loss of function was all-null at whole-transcriptome FDR<0.10 in the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal Perturb-seq surface.
The embryonic E15.5 NfiB-null cortical program—cell-cycle, Notch, axonogenesis and migration genes—was not recapitulated after P16 Nfib editing.
The three NFI paralogs represented in the screen, Nfia, Nfic and Nfix, also lacked any Nfib-like single-gene signature.
An unbiased full-score search did not find a meaningful Nfib molecular neighbor.
The NFIB haploinsufficiency disease axis is not phenocopied by a 3-4 week partial mosaic P16 neuronal perturbation.
NFIB-linked astrocyte and gliogenic marker output is absent from the NeuN-enriched neuronal screen surface.
Acute Nfic loss produced a real but very small three-gene module only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Bambi and Septin5 increased while Dbn1 decreased.
The Bambi increase is uncoupled from a canonical TGFβ/BMP receptor-SMAD loss-of-function signature.
The top data-driven restricted-signature neighbor was Uba5, whereas Thoc1 was the strongest restricted anti-neighbor.
Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix did not phenocopy Nfic in the responding 151 group or elsewhere in the matched screen surface.
155 MB Glut showed significant Nfic mRNA depletion without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

P16 mosaic Nfix loss of function produced a nearly pan-null transcriptional surface in P37-P44 NeuN+ neurons: only 1 of 388,023 downstream tests passed FDR<0.10, and no canonical astroglial, neural-progenitor, intermediate-progenitor or neuroblast marker did.
The only adjusted Nfix downstream hit was lower Cwc27 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA nuclei.

The represented NFI paralogs did not phenocopy Nfix: Nfia and Nfib were completely flat, while Nfic produced a separate three-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature and did not regulate Cwc27 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Malan/Sotos-overgrowth differential genes represented in the screen did not converge with Nfix: Nsd1, Setd2 and Fbn1 had near-zero all-score cosines to Nfix and no Cwc27 overlap.
The data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Nfix were numerically negligible and failed direct overlap tests.
Nfkb1 gave 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups, with one weak NP-CT-L6b-OB crest just above threshold.
Represented canonical NF-κB/TNF/TLR comparators phenocopied the Nfkb1 flat state rather than revealing a hidden related-target response.
Canonical NF-κB feedback, cytokine, chemokine, and survival-output genes were absent from the Nfkb1 DE surface.
The all-zero Nfkb1 robust signature had no signed FDR<0.10 neighbor, while Psmb4, Psmc1, Tpr, and Uba5 were the strongest divergent responders in the same 22 cell groups.
Nfs1 produced no transcriptome-wide downstream DE in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Direct Fe-S comparators represented in the parquet also failed to form a coherent ISC-loss signature.
Iron-starvation, ferroptosis/redox, and mitochondrial ISR sentinel RNAs were not induced after Nfs1 perturbation.
Acute Nfx1 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered mouse neuronal group.
The canonical NFX1 MHC-II/IFN, TERT, and NF-kB programs were absent rather than weakly derepressed in Nfx1-perturbed neurons.
A full-surface neighbor search did not reveal a robust Nfx1-like or anti-Nfx1 module.
Nfyc produced a real but very small, entirely down-regulated signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Nfyc loss did not recover an NF-Y/ATF6 ER-chaperone, p62, or ISR transcriptional program in any measured cell group.
The nominal Nfyc signature had only weak cross-perturbation neighbors, and those neighbors did not phenocopy the restricted Nfyc response at FDR<0.10.
Ngfr produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
Ngfr's nearest data-driven signature neighbors had essentially zero cosine similarity and did not reveal a coherent Ngfr module.
Represented Trk, Sort1, NgR/LINGO1, JNK, NF-kappaB, and death-receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Ngfr.
The pan-null Ngfr surface should not be used to deprioritize p75NTR modulation in injury or Alzheimer-like settings.
Nhs loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal groups.
The expected NHS/WAVE/Arp2/3 and ZO-1 junction axes were transcriptionally silent after Nhs perturbation.
Unbiased cross-target similarity found no meaningful Nhs transcriptional neighbors.
Nin-targeted CRISPR produced no robust downstream DE in any of the 22 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The expected embryonic progenitor-depletion and differentiation-marker signature was absent from the postnatal Nin surface.
Dctn1, a dynein/dynactin microtubule-transport comparator, strongly induced sterol and cholesterol biosynthesis genes where Nin was flat.
Tuba1a loss elicited compensatory up-regulation of other tubulin isotypes in two neuronal groups, but Nin loss did not.
The pre-literature signature-neighbor search found only very weak positive or negative neighbors for Nin.
Represented centrosome, ciliary, microcephaly, and microtubule comparators mostly failed to phenocopy Nin or each other in postmitotic neurons.
Acute postmitotic Nipa1 loss-of-function produced no FDR-supported nuclear RNA response in any of the 22 cell groups in which it was recovered.
The expected NIPA1-BMPRII-BMP/SMAD transcriptional branch was not detectably activated after Nipa1 perturbation.
Nipa1 did not acquire the signature of its obvious Mg-transport, 15q11.2, BMP, or hereditary-spastic-paraplegia comparators.
The Nipa1 CRISPR loss-of-function signature lacks the ER-stress/UPR component reported for HSP missense alleles.
The data-driven neighbor search found no robust Nipa1-like target state.
Acute Nkain2 loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a cell-type-selective DEG module.
Nkain2 did not phenocopy represented Na,K-ATPase alpha-subunit perturbations, especially the Atp1a3 thalamic response.
The human NKAIN2/TCBA1 developmental-disorder link is not reproduced as a broad juvenile postmitotic transcriptional program.
Acute P16 Nkx2-1 loss yielded one total FDR<0.10 downstream gene across 22 measured neuronal classes rather than a Lhx6/Nrp2/Pomc fate-collapse program.
Med13 down-regulation was the single Pvalb-restricted transcript that survived FDR<0.10 after Nkx2-1 perturbation.
The expected MGE markers Lhx6, Lhx8, Nrp2, Pvalb, Sst and Chat, and hypothalamic markers Pomc, Isl1, Prdm12 and Tbx3, were measured but did not move at FDR<0.10.
Nkx2-1 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, and measured NK-homeobox or ventral-patterning comparators did not phenocopy its Pvalb Med13 hit.
Nkx2-5 produced a sparse, positive-only neuronal response restricted to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, with exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in each group.
The canonical Nkx2-5 cardiac progenitor, myocardial, conduction, and spleen-module genes were absent or completely flat in the neuronal Nkx2-5 DE surface.
Mef2c had a broad cortical neuronal response while Nkx2-5 and other cardiogenic relatives failed to reproduce either Nkx2-5 singleton feature in matched groups.
Unbiased two-feature signature neighbors of Nkx2-5 were only sub-threshold and no other target made the B4galnt1 or Fmnl1 feature significant at FDR<0.10.
The postnatal NeuN+ brain screen localizes Nkx2-5's LoF liability away from broad autonomous neuronal transcription and toward its established non-neuronal developmental lineages.
Nkx3-1 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured juvenile neuronal cell groups.
The genome-wide Nkx3-1 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Represented NK-family and prostate-axis perturbations did not uncover an Nkx3-1-like neuronal program.
Expected prostate epithelial and NKX3.1/MYC target programs were not recovered in the Nkx3-1 neuronal DE surface.

Nkx6-2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured P16-perturbed neuronal cell group; 22 groups were assayed, all had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.
Nkx6-2 loss in the sampled neurons did not mobilize oligodendrocyte/myelin markers or core Myrf/Sox10-like maturation programs.

The unbiased Nkx6-2 signature search produced only tiny whole-transcriptome cosines, with safe targets among the closest positive neighbors and no shared FDR<0.10 downstream genes for the top non-safe neighbors.

Measured literature-obvious relatives in oligodendrocyte and Shh/ventral-patterning networks were themselves flat or single-gene responders in the same neuronal groups and did not phenocopy Nkx6-2 or each other.
Nlgn3 loss produced a pan-surface downstream transcriptomic null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Literature-obvious Nlgn3 neighbors did not phenocopy Nlgn3, and most were themselves transcriptionally sparse.
The unbiased Nlgn3 signature-neighbor search found no real convergent or inverse module.
Nlgn3 was uncoupled from transcriptional programs elicited by NMDA-receptor and mTOR-pathway perturbations in the same screen universe.
Acute neuronal Nlgn3 loss is a poor transcriptomic proxy for R451C autism and paracrine glioma mechanisms.
Nobox produced one FDR<0.10 downstream change, down-regulation of Atp2a2, confined to 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Postnatal neuronal Nobox loss did not engage the oocyte and early-folliculogenesis regulon.
The represented ovarian-network perturbations Figla, Sohlh1, Foxl2, and Kit were also flat across the 22 Nobox-matched neuronal groups.
The data-driven Nobox neighbor scan nominated no robust convergent or opposing perturbation module.
The Atp2a2 singleton under Nobox is uncoupled from the stress response seen after direct Atp2a2 perturbation.
Nod2 CRISPR loss-of-function produced no significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Nod2 perturbation did not induce or repress the expected MDP/NF-kB, cytokine, interferon, inflammasome, or autophagy panel in any measured neuronal group.
Canonical represented NOD2 relatives and pathway neighbors did not produce a shared neuronal signature with Nod2.
The apparent top data-driven Nod2 neighbors were rejected as subthreshold restricted-signature artifacts rather than biological convergence or divergence partners.

Nop56 loss produced a narrow postnatal neuronal response: all 23 groups were measured, but only 4 had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene and 39 of 44 downstream DE rows were concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature is dominated by a negative RNA-processing/SR-splicing branch—Rsrp1, Ddx17, Srsf5, Srsf11, Ddx5, Srsf6, Pabpn1, Clk4, Srrm2, Fus, and Hnrnpu—and this branch converges with Tnpo3 perturbation.
Snu13 was the only queried core box C/D snoRNP transcript induced at FDR<0.10 after Nop56 perturbation, and the induction was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The top robust positive neighbors of the Nop56 signature were Uba5 and Ufc1, the E1 and E2 enzymes of UFMylation, with 34 and 21 significant same-direction overlaps among the 44 Nop56 anchor rows.
Nop56 did not activate a canonical nucleolar-stress, p53/apoptosis, ISR, or autophagy transcriptional program; Hspa5 and Ero1b instead decreased in the main 151 responder.
Hnrnpu was the strongest robust anti-neighbor: Hnrnpu perturbation reversed 12 Nop56 anchor genes, including Srsf11, Tcea2, Dbn1, Slc17a6, Syt1, and Cdk5r1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also showed a bidirectional synaptic and vesicle/endomembrane branch, with Slc17a6, Cdk5r1, Rims3, Syt1, Rab14, and Rab2a up while Dbn1, Prrt1, and Lgi3 were down.
Only Tcea2 and Dbn1 recurred across Nop56 responders, appearing as significant decreases in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The 155 MB Glut response was real but extremely sparse, limited to down-regulation of Slf2 and Ncapd3 at FDR<0.10.
012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut contained a single Kdm4b induction and no second FDR<0.10 gene.
110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed significant Nop56 mRNA depletion but no downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The SCA36-relevant cerebellar bin, 308 CB GABA, had no Nop56 downstream transcriptome in juvenile CRISPR loss-of-function cells.
The literature-obvious nucleolar 60S comparator Rbm28 was present but rejected: it produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 measured groups and did not overlap the Nop56 anchor in 151.
Nos1ap produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic event: Zcchc14 was down-regulated only in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
Nos1ap loss did not phenocopy NMDAR-subunit loss in the postnatal snRNA-seq readout.
Cpe and Syn1, two represented NOS1AP pathway partners, fired weakly in the same 009 cell group but on Aff3 and mt-Nd1 rather than on Zcchc14.
Score-space neighbors around Nos1ap were extremely weak, indicating that the target is isolated rather than part of a strong model-visible transcriptional module.
The neuronal loss-of-function surface should not be read as refuting disease biology driven by CAPON overexpression, isoform regulation, or cardiac NOS1AP genetics.
Notch1 loss produced a single robust transcriptional event: Camk2g was up-regulated only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The canonical NICD1/RBPJ/MAML transcriptional program was not recovered after Notch1 perturbation in any measured neuronal group.
Represented core Notch-pathway perturbations did not converge with Notch1 in L5 ET neurons.
Mib1, the Notch-ligand E3 ligase comparator, diverged from Notch1 and drove a sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis program in Pvalb, hypothalamic, and caudal neuron groups.
The model-visible screen offered no robust data-driven Notch1 signature neighbor.
NOTCH1 disease and drug logic should not be back-projected from this mature-neuron screen onto progenitor or cancer contexts.
Notch2 loss of function produced a whole-surface neuronal null: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Canonical Notch-output and proneural genes were measured but not regulated by Notch2: Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, Dtx1, Rbpj, Maml1, Ascl1, Neurog2, Neurod1 and Neurod2 all had FDR=1.0 in the Notch2 surface.
A Notch-pathway neighbor was active where Notch2 was silent: Mib1 perturbation, but not Notch2, drove a recurrent up-regulated SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthesis signature in nine neuronal groups.

The obvious receptor and cleavage comparators did not phenocopy each other: Notch1 and Notch4 yielded only one or two isolated DEGs, Dll1, Adam10 and Psen1 were flat, and Fbxw7 had a single TH-associated DEG, whereas Notch2 was flat in all matched groups.

Genome-wide signature-neighbor analysis placed Notch2 in the null cloud: the strongest positive score correlations were Fxr1, Npy5r and Kcnh1, and the strongest biological negative correlations were Fbxo11, Atp6v1e1 and Timmdc1, but all score correlations were tiny in magnitude.
The acute neuronal Notch2 null does not phenocopy known NOTCH2 developmental or allelic disease mechanisms.
Notch4 loss produced a single Mpc2-up signature in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
A borderline but FDR<0.10 Slc6a8 decrease was the only Notch4 response in 155 MB Glut.
The two singleton responses were uncoupled from a HES/HEY Notch transcriptional program.
Neither unbiased neighbors nor measured Notch-pathway relatives phenocopied Notch4.
The neuronal Notch4 null surface redirects Notch4 follow-up to endothelial and developmental assays.
Npas3 was transcriptomically buffered across the recovered mature neuronal surface: 22 measured cell groups and 371,818 rows yielded 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The Fgfr1/Vgf/neurosignaling program expected from NPAS3 literature was not recovered after acute Npas3 perturbation.
Measured bHLH-PAS relatives split into a flat ARNT/AHR/HIF branch versus an active CLOCK/BMAL1 circadian branch, with Npas3 in the flat class.
The unbiased cross-perturbation search found only near-zero Npas3 signature correlations, so no hidden recurrent transcriptional module was missed by the canonical NPAS3 priors.
Npr2 loss of function produced no FDR-supported basal transcriptional state in any measured P37-P44 central neuronal group.
Canonical CNP/GC-B-cGMP and chondrocyte FGFR3-MAPK biology did not appear as a hidden neuronal DE module, and represented pathway-adjacent perturbations did not phenocopy Npr2.
The apparent top positive and negative whole-surface signature neighbors of Npr2 were near-zero correlations, so the data-driven neighbor search rejected a coherent Npr2-like module.

Postnatal Npsr1 loss produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream events, both single-gene up-regulations in glutamatergic limbic or hypothalamic classes: Gpt2 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Hemk1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
direction_pattern: Gpt2 and Hemk1 up; all other measured groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes except the weak 145 class

canonical_summary: The expected NPSR1 Gs/Gq-Ca2+/cAMP-CREB axis was not recovered as RNA after basal CRISPR loss of Npsr1. Gnas, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Pde1c, Pde4b and Pde4d perturbations were also flat in the two Npsr1 responder classes, and Npsr1 did not induce immediate-early/CREB-adjacent genes.
direction_pattern: expected CREB/immediate-early RNA module absent after Npsr1 LoF

canonical_summary: Npsr1 did not trigger a detectable stress, ISR, proteostasis, or synaptic-collapse response in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, even though least-concordant proteasome perturbations Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced broad 110 signatures.
direction_pattern: broad proteasome/ISR RNA response after Psmb4/Psmc1 but not after Npsr1

canonical_summary: Npy1r loss did not remodel the basal transcriptome of any recovered neuronal class.
Npy2r and Npy5r were also basal-flat rather than revealing a hidden NPY-receptor RNA module.
Npy1r did not converge with Gi/o-adenylyl-cyclase perturbations.
The unbiased target-neighbor search found no meaningful transcriptomic module around Npy1r.
Activity and compensation sentinels were not induced after Npy1r perturbation.
Npy2r loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had only a subthreshold Insig1 candidate.
The measurable NPY receptor paralogs Npy1r and Npy5r also lacked downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and their score-vector correlations with Npy2r were near zero.
A universe-wide search found no meaningful Npy2r signature neighbor: the strongest Pearson correlation was only 0.033 and the strongest anticorrelation was only -0.019.
Canonical Gi/o effectors and appetite-axis perturbations failed to phenocopy Npy2r, and Npy/Pomc were not induced in broad hypothalamic-enriched Npy2r groups.
Postnatal mosaic Npy5r loss did not produce a robust nuclear RNA signature in any of the 19 recovered neuronal groups.
The represented NPY receptor targets Npy1r, Npy2r, and Npy5r were all single-perturbation transcriptomic nulls.
The strongest empirical Npy5r signature neighbors were very low-cosine and failed robust overlap tests.
Selective Y5 loss is unlikely by itself to remodel broad juvenile neuronal transcriptomes in a stable anti-orexigenic direction.
An acute Nr1d1 perturbation generated real FDR-level transcriptional signal only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 response contains the expected de-repression of clock-loop and clock-output genes.
Nr1d1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coupled the clock signature to synaptic vesicle, calcium, glutamate-receptor, cAMP, and ion-channel genes.
The Nr1d1 151 signature includes axonal and cytoskeletal remodeling rather than a pure clock-only transcriptome.
Metabolic, lipid/cholesterol, and mitochondrial transcripts were recruited into the thalamic Nr1d1 program.
Nr1d1 perturbation induced a Pdgfa/Col4a1/Col4a2 secreted-matrix program while repressing the matrix inhibitor Timp3 and Agrn.
Bmal1 was the strongest data-driven positive neighbor of Nr1d1 despite opposite positions in the core feedback loop.
Rora, an RORE activator, opposed a larger portion of the Nr1d1 thalamic signature than other circadian paralogs or subunits did.
Most measurable circadian relatives failed to phenocopy Nr1d1 in the thalamic responder group.
A ligandable clock receptor can drive a cell-type-restricted thalamic synaptic/metabolic program rather than a uniform pan-neuronal clock reset.
Nr1d2 loss produced real downstream DE in only three of the 22 measured neuronal groups: Pvalb GABA, TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic, and P MY Pineal glutamatergic cells.
The dominant Nr1d2 loss response was up-regulation of its paralog Nr1d1 in every FDR-supported responder.
Nr1d1 was the top data-driven Nr1d2 neighbor, but acute Nr1d2 loss captured only a small thalamic subset of the Nr1d1 program.
The 151 thalamic bin could mount large Bmal1, Rora, Clock, Cry2, and Nr1d1 clock-network signatures, but Nr1d2 loss in the same bin stopped after Nr1d1 plus Cacna2d3.
Cacna2d3 up-regulation nominated a thalamic calcium-channel output shared by Nr1d2 loss, Nr1d1 loss, and Bmal1 loss.
Nr1d2 responders did not show a broad secondary stress, proteostasis, unfolded-protein, autophagy, or synaptic-collapse program at FDR<0.10.
Isoform-selective REV-ERBβ inhibition in mature neurons may be self-limited by Nr1d1 feedback rather than producing a full REV-ERB loss state.
Nr1h2 loss produced a complete postmitotic neuronal transcriptional null: no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of the 23 measured groups.
The expected LXR cholesterol-efflux and sterol-regulatory transcripts were absent from the Nr1h2 DE surface.
Represented LXR/RXR pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Nr1h2 and did not expose a hidden neuronal LXR/RXR module.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search itself failed to nominate a robust Nr1h2 module.
Nr1h4 loss of function was a pan-neuronal non-responder: every recovered P16-P37 NeuN+ group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Represented RXR, NR1H/LXR, PPAR, and hepatic FXR-cofactor perturbations did not phenocopy Nr1h4; all matched cosines were ≤0.031 in magnitude and nearly all were FDR-flat.
The screen did not recover a basal neuronal FXR-SHP axis, even though agonist studies have reported functional neuronal FXR.
A whole-universe signature search found no convincing positive or negative Nr1h4 module; the best cosine neighbors were extremely small and had zero shared FDR-significant genes.
Nr1h5 produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
Nr1h5 loss did not perturb the expected sterol, cholesterol-biosynthesis, LXR-efflux, or enterohepatic-FXR marker transcripts.
Literature-obvious NR1H/RXR relatives did not converge with Nr1h5 in the matched neuronal groups.
No model-visible target had a meaningful positive or negative whole-surface signature correlation with Nr1h5.
Nr1i2 loss produced a robust but extremely narrow neuronal signature: Akr1a1 increased and Nup214 decreased only in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Akr1a1 was the sole FDR-significant up-regulated detoxification gene after Nr1i2 perturbation.
Nup214 repression points to a nuclear-pore/export axis as the only FDR-significant down-regulated component of the Nr1i2 neuronal response.
Nr1i2 loss did not recover a coordinated canonical PXR-RXR CYP/ABC efflux program in any sampled neuronal group, including the 059 responder.
Canonical xenobiotic-receptor relatives and RXR partners did not phenocopy Nr1i2 in the matched neuronal DE surface.
The full Nr1i2 signature had no strong model-wide positive or negative neighbor.
Nr1i3 loss produced no corrected downstream DE gene in any measured NeuN+ neuronal cell group.
The hepatic and blood-brain-barrier CAR detoxification program was absent from the Nr1i3 neuronal DE surface.
Nr1i3 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the whole perturbation universe.
PXR/VDR/RXR/AHR-family comparators were represented but did not phenocopy Nr1i3.
Nr2c1 loss of function produced a single robust downstream transcriptional hit: Camta2 up-regulation restricted to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
The LSX GABA Camta2 hit did not expand into a measurable calmodulin, CaMKII, calcineurin, or Camta1 RNA module.
The closest NR2C paralog Nr2c2 did not phenocopy Nr2c1: Nr2c2 triggered glutamatergic down-regulation in 017/151/155 groups but no LSX Camta2 response.
Nr2c1 LoF in P16-to-P37/44 neuronal brain did not recover the known retinal, olfactory, or erythroid TR2/TR4 programs.
A data-driven pre-literature neighbor search found no robust Nr2c1-like perturbation module.
Nr2c2 produced a sparse, all-downstream-down response in only 3 of 22 measured cell groups: CA3/CA2/DG glutamatergic, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
Ccdc84 was the lone repeated downstream transcript, down in all three Nr2c2 responder groups.
The strongest responder, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, coupled Ccdc84 loss to decreases in Stxbp2, Qsox2, Miga1, and Dclre1c.
The expected NR2C paralog Nr2c1 did not phenocopy Nr2c2, and neither did other represented NR2/RXR/RAR nuclear receptors.
Exact-overlap scanning kept Yy1, Bptf, and Ctcf as partial same-direction comparators, whereas Rnpc3 inverted the recurrent Ccdc84 output.
The pre-literature full-vector neighbors Fgfr2 and Kcnh1 were rejected as meaningful Nr2c2 comparators.
Acute Nr2e1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream DE genes in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
The canonical TLX p21/PTEN, glial, stem-cell, cell-cycle, and Wnt marker panel was absent after Nr2e1 perturbation.
Nr2e1 did not phenocopy measured NR2-family, Wnt/TCF, or progenitor-related perturbations that produced sparse-to-strong FDR responses in the same 22 cell groups.
The model-visible whole-universe signature search found no robust positive or negative Nr2e1 neighbor.
The screen supports TLX context restriction for target modulation: postmitotic normal neurons did not activate the canonical TLX program after acute Nr2e1 loss.
Nr2e3 acute postnatal loss of function produced no accepted downstream transcriptional response in any recovered brain neuronal group.
The canonical retinal rod/cone Nr2e3 program was completely absent: phototransduction and S-cone/rod sentinel RNAs stayed at FDR=1.0.
A pre-literature global neighbor search found no meaningful Nr2e3 phenocopy or antagonist.
The Nr2e3 null is family- and circuit-specific rather than a universal failure of nuclear-receptor or transcription-factor perturbations.

Nr2f1 loss produced a sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response: only Ell in 008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic neurons and Sorl1/Sema7a in 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons crossed FDR<0.10.
The more robust Nr2f1 responder class, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showed Sorl1 induction and Sema7a repression.
Nr2f1 perturbation decreased Ell in 008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic neurons.
The expected cortical arealization and projection-neuron marker program was absent in acute P16 Nr2f1-edited cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Tbr1, but not Nr2f1, retained a small cortical transcription-factor signature in the same acute P16 assay.
Neither the top algorithmic Nr2f1 score neighbors nor represented nuclear-receptor/cortical-patterner comparators phenocopied the Nr2f1 signature.
A P16 acute mosaic Nr2f6 loss-of-function did not elicit a robust downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal group.
The canonical Ear2/Nr2f6 locus-coeruleus and forebrain-clock readouts were expected from germline mutants but absent from this postnatal neuronal screen.
The screened COUP-TF paralog Nr2f1 did not phenocopy Nr2f6: the matched score-space correlation was r=0.003 and the two targets shared no FDR<0.10 genes.
Postnatal Phox2a and Phox2b perturbations, the LC-specification factors downstream of embryonic Nr2f6, also failed to converge with Nr2f6.
Data-driven signature search placed Nr2f6 in correlation noise, not in a recognizable multi-target transcriptional module.
The neuronal null should not be read as a failed Nr2f6 biology assay for the therapeutic immune-checkpoint axis, because that axis lives in T lymphocytes that were not profiled.
Juvenile postmitotic Nr3c1 loss produced only 5 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 371796 tests and only 3 effect cell groups.
Nr3c1 perturbation selectively up-regulated the orphan nuclear receptor Nr2f1 in hypothalamic GABAergic neurons.
Nr3c1 loss up-regulated Mapk8ip1/Jip1 in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons.
The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c response to Nr3c1 contained Axin2 up-regulation with Aifm3 and Ptprm down-regulation.
Canonical glucocorticoid-response and AP-1/NF-kappaB readouts were absent after Nr3c1 perturbation.
Measured steroid-receptor paralogs and GR chaperone/cofactor targets did not phenocopy Nr3c1.
Rora, Nr1d1, and Klf9 perturbations produce strong thalamic signatures where Nr3c1 remains minimal and nonconvergent.
Nr3c2 loss produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal group at the P37-44 endpoint.
The hippocampal MR target-gene program reported for forebrain MR knockout was not recovered after sparse postnatal Nr3c2 perturbation.
Nr3c2 had no robust data-driven signature neighbor; even the nearest whole-surface correlations were approximately zero.
The literature-obvious steroid-receptor relatives represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Nr3c2 and did not reveal a common MR/GR transcriptional module.
Nr4a1 loss-of-function produced no FDR-gated downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
The expected hippocampal NR4A plasticity targets and immediate-early transcripts were not recovered downstream of Nr4a1 perturbation.
The represented NR4A paralog Nr4a3 was almost as flat as Nr4a1, and no Nr4a2 or Nr4a3 compensatory transcript was induced after Nr4a1 loss.
Represented CREB/AP-1/EGR pathway neighbors did not phenocopy Nr4a1 in the matched screen.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of the full Nr4a1 score vector were numerical artifacts of a flat surface, not biological convergence or opposition.
A basal sparse LoF snRNA signature is the wrong biomarker for NR4A pro-memory pharmacology.
Nr4a3 produced one FDR<0.10 downstream hit, Xpo6 down-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 21 measured groups.
The sole robust DEG nominates Xpo6, not Bdnf/Fosl2/Pak6 or a broader stress module, as the candidate marker of Nr4a3 loss in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.

The Nr4a3 217 signature was empirically isolated: no other tested target significantly repressed Xpo6, and the best all-gene positive and negative neighbors were weak and failed to share the FDR Xpo6 hit.
Nr4a1 and RXR/NCOA perturbations did not phenocopy Nr4a3 in the basal neuronal screen.

CREB/CBP and immediate-early comparator perturbations were separable from Nr4a3: Creb1 and Crebbp produced measurable signatures in thalamic/midbrain groups where Nr4a3 was null or weak, whereas Fosl2, Egr2, and Kdm6b did not converge with Nr4a3.
Postmitotic mosaic Nr5a1 loss produced a near-pan-neuronally buffered transcriptional surface: 22 of 23 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the 23rd had only one.
The only FDR-level Nr5a1 downstream gene was Reep2 up-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
The represented NR5A paralog Nr5a2 and broader nuclear-receptor comparators did not phenocopy Nr5a1 in matched neuronal surfaces.
No data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor showed meaningful convergence with Nr5a1.
Nr5a2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered NeuN+ neuronal group.
The expected NR5A2–Prox1 neurogenic program was absent from the broad hippocampal/DG glutamatergic groups.
Nr5a2 loss did not reproduce hypothalamic Agrp/Kiss1 neuropeptide regulation in the broad hypothalamic neuronal groups.
β-catenin/TCF perturbations were detectable where Nr5a2 was flat.
All-transcriptome data-driven neighbors of Nr5a2 were negligible and were rejected as biological convergence.
The expected nuclear-receptor relatives and reprogramming partner did not phenocopy Nr5a2 through a strong shared postmitotic neuronal module.
Nr6a1 perturbation produced one robust downstream transcript in the entire measured surface: Trim23 was down in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Nr6a1 had no reproducible cross-perturbation module in postnatal neurons.
P16 Nr6a1 loss was uncoupled from the embryonic Hox, pluripotency, and isthmic-organizer programs that define germline Nr6a1 biology.
The hippocampal CREB-BDNF literature did not translate into a basal CA1/DG transcriptional response after mosaic Nr6a1 loss.
Represented Nr6a1 developmental comparators were also nearly silent, supporting a shared postmitotic state mismatch rather than an Nr6a1-specific failed guide set.
Acute postmitotic Nrcam perturbation was broadly buffered on the nuclear transcriptome despite direct measurement of the target transcript.
The only cortical FDR<0.10 downstream event was a Crebbp decrease in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
The only thalamic responder was 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Letm2 increased as a one-gene signature.
Represented L1-family, neuropilin, ankyrin, and node/paranode comparators did not phenocopy Nrcam in matched cell classes.
The top whole-universe signed-score neighbors of Nrcam were statistically very weak rather than a recurrent module.
Genes from the expected Sema3F/NrCAM, L1-CAM, ankyrin, and postsynaptic scaffold neighborhoods were not transcriptionally recruited after Nrcam loss.
Acute Nrf1 loss caused a selective 7-of-22 measured-group response, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
Cdc7/Kifc2 down-regulation with Pigp/Itfg2 up-regulation formed a recurrent empirical Nrf1 core across the smaller and larger responders.
Nrf1 perturbation captured a small mitochondrial strand but failed to recover a broad Tfam/Tfb1m/Tfb2m, COX, Gria2, Nos1, or Gabrb1 program.
Responder groups showed down-regulation of RNA-processing and DNA-maintenance-associated transcripts including Cdc7, Tia1, Rbm14, Srrm2, Srsf11, Prmt2, Ercc6, Xrcc1, and Xpa.
Nrf1 responders also carried a vesicle/endolysosomal/trafficking branch marked by Nrsn2, Pcsk1n, Snrpn, Tbc1d24, Sgcb, Bbs2, Sbf2, Vps13a, Zfyve16, Ccdc93, Tmed4, Slc36a4, Sumf2, and Psap.
Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the top two positive Nrf1 signature neighbors, followed by Ogt, Prpf6, and Setd1a.
The mitochondrial relatives Ppargc1a, Esrra, and Esrrg did not phenocopy Nrf1.
Nfe2l1 and Nfe2l2 failed to reproduce the official-symbol Nrf1 signature.
No measured perturbation produced a strong inverse Nrf1 signature; the top negative neighbors Hnrnpc, Zbtb7a, and Hnrnpu had only weak, mixed anti-overlap.
Nrg1 loss produced one robust downstream event, Top1 up-regulation, in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and nowhere else.
Nrg1 was almost completely buffered as a cell-autonomous postnatal neuronal transcriptional perturbation.
The measured neuregulin and ErbB relatives did not phenocopy Nrg1, and Nrg1 did not phenocopy their weak DE surfaces.
Canonical immediate-early, GABA-interneuron marker, ErbB-receptor, and myelin transcripts were absent from the Nrg1 FDR surface.
Postnatal Nrg2 loss produced an exceptionally sparse cell-autonomous nuclear response: five FDR<0.10 downstream genes in only two of 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The only multi-gene Nrg2 response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Kcnk4, Notum, Dlk2, and Ccdc141 were all increased at FDR<0.10.
Noc3l was the sole FDR<0.10 cortical hit, up in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut after Nrg2 perturbation.
Grin1 loss opposed the Nrg2 thalamic signature: all four Nrg2-up genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were significantly down after Grin1 perturbation.
NRG-family and receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Nrg2: Nrg1, Nrg3, Erbb3, Erbb4, and Adam10 were flat or nearly flat and had no FDR-level overlap with Nrg2 in the Nrg2-responsive groups.
Apparent positive nominal neighbors were not robust phenocopies: Kcnq2, Gipr, Slc32a1, Gabrg2, and Timp3 shared no FDR<0.10 Nrg2 hit in 007 or 151.
Nrg2, Erbb4, and the NRG-like comparators were almost silent in snRNA despite literature linking NRG2/ErbB4 to rapid channel trafficking and dopamine physiology.

Nrg3 CRISPR loss after P16 produced a target-wide absence of downstream differential expression: all 23 measured neuronal cell groups had 0 non-Nrg3 genes at FDR<0.10, even though the Nrg3 transcript itself trended downward in every group and reached FDR<0.10 in three groups.

The flat Nrg3 surface is shared by the directly measured neuregulin/ErbB relatives: Nrg1 and Nrg2 produced only isolated one-cell-group signatures, while Erbb3 and Erbb4 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

An unbiased screen-wide signature search failed to find meaningful Nrg3 neighbors: the strongest positive and negative z-score cosines were only +0.0439 for Nhs and -0.0441 for Fbxo11, and neither neighbor carried a shared FDR-level module.

The expected downstream molecular neighborhoods were also absent at the marker-gene level: neuregulins, ErbB receptors, Bace1, core presynaptic SNARE genes, GABA/glutamate markers, a dopamine marker, and Cntnap3 all failed FDR<0.10 under Nrg3 perturbation.
The P16 loss-of-function screen did not nominate a pan-neuronal transcriptomic pharmacodynamic marker for NRG3/ERBB4 inhibition.
Acute P16 Nrp1 loss was a complete downstream neuronal transcriptomic null across all 21 recovered cell groups.
The represented NRP1 family and pathway neighbors also failed to produce a broad Nrp1-like transcriptional phenotype.
Genome-wide signature search found no hidden convergent or opposing Nrp1 module.
The neuronal null should not be extrapolated to anti-angiogenic NRP1 biology.
Nrp2 perturbation produced a single significant downstream event: Lrp1 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Nrp2 loss was buffered or transcriptionally silent in 21 of 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The unbiased cross-target search found only negligible Nrp2 signature neighbors.
Represented neuropilin, Plexin-A, VEGF-receptor, and AMPAR comparators failed to phenocopy Nrp2.
The neuronal Nrp2 null does not evaluate the vascular and lymphatic compartments that motivate anti-NRP2 therapy.
Acute Nrxn1 loss produced a Pvalb-restricted Grm1 induction and no other robust downstream gene in 21 measured neuronal groups.
Represented neurexin-family and synaptic-complex relatives did not phenocopy the Pvalb Grm1 hit or form a shared transcriptomic module with Nrxn1.
The top Nrxn1 signature neighbors in the full measured perturbation universe were extremely weak.
Eight neuronal groups showed significant Nrxn1 mRNA depletion but zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
P16 mosaic Nrxn2 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream nuclear transcriptome response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal classes.

The germline Nrxn2α qRT-PCR program and the canonical neurexin Ca2+-channel/NMDA-receptor axes were absent: Dlg4, Stxbp1, Grin2a, Pvalb, synaptic markers, NMDA-receptor genes, and Ca2+-channel genes all stayed non-significant under Nrxn2 CRISPR.

The directly represented neurexin-family and ligand-side perturbations converged with Nrxn2 mostly by also being transcriptionally silent: Nrxn1 and Nrxn3 had only one isolated FDR<0.10 gene each, and Nlgn3, Lrrtm3, Grid1, Grid2 and Cntnap1 had none.
Other synaptic or neurodevelopmental perturbations in the same parquet did produce FDR-supported responses, including Grin1, Mef2c, Chd8 and Scn2a, whereas Nrxn2 remained flat.
A feature-centered full-signature neighbor scan found no robust Nrxn2-like or anti-Nrxn2-like transcriptional state; the largest residual correlations were near zero.
No FDR-supported RNA biomarker for acute Nrxn2 loss emerged, even among expected synaptic transcripts.
Nrxn3 produced a singleton thalamic response: Vps4a was up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and no other gene in any measured group reached FDR<0.10.
Nrxn3 was transcriptionally buffered in 20 of 21 measured cell groups, and an expected AMPAR/NMDAR/GABA/activity/stress marker panel was completely absent at FDR<0.10.
The neurexin paralogs Nrxn1 and Nrxn2 did not converge with Nrxn3 in this Perturb-seq surface.
Represented neurexin-ligand and ligand-side targets were mostly transcriptionally flat and did not form a shared Nrxn3-like module.
NMDAR subunit perturbations produced multi-gene transcriptional responses where Nrxn3 remained flat or singleton.
An unbiased all-target Wilcoxon-score search found no meaningful Nrxn3 signature cluster: the best positive and negative neighbors had near-zero Pearson correlations.
The flat stress and activity transcriptome after Nrxn3 editing is not a safety proof for NRXN3 modulation.
Nsd1 produced a narrow P16 neuronal RNA response: 24 of 26 downstream FDR<0.10 events were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with one-gene effects in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The 151 thalamic response was an ectopic mostly-up module containing metabolic, extracellular/structural, and immune-like genes rather than a simple repression program.
Zmynd8 and Kdm5c were the main same-direction FDR-overlap neighbors of Nsd1, with Zmynd8 sharing 11 and Kdm5c sharing 5 Nsd1 significant coordinates.
Sin3a opposed the Nsd1 thalamic module more than any other FDR-overlap comparator, reversing 8 Nsd1 151 signature genes while sharing only 2 in the same direction.
Myo5c was the only repeated Nsd1 downstream gene, rising both in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Zmynd8 reproduced both same-direction Myo5c events.
H3K36-pathway relatives Nsd2, Ash1l, Setd2, and the NSD1-linked methylation effector Dnmt3a did not converge with the Nsd1 signature in matched cell groups.
The Pvalb GABA signal was a single FDR-level up-regulation of Rhbdl1 without a broader Nsd1 program.
The strong 151 Nsd1 response did not contain a broad UPR, ISR, heat-shock, proteasome, autophagy, lysosomal, or redox program.
Nsd2 produced no robust postnatal neuronal transcriptome: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 recovered neuronal groups and 371818 Wilcoxon rows.
The embryonic-KO synaptic and protocadherin-beta mRNA program was expected but absent in every measured Nsd2 cell group.
Direct H3K36-axis comparators did not converge with Nsd2; Nsd1 showed only a small thalamus-concentrated response, Setd2 only a singleton, and Ash1l and Dnmt3a were flat.
The unbiased Nsd2 signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor; the most extreme Wilcoxon-score cosine values were between -0.014 and +0.028.
Acute Nsd2 loss in postmitotic neurons did not resemble the broad H3K36me2 oncogenic transcriptional role that motivates NSD2 inhibition in cancer.
The only robust Nsf downstream hit was Xpo1 down-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Postnatal Nsf loss did not elicit the transcriptional programs expected from a strong chronic SNARE/vesicle-trafficking failure.
The nearest Nsf signature neighbors were weak proteostasis and vesicle-trafficking stresses rather than direct SNARE-complex members.
Nsf did not phenocopy STXBP1, AMPAR-subunit targets, or most assayed SNARE-cycle perturbations.
NSF-related DEE variant biology, including mTOR/autophagy activation, is not reproduced by sparse postnatal Nsf loss-of-function.
Nsmce2 loss did not produce a BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal group.
Nsmce2 perturbation failed to launch a detectable p53, DNA-damage, apoptotic, or ER-stress secondary transcriptome.
Nsmce2 and the represented SMC5/6-localization factor Slf2 were flat or nearly flat, whereas some broader SUMO or SMC/chromosome-maintenance perturbations were not.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no convergent or anti-convergent Nsmce2 module.
The neuronal null shifts Nsmce2 disease interpretation away from an acute, specified-neuron transcriptional requirement and toward cycling developmental or unsampled proliferative compartments.
Nsmf produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had only a self-transcript hit.
Nsmf did not phenocopy represented NMDAR/CREB/BDNF-axis perturbations that did produce FDR-supported signatures in the same assay.
Postnatal Nsmf perturbation was silent in broad hypothalamic/thalamic groups and did not converge with represented GnRH/Kallmann comparators.
The expected BDNF-CREB hippocampal program was absent after P16 Nsmf loss in CA1/CA3/DG-containing glutamatergic groups.
The data-driven Nsmf nearest-neighbor structure was noise-scale and noncanonical.
Postnatal mosaic Nsun2 loss produced no BH-significant downstream mRNA signature in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The same single-nucleus assay can detect a tRNA-modification stress program, because Elp1 and Elp2 converged on a strong ISR/amino-acid signature while Nsun2 was flat.
Represented tRNA methyltransferases separated into an Elongator-responsive branch and a mostly silent Nsun2/Alkbh8/Trmt1 branch in this P16 neuronal screen.
Full-universe signature matching found only near-zero Nsun2 neighbors, so the top Wdr26/Zbtb7a/Wwox and negative Safe_target_81/Fbxo11/Adam10 matches are rejected as biological convergence.
The screen refines NSUN2 neuropathology toward embryonic survival and mature tRNA/proteome/synapse phenotypes rather than a large autonomous juvenile mRNA program.
Acute Nt5c2 loss produced a one-gene, L4/5 IT cortical response: Ddx50 was down-regulated only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Nt5c2 perturbation did not induce the AMPK/mTOR/ISR/p53 or purine-enzyme transcriptional programs that would be expected if nucleotide-pool imbalance became a cell-wide stress.
Zfp804a, the cortical-neuron protein interactor of NT5C2 nominated by the schizophrenia literature, was completely flat and did not share Nt5c2-Ddx50 down-regulation.
The screened purine-metabolism neighbor Adk did not phenocopy Nt5c2 across the 22 matched groups and was itself transcriptionally silent across all 23 cell groups.

The unbiased signature-neighbor search found only extremely weak Nt5c2 neighbors; the one robust Nt5c2 gene, Ddx50, was not shared by the top positive neighbors and was weakly significant in the opposite direction after Tpr perturbation.
Ntrk1 is a uniformly null transcriptional perturbation in the sampled postnatal neuronal classes: all 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and indistinguishable Ntrk1 self ranks.
The TrkB paralog Ntrk2 produced molecular engagement and a small Pvalb/thalamic response where Ntrk1 stayed flat.

Ntrk1 had no convincing same-family or data-driven convergent module: global cosine similarities to Ntrk2, Ntrk3, and Ngfr were between -0.0077 and +0.0141, and the strongest non-control full-signature neighbors also had no shared FDR-level genes.
The expected NGF-TrkA nuclear output was absent: Fos/Egr/Jun/Arc/Npas4, Dusp/Spry MAPK-feedback genes, Bdnf, and Bcl2 never reached FDR<0.10 in any Ntrk1-measured group.
Ntrk2 produced downstream FDR<0.10 genes only in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 20 recovered groups were weak and 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this target.
Ntrk2 loss selectively repressed Akap5 in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Vgf was downregulated by Ntrk2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Atp2a2 was downregulated together with Vgf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Ntrk1, Ntrk3, Ngfr and Sort1 did not converge on the Ntrk2 response.
Perturbing represented RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT, MTOR, CREB-axis and Camk2a nodes did not reproduce the Ntrk2 Akap5, Atp2a2 and Vgf FDR gene-cell pairs.
Residual whole-surface correlation found no robust data-driven positive or negative phenocopy of Ntrk2.

Ntrk3 loss produced a two-gene, GABA-biased transcriptome: Arhgap12 was up in 052 Pvalb Gaba and P3h3 was up in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, while the other 21 measured cell groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
Arhgap12 up-regulation is the only robust Pvalb GABA downstream event after Ntrk3 perturbation.
P3h3 up-regulation is the only robust CNU-LGE/LSX GABA downstream event after Ntrk3 perturbation.
The expected Ras/MAPK, PI3K/AKT, PLCG1, feedback, and immediate-early transcriptional outputs of Trk signaling were not recovered anywhere in the Ntrk3 DE surface.
Ntrk3 had no strong data-driven neighbor: the best whole-signature cosine was only 0.029 and no other target reproduced either focal Arhgap12 or P3h3 FDR event.

Ntrk3 failed to phenocopy measurable NTRK-family and Trk-proximal pathway perturbations: Ntrk1 and Ngfr were silent, Ntrk2 produced a different small Akap5/Vgf/Atp2a2-down signature, and Fyn, Mapk1, Akt3, Runx3, and Sos1 were flat or nearly flat.
Ntsr1 loss produced a globally buffered neuronal snRNA-seq phenotype: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene and the remaining group had only Prr7.
