Prr7 was selectively downregulated in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut after Ntsr1 perturbation and was the only FDR<0.10 downstream gene in the full Ntsr1 surface.
The represented neurotensin-family receptor Sort1 and canonical downstream signaling nodes Plcb1, Prkca, Mapk1, Mtor, and Adcy1 did not converge with Ntsr1 and did not reproduce the Prr7 response.
Data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbors of Ntsr1 were near-zero correlations rather than a coherent convergent or anti-convergent class.
The flat 215 MB Dopa result should not be read as evidence that NTSR1 is an inert dopamine-circuit drug target.
Acute Ocrl perturbation produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null rather than a cell-type-restricted Lowe-like signature.
Ocrl did not activate the lysosomal-autophagy, TFEB, or ISR/UPR mRNA programs that would be expected after unbuffered endolysosomal stress.
The dataset supports tonic Inpp5b-family buffering rather than induced Inpp5b transcription as the most plausible mouse explanation.
Literature-obvious endocytic and phosphoinositide relatives did not reveal a local Ocrl-like transcriptome.

Ogdh knockdown produced an almost completely buffered neuronal nuclear transcriptome: only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups despite a negative Ogdh self-transcript in every measured group.
The strongest positive Ogdh downstream hit was Prdx5 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Ogdh perturbation up-regulated Borcs7 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, pointing to a restricted lysosome-positioning or axonal cargo response rather than a generic mitochondrial program.
Same-complex and neighboring mitochondrial enzyme perturbations did not phenocopy the Ogdh Prdx5/Borcs7 signature.
Canonical OXPHOS, integrated-stress, UPR, and macroautophagy/lysosomal transcriptional programs expected after a severe mitochondrial lesion were absent from the Ogdh surface.
Data-driven restricted-signature neighbors were not robust Ogdh phenocopies.
Ogfrl1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 measured postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
A row-centered whole-universe neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Ogfrl1 signature neighbor; even the numerical top residual correlations were only +0.0165 and -0.0172.
Ogfrl1 loss did not engage OGF/opioid sentinels or TNF-RANKL-CSF1R osteoclast-inflammatory sentinels, and measurable receptor perturbations in those axes were also flat in neurons.

Ogt loss produced a real but highly uneven postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response: 18 of 21 measured groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, with the bulk of the 2,154 downstream calls concentrated in MB Glut, MB P MY GABA, CNU-HYa HY GABA, Pvalb, L4-5 IT and CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Ogt perturbation repeatedly decreased the opposing eraser Oga, most strongly in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and across six additional responders.

The most recurrent Ogt module was nuclear RNA processing plus nucleocytoplasmic transport: Rsrp1/Snhg11/Srrm2/Rbm14/Srsf5/Snrnp70 and related splicing genes went down while Xpo1 went up, and the nearest positive perturbation neighbors included Tnpo3, Ranbp2, Tpr, U2af2 and Prpf6.
Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations were the strongest FDR-overlap neighbors of Ogt, and Ogt responders carried a smaller direct proteostasis module with Lamp1, Sec62, Gnptg, Psma3, Syvn1 and Stub1.
Ogt loss down-regulated synaptic and excitability genes including Iglon5, Kcnab3, Cacng7, Adam22, Prrt1, Ache and Slc6a1, yet did not measurably alter Gria1-4 mRNAs.
Cyp46a1, Tecr, Far1 and Srebf2 formed a recurrent down-regulated lipid/cholesterol module, with Lypla2 up-regulation in the same broad responders.
The large Ogt signatures selectively depressed mitochondrial and organic-acid metabolism genes, including Mdh1, Pcca, Acadvl, Cox7b, Samm50 and Slc25a carriers.
The upstream HBP enzyme Gfpt1 and the OGT-associated chromatin regulator Sin3a failed to phenocopy Ogt strongly in matched cell groups.
No perturbation in the model-visible universe was a high-overlap inverse Ogt phenocopy; Huwe1 was only a shallow anti-neighbor.
Expected embryonic Wnt/Notch targets, Gria1-4 AMPA-receptor mRNAs, and a broad Atf4/Hspa5/Xbp1 UPR were absent from the Ogt FDR<0.10 surface.
Opa1 loss generated a FDR-resolved response in 10 of 22 measured neuronal groups and was silent in a large forebrain/cerebellar surface under the P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic CRISPR window.
The dominant Opa1-positive module is an ATF4/ISR-like amino-acid stress program.
Opa1-responding neurons up-regulated amino-acid import, aminoacyl-tRNA charging, and serine/one-carbon metabolism as a compensation layer.
The broadest midbrain and hypothalamic responses coupled nuclear ISR induction to loss of mitochondrial genome-encoded respiratory-chain transcripts.
Opa1's closest FDR-confirmed neighbors were mostly non-canonical stress perturbations rather than OPA1-processing factors.
Direct OPA1-processing and mitochondrial fission comparators represented in the screen did not phenocopy Opa1 loss.
The Opa1 signature had no robust inverse transcriptional target among represented perturbations.
A postmitotic juvenile brain Opa1 knockout recapitulated stress and respiratory compensation, not the retinal-ganglion-cell loss that defines dominant optic atrophy.
Opa1 activated Lonp1 in a few groups but did not induce a canonical Hspd1/Hspe1/Clpp mitochondrial UPR or Pink1/Prkn mitophagy transcriptome.
Opn1sw produced no FDR<0.10 downstream DE in any of the 22 recovered brain-neuron cell groups.
The top data-driven Opn1sw signature neighbors are only noise-floor neighbors and generate no shared FDR module.
Opsin and photoreceptor-regulatory perturbations represented in the screen do not phenocopy Opn1sw in matched brain-neuron groups.
Oprd1 loss of function produced no BH-significant downstream mRNA program in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The Oprd1 null is shared by the measurable opioid-receptor family and proximal Gi/o-related targets rather than being a delta-receptor-only failure to register.
Oprd1 LOF did not produce the Bdnf or immediate-early transcriptional outputs that opioid agonist studies make worth checking.
A whole-universe signature-neighbor search rejected strong hidden convergence for the Oprd1 nominal vector.
The screen is a poor negative proxy for delta-opioid agonist pharmacology.

Sparse postnatal Oprk1 loss did not produce a robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; even CREB/MAPK- and dynorphin-related candidate genes stayed at FDR=1 across the Oprk1 surface.

The opioid-receptor paralogs Oprm1, Oprd1 and Oprl1 also lacked FDR<0.10 downstream signatures, with near-zero Oprk1 score correlations, so Oprk1 belongs to a receptor-family-wide basal null rather than being an isolated failure.

A whole-parquet Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found no meaningful Oprk1 signature neighbor: the strongest positive score correlation was Cit at r=0.0339 and the strongest negative was Fgfr2 at r=-0.0321.

Perturbing Oprk1 did not phenocopy measurable intracellular Gi/o-cAMP/PKA/MAPK targets: Gnao1, Adcy3, Prkaca and Mapk1 showed target-transcript FDR signals in selected groups, whereas Oprk1 remained flat and had |r|≤0.0175 to these pathway perturbations.
The Oprk1 perturbation offers no resting snRNA-seq biomarker for kappa-receptor target engagement.
Oprl1 loss was buffered at the persistent basal snRNA-seq level: all 22 measured neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa had no Oprl1 rows rather than a measured zero.
The opioid-receptor paralogs Oprm1, Oprd1 and Oprk1 shared the same lack of robust basal transcriptomic output and did not form a distinct Oprl1-like signature.
Oprl1 perturbation did not produce a sustained CREB/activity or neuropeptide-feedback program: 30 expected marker genes were tested across 22 groups with zero FDR<0.10 calls.

The genome-wide data-driven nearest neighbors of Oprl1 were numerically tiny: Madd and Lrp1 were the top positive score neighbors, whereas Acvr2a and Kat6b were the top negative non-safe-target neighbors.

Represented proximal GPCR effector perturbations also failed to phenocopy Oprl1: G proteins, adenylyl cyclases, Kcnj6 and calcium-channel genes had Oprl1 score correlations between -0.008 and +0.022 and only Cacna1g exceeded ten FDR<0.10 genes.
Oprm1 perturbation produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Single-receptor LoF of the represented opioid receptor paralogs Oprd1, Oprk1, and Oprl1 was also FDR-flat and did not phenocopy Oprm1.
Oprm1 loss did not change cAMP/CREB/MAPK or immediate-early transcripts even though some downstream signaling-node perturbations were detectable.
The unbiased nearest Oprm1 transcriptomic neighbors were noise-scale rather than biologically convergent signatures.
The Oprm1 null warns that basal CRISPR-snRNA screens can miss classical druggable neuromodulatory receptors.
Or51e2 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in any of the 18 recovered NeuN-positive neuronal cell groups.
The represented canonical olfactory transduction neighbors Gnal and Adcy3 did not generate an Or51e2-like signature in the same 18 neuronal groups.
Unbiased signature neighbors of Or51e2 were rejected: correlations were near zero, Safe_target perturbations appeared among extrema, and neighbor DE genes did not overlap an Or51e2 FDR signature.
Acute Orc4 loss of function after P16 produced no robust downstream nuclear-transcriptomic response in any of the 21 Orc4-measured neuronal cell groups.
The only same-complex comparator available in the screen, Orc6, was also flat, while Orc4's nearest genome-wide rank neighbors were unrelated and had near-zero correlations.
Orc4 perturbation did not induce p53/DNA-damage, apoptosis, unfolded-protein, autophagy, or cell-cycle marker transcripts despite explicit testing of sentinel genes.
Orc6 loss was pan-buffered at the nuclear-RNA level across all 22 measured neuronal classes.
Orc4, the only directly represented ORC/pre-RC comparator, was also silent, and the Orc6-Orc4 score-space correlation was essentially zero.
The expected replication-licensing, S-phase, and stress-response readouts of ORC6 failure were completely absent after postnatal neuronal knockout.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search found no high-amplitude Orc6 signature neighbor.
Reported postmitotic ORC dendrite/spine biology was not recovered as an Orc6/Orc4 nuclear-transcriptomic module in vivo.
Osbpl2 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across every measured brain neuronal class in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen.
The expected cholesterol/SREBF program was absent after Osbpl2 perturbation even though the same dataset readily detected sterol genes after Srebf2 and Tsc2 perturbation.
The DFNA67 autophagy/proteinopathy program was not reproduced by generic Osbpl2 CRISPR loss of function in brain neurons.
Before applying priors, the whole-transcriptome Osbpl2 vector had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor.
The Osbpl2 ciliary-PI(4,5)P2/Hedgehog hearing-loss axis was not active as a postnatal brain-neuron transcriptional module.
Osmr loss of function produced a full-surface molecular null across every neuronal cell group in which the target was recovered.
The expected OSMR/JAK-STAT inflammatory transcript program, represented by Socs3, Stat1/Stat3, Gfap, Il6, Ccl2, Ccl5, Cxcl10, and Timp1, was not detectably inhibited or induced by Osmr perturbation.
Neither biochemical OSMR partners nor gp130/JAK-STAT pathway neighbors phenocopied Osmr with a broad transcriptomic response in the same neuronal groups.
A data-driven all-gene neighborhood search found only background-level Osmr signature neighbors, with the strongest cosine belonging to a safe-target control.
Otud7a produced a single robust downstream event: Wfs1 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
Canonical cortical synaptic and ankyrin biology did not become a broad nuclear RNA signature after sparse P16 Otud7a loss.
The nearest pre-literature Otud7a signature neighbors were low-amplitude and failed a Wfs1 overlap retest.
Represented 15q13.3 and ankyrin-family perturbations did not phenocopy the Otud7a-Wfs1 response.
Otulin loss produced a one-gene responder state in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, where Gpm6a was up-regulated and was the only downstream gene passing FDR<0.10 anywhere in the Otulin surface.
The Otulin perturbation did not recover a TNF, innate-receptor, NF-kappaB, or cell-death transcriptional module in postnatal NeuN-positive neurons.

The postnatal neuronal Otulin perturbation did not reproduce the Wnt/beta-catenin program expected from embryonic Gumby/Fam105b biology, even though Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 perturbations made Wnt-responsive genes detectable in this screen.
Full-transcriptome cross-perturbation search found no strong Otulin signature neighbor: all target-level cosines were between -0.027 and 0.031.
An ORAS-like inflammatory transcriptome was absent from all sampled postnatal neuronal Otulin perturbations.

Otx2 produced a vertically flat postnatal NeuN+ neuronal response: 22 measured cell groups, 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every group, and an unstable on-target transcript with FDR=1.0 everywhere.

The most direct adult Otx2 target class, midbrain dopaminergic neurons, was not recovered for Otx2, while nearby Otx2-tested midbrain/thalamic groups carried no Th/Slc6a3/Ddc/Nr4a2/Pitx3/Lmx1b response.

Otx2-gRNA Pvalb neurons did not modulate Pvalb, Gad1/Gad2, or perineuronal-net markers, matching a model in which cortical PV biology depends on OTX2 imported from choroid plexus rather than on the recipient neuron's Otx2 locus.

The pineal-containing 217 P MY Pineal Glut group did not recover the Otx2-Crx-melatonin program: Crx, Aanat, Tph1 and Asmt were all FDR=1.0 after Otx2 perturbation, and Crx itself had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes anywhere.

Literature-driven relatives did not reveal an Otx2-like response: Otx1 was absent as a target, Crx/En1/Lmx1b/Pax6/Pitx3 were themselves completely flat, and En2/Rax/Six3/Rarb produced only 1-3 total FDR<0.10 genes with near-zero correlations to Otx2.
Otx2 had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor across the complete parquet: the strongest Pearson score-vector correlations were Erbb3 at 0.029 and Cspp1 at -0.012.
Ovol2 loss produced a complete FDR-level null across all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The epithelial EMT/MET output normally controlled by OVOL2 was absent from Ovol2-perturbed neurons.
Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 were active in thalamic glutamatergic neurons while Ovol2 and most BMP/TGF-beta relatives were flat.
Unbiased all-target matching found no meaningful positive or negative Ovol2 signature neighbor.

Oxtr loss after P16 produced a nearly flat steady-state neuronal transcriptome: only three downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 23 measured cell groups and no BH-significant Oxtr self-transcript drop.
All Oxtr FDR-level positives localized to three broad subcortical classes—CNU-HYa/HY GABA, MB/P/MY GABA, and MB dopamine—while all cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups were null.

The 066 CNU-HYa/HY GABA response was Acly-only: Oxtr increased the acetyl-CoA enzyme Acly, and data-driven neighbors Dctn1 and Sin3a converged on the same Acly-up feature, but Oxtr did not induce the broader sterol/SREBP lipid module seen under Dctn1.
Wdr83os and Odr4 were isolated, Oxtr-selective hits in 191 MB/P/MY GABA and 215 MB Dopa, respectively, suggesting but not proving a weak multipass-membrane/GPCR-biogenesis compensation arm.

Oxtr did not phenocopy its receptor-family and downstream signaling relatives: Avpr1a, Avpr1b, Plcb1, Gnao1, Camk2a, Camk2b, Creb1, Mapk1, and Prkca failed to reproduce any Acly/Wdr83os/Odr4 hit in matched responder groups.
An oxytocin-linked activity/immediate-early transcriptional program was absent: Fos, Egr1, Arc, Npas4, Nr4a1, Bdnf, Crem, and Srf were all FDR=1.0 under Oxtr across every measured cell group.
The sparse Oxtr LoF signature should not be used to infer that OXTR is inert or transcriptionally safe as a CNS drug target.
P2ry12 produced only a CNU-MGE GABA singleton: Elavl3 was up-regulated at FDR 0.051 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and no other measured cell group had a robust downstream DEG.
The expected microglial homeostatic and activation transcript sets were absent from the P2ry12 DE surface.

Loss of other microglia-lineage receptors represented in the screen was likewise flat in neuronal groups: P2ry14, Cx3cr1, Csf1r, Ccr2, Axl, and Mertk had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered surfaces, while Sall1 had one isolated Rgs11 hit.

The strongest data-driven P2ry12 neighbors were only nominal: Atxn1 and Tbx6 had restricted-feature cosines of 0.136 and 0.134, Camta1 and Grm8 had -0.122 and -0.100, and none reproduced Elavl3 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The neuronal CRISPR surface gives little evidence for a broad cell-autonomous neuronal liability of P2ry12 loss, but it is not evidence against microglial or platelet P2Y12 pharmacology.
P2ry14 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured NeuN-enriched neuronal cell groups.
The expected chemokine, cytokine, inflammasome, immediate-early, and apoptosis sentinels were all absent from the P2ry14 DE surface.
The only directly represented purinergic-family comparator, P2ry12, was also essentially flat in the NeuN+ neuronal screen.
The data-driven P2ry14 signature neighbors were negligible and were rejected as biologically convergent modules.
A healthy neuronal nuclear RNA signature is unlikely to be a useful proximal biomarker for P2Y14 antagonism.
Pacs1 loss produced a one-gene Pde9a-up signature in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
The Pde9a effect was restricted to Pacs1 perturbation in 008 and was not reproduced by the pre-literature score neighbors Kcnb1 or Camk2a.
Pacs2, the lone represented PACS paralog, did not phenocopy Pacs1 and Pacs1 did not transcriptionally induce Pacs2.
The PACS1-GGA3-CK2 biochemical module was uncoupled from Pacs1's postnatal transcriptional phenotype.
The only Pacs1 responder did not activate a detectable TGN/lysosomal, autophagy, UPR/ISR, or synaptic-downshift transcriptional program.
The screen supports allele-specific disease logic: acute wild-type Pacs1 loss was a weak transcriptomic perturbation rather than a p.Arg203Trp-like neurodevelopmental program.

Acute Pacs2 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal buffered state: no cell group had even one downstream transcript at FDR<0.10, including high-cell groups such as 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
The severe-stress branches most expected from MAM disruption—UPR/ISR genes, autophagy/mitophagy markers and apoptosis genes—were not activated at FDR<0.10 in any Pacs2 group.
A juvenile CRISPR LoF signature did not phenocopy known PACS2 syndrome mechanisms centered on recurrent de novo p.Glu209Lys missense biology.
Represented PACS-adjacent comparators converged with Pacs2 on near-absence of neuronal transcriptional phenotypes rather than on a shared FDR gene signature.

The unbiased Pacs2 neighbor search found only tiny score-space similarities and anti-similarities; nearest non-safe neighbors such as Camta1 and Thoc1 were broad responders whereas Pacs2 itself had no robust downstream DE.
Pah loss-of-function did not create an FDR-level transcriptional program in any recovered neuronal class.
Canonical PKU secondary programs were absent after neuronal Pah perturbation.
The apparent Pah signature neighbors are tiny score-cosine matches with no FDR-level overlap.
The screen is consistent with liver or circulating-phenylalanine correction, not direct mature-neuron PAH targeting, as the actionable PKU axis.
Sparse postnatal Pak1 loss produced a single FDR-supported downstream transcript: Rbbp4 up in 308 CB GABA.
The only Pak1-induced gene, Rbbp4, points to a chromatin-remodeling rather than canonical kinase-output transcript.
Pak1 and Pak3 do not phenocopy in the same cerebellar GABAergic assay despite being neuronal group-I PAK paralogs that can heterodimerize.
Pak1 is transcriptomically uncoupled from represented Rac/Cdc42-LIMK and MEK/MAPK nodes.
The P16 mosaic LoF surface does not mimic the macrocephaly, migration, spine, or endocannabinoid phenotypes reported for developmental PAK1 biology and human activating alleles.
Pak1 has no credible global positive or negative ranked-signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Acute Pak2 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal cell group.
Pak2 did not phenocopy its group-I paralogs Pak1 or Pak3; those targets were themselves almost entirely target-self or singleton surfaces.
Canonical CDC42/RAC1-to-PAK/LIMK actin signaling was not recovered as a transcriptional cascade.
RAF/MEK/MAPK comparators produced a sparse Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a/Etv5 thalamic program that Pak2 did not share.
The unbiased neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Pak2 signature neighbor.
The Pak2 disease signal is not recapitulated as an acute juvenile neuronal cell-state program.
The neuronal null does not de-risk PAK2 inhibition in the lineages where Pak2 is known to be essential.
Acute Pak3 loss nominated Ccm2 as a single-gene, cerebellar GABA-restricted response: Ccm2 was the only downstream transcript with FDR<0.10 and was up-regulated in 308 CB GABA.

The annotated group-I PAK/Rac/Cdc42/Limk axis was nearly transcriptionally silent: Pak1 and Rac1 each produced one FDR<0.10 gene, whereas Pak2, Cdc42, and Limk1 produced none and did not reproduce Pak3-driven Ccm2 induction.

Pak3 loss was buffered at the level of the juvenile neuronal nuclear transcriptome: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 308 CB GABA had only Ccm2 rather than a synaptic, cytoskeletal, stress, UPR/ISR, proteostasis, or autophagy module.

Unbiased Pak3 signature neighbors were weak and noncanonical: absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations across the transcriptomic surface were below 0.05, and querying those neighbors returned no Pak3-like shared FDR module.
Pank2 loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null: 21 recovered neuronal groups, including large thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic samples, had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
No expected CoA-production, mitochondrial respiration, iron/redox, lipid, or synaptic transcript set was recovered after Pank2 perturbation.

Whole-transcriptome correlations placed unrelated perturbations nearest to Pank2, but the score correlations were only about |r|≤0.025 and the nearest targets had no shared FDR-supported genes with Pank2.
The direct PanK/CoA paralog test was structurally under-sampled as perturbations, and the represented indirect mitochondrial and iron comparators were also sparse and non-convergent.
Paqr7 loss of function produced an almost globally buffered basal neuronal transcriptome in this P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR screen: only one of 371,796 downstream gene-by-cell-group tests reached FDR<0.10.
The only Paqr7 downstream hit was Arnt up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA, with no accompanying Hif1a, Akt/Mapk, apoptosis, or immediate-early transcriptional module.

The measured progesterone-receptor and PAQR comparators did not phenocopy Paqr7: Paqr8, Pgr, and Pgrmc1 had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in Paqr7-matched groups, and Adipor2 produced one unrelated Smim10l1 hit in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

The unbiased whole-coordinate Paqr7 signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor: the extrema were Bcap31 at r=+0.04597 and Xrn1 at r=-0.02129, and neither regulated Arnt significantly in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Paqr8 loss-of-function produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Represented progesterone/PAQR-axis perturbations did not converge with Paqr8; Paqr7, Pgr, Pgrmc1, and Adipor2 had near-zero score correlations to Paqr8 and either zero or a single downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

Across the full model-visible universe, Paqr8 had no strong positive or negative whole-surface neighbor; the best full-surface positive Pearson r was only 0.0283, and the most negative real-gene correlation was -0.0125.
Acute P16 Park7 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Park7 loss failed to induce expected NRF2 antioxidant, ISR/UPR, autophagy, or PINK1/Parkin-mitophagy sentinel transcripts, even though a UPR-like response was detectable after Hspa5 perturbation.

Represented Parkinson and stress comparators did not converge with Park7; Vps35 and Hspa5 responded in the same analysis universe while Park7, Atp13a2, Nfe2l2, Atp13a3, and Sncb were downstream-null or nearly flat.
P16 mosaic Pax2 loss produced a nearly flat neuronal transcriptome: all 23 cell groups were recovered, but only one of 388023 downstream tests reached FDR<0.10.
Pdia6 was selectively down-regulated in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut after Pax2 perturbation, and it was the only FDR<0.10 downstream gene detected for Pax2.
Canonical Pax2-regulated midbrain-hindbrain and GABAergic differentiation transcripts were absent from the Pax2 DE surface.
Measured literature comparators Pax8, Pax6, En1, En2, Otx2, Gata3 and Lbx1 did not phenocopy Pax2: their global correlations to Pax2 were near zero and none shared the 007 Pdia6 signal at FDR<0.10.
Agnostic score-neighbor search found no strong Pax2 module; even the best whole-surface correlations were Kif2a r=0.0346 and Hs6st2 r=-0.0159 on the positive and negative sides.
The screen argues that PAX2 renal-coloboma biology is displaced away from the assayed axis: P16 NeuN+ brain neurons did not recapitulate embryonic kidney, eye, ear or organizer abnormalities.
Pax3 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured postnatal neuronal cell groups.
The canonical Wnt effector Ctnnb1 responded strongly in thalamic glutamatergic neurons in which Pax3 was completely flat.
PAX-family and neural-crest/myogenic comparators that would be obvious from developmental literature did not recover a postnatal neuronal Pax3-like module.
An unbiased all-target score-neighbor search found no meaningful Pax3 signature neighbor.
The postnatal neuronal Pax3-null surface does not phenocopy either PAX3 haploinsufficiency in neural-crest diseases or the PAX3-FOXO1 allele in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.
Pax4 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered postmitotic neuronal class.
Pax4 loss did not derepress the pancreatic alpha-cell antagonist program or perturb beta/delta endocrine marker genes in neurons.
Arx, the canonical pancreatic antagonist of Pax4, had a small GABAergic response whereas Pax4 and Pax6 were flat in the same cell groups.
Whole-surface neighbor search found no meaningful Pax4-like perturbation module.
Acute Pax6 loss after P16 was transcriptionally silent across all 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
Expected Pax6-effector genes from cortical and adult-neurogenic programs were measured but absent.
Tbr1, but not Pax6, retained a cortical glutamatergic response in the same postnatal assay.
Arx responded in three GABA groups where Pax6 was flat.
Pax-box paralogs did not phenocopy Pax6 and generated only three singleton corrected genes in the entire parallel query.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Pax6 neighbor or anti-neighbor.
The P16 mature-neuron screen does not phenocopy the developmental PAX6 haploinsufficiency disease axis.
Several other embryonic neural transcription factors were also off-window, whereas Tbr1 and Arx were the exceptions with cell-restricted postnatal responses.

Pax7 loss of function after P16 produced an almost completely buffered neuronal transcriptome: only Ruvbl1 in L5 ET neurons crossed FDR<0.10 among 371796 downstream tests across the 22 recovered cell groups.
Ruvbl1 up-regulation is a narrow L5 ET readout of Pax7 perturbation and is unusually Pax7-selective within the L5 ET comparison set.
The represented Pax family perturbations did not phenocopy Pax7: Pax2, Pax3, Pax4, Pax6, and Pax8 all had near-zero score-vector similarity to Pax7 and none reproduced the L5 ET Ruvbl1 induction.
The unbiased signature-neighbor graph had no meaningful Pax7 module: the strongest positive neighbor was Kctd1 at cosine 0.0387 and the strongest negative neighbor was Ago1 at -0.0172.
Pax8 loss produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream gene, Ids down in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Pax8 perturbation did not recover thyroid differentiation or embryonic midbrain-hindbrain organizer programs in any measured neuronal group.
The one-gene Pax8 signature was not shared by data-driven neighbors or by measured Pax, thyroid-axis, and isthmic-organizer comparators.
Pbx1 loss produced a single FDR-supported downstream response: Usp48 was selectively downregulated in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
The Pbx1→Usp48 edge in 059 was not shared by weak data-driven neighbors or by represented TALE and developmental TF comparators.
P16 Pbx1 perturbation did not engage the expected cortical arealization, SVZ neurogenic, or dopaminergic effector transcripts in any recovered NeuN+ cell group.
Nfe2l1 perturbation was transcriptionally detectable in thalamic and brainstem-like groups, but Pbx1 did not regulate Nfe2l1 there.
Pbx3 loss-of-function yielded no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not find a convincing Pbx3 phenocopy or anti-phenocopy.
Literature-obvious TALE, HOX, and Phox comparators failed to phenocopy Pbx3 in the same cell groups.
Canonical respiratory-neuron and glutamatergic-specification marker programs were absent after Pbx3 perturbation in sampled P16 neurons.

Pcca loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null rather than a propionic-acidemia stress signature: 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and selected ISR, ER-stress, redox, ubiquitin, and autophagy genes all had minimum FDR 1.000 across those groups.

Pcca fell into a broader buffered organic-acidemia module in this assay: represented BCAA/organic-acid neighbors Mmaa, Bckdhb, Bckdk, Dld, and Ivd also produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in matched Pcca groups, and several core TCA/OXPHOS targets were similarly weak.

The data-driven Pcca neighbors were rejected as pathway convergence: the five top all-gene positive neighbors were nearly null targets, whereas the least-similar neighbors included broad responders Psmc1, Psmb4, and Tnpo3.
Pcdh19 loss of function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal supergroup.
The P16 Pcdh19-null surface did not recover the literature-expected Wnt/beta-catenin, GABA_A receptor, immediate-early, or synaptic-adhesion transcriptional programs.
The null surface is most consistent with PCDH19 pathology being displaced to early mosaic adhesion and sorting rather than to a chronic autonomous mRNA state in already specified neurons.
Data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Pcdh19 were near-zero and safe-target-like, not a hidden cadherin, Wnt, GABA_A-receptor, or epilepsy module.
Pclo was pan-null across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups in the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR snRNA-seq assay.
Pclo did not phenocopy most literature-obvious active-zone perturbations; Bsn, Unc13a/b, Cacna1a, and Cacna2d2 were also nearly flat, whereas Stxbp1 produced a broader 151-gene response.
Pclo loss did not induce an autophagy, ubiquitination, or proteasome-bounce-back mRNA program.
Unbiased whole-surface signature search found no robust Pclo convergence or antagonism: the strongest positive and negative score correlations were only 0.033 and -0.017.
The Pclo PCH3/pontocerebellar phenotype was not recapitulated as an acute stress or degeneration transcriptome in postmitotic surviving neurons.
Pcsk2 perturbation lowered Pcsk2 self-transcript in all 20 measured neuronal cell groups but produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the full surface.

The only adjusted Pcsk2 downstream responses were single-gene, cell-restricted hits: Rnf25 decreased in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons and Rgp1 increased in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Canonical propeptide, granin, and peptide-processing transcripts were not transcriptionally compensated after Pcsk2 loss.
Cpe and Pcsk5, the two directly measured convertase-pathway comparator targets, did not converge with Pcsk2.
Pcsk2 had no strong empirical signature neighbor; the most positively and negatively correlated gene perturbations were unrelated and had absolute Pearson r below 0.026.
The dataset is silent about the classic pancreatic glucagon and glucose-homeostasis effects of PC2 loss because those lineages and peptide products were outside the screen.
Pcsk5 loss in P16 postmitotic neurons produced an almost flat snRNA-seq DE surface rather than a secreted-TGF-family developmental program.
The only FDR-supported Pcsk5 downstream genes were Ssb down in hippocampal/amygdalar glutamatergic nuclei and Ccdc90b up in pons/medulla/pineal glutamatergic nuclei.
Pcsk2, the only represented PCSK-family comparator, did not phenocopy Pcsk5 and had its own two weak singleton effects in 017 and 022 rather than Ssb or Ccdc90b in the Pcsk5 responder groups.
Perturbing represented TGF/BMP receptor and SMAD nodes failed to create a Pcsk5-like response in the two Pcsk5 responder groups.
A habenula/thalamus-containing Pcsk5 perturbation did not recover the chronic-stress PCSK5-MMP-neuroinflammation program.
Pdcd10 produced a single robust downstream call, Hsf2 up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Canonical endothelial CCM outputs were absent from the Pdcd10 neuronal DE surface.
Neither non-obvious global signature neighbors nor the represented CCM-complex member Krit1 converged meaningfully with Pdcd10.
Acute Pdcd10 loss was transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic neuronal nuclei: the target had one downstream FDR<0.10 hit among 371818 target-gene tests over 22 measured cell groups.
Pde10a CRISPR produced its clearest canonical response in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA: Pde10a itself was FDR-supported down and the only downstream FDR<0.10 genes were Scg2 and Crem, both up.
The persistent Scg2/Crem branch was not accompanied by the acute striatal Fos/Fosb/Egr/Arc/Npas4 or Tac1/Penk/Pdyn neuropeptide induction expected after full PDE10A inhibitor exposure.
Represented PDE and dopamine/cAMP/PKA pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Pde10a in the matched striatal-associated group.
The data-driven global neighbors of Pde10a were not robust biological phenocopies.
The 155 MB Glut response was an isolated mt-Cytb increase that points opposite to mt-Cytb decreases produced by Opa1, Psmb4, and Psmc1 in the same cell group.
Pde10a induced a unique but minimal Ubac2/Cnnm3 pair in 308 CB GABA.
Pde1c showed a pan-measured central neuronal null: 22 recovered cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and every Pde1c self row had FDR=1.0.

Measured cyclic-nucleotide pathway perturbations did not expose a PDE1C-like basal mRNA module: Pde10a, Pde4b, Pde4d, Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, and Prkar1a all had near-zero score correlations with Pde1c, and only Pde10a/Pde4b produced a few isolated FDR hits.

The data-driven Pde1c signature-neighbor search returned only negligible correlations; the strongest positive neighbor was Wdr26 at r=0.052677 and the strongest negative neighbor was Fbxo11 at r=-0.060997.
The P16 central-neuron Pde1c LoF null does not phenocopy the reported dominant PDE1C p.A320S cochlear hair-cell disease mechanism.
Basal Pde1c LoF in sparse mouse neurons did not yield a transcriptomic biomarker for PDE1 inhibition despite the druggability and CNS engagement of PDE1 inhibitors.
Pde4b produced only two robust downstream transcriptomic hits, restricted to 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
direction_pattern: up in the two responder groups

canonical_summary: Map2k2 was the strongest Pde4b-dependent transcript and increased in 155 MB Glut.
Snx14 increased as the sole robust Pde4b hit in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Pde4b loss failed to induce a detectable cAMP/CREB immediate-early transcriptional program.
direction_pattern: canonical IEG program absent after Pde4b LoF

canonical_summary: The literature-obvious PDE comparators did not phenocopy Pde4b.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of Pde4b were unrelated and numerically very weak.
Sparse neuronal Pde4b LoF is not a transcriptional phenocopy of PDE4B inhibition or germline Pde4b loss.
Acute P16 Pde4d loss was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered neuronal brain surface.
The canonical PDE4D-to-cAMP/PKA/CREB transcript program was absent even for Bdnf, Vgf, Crem, Fos/Jun, survival, apoptosis, and mitochondrial-biogenesis markers.
Pde4d did not phenocopy the measurable PDE-family perturbations Pde4b or Pde10a.
Unbiased genome-wide signature search found no meaningful Pde4d convergence or anti-convergence module.
The acrodysostosis link should not be read as simple vulnerability of P16-specified neurons to Pde4d loss.
Pdgfrb loss did not produce a robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured NeuN-positive neuronal groups.
Queryable pericyte-marker, Type III RTK, and proximal PDGFR signaling comparators failed to phenocopy a neuronal Pdgfrb program.
The unbiased global signature neighbors of Pdgfrb were extremely weak and did not define a recurrent FDR-supported module.
The neuronal null argues against acute postmitotic neuronal Pdgfrb loss as a primary explanation for PDGFB/PDGFRB-associated brain disease programs.
A PDGFR-beta-directed intervention is unlikely to act by directly rewiring juvenile neuronal transcription over 3-4 weeks.
Pdha1 produced only two single-gene downstream FDR<0.10 events: Vps4a up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Slc4a3 down in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Pdha1 did not induce the expected lactate/cAMP, ATF4/DDIT3 ISR, proteostasis, autophagy, or OXPHOS marker programs in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups.
Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA groups showed significant Pdha1 self-transcript decreases without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Measured PDC comparators Dlat, Dld, and Mpc1 were flat or nearly flat, and related TCA comparators Dlst, Ogdh, Sdha, and Idh3a were also sparse.
Global Pdha1 signature-neighbor correlations were near zero and the closest positive and negative non-safe neighbors had no FDR<0.10 surface of their own.
Pds5a-targeting CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal FDR-level non-response in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic screen.
Pds5a did not phenocopy the restricted thalamic response elicited by Smc1a and Stag2 perturbations.
Unbiased signature search found no robust positive or inverse Pds5a neighbor.
Pdx1 produced a single FDR<0.10 response, down-regulation of the neuronal calcium-sensor transcript Vsnl1, and only in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
The significant Pdx1 Vsnl1 decrease converged with Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations in the same 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cell group.
Pdx1 did not activate the broad ISR, proteostasis, apoptosis, and synaptic-down program produced by Psmc1 and Psmb4 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Directly represented PDX1 pancreatic TF partners and pathway neighbors failed to phenocopy the Pdx1 Vsnl1 hit or create a shared 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut signature.
Expected endocrine identity, glucose-sensing, prohormone-processing, and PDX1-ATF stress genes were absent from the Pdx1 neuronal response surface.
Acute Peg3 loss is almost completely buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons: only two non-self transcripts reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The strongest Peg3 downstream event is Gpx3 induction in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM glutamatergic neurons.
Peg3 perturbation up-regulates Pigc as the sole significant downstream gene in L5-6 IT glutamatergic neurons.
Peg3 loss did not derepress the expected Zim1/Oxtr/direct-target, Wnt/β-catenin, TNF/NFκB, or p53/Bax mRNA programs.
Wnt/β-catenin pathway knockouts were readily detected in thalamic glutamatergic neurons where Peg3 was flat.
The data-driven Peg3 signature neighbors were too weak and too mismatched to be kept as a convergent module.
Yy1, a represented Peg3-imprinted-domain regulator, triggered a broad neuronal response that Peg3 did not phenocopy.
Pex14 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in any of 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
Pex14 perturbation did not induce obvious peroxisome-biogenesis, lipid-metabolic, redox, ISR, autophagy/lysosomal, or BDNF-TrkB marker transcripts.
Represented peroxisome-linked comparators did not converge on a Pex14-like RNA state.
Full-universe signature-neighbor analysis placed Pex14 in the correlation noise floor rather than in a coherent related-target cluster.
The Pex14 neuronal null should not be used as a broad CNS safety signal for PEX14-PEX5 inhibition.
Pex1 produced only two robust singleton neuronal DEGs: Cabp1 was up in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Tceal9 was down in 308 CB GABA.
Acute Pex1 perturbation did not trigger a nuclear peroxisome-import, lipid-metabolism, oxidative-stress, pexophagy/autophagy, ISR, or UPR module in any measured neuronal class.
The literature-obvious peroxisome comparators represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Pex1.
direction_pattern: nonconvergent; Agps-specific up-regulation of Dhcr24, Cyp51 and Lmtk3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

canonical_summary: Full-universe signature search found no credible Pex1-like target; the strongest positive and negative neighbors had Pearson correlations close to zero.
Acute postnatal Pfkm perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every measured neuronal group, even though six groups showed significant Pfkm RNA depletion.

Pfkm sits in a glycolytic module whose represented neighbors were also nearly flat: Hk1, Eno1, Gpi1, Slc2a1, and Tpi1 had Pearson r=0.00490-0.01783 to Pfkm and only five isolated downstream hits across the Pfkm-matched surfaces.
The unbiased whole-transcriptome Pfkm neighbor search did not reveal a hidden recurrent module: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations to other perturbations were only |r|≤0.03265.
Pgr loss of function caused no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any recovered juvenile neuronal cell group.
Canonical hypothalamic progesterone/estradiol neuroendocrine markers were not recovered as a Pgr-loss transcriptional program.
Steroid-receptor, PR-coactivator, and membrane-progesterone-related perturbations failed to converge with Pgr and were themselves mostly flat.
Unbiased signature neighbors of Pgr were only nominally correlated and did not nominate a robust biological module.
The juvenile neuronal null does not de-risk progesterone-receptor perturbation in adult reproductive, endocrine, or peripheral therapeutic settings.
Pgrmc1 showed strong pan-neuronal self-transcript reduction but no downstream transcriptome at FDR<0.10 in any of 23 measured neuronal groups.
The expected sterol/P450, UPR-ISR, autophagy-lysosomal, immediate-early, and BDNF panels were absent under Pgrmc1 loss, and Pgrmc2, Tmem97, and Ldlr did not show compensatory mRNA feedback.
Both unbiased score neighbors and represented PGRMC1-adjacent perturbations failed as robust convergence partners.

The basal neuronal null is compatible with PGRMC1 being a druggable off-axis trafficking or glial target, but it does not validate neuronal inactivity under Aβ, apoE, progesterone, or inflammatory challenge.
The only FDR<0.10 Phactr1 downstream response was Vps13b up-regulation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
Acute postnatal Phactr1 loss was buffered at the steady-state snRNA level across almost the entire neuronal taxonomy.
No data-driven whole-surface signature neighbor converged strongly with Phactr1.
The represented PHACTR paralog Phactr2 did not phenocopy Phactr1.
The Phactr1-KCNT1/Slack relationship did not appear as a paired transcriptional module.
Actin/Rho/MRTF comparators were measurable but did not recreate the Phactr1 signature.
Phactr2-targeting CRISPR produced a single robust downstream transcript: Lrfn4 was induced in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and nowhere else at FDR<0.10.
Acute postnatal Phactr2 CRISPR was transcriptionally buffered in 22 of 23 measured neuronal groups and did not trigger a canonical actin/PP1/MRTF/SRF module.
Neither literature-obvious PHACTR/actin relatives nor the nearest data-driven neighbors phenocopied the Phactr2 Lrfn4 response.

Phf12 loss was not pan-neuronal: the FDR<0.10 response was concentrated in caudal thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic and pons/myelencephalon-associated neuronal classes, with the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c group dominating the surface.
The active Phf12 signatures were strongly up-biased: 341/544 genes in 151, 94/121 in 155, 39/46 in 191, and 29/31 in 066 were up-regulated.
Phf12 perturbation induced a nuclear RNA-processing and spliceosome module, including Dhx38, Sf3b2, Snrnp70, Srsf11, Srsf5, Sfswap and U2af1.
A secretory-proteostasis module was induced across Phf12 responders: ER membrane complex, glycosylation, Golgi-trafficking, lysosomal and ubiquitin-system genes all rose.

Ptcd3-centered mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes were repeatedly up-regulated, with Ptcd3 significant in six of ten responder groups and Idh3b/Nduf/Timm/Tomm genes induced in the large thalamic and midbrain signatures.
The negative arm of the strong Phf12 signatures was neuronal: Gls, Syt7, Snap25, Sv2a, Ntng1, Grm1, Gabrg2, Nrxn1 and cytoskeletal genes such as Tuba1a and Tubb3 were reduced.
Srebf2, Dhcr24, Sqle, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Insig1 and Cyp46a1 formed a smaller down-regulated sterol/cholesterol module.
The top positive Phf12 neighbors were proteasome and RNA-processing perturbations, not SIN3 components: Psmb4, Prpf6, Hnrnpu, Yy1, Psmc1 and U2af2 were the strongest same-direction matches.

Sin3a, the literature-obvious scaffold partner, did not phenocopy Phf12 despite being a broad responder; it had a near-zero/slightly negative Phf12-query cosine with nearly balanced same- and opposite-direction overlaps.

The strongest anti-neighbors were Arid2, Setd5 and Nrf1, showing that some chromatin-like or stress-related perturbations invert the Phf12 RNA/proteostasis signature rather than merely fail to match it.
The neural-crest Cad6b/Cdh6-Snail2 program expected from embryonic PHD12 biology was absent: Cdh6 and Snai2 were tested in every Phf12 cell group and never reached FDR<0.10.
A postmitotic juvenile Phf12 loss-of-function can perturb mature neuronal RNA, proteostasis, mitochondrial and synaptic mRNAs without embryonic cell division.
Experimental SIN3A-PF1 inhibition proposed for cancer would be expected to intersect neuronal RNA/proteostasis programs if achieved in PHF12-dependent neurons.
Phf21a loss produced a real but narrow P16-postmitotic transcriptional response: 18 FDR<0.10 downstream events in 5 of 22 measured cell groups, with the largest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Rreb1 induction was the dominant recurrent Phf21a downstream event, appearing in every responder and often as the only FDR-supported gene.
The 151 thalamic and 191 posterior GABA signatures added an induced local membrane/extracellular module around Col4a5, Cdh13, Jam2, Adam15, Tapbp, and Wls.
L3mbtl3 was induced with Rreb1 in 155 MB Glut, giving a one-gene hint of chromatin-reader compensation rather than a broad generic chromatin program.
Zbtb7a was the chief FDR-overlap neighbor of Phf21a, sharing Rreb1 up-regulation in 4 matched responder groups while also opposing 3 weaker Phf21a events.
Yy1 and Sin3a opposed pieces of the Phf21a 151-thalamic signature, including Rreb1 down after both Yy1 and Sin3a perturbation, while Phf21a drove Rreb1 up.

The obvious REST and H3K4 comparators failed to phenocopy Phf21a: Rest, Phf6, Phf8, Kdm5b, and Kdm6b were FDR-flat, whereas Setd1a, Kmt2a, and Sin3a responded but did not share Phf21a's FDR signature.
The dataset supports PHF21A haploinsufficiency as a disease gene but redirects the major causal biology away from a broad pan-neuronal basal transcriptome at P16-P44.
Phf6 loss after P16 produced a globally buffered neuronal nuclear transcriptome: all 21 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and Phf6 itself had FDR=1 in every group.

The canonical fetal cortical PHF6-PAF1/migration program was not reactivated by postmitotic Phf6 editing: Cspg5 and the fetal-cortical genes Reln, Nr4a2, Slc12a5, Phip, and Zic1-Zic4 all had FDR=1 in every measured Phf6 group.
PHF/PHD-domain targets did not phenocopy Phf6: Phf8 was flat, Phf21a had only 18 downstream FDR genes, Phf12 had 754, and their Phf6 all-feature score correlations were 0.004-0.010.

The PHF6-NuRD physical interaction did not translate into a matched neuronal loss-of-function signature: Chd4 produced 158 downstream FDR genes in the same groups, while Mbd2 and Gatad2b produced only 1 and 2, and all three correlated with Phf6 at |r|≤0.0024.
The data-nominated Phf6 signature neighborhood collapsed to noise: the strongest non-safe positive neighbor was Ror1 at r=0.027, and the strongest negative neighbor was Psmb4 at r=-0.022.

Phf8 was a pan-neuronal transcriptional non-responder in the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function assay: 22 assayed neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and even FDR<0.20 returned zero genes across 371,796 downstream tests.

The hippocampal Ras/mTOR expectation from Phf8-deficient mice was not recovered after sparse P16 Phf8 loss: both hippocampal glutamatergic groups were FDR-null, and model-visible Mtor/Ras sentinels remained uncorrected.
Phf8 lacked a meaningful positive or inverse signature neighbor, and represented PHF/JmjC or neurodevelopmental chromatin comparators did not phenocopy it.
The Phf8-null surface separates PHF8 loss-of-function disease biology from acute neuronal knockdown in the juvenile brain.
Phka1 is transcriptionally silent after acute postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function across every recovered cell group in this screen.
The phosphorylase-kinase complex does not behave as one neuronal transcriptional module: Phka1 and Phkb were both null, while Calm1 and Calm3 had small non-overlapping responses.
A dataset-wide signature scan could not assign Phka1 a robust convergent or inverse neighbor.
Phkb loss of function was FDR-flat in every recovered neuronal cell group.
Same-holoenzyme PhK comparators did not phenocopy Phkb.
The represented lysosomal glycogen-storage comparator Gaa was strongly self-repressed but downstream-flat in neurons, paralleling Phkb's flatness on the output axis.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Phkb neighbor.
Phox2a loss of function was nearly silent across the recovered P16-edited neuronal taxonomy: 22 of 23 groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the remaining group had only one.
A single CNU-MGE GABA gene, Itfg1, decreased after Phox2a perturbation.
Canonical catecholaminergic and autonomic Phox2a-associated genes were not detectably altered in the Phox2a perturbation surface.
Phox2-pathway comparators represented in the parquet did not converge with Phox2a.
The data-driven whole-surface neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Phox2a signature neighbor.
Phox2b had no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was only weak by a single Rasgef1a near-miss at FDR=0.130.

The canonical Phox2b autonomic/noradrenergic output was absent: Th, Dbh, Ret, Gfra1, Gata2, Gata3, Phox2a, Ascl1, Atoh1, Sox10, Egr2, Lbx1, and Slc6a2 all had min FDR=1.0 in Phox2b-perturbed groups, and Phox2a/Ret/Sox10/Gfra1/Atoh1/Gata3/Egr2/Lbx1 perturbations were themselves flat or single-gene in the same taxonomy.
The Phox2b score vector had only near-zero data-driven neighbors; Wdr26 was the strongest anti-neighbor and produced 96-1807 FDR<0.10 genes in several matched groups where Phox2b produced zero.

The Phox2b CRISPR null in sampled P16 mouse neurons does not model PHOX2B disease mechanisms centered on embryonic autonomic/RTN development, neural-crest neuroblastoma susceptibility, or CCHS-associated repeat and non-polyalanine alleles.
Pi4kb produced only three downstream FDR<0.10 gene-cell events, all up-regulated and restricted to 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Itpk1 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA is a candidate transcriptional biomarker for a soluble inositol-phosphate adjustment after Pi4kb loss.
Pi4kb up-regulated Tmem50b and Rnf145 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, nominating a small ER/Golgi membrane and sterol-E3-ligase compensation module.
Coverage-filtered whole-transcriptome correlations found no robust Pi4kb phenocopy or anti-phenocopy across the 1,773-target universe.

Represented phosphoinositide and PI4KB-adjacent targets did not converge on Pi4kb; Pitpna was the only broad phosphoinositide comparator but was weakly anti-correlated and shared zero Pi4kb FDR genes.
Pi4kb loss did not induce a detectable canonical Golgi-effector, CERT, ISR/UPR, autophagy/lysosome, or broad cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional program.
The broad null in postmitotic NeuN+ central neurons argues that this assay did not phenocopy the known PI4KB inner-ear or Schwann-cell disease contexts.
Acute Pibf1 loss did not generate any FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in 22 measured NeuN-enriched juvenile mouse brain cell groups.
Pibf1 did not recover a shared neuronal ciliary-gene loss-of-function module: represented ciliopathy perturbations were themselves nearly flat and had near-zero score correlations with Pibf1.
Canonical Hedgehog/ciliary and PIBF-IL4R/STAT sentinel genes were present but unchanged after Pibf1 perturbation across all measured groups.
Acute P16 Pign loss was pan-neuronally transcriptionally buffered: every recovered neuronal cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a returned Pign self row.
Pign did not induce a detectable ER-stress, unfolded-protein-response, or ISR transcript program in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The only represented GPI-related pathway neighbor, Dpm1, did not phenocopy Pign and showed only a restricted Pdia6/Ttyh3 two-gene signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

The genome-wide Pign signature had no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor: the top Wilcoxon-score correlations were only r=0.030787 for Lztfl1 and r=-0.027656 for Safe_target_23, with the top non-safe negative comparator Prepl at r=-0.022035.
Pik3cb had no FDR-level downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Downstream Tsc2, and weakly Mtor, produced detectable mTOR-axis transcriptional signatures where Pik3cb and direct PI3K-core comparators were flat.
Wild-type postnatal Pik3cb LoF did not recapitulate the FMR1/mGluR5/p110β synaptic-translation literature as a basal nuclear-RNA module.
No data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbor showed meaningful convergence or divergence with Pik3cb; all top positive and negative Pearson correlations were |r|<0.05.
Pik3r1 loss was pan-neuronally FDR-flat: no recovered cell group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Tsc2, but not Pik3r1, exposes a detectable mTORC1-linked sterol/lysosomal/PI3K-feedback program in matched neuronal groups.
The directly represented class IA PI3K relatives Pik3r2 and Pik3cb were just as transcriptionally buffered as Pik3r1.
Represented receptor, Akt, and mTOR-neighbor perturbations failed to converge on a Pik3r1-like signature.
A genome-wide score-neighbor search found no meaningful Pik3r1 positive or negative signature neighbor.
Pik3r2 loss of function is transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal group in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen.
The juvenile neuronal LoF surface does not recapitulate the activating PIK3R2 brain-overgrowth program.
Tsc2, but not Pik3r2, exposes a strong mTOR-axis transcriptional state in the same neuronal atlas.
Literature-obvious PI3K relatives represented in the screen did not phenocopy Pik3r2 because they were themselves mostly flat.
The data-driven neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Pik3r2 signature neighbor.
Pitpna loss elicited a sparse, caudal-biased neuronal response rather than a pan-neuronal phosphoinositide-stress program.
The main TH Prkcd/Grin2c response coupled phosphoinositide/Ca2+/secretory genes to reduced synaptic receptor/scaffold transcripts.
Pitpna depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also remodeled a neurite/microtubule module.
Jun was the recurrent caudal responder, with Crem co-induced only in the low-cell 217 P MY Pineal Glut signature.
217 P MY Pineal Glut showed a small secretory and cell-surface remodeling program on top of Jun/Crem activation.
The strongest same-direction neighbors of Pitpna were Rab7, Gfpt1, Uba5 and Grin1, not the measured phosphoinositide-transfer relatives.
Brd4, Tpr and Ankrd11 supplied the dominant opposite-direction contrasts to the Pitpna thalamic signature.
Measured phosphoinositide-transfer, PI4P-turnover, PLC and PKC perturbations did not phenocopy Pitpna.
Two high-on-target-drop nulls uncoupled Pitpna mRNA depletion from a downstream transcriptome.
Pitpnm3 did not produce a robust basal snRNA-seq response in any recovered neuronal class.
Canonical PIP2/Ca2+-linked transcriptional surrogates were absent after Pitpnm3 loss.
The only represented PI-transfer-family comparator, Pitpna, diverged from Pitpnm3.
Whole-surface score neighbors of Pitpnm3 were essentially uncorrelated.
The CCL18/PITPNM3 tumor-migration axis is not recapitulated in mouse NeuN+ brain nuclei.
Pitx2 loss produced a pan-null juvenile neuronal transcriptomic surface: every Pitx2-measured cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The closest hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain classes also lacked a Pitx2 response, including no FDR-level changes in Gad1, Gad2, Slc17a6, or Dkk2.

Canonical upstream Wnt/TGF-beta relatives did not converge with Pitx2: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 shared a thalamic Wnt-effector response while Pitx2 was flat there, and Nodal/TGF-beta-proximal receptor or Smad perturbations were null or singletons.

The represented paired-like and mesodiencephalic dopaminergic transcription-factor comparators Pitx3, En1, Lmx1b, Foxa2, and Otx2 also produced no FDR<0.10 downstream response in the 22 Pitx2-matched groups.

A de novo cross-target scan found no convincing Pitx2 signature module: even the top non-control neighbors had Pearson correlations no larger than 0.032 in Wilcoxon-score space and lacked shared FDR-level biology.

Pitx3 loss produced a completely FDR-flat postnatal neuronal response across the whole 23-cell-group taxonomy; the broad non-dopaminergic surface is therefore a true cell-type-restricted negative result, not an occult cortex-wide or striatum-wide transcriptional program.

The expected Pitx3/Nurr1 dopaminergic terminal-differentiation program was not recovered even in 215 MB Dopa: Th, Slc6a3, Ddc, Aldh1a1, Nr4a2, Lmx1a/Lmx1b, En1/En2, Foxa2, Otx2, Ret, Bdnf, Drd2, Dlk1, Syt4, Cck, and Gdnf all remained non-significant after correction.

Pitx3 did not converge with represented mDA-network or family comparators: Pitx2, Lmx1b, Foxa2, Otx2, En1, Ret, and Nr4a1 were themselves globally flat, while En2, Drd2, Nr4a3, and Msx2 had only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene each and all score-vector correlations to Pitx3 were between -0.001 and 0.017.

A genome-wide neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Pitx3 signature neighbor; the strongest positive score-vector neighbor was Zic3 at r=0.029 and the strongest negative was Fbxo11 at r=-0.022.
Pkd1 loss was fully buffered at the FDR<0.10 transcriptomic level across all 21 measured postnatal neuronal groups.
Pkd1 had no strong positive or negative transcriptional neighbors; top correlations were near zero and mixed with safe-target controls.
Ciliary trafficking and assembly perturbations did not produce a broad Pkd1-like transcriptional response in the Pkd1-matched neuronal groups.
Tsc2, not Pkd1, activated a detectable mTORC1/SREBP/lysosome-like transcriptional program in the matched neuronal atlas.
Ctnnb1 β-catenin loss produced a strong thalamic/hypothalamic Wnt transcriptional signature that Pkd1 loss did not share.
Represented cAMP/PKA/STAT perturbations were nearly as flat as Pkd1, so this neuronal screen does not recover the kidney ADPKD calcium/cAMP/STAT axis.
Pknox2 produced a complete corrected null across every recovered P16 neuronal group: 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 21 of 23 possible cell groups.
The measured Pknox2 null did not include a compensatory PREP/MEIS/PBX or cochlear target-gene signature.
Represented TALE relatives and PBX partners did not reveal a coherent single-gene TALE phenotype in the same 21 Pknox2-matched groups.
The top data-driven positive and negative neighbors of Pknox2 were all near zero and did not constitute biological convergence or divergence.
Positive Pknox2 biology in cochlea and fibroblast remodeling is displaced away from this NeuN+ P16 neuronal assay.
Plcb1 loss produced no robust downstream whole-transcriptome response in any recovered neuronal group: 22 of 22 measured groups had 0 non-Plcb1 genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected activity-responsive transcriptional axis was absent: Arc, Fos/Fosb, Jun/Junb/Jund, Egr1-4, Npas4, Nr4a1/2, Homer1, Bdnf, Rgs2/4, and Dusp1/6 all had 0 significant Plcb1 responses across 22 groups.

Directly measured Gq/PLC-pathway relatives did not phenocopy a hidden Plcb1 RNA module: Chrm3, Grm1, Grm5, Htr2c, Itpr1, and Prkca had no downstream genes, while Htr2a, Htr2b, and Prkcg produced only 6 significant genes over 193 matched target by group tests.

No data-driven convergent or inverse module emerged for Plcb1: the strongest feature-centered correlations with any other perturbation were only r=0.0116 positively and r=-0.0158 negatively, and the top biological neighbors were themselves downstream-null.

Basal nuclear transcriptomics is a poor proxy for PLCB1 target engagement: a screen seeking PLCB1 disease modulation should use evoked GPCR, calcium, PIP2, DAG/PKC, or electrophysiology readouts rather than resting snRNA-seq alone.
Pld3 loss was buffered from large nuclear transcriptome changes in almost every recovered neuronal class.
The only downstream Pld3 hit was Ncapd2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
Pld3 did not phenocopy represented APP, TLR7, autophagy, or lysosomal trafficking perturbations.
Genome-wide data-driven neighbors of Pld3 had near-zero signed-score correlations and did not reveal a hidden module.
A simple acute PLD3-loss transcriptome is a poor proxy for PLD3 neurodegenerative disease biology.
Plec loss produced a near-pan-neuronal buffered transcriptional footprint: among 371,796 downstream tests in 22 recovered cell groups, only Eprs in 001 L5-6 IT Glut reached FDR<0.10.
The sole robust Plec-induced transcript was Eprs up-regulation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
Plec did not activate the cytoskeletal, microtubule, UPR/ER-stress, ISR, or autophagy programs expected if P16 neuron loss caused broad cytoskeletal collapse or organelle stress.
Plec was not phenocopied by the directly measured plakin/cytoskeletal comparators Dst, Nefl, Nefm, Nefh, Actg1, Actn4, Map1b, Tuba1a, or by the EPRS-complex scaffold Aimp1.
Unbiased whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Plec convergence or anti-convergence across the 1,772 other perturbations.

Acute postmitotic Plpbp perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups and did not induce robust B6-salvage, PLP-dependent enzyme, immediate-early, ISR/UPR, or autophagy sentinels.
The unbiased Plpbp Wilcoxon-score vector had only noise-scale positive and negative neighbors across the full target universe.
Represented PLP-dependent enzyme targets Gad2, Abat, Srr, Got1, and Got2 did not converge with Plpbp, and core B6-salvage genes Pdxk, Pnpo, and Pdxp were not themselves perturbation targets.
Plxna1 loss yielded only two downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional hits, Kif21a up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Arhgap35 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Measured plexin, neuropilin, and semaphorin relatives did not phenocopy Plxna1 in the matching responder groups and had near-zero full-signature correlations.
Genome-wide data-driven Plxna1 signature neighbors were all too weak to keep as biological comparators.
The broad postnatal neuronal null refines PLXNA1 neurodevelopmental genetics toward early circuit construction and local morphology rather than a sustained pan-neuronal mRNA program.
Neuronal Plxna1 nulls should not be used to dismiss oligodendrocyte Sema3A-Plexin-A1 remyelination biology.
Plxna2 produced a single robust downstream change, Med15 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.

The P16 postmitotic Plxna2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: 22 of 23 groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c, and MB Glut groups showed significant Plxna2 mRNA decreases without any downstream DE.
Represented plexin, neuropilin, and semaphorin perturbations did not converge with Plxna2 in this assay.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found only near-zero global neighbors for Plxna2.
Acute Plxna4 loss produced a singleton Zfp384 up-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and no other FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any measured cell group.

The unbiased centered whole-transcriptome surface had no strong positive or negative Plxna4 neighbor: Srebf1 and Tlr8 were the top non-safe MEA-measured neighbors but had cosine_z values of only +0.0106 and -0.0130 and did not reproduce Zfp384 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Represented semaphorin/plexin relatives were disjoint from Plxna4: none phenocopied the 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut Zfp384 response, and their own significant DEGs were isolated in other groups.

Plxna4 loss did not transcriptionally regulate assayed semaphorin co-receptors or canonical intracellular signaling nodes, including Nrp1, Nrp2, Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxnd1, Sema4d, Sema5a, Sema6a, Farp2, Rac1, Fyn, Dpysl2, Dpysl5, Cdk5, Cdk5r1, Rasa1, and Rras.
Acute postmitotic Plxnd1 loss caused no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The literature-predicted Sema3E-Plexin-D1-Mtss1 response was not recovered in the broad CNU-LGE/LSX GABA group.
Top data-driven neighbors and measured semaphorin/plexin-family perturbations failed to converge with Plxnd1.
A flat NeuN+ Plxnd1 surface does not de-risk endothelial or developmental PLXND1 loss.

Pnkd loss after P16 was globally buffered at the snRNA-seq level: no recovered neuronal group contained even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10, despite corrected Pnkd mRNA decreases in Pvalb, CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA groups.
Expected oxidative-stress, UPR/ISR, activity-immediate-early, and active-zone compensation panels were all absent from the corrected Pnkd surface.

Pnkd did not phenocopy the represented core vesicle-fusion target Stxbp1: Pnkd had 0 downstream genes everywhere, whereas Stxbp1 had 140 corrected downstream genes concentrated in L4/5 IT cortex, Pvalb interneurons, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Pnkd signature neighbor; the largest positive score cosine was only 0.0348 and the largest negative was only -0.0220.

Represented paroxysmal-dyskinesia/channel/transport disease comparators also failed to form a shared juvenile neuronal transcriptomic module with Pnkd: Adcy5, Cacna1a, Kcna1, Kcnj6, Kcnma1, Sgce, and Tbc1d24 each had zero downstream genes, while Drd2, Gnal, and Slc2a1 had one each across all recovered groups.
Pogz did not generate a corrected downstream transcriptional response in any neuronal group recovered for this target.
The expected POGZ-ADNP-HP1 relationship did not phenocopy: Adnp had a measurable multi-cell-group response, whereas Pogz was flat in the same groups.
Pogz was buffered in a screen that did detect several other ASD or chromatin regulators, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
A de novo search of the complete perturbation universe gave Pogz no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor.
Pola1 loss of function produced no robust downstream DE in any recovered postnatal neuronal class.
The expected secondary p53/replication-stress, ISR/UPR, and interferon-stimulated programs were absent rather than merely below program annotation.
Pola1 had no meaningful convergent or anti-convergent transcriptomic neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Represented checkpoint relatives did not reveal a hidden replication-stress axis: Atr and Trp53 were also broad nulls and Cdkn2a had only one off-axis hit.
The POLA1 neurodevelopmental and immunologic disease record is not phenocopied by acute P16 neuronal LoF.

Polr3b produced a sparse response: 19 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 3 of 21 measured neuronal cell groups, with 16 measured null groups, 2 weak groups, and 2 taxonomy groups not recovered for this target.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Polr3b loss mainly down-regulated a neuronal adhesion, Rap-family, calcium, and neurite-growth module, while Rap2a and Nup98 were the only up-regulated FDR genes.
Psmb4 and Psmc1 were the strongest positive Polr3b signature neighbors and updated the same-direction thalamic Adgrb1/Rap1gap/Pcp4/Plekhg1/Lrrc7/Mgat5/Atp2b1 module.

Bdp1, the only additional Pol III-initiation target in the parquet, did not phenocopy Polr3b: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut it induced Ddit3 and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and shared zero FDR genes with Polr3b.
Polr3b did not induce a measurable ISR, aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase, or UPR/ERAD program, even though Bdp1 and Hspa5 perturbations show those mRNAs are detectable in the same analysis layer.
The 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA effects were only two genes each and were disjoint from each other: Rabgap1 and Tardbp up in 155, Ccl19 and Zfp827 down in 191.

Por produced a narrowly thalamic transcriptional hit: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Por itself was the top on-target transcript and Mzt1 was the only downstream FDR<0.10 gene, decreased with logFC -0.642.
Por had no strong signature neighbor in the full perturbation universe; even Uba5, the strongest 151-local neighbor, changed Mzt1 opposite to Por and carried thousands of additional DEGs.
Por loss was transcriptionally uncoupled from the expected P450/retinoid, AhR xenobiotic, NRF2 redox, and SREBP/LXR sterol modules across the measured neuronal surface.
Pou1f1 loss produced no FDR-supported postnatal neuronal transcriptional response and did not move the canonical Gh/Prl/Tshb hormone targets in any recovered cell group.

The anterior-pituitary transcription-factor cascade around Pou1f1 was absent as a coordinated neuronal module: Prop1, Hesx1, Lhx3, Lhx4, Pitx2, Otx2, and Pax6 were themselves FDR-null in matched groups, while Six3 and Sox2 had only one- or two-gene off-module signals.

Pou1f1 did not phenocopy measurable POU-homeodomain relatives in postnatal neurons; the class II, III, IV, V, and VI POU targets available in the parquet were either FDR-null or had only scattered one-gene effects.

Data-driven Pou1f1 signature neighbors were numerical rather than biological: the best restricted-signature cosines were small, and matched DE surfaces either remained null or responded in cell groups where Pou1f1 had no FDR genes.
Pou2f1 loss is pan-buffered across the sampled postnatal neuronal taxonomy under basal conditions.
Canonical Oct1 stress, ISR/UPR, and metabolic sentinel genes were not induced or repressed after basal neuronal Pou2f1 perturbation.
Measured POU-domain relatives do not substitute for, or phenocopy, Pou2f1 in the assayed P16 neuronal states.
The whole-universe neighbor search found only near-zero Pou2f1 signature correlations, rejecting strong convergence with any represented target.
Pou2f2 loss after P16 produced no robust FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal class.
The class-2 POU paralog Pou2f1 did not phenocopy or compensate Pou2f2 in this postmitotic neuronal assay.
A model-visible neighbor scan found no substantive Pou2f2-like signature; even the best non-safe residual correlations were |r|<0.03.
Canonical Oct2 target programs—B-cell Bcl2/OCA-B, hypothalamic Tgfa, retinal Nrl, and ischemic Sesn2—were absent from the Pou2f2 neuronal DE surface.

Pou3f3 loss in P16 postmitotic neurons produced a genome-wide transcriptional near-null: only three downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 23 measured cell groups, and each responding group had a single significant gene.
direction_pattern: Dync1h1 up in 012; Pithd1 up in 052; Zcchc18 down in 110; all 20 other groups null

canonical_summary: The 012 MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic aggregate carried a Dync1h1-only increase after Pou3f3 perturbation.
The Pvalb Pithd1 increase and hypothalamic Zcchc18 decrease were singleton Pou3f3 effects, but each recurred in at least one other perturbation in the same cell group.
The measurable POU-family and layer-neighbor comparators Pou3f4 and Rorb did not phenocopy Pou3f3.
Pou3f3 perturbation failed to recover the embryonic Brn1/2 Cdk5-migration or cortical layer-marker program in the cortical excitatory groups.
The sparse postnatal LoF signature separates POU3F3-related developmental disease from acute young-adult neuronal transcript maintenance.
direction_pattern: disease program absent in acute P16 LoF transcriptomes

canonical_summary: Pou3f4 produced an almost flat postmitotic neuronal DE surface, with only two single-gene FDR<0.10 responses across 22 measured cell groups and no recovery of the canonical Epha4/Efnb2 or Gjb2/Gjb6 otic programs.
A restricted CNU-MGE GABA response consisted of Grin2b down-regulation and no broader FDR-supported synaptic module.
A restricted MB P MY GABA response consisted of Myo9a down-regulation.
The top full-transcriptome positive and negative neighbors of Pou3f4 had absolute signed-score cosine values below 0.031 and did not share the Grin2b or Myo9a responder genes.
The represented POU/Eph literature relatives Pou3f3 and Epha4 did not phenocopy Pou3f4 in matched P16 neuronal cell groups.
Pou4f3 loss of function produced a uniform FDR-level null across every measured postnatal brain neuronal class.
Canonical Pou4f3 hair-cell targets and cell-death readouts were absent from the Pou4f3 brain-neuron DE surface.
Represented ATOH1–GFI1–POU4F3/GATA3 network perturbations were also essentially flat in the same brain-neuronal assay.
The unbiased Pou4f3 signature-neighbor search returned only near-zero similarities and no shared FDR-level genes.
Pou5f1 loss-of-function is a pan-neuronal transcriptional null in the P16 to P37-44 assay: all 22 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical OCT4-SOX2-NANOG and extraembryonic escape programs were absent rather than merely weak.
Represented pluripotency and POU-family relatives did not phenocopy Pou5f1.
A blind neighbor search found no coherent Pou5f1-like module: the best whole-surface cosine was only 0.035 and one top neighbor was a Safe_target label.
Pou6f2 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.
Pou6f2 had no meaningful full-surface positive or negative signature neighbor across all represented targets; the strongest centered score correlations were close to zero.
Screen-represented POU targets did not phenocopy Pou6f2 or reveal a generic acute POU-family response in P16 brain neurons.
Canonical ocular, kidney, and GnRH-linked Pou6f2 programs were not recovered in the sampled brain screen.
Ppara is a pan-neuronal transcriptional null in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR screen: 22 measured cell groups contained zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Loss of Ppara failed to move the expected fatty-acid transport, beta-oxidation, ketogenesis, and triglyceride-clearance target mRNAs.
Hippocampal-inclusive glutamatergic groups did not recover the reported PPARA-CREB/BDNF/NMDA plasticity program.
The literature-obvious PPAR/RXR neighborhood was also almost flat and did not phenocopy Ppara.
A model-wide signature search returned no meaningful Ppara neighbor.
A sterol transcription factor, Srebf2, produced a cholesterol-biosynthetic response in the same neuronal DE universe where Ppara was silent.
Ppard loss of function was a whole-surface neuronal transcriptomic null: all 23 recovered groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical PPAR/RXR fatty-acid oxidation, lipid-droplet, desaturation and elongation transcripts were not altered by Ppard perturbation in any neuronal group.
Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor literature-obvious PPAR/RXR-family targets converged with Ppard; all whole-surface score correlations were near zero.

The screen separates two PPARδ therapeutic priors from basal wild-type neuronal LoF: neither the HD-like mitochondrial/neuropeptide program nor the myelin fatty-acid program appeared after Ppard editing.
P16 Pparg loss produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 20 recovered juvenile neuronal cell groups.
Canonical lipid/adipogenic PPARgamma targets and candidate oxidative, UPR/ISR, autophagy, and immediate-early secondary programs were not FDR-significant after Pparg perturbation.
PPAR paralogs, RXR partners, nuclear-receptor coactivators, retinoid receptors, and Ppargc1a did not phenocopy a Pparg module because the matched surfaces were flat or singleton-only.
The nearest data-driven positive and negative Pparg signature neighbors were only weakly correlated and carried no robust downstream programs.
The Pparg null in basal NeuN-enriched nuclei should not be read as a negative test of PPARgamma agonist neuroprotection.
Ppargc1a acute CRISPR loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic signature in any recovered neuronal group.
The basal Ppargc1a null uncoupled PGC-1α from downstream mitochondrial transcription factors that were active in the same parquet.
direction_pattern: Ppargc1a flat; Nrf1 and Esrra responsive

canonical_summary: The expected PV-interneuron PGC-1α program was absent in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Ppargc1a had no credible data-driven cross-perturbation signature neighbor.
Htt loss-of-function did not reproduce a Ppargc1a-loss signature in this juvenile neuronal CRISPR readout.
Acute Ppib loss was a pan-neuronal transcriptional non-responder: 22 of 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 non-Ppib genes at FDR<0.10 despite consistently negative Ppib self-transcript logFCs.
The expected ER-stress, ER-redox, UPR, autophagy, and apoptosis reporters were absent after Ppib perturbation.
No collagen-processing or PCP-complex transcriptional module accompanied Ppib loss in NeuN-enriched brain nuclei.
Ppib did not phenocopy the measurable immunophilin/calcineurin axis: Fkbp1a and Ppp3cc were null, while Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1 responded where Ppib remained flat.
Ppib lacked a reproducible whole-transcriptome neighbor: the largest positive and negative score-vector cosines were only 0.030 and -0.018.
Ppip5k2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured postnatal brain-neuron group.
The data-driven Ppip5k2 signature neighbors were tiny whole-profile correlations and collapsed to flat signatures on direct re-query.
Tsc2, but not Ppip5k2, triggered a sterol/lysosomal/stress transcriptional module in postnatal neurons.
The PPIP5K2-InsP8-XPR1 phosphate-efflux axis did not appear as a durable gene-expression program.
The deafness-linked PPIP5K2 mechanism is not phenocopied by acute brain-neuron full-gene LoF.
