Ppm1g produced an FDR-supported downstream response in only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where 3 genes passed FDR<0.10; the other 21 measured neuronal groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The strongest Ppm1g thalamic responders were Col4a2 and Col4a1, both down, defining an extracellular-matrix-like collagen IV signal rather than a canonical spliceosome, p53, p38, UPR/ISR, or heat-shock RNA program.
H2ac25 was up in the same thalamic Ppm1g cells in which Col4a1 and Col4a2 were down, making a single H2A-family transcript an exploratory marker of the Ppm1g response.
155 MB Glut showed a strong decrease of the Ppm1g transcript with no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Full-transcriptome data-driven neighbors of Ppm1g in 151 TH were rejected because the best z-scored correlations were only r=0.046 and r=-0.0416; a three-gene restricted search instead placed Ppm1g on a recurrent Col4a1/Col4a2/H2ac25 axis with a partial same-direction Elp1 signature and an opposite-collagen Hnrnpu signature.
Ppp2r5d, the represented B56delta-family comparator for the reported PPM1G-B56delta holoenzyme, was flat in 151 TH and showed its few downstream DEGs in different glutamatergic groups.

Represented Mtor and Map2k6 perturbations did not recover the Ppm1g thalamic Col4a/H2ac25 signature, and Ppm1g itself did not induce RNA-visible p38, p53, UPR/ISR, heat-shock, or translation-marker genes.
Ppp2r2b perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
Ppp2r5d/B56delta did not converge with Ppp2r2b despite being the other assayed PP2A regulatory-subunit target.
Ppp2r2b loss was uncoupled from the broad Opa1 mitochondrial-response surface and from the flat Mff, Mapt, Prkar1a, and Dnm1 surfaces.
Whole-universe signature-neighbor analysis found no strong positive or negative Ppp2r2b neighbor.
The basal Ppp2r2b null redirects Bbeta2 neuroprotection hypotheses toward injury challenge, phospho-Drp1, and mitochondrial-morphology assays.
Ppp2r5d loss produced a very sparse superficial intratelencephalic response: 3 downstream FDR<0.10 genes total, restricted to 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
direction_pattern: Cdadc1 and Zdhhc8 down in 007; Nrsn2 up in 009

canonical_summary: Zdhhc8 down-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut is the only exact Ppp2r5d downstream gene that recurred for another perturbation, Mef2c, in the same cell class.
direction_pattern: Zdhhc8 down in both Ppp2r5d and Mef2c 007 signatures

canonical_summary: Canonical PPP2R5D-associated AKT-mTOR/RPS6 and tau/CDK5/GSK3beta mechanisms were absent at the snRNA transcript level after Ppp2r5d loss.
direction_pattern: expected phosphorylation modules not transcriptionally induced

canonical_summary: Ppp2r5d did not phenocopy represented PP2A, mTOR, or tau-pathway relatives; Tsc2 generated 636 FDR<0.10 genes in nine groups whereas Ppp2r5d was flat in the largest Tsc2-responsive groups.
direction_pattern: divergent from Tsc2; no convergence with Ppp2r2b or most pathway comparators

canonical_summary: Whole-transcriptome signature-neighbor analysis placed Ppp2r5d at the correlation noise floor: the strongest non-safe positive neighbors were Fxr1, Cltc, and Notch2 with r=0.033-0.035, and the strongest negative neighbors were Fbxo11, Cog4, and Tspoap1 with r=-0.028 to -0.018.
The weak pan-Ppp2r5d loss-of-function transcriptome warns against treating WT LoF as a Jordan-syndrome surrogate for therapy testing.
direction_pattern: no broad acute stress transcriptome after partial WT LoF

canonical_summary: Ppp3ca loss produced a very small resting transcriptomic surface and did not turn on a canonical NFAT, immediate-early, or ISR/UPR program.

The robust Ppp3ca response was confined to 2 of 22 measured cell groups: one Zbtb11 hit in L4/5 IT cortex and a five-gene mixed secretory/signaling/lipid signature in TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
Pcsk1n is the clearest recurrent Ppp3ca/Ppp3r1 readout in TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
Ppp3r1 is the nearest Ppp3ca neighbor but is not interchangeable with Ppp3ca.
Ppp3cc, the represented catalytic-subunit paralog, did not phenocopy Ppp3ca.
Upstream calmodulin perturbations were gene-specific and not a simple proxy for Ppp3ca loss.
Ppp3ca loss separated calcineurin from calcium-entry and immediate-early transcriptional programs.
The strongest negative Ppp3ca signature neighbors were too weak to define a convincing anti-calcineurin state.
NFAT-family and major CaM-activated kinase/PKC/IP3R comparators were flat or nonoverlapping.
The screen argues that acute postmitotic Ppp3ca loss is not sufficient to create a broad cell-autonomous disease transcriptome over 3-4 weeks.
Ppp3cc did not produce a robust nuclear transcriptomic response in any measured neuronal class.

The Ppp3cc null is isoform-selective rather than a universal inability to detect calcineurin perturbation: Ppp3ca and Ppp3r1, but not Ppp3cc, produced weak mixed-direction signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
A constitutive calcineurin-to-NFATC3 transcriptional module was not recovered.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no hidden Ppp3cc-like transcriptomic module.
The reported PPP3CC neuropsychiatric link is not phenocopied by acute juvenile neuronal Ppp3cc loss as a robust resting transcriptome.
Ppp3r1 loss produced a strict thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic transcriptomic response: 14 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero in every other measured cell group.
The thalamic signature contained one direct calcium-handling effector, Atp2a2/SERCA2, down-regulated with Ppp3r1, but lacked robust NFAT-feedback or immediate-early transcriptional activation.
Ppp3r1 perturbation shifted a synapse, neurite, and cytoskeletal remodeling module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Ptprs, Kalrn, and Sez6 rose, while Slc6a17, Cntnap5b, Coro6, and Septin4 fell.
Pcsk1n was the strongest Ppp3r1-induced transcript in the thalamic response and the only downstream transcript shared in the same direction with Ppp3ca perturbation.

Same-pathway calcineurin perturbations did not phenocopy Ppp3r1: Ppp3ca gave only five thalamic downstream genes and shared Pcsk1n alone, while Ppp3cc, Nfatc3, and strongly knocked-down Fkbp1a were transcriptionally flat.

The unbiased nearest neighbors of the 14-gene Ppp3r1 thalamic signature were non-calcineurin targets: Atxn2, Kdm5c, and Nrg2 in the positive direction; Npr2, Far1, and Auts2 in the negative direction.

NMDAR and CaMKII perturbations had response surfaces separable from Ppp3r1: Grin1 was much broader in the same thalamic group, Grin2a/Grin2b responded mainly in cortical IT neurons where Ppp3r1 was flat, and Camk2 paralogs did not recreate the Ppp3r1 thalamic state.

Upstream calmodulin genes did not behave interchangeably with Ppp3r1 in the responder: Calm1 had its own 20-gene thalamic signature and moved Coro6 opposite to Ppp3r1, while Calm2 and Calm3 produced no thalamic downstream genes.
Acute Ppt1 loss produced a pan-neuronal downstream null: 0 non-Ppt1 FDR<0.10 genes in every one of 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
Ppt1 perturbation did not induce the expected lysosomal/autophagy, UPR/ISR, immediate-early, or synaptic-vesicle RNA programs in any measured neuronal group.
The all-gene Ppt1 signature had no strong data-driven neighbor: the leading non-synthetic positive and negative correlations across 1,772 alternate targets were all |r|<0.04.

Represented NCL/lysosomal perturbations failed to converge with Ppt1: Grn, Atp13a2, Dnajc5, Lamp2, Psap, and Ctsb each had Ppt1 correlations between -0.00465 and 0.0111, and none produced a shared multi-group neuronal FDR module.
Prdm10 had real but restricted downstream signal: 11 of 23 measured cell groups had ≥1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with strongest counts in thalamic, midbrain, HYa/HY, MB/P/MY GABA, and Pvalb groups.
The Prdm10 signature is dominated by recurrent down-regulation of Madd, Cadm3, Ptov1, Myt1, Stmn2, Uchl1, Ackr1, Hap1, Psip1, and Them6 across the 11 responder groups.
Prdm10 loss reduced neuronal connectivity and membrane-excitability genes, including Cadm3, Stmn2, Kcnt1, Shisa7, Plxna3, Celsr3, Ephb2, and Syn1, in the responder groups.
The canonical PRDM10-EIF3B global-translation axis and major ISR/UPR markers were absent from the neuronal DE surface.
Prdm10 LoF only partially engaged the PRDM10-FLCN axis: Flcn was down in Pvalb and MB Glut, but canonical TFEB/TFE3 lysosomal targets did not rise.

A small posterior autophagy/mitophagy compensation appeared in the strongest groups: Wdr45 was up in 151, 155, and 191, with Pink1 and Atp6v0a1 up only in 151 while Mlst8 was down in 151, 155, and 191.
Psmc1, Psmb4, and Uba5 were the strongest positive cross-perturbation neighbors of the 204-feature Prdm10 signature.
Sin3a and Wdr26 were top net-negative Prdm10 neighbors, opposing genes such as Hap1, Madd, Myt1, Plxna3, Shisa7, Rnasek, and Uchl1 in matched responder groups.
Represented PRDM-family perturbations did not phenocopy Prdm10: Prdm16 and Prdm5 were flat, and Prdm2 had one non-overlapping Pvalb gene.
Madd was repeatedly down after Prdm10 perturbation, yet Madd perturbation itself was almost transcriptionally silent and shared none of the 204 Prdm10-significant features.
Prdm16 loss of function was transcriptionally inert in the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal screen: all 23 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected PRDM16 radial-glia and progenitor effector genes were explicitly absent: Pdzrn3, Mycn, Smoc1, Foxj1, Ppargc1a, Sox2, Pax6, Eomes, Mki67, and Dcx all had FDR=1.0 in every Prdm16 cell-group test.
The P16 neuronal assay was capable of detecting a PRDM-family response, because Prdm10 produced 204 FDR<0.10 downstream genes while Prdm16 and Prdm5 produced none.
A PRDM16-linked lissencephaly or microcephaly mechanism is most consistent with a progenitor-stage defect, not with an ongoing pan-neuronal transcriptomic requirement after P16.
Global cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Prdm16 signature neighbor: the largest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.038 and the largest negative was r=-0.021.
Prdm2 loss produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic hit: Tnrc6a up-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Prdm2 perturbation was buffered across the juvenile NeuN+ brain: only 1 of 371796 downstream tests reached FDR<0.10 and every measured on-target Prdm2 transcript had FDR 1.0.
Prdm2 was not interchangeable with represented PRDM-family or H3K9-writer targets.
The Pvalb Tnrc6a hit did not behave like a core miRNA-effector loss state.
Data-driven Prdm2 signature neighbors were numerically near zero and did not reveal a hidden convergent module.
Prdm5 loss-of-function produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups in the basal P16-to-P37/44 screen.
Canonical PRDM5 target programs, including collagen/SLRP extracellular matrix genes, Wnt/cell-cycle readouts, and the striatal Mgll transcript, were absent from the Prdm5 FDR surface.
Prdm10, but not Prdm5 or Prdm16, produced a multi-cell-type neuronal PRDM-family signature in the same analysis universe.
Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 generated thalamic Wnt-effector signatures where Prdm5 was flat, separating Prdm5 loss from direct Wnt-transducer loss in this postmitotic neuronal assay.
Prdx1 produced an isolated CTX-CGE GABA response: Luc7l3 was the only downstream gene below FDR 0.10 and was lower after perturbation.
Prdx1 loss did not induce the expected oxidative-stress, NRF2, thioredoxin/peroxiredoxin compensation, ISR, or apoptosis transcripts in any measured neuronal group.
Literature-obvious stress and redox comparators represented in the parquet--Nfe2l2, Gpx4, Nfkb1, and Trp53--were themselves flat and did not converge with Prdx1.
A data-driven whole-universe neighbor search found no meaningful Prdx1 signature neighbor; the closest coding-gene cosine was only +0.035 and the strongest coding-gene anticorrelation was -0.016.

Prep loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of 23 measured neuronal cell groups, despite mild-to-moderate negative Prep mRNA shifts and one significant self-transcript decrease in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The basal Prep knockout surface did not contain an alpha-synuclein, autophagy-lysosomal, or proteostatic transcriptional program, including in the 215 MB Dopa group.

Neither the PREP-like/family targets nor neuropeptide-processing and inositol-signaling targets phenocopied a strong Prep module; Prep nearest-neighbor cosines on its top subthreshold genes were very small and bracketed by safe controls.
Prep LoF left selected autophagy-marker transcripts and synaptic/neuropeptide transcripts at FDR=1 across all measured groups.
Acute P16 Prepl perturbation was completely downstream-buffered by nuclear RNA criteria: every one of the 21 measured neuronal groups had zero non-Prepl genes at FDR<0.10.
Prepl loss did not phenocopy AP-1/clathrin disruption: Ap1b1, Ap1s2, and Prep were essentially flat, whereas Cltc produced 173 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across eight matched neuronal groups.
The mitochondrial arm of PREPL biology was not recovered as a neuronal nuclear transcriptome: Prepl was downstream-null and Ndufv2/Ndufs4/Ndufa9 did not converge with it.
The data-driven Prepl neighbors were only vanishing score correlations, with top positive r=0.0299 and top negative r=-0.0220; their DE surfaces were also null or one-gene isolated.
Hippocampal Prepl perturbation did not evoke the RNA signatures one might expect from AD-oriented PREPL knockdown models: both hippocampal glutamatergic groups were FDR-null downstream.
Acute P16 Prickle1 loss produced a two-cell-class, one-gene-per-class response rather than a broad neuronal RNA program.
Tigar was a robust but isolated Prickle1-induced marker in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
Fbxo44 was selectively down-regulated after Prickle1 perturbation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Prickle1 had no meaningful global signature neighbor; its exact robust Tigar and Fbxo44 calls were unique in the screened universe.
Represented Wnt/PCP comparators Celsr2, Fzd6, Ror2, and Ryk did not phenocopy Prickle1 in the two responder cell groups.
Prickle1 loss did not derepress a canonical Wnt beta-catenin target program.
Prickle1 disease biology was not expressed as a broad acute neuronal stress or Wnt RNA state after juvenile mosaic loss.
Prkaa2 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal cell group.

Prkaa2 was uncoupled from the AMPK-mTOR/TSC branch in this assay: Prkaa2, Prkag2, Strada, Mtor and Rptor were flat or nearly flat, whereas Tsc2 produced hundreds of DE gene-cell rows with no correlation to Prkaa2.
An unbiased full-parquet neighbor search found no meaningful Prkaa2 signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Prkaca perturbation produced a detectable target-transcript decrease but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups.
The strongest data-driven Prkaca neighbors were only near-zero cosine matches and did not reveal a convergent downstream module.
Direct and upstream cAMP/PKA relatives were flat or single-gene sparse rather than phenocopying Prkaca or showing the expected Prkar1a anti-phenocopy.
The Hedgehog/Gli transcriptional program expected from embryonic complete PKA loss was not recovered after postnatal Prkaca perturbation.
Creb1 perturbation was transcriptionally visible, with recurrent Crem up-regulation, but Prkaca loss did not induce or suppress CREB/immediate-early readouts.
The neuronal Prkaca loss-of-function null is directionally unlike major PRKACA disease alleles, which are constitutive-gain or fusion events in non-neuronal tissues.

Prkag2 produced a sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptional response: one FDR<0.10 gene, Faf1, decreased in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, while every other measured Prkag2 cell group had zero downstream DE genes.
The lone Prkag2-regulated transcript, Faf1, points to a VCP-linked ER-associated degradation adaptor rather than to a canonical multi-gene AMPK, mTOR, glycogen, or autophagy module.

Prkag2 did not phenocopy represented AMPK-mTOR-axis perturbations: Prkaa2 and Rptor were FDR-flat, Mtor had only six downstream genes in two non-CTX-CGE groups, and Tsc2 fired strongly in several groups where Prkag2 was null but not in CTX-CGE GABA.

The data-driven Prkag2 signature-neighbor search found no robust neighbor: the top positive and negative score correlations were only 0.0255 for Nrxn1 and -0.0128 for Cspp1, and neither shared the Faf1 CTX-CGE hit.

A juvenile brain Prkag2 loss-of-function perturbation did not recover the transcriptome expected from activating PRKAG2 cardiomyopathy models: no glycogen-storage, oxidative-metabolism, survival, fibrosis, mTORC1, or multi-gene autophagy program appeared downstream of Prkag2.
Prkar1a loss-of-function was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: 21 of 21 recovered cell groups had zero non-target downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected CREB/immediate-early and mTOR-autophagy RNA outputs were absent after Prkar1a perturbation.
Prkar1a, its represented catalytic partner Prkaca, and represented AKAP localizers were buffered at the downstream RNA level.
Downstream CREB/CBP, mTOR, and PDE-family perturbations generated small cell-type-restricted signatures that Prkar1a did not phenocopy.
The nearest whole-transcriptome Prkar1a signature neighbors were essentially background-level, and safe-target perturbations were the strongest anti-neighbors.
Prkca is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic non-responder in this postmitotic basal CRISPR screen.
The measurable transcripts closest to PKCα signaling did not move after Prkca perturbation.
Transcriptome-wide neighbor search found no convincing Prkca-like signature.
The only represented conventional paralog, Prkcg, and nearby synaptic targets failed to phenocopy Prkca.
The Prkca LoF null does not model Alzheimer-linked PKCα gain of function.
Prkcg produced a singleton-positive DE surface: only Sestd1 in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Speg in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and Etv5 in 308 CB GABA passed downstream FDR<0.10 across 21 measured groups.
The 308 CB GABA Etv5 decrease is the only Prkcg edge that falls in the cell group closest to canonical Purkinje-cell biology and points to a weak ERK/ETS-compatible transcriptional readout.
Canonical Purkinje synapse transcripts stayed flat in Prkcg-perturbed 308 CB GABA despite the Etv5 edge.
Robust Prkcg self-transcript reductions in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Data-driven neighbor searches did not identify a strong Prkcg-like perturbation; the closest genome-wide neighbors in the three responder groups had score-cosine magnitudes below 0.06, and Ogt shared only the 066 Speg decrease while carrying hundreds of additional DE genes.

The assayed conventional-PKC paralog Prkca and the assayed Purkinje mGluR/Ca2+/MAPK-neighbor comparators Grm1, Plcb1, Itpr1, Cacna1a, Grid2, Mapk1, and Raf1 failed to reproduce Prkcg's transcriptional edges in 308 CB GABA.
Acute Prkcg LoF at P16 did not reproduce a SCA14-like stress or synaptic transcriptome in young nuclei.
Prkdc loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a p53, heat-shock, or DNA-repair stress state in the unchallenged P16-to-P37/44 brain.
Canonical secondary reporters of unrepaired DNA damage were absent: 0 of 1,012 queried p53/apoptosis, ISR/heat-shock, interferon, and immediate-early gene tests were FDR-significant.
Represented DNA-damage relatives did not phenocopy Prkdc: Atr and Trp53 were also flat, while Mtor produced a small TH/midbrain signature where Prkdc had zero FDR-significant genes.
Screen-wide restricted-signature neighbors of Prkdc were essentially zero-correlation and were rejected as biological phenocopies.
The absence of a basal neuronal stress signature should not be read as evidence that DNA-PK inhibition is harmless to neurons during radiotherapy or other DSB-inducing exposures.
Prlr perturbation produced an isolated Spcs1 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, the only downstream FDR<0.10 event in the screen for this target.
The basal juvenile neuronal Prlr perturbation did not recover the canonical PRLR-JAK/STAT-SOCS transcriptional program in any measured group.
Neither the weak data-driven neighbors nor PRLR-adjacent STAT, PI3K/Src, and class-I-cytokine-receptor perturbations phenocopied the Prlr Spcs1 response.

Prnp loss produced an extremely sparse neuronal snRNA-seq response: only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured cell groups, one in CNU-MGE GABA and one in CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic neurons.
CNU-MGE GABA neurons selectively up-regulated Dnajc27, a DNAJ/HSP40-family gene, after Prnp perturbation.
CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic Prnp perturbation uniquely decreased Setd1b while also decreasing Prnp itself.
Prnp did not phenocopy measurable PrP-synaptic, PrP-shedding, amyloid, or myelin-maintenance pathway partners such as Grm5, Fyn, Grin1, Adam10, Adgrg6, App, Ncam1, Lrp1, or Psen1.
Even where Prnp mRNA was significantly depleted, Prnp loss produced no UPR/ISR, heat-shock, or neuronal injury transcriptome.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search placed Prnp in practical isolation: the best positive and negative whole-surface neighbors had score correlations near zero and failed matched-gene validation.
Prop1 loss of function produced a global postmitotic-neuron null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical PROP1 targets and pituitary-output genes were not detectably redistributed in any Prop1-perturbed neuronal group.
Within the PROP1 pituitary EMT module, Zeb2 retained a small neuronal DE surface whereas Prop1, Pou1f1, Hesx1, Lhx3, Lhx4, Notch2, Gli2, and Otx2 were flat in the same 22 groups.
P16 Prox1 loss of function yielded a real transcriptional response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 response included an up-regulated secreted and extracellular-matrix module.
Prox1 perturbation shifted neuromodulatory and excitability-related transcripts in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 signature also contained endomembrane, vesicle, and mitochondrial-trafficking remodeling.
The Prox1 thalamic response did not phenocopy the represented thalamic terminal-selector perturbation Tcf7l2.
Significant cross-perturbation overlap was dominated by broad signatures that oppose Prox1, while positive neighbors were weak.
The screen did not recover Prox1's canonical dentate/Wnt/Notch or CGE-interneuron programs.

Prpf6 produced a real but sharply graded postnatal neuronal response: 11 of 21 measured groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the two largest surfaces, 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, contributed 2306 of the 3142 significant downstream genes.
Responding Prpf6 cells activated a compensatory RNA-processing module rather than simply losing spliceosome transcripts.
The literature-obvious spliceosome-process neighbors Cdc40, U2af2, Snrnp70, and Rnpc3 converged with Prpf6 in the same strongest midbrain/thalamic responders.
The two strongest data-driven positive neighbors of Prpf6 were proteasome subunit perturbations, Psmc1 and Psmb4, not spliceosome factors.
Prpf6 induced a p53/DNA-damage-apoptosis arm in a subset of responders, with the clearest signal in 155 MB Glut.
The broad positive RNA/stress response was paired with a recurrent downshift of mature synaptic, ion-handling, and neuronal-identity transcripts.
Nuclear-pore and SR-protein import perturbations were unexpected positive neighbors of the Prpf6 signature.
A postmitotic-neuron PRPF6 loss signature argues for neuronal-liability testing of any anti-PRPF6 cancer strategy.
Prpf6 lacked a robust inverse transcriptomic neighbor in the measured perturbation universe.
A smaller mitochondrial and redox quality-control arm accompanied the RNA and proteasome modules.
Acute P16 Prr12 perturbation was transcriptomically silent across the recovered postmitotic mouse-brain neuronal surface.

Prr12 did not phenocopy represented cohesin and chromatin comparators; Smc1a and Stag2 triggered overlapping 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signatures while Prr12 had only a weak sub-threshold best gene in the same group.
A Prr12 rank-signature module was not recovered: the nearest genome-wide neighbors had correlations close to zero and inconsistent FDR surfaces.
P16 mosaic Psap perturbation produced a pure on-target/self-transcript signal with no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of 20 measured neuronal groups.
The Psap null surface contained no TFEB/CLEAR, autophagy, cathepsin, v-ATPase, or ISR transcriptional rebound.

Represented PSAP-related lysosomal perturbations did not phenocopy Psap: Asah1, Ppt1, Ctsb, Atp6v0a1, and Manba were flat, and Grn, Sort1, Lamp2, Scarb2, Tmem106b, and v-ATPase subunits generated only isolated islands of downstream DE.
Agnostic cross-target signature search found no robust positive or negative Psap neighbor; all absolute cosines were below 0.04 after excluding self-gene rows.
Acute Psen1 loss produced no neuronal FDR-supported downstream transcriptome in any recovered cell group.
The flat surface extends to literature-predicted Notch, APP/secretase, lysosome-autophagy, UPR/ISR, and synaptic marker transcripts.
Psen1 lacked a meaningful data-driven signature neighbor despite a genome-scale comparator search.
Measured APP/Notch/Ctnnb1 pathway-neighbor perturbations did not rescue a hidden Psen1-like signature.

Psmb4 is a broad neuronal responder but not an all-neuron responder: 18 of 20 measured groups had FDR<0.10 DE, yet the signal ranged from 2,489 genes in 155 MB Glut to one gene in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and zero in the two hippocampal glutamatergic groups.
Psmb4 loss induced a proteasome bounce-back program, with other 20S, 19S, and PA200/regulatory PSM genes up-regulated in 15 cell groups.
The strongest Psmb4 responders co-activated integrated-stress, heat-shock, and redox defenses, including Ddit3, Ppp1r15a, Zfand2a, Hspa1a/Hspa1b, Hspb1, Hmox1, Mt1/Mt2, and small-Maf genes.

A p53/mitochondrial-apoptosis-like RNA module was superimposed on the proteostasis response, with Bax, Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Ccng1, Apaf1, Pmaip1, and Bid induced in overlapping caudal and inhibitory populations.
Psmb4 perturbation also induced an autophagy/lysosome and ubiquitin-handling arm, including Sqstm1, Optn, Gaa, Atp6v1h, Nploc4, Rab21, Uchl1, and high Atp13a4 in the largest caudal signatures.

Across broad and thin responders, neuronal-activity and synaptic genes were repressed, including recurrent down-regulation of Syt1, Syt7, Atp1a3, Cx3cl1, Gria2, GABA receptor genes, Adam11, Cadm2, and class-specific transporters Slc17a6/Slc17a7/Slc6a1/Slc32a1.
The top data-driven neighbor of Psmb4 was Psmc1, and the 20S beta-7 and 19S ATPase signatures agreed in sign for 5,107 of 5,113 shared significant features.
Basal perturbation of the expected stress regulators and accessory proteostasis genes Nfe2l1, Nfe2l2, Vcp, Atf6, Hspa5, Hspa8, Ube3a, Ube2e2, Usp48, and Sqstm1 did not reproduce the Psmb4 program.
Prpf6 and Tpr were the second and third positive Psmb4 neighbors, but their overlap was much smaller than Psmc1 and concentrated in a shared terminal stress subset.
The model-visible universe contained no strong inverse of the Psmb4 state; the most negative neighbor, Ankrd11, had a cosine of only -0.0188 and a 26-gene opposite overlap.

Psmb4-perturbed neurons activated exactly the compensatory axes that cancer proteasome-inhibitor combinations try to defeat: proteasome bounce-back plus p62/OPTN/lysosomal clearance, alongside pro-apoptotic RNA.
Psmc1 loss produced a large neuronal response, but the burden was concentrated in midbrain, pontine/medullary, hypothalamic and thalamic groups rather than being uniform across the whole brain.
Psmc1 perturbation induced a proteasome/ubiquitin bounce-back module: other 19S and 20S-associated mRNAs and Ubc/Uchl1 rose while the targeted Psmc1 transcript itself usually did not fall.
Psmc1 responders coupled the proteasome bounce-back to endolysosomal, ESCRT and autophagy transcripts.
Heat-shock chaperones and integrated-stress-response genes were induced in the same Psmc1-responsive neurons.
The stress state included p53/apoptotic and redox-defense arms, marked by Bax, Apaf1, Trp53, Cdkn1a/Mdm2 and metallothionein/NRF2-linked genes.

Proteotoxic compensation was paired with recurrent down-regulation of mature neuronal function genes, including ion pumps, vesicle machinery, glutamate receptors, sodium channels and synaptic markers.
Psmb4, the only other assayed constitutive 26S proteasome subunit, was the single strong positive Psmc1 signature neighbor.
Nfe2l1, Vcp, Uchl1 and Uba5 did not phenocopy Psmc1, despite being proteostasis or ubiquitin-system relatives.
Tpr, Prpf6 and U2af2 converged with Psmc1 on a large downstream distress module but not on a same-complex proteasome mechanism.
The acute P16-to-P37/44 Psmc1 CRISPR lesion captured neuronal proteotoxic stress rather than a developmental fate program.
Acute Ptch1 CRISPR loss did not produce any downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected Hedgehog feedback and proliferative marker panel was not induced after Ptch1 perturbation.
Represented Hedgehog receptor, ciliary-transduction, co-receptor and effector perturbations did not reveal a matched neuronal Hedgehog module.
An unbiased whole-surface nearest-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Ptch1.
The Ptch1-SHH-MYCN medulloblastoma axis was not recovered in 308 CB GABA after P16 perturbation.
Acute Ptch2 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class: 23/23 cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The absence of Ptch2 signal extended to measured Hedgehog-pathway neighbors: Ptch1, Gli2, and Gpr161 were fully null, while Smo, Gli1, Ift88, and Cdon produced only isolated one- or two-gene signatures that did not overlap Ptch2.
The whole-universe Ptch2 signature had no meaningful positive or negative nearest neighbor; the best absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations were approximately 0.03.
Ptch2 single-gene loss in healthy juvenile neurons did not mimic oncogenic Patched loss: Ptch1, Gli1 and Hhip were not induced, and Ptch1 perturbation itself was null in the same screen.
Ptchd1 acute P16 mosaic loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of 21 measured neuronal groups.
The expected Patched/Smoothened/GLI module is absent after Ptchd1 perturbation and Ptch1, Ptch2, Smo, Gli1, and Gli2 perturbations do not share the Ptchd1 surface.
The hippocampal synaptic/immediate-early program reported in germline Ptchd1-deficient mice was not reproduced by sparse P16 editing in the two hippocampal-containing glutamatergic groups.
Ptchd1 does not phenocopy the only clear retromer-related comparator response: Vps35 drives a 30-gene thalamic glutamatergic signature where Ptchd1 is flat.
The TRN SK-current axis was not recovered as Kcnn2, Kcnn3, Hcn1, or Hcn2 transcriptional convergence in the sampled non-TRN neuronal groups.
Postsynaptic scaffold and receptor comparators were measured and rejected as Ptchd1 phenocopies in this screen.
Ptchd1 has no strong data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor in the full target universe.
Ptf1a produced no FDR<0.10 downstream DE genes in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.
The embryonic Ptf1a fate-switch program was expected but absent: inhibitory markers and downstream factors, excitatory switch markers, and retinal Ptf1a-effectors were all non-significant.

PTF1/bHLH developmental relatives represented in the screen did not phenocopy Ptf1a: Atoh1, Tcf3, Tcf12, Neurod1, and Lmx1b were flat, while Pax2 and Tcf4 had only one or two FDR<0.10 genes and nearly zero cosine to Ptf1a.
The data-driven nearest-neighbor search found only noise-scale Ptf1a neighbors; absolute signed-score cosine was at most 0.034 among gene targets.
Pth1r loss of function was transcriptionally silent in every measured postmitotic neuronal cell group in the P16-to-P37/44 mouse-brain CRISPR screen.
The canonical PTH1R-to-G protein, adenylyl-cyclase, PKA, PLC, and CREB transcriptional axis was not recovered after neuronal Pth1r targeting.
Data-driven signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Pth1r neighbor in the full perturbation universe.
The P16 neuronal LoF surface did not activate PTH1R skeletal, Wnt, or RANKL/OPG marker programs and therefore does not model the main PTH1R disease axis.
The neuronal basal null should not be used as evidence that PTH1R is non-druggable or inert to agonists.
P16 sparse CRISPR loss of Ptpn11 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The expected chronic ERK-feedback, immediate-early, and major synaptic-mRNA programs were absent after Ptpn11 perturbation.
A small Braf/Map2k1/Ntrk2 downregulated Vgf module appeared in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Ptpn11 was flat on the same genes in the same cell group.
Unbiased cross-target score neighbors of Ptpn11 were noise-level rather than a coherent biological module.
The Ptpn11 null surface is more compatible with allele-, stage-, and lineage-specific RASopathy biology than with a simple postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome.
The only robust Ptpn1 downstream genes were two positive, nonrecurrent cortical IT singletons: Galnt18 in 001 L5-6 IT Glut and Zw10 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
Ptpn1 loss did not produce the expected basal leptin/insulin/JAK-STAT, BDNF-TrkB, or PERK/UPR transcriptional programs in any measured neuronal group.
Ptpn1 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Direct Ntrk2 perturbation was detectable in Pvalb and thalamic glutamatergic neurons, whereas Ptpn1 did not phenocopy Ntrk2 or activate BDNF/TrkB target transcripts.
The druggable PTP1B node is transcriptionally quiet in basal postmitotic neurons despite strong metabolic and neurotrophin priors.
Ptprc produced a pan-neuronal postnatal null: none of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10 after Ptprc perturbation.
The global Ptprc score vector did not join a real perturbational module: the strongest positive and negative cosine neighbors were only 0.050846 and -0.023146, respectively.

CD45-associated and receptor-PTP relatives were directly measurable but did not phenocopy Ptprc in neurons: Cd247, Fyn, Ptprd, Ptprf, Ptprm, Ptprn, Ptprt, Ptpro, and Ptprn2 all had zero or one downstream FDR<0.10 hit across their recovered surfaces and zero shared FDR<0.10 overlap with Ptprc.
The Ptprc neuronal null should not be used to de-risk or deprioritize CD45-directed immune therapies.
Ptprd is a broad nuclear-transcriptome null in this sparse P16 neuronal CRISPR assay: 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Ptprd.

The measured synaptic-adhesion relatives of Ptprd did not form a coherent FDR-level transcriptomic module: Ptprf, Ptprm and Ptprt were flat, and Il1rapl1, Il1rapl2, Ntrk3 and neurexin/neuroligin comparators were null or singleton responders.

The closest data-driven non-safe neighbors of the Ptprd restricted signature were not robust phenocopies: Kif1a was the top positive neighbor and Csnk2b the top negative neighbor, but their real FDR<0.10 effects occurred in groups where Ptprd was FDR-null or only weak.
This dataset provides no high-confidence neuronal mRNA biomarker for Ptprd inhibition: neither Ptprd nor NMDAR/TrkB/PDGFRβ expected genes were FDR-altered after P16 Ptprd CRISPR.

The null across cortical glutamatergic, Pvalb and Sst classes argues that reported Ptprd cortical disease phenotypes are more consistent with shifted production, placement or synaptic function of neurons than with a persistent postmitotic transcriptional state in juvenile surviving neurons.
Ptprf was a pan-measured transcriptional non-responder: every recovered neuronal class had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.
Ptprf did not phenocopy direct NMDAR-subunit perturbation, and the represented LAR-family paralog Ptprd was also flat in this single-gene assay.
Full-universe score matching found no strong positive or negative Ptprf signature neighbor.
The CSPG-LAR axon-regeneration axis has no uninjured whole-brain NeuN+ snRNA pharmacodynamic surrogate in this Ptprf surface.
Ptprm targeting was transcriptomically buffered across the recovered neuronal atlas: every one of the 21 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected cadherin/catenin axis was not reciprocally activated by Ptprm loss: direct Ctnnb1 targeting produced a large thalamic/hypothalamic program and reduced Ptprm and L1cam transcripts, whereas Ptprm targeting produced zero downstream DE genes in the same groups.
Ptprm perturbation did not transcriptionally induce assayed receptor-phosphatase paralogs or adhesion comparators.
An all-target score-vector search found no strong Ptprm transcriptional neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Ptprn2 loss was broadly visible at its own transcript but was almost completely buffered at the downstream nuclear-transcriptome level.
The sole robust downstream mark of Ptprn2 perturbation was Sh2b1 down-regulation in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Ptprn, Insr, Irs1, and Lepr perturbations did not reproduce the Ptprn2-Sh2b1 L5 ET response.
Ptprn2 perturbation did not induce the expected dense-core-vesicle, regulated-secretion, autophagy, lysosomal, or UPR transcriptional compensation programs.
Ptprn2 had no robust genome-wide signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Acute Ptprn loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 21 measured NeuN+ brain cell groups.
Ptprn perturbation did not induce a DCV, neuropeptide, immediate-early, UPR, heat-shock, or autophagy compensation program in any measured group.
The IA-2 paralog Ptprn2 and other secretory/neuropeptide comparators did not converge on Ptprn in matched neuronal groups.
Stxbp1, a core Munc18 vesicle-fusion factor, produced 140 FDR<0.10 genes in Ptprn-matched cell groups whereas Ptprn produced none.
The unbiased cross-target neighbor scan found no meaningful Ptprn transcriptomic neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Ptpro loss produced a single robust downstream hit, Grik5 down-regulation, restricted to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Ptpro was transcriptionally buffered across the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq surface: only 1 non-target gene passed FDR<0.10 in 22 measured groups.
Ogt, the top restricted-signature anti-neighbor, opposed Ptpro at Grik5 in L4-5 IT neurons.
Represented receptor-PTP, RTK, Eph, and kainate-receptor comparators did not reproduce the Ptpro response.
Ptprt loss is a stringent neuronal snRNA-seq null: 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, even though 155 MB Glut showed a significant Ptprt self-transcript decrease.
The direct synaptic substrate target Stxbp1 produced a 140-gene response whereas Ptprt had 0 downstream genes and a Ptprt-Stxbp1 whole-profile correlation of -0.004.
The cancer-linked PTPRT-STAT3 branch was not transcriptionally engaged by Ptprt loss in neurons.
Neither unbiased signature search nor literature-guided relatives produced a robust Ptprt neighbor.

Pura produced a sparse postmitotic neuronal response: 6 of 23 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 53 of 59 significant group-gene calls came from 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
The largest Pura responders induced an axonal/cytoskeletal module, with Nefl up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, plus Tubb2a and Nefh in 151 and Dclk2 in 191.

Pura loss up-regulated a synaptic-adhesion and excitability gene set in the two glutamatergic responder classes, including Cntnap1, Kcna6, Lingo1, Cacng5, Pcdh1, and Slitrk6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Nlgn2, Pcdh7, and Dnm1 in 155 MB Glut.

Multiple Pura-responsive groups carried down-regulation of RNA/chromatin regulators: Ogt and Pnisr fell in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, Setd7 fell in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151, and 155 additionally down-regulated Phf1, Mysm1, and Alkbh6.

Pura responders showed a small, mixed proteostasis/lysosome/secretory response: Fbxo33 was lower in 066 and 151, Gaa and Ctsb were lower in 155, Ubqln2 and Sh3glb2 were higher in 155 and 151 respectively, and Pcsk1n was lower in 066 and 155.

The Pura CRISPR neuronal surface did not recover the expected HeLa PURA-depletion P-body/mitochondrial/autophagy markers: Lsm14a, Ddx6, Sqstm1, Il6st, Stard7, Cox7c, and Fis1 all failed FDR<0.10 across 23 cell groups.

The obvious PUR paralogs did not phenocopy Pura: Purb was the top weak 59-feature Pearson neighbor but had zero exact FDR-significant overlaps with Pura-responsive genes, and Purg was completely flat in this surface.
Unbiased cross-perturbation overlap nominated Zbtb7a, Atxn1, and Tsc2—not a PUR-family axis—as the strongest robust same-direction partners for the Pura thalamic/midbrain module.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 often reversed Pura-responsive cytoskeletal and synaptic genes, including strong Nefl repression in 191 MB P MY GABA where Pura increased Nefl.
Igip down-regulation and Nefl up-regulation are the compact recurring markers of the Pura response: Igip fell in 151, 155, and 308, whereas Nefl rose in 151, 155, and 191.

Represented neuronal RNP/motor partners did not phenocopy Pura: Fmr1, Kif5a, Kif5c, and Myo5a were flat, while Hnrnpu was a broad responder with only weak, mixed overlap to the Pura 59-feature signature.
Purb knockout produced one reproducible nuclear mRNA change: Hnrnpr was down-regulated in 308 CB GABA and no other downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any Purb-tested cell group.

Acute postnatal Purb loss was almost completely buffered at the nuclear transcriptome: 21 of 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the most responsive group had only one.
Purb did not phenocopy the PUR paralogs or nearby RNP-granule comparators represented in the screen.
The smooth-muscle/myofibroblast actomyosin program expected from Purb loss in responsive mesenchymal lineages was absent from every neuronal Purb comparison.
Purg was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function: none of the 22 recovered neuronal groups contained even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

Purg did not phenocopy the neurologically active paralog Pura: Pura produced 59 FDR<0.10 downstream genes across the same 22 groups, whereas Purg produced 0 and was essentially orthogonal to Pura by whole-surface Wilcoxon-score cosine.

The full model-visible target space did not contain a meaningful Purg-like module: the strongest positive and negative whole-surface neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score cosines of only 0.0217-0.0333 and no shared FDR-significant genes with Purg.

Qrich1 loss was not globally silent: it produced an FDR<0.10 response in 11 neuronal groups, with the strongest surface in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and smaller but reproducible signals in midbrain, hindbrain-adjacent, hypothalamic, and Pvalb/MGE GABA groups.

The most diagnostic Qrich1 module was a recurrent downregulated set centered on Ldhd, Scn2b, Celf3, and Tlcd3b; these genes recurred in 8-10 FDR<0.10 groups and all significant instances were negative.

In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Qrich1 loss broadened the same repressive signature into synaptic/cAMP and phosphoinositide signaling, endolysosomal/autophagy, and mitochondrial- or amino-acid/heme-metabolic genes.

The top positive restricted-signature neighbors of Qrich1 were Tnpo3, Ogt, Wac, Psmc1, and Psmb4, not the canonical UPR targets Atf6 or Hspa5; Tnpo3 had the strongest cosine similarity to the Qrich1 FDR signature.

Canonical ER-stress/UPR and ISR transcripts were absent from the Qrich1 DE surface, and represented UPR comparators did not phenocopy it: Atf6 and Nfe2l2 were flat, and Hspa5 had a small distinct surface with zero overlap to the Qrich1 FDR signature.
Rab18 loss produced one FDR<0.10 downstream transcript, Ipo11 up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA, with no corrected downstream genes in the other 20 measured Rab18 groups.

Canonical ER-stress, lipophagy/autophagy, lysosomal, and lipid-homeostasis transcripts were absent after Rab18 perturbation even though the same assay detects lysosomal and sterol programs after Rab7 or Htt perturbation.

The RAB18 GEF subunits Rab3gap1 and Rab3gap2 failed to phenocopy the Rab18 transcriptomic surface: Rab3gap1 was entirely flat, and Rab3gap2 had a different one-gene 191 MB P MY GABA response through Ttbk1 rather than Ipo11.

Rab18 did not sit in a strong global transcriptional module: the top non-safe-target all-feature neighbors were Htt in the positive direction and Ttll5 in the negative direction, but both cosine similarities were near zero.

Genes connected to the embryonic RAB18 neuronal-migration and cytoskeletal phenotype, including Cdh2 and major neuronal cytoskeletal markers, were not transcriptionally changed after postnatal Rab18 loss.

Rab27a was a complete corrected transcriptomic null in all 21 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups: 924 total Rab27a-perturbed nuclei, 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every measured group, and no corrected change in the Rab27a transcript itself.

The whole-signature correlation search nominated no meaningful Rab27a neighbor: the strongest positive score correlations were Mt3, Ndufb7, and Kcnn3 at r=0.0260, 0.0258, and 0.0247, and the strongest biological negative correlations were Kif2a, Nkx6-2, and Trpm3 at r=-0.0249, -0.0208, and -0.0190.

Rab27a diverged from perturbations that the same screen could detect on vesicle and lysosomal axes: Rab7 produced 738 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the 21 Rab27a-matched groups, including lysosomal genes Atp6v1b2, Atp6v0b, Lamp2, Mcoln1, Gba, and Grn, while Stxbp1 produced 140 genes including synaptic genes Nrxn2, Slc30a3, Homer1, Camk2n1, Slc6a1, and Erbb4.

Represented literature-obvious relatives did not rescue a hidden Rab27a-like module: Myo5a, Rab3gap1, Ap3b1, Cplx1, Cplx2, Stx1b, Syt2, and Unc13c each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in Rab27a-matched groups, while Rab3gap2, Rab18, Unc13a, Nsf, Syn1, and Syn2 were only isolated one-gene responders.

The acute neuronal null is concordant with Griscelli genetics that place primary Rab27a pathology in secretory lysosomes of immune and pigment cells rather than in a broad autonomous neuronal mRNA program.
Rab3gap1 perturbation was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: each of the 21 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected proteostasis-autophagy readout was absent: 22 UPR/ISR, lysosomal, and autophagy markers had 0 Rab3gap1 FDR<0.10 hits across all 21 measured cell groups.
The represented Warburg Micro module partners Rab3gap2 and Rab18 converged with Rab3gap1 mainly by being almost flat, not by sharing a transcriptional module.
A core synaptic-vesicle comparator, Stxbp1, produced 140 downstream DE genes whereas Rab3gap1 produced none.
Unbiased whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Rab3gap1 neighbor; the largest feature-centered residual correlations were only +0.0399 and -0.0364.
Rab3gap2 produced a real but extremely restricted Ttbk1 induction in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The represented Rab3GAP-Rab18 relatives did not phenocopy Rab3gap2 in the postnatal neuronal transcriptome.
Rab3gap2 loss did not activate an autophagy, lysosomal, proteostasis, UPR, ISR, or ER-stress transcriptional rebound.
Unbiased signature search found no robust transcriptomic neighbor for Rab3gap2.
052 Pvalb Gaba had a significant Rab3gap2 self-transcript decrease but no downstream genes.
Rab7 was measured in all 23 neuronal cell groups but had downstream FDR<0.10 signal in only 8, with the broad response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
Rab7 loss induced a recurrent late-endosomal/lysosomal compensation module with Atp6v0b and Dpp7 as the most recurrent transcripts.
A sterol/lipid biosynthetic branch was repeatedly induced downstream of Rab7 perturbation.
Rab7 engaged ISR/UPR, amino-acid, autophagy and redox/apoptotic stress transcripts in the broad TH and MB responders.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-regulated multiple proteasome-subunit mRNAs, and Psmb4/Psmc1 were among the strongest positive Rab7 signature neighbors.
The main TH Rab7 responder coupled catabolic stress to a decrease in synaptic, receptor and ion-channel transcripts.
The Rab7 signature aligned with Tsc2 loss and was most inverse to Rptor loss, rather than matching simple lysosomal mTORC1 inhibition.
Transport, ER-calcium and dolichol/isoprenoid pathway perturbations converged with the Rab7 signature.
Measured HOPS, retromer, WASH, V-ATPase and lysosomal comparator targets mostly failed to phenocopy Rab7 at FDR level.
Rab7 acute CNS loss of function elicited lysosomal and lipid stress in young subcortical neurons but should not be equated with dominant human RAB7A CMT2B alleles.
Cpeb1 was a recurrent, non-lysosomal Rab7-induced transcript across hypothalamic, thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responders.
Rac1 loss produced a single robust Sst-restricted RNA event, Ranbp1 up-regulation, instead of a multi-gene Rac actin program.

Postnatal neuronal Rac1 perturbation is transcriptionally buffered: 21 of 22 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes, two of those were only weakly sub-threshold, and the one responder had only Ranbp1.
Represented Rac/Cdc42/PAK/WRC/GEF/GAP relatives failed to phenocopy the Rac1 Sst Ranbp1 event.
Unbiased score-vector search found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Rac1.
P16 Rac1 LoF in mouse neurons did not create the WRC/PAK transcriptomic response one might expect from human activating RAC1 disease alleles.
Rack1 produced a real FDR<0.10 response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Aplp2 and Ppp2r1a were both downregulated.
Rack1 loss failed to induce a durable ISR/UPR, mitochondrial, NMDA-receptor, or astrocyte-Kir4.1-like mRNA program despite the assay detecting such programs in other perturbations.
Neither data-driven signature neighbors nor literature-obvious Rack1 pathway comparators converged on the thalamic Aplp2/Ppp2r1a down signature.
Raf1 produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered neuronal group, despite being measured in 21 of the 23 possible groups.

Raf1 loss did not move the expected ERK immediate-early or feedback reporter panel; Fos, Fosb, Junb, Egr1, Arc, Dusp5, Dusp6, Spry2, Spry4, Etv1, Etv4, Etv5 and Vgf all had FDR 1.0 across Raf1 groups.
The small Braf/Map2k1 thalamic signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was not shared by Raf1.
Raf1 had no strong data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor across the model-visible perturbation universe.
The Raf1 loss-of-function null should not be read as a negative test of activating RAF1 RASopathy alleles or pharmacologic RAF inhibition.
Postnatal Rai1 loss produced its only robust transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, where Slitrk6 and Grik1 were both down-regulated.
The P16 mosaic snRNA-seq Rai1 signature was uncoupled from the canonical Bdnf/Htr2c/Clock and immediate-early programs previously linked to Rai1.

The two Rai1 down-regulated 151 TH genes form a restricted cross-perturbation node: Psmb4 and Ctnnb1 push Slitrk6/Grik1 in the same direction, whereas Zbtb7a pushes both genes in the opposite direction.
Literature-obvious chromatin and path-neighbor targets were active in the assay but did not phenocopy Rai1 in the matched thalamic group.
Rala loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 neuronal classes in which it was recovered.
Canonical effector and pathway sentinel transcripts for RalBP1/exocyst, PAR polarity, AMPAR trafficking, PLD1, and mTOR were present but not corrected-DE after Rala perturbation.
Represented Ras/Rho/Rap relatives and regulators did not reveal a hidden Rala-like transcriptomic module.
Sparse postmitotic Rala loss did not phenocopy RALA neurodevelopmental missense or focal-cortical-dysplasia gain-of-function biology.
The de novo, data-driven nearest Rala signature neighbors were essentially zero-correlation targets rather than interpretable Ral biology.
Ranbp2 loss produced its largest signature in 308 CB GABA, where 202 downstream genes were significant and Purkinje/cerebellar calcium-synaptic genes were mostly induced.
155 MB Glut converted Ranbp2 perturbation into a p53-feedback and proteostasis/RNA-processing response that included Mdm2, Trp53, Ccng1, Psmd2, Derl1, Uba5, Ube2v1, and spliceosome-associated genes.

Among cortical excitatory groups, L5 ET neurons were the only broad responder, with RNA-processing genes and transport/autophagy-linked Wdr45 and Dync1h1 induced while synaptic genes such as Grik2, Rims2, and Cyp46a1 fell.
Pvalb interneurons were the only inhibitory cortical/MGE class with a reproducible Ranbp2 transcriptome: Kcnc1, Exoc1, Syt3, and Myo5b decreased while Eif3l and Eif4g1 increased.

Tpr and Ogt, but not most obvious Ranbp2 biochemical partners, converged with Ranbp2: Tpr shared 66 significant restricted-signature coordinates, Ogt shared 45, and the shared genes were almost all same-direction.
Kif5c, Cox11, Hk1, Kpna3, and Trp53 perturbations did not phenocopy Ranbp2, and the strongest negative data-driven neighbors were globally anti-correlated but FDR-flat on Ranbp2 genes.

The neuronal snRNA screen did not recover the Acc1/Mmp28 chemokine, Hnrnph3 proteostasis, Cox11/Hk1 metabolic, or ANE1-like inflammatory programs predicted from retina, motoneuron, and human ANE1 work.
Three measured Ranbp2 effect groups crossed FDR only as one- or two-gene signatures: Ift20/Ache in L5-6 IT, Rims1/Stau2 in L4-5 IT, and Snhg11 in CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Acute postmitotic Rapgef2 perturbation produced no downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in any of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The embryonic RapGEF2-Rap1/Reelin-cadherin migration branch is absent after postmitotic cortical perturbation; Rapgef2, Dab1, and Vldlr were all 0-DE transcriptional perturbations.
Basal Rapgef2 loss did not connect to the restricted BRAF/MEK/NTRK2 ERK-output signatures seen for Braf, Map2k1, and Ntrk2 perturbations.
NMDAR subunit perturbations were transcriptionally visible whereas Rapgef2, Magi2, Dlg4, and Syngap1 were flat.
Residualized cross-perturbation search found no substantive phenocopy or anti-phenocopy for the Rapgef2 signature.
Rapgef4 produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of its 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Canonical cAMP/EPAC2-Rap, MAPK, AMPAR/NMDAR, neuroligin, postsynaptic, and immediate-early mRNA sentinels were all non-significant after Rapgef4 perturbation.
Rapgef4 full-vector signature neighbors were dominated by other null targets, while broad proteasome-subunit responders were the least similar measured perturbations.
Measured cAMP and synaptic literature comparators did not phenocopy Rapgef4 in a way that exposed an EPAC-like nuclear response.
The Rapgef4 null refines autism-variant and spine findings toward allele- and compartment-specific signaling rather than a required postnatal nuclear mRNA disease program.
The 215 MB Dopa class, the closest screened class to dopamine-neuron Epac2 biology, was not recovered for Rapgef4.
Rarb loss produced a single significant downstream response, Arhgef4 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, with no broad stress, proteostasis, translation, or RA-target module.
The represented RAR/RXR relatives Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb, and Rxrg did not phenocopy the L5 ET Arhgef4 response, and Rxrb's only FDR<0.10 event occurred in a different hypothalamic glutamatergic group.

Rarb perturbation did not recover the expected CNU-LGE/striatal RARβ program: no D1/D2 MSN markers, GABA markers, Meis/Ascl developmental genes, or candidate neuroprotective outputs reached FDR<0.10 in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
Top data-driven signature neighbors of Rarb had tiny signed-score cosines and were rejected as robust phenocopies after direct surface inspection.
Acute P16 Rarg loss produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
RAR/RXR-family perturbations represented in the parquet did not form a convergent Rarg-like module.
The unbiased Rarg nearest neighbors were not meaningful convergent or divergent biology.
Rarg loss did not reproduce the striatal RA program associated in the literature with Rarβ.
Rars2 produced a single corrected downstream hit, Dpysl5 up-regulation, only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The Rars2 perturbation did not recover the mitochondrial translation, OXPHOS, ATF4/ISR or UPRmt transcriptional programs predicted from RARS2 biology.
Literature-obvious mitochondrial-translation relatives Fars2, Lars2 and Gfm2 did not phenocopy the already narrow Rars2 surface.
The unbiased Rars2 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor across 1772 other target surfaces.
Rasa2 is transcriptionally inert in the assayed resting postmitotic neuronal nuclei: every measured group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical Ras/ERK transcriptional echo expected after sustained RasGAP loss was absent: Fos/Jun/Egr, Dusp/Spry, and Etv feedback genes all remained non-significant.

Rasa2 did not phenocopy the represented Ras/MAPK neighbors: the neuronal RasGAP Syngap1 and the negative regulators Spred1/Spred2 were also null, while Braf and Map2k1 produced only sparse downstream DE in matched groups.
The all-null Rasa2 surface is not explained by a globally blunt assay: Ranbp2, Tsc2, and Wdr26 each generated hundreds to thousands of FDR<0.10 genes in the same matched neuronal universe.

The neuronal null should not be generalized to systemic RASA2 inhibition: published RASA2 phenotypes are strongest in mitogenic melanoma and antigen-stimulated T cells, lineages absent from the NeuN-enriched brain screen.
Rax yielded three isolated negative FDR-level events: Gosr2 in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Myl12b in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Mapre2 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
Rax had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, and canonical RAX-network perturbations did not phenocopy its three responder groups.
Rax loss in P16 postmitotic brain neurons did not activate or repress expected retinal, pineal, or hypothalamic transcriptional markers despite those genes being queryable.
Postnatal Rb1cc1 loss produced a sparse neuronal transcriptome: 4 of 21 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and three of those responders were thalamic/midbrain groups.
RB1CC1 loss drove ER protein-folding transcripts downward, not upward, in the two strongest ER-like responders.
The MB Glut Rb1cc1 signature partially converged with Becn1 and Atg5, centered on Calr down and, for Becn1, Ctsb down.
Rb1cc1-responsive MB neurons down-regulated synaptic, ion-pump, and energy genes after P16 perturbation.
Canonical autophagy and lysosome perturbations did not phenocopy Rb1cc1 as a class.
The strongest FDR-backed noncanonical Rb1cc1 neighbor was U2af2, with weaker overlap from Caml, Snrnp70, Thap11, Wac, and Rab7.
Rb1cc1 did not elicit a detectable NRF2, proteasome, SQSTM1, LC3, LAMP1/2, or TFEB transcriptional bounce-back even in the responder groups.
066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed an isolated Dmpk up-regulation and no broader Rb1cc1 stress module.

Rbm28-targeting CRISPR was a broad postnatal neuronal whole-transcriptome null: every one of the 22 measured brain cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the on-target Rbm28 transcript never reached self-FDR significance.

Literature-obvious 60S/rRNA-processing comparators did not phenocopy each other: Las1l was flat like Rbm28, while Nop56 produced a small but real signature of 44 downstream FDR<0.10 genes concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.

The universe-wide Rbm28 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor: even the top signed-score cosines were tiny, with Uba5, Ufc1, and Nop56 at 0.0675, 0.0502, and 0.0378, while top negatives were only about -0.013. UFMylation targets that weakly approached Rbm28 in the continuous ranking produced thousands of DE genes, including Ddit3 induction, that Rbm28 lacked.
Rdx loss produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic event: Stard3nl down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The L5 ET Stard3nl response was Rdx-specific in this atlas and was not reproduced by data-driven neighbors or by α5-GABAA receptor subunit perturbations.
Rdx perturbation uncoupled the canonical α5-GABAA receptor-localization mechanism from a detectable GABAA, gephyrin-scaffold, or immediate-early mRNA program.
Two groups showed significant loss of the Rdx self-transcript but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
Reep1 acute loss was transcriptionally buffered across every measured neuronal group: 23/23 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and FDR<0.25.
Biochemically and genetically related HSP targets did not phenocopy a Reep1-like response in the same screen.
The a priori ER-stress, ERAD, lipid-droplet, and sterol programs expected from REEP1 models were absent across the Reep1 surface.
Unbiased centered signature search found no meaningful Reep1 neighbor; the nearest signatures were safe or sparse perturbations with |r|<0.078.
Juvenile brain snRNA is a poor pharmacodynamic endpoint for proposed REEP1 ER-stress therapies.
Reep2 perturbation produced a self-only FDR signature: the target transcript was significantly lower in five caudal/subcortical groups, but no non-target gene reached FDR<0.10 anywhere.
Unsupervised cross-target signature search found no biologically strong positive or negative Reep2 neighbor.
The literature-obvious ER-shaping and HSP-family comparators Reep1, Atl1, and Spast were as flat as Reep2, while related HSP genes showed at most sparse, non-overlapping hits.
Canonical secondary ER stress, integrated-stress, autophagy-lysosome, redox, mitochondrial-shaping, and lipid-droplet marker genes were not induced by Reep2 loss.
Reg1 perturbation produced no downstream transcript meeting FDR<0.10 in any measured neuronal cell group.
Neither the data-driven nearest neighbors nor represented Reg1-pathway comparators converged on a Reg1 module.
The screen argues against an autonomous requirement for Reg1 in maintaining juvenile neuronal transcription.
Acute Rel loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups.
Rel had no strong cross-perturbation neighbor, and directly queried NF-κB-pathway relatives Nfkb1, Chuk, and Traf3 were also flat.
The MB dopamine Rel perturbation did not reproduce a Parkinsonian redox-survival signature.
The hippocampus/amygdala-enriched 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut group was transcriptionally quiescent after Rel loss.
The lack of a broad acute neuronal Rel-loss signature is only limited reassurance for c-Rel inhibition strategies.
Reln was almost completely buffered at the nuclear transcriptome: only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered neuronal classes.
The only formal Reln responder was 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, where Snrnp48 was down-regulated as a solitary DEG.
The literature-obvious receptor/adaptor targets Vldlr, Lrp8, Dab1, Fyn, Akt3 and App were flat or nearly orthogonal to Reln and did not repeat its Snrnp48 change.
Gsk3b was the one represented downstream pathway target with a real transcriptional surface, but it diverged from Reln.
Reln loss did not recover an LRP8-Reelin enhancer, immediate-early, synaptic-plasticity, or receptor-feedback program.

Acute postnatal Reps1 loss was pan-flat in neuronal nuclei: none of the 22 recovered cell groups had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and only 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut reached merely subthreshold FDR≈0.188 leaders.
Reps1 did not phenocopy Cltc: Cltc loss gave 173 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in eight Reps1-matched groups, whereas Reps1 had zero in those same groups.

The represented Ral/vesicle comparators Dnm1 and Rala were also transcriptionally flat across the 22 Reps1-matched groups; Dnm1 had zero downstream FDR genes even where its own mRNA was strongly reduced.
Reps1 perturbation did not induce a transferrin-receptor or iron-homeostasis mRNA program: Tfrc, Fth1, Hmox1, Ireb2, Ncoa4, Slc11a2, and Aco1 all had FDR=1.0 in every recovered Reps1 cell group.

Whole-signature nearest-neighbor analysis found no robust Reps1 transcriptional module: the strongest complete-coverage positive cosine was only 0.027936 for Celsr2, and the strongest negative cosine was -0.012038 for Sgce.

Acute P16 Rest loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional zero: 23/23 cell groups lacked downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and a 13-gene REST neuronal/stress target panel was measured but never significant.

Rest does not phenocopy measurable REST-adjacent chromatin regulator perturbations: Sin3a, Chd4, Zmynd8, and Mecp2 generated real neuronal signatures, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but their whole-surface correlations with Rest were approximately zero.

The unsupervised Rest signature has no convincing positive or negative module: its nearest whole-surface neighbors were Rax at r=0.0400 and Fbxo11 at r=-0.0476, both near-zero and themselves null or near-null.
Rest loss did not elicit a detectable oxidative-stress, cell-death, Alzheimer-linked, or autophagy/proteostasis-like secondary transcriptome in young baseline neurons.
Postnatal mosaic Ret loss did not produce a robust single-nucleus transcriptional program in any of the 23 assayed neuronal groups.
The most RET-relevant recovered class, 215 MB Dopa, showed only a weak Ret mRNA decrement and no loss of dopaminergic identity, dopamine-handling, mitochondrial, or Parkin-axis transcripts.

The GDNF co-receptor Gfra1 phenocopied Ret as a flat perturbation, whereas other receptor-tyrosine-kinase or downstream signaling perturbations did generate FDR<0.10 genes in the same analysis universe.
Ret's data-driven signature neighbors were weak restricted-signature matches, not reusable biological comparators.
The screen's inert Ret LoF surface should not be read as a MEN2/RET-fusion or systemic RET-inhibition model.

Retreg1 loss produced an almost empty central-neuron transcriptomic surface: only Edf1 up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Srsf7 down in 191 MB P MY GABA reached downstream FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered groups.
Retreg1 perturbation did not induce the expected ER-stress, UPR, ER-phagy, core autophagy, or lysosomal transcriptional compensation program in any recovered group.
Three groups achieved significant Retreg1 mRNA depletion yet still had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The two-gene data-driven Retreg1 signature did not yield a robust transcriptomic neighbor: the formal top same- and opposite-direction targets, Dld and Cacnb2, changed Edf1/Srsf7 in the matched directions only at FDR=1.0.
Represented ER-phagy, macroautophagy, and HSAN2-pathway relatives failed to phenocopy the two Retreg1 downstream hits.
The Retreg1 null surface is more consistent with a peripheral long-axon and FAM134-family-combinatorial vulnerability than with universal CNS soma stress after Retreg1 loss.
Rfx3 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
A literature-derived RFX/ciliary target panel was completely absent from the Rfx3 FDR surface.
Data-driven positive and negative signature neighbors were all near zero and failed the FDR-overlap test.
Represented RFX-family and ciliary effector comparators also failed to reveal a shared acute neuronal ciliary signature.
Rfx7 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The p53-stress RFX7 direct-target module was not transcriptionally engaged after Rfx7 perturbation in juvenile neurons.
Rfx7 did not activate any robust Rfx4 or ciliary sentinel transcript change after postnatal neuronal knockout.
Rfx3, Myc, and represented ciliary machinery perturbations failed to reveal a broad Rfx7-like signature in the matched groups.
Rfx7 lacked a meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor; even the strongest score-neighbors were near zero and did not phenocopy at FDR.
Sparse postnatal neuronal Rgma loss was a broad, adjudicated transcriptional null: no recovered cell group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Rgma perturbation did not recover the canonical BMP-SMAD transcriptional branch or compensatory RGM-neogenin feedback.
Neogenin/BMP-axis relatives did not phenocopy Rgma in the same cell groups.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Rgma transcriptomic module.
The flat healthy-neuron CRISPR phenotype should not be used to de-prioritize extracellular anti-RGMa strategies for injured or demyelinated CNS.
Rgs6 loss-of-function exposed only one FDR<0.10 downstream transcript: Wdfy3 decreased in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Pvalb Wdfy3 decrease was not reproduced by the obligatory R7 partner Gnb5 or by represented GABA_B/GIRK and inhibitory-GPCR perturbations.
The pre-literature top signature neighbors, Map2k1 and Grin2b, were weak restricted-feature matches and did not phenocopy Rgs6 in Pvalb.
Postmitotic basal Rgs6 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in 20 of 21 measured cell groups.

Rho genomically-targeted nuclei were almost transcriptionally inert in sampled juvenile brain neurons: 21 measured cell groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene and the remaining 046 CTX-CGE GABA signal contained only one borderline downstream transcript.
Canonical rod phototransduction transcripts and the ER-stress/ISR/autophagy markers expected from misfolded pathogenic RHO alleles were absent from the Rho DE surface.
Photoreceptor relatives that were measurable as perturbation targets—Gucy2e, Spata7, Crx, Nr2e3, Opn1sw, Rpgr, and Rpgrip1l—also failed to produce FDR<0.10 signatures in the Rho-matched brain groups.

Unbiased Rho score neighbors were numerical rather than biological: the strongest positive and negative full-score cosines were only 0.040 and -0.024 and none reproduced the 046 CTX-CGE GABA Tcerg1 hit.
The only FDR<0.10 Rho downstream event was a Tcerg1 increase in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
Rhot1 CRISPR was uncoupled from the Opa1-like mitochondrial ATF4/ISR program in young postmitotic neurons.
Represented Miro transport and basal fission/autophagy neighbors did not phenocopy Rhot1 at the nuclear-transcriptome level.
The genome-wide Rhot1 signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor.
Postnatal neuronal Ripor2 CRISPR produced a nearly flat transcriptomic surface: 1/21 recovered cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the only such gene was Auts2 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Auts2 was the only Ripor2 downstream DEG, selectively decreasing in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Ripor2 were near zero and did not share an FDR<0.10 gene.
Represented Rho/AUTS2 comparator perturbations did not phenocopy Ripor2.
Ripor2 loss did not induce an expected Rho/actomyosin, HDAC6, stereocilia, or autophagy transcriptional program in any recovered neuronal cell group.
Rlf produced a single significant postnatal neuronal signature: Abhd12b, Gde1, and Atp1b2 were all down only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The Rlf thalamic triad converged most strongly with Cic and Rora perturbations, not with textbook Rlf paralogs or methylation enzymes.
Top negative neighbors in 151 TH drove the Rlf-down genes in the opposite direction, with Ehmt1, Zmynd8, Usp48, and Chd4 up-regulating Abhd12b and Zbtb7a/Chd4 up-regulating Atp1b2.
Zfp292 and other literature-obvious Rlf relatives failed to phenocopy Rlf in 151 TH despite being directly represented in the screen.
Embryonic heart Notch/Jagged and E14.5 fetal-liver Rlf mRNA programs were absent from the P16 neuronal Rlf surface.
Rlim loss was uniformly null across the recovered postnatal neuronal surface: 22 measured cell groups and 371,796 downstream tests produced zero genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical REX1/Xist and LDB/CLIM outputs were not recovered after Rlim perturbation: Ldb1, Ldb2, and Zfp42 were FDR=1 in every measured group, and Xist was absent from the parquet.

The whole-universe nearest neighbors of the Rlim score vector were not meaningful phenocopies: the strongest positive cosine was 0.044, the strongest negative was -0.028, and returning to those targets showed either flat safe/low-hit targets or broad signatures with no Rlim overlap.
Represented LIM-homeodomain partners Isl1, Lhx3, and Lhx4 were also flat in the groups matched to Rlim.
Acute mosaic Rmnd1 perturbation produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
Rmnd1 did not induce the expected ATF4/mitochondrial integrated-stress or mtUPR-like transcriptional program.
Screen-visible mitochondrial-translation and OXPHOS comparators were themselves almost completely flat and did not phenocopy Rmnd1 by a coherent shared transcriptional module.
Unbiased global neighbors of Rmnd1 had near-zero cosine similarity and were led by safe-target or unrelated weak signatures.
Rnf216 had no FDR-supported acute transcriptional effect in any recovered NeuN+ neuronal group.
The TLR/RIG-I/NF-kB/type-I-interferon program predicted from RNF216 innate-immune work was absent.
RNF216-linked BECN1/SQSTM1/autophagy and Arc synaptic-substrate biology did not become a transcriptional compensation module.
Rnf216 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
Core proteasome perturbations cause large neuronal DE surfaces where Rnf216 is flat.
P16 mosaic Rnf220 loss produced a uniform FDR-null neuronal transcriptome: all 23 assayed cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical RNF220 Shh/Gli, ventral-progenitor, EED/WDR5/Hox, and Olig sentinel transcripts were not activated or repressed after Rnf220 perturbation in any measured neuronal group.

RNF220's AMPAR-substrate axis is transcriptionally quiet: Rnf220 did not change Gria1/Gria2/Gria3 mRNAs, and direct Gria1-3 perturbations produced only singleton downstream calls and near-zero correlations to Rnf220.
Tardbp, a represented RNF220 proteolytic substrate, is a broad neuronal responder that does not phenocopy Rnf220.
Canonical beta-catenin/Wnt perturbations could signal in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, whereas Rnf220 remained flat there and globally.
The full ranked Rnf220 signature had no substantive data-driven neighbor among the 1672 non-safe comparator targets with >100000 matched pairs.

Rnpc3 produced significant downstream whole-gene DE in 18 of 21 measured neuronal groups, but the effect was sharply graded and peaked in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
Amy1 down-regulation together with up-regulation of Mapk8, Pcyt2, and Ap2a1 formed a recurrent empirical RNPC3 signature across 13-15 measured groups.
Rnpc3 loss increased rather than decreased several whole-gene RNAs that sit in minor-intron-enriched functional classes, including Mapk8, Mapk10, Pten, and Srsf10.
Rnpc3 induced a vesicle, Golgi, endosomal, and ciliary-trafficking module led by Ap2a1, Wdfy1, Rab6b, Gosr1, Vps9d1, Smap1, Ift122, Ift88, and Trappc10.
Rnpc3 repeatedly up-regulated phospholipid and ER/protein-quality-control genes, including Pcyt2, Derl2, Psma1, Sptssa, Pign, Atp13a2, Hectd2, and Rnf123.

Rnpc3 altered RNA-processing and transcription/export genes: Srp72, Srsf10, Ncbp1/2, Exosc1, Dhx16, Hnrnpm, and Tcea1 tended to increase, whereas Tcea2, Rsrp1, and Srrm2 decreased in the broadest signatures.
The largest Rnpc3 signatures down-regulated neuronal and synaptic maintenance genes, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
Amy1 was the single most recurrent down-regulated gene after Rnpc3 perturbation, appearing in 15 FDR<0.10 cell-group signatures and reaching logFC -3.05 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
RNA-splicing perturbations converged with Rnpc3, with Prpf6 as the strongest continuous neighbor and Snrnp70, U2af2, Cdc40, and Hnrnpu sharing hundreds of same-direction RNPC3-coordinate DE events.
Proteasome subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 were top positive Rnpc3 signature neighbors, nearly matching Prpf6 and exceeding most RNA-splicing comparators by shared same-direction overlap.
Broad chromatin/TF perturbations did not anti-phenocopy Rnpc3 cleanly: Ctcf and Zbtb7a had excess opposite-direction overlap, whereas Yy1 and Uba5 were mixed rather than coherent negatives.

P16 Robo1 perturbation produced no FDR-level downstream DE in any measured neuronal class despite significant on-target Robo1 mRNA depletion in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut.
Robo1 loss did not secondarily regulate measured genes encoding Slit-Robo ligands, Robo paralogs, srGAPs, Rho-family effectors, Abl adaptors, N-WASP/Arp2/3 genes, or Ena/VASP-family actin regulators.
Robo2, Slit2, Robo4, Cdc42, and Dcc perturbations were all rejected as convergent Robo1 phenocopies because their matched DE surfaces also contained zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Data-driven signature-neighbor search found no meaningful convergent or divergent module for Robo1; the strongest non-control cosines were Wwox at +0.0336, Cntnap1 at +0.0310, Kif1b at -0.0193, and Fras1 at -0.0135.
The mouse P16 Robo1 null surface refines ROBO1 neurodevelopmental disease genetics toward early wiring and cell-morphology mechanisms rather than an ongoing adult neuronal transcriptional state.
Robo2 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across every measured neuronal group: 22/22 groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

Represented Slit/Robo and guidance-cytoskeleton relatives did not converge with Robo2; Robo1, Robo4, Slit2, and Cdc42 were flat in matched groups, Rac1 was nearly flat, and all signed-score correlations to Robo2 were near zero.
The adult VTA dopamine phenotype of Robo2 was essentially outside the tested Robo2 surface because 215 MB Dopa had no Robo2 DE rows.

The enterocyte lipoprotein program central to chylomicron retention disease was off-axis in Sar1b-perturbed neurons.
Data-driven signature neighbors of Sar1b were near-zero correlations rather than a meaningful convergent or opposing module.
P16 Satb2 loss of function produced no corrected baseline nuclear-mRNA response in any recovered neuronal group.
The canonical Satb2 cortical projection-neuron switch was not reactivated or inverted after juvenile CRISPR.
Tbr1 and Ski retained detectable postnatal cortical transcriptomic effects while Satb2 and Bcl11b were flat.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Satb2 convergence module.
The negative P16 mRNA surface pushes SATB2-associated phenotypes away from a simple resting juvenile neuronal mRNA-maintenance model.
Sbf2 did not trigger a robust downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal group, and expected MTMR13-linked autophagy or lysosomal genes were also FDR-flat.
Sbf2 and the Schwann-cell CMT4H comparator Fgd4 were both transcriptionally silent in the measured neuronal groups.
Sbf2 failed to phenocopy represented endolysosomal, PI3K, mTOR, retromer, or core-autophagy perturbations that were detectable elsewhere in the parquet.
A model-wide Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found only near-zero positive and negative correlations for Sbf2.
Postnatal Scamp5 loss is a very sparse transcriptional perturbation: only 3 of 23 measured neuronal groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene and only 7 downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 in total.
The clearest CNU-MGE GABA hit was Ddit3 down, not a CHOP/UPR induction: Ddit3 was the only FDR<0.10 gene in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
