Scamp5 lowered the endolysosomal membrane transcript Tmem9b in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut as that group's only downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The thalamic Scamp5 response included Msmo1 up, a marginal but FDR<0.10 sterol-biosynthesis hit that recurred in Marchf6 and Dctn1 perturbations and opposed direct Srebf2 loss.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coupled Fyttd1 up with Gabra1, Cx3cl1, and Sparcl1 down.

Literature-obvious vesicle comparators did not phenocopy Scamp5: Nbea, Synj1, Syt2, Stx1b, Stxbp1, Vamp1, Unc13a, Syn1, Syn2, Cplx1, and Cplx2 reproduced none of the seven Scamp5 significant coordinates.
The strongest same-direction neighbors were not the synaptic textbook comparators: Rnpc3 shared Sparcl1, Cx3cl1, and Msmo1 directionality with Scamp5 in 151, and Wac shared Gabra1 and Sparcl1.
Expected stress, autophagy/protein-clearance, and core transmitter-gene programs were absent as broad FDR<0.10 responses.
Scarb2 loss produced a nearly transcriptionally buffered neuronal phenotype: only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The only Scarb2 downstream DEG was Cox7a2l up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
Classical GCase, lysosomal, TFEB, autophagy, and α-synuclein sentinel transcripts were not FDR-level responders to Scarb2 perturbation in any measured neuronal group.
Neither the weak data-driven signature neighbors nor represented lysosomal/endosomal comparators phenocopied the 007 Scarb2-Cox7a2l response.
Short-term sparse neuronal CRISPR knockdown of Scarb2 is a poor transcriptional proxy for LIMP-2/GCase therapeutic biology.
Sclt1 produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream hit, Zmym2 up-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.

The Sclt1 DE surface did not recover a Hedgehog, cilium-gene, UPR, or ISR transcriptional program, and represented ciliary comparator perturbations were likewise flat or single-gene-only in the same neuronal groups.

Kiz, a distal-appendage/ciliary comparator, was the top unthresholded positive neighbor of Sclt1 across the full measured score vector, but the cosine was only 0.02497 and Kiz had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the matched groups.

Postnatal mosaic Scn1a loss produced a sharply buffered transcriptome: all 23 cell groups were recovered, Scn1a itself fell significantly or near-significantly in several groups, yet only three non-target FDR<0.10 genes were detected genome-wide.
The only FDR<0.10 non-target genes after Scn1a perturbation appeared in MGE inhibitory classes: Ttc8 and Amy1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Msl1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

Literature-obvious sodium-channel comparators did not phenocopy Scn1a in the matched responders: Scn1b, Scn2a, Scn3a, Scn8a, and Fgf13 produced no Amy1, Ttc8, or Msl1 overlap at FDR<0.10 in Pvalb or CNU-MGE GABA.

The data-driven Scn1a neighbors were not a hidden Nav1.1 module: positive and negative overlaps with Cdk13, Yy1, Hnrnpu, Wac, Rnpc3, Sin3a, Psmb4, U2af2, Psmc1, Setd1a, and Snrnp70 touched only Amy1 or Ttc8 in Pvalb GABA, and no other target shared the Msl1 CNU-MGE hit.

Scn1a loss did not induce seizure/immediate-early genes or a channel-compensation program: Fos, Jun, Egr1, Egr2, Arc, Npas4, Bdnf, heat-shock genes, sodium-channel relatives, Fgf13, and selected potassium-channel genes were all FDR=1.0 across their Scn1a tests.
Postnatal sparse Scn1b loss produced a sharply buffered mRNA phenotype: only four downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 23 neuronal groups.
Scn1b perturbation selectively up-regulated the bicarbonate/chloride exchanger Slc4a10 in Pvalb interneurons.
A single AP-1 activity marker, Jun, was induced in TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons and was not part of a global immediate-early response.
Scn1b perturbation induced Celsr3 in MB P MY GABA neurons, connecting an isolated cadherin/axon-guidance gene to a β1 adhesion-molecule perturbation.
The strongest single-gene Scn1b response was Cd2bp2 down-regulation in CNU-HYa HY GABA neurons, but it was not accompanied by a broader U5-snRNP/spliceosome signature.
Canonical Nav α-subunit paralogs and β1 partners did not phenocopy Scn1b in the same assay.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors failed to reveal a robust convergent Scn1b module.
Scn1b did not transcriptionally rewire the expected sodium-channel, AIS/nodal, FHF, Kv4, or KCNQ machinery.
Acute P16 Scn2a loss produced a highly sparse transcriptomic response: only Dgkd, Slc6a8, and Stn1 were downstream FDR<0.10 hits across 22 measured cell groups.
Dgkd and Slc6a8 were upregulated together in Scn2a-perturbed L4/5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons.
Stn1 was the sole downstream FDR<0.10 gene in Scn2a-perturbed MH-LH-TH glutamatergic neurons.
Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn3a, and Scn8a did not share Scn2a's downstream genes, and whole-surface residual similarity between Scn2a and other targets was near zero.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Scn2a knocked down its own RNA without downstream FDR<0.10 genes, whereas Cacna1g produced 14 downstream genes in the same cell group.
Scn3a loss-of-function leaves one robust downstream mark, Slc4a1ap up-regulation, confined to 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
The Scn3a responder does not phenocopy the assayed sodium-channel relatives Scn1a, Scn1b, Scn2a, or Scn8a.
Whole-universe residual signature search found no meaningful Scn3a convergence or opposition.
Postnatal Scn3a CRISPR loss did not induce channel-family compensation or activity-regulated transcription, despite SCN3A's strong developmental channelopathy literature.
Scn8a produced a self-transcript knockdown signature in a small subset of neuron classes but no FDR<0.10 downstream genes anywhere in its measured surface.
Expected activity-dependent and ion-channel compensation transcripts were absent rather than coherently up- or down-regulated.
Scn8a did not phenocopy the represented Nav-family perturbations.
The Scn8a null is not a global failure of the neuronal Perturb-seq readout: Grin1, Grin2b, Tardbp, and Stxbp1 produced many downstream DE genes in matched groups.
A sparse Scn8a loss-of-function indel is a poor transcriptional proxy for gain-of-function SCN8A-DEE.
Partial Scn8a suppression looked transcriptionally quiet over 3-4 weeks but cannot be read as electrophysiological safety.

Sdha produced a broadly buffered neuronal RNA response: all 23 groups were measured and all self-logFC values were negative, but only Ndrg4 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Edem2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were downstream FDR<0.10 hits.
Ndrg4 was selectively down-regulated in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut after Sdha perturbation and the same cell-by-gene effect was significant only for Sdha among 1733 comparable perturbations.
Edem2 was down-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but the surrounding ERAD/UPR and ISR markers were not induced.
Sdha perturbation did not recover HIF/pseudohypoxia, mitochondrial ISR/UPRmt, NRF2/redox, or broad ER/ISR transcriptional programs in the 23 measured neuronal groups.
Represented TCA-cycle and respiratory-chain targets did not phenocopy the Sdha Ndrg4 or Edem2 responses; direct SDHB/C/D and SDHAF comparators were absent from the target set.
The data-driven all-target residual signature search found only near-zero Sdha neighbors: Sp7 was the top positive and Fbxo11 the top negative.
Sec23a loss produced no adjusted downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured postmitotic neuronal groups.
Sec23a did not induce the UPR/ERAD marker program that was detectable from matched ER-proteostasis perturbations.
The measured COPII initiation neighbor Sar1b converged with Sec23a on a flat downstream phenotype.
Whole-surface neighbors of Sec23a were dominated by flat signatures; strong proteasome perturbations sat at the least-convergent edge.
Sec23a perturbation did not transcriptionally upregulate Sec23b or other COPII coat transcripts.
Sec63 loss evoked a selective ER-chaperone/UPR transcriptome in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only a one-gene Hspa5 echo in 155 MB Glut.
The 151 response includes an ATF4-like integrated-stress/redox arm, not just ER foldases.
The significant 151 signature also contains mixed neuronal surface, synaptic, and cytoskeletal remodeling genes.
Sec63's closest positive neighbors were not only BiP/Hspa5 but also GFPT1, DHDDS, UBA5, and ELP1, pointing to a broader ER-proteostasis attractor.
Direct Hspa5 perturbation partially phenocopied Sec63 in 151 but did not recreate the full Sec63 UPR/ISR signature.
The UPR sensor Atf6 was silent where Sec63 evoked chaperone genes.
The strongest negative signature neighbors of Sec63 were weak and did not reveal a reproducible inverse ER-stress program.
Sele loss-of-function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups; only 001 L5-6 IT Glut had a weak sub-threshold tail at FDR 0.1815.

Sele had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the model-visible universe: the strongest nonsafe positive neighbors were Tgif1, Ptpro, and Eda with cosines of only 0.034-0.035, and the strongest nonsafe negative neighbors were Fbxo11, Ranbp2, and Timmdc1 with cosines no lower than -0.030.

The represented endothelial or inflammatory comparators Kdr, Tek, Nfkb1, and Stat3 did not reconstruct a hidden Sele-like neuronal program; all four were essentially orthogonal to Sele, and only Kdr produced a single isolated FDR<0.10 gene.
Selenoi loss produced a compact, FDR-corrected sterol-feedback signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Mib1, Dctn1, Marchf6, and Rab7 were the strongest positive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature neighbors and each re-induced Selenoi sterol genes.
Srebf2, Zbtb7a, and Uba5 opposed the Selenoi sterol signature in the same thalamic glutamatergic group.
Literature-obvious ether-lipid and sterol-enzyme comparators did not strictly phenocopy Selenoi.
The Selenoi-positive thalamic signature lacked a canonical UPR, ISR, autophagy-lysosome, redox, or Tardbp transcriptional tail.
Sema4d loss produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream response, Ablim1 up-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Sema4d did not induce a canonical GABAergic-synapse mRNA program in the Pvalb responder or in hippocampal glutamatergic groups.
Represented semaphorin, plexin/neuropilin, Met, Rac1, and Limk1 perturbations failed to phenocopy Sema4d in Pvalb and were nearly all flat across the full matched neuronal surface.
The top data-driven Pvalb signature neighbors of Sema4d were weak or noise-level rather than a recurrent Sema4d-like module.
Sema5a produced a single resolved downstream transcriptomic hit: Ndufa11 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
A clean Sema5a self-transcript decrease can occur without a downstream transcriptome: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had Sema5a logFC -0.915 at FDR 3.94e-9 but zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The literature-obvious Sema5A/PlexinA-family axis did not phenocopy at the mRNA level: semaphorin, plexin, neuropilin and other axon-guidance perturbations were themselves one-gene or zero-gene responders, and none reproduced the Ndufa11 hit.
An unbiased cross-perturbation search found no strong recurrent Sema5a-like module.

The failure to elicit ASD/infantile-spasm-like transcriptional programs after P16 mosaic Sema5a loss refines human disease links toward embryonic and early-postnatal wiring, extracellular-matrix gating, and allele-specific mechanisms.
Sema6a loss produced a single robust responder: Camk2n1 was down-regulated only in 191 MB P MY GABA.
Canonical Sema6A receptors Plxna2 and Plxna4 did not phenocopy the Sema6a perturbation in the postnatal neuronal assay.
The Sema6a disease-relevant germline wiring phenotype was not accompanied by a persistent postmitotic neuronal transcriptional program in this screen.
B3gnt2 was the only FDR<0.10 downstream transcript after Serpinb6a perturbation and was induced only in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.

Serpinb6a loss in sampled brain neurons did not trigger the apoptosis, inflammasome/GSDMD, granule-protease, UPR, or ISR transcriptional modules predicted for cells undergoing damaging protease leakage.
Whole-signature cross-perturbation search found no convincing Serpinb6a-like module: the strongest positive score correlation was Fbxo11 at r=0.0515 and the strongest negative was Cckar at r=-0.0330.
The represented serpin-family perturbations Serpine2 and Serpini1 did not phenocopy Serpinb6a in matched neuronal groups.
Serpine2 loss produced only two robust downstream transcriptional hits, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA.
The two FDR-supported downstream genes both point to neurite or microtubule cytoskeleton rather than to a secretory, UPR, autophagy, or immediate-early stress response.
Neither the weak data-driven Serpine2 neighbors nor the represented thrombin/serpin/LRP1 comparators phenocopied the Clip2/Crmp1 response.
Canonical protease-axis, immediate-early, UPR/ISR, autophagy, and proteasome reporters were absent from the Serpine2 FDR surface.

Acute postmitotic Serpini1 loss produced a pan-neuronal buffered transcriptome: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite directionally negative Serpini1 self-logFC in all 21 groups.
The FENIB-like proteotoxic arm was absent after Serpini1 LoF: curated UPR, ISR, autophagy, and NF-kappaB reporters all had FDR=1.0.

Represented relatives in the extracellular protease-control axis did not phenocopy Serpini1: Serpine2 and Lrp1 had near-zero Serpini1 correlations and only singleton, cell-type-restricted DE events; Serpinb6a was similarly uncorrelated.
The unbiased perturbation neighborhood contained no meaningful convergent or inverse Serpini1 signature: the strongest non-self correlations across 1,772 targets were only r=0.036 and r=-0.035.
Set caused a single resolved downstream change, Man2c1 down-regulation, restricted to 155 MB Glut.
Set had no strong convergent or inverse whole-transcriptome neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Setbp1, the direct SET-binding comparator present in the screen, did not phenocopy Set.
The measured PP2A regulatory-subunit perturbations were disjoint from Set.
Setbp1 loss of function produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 measured P16-edited neuronal groups.
Canonical SETBP1-HD WNT/beta-catenin, FOXG1/ventral-fate, POLR2A, and GATA2 neural differentiation signals were not recovered after postmitotic Setbp1 LoF.
SET, KMT2A/PHF, PP2A, and AKT pathway relatives failed to define a Setbp1-like neuronal signature.
The WNT and SET/PP2A pharmacodynamic axes suggested by progenitor models did not appear as postnatal neuronal transcriptional biomarkers of Setbp1 LoF.

Postnatal mosaic Setd1a loss caused a real but sharply nonuniform neuronal transcriptomic response: 11 of 22 measured cell groups had downstream FDR<0.10 genes, with the broadest signatures in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The most recurrent Setd1a program was decreased nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and mitochondrial-quality-control RNA.
Setd1a loss repeatedly depressed GPI-anchor biosynthetic transcripts, especially Pigq.
ER proteostasis, UFMylation, glycoprotein processing, and Golgi/vesicle-trafficking RNAs formed a second recurrent down-module.
Primary-cilium and intraflagellar-transport genes were uniformly down in seven Setd1a-responsive groups.
Setd1a also lowered lysosomal, GATOR1/mTOR, and autophagy/mitophagy genes.
A mixed RNA-processing signature, including down-regulated RNA-modification/export genes and up-regulated spliceosomal factors in 155 MB Glut, links the Setd1a state to RNA-biogenesis stress.
The top positive signature neighbors of Setd1a were Ranbp2, Ogt, Tnpo3, Prpf6, and Snrnp70, not other measured KMT2-family writers.
Yy1, Hnrnpu, Phf12, U2af2, and Huwe1 were the strongest negative Setd1a neighbors, with Yy1 showing more than twice as many opposite- as same-direction shared FDR features.
Measured KMT2 and chromatin-disorder comparators did not phenocopy Setd1a in this assay.
Setd1a did not recover broad literature-nominated synaptic, cAMP/PKA, or replication-fork DNA-repair transcriptional programs.
Setd2 produced one robust downstream gene, Septin5, and only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Septin5 is a candidate single-gene reporter of acute Setd2 loss in Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
H3K36-adjacent perturbations did not phenocopy the Setd2-Septin5 thalamic response.
The Setd2-Septin5 coordinate is bidirectionally controlled by non-obvious regulators: Tardbp, Uba5, Ctnnb1, Chd4, and Nfic converge positively, while Wac, Rora, Tpr, Psmb4, Psmc1, and Yy1 oppose it.
Canonical SETD2 programs were buffered from whole-gene transcriptional remodeling after sparse P16 neuronal knockout.

Acute Setd5 loss produced only two FDR-positive cell-group responses and did not recover progenitor, E2F/cell-cycle, Hox/Pax6/Nes, RNA polymerase I, or ribosomal-protein programs anywhere in the 21 recovered neuronal groups.
Setd5 perturbation selectively up-regulated a TH Prkcd/Grin2c neuronal-signaling module, with 12 of 13 significant genes going up and Kat6b going down.
The Pvalb response was limited to a single FDR-supported Slc6a1 up-regulation.
Ankrd11 was the strongest same-direction data-driven neighbor of the Setd5 responder signature and reproduced seven Setd5 TH up-genes at FDR<0.10.
Cic and Psmb4 drove the Setd5 responder signature in the opposite direction, with Psmb4 inverting 12 of 14 Setd5 FDR coordinates and Cic inverting seven TH coordinates.
Represented SET-family, MLL/COMPASS-related, CBP/p300, and chromatin-NDD comparators failed to phenocopy the exact Setd5 FDR signature despite several being active in the same TH group.
Acute postnatal Setdb1 loss produced a sparse coding-gene response: only 9 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, with the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Gamma-protocadherin variable exons were the clearest Setdb1-repressed coding module: 15 significant Pcdhga/Pcdhgb cell-gene calls were all up across six responder groups.
Setdb1 perturbation up-regulated Atf7ip and Tasor, components of the SETDB1/HUSH silencing machinery, in thalamic and midbrain responders.
The cancer-like ERV-to-type-I-interferon viral-mimicry program was not recovered after neuronal Setdb1 perturbation.
Ctcf, the strongest negative Setdb1 signature neighbor, opposed Setdb1 on the gamma-protocadherin axis.
Setdb1 did not phenocopy measurable neighboring methylation and Pcdh regulators: Ehmt1 shared only a three-gene TH submodule, whereas Dnmt3a and Smchd1 were flat across Setdb1-matched groups.
The unbiased positive neighbors Sin3a and Chd4 met Setdb1 only on a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut submodule rather than on a global chromatin-repression signature.
Ccdc84 and Zmym6 recurred as noncanonical Setdb1-upregulated markers in small responder subsets.
Setdb1 had a one-gene negative synaptic-release output in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, where Unc13a was the only FDR<0.10 downstream gene and was down-regulated.
Setx produced a uniform measured transcriptional null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 across 22 tested neuronal groups and 371796 downstream gene-group tests.
No Setx-tested neuronal group activated the expected DDR, ISR/UPR, interferon, autophagy/mitophagy, proteostasis, or Bambi/TGFbeta marker programs at FDR<0.10.
Setx did not phenocopy the ALS/RNA-binding targets Tardbp or Matr3, which generated hundreds of FDR-scale downstream genes in the same screen.
The Setx LoF surface did not reproduce the dominant ALS4 Bambi/TGFbeta or TDP-43-linked axis.

Acute Sgcd loss produced a very small, cell-class-restricted response: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut only Sik2 and Porcn increased at FDR<0.10, while every other measured group had zero downstream genes.

Sgcd did not behave like an acute neuronal knockdown of the core DGC or related sarcoglycan/ECM receptors: Dmd, Dag1, Snta1, Sgce, Itga7, and Itgb1 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and did not reproduce Sik2 or Porcn in 151 TH.

Data-driven Sgcd-neighbor searches did not reveal a robust positive phenocopy, but they placed the Sgcd Porcn increase opposite Tpr and Uba5 perturbations, which strongly downregulated Porcn in the same 151 TH class.
Sgce was transcriptomically silent by FDR in every measured neuronal group.
Sgce did not join a coherent dystrophin/sarcoglycan-complex transcriptomic module.
A clean Sgce CRISPR LoF did not induce ERAD, UPR, autophagy, or sarcoglycan-transcript compensation.
The unbiased nearest neighbors of Sgce were rank-order noise, not a biological convergence class.
Represented myoclonus-dystonia differential genes also failed to form an Sgce-like nuclear state.
Sh3kbp1 LoF produced one robust downstream event, Apmap up-regulation, confined to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Apmap is a hypothesis-generating positive marker of the Sh3kbp1 response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Sh3kbp1, Cblb, and Cd2ap were flat while Cltc generated broad DE, separating receptor-specific CIN85 family scaffolding from core clathrin disruption.
The Sh3kbp1 vector had no robust positive or negative signature neighbor in the full model-visible target universe.
The expected D2-receptor and BCR/NF-kB outputs were absent from neuronal Sh3kbp1 nuclei.
Shank2 mRNA decreased in the expected direction across the measured surface but acute P16 Shank2 perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 measured cell groups.
The canonical SHANK-Homer-GKAP-NMDA/mGluR mRNA panel was entirely absent from the Shank2 downstream surface.
NMDAR subunit perturbations produced activity-linked transcriptomic signatures in matched groups where Shank2 was flat.
The closest represented PSD scaffolds and synaptic adhesion genes did not converge on a common Shank2-like transcriptional phenotype.
The unbiased all-target neighbor search found only near-zero positive and negative correlations with Shank2.

The Shank3 transcriptional response was essentially a two-cell-group, two-singleton surface: Uba5 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Zfp810 up in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with no other downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 20 measured groups.
Uba5 was the only downstream Shank3 DEG in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and was up-regulated.
Zfp810 was the only downstream Shank3 DEG in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and the only Zfp810 hit among 1306 targets tested in that group.
Shank3 loss did not significantly move the core postsynaptic scaffold, AMPAR, NMDAR, mGluR, neurexin-neuroligin, Fmr1, or Cyfip1 transcripts in any measured Shank3 cell group.
The pre-literature score-vector neighbors of Shank3 had absolute correlations below 0.03 and did not share the Uba5 or Zfp810 singleton hits.

Literature-obvious PSD partners did not phenocopy Shank3: Shank2, Dlg4, Homer2, Grm5, Nlgn3, Nrxn1/2/3, Fmr1, Cyfip1, Gria1/2, Grm1, and Syngap1 were flat or nearly flat, whereas Dlgap4 produced its own 10-gene response in L5 ET, CNU-LGE, and thalamic glutamatergic groups.
Direct NMDAR-subunit perturbations were readily detected but diverged from Shank3, with Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b producing tens to hundreds of DEGs where Shank3 had zero or one.
Shoc2 loss produced a single robust downstream DEG, Vgf down-regulation, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Braf, Map2k1, and Ntrk2 converged with Shoc2 on Vgf down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Uba5 drove Vgf in the opposite direction.
Most measurable RASopathy and RAS-MAPK relatives did not phenocopy the Shoc2 thalamic Vgf response.
Shoc2 did not recover a broad canonical ERK immediate-early or feedback transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.
The only neuronal Shoc2 LoF signal, Vgf down-regulation, is aligned with Braf and Map2k1 suppression and therefore flags a focused CNS pharmacodynamic endpoint for SHOC2-axis inhibitors.
Sigmar1 loss was a pan-cell-type nuclear-transcriptome null across all 23 measured neuronal groups.

Sigmar1 perturbation did not recruit the UPR/ISR, ER-mitochondria calcium, mitochondrial-dynamics, or autophagy/lysosomal transcriptional programs that are the canonical secondary readouts of strong sigma-1-receptor loss.
ER-stress and MAM-neighbor perturbations were themselves mostly buffered, while the one responsive chaperone node, Hspa5, produced a thalamic ER-proteostasis signature that Sigmar1 did not share.
Opa1 and Tsc2 elicited broad ISR, amino-acid, sterol, lysosomal, and neuronal-remodeling signatures in matched groups where Sigmar1 remained silent.
Sigmar1 did not phenocopy broad ALS/FTD RNA-binding-protein perturbations even though Tardbp and Matr3 were strong responders in the same thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
Sigmar1 lacked a meaningful high-dimensional signature neighborhood: its top positive and negative data-driven neighbors had near-zero correlations and no robust downstream signatures themselves.
Sil1 produced a one-gene FDR<0.10 response: Rsrp1 was up only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Acute Sil1 loss was uncoupled from the expected BiP/UPR, ERAD, and autophagy transcriptional programs across all measured neuronal groups.
The same dataset detects a BiP/UPR-like module after Hspa5, Sec63, and Manf perturbation, but Sil1 does not join that module.
Phenotype-first nearest neighbors of Sil1 were essentially random and were rejected by FDR overlap.

Sin3a loss produced a broad but selective P16 neuronal response, with 3761 downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 14 of 21 measured cell groups and the dominant burden in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
A recurrent ER protein-quality-control program was induced by Sin3a and was most similar to proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4.
direction_pattern: up; convergent with proteasome loss signatures

canonical_summary: Sin3a loss repeatedly down-regulated nuclear-speckle and splicing factors, including Srrm2, Pnisr, Ddx17, Srsf5, Srsf6, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, and Leng8.
Sin3a responders induced a lipid, cholesterol, mitochondrial, and redox metabolic arm marked by Cyp46a1, Mboat7, Gcdh, Pcx, Acly, Cyb5r3, Qdpr, Aldh6a1, and Gsto1.
An endolysosomal clearance branch rose in broad Sin3a responders, including Grn, Pld3, Dpp7, Hdac6, Tmem9, Mcoln1, and Wipi1.
Sin3a loss induced a ciliary and basal-body transcript module, with Odf2 up in 12 responder groups and recurrent increases of Alms1, Ift57, Dzip1, Cep192, Cep152, Cfap69, and Dnah9.
The prior Homer1/mGluR hippocampal program was only partly recovered: Homer1 rose in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responders, Grm1 but not Grm5 was significant, and CA3/CA2-FC/DG was weak.
Embryonic cortical layer and progenitor targets were absent, while axon-guidance, adhesion, and actin-remodeling genes were induced after P16 perturbation.
Sin3a perturbation weakly induced its paralog Sin3b and several Sin3-associated corepressor transcripts in the strongest cell groups.
The literature-obvious recruiter perturbations Rest and Mecp2 did not converge with Sin3a in the measured postnatal neurons.
Bap1, Kdm5c, and Zmynd8 were the three strongest negative Sin3a restricted-signature neighbors.
Sipa1l3 loss-of-function produced no robust whole-transcriptome response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
The embryonic SIPA1L3 eye-development/Wnt program was absent from postmitotic P16 brain neurons.
A postsynaptic Sipa1l3 prior did not translate into a PSD transcriptional module in the young adult neuronal nuclei assayed here.
The unbiased Sipa1l3 signature had no meaningful same-direction or opposite-direction neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
There was no transcriptional bounce-back by other measured Sipa-family transcripts.
Six3 loss induced only Slc6a6 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and the edge was unique for Slc6a6 within that cell group across 1742 tested perturbations.
P16 Six3 perturbation failed to move canonical embryonic Wnt/BMP/SHH/FGF sentinels or anterior forebrain/eye transcription factors in any measured neuronal group.
Unbiased signature neighbors and represented SIX/homeobox/Wnt-Hh relatives did not converge with the Six3 Slc6a6 signature.
Six5 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 23 measured mouse-brain neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The canonical SIX5/MEF3-ARE target readout was absent: Igfbp5, Atp1a1, and Myog were never FDR-significant after Six5 perturbation.
No latent Six5 response module was recovered by cross-perturbation: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score neighbor reached only r=0.0349 and the strongest anti-neighbor only r=-0.0314.
Represented SIX/retinal-determination comparators failed to phenocopy or diverge from Six5: Six3, Dach1, and Pax6 all had near-zero correlations with Six5 and no broad DE where Six5 was null.
Six5 deficiency alone did not elicit a DM1-relevant neuronal transcriptional stress or IGF-target response in young brain neurons.

Ski loss produced a narrow, postmitotic neuronal response: 27 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with no FDR-supported downstream gene in the other 21 measured groups.
The strongest L2/3 IT cortical component was an up-regulated chromatin/RFX module centered on Chd3, Rfx3 and Macroh2a1.
Ski loss up-regulated an L2/3 IT neuronal adhesion and projection-remodeling gene set including Wscd2, Begain, Igsf11, Dok6, Fat3, Ncam1, Ptprf and Sidt1.
L2/3 IT Ski loss also carried a smaller decreased neuropeptide/secretory arm, with Penk, Chgb and Plk5 reduced while most significant genes were up.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a weak but real all-up Ski signature: Cck, L1cam, Spock2 and Ywhah.

Ski phenotypes were uncoupled from the canonical TGF/BMP receptor-SMAD signature: Id1/2/3/4, Smad7, Serpine1, Cdkn1a, Ccn2, Msx1, Msx2 and Junb never reached FDR<0.10, and 16 represented pathway receptors/SMADs generated only two isolated hits in Ski-responsive cell groups.
Ski did not phenocopy the represented corepressor neighbor Sin3a: Sin3a had 3761 FDR<0.10 downstream genes across 14 groups and regulated thalamic Spock2 opposite to Ski.
The unbiased top positive FDR-backed neighbor of Ski was Mib1, which shared same-direction L2/3 up-regulation of Pde4a, Ptprf and Rfx3.
Ski's L2/3 program was directionally opposed by Grin2a at Penk, Plch2 and Atp8a2, while Grin2b converged only at Tbkbp1.

The P16 neuronal Ski loss-of-function surface does not resemble Shprintzen-Goldberg SKI pathobiology: it lacks canonical neuronal TGFβ/BMP de-repression and is generated in NeuN+ postmitotic lineages rather than the embryonic craniofacial, connective-tissue and vascular contexts emphasized in disease.
Slc12a2 loss of function was a pan-neuronal FDR-level transcriptomic null in this P16-to-P37/44 acute CRISPR screen.
Represented WNK/SPAK/OSR1/PKC chloride-cotransporter regulators did not converge on a Slc12a2-like program.
Small GABA_A-receptor activity signatures exist in the same universe, but Slc12a2 does not phenocopy them.
A whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Slc12a2 transcriptomic neighbor.
The null surface cautions that juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq will miss the SLC12A2 phenotypes most relevant to systemic disease and NKCC1 pharmacology.
Slc1a1 perturbation produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 23 measured neuronal groups.
Slc1a1 down-regulated Msantd2 only in L2/3 IT CTX neurons.
Slc1a1 up-regulated the ESCRT-associated cargo-sorting gene Ptpn23 only in L5 ET CTX neurons.
Slc1a1 loss did not recover an Nrf2, glutathione-synthesis, glutathione-recycling, or ISR transcriptomic program.
Slc1a2 did not converge with Slc1a1 despite being the nearest represented SLC1 glutamate-transporter paralog.
Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations elicited broad L2/3 IT CTX responses that Slc1a1 did not share.
Slc1a1 had no strong unbiased signature neighbor or anti-neighbor across the 1772 other represented targets.
The assay nominates no broad acute mRNA pharmacodynamic marker for EAAT3 inhibition or activation in juvenile neurons.
Slc1a2 knockdown was a target-transcript-only event in all assayed neuronal groups: even the three groups with corrected Slc1a2 self-decrease had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
direction_pattern: on-target down in 19/22 groups; no downstream FDR response

canonical_summary: Glutamate receptor perturbations responded where Slc1a2 was flat: Grin2a, Grin2b, and Grin1 produced corrected neuronal DE in matched groups, including Nptx2/Bdnf/Scg2 and Vgf/Kcnv1/Nr4a1 activity-associated signatures.
direction_pattern: NMDAR subunit LoF responsive; Slc1a2 LoF flat

canonical_summary: The represented EAAT paralog and glutamate-metabolic relatives did not reveal a hidden transporter module: Slc1a1 was nearly flat and uncorrelated with Slc1a2, and Gfap, Atp1a2, Gls, Glud1, Got1, Got2, and Srr were either flat or one-group/minimal responders.
The P16 juvenile neuronal LoF screen does not phenocopy the severe epilepsy biology of SLC1A2 dominant-negative or global GLT-1 loss.
direction_pattern: LoF snRNA phenotype absent despite disease-positive priors

canonical_summary: Data-driven whole-signature neighbors of Slc1a2 were not meaningful biological relatives: the strongest full-coverage positive neighbor had r=0.028 and the strongest negative neighbor had r=-0.010 across the 371,818-dimensional Wilcoxon-score vector.
Slc20a2 produced a pan-neuronal FDR-flat response after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation.
Slc20a2 loss did not induce the expected PFBC phosphate-calcification, neurovascular, osteogenic, or glial-injury marker genes in any recovered neuronal group.
Represented PFBC comparators Xpr1 and Pdgfrb were FDR-flat in matched neuronal groups and did not converge with Slc20a2.
The unbiased signed-score neighbor scan found no meaningful Slc20a2-like or Slc20a2-opposing perturbation.
The Slc20a2 null warns that juvenile NeuN+ snRNA markers are poor proximal biomarkers for SLC20A2-restoration strategies.
Slc22a17 loss produced a single corrected downstream gene, Msmo1 up-regulation, restricted to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Rab7 perturbation phenocopied the L4/5 IT Msmo1 hit: Rab7 and Slc22a17 were the only two targets with corrected Msmo1 induction in that cell group.

The Msmo1 response did not track the obvious LCN2 or sterol comparators: Lrp2 was flat, Srebf2 drove multi-gene sterol repression in other neurons rather than L4/5 Msmo1 induction, and Tfrc, Hmgcr, and Trp53 did not converge.
Slc22a17 transcript was reduced in most measured cell groups, yet 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Neuronal Slc22a17 loss did not recreate the LCN2 inflammatory, Bim-apoptotic, or iron-stress programs reported after ligand, LPS, or glial activation.

Slc25a12 perturbation gave a self-gene-only signature: the target transcript decreased in every recovered neuronal class and was FDR-significant in thalamic and midbrain classes, but no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 measured groups.

Direct malate-aspartate-shuttle enzyme neighbors responded where Slc25a12 did not: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Mdh1 had 42 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, Got1 had 6 and Got2 had 1, while Mdh2 had only one Pvalb Gaba hit across the matched surface.
The exact AGC paralog Slc25a13 did not phenocopy Slc25a12: AGC2/citrin perturbation had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 21 matched neuronal groups and no significant self-transcript effect.
Expected secondary ISR, proteostasis, redox, neurotransmitter, MAS-compensation and NAA/myelin-marker transcripts were all absent from the Slc25a12 DE surface at FDR<0.10.
The data-driven neighborhood of Slc25a12 was at the noise floor: the top positive and negative whole-vector neighbors had Wilcoxon-score correlations of only +0.034 and -0.014.
Slc25a13 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional zero rather than a cell-type-restricted responder.
Mitochondrial-carrier depletion was uncoupled from the malate-aspartate-shuttle enzyme response: Mdh1 and Got1 fired in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Slc25a13 did not.
The brain AGC paralog Slc25a12 did not phenocopy either Mdh1/Got1 or a predicted AGC-stress response despite a significant self-transcript decrease in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The unbiased cross-perturbation search found no robust positive or negative Slc25a13 signature neighbor.
Slc25a26 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR perturbation.
Slc25a26 did not induce the expected mitochondrial ISR/UPRmt/OXPHOS RNA programs even though Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations showed that these programs can be detected in the dataset.
Unbiased Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Slc25a26 signature neighbor across the 1772 other perturbations.
SLC25 carrier-family perturbations represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Slc25a26.
The Slc25a26 neuronal null is most consistent with a recessive, near-complete functional threshold rather than haploinsufficient transcriptional toxicity.
Slc25a27 loss of function produced a pan-null basal snRNA-seq response: every one of the 21 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The Slc25a27 null was not hiding a canonical mitochondrial-stress aftershock: ISR, ER-UPR, UPRmt, Nrf2/antioxidant, OXPHOS, glycolysis, mitophagy, apoptosis, Ucp2, and Slc25a14 transcript responses were all absent at FDR<0.10.

Slc25a27 did not converge with measurable mitochondrial-carrier or stress-axis perturbations, and the pre-literature sparse-vector neighbors were rejected once complete matched DE surfaces were inspected.
The 308 CB GABA null does not phenocopy the published Purkinje-cell Ucp4 phenotype at the level of snRNA-seq.
Acute Slc25a36 perturbation was a pan-measured-neuronal transcriptional null: no cell group produced a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The mitochondrial ISR/one-carbon module was assay-detectable after Opa1 perturbation but absent after Slc25a36 perturbation.
The whole-surface signature-neighbor search found no substantive positive or negative neighbor for Slc25a36.
Represented SLC25-family and mitochondrial-nucleotide/TCA comparators also failed to converge with Slc25a36.

The neuronal null displaces the clearest pathogenic SLC25A36 biology toward embryonic pluripotency and pancreatic mtGTP/insulin coupling rather than acute postmitotic neuron-autonomous nuclear stress.
Acute postnatal Slc25a46 loss is almost completely buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level: one downstream FDR hit was detected across 22 measured neuronal groups.
The only Slc25a46 downstream hit was Cdc27 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, weakly nominating an APC/C-linked response restricted to one coarse glutamatergic class.

Opa1, the represented fusion partner/pathway comparator, produced a broad amino-acid/ISR-like response in thalamic, midbrain, and P-MY-labeled groups where Slc25a46 showed self-mRNA loss but no downstream DE.
Most represented SLC25-family and mitochondrial-dynamics relatives were as transcriptionally flat as Slc25a46, whereas Opa1 was the exception with 241 downstream calls.
The data-driven whole-surface neighbor search did not identify a credible Slc25a46 transcriptional module.
Slc25a4 loss produced exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene, Preb down, and only in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
The Ant1-null OXPHOS, mitochondrial-biogenesis, antioxidant, and ISR programs expected from muscle models were absent from Slc25a4-perturbed brain neurons.
Nrf1, but not Slc25a4, generated a broad response in matched neuronal groups, including the matched 110 group.
Slc25a4 did not elicit Slc25a5 or Slc25a31 mRNA induction, so any ANT-family buffering is non-inducible at the assayed transcript level.
Data-driven neighbor searches found no robust Slc25a4-like target in the parquet.
Slc2a1 loss produced an almost pan-neuronal buffered transcriptome: only 1 downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 across 388023 downstream tests in 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The only FDR<0.10 Slc2a1 downstream gene was Arih2 down in 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells.
Slc2a1 perturbation failed to induce expected glucose-starvation, glycolytic, HIF, ATF4/ISR, autophagy, or UPR transcripts in any cell group.
Slc2a1 had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor; maximum positive and negative correlations across the parquet were only r=0.041 and r=-0.018.
The Slc2a1 surface diverged from Tsc2: Tsc2 generated 636 corrected downstream genes while Slc2a1 was flat in every Tsc2-responsive group.
The null Slc2a1 neuronal surface refines GLUT1 deficiency modeling by separating direct P16 neuronal LoF from the early BBB/endothelial disease compartment.
Slc32a1 produced a downstream pan-null: every one of the 23 recovered cell groups had zero non-self genes at FDR<0.10.
The flat Slc32a1 surfaces in glutamatergic and dopaminergic groups are expected transmitter-mismatch negatives rather than failed recovery of a GABAergic program.
Literature-obvious GABA-synapse relatives also failed to phenocopy Slc32a1 with a coherent DE program.
The data-driven Slc32a1 nearest neighbors were all near-zero cosine matches rather than a biological module.
The P16 sparse LoF snRNA-seq null is poorly matched to SLC32A1 disease mechanisms, which are missense and electrophysiological.

Sparse postnatal Slc4a7 loss was transcriptionally buffered across the neuronal panel: 21 measured groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 and the Slc4a7 self-transcript never corrected below FDR 1.0.

Slc4a7 did not phenocopy NMDAR-subunit perturbations: Grin2a and Grin2b produced robust, subunit-specific cortical IT signatures and Grin1 produced a 126-gene thalamic signature where matched Slc4a7 groups were flat.
The PSD-95 interactor Dlg4 was also transcriptionally flat in the Slc4a7-matched groups, despite direct Dlg4 self-transcript reduction in some groups.
An unbiased Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found no meaningful Slc4a7 signature neighbor; the extreme correlations across 1772 comparators were only r=+0.0265 and r=-0.0199.

Acute neuronal Slc4a7 loss did not lower Dlg4, Grin1, Grin2a, or Grin2b transcripts, refining germline NBCn1 knockout reports of reduced GluN1/PSD-95 protein to a context-, protein-, or challenge-dependent effect.
Slc52a2 produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered postnatal neuronal groups.
Slc52a2 did not activate the mitochondrial ISR/amino-acid module that the same screen detected after Opa1 perturbation.
Measured FAD/flavoprotein comparators also failed to form a Slc52a2-like convergent module.
The unbiased whole-surface neighbor search found no interpretable positive or negative Slc52a2 neighbor.

Slc6a17 loss produced a very sparse basal nuclear RNA response: only four non-target genes reached FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups, and all four were confined to CTX-CGE GABA and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: Ythdf1, Jun, Stmn4, and Kctd16 up in the two responder groups; no FDR<0.10 down-regulated downstream gene

canonical_summary: In TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the full Slc6a17 three-gene response, Jun/Stmn4/Kctd16 up, was recapitulated by Grin1 and Vps54 and inverted by Wdfy3 and Uba5.
direction_pattern: up after Slc6a17, Grin1, and Vps54; down after Wdfy3 and Uba5

canonical_summary: Slc6a17 perturbation isolated Ythdf1 up-regulation in CTX-CGE GABA as the only cortical GABA FDR<0.10 downstream event.
Most literature-obvious transporter and glutamate-receptor neighbors did not phenocopy Slc6a17 in the two responder groups; the exception was Grin1 in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: mostly nonconvergent; Grin1 selectively convergent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

canonical_summary: There was no strong whole-transcriptome signature neighbor for Slc6a17 across the perturbation universe.
Acute Slc6a1 loss was almost completely transcriptionally buffered: only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured neuronal groups.
Yif1a induction in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut was the sole FDR<0.10 downstream event for Slc6a1.
Slc6a1 loss did not induce activity-regulated, GABA-receptor/metabolic, or UPR/ER-stress transcriptional programs.

Literature-obvious GABA and epilepsy comparators did not phenocopy the Slc6a1 Yif1a event, while Gabrb2 and Stxbp1 showed that related neuronal perturbations can be transcriptionally visible in the same universe.
The pre-literature whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Slc6a1 signature neighbor.
The transcriptional null should not be read as evidence that further GAT1 inhibition is benign in SLC6A1 disease.
Slc6a5 had one real downstream response: a three-gene, L2/3 IT cortical signature with Ppat and Foxg1 up and Ltk down.
The Slc6a5 L2/3 response did not converge with glycine-receptor, gephyrin/collybistin, VGAT, or related SLC6 transporter perturbations.
The data-driven Slc6a5 neighbors were rank artifacts rather than phenocopies.
Proteasome comparators responded broadly where Slc6a5 was flat.
This screen should not be used to de-risk GlyT2 inhibition in spinal pain circuits.
Slc7a14 produced only five downstream FDR<0.10 DEGs in 22 measured groups, and the only multi-gene response was in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
The 217 P MY Pineal Glut response combined up-regulation of Efr3a and Dmxl2 with down-regulation of Gabbr2.
Pvalb neurons showed significant Slc7a14 transcript reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Represented lysosome, autophagy, GABA, and TSC/mTOR comparators failed to share Slc7a14's five significant downstream hits, while Tsc2 produced hypothalamic DEGs where Slc7a14 was null.
The top data-driven positive and negative restricted-signature neighbors, Ptf1a and Arid1b, were rejected after matched FDR lookup.

Slc7a6os loss produced recurrent Polr2a up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Son/Snrnp200/Dhx37/Cpsf1 gains and Srrm2/Pnisr losses concentrated in 110 and 151.

The postmitotic Slc7a6os response was sharply selective: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 95 of the 116 FDR<0.10 downstream calls, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut had 15, 155 MB Glut had 3, and three other groups had only single-gene responses.
In the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response, synaptic and excitability genes were preferentially down-regulated while chaperone, lysosomal and metabolic genes rose.
The Slc7a6os 116-gene signature most strongly converged with proteasome perturbations Psmb4/Psmc1 and spliceosome perturbations Snrnp70/Prpf6/U2af2 rather than with a textbook SLC7-family neighbor.
Direct Pol II-import relatives were absent from the target set, and the represented nuclear-transport factor Tnpo3 converged with Slc7a6os in 151 whereas Ranbp2 did not.
Progressive-myoclonus-epilepsy family perturbations did not phenocopy the Slc7a6os responder signatures in the matched cell groups.
The hippocampal Nicn1 and 191 MB P MY GABA Pld3 calls were isolated sentinels, not broad ER, Nodal, lysosomal or inflammatory programs.

Slc9a7 perturbation was buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level: all 20 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream Wilcoxon DE genes at FDR<0.10, even though three groups showed FDR-level reduction of the Slc9a7 transcript.

Literature-obvious acidification relatives did not share a Slc9a7 signature: Slc9a9, Atp6v0a1, Clcn3, and Clcn4 were flat in matched groups, while Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, and Atp6v1e1 produced only sparse, non-overlapping FDR<0.10 responses with near-zero Slc9a7 score cosines from -0.0053 to 0.0114.

The all-target, data-driven neighbor search found no hidden Slc9a7-like transcriptional module: the strongest positive and negative score cosines across 1772 other targets were only +0.0224 and -0.0145.

The null Slc9a7 LoF surface is most consistent with SLC9A7 biology being off-axis and allele-sensitive: the published XLID allele perturbs TGN/post-Golgi pH and N-glycosylation, whereas acute CRISPR LoF in postmitotic neurons did not induce a detectable secondary stress transcriptome.
Postnatal Slc9a9 perturbation produced a pan-neuronal FDR-zero snRNA signature: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Severe endolysosomal and V-ATPase perturbations were transcriptionally detectable in this screen, whereas Slc9a9 was not.
The only represented SLC9A endomembrane paralog, Slc9a7/NHE7, also lacked downstream FDR genes in its 20 recovered groups.
Unbiased whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Slc9a9 convergence or anticorrelation with any other perturbation.
Known NHE9 cargo and synaptic-trafficking readouts were absent at the mRNA level after Slc9a9 perturbation.
Slf2 loss was nearly transcriptionally silent after P16 neuronal CRISPR, producing only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 21 measured cell groups.
Ppp5c was the lone robust Slf2-dependent transcript and was up-regulated specifically in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Nsmce2 and Atr converged with Slf2 by being flat, not by sharing an induced repair transcriptome, in the same postnatal neuronal screen.
Smc1a, unlike Slf2, Nsmce2, and Atr, produced a real 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response dominated by down-regulated neuronal and adhesion genes.
The Slf2 full-transcriptome score vector had no strong cross-perturbation neighbor; even the top neighbors had absolute cosines below 0.028.
Acute mosaic Slit2 loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered neuronal group, with a flat Slit2 snRNA self-response.

The directly measured Slit/Robo neighborhood was also transcriptionally silent: Robo1, Robo2, and Robo4 each had 0 matched downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Dcc, Unc5c, Unc5d, Cdc42, Rac1, Rho, and Gsk3b were silent or nearly silent.
The top data-driven neighbors of Slit2 had near-zero global score correlations, led by Wdr26 at r=0.0387 and by non-safe anti-neighbors no more negative than Nipa1 at r=-0.0202.
Smad1 perturbation produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The canonical BMP-SMAD Id/Msx output was completely absent after Smad1 perturbation.
BMP-SMAD relatives represented in the parquet were also flat or singleton-only, so Smad1 was not hiding a pathway-level module shared with Smad9, Smad4, Smad6, or BMP receptors.
The 052 Pvalb Gaba aggregate did not recover the adult neocortical PV-interneuron BMP2-SMAD1 synapse/perineuronal-net program.
Empirical Smad1 signature neighbors were extremely weak and failed full-surface validation.

Postnatal Smad2 loss produced an ultra-sparse, negative response: Cpne7 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Ache decreased in 155 MB Glut, with no other Smad2 cell group containing a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

The two Smad2 marker genes were recurrent downstream endpoints of non-SMAD perturbations: Cpne7 fell after Chd4, Adnp, Tpr, Tnpo3, Zbtb7a, Wac, and Psmc1 in 151, while Ache fell after Ranbp2, Psmc1, Ogt, Ascc3, Wac, Psmb4, Tnpo3, Tpr, and Zbtb7a in 155.

Smad2 did not phenocopy the directly measured TGFβ/activin/BMP SMAD pathway relatives Smad3, Smad4, Smad1, Smad6, Smad9, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr3, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, or the Smad corepressor Ski.

Smad2 perturbation did not recover a canonical TGFβ/SMAD feedback program or the neuronal Cdh1-APC/SnoN-axis transcripts queried here: Smad7, Skil, Fzr1, Id2, Ccn2, Serpine1, and Junb had zero FDR<0.10 events across the 21 measured Smad2 groups.
Smad3 is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null after juvenile postmitotic CRISPR: all 22 tested cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The data-driven nearest neighbors of Smad3 are not biologically strong convergences: the largest Wilcoxon-score correlations were only +0.039 and -0.041 and the four leading neighbors produced at most one FDR<0.10 gene each.

Literature-obvious TGFβ/BMP branch comparators also failed to phenocopy Smad3: Smad1, Smad4, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr3, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, and Acvrl1 were fully flat in matched groups, while Smad2, Acvr1, and Tgfbr2 each had only isolated one-gene hits.

The null neuronal surface should displace, not dismiss, Smad3 biology: human SMAD3 disease and mouse injury or neurogenesis phenotypes live mainly in vascular/connective, astroglial, assaulted, or progenitor compartments that this NeuN+ baseline assay either did not sample or did not stress.
Smad4 was a complete FDR-level non-responder across the recovered postmitotic neuronal surface.
Canonical TGFβ/BMP-SMAD target readouts and directly targeted receptor/R-SMAD relatives did not uncover an ongoing Smad4-dependent pathway in P16-perturbed neurons.
Ski produced a restricted L2/3 IT cortical and thalamic response that Smad4 and Tgif1 did not phenocopy.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Smad4 convergence or anticorrelation in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The postmitotic neuronal null should not be extrapolated to global TGFβ/BMP pathway inhibition.
Smad6 loss produced no corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured neuronal cell groups.
Smad6 LoF did not derepress the expected canonical BMP/SMAD ID-MSX-feedback gene panel.
Represented BMP/TGFβ receptors and SMAD signal transducers also failed to produce a broad transcriptional module in the matched cell groups.
Ski, a SMAD corepressor, was measurably active where Smad6 was flat.
The juvenile neuron null refines SMAD6 LoF disease biology toward earlier and unsampled BMP-sensitive tissues.
Unbiased continuous signature neighbors of Smad6 were near-zero and biologically non-convergent.
Acute postnatal Smad9 loss produced a transcriptome-wide zero in every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class.
Canonical BMP receptor and R-SMAD relatives did not collapse into a shared Smad9-like module.
The strongest unbiased Smad9 neighbors were extremely weak and off-pathway rather than BMP relatives.
The neuronal screen does not recover the disease-relevant pulmonary SMAD9 microRNA program.
A single CA3-region hippocampal glutamatergic response survives FDR correction after Smarca2 perturbation: Ppfia2 is down in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
Perturbing core nBAF members was transcriptionally visible in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, but Smarca2 and its ATPase paralog Smarca4 did not phenocopy that response.
The unbiased signed-score neighborhood of Smarca2 is essentially empty: the top positive and negative non-safe neighbors were Nr1h4 and Fbxo11 with correlations of only 0.0366 and -0.0278.
A postnatal Smarca2 loss-of-function perturbation does not reproduce the broad gene-dysregulation expectation created by SMARCA2 Nicolaides-Baraitser alleles.

Smarca2-only inhibition in Smarca4-intact juvenile neurons is transcriptionally quiet in this screen, whereas published synthetic-lethal SMARCA2 dependencies are concentrated in SMARCA4-deficient cancer contexts.
Acute P16 Smarca4 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
The expected BRG1/MEF2 activity-response and synapse-gene program was absent rather than recovering as a basal juvenile signature.
Smarca4 was flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut precisely where multiple mSWI/SNF accessory subunits converged on a recurrent thalamic module.
The BRG1 paralog Smarca2 also failed to generate a broad matched response, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Smarcc2 and Arid2 were active.
The unbiased full-parquet neighbor calculation found no robust convergent or anti-convergent Smarca4 signature.
Smarcad1 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across all 20 measured neuronal groups, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no corrected self-transcript depletion.
Setdb1, the represented H3K9/retroelement pathway neighbor, responded where Smarcad1 did not: Setdb1 produced 45 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across Smarcad1-matched groups versus 0 for Smarcad1.

Multiple represented SWI/SNF, BAF, CHD, and ATRX chromatin-remodeler comparators produced FDR<0.10 neuronal signatures, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Smarcad1 remained flat in the same matched groups.
Whole-universe neighbors of the Smarcad1 signed-Wilcoxon profile were essentially uncorrelated, with r values between -0.025 and 0.043 for the strongest positive and negative neighbors.
Smarcc1 produced a single adjusted downstream hit, Srpk1 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
Smarcc1 failed to phenocopy a thalamic BAF/SWI-SNF module driven by Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1.
Smarcc1 had no robust global positive or negative signature neighbor across the target universe.
Smarcc2 produced a 263-gene downstream response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the other 21 recovered groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and 215 MB Dopa was missing.
Smarce1 and Arid1a were the top two positive restricted-signature neighbors of Smarcc2 in 151, and all of their FDR-controlled overlaps with the 263-gene Smarcc2 signature were same-direction.
Smarcc1, Smarca2, Smarca4, and Bicra did not phenocopy Smarcc2 in the matched 151 group; Arid1b and Smarcd1 were nearly flat, while Arid2 was only partially overlapping.

The strongest Smarcc2-negative genes in 151 included Ptpn3, Reep2, Tiam1, C1qtnf4, Prkcd, Ptprz1, Pdp1, and Adarb1, with additional down-regulation of receptor and signaling genes Grin2b, Grm1, Prkcb, Gabra4, Gabbr1, Cacnb2, Kcnk9, Cnih3, and P2rx4.
Smarcc2 loss in 151 significantly down-regulated adhesion and extracellular-interface genes including L1cam, Sdk2, Itga3, Serpine2, Agrn, Adamts16, Adamts19, Col15a1, Fbln5, and Col4a1.
The 151 response included a large positive arm, with Syt4, Clstn1, Clstn2, Epb41l1, Ndrg1, Pth2r, Gfra1, Tafa1, Sertm1, and Grin3a up-regulated.
A small FDR-controlled but heterogeneous cell-cycle, histone, microtubule, and ciliary-gene arm accompanied the 151 response.
Canonical ISR/UPR and proteasome sentinel genes were absent from the only Smarcc2 responder, even though the data-driven neighbor Dhdds produced a strong 151 response and known stress-like genes.
The strongest negative restricted-signature neighbors of Smarcc2 did not yield robust FDR-controlled anti-phenotypes in 151.
Acute Smarcd1 loss of function produced a real but very sparse response confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Ankrd40 up and Ptpn3 down as the only downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut effect was shared only partially across BAF relatives: Ptpn3 was also down after Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a perturbation, whereas Arid2 had a larger thalamic signature without Ptpn3 and Smarca2, Smarca4, and Smarcc1 were flat in this same group.
Smarcd1 had no strong transcriptome-wide signed-score neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
A P16 mosaic Smarcd1 loss-of-function perturbation does not recapitulate a broad Coffin-Siris or neural-BAF transcriptional state in young postmitotic mouse neurons.
Smarce1 generated a robust downstream signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 16 FDR<0.10 genes versus zero in 21 other measured groups.
The core 151 Smarce1 signature down-regulated Prkcd, Prkcb, Ptpn3 and Rasa4.
Smarce1 loss in 151 suppressed a postsynaptic and membrane-lipid gene subset, including Begain, Lrrc7, Sdk2, Abhd12b and Serinc2, while increasing Dagla.
direction_pattern: mixed; scaffold genes down and Dagla up

canonical_summary: A small mixed ER, mitochondrial and redox module accompanied the 151 signature: Reep2, Slc25a37 and Msra decreased, while Ndufv3 and Acat1 increased.
Smarcc2 was the top unbiased positive neighbor of Smarce1 and reproduced 12 of the 16 Smarce1 151 DEGs in the same direction; Arid1a and Arid2 reproduced smaller same-direction subsets.
Several represented BAF relatives failed to phenocopy Smarce1 in 151: Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcc1 and Bicra had zero downstream genes there, whereas Smarcd1 and Arid1b had only two and one.
Chd4 was the strongest negative neighbor of the Smarce1 151 signature and reversed Begain, Abhd12b, Ccdc141 and Msra.
Acute Smarce1 CRISPR loss after P16 spared most NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal transcriptomes and therefore did not mimic broad SMARCE1 developmental disease in this assay.

Smc1a loss produced a downstream transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 34 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 20 other measured groups had 0 and 155 MB Glut had only target-transcript reduction.

The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c response was dominated by down-regulation of adhesion, extracellular-matrix/guidance and excitability genes, including Ptprm, Spon1, Sema5a, Slit3, Adamts2, Adamts19, Dner, Atp2a2, Atp2b1, Grin2c, Grin2a, Pcp4, Necab2, Kcns2 and Lrrc7.

Literature-obvious cohesin relatives diverged: Stag2 was the strongest same-direction Smc1a neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, sharing 14 of 34 Smc1a genes all in the same direction, whereas Stag1 shared none and Hdac8, Pds5a and Ncapd3 were flat in the same cell group.
Ctcf perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recovered only a partial Smc1a subset: 7 of the 34 Smc1a downstream genes, 6 in the shared direction and Sirt5 in the opposite direction.

The data-driven 151 signature search nominated non-cohesin neighbors: Ctnnb1 and Psmb4 had the largest same-direction FDR overlap with Smc1a, Uba5 was high-overlap but mixed, and Sin3a was the clearest inverse neighbor.

Only six Smc1a FDR<0.10 genes were up-regulated and they were heterogeneous; the sole downstream signature also lacked FDR<0.10 p53, integrated-stress, unfolded-protein, autophagy, or proteasome bounce-back sentinels such as Trp53, Cdkn1a, Bbc3, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Sqstm1, and Psmb7.

Acute P16 Smchd1 loss was pan-null across the measured neuronal surface: every one of 22 tested groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the expected Pcdh, Hox, and imprinted-cluster candidates were also absent at FDR<0.10.

The missing Smchd1 Pcdh phenotype is not a Pcdh detectability failure: Setdb1 loss up-regulated 15 Pcdh calls in 6 groups and Ctcf loss changed 48 Pcdh calls, mostly downward, while Smchd1 had no FDR-level Pcdh call among 1,496 Pcdh tests.
The direct SMCHD1 recruitment partner Lrif1 phenocopied the Smchd1 nullity, with 0 FDR<0.10 genes in 22 groups and essentially no score-level correlation to Smchd1.
The genome-wide signature-neighbor search did not nominate a meaningful convergent or antagonistic module for Smchd1; the strongest non-self Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.027.

Smchd1 was not interchangeable with canonical chromosome-architecture factors: Ctcf, Smc1a, and Stag2 produced robust DE, particularly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Smchd1 remained at 0 FDR<0.10 genes despite 152 perturbed Smchd1 nuclei.
Smo loss produced a lone Rnf220-up transcript in 155 MB Glut.
The expected canonical GLI feedback program was absent after Smo perturbation in all recovered neuronal classes.
Perturbing measurable Hedgehog neighbors did not reveal a coherent Smo-like or opposite module.
The unbiased Smo signature has no strong positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Sms perturbation produced a one-gene FDR-level response, Elfn2 up-regulation, restricted to 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
Sms loss did not recover the severe-SMS-deficiency autophagy-lysosome, oxidative, mitochondrial, UPR, or ISR transcriptome in any measured neuronal group.
Represented polyamine-neighborhood perturbations Eif5a, Atp13a2, and Atp13a3 did not converge with Sms.
191 MB P MY GABA reduced Sms mRNA but showed no robust downstream transcriptional response.
The top data-driven Sms score neighbors were weak low-cosine matches and did not share the CTX-CGE Elfn2 effect.

Snai2-targeted CRISPR was transcriptionally inert across the measured postnatal neuronal surface: 19 measured cell groups, 819 perturbed nuclei in aggregate, and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 or FDR<0.25.

The expected Slug/Snail2 EMT and neural-crest cadherin program was absent: Cdh1, Cdh6, Ocln, Vim, Fn1, Sox10, Tfap2a, Mitf, Pax3, Krt8, Krt18, and Krt19 all had adjusted P=1.0 in every Snai2-measured neuronal group.

EMT-family comparators did not phenocopy Snai2: Zeb1 and Zeb2 had 22 and 15 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in Snai2-matched groups, whereas Snai2, Twist2, Sox10, Pax3, Tgfbr1, Smad3, Smad4, and Stat3 were flat in the same groups.

Across the complete model-visible universe, Snai2 had no meaningful whole-signature neighbor: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was Gabrg2 at r=0.0305 and the strongest negative was Bcl11a at r=-0.0170 over 321,942 matched rows.

The published hypothalamic Slug-LepRb axis was not recovered in the two Snai2-measured HY groups: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut each had 0 downstream genes, and Lepr/Stat3/Socs3/Pomc/Agrp were all FDR=1.0.

Postnatal Snca loss produced a near-pan-neuronal transcriptional buffer: all 21 self-transcript rows trended negative, but 20 of 21 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene and the whole Snca surface contained only one downstream hit.
The only robust Snca downstream gene was an isolated decrease of Copg2, the COPI γ2 coatomer subunit, in 052 Pvalb Gaba.

Synuclein and presynaptic-vesicle loss-of-function perturbations did not phenocopy Snca: Sncb, Stx1b, Sv2a, Syp, and Synj1 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, Dnajc5 had only one, and Snca did not induce Sncb or Sncg transcripts.

Parkinson/trafficking comparators separated from Snca: Vps35 produced a real 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature, whereas Snca was flat in the same group and Park7 and Atp13a2 were flat across all measured groups.

The unbiased whole-surface nearest neighbors of Snca were essentially orthogonal: Arx was the top positive neighbor at cosine +0.0308 and Atp6v1e1 the top negative neighbor at -0.0178, with no shared FDR<0.10 gene.
Sncb loss is downstream-silent across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups: every group has zero non-Sncb genes at FDR<0.10 even though the Sncb transcript itself is significantly lower in 10 groups.
The measurable synuclein paralog Snca also fails to generate a robust downstream signature and does not correlate with Sncb.
Wild-type Sncb loss does not phenocopy β-synuclein missense or aggregation biology at the RNA level.
Unbiased full-transcriptome neighbor analysis found no meaningful Sncb signature neighbor.

Snrnp70 loss produced a gene-level response in 12 of 21 measured neuron groups, with the largest signatures in MB Glut, TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, MB P MY GABA and L2-3 IT CTX Glut rather than uniformly across all neurons.
Responder groups repeatedly altered RNA-processing genes, including Drosha, Clasrp, Sart1, Srek1, Cpsf1 and Snrnp200 up-regulation and Pnisr, Rsrp1, Arglu1, Luc7l2 and Luc7l3 down-regulation.
Snrnp70 responders up-regulated transcriptional and chromatin regulators such as Smarcc2, Mbd6, Dot1l, Kdm6b, Dnttip1, Gtf2i, Gtf2ird1 and Ints7.
The Snrnp70 signature converged strongly with proteasome subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 and contained recurrent ubiquitin/proteostasis genes.

Nuclear Snrnp70 disruption propagated to neuronal connectivity genes: Dgkz, Dbn1, Cttnbp2 and Kif1a were recurrently up, whereas Gria2, Ntng1, Icam5, Kcnc1/Kcnc2, Scn8a, Cck and Lrrc7 marked a smaller down-regulated synaptic/electrical surface.

The closest positive neighbors of Snrnp70 were a mixed RNA-biogenesis/proteasome set rather than a pure U1 snRNP set: Thoc1, Psmc1, Psmb4, Prpf6, U2af2, Hnrnpu, Tpr, Rnpc3, Ddx39b and Cdc40 occupied ranks 1-10.
Snrpb, the only directly represented Sm-core U1 snRNP subunit among the queried U1/Sm comparators, did not phenocopy Snrnp70.
Snrnp70 perturbation did not broadly induce canonical ISR, UPR, NRF2 or autophagy marker transcripts despite hundreds of RNA-processing and proteostasis DEGs in the strongest responders.
No robust negative mirror of the Snrnp70 signature was found: Eif5a and Mtor were the top two anti-neighbors by cosine but each shared only one opposite-direction FDR<0.10 Snrnp70 feature.

Acute postnatal Snrpb loss produced a near-flat gene-level neuronal surface: all 23 cell groups were measured, every Snrpb self-transcript FDR was 1.0, and only Foxp1 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut was a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Foxp1 up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut was the only robust downstream Snrpb hit.
Represented spliceosome relatives U2af2, Prpf6, and Snrnp70 generated broad FDR gene-expression waves while Snrpb remained nearly flat.
The SmN paralog target Snrpn did not phenocopy Snrpb in this neuronal assay.
Unbiased Snrpb signature-neighbor search found no robust convergent or opposing perturbation module.
Snrpn coding loss was almost transcriptionally silent and produced a two-gene downstream response only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The strongest Snrpn-induced downstream transcript was Pja1, an E3 ubiquitin-ligase marker, in L4-5 IT neurons.
Lin7a was the only down-regulated downstream gene after Snrpn perturbation in L4-5 IT neurons.
Snrpn failed to phenocopy directly measured spliceosome perturbations.
The embryonic Nr4a1 rescue axis was not recovered after postnatal Snrpn loss.
Single coding-gene perturbations from the paternally expressed PWS set and neighboring PWS/AS GABA-receptor set were flat or nearly flat like Snrpn.
Unbiased signature-neighbor search found no convincing Snrpn phenocopy or anti-phenocopy.
Postmitotic neuronal Snta1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic signature in any measured cell group.
The neuronally read DGC/DAPC module was largely transcriptionally silent: Dag1, Dmd, and Sgce mirrored the Snta1 null, while Sgcd had only two accepted genes in one thalamic group.
Canonical Snta1-linked AQP4/K+ and nNOS/sodium-channel axes were not recovered as mRNA programs in NeuN+ neurons.
A sparse postnatal Snta1 LoF does not phenocopy the transcriptomic consequences one might expect from rare human SNTA1 cardiac sodium-channel variants.
Sgcd, but not Snta1, Dag1, or Sgce, produced a small Sik2/Porcn-positive response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Postnatal neuronal Snx10 loss was a complete FDR-level transcriptional negative across all 22 recovered cell groups.
Snx10 did not converge with represented V-ATPase, autophagy, myeloid, or PDGFR/stemness comparators, and its data-driven raw-signature neighbors were only very weak.

Acute P16 Sod2 perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups, even though the Sod2 transcript itself was significantly lower in four groups.
The expected Nrf2/antioxidant-response and ATF4/integrated-stress transcripts were absent after Sod2 perturbation.
Opa1 loss, a mitochondrial inner-membrane perturbation measured in the same cell groups, generated a recurrent amino-acid/ATF4-like stress signature that Sod2 did not.
Represented antioxidant and superoxide-damage pathway comparators, Gpx4, Nfe2l2, Park7, Prdx1, and Aco2, also failed to produce a broad Sod2-like or NRF2-like signature.
A transcriptome-wide neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Sod2 signature neighbors.
Sohlh1 is a complete transcriptional null across every recovered neuronal class in this P16-to-P37/44 mouse-brain CRISPR screen.
Sohlh1 does not participate in a detectable brain perturbation module, and inspected germline-network relatives do not reveal an active shared Sohlh1 module.
A glioblastoma Wnt/β-catenin phenotype for SOHLH1 loss is not recovered in normal NeuN+ postmitotic neurons.
Son produced a sharply restricted response: the only downstream FDR<0.10 gene was Coro6 down-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Son Pvalb Coro6 decrease converged with Prpf6, U2af2, and Hnrnpu perturbations, which also significantly down-regulated Coro6 in 052 Pvalb Gaba.

Son did not phenocopy broad RNA-processing-factor loss: Prpf6 was the top positive nominal neighbor but had 3134 FDR<0.10 genes across matched groups, and U2af2, Hnrnpu, Snrnp70, and Tardbp were also far broader than Son.
direction_pattern: Son minimal; multiple pathway comparators broad

canonical_summary: The P16 Son perturbation failed to recover gene-level down-regulation of canonical ZTTK brain-development, migration, metabolism, or pluripotency substrates.
Sorbs1 was a broad neuronal transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 after acute P16 CRISPR perturbation.
The canonical CAP-Cbl-insulin program was absent from both Sorbs1 guide cells and measured pathway-neighbor perturbations.
Sorbs1 loss did not trigger SORBS paralog compensation or an actin-adhesion transcriptional substitute in the measured neuronal nuclei.
Sorbs1 had no nontrivial unbiased signature neighbor in the model-visible target universe.
The Ataxin-7/Sorbs1 link is not reproduced by simple loss of either gene in this postnatal neuronal snRNA screen.
Acute Sorl1 CRISPR produced a pure self-transcript perturbation with no robust downstream transcriptome in any measured neuronal group.
The Sorl1 null sits inside a broader APP-secretase/endosomal module that is largely invisible to this juvenile neuronal snRNA readout.
No robust data-driven signature neighbor of Sorl1 was recovered across 1,772 other target surfaces.
The directly measured retromer core gene Vps35, unlike Sorl1 or the retromer-like Vps35l, generated a focused response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The only Sort1 downstream FDR<0.10 event was Sfpq down-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA, and the same Sfpq-down event recurred in that group after Ogt, Hnrnpu, Tpr, and Psmc1 perturbation.
Sort1 RNA depletion was detectable in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and weak 155 MB Glut without any downstream FDR<0.10 response.
Sort1 loss did not induce a lysosomal, autophagy, UPR/ISR, or AP-1 marker-gene program across the measured surface.
Literature-obvious Sort1 relatives did not phenocopy Sort1: Sorl1 was fully flat, Grn and Tmem106b produced only isolated one-gene responses, and Ngfr/Ntrk/Ntsr1 targets were flat or nearly flat.
Core membrane-trafficking perturbations, especially Cltc and Vps35, generated FDR<0.10 programs in matched neuronal groups where Sort1 was flat.
Sort1 had no strong global signature neighbor; the maximum positive all-score cosine was 0.035 and the maximum negative magnitude was 0.014.
Sos1 produced a single FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response: Cul7 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Sos1 did not recapitulate the thalamic RAF/MEK attenuation signature seen after Braf or Map2k1 perturbation.
Zbtb7a was the only FDR-significant same-coordinate neighbor of Sos1, sharing Cul7 up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Full transcriptome-wide residual matching found no stable positive or negative Sos1 signature neighbor.
Postnatal neuronal Sos1 loss did not induce a basal ERK/immediate-early transcriptional program resembling RASopathy pathway activation.
The broad neuronal flatness of Sos1 loss should not be read as blanket safety for systemic SOS1 inhibition.
Sox10 perturbation was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: none of the 22 recovered NeuN+ cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The expected Sox10 myelin and neural-crest target program was absent, including Mbp, Plp1, Mag, Mog, Myrf, Pdgfra, Erbb3, Ngfr, Egr2, Mpz, Mitf, Sox9, and Dusp15.

Literature-obvious Sox10 relatives also failed to form a coherent neuronal signature: Sox9, Erbb3, Pax3, and Ret had 0 FDR<0.10 genes in Sox10-matched groups, while Myrf had only a single Mapk8 hit in L5 ET neurons.

Data-driven Sox10 neighbors were rejected as biological convergence: Wdr26 was the top positive score-vector neighbor and Fbxo11 the top negative neighbor, but their cosine similarities were only +0.055 and -0.031 and Sox10 shared no FDR genes with either.
The null argues against this P16 sparse neuronal LoF assay as a model of SOX10-linked Waardenburg-Hirschsprung or PCWH biology.
Sox11 acute LoF produced no robust transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Whole-universe signature neighbors of Sox11 were near-zero correlations, with Tgfbr2/Mycn as the top positive and Unc13b/Htr1a as the top negative neighbors.
The SOXC / immature-neuron program expected from Sox11 biology was absent in this P16 postmitotic screen.
The postmitotic Sox11 null argues that SOX11 haploinsufficiency phenotypes are not replayed by acute loss in already specified juvenile neurons.
Sox17 loss produced a complete postmitotic-neuronal transcriptomic null: all 23 measured neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
None of the prespecified Sox17-linked endodermal, arterial/endothelial, Wnt, or OPC/myelin marker panels were recovered after Sox17 perturbation.
The assay can detect a Wnt/β-catenin-related neuronal signature, but it belongs to Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2, not Sox17.
Sox17 did not participate in a generic SOX-family neuronal response.
The unbiased Sox17 signature had no meaningful positive or negative whole-surface neighbor.
The SOX17 pulmonary-arterial-hypertension prior maps to vascular endothelium, not to the Sox17-null neuronal compartment sampled here.

Sox18 had a very sparse neuronal response: one up-regulated singleton in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and one up-regulated singleton in 215 MB Dopa, with no other measured group containing a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

The Sox18 perturbation did not recover the canonical endothelial or lymphatic program: Prox1, Flt4, Lyve1, Pdpn, Cldn5, Kdr, Sox7, Sox17, Mef2c, and related markers were FDR-null across the Sox18 neuronal surface.
St8sia3 was the only FDR-positive Sox18-induced gene in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Tsr3 was the only FDR-positive Sox18-induced gene in 215 MB Dopa.

Literature-obvious vascular comparators failed to phenocopy Sox18 in neurons: Sox17 was FDR-flat in all 23 groups, while Mef2c, Prox1, Kdr, and Flt4 responded in other or nonoverlapping groups and did not share the Sox18 St8sia3/Tsr3 singletons.

The data-driven Sox18 neighborhood was effectively unclustered: the best broad positive score cosines were only about 0.03 and the best negative cosines were about -0.01, with no reproduced St8sia3 or Tsr3 hit.
The screen shows no broad postmitotic neuronal transcriptional liability for Sox18 loss but is not an efficacy test for vascular SOX18 inhibition.
Sox2 produced one robust acute neuronal response: Tnnt1 and Stam were both down-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while every other measured cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The thalamic two-gene hit did not recover canonical Sox2 neural-stem, pluripotency, proliferation, Notch/Hes, or published dLGN Efna5/serotonin-transporter outputs.
Tnnt1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recurred across thalamic transcriptional perturbations: Rora down-regulated it even more strongly, whereas Sox5 up-regulated the same gene.
The full-transcriptome nearest neighbors of Sox2 were numerical but not biological convergences.
Measured Sox-family, pluripotency, REST, Notch, and chromatin-neighbor targets did not phenocopy Sox2 in the responding thalamic class.
Acute Sox4 loss in P16-postmitotic neurons produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any measured brain cell group.
The canonical SoxC neurogenic output genes were silent as a program after Sox4 perturbation.
Sox11, the measurable SoxC paralog, failed to converge with Sox4 because both single perturbations were buffered in the Sox4-matched postnatal neurons.
The flat Sox4 result contrasts with a detectable Tbr1 program in matched postmitotic cortical groups.
Sox4 had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
The human SOX4 haploinsufficiency phenotype is not reproduced by postnatal single-neuron Sox4 loss, favoring a developmental or progenitor mechanism for this assay gap.
P16 Sox5 loss induced a real but extremely sparse signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, up-regulating Dgkh and Tnnt1 while the Sox5 transcript itself was essentially flat.
The expected postmitotic cortical projection-neuron fate program was absent after juvenile Sox5 disruption.
