Tbr1, but not Sox5, produced a detectable post-P16 cortical transcriptomic response in matched cortical groups.
Represented Sox-family perturbations did not phenocopy Sox5.
The genome-wide Sox5 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor in the full model-visible perturbation universe.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was broadly responsive to other perturbations even though Sox5 was two-gene sparse.

Sox9 loss of function is essentially silent in the NeuN-enriched postmitotic neuronal screen: 21 cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, 308 CB GABA had only a subthreshold Pan2 signal, and 215 MB Dopa had a single FDR<0.10 gene.
The only robust downstream Sox9 DEG was Sec23a down-regulation in 215 MB Dopa.
Neither the unbiased neighbor scan nor the SOX/NFI/Notch-STAT/BMP comparator panel produced a convincing Sox9 phenocopy.
The Sox9 screen result is a context guardrail for SOX9 disease interpretation, not a negative test of SOX9 haploinsufficiency.
Acute postmitotic Sp110 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The interferon, NF-kB/cytokine, and apoptosis genes expected from Sp110 macrophage biology were absent from the neuronal Sp110 DE surface, and represented IFN-pathway targets failed to phenocopy it.
Data-driven full-score neighbors of Sp110 were all extremely weak, with absolute Pearson correlations below 0.04 and no coherent shared DE program.
Sp7 loss caused a two-gene downstream response only in 308 CB GABA, with Fam32a up and Scd2 down; every other measured neuronal group was FDR-null or weak.
Scd2 was significantly decreased after Sp7 perturbation in 308 CB GABA.

Wdr26 was the strongest robust positive empirical neighbor of the Sp7 308 CB GABA rank signature, whereas Eef2 was the strongest robust negative neighbor but failed to share Fam32a or Scd2 at FDR<0.10.
Runx2/BMP/SMAD/Wnt and related osteogenic perturbations represented in the dataset did not phenocopy Sp7 in 308 CB GABA.
Sp7 perturbation in NeuN-enriched postnatal neurons did not recover the osteoblast ECM/mineralization or oligodendrocyte ECM/node-of-Ranvier programs expected from other SP7 contexts.
Spast perturbation produced no downstream FDR<0.10 gene in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups, with Spast mRNA itself FDR=1.0 everywhere.
No ER-endosomal, lysosomal, autophagy, ISR/UPR, or proteostasis program was recovered after Spast perturbation.
Measured HSP, tubular-ER, ESCRT, and microtubule-motor relatives did not phenocopy Spast in the matched neuronal groups.
The unbiased DE-neighbor scan found no meaningful positive or negative Spast signature neighbor.
Acute postnatal Spata7 loss produced no FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
Represented retinal/ciliary comparators did not reveal a Spata7-like brain ciliary module.
The top data-driven neighbors of Spata7 were near-zero score-cosine matches rather than a coherent convergent module.
The brain null should not deprioritize photoreceptor-directed Spata7 rescue or retinal safety testing.
Specc1l P16 loss-of-function was pan-neuronally downstream-null across all 22 recovered cell groups.
Specc1l did not phenocopy the β-catenin transcriptional response that Ctnnb1 produced in the same thalamic glutamatergic groups.
Represented Rho/WAVE-proximal and PI3K-AKT comparators were also flat or singleton-only, placing Specc1l within a broader postmitotic-neuron cytoskeletal buffering pattern.
The data-driven Specc1l nearest neighbors were essentially correlation-null and noncanonical.
The screen result refines SPECC1L disease modeling: acute neuronal LoF does not reproduce the congenital structural-birth-defect axis or the reported gain-of-function microtubule-domain allele class.
Sphk1 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every assayed postmitotic neuronal group.
The expected ceramide/S1P stress, apoptosis, UPR/ISR, NF-kappaB, cytokine, immediate-early, and lipid-feedback programs were absent at FDR level.
Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor represented sphingolipid-pathway targets converged with Sphk1.
Basal NeuN+ neurons did not expose the glial inflammatory SphK1/S1P axis often used to motivate SphK/S1P targeting in CNS disease.
Spi1 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across every recovered postnatal NeuN+ neuronal group.
The Alzheimer/microglial PU.1 module was expected from the literature but absent from the Spi1 neuronal DE surface.
Myeloid-lineage Spi1 comparators were flat, while neuron-active benchmarks produced large signatures in the same matched taxonomy.
The rank-vector neighbors of Spi1 were rejected as biological convergence.
Other ETS-family targets in the parquet did not phenocopy Spi1 in neurons.
Sppl2a loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 neuronal cell groups in which the target was recovered.

The known SPPL2 proteolysis network did not converge on the Sppl2a null surface: Itm2b, Tmem106b, Vamp1, Nrg1, Adam10, and Psen1 perturbations had only isolated FDR<0.10 genes or none, and none overlapped a Sppl2a DEG set because Sppl2a had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
An unbiased feature-centered search found no meaningful Sppl2a signature neighbor; the top biological positive and negative residual cosines were only +0.0388 and -0.0437.

The neuronal Sppl2a null does not de-risk systemic SPPL2a inhibition: the pharmacology and disease biology act through CD74/p8 accumulation and antigen-presenting-cell loss, which are outside this NeuN+ postnatal assay.
Acute postmitotic Spred1 loss is a pan-measured-neuronal basal-transcriptome null.
The expected Spred1 hyper-ERK/activity RNA program was absent even though direct Braf and Map2k1 perturbations produced a small shared TH-neuron signature.
The closest assayed paralog, Spred2, phenocopied Spred1 only by being silent itself.
Unconstrained signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Spred1-like or anti-Spred1 module.
The null snRNA-seq surface should not be read as absence of MEK-dependent Spred1 disease biology.

Spred2 acute loss-of-function was a pan-neuronal basal transcriptome null: all 23 measured neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 299 tests of ERK/TrkB sentinel transcripts were all non-significant.

Core pathway perturbations showed that the assay can recover a sparse Ras/MAPK-linked neuron state, but Spred2 did not converge with it. Braf, Map2k1, and Shoc2 loss each down-regulated Vgf in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut or 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, whereas Spred2 had zero genes in those same groups.

The closest represented paralog, Spred1, also had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in its 21 recovered groups and was nearly orthogonal to Spred2 by centered logFC correlation, supporting a buffered single-SPRED state rather than a Spred1-to-Spred2 phenocopy.

The unbiased signature search found no strong Spred2 neighbors: among 382 complete 23-group profiles, the best positive Pearson correlation was Pou3f3 at r=0.119 and the most negative was Reep1 at r=-0.034.
P16 mosaic Sptan1 loss produced an almost flat nuclear RNA phenotype across the recovered neuronal taxonomy: every cell group was measured, but only two non-target genes reached FDR<0.10.
The only FDR<0.10 Sptan1 downstream genes were two negative, cell-class-restricted hits: Mtor in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Gnpat in 191 MB P MY GABA.

Represented actin-spectrin/ankyrin-adducin comparators did not phenocopy Sptan1: Add1, Add2, Add3, Ank2, and Sptb were downstream-null, while Actg1 and Ank1 had only one or two total FDR genes in distinct groups.
Gnpat down-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA recurred in Setd1a and Psmc1 perturbations in the same cell class, even though the whole-surface Sptan1 vector had essentially no strong positive neighbor.

The 009 Mtor decrease should not be read as Sptan1 engaging an mTOR pathway: Mtor perturbation itself was null in 009 and 191, and the Sptan1 response lacked a multigene growth/autophagy transcriptional program.
Score-vector neighbors of Sptan1 were vanishingly weak; the best non-control cosine was Ifnar1 at 0.025635 and the strongest anti-neighbor was Wdr26 at -0.020084.
Sptb is a screen-wide flat perturbation in postnatal neuronal nuclei: every tested cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected βI-spectrin postsynaptic NCAM/AnkR/PSD program was not converted into detectable nuclear mRNA changes in L2/3, hippocampal, or medial-habenula/thalamic glutamatergic groups.
Sptb sits in a locally buffered membrane-skeleton neighborhood: the represented αII-spectrin, ankyrin, and adducin perturbations were also null or one-to-two-gene responders in the same cell groups.
Sptb had no meaningful transcriptomic nearest neighbor; its strongest positive and negative whole-surface correlations were tiny.
Sptlc2 produced exactly two downstream FDR<0.10 hits: U2af1 up in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Creld1 down in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Pvalb, TH Prkcd Grin2c, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed significant Sptlc2 mRNA depletion but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The expected ER-stress, ISR, autophagy and sphingolipid-compensation transcript program was absent across every Sptlc2 cell group.
Sparse Sptlc2 CRISPR loss-of-function in juvenile central neurons did not phenocopy dominant SPTLC2 neuropathy or ALS mechanisms at the transcriptome level.
Neither unbiased score-neighbor search nor the represented sphingolipid salvage target Asah1 revealed a strong Sptlc2 phenocopy or inverse signature.
Sqstm1 loss produced a very sparse neuronal transcriptional surface: only 3 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responding group had exactly one such gene.
Pvalb interneurons were the only forebrain inhibitory class with a robust downstream hit, down-regulating the synaptic adhesion-family transcript Lrfn5.
The two non-cortical glutamatergic responses pointed to mitochondrial ion-homeostasis genes: Sfxn5 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Micu3 increased in 155 MB Glut.
Canonical p62-adjacent NRF2/redox, lysosomal-autophagy, proteasome, UPR, and ISR transcripts were absent from the Sqstm1 FDR<0.10 surface.
Uba5 was the strongest FDR-restricted same-direction neighbor of Sqstm1, sharing Sfxn5 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Micu3 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
Literature-obvious autophagy, NRF2, NF-kB, mTOR, and lysosomal comparators did not phenocopy Sqstm1, and the closest p62-family receptor Nbr1 was not a represented perturbation target.

No global positive or inverse signature neighbor was convincing: Esr2, Gprasp2, Adgrg2, and Wdr26 were the top whole-surface score hits but had near-zero correlations and no robust shared Sqstm1 features.
Srebf1-targeting CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic effect in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
The direct paralog Srebf2, but not Srebf1, drove a detectable sterol-biosynthetic loss signature in the same neuronal survey.
A Tsc2/Srebf2-opposed sterol module was present, whereas Srebf1 was uncoupled from that neuronal mTORC1-responsive lipid arm.
Whole-signature neighbors of Srebf1 were themselves near-null, so the closest cosine relationships are not interpretable as a shared pathway.
The screen does not support a constitutive stress, proteasome, or lipid-toxicity response to Srebf1 loss in juvenile neurons; SREBP1 neurotoxicity is likely activation-context dependent.

Srebf2 loss did not trigger a pan-neuronal lipid response; the FDR<0.10 sterol program was concentrated in hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and pontine/myelencephalic groups, with only an edge Dhcr24 hit in cortical L5/6 IT neurons.
The responder genes form a compact SREBP2 cholesterol-biosynthesis module: Dhcr24, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Fdps, Sqle, and Lss were all down-regulated where Srebf2 responded.
Insig1 was the most recurrent Srebf2-dependent gene, falling in six responder groups, while Ldlr fell only in the two strongest MB/P-MY signatures.
Srebf2 loss in postnatal neurons was sterol-selective rather than broadly lipogenic: Acaca in 155 MB Glut was the only canonical fatty-acid enzyme among the 34 significant downstream rows.
Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, and Msmo1 were the most recurrent Srebf2-responsive genes and provide a short neuronal engagement panel.
Marchf6 knockdown, an ER-ubiquitin control point in cholesterol synthesis, was an inverse Srebf2 neighbor and up-regulated 12 of the Srebf2 sterol features at FDR<0.10.

The strongest data-driven inverse neighbors were not the canonical SREBP machinery: Mib1 and Dctn1 each up-regulated 32 of the 34 Srebf2 sterol features at FDR<0.10, and Txndc15 was weaker with 5 inverse overlaps.
Among same-direction data-driven neighbors, Phf12 and Uba5 reproducibly lowered the Srebf2 sterol features, whereas Slc7a6os was rejected after FDR-overlap testing.

The measured obvious relatives did not phenocopy Srebf2: Srebf1 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 groups, and Hmgcr produced only two non-sterol hits with no overlap to the Srebf2 signature.
Srr is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR assay: 20 tested cell groups had 0 genes at FDR<0.10.

Srr did not phenocopy direct NMDAR-subunit perturbation: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced 144, 31, and 83 FDR<0.10 genes in the same 20 cell groups, whereas Srr produced none and had near-zero score correlations with those targets.
Whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Srr neighbor: the largest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was Wdr26 at r=0.0387, and the largest negative was Trpm7 at r=-0.0215.
Canonical NMDAR-response and compensation transcripts were absent after Srr perturbation: Arc, Fos, Egr1, Npas4, Bdnf, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b were never significant in any Srr-tested group.
Ssr4 loss produced a single ER-luminal foldase hit, Ppib down in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, without a broader ER-stress or glycosylation transcriptome.
Three neuronal groups lowered the Ssr4 self-transcript at FDR<0.10 but had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
ER-biogenesis comparators Hspa5 and Sec63 induced detectable ER-stress/ER-translocation programs in matched thalamic or midbrain groups, whereas Ssr4 did not.
Data-driven Ssr4 signature neighbors were negligible across the whole model-visible target universe.
The SSR4-CDG prior does not translate into a broad postmitotic neuronal UPR or N-glycosylation RNA signature after P16 Ssr4 perturbation.
Sstr5 loss produced no FDR-supported neuronal transcriptome in any recovered taxonomy group.
The Sstr5-null surface did not phenocopy represented Gi/o, cAMP/PKA, calcium, GIRK, or CB1-crosstalk nodes.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis placed Sstr5 on the noise floor rather than in a coherent perturbation module.
The negative brain result should be read as context displacement of endocrine SSTR5 pharmacology, not as evidence that SSTR5 antagonism or agonism is biologically inert.
St3gal5 produced a single downstream hit, Pggt1b up in 155 MB Glut, and this was the top Pggt1b induction among all target perturbations measured in that cell group.
The St3gal5 surface lacks a canonical GM3-ganglioside, glucose/mitochondrial, immediate-early, UPR/ISR, or apoptosis transcriptional program despite on-target St3gal5 RNA reduction in many groups.

Represented sphingolipid comparators do not phenocopy St3gal5: Sptlc2 responds in 007 and 027 where St3gal5 is flat or weak, and Sptlc2, Asah1, and Psap do not reproduce the 155 MB Glut Pggt1b signal.
Clinical epilepsy and Rett/Pitt-Hopkins-like comparators represented in the parquet generated cell-type-specific signatures distinct from the Pggt1b-only St3gal5 response.
The pre-literature all-target neighbor search did not identify a robust convergent or anti-convergent module for St3gal5.
Stag1 produced a minimal but FDR-supported response restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Gabra1 was lower in perturbed nuclei.
The measured cohesin relatives did not phenocopy Stag1: Stag2 opposed the Stag1 Gabra1 effect while Smc1a, Pds5a, Hdac8, and Ctcf were absent or transcriptionally distinct.
Data-driven neighbor analysis collapsed to a one-gene 151 TH Gabra1 axis rather than a multi-gene Stag1 module.
Stag1 loss failed to recover the broad cohesin-dependent neuronal maturation, synaptic, glutamate-receptor, or activity-regulated program expected after core RAD21 depletion.
Stag2 produced a single robust response, 55 FDR<0.10 genes, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero FDR<0.10 genes in every other measured Stag2 cell group; 215 MB Dopa was not tested.

The thalamic Stag2 signature is dominated by down-regulated adhesion, extracellular-matrix, synaptic, and neuronal-signaling genes including Ptprm, Ptprz1, Adamts2, Adamts19, Sema5a, Necab2, Npy1r, Lrrc7, Sez6, Asic2, Begain, and Aplp2.
A smaller up-regulated arm, Stmn2, Nipa1, Tspan5, Gabra1, Syt11, Inhbb, Atl1, Tubb4b, Ntm, Adgrl3, Rab6b, and Sav1, accompanies the down-regulated thalamic module.

Smc1a was the strongest positive Stag2 neighbor over the 55-gene thalamic signature, with cosine 0.905 and 14 same-direction shared FDR genes, whereas data-driven negative neighbors had no FDR-supported opposite overlaps.
The literature-obvious relatives Stag1, Pds5a, and Hdac8 did not phenocopy Stag2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Stag1 had only an opposite Gabra1 call, and Pds5a and Hdac8 had no FDR<0.10 genes.
Ctcf, Elp1, Brd4, and Ctnnb1 shared the Stag2 thalamic module only as a restricted sub-signature nested inside much larger or broader transcriptional responses.
Stag2 loss did not induce a FDR-supported immediate-early, p53, ISR/UPR, cell-cycle, or oligodendrocyte myelination/cholesterol program in any measured NeuN+ neuronal group.

Stard7 loss produced an almost flat postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq surface: only 1 downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in 22 recovered cell groups, and canonical ER-stress, ISR, redox and mitochondrial-transcript genes were absent.
The only Stard7 FDR<0.10 responder was a Pcmtd1 decrease in 191 MB P MY GABA.

A matched mitochondrial perturbation, Opa1, strongly induced an amino-acid/ISR and mitochondrial transcript program in 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas Stard7 was reduced to Pcmtd1 alone in the same control stratum.
Coding loss of Stard7 and of represented FAME repeat-host genes did not phenocopy one another in juvenile mouse neurons.
STARD7 did not collapse into a general lipid-transfer transcriptomic class: Cert1, Osbpl2 and Acbd5 were flat, while Pitpna produced a small, different response.
Pre-literature signature-neighbor search found only weak restricted-score neighbors, and measuring them back rejected them as robust Stard7 phenocopies.
Stat1 loss of function was transcriptomically silent downstream of the target transcript in every measured neuronal group.
The flat Stat1 result matched the broader unliganded IFN/STAT neighborhood rather than standing out as an isolated failed target.
The expected antiviral ISG and MHC-I antigen-presentation modules were absent after Stat1 perturbation.

Stat2 loss produced an almost completely buffered steady-state neuronal transcriptome: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10, the remaining group had a single FDR<0.10 hit, and the Stat2 transcript itself never passed FDR correction.
The only Stat2 downstream gene at FDR<0.10 was Qrich1 down-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.

The ISGF3 axis did not phenocopy Stat2: Stat1 and Ifnar2 were completely flat in the 22 matched groups, Ifnar1 and Irf9 had one isolated hit apiece elsewhere, and none reproduced the 008 Qrich1 decrease.

Stat2 had no meaningful transcriptome-scale signature neighbor in the model-visible screen; even the highest signed-score cosines were near zero and a Safe_target profile ranked among the apparent nearest neighbors.
The disease-relevant antiviral role of STAT2 is separable from basal postnatal neuronal transcriptome maintenance.

Stat3 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and canonical STAT3-responsive transcripts Socs3, Bcl2l1, Junb, Fos, and Gfap were FDR=1.000 everywhere they were tested.

The flat Stat3 surface was pathway-wide rather than Stat3-specific: perturbing represented STAT paralogs and IL-6/IL-10/IFN/OSM receptor nodes yielded only three isolated downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 219 target-by-cell tests and did not correlate with Stat3.

An unbiased nearest-neighbor search found no meaningful Stat3 signature neighbor; the strongest positive score correlation was Litaf at r=0.02847, and the strongest biological negative was Ago1 at r=-0.00834.
Stat4 loss of function produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional response in any measured brain group.
The measurable IL-12/IFN/STAT relatives did not reveal a hidden neuronal cytokine-JAK-STAT module.
Stat4 had no meaningful data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor.
Autoimmune and myeloid Stat4 biology should not be read as evidence for a direct basal neuronal transcriptomic liability of Stat4 loss.
Stat5b perturbation was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of 22 assayed cell groups.
Canonical STAT5/GH response transcripts were present in the tests but not regulated by Stat5b: Cish, Socs2, Socs3, Bcl2l1, Pim1, and Igf1 all had FDR=1.0 wherever tested.

Literature-obvious STAT and receptor comparators did not reveal a hidden JAK-STAT module: Stat1, Stat3, Stat4, Ghr, the IL2/21/23 receptor genes, Ifnar2, Ifngr1, Ifngr2, and Bcl2 had 0 DEGs, while Stat2, Prlr, Lepr, and Ifnar1 each produced only one non-overlapping DEG in the Stat5b-matched groups.

The unbiased signature-neighbor search returned only near-zero neighbors: the strongest positive Stat5b neighbor had a Wilcoxon-score cosine of 0.027 and the strongest overall anti-neighbor was -0.018.
The screen separates STAT5B growth, immune, and hematologic-disease biology from a broad mature neuronal basal phenotype.
Acute Stk39 perturbation was completely flat at the FDR<0.10 downstream-gene threshold across the 21 neuronal groups in which it was recovered.

The directly represented WNK-SPAK/CCC relatives Wnk1, Wnk3, and Slc12a2 did not converge with Stk39: Wnk1 and Slc12a2 were also transcriptomically silent, and Wnk3 produced only three isolated FDR<0.10 genes.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no coherent Stk39 neighbor or anti-neighbor; the largest Wilcoxon-score correlations across 355046 matched entries were only +0.032 and -0.027.
The mouse-neuron Stk39 null does not phenocopy the established renal and vascular SPAK biology that links STK39 to blood pressure.
Acute P16 Stmn2 CRISPR loss was almost completely transcriptionally buffered: only one downstream gene, Tuba1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
The only downstream response was selective Tuba1a down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Stmn2 did not phenocopy direct microtubule-subunit perturbations: Tuba1a loss induced a multi-tubulin replacement program whereas Stmn2 loss only reduced Tuba1a in one group.
Tardbp converged with Stmn2 only on 151 Tuba1a suppression and otherwise diverged: Tardbp caused a broad RNA signature without gene-level Stmn2 loss.
The unbiased cross-perturbation nearest neighbors of Stmn2 were essentially uncorrelated and were rejected as biological signature matches.
The Parkinson-relevant 215 MB Dopa class had no Stmn2 rows and therefore the screen did not test the dopaminergic Stmn2 phenotype.

Stra6 was transcriptionally flat in every measured NeuN+ neuronal group: 22 of 22 recovered groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Stra6 self-transcript had FDR=1.0 wherever it was measured.
Loss of Stra6 did not lower a retinoic-acid feedback program in sampled neurons: Rarb/Rarg/Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Cyp26 genes, Dhrs3, Rbp1, Lrat, Rbp4, Ttr, Crabp1/2 and Aldh genes had no FDR<0.10 changes.

The measured nuclear retinoid receptors Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb and Rxrg did not phenocopy Stra6; cosine similarity to Stra6 was only 0.001-0.021 and each receptor perturbation produced at most one downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Unbiased score-space comparison did not uncover a hidden Stra6 module: the strongest positive and negative whole-surface neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score cosines of only 0.031 or less.
Strada loss produced an almost pan-neuronal transcriptional non-response after P16: 21 of 22 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene and the 22nd had only Epn1.
Epn1 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the sole FDR<0.10 Strada response.
Strada did not phenocopy Tsc2 even where a Tsc2 loss response was readily detectable.
Other represented AMPK/mTOR pathway neighbors also failed to converge with Strada.
Whole-transcriptome neighbor search put Strada in a near-null, non-modular signature neighborhood.
Stub1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups despite a consistent negative Stub1 self-transcript logFC.
Stub1 was uncoupled from core proteasome collapse: Psmb4 and Psmc1 loss caused thousands of DE genes and Psmb4 induced HSF/ISR/autophagy transcripts that Stub1 never induced.
Hsp70/Hsp90/HSF1/DNAJ comparators were flat or weak and did not converge with Stub1, contrasting with the broad Psmb4/Psmc1 response.
Perturbing aggregate-associated neurodegenerative targets did not recreate a Stub1 program, and Stub1 did not recreate theirs.
Unbiased full-transcriptome signature neighbors of Stub1 were near zero in both directions.

Stx16 loss produced a single robust downstream event, Ddx27 down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, rather than the broad Golgi, autophagy, or stress signature expected from a severe STX16 trafficking defect.

Measured STX/GARP/retromer/endolysosomal comparators did not phenocopy the Stx16 L5-ET Ddx27 signature; instead Rab7, Cltc, Stxbp1, Vps35 and Vps54 responded in different cell groups where Stx16 was flat.
Stx16 perturbation did not induce target-excluding Golgi/SNARE, lysosomal, autophagy, or UPR/ISR transcripts at FDR<0.10 in any recovered cell group.
Mouse neuronal Stx16 coding perturbation did not reproduce the human STX16-deletion/GNAS-imprinting axis: Gnas was FDR=1.0 in every recovered Stx16 group.
Data-driven whole-surface neighbor search failed to find a meaningful Stx16 convergent or opposing module; the largest residualized cosine magnitudes were near zero.
P16 Stx1b CRISPR produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Stx1b did not phenocopy Stxbp1/Munc18-1, the syntaxin-binding SNARE regulator that generated 140 downstream DE genes in matched groups.

The ranked Stx1b signature had no meaningful genome-scale or presynaptic-pathway neighbor; the strongest non-safe correlations were only |r|<=0.034 and most SNARE-cycle comparators were transcriptionally null or singleton responders.
The absence of an Stx1b nuclear biomarker warns against using this mosaic LoF snRNA-seq readout to rank therapies for variant-specific STX1B epilepsies.
Stx5a loss produced an almost empty snRNA-seq surface: only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 21 measured neuronal groups.
The only FDR-significant Stx5a signals were two isolated cell-group singletons: Sidt2 up in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons and Copg1 down in cerebellar GABA neurons.
Measured Golgi-traffic relatives did not phenocopy Stx5a; COG, COPI, Sar1b, Vcp and Stx16 perturbations were themselves largely flat and never reproduced the two Stx5a singleton genes at FDR<0.10.
A pre-literature restricted-signature search nominated Psmc1, Psmb4 and Gfpt1 as the nearest positive Stx5a neighbors, with Plxnd1, Smo and Ephb2 as the most negative gene-target neighbors.
Canonical nuclear stress programs expected from severe secretory-pathway failure were not recovered after Stx5a perturbation.

Stxbp1 drove a restricted postnatal neuronal transcriptional response rather than a universal Munc18-1 loss program: the largest signatures were in L4/5 IT cortical neurons, Pvalb interneurons and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, while many other neuronal classes had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

The dominant cortical IT program was down-regulation of excitatory synaptic and activity-coupled genes, including Nrxn2, Grin2b, Gria3, Homer1 and Dlg4 in L4/5 IT neurons and a smaller Camk2a/Gria3/Cpne6/Plekhg5 module in L2/3 IT neurons.
Pvalb interneurons engaged an inhibitory-synapse response with strong Slc6a1 down-regulation and additional Erbb4, Neto2, Nxph1, Nalcn and Slc24a2 decreases.
L4/5 IT neurons up-regulated dense-core-vesicle and secretory genes (Nrsn1, Pcsk1n, Scg2, Chgb, Cplx1) together with lipid-feedback genes Insig1 and Dhcr24.

A membrane-sorting module appeared across the broad L4/5 response and several one-gene effects: Fcho1 and Pacsin1 were down in L4/5 IT neurons, and Ankrd13d, Sort1, Snx1 and Znrf1 were the sole robust hits in ENT/PIR L2/3 IT, L5 ET, SST, and hypothalamic glutamatergic groups.
Midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed a mixed response with Mt1, Tfrc, Rnft1 and Fos up, but Cntnap1, Clptm1l, Psmc2, Tubb3, Aifm3, Paip2 and Abca2 down.
Stxbp1 loss did not induce a canonical UPR, heat-shock or proteasome-bounce-back transcriptome in any measured cell group.
The nearest positive Stxbp1 neighbors were not SNARE genes but Psmb4, Tpr, Psmc1 and Cltc; Psmb4 alone shared 74 Stxbp1 significant gene-by-cell features, 67 in the same direction.

Canonical release-machinery perturbations represented in the screen—Stx1b, Vamp1, Cplx1, Cplx2, Unc13a/b/c, Syt2, Cacna1a and Cacna1e—largely failed to phenocopy Stxbp1, despite being in the same vesicle-fusion pathway.

Acute P16 Sucla2 CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, including groups with significant or borderline Sucla2 mRNA depletion.

The Sucla2 null is informative for the ATF4/mitochondrial ISR axis: Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Aldh1l2, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, Fgf21, and Gdf15 were all absent from Sucla2, while Opa1 perturbation drove a recurrent ISR-like program in the same analysis universe.

The near-null response extended across the assayed SUCL/TCA neighborhood: Suclg1 and seven core TCA-enzyme perturbations collectively produced only nine downstream DEGs over 175 target-by-cell-type tests and no Sucla2-like convergent module.
Sucla2 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce Suclg1 or the alternative beta subunit Suclg2 in any measured neuronal group.

Whole-universe signature-neighbor analysis found no meaningful Sucla2 convergence: after excluding Safe_target controls, the top positive cosine was Mff at 0.034 and the strongest negative cosine was Zfp236 at -0.020.
Suclg1 loss produced one reproducible-threshold downstream transcript: Mapk1 was down only in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The same-complex beta subunit Sucla2 did not produce a downstream transcriptome and did not share the Suclg1-Pvalb Mapk1 hit.
TCA, OXPHOS, and mtDNA-linked comparator perturbations failed to converge on a shared Suclg1-like mitochondrial stress state.
Suclg1 did not activate the expected mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, OXPHOS-remodeling, TCA, or mitophagy sentinels in any recovered cell group.
Whole-signature nearest neighbors of Suclg1 were effectively absent, with the strongest positive target at cosine 0.033658 and the strongest negative target at -0.020731.
Suco loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal FDR-corrected transcriptional null across every recovered cell group.
Suco did not activate an ER-stress/UPR module that was detectable after Hspa5 perturbation in the same analysis universe.
The full-rank Suco signature sits at the origin: even the strongest positive and negative score-cosine neighbors were near zero and had DE surfaces that did not phenocopy Suco.
Acute postmitotic Sv2a perturbation depleted the target transcript in many neuronal classes but produced no FDR-controlled downstream mRNA program in any measured class.
The expected synaptotagmin/SNARE/vesicle and E/I-balance marker transcripts were not FDR-regulated after Sv2a perturbation.
Stxbp1, but not Sv2a, is a presynaptic release-pathway perturbation that crossed into a nuclear transcriptional response in this assay.
Most represented presynaptic vesicle-cycle comparators were as weak as Sv2a rather than Stxbp1-like.
SV2A CRISPR loss did not produce a robust mRNA biomarker for levetiracetam/SV2A pharmacology.
Genome-wide Sv2a signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative transcriptional neighbor.
Syn1 showed a broadly buffered single-nucleus transcriptome: 20 of 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the two responders each contributed only one downstream gene.
The 217 P MY Pineal Glut response was limited to down-regulation of the ER oxidoreductase Pdia6.
The 009 L2-3 IT PIR/AON/ENT Glut response was a single strong increase of the mitochondrial complex-I transcript mt-Nd1.
Syn1 loss did not induce a cell-autonomous immediate-early/activity program in any recovered neuronal group.
Syn1 did not phenocopy either Syn2 or the broader presynaptic-vesicle comparator set; Stxbp1 was the only tested presynaptic-fusion comparator with a broad DE surface.
A whole-signature search found no meaningful convergent or anti-correlated Syn1 neighbor.
Syn2 had one FDR-level downstream hit, Alg10b up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, without a broader ER-stress or synaptic-vesicle transcriptional program.
Large Syn2 self-transcript drops in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and a near-threshold drop in 052 Pvalb Gaba, did not propagate to any downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Syn2, Syn1, Syp, Sv2a, Dnm1, Cplx1, and Unc13a were self-only or nearly flat, whereas Stxbp1 produced 140 downstream genes in Syn2-matched groups.
A full-parquet Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found only near-zero Syn2 signature similarities and no FDR-level shared downstream genes among the top data-driven neighbors.
Sparse postmitotic Syn2 loss did not induce an activity, seizure, paralog-compensation, or ISR/UPR RNA state across the measured neuronal groups.
Syncrip produced an extremely restricted two-gene response in 308 CB GABA, with Narf up and Cdk10 down as the only downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all measured groups.
Canonical Syncrip-linked neuronal differentiation, synaptic, circadian, and ULK1/autophagy genes were not recovered after P16 Syncrip perturbation.
Syncrip is far flatter than represented hnRNP and RBP comparators: Hnrnpu, Tardbp, and Hnrnpc yielded broad DE surfaces while Syncrip had only two total downstream genes.
No measured target reproduced Syncrip's two-gene 308 CB GABA signature; Wdr26 was the only high-confidence same-cell-group overlap and moved Cdk10 in the opposite direction.
Fmr1 and core miRISC pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Syncrip in the postmitotic snRNA-seq surface.
Syncrip was uncoupled from core clock-output signatures even though Bmal1, Clock, and Cry2 perturbations produced Dbp and Nr1d responses in the same dataset.
Syne1 perturbation was nearly silent at the downstream RNA level across P16-perturbed juvenile neurons, with only 1 FDR<0.10 downstream call in 22 measured groups.
Dicer1 was selectively up-regulated in Syne1-perturbed 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA nuclei.
Data-driven global signature search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Syne1.
Dctn1, Kif5a, Kif5c, and reciprocal Dicer1 perturbations did not converge with Syne1.
The 308 CB GABA null indicates that juvenile broad cerebellar GABA neurons did not mount a corrected Syne1-loss RNA response despite the SYNE1 ataxia prior.
Acute P16 Syngap1 CRISPR produced a pan-null downstream snRNA-seq surface: no measured neuronal group contained even one non-target gene at FDR<0.10.
Canonical Ras/MAPK-, activity-regulated-, receptor-, and ISR/UPR sentinel genes did not become a detectable nuclear program after Syngap1 perturbation.
The PSD/SynGAP scaffold branch was transcriptionally quiet, whereas NMDAR subunit perturbations, especially Grin2b and Grin1, generated real DE signatures in matched neurons.
mTOR/translation-linked perturbations and an active data-driven comparator produced hundreds to thousands of FDR-significant genes where Syngap1 produced none.
The data-driven signature-neighbor search found no robust Syngap1 convergence module: the best full-surface positive and negative correlations were only +0.051 for Grin2b and -0.043 for Mff.

Synj1 loss-of-function produced a pan-surface transcriptional zero: all 21 recovered neuronal groups had no downstream gene at FDR<0.10, while Synj1 itself trended downward in every group and reached FDR<0.10 in four groups.

A core clathrin perturbation was readily transcriptional in matched groups whereas Synj1 was not: Cltc had 173 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 8 of 18 matched groups, including Jun/Ddit3 stress and synaptic-gene changes, while Synj1 and Dnm1 each had zero downstream genes.

Dnm1, the literature-obvious synaptic-vesicle fission comparator, phenocopied Synj1 at the transcriptomic level with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the same 21 cell groups despite on-target Dnm1 depletion in 9 groups.

Represented PI(4,5)P2 5-phosphatase relatives did not uncover a compensatory phosphoinositide transcriptional module: Ocrl and Inpp5k each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the same 21 groups and near-zero score correlations with Synj1.

The screen did not recover a PARK20 or Down-syndrome-like transcriptional module: MB dopaminergic neurons were not recovered for Synj1, and acute loss-of-function of the represented Down-syndrome comparators App and Dyrk1a had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in matched groups.

A de novo cross-target search found no meaningful Synj1-like or anti-Synj1 signature; the strongest biological positive neighbor had r=0.0358 and the strongest negative neighbor had r=-0.0172 across matched Wilcoxon-score vectors.

Activity-dependent Synj1 regulators did not phenocopy Synj1: Dyrk1a was downstream-flat, Ppp3cc was downstream-flat, and the only calcineurin response was a small Ppp3ca/Ppp3r1 signal concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a Synj1-like module.
Acute Syp perturbation lowered the target RNA across 21/22 recovered groups but produced no non-Syp DE genes at FDR<0.10 anywhere in the measured neuronal surface.
Data-driven nearest-neighbor analysis found no meaningful positive or negative transcriptional signature neighbor for Syp.
The canonical Syp-Syb2/Vamp2 axis was absent at the RNA level: Vamp2 and a broader vesicle-gene compensation set were FDR=1.0 in every Syp-tested group.

Measured presynaptic and vesicle-cycle comparator targets did not phenocopy Syp; Cltc generated the only multi-group comparator response, whereas most vesicle/SNARE targets were flat or single-gene responders.

Syt14 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered juvenile neuronal atlas: 21 measured cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the two remaining taxonomy groups had no Syt14 rows.

The Syt14-linked cerebellar prior did not translate into an acute broad 308 CB GABA transcriptome: Syt14 had 0 corrected downstream genes there, and eight represented ataxia or Purkinje-linked comparators were also flat in the same CB GABA bin.

Represented synaptic-vesicle relatives did not phenocopy Syt14 at the downstream RNA level: Syt2, Cplx1, Cplx2, and Stx1b each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across matched groups, while Syn1 and Unc13a produced only one isolated corrected gene apiece.

The data-driven Syt14 signature neighborhood was nearly orthogonal and noncanonical: the strongest positive neighbor was Kcnb1 with cosine 0.034761, and the strongest negative neighbor was Npy1r with cosine -0.017543.

Syt2 loss was nuclear-transcriptome buffered in every measured neuronal group: no cell group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10 despite measurable Syt2 transcript reduction in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut.

Loss of Syt2 did not induce transcriptional replacement or suppression of the fast-release apparatus: 22 transcripts spanning synaptotagmins, complexins, syntaxin/Munc18/Munc13, synapsins, Bassoon, RIMs, Rab3a, Snap25 and Vamp2 were all FDR=1.0 across the Syt2 surface.

Whole-surface neighbors placed Syt2 with essentially silent perturbations, while the least-aligned signatures were proteasome components Psmb4 and Psmc1, which produced 14008 and 11089 downstream FDR<0.10 genes respectively.
direction_pattern: Syt2 co-null and divergent from proteasome signatures

canonical_summary: Perturbing another core vesicle-fusion factor, Stxbp1, yielded a small but reproducible transcriptomic response in 8 cell groups, whereas Syt2 and most active-zone/SNARE comparators were flat or singletons.

The disease-relevant Syt2 perturbation axis is not a robust juvenile CNS neuronal stress transcriptome: even groups with Syt2 self-transcript depletion lacked downstream genes and the two missing groups were untested rather than negative.
Taar1 produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream events, one Tmem9 up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and one U2af1 down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
The postnatal sparse Taar1 loss-of-function surface did not recover monoaminergic, cAMP/D2, immediate-early, or NMDA/glutamate receptor transcript programs.
Neither the data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbors nor the literature-obvious Drd2/Drd4/Drd5/Gnas/Gnal/Comt comparators phenocopied Taar1.
direction_pattern: no_convergence_or_divergence; all global cosines near zero

canonical_summary: Tacr3 produced a single statistically robust downstream event: Dazap1 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while every other measured cell group was FDR-flat.
The 066 singleton was not accompanied by an immediate-early, Tac2/Pdyn/Gnrh1, or broad stress/compensation program.
Represented KNDy/GnRH-axis comparators did not phenocopy the Tacr3 Dazap1 response.
Tacr3 had no strong data-driven positive or negative signature neighbor across the model-visible perturbation universe.
Taf1b CRISPR loss-of-function was mRNA-transcriptionally flat across the recovered juvenile neuronal surface.
Canonical p53, unfolded-protein, and integrated-stress sentinel mRNAs were not induced by Taf1b perturbation.
Nearby ribosome/RNA-biogenesis perturbations, especially Nop56 and Polr3b, produced thalamic and midbrain-associated DE where Taf1b was flat.
The MYC arm of rDNA growth control was also largely quiescent in this postmitotic screen.
A de novo signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Taf1b co-signature or anti-signature.
Tanc2 loss produced a single, L5-6 IT-restricted FDR hit: Clec16a was up-regulated, with no accompanying autophagy or synaptic module at FDR<0.10.
The P16-to-P37/44 Tanc2 perturbation did not recover the mTORC1/2 hyperactivity program that dominates early Tanc2 biology.
Direct PSD and excitatory-synapse comparators did not phenocopy the Tanc2 L5-6 IT response.
Across the model-visible perturbation universe, the strongest full-profile Tanc2 signature neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations below 0.045.
Tango2 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16 acute CRISPR perturbation.
Tango2-null neurons did not activate Opa1-like mitochondrial ISR genes or Hspa5-like ER-quality-control genes, although those programs were detectable elsewhere in the same dataset.
Represented ER-Golgi, lipid/FAO, OXPHOS, mitochondrial-trafficking, and autophagy targets failed to phenocopy Tango2, while Opa1 produced a large divergent stress response.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found only near-zero Tango2 correlations, with Rel as the top positive score-cosine neighbor at 0.028 and Crebbp as the top negative at -0.019.
The screen supplies no basal neuronal mRNA biomarker for TANGO2 rescue hypotheses centered on B vitamins, lipid balance, or autophagy activation.
Taok1 loss of function produced a transcriptomically buffered surface: every one of the 20 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a measured Taok1 transcript.

The p38/JNK/MARK/Hippo transcriptional shadow expected from a TAOK1 MAP3K was absent; Map2k6 and Mapk9 perturbations were also flat, and Mark3 yielded only one downstream FDR gene in the same 20 groups.
The Taok1 flat surface is not a property of the assayed cell groups: in matched groups Wdr26 had 3128, Tsc2 had 636, and Ranbp2 had 420 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, while Taok1 had 0.

A P16-to-P37/44 whole-brain nuclear RNA screen is a poor proxy for the kinase-active dorsal-raphe phenotype of Taok1: broad midbrain/thalamic/cerebellar groups were flat even though published mouse phenotypes arise from altered DRN VGlut3-neuron activation and phosphoproteins.

Tardbp produced a real but uneven postmitotic neuronal response: 16 of 22 measured cell groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.

A recurrent secretory/ER-lysosomal trafficking module was the most stereotyped whole-gene output of Tardbp loss, centered on Uggt2 up-regulation and reinforced by Sec24b, Snx14, Gga2, Hgsnat, Laptm4a, Tsc2, and Usp15 in broader responders.
The ER/trafficking response was selective: canonical Hspa5/Ddit3/Atf4/Atf6/Xbp1 UPR genes and the published ATG4B/LC3B autophagy axis were not induced as whole-gene changes.

The dataset recovered a compact RNA-processing response: Snrnp70 was repeatedly down-regulated, larger responders altered Fus, Hnrnpm, Srsf-family, Prpf39, Tcerg1, Drosha, and Rbmx, and spliceosome-associated U2af2/Prpf6/Cdk13 perturbations were among the strongest same-direction comparators.

Human TDP-43 loss-of-function sentinels did not move in their textbook direction: Unc13a increased at whole-gene level in six mouse groups, whereas Stmn2, Sort1, and Atg4b were not detected as decreased whole-gene transcripts.

Mitochondrial and small-molecule metabolic genes were secondarily recruited in the broadest responders, with recurrent Gabpa up-regulation plus Mfn1 and Spg7 induction, Samm50 repression, and 191 MB P MY GABA-specific Gfm2/Rars2/Iscu/Mthfd2/Apoo increases.
Tardbp also induced a small-GTPase/cytoskeletal trafficking layer, including recurrent Abr, Ngef, Cyth1, Adgrb2, Ank3, Myrip, Radil, and Actr1a up-regulation.

Cross-perturbation testing separated Tardbp from obvious ALS/FTD RBP relatives: Psmc1, U2af2, and Prpf6 shared many Tardbp FDR hits, whereas Matr3 mostly shared only Uggt2 and Hnrnpa2b1, Atxn2, Tia1, Vcp, Stmn2, Sort1, Grn, and Sqstm1 had little or no FDR-level overlap.
Tas2r118 produced a pan-sampled neuronal null: all 21 measured cell groups had 0 downstream DE genes at FDR<0.10.
The Tas2r118 null did not hide a canonical taste-cell or tuft-cell secondary program: Gnat3, Plcb2, Trpm5, Chat, Il25, Tslp, Dclk1, Pou2f3, and Ptgs1 were never DE at FDR<0.10.

Tas2r118 had no meaningful cross-perturbation neighbor: the strongest positive and negative whole-surface cosines were only 0.033832 for Ranbp2 and -0.017396 for Mbd5, and no other Tas2r or taste-transduction perturbation was present for a family phenocopy test.
Acute postnatal Tbc1d23 loss of function was a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null: 0 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in all 21 recovered cell groups.
The unbiased whole-universe signature search found no substantive positive or negative neighbor for Tbc1d23.
Tbc1d23 did not phenocopy measured paralog, WASH/AP-1, or retrograde-Golgi perturbations; notably Vps54 produced 45 FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while matched Tbc1d23 cells were flat.
Tbc1d24 is a pan-measured transcriptional null in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse neuronal CRISPR screen.
The expected synaptic-vesicle, activity-regulated, V-ATPase/lysosomal-autophagy, ER/oxidative-stress, and apoptosis marker transcripts were measured but fully absent from the Tbc1d24 DE surface.
No perturbation in the model-visible universe formed a robust positive or negative transcriptional signature neighbor of Tbc1d24.

Vesicle/endolysosomal comparators were detectable where Tbc1d24 was flat, with Rab7 and Stxbp1 producing broad signatures and V-ATPase subunits producing smaller signatures across the same matched cell groups.
Fast synaptic-vesicle cycle genes were themselves mostly transcriptionally buffered in the same assay.
Mutant TBC1D24 oxidative-stress biology did not appear as a constitutive P37/44 activity/stress transcriptome after sparse P16 Tbc1d24 CRISPR.
Tbc1d32 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal blank rather than a cell-type-restricted transcriptional responder.
The expected cilium-to-Hedgehog transcriptional output was absent.
Ciliary and Hedgehog relatives were largely flat or only weakly cell-restricted, so Tbc1d32 did not fall into a uniform postnatal neuronal ciliopathy module.
Unbiased signature-neighbor search did not reveal a strong convergent or antagonistic Tbc1d32 partner.
The disease-relevant TBC1D32 axis is displaced away from P16 NeuN+ brain transcription.
Tbcd produced a sparse but real response in 6 of 22 measured cell groups, with 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut concentrating 12 of the 19 FDR<0.10 downstream gene-cell pairs.
Alpha-tubulin mRNA up-regulation was the recurrent Tbcd output: Tuba1a rose in every responder and Tuba1b rose in the two strongest glutamatergic responders.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried a non-tubulin adaptation module with Jun and Nfil3 induction, Ypel4/Mturn/Satb1/Slc25a23/Kctd16 induction, and Lrrc7/Ptprn2/Samd5 repression.
Cic and Grin1 were the top positive signature neighbors of Tbcd on its 19 significant features, sharing seven and six same-direction thalamic Prkcd hits, respectively.
Proteasome targets Psmb4 and Psmc1 were the top negative neighbors and inverted most recurrent Tbcd tubulin features while sharing only a minority of down-regulated thalamic features.
Tuba1a, Tuba4a, and Arl2bp failed to phenocopy Tbcd: Tuba1a self-RNA moved opposite to Tbcd-induced Tuba1a, Tuba4a had no overlap with the 19 Tbcd features, and Arl2bp had no FDR<0.10 surface.
Tbcd did not induce a coordinated UPR/ISR, autophagy/lysosome, redox, or proteasome-subunit transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.
Tbl1x loss produced a single robust downstream event: Dner up-regulation specific to 155 MB Glut.
Acute Tbl1x perturbation was globally buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
Tbl1xr1 did not phenocopy Tbl1x despite being the in-parquet paralog and weak whole-signature neighbor.
Tbl1x is uncoupled from the β-catenin/TCF7L2 thalamic program that is readily detected in this assay.
Nuclear-receptor and MeCP2/NCoR-related comparators were not Tbl1x-like in the measured neurons.
The data-driven Tbl1x neighborhood does not support a broad convergent module.
Tbl1xr1 loss produced an FDR-defined transcriptional response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a single-gene Tet2 response in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
The thalamic signature touched Wnt/PCP through Vangl1 down-regulation, but it did not recover a canonical beta-catenin target program.
Data-driven restricted-signature scoring linked Tbl1xr1 most strongly to Rora and Cic in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Sin3a perturbation inverted most of the overlapping Tbl1xr1 thalamic genes.
The closest TBL-family comparator, Tbl1x, was nearly inert and did not phenocopy Tbl1xr1.
St6galnac6 and Neu1 were both up-regulated in the thalamic Tbl1xr1 response, suggesting a small sialoconjugate/lysosomal glycan remodeling component.
The entire 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut response was a single up-regulated Tet2 hit.
Ppard induction after Tbl1xr1 loss did not mean that a PPAR perturbation program had been engaged.
The 151 TH response rewired neuronal signaling and scaffold transcripts rather than activating a generic stress or proteostasis program.
P16 Tbr1-targeting CRISPR produced a sparse but real response limited to four telencephalic cortical glutamatergic groups.
Dkk3 down-regulation and Cpne6 up-regulation were the most recurrent markers of the postnatal Tbr1 perturbation state.
The two IT responses were dominated by membrane, neurite, and axon-growth remodeling rather than cell-death or generic integrated-stress genes.
Tbr1 perturbation exposed a small ion-handling signature, strongest as Cacna1g up-regulation in NP/CT/L6b neurons and Kcna1/Slc24a2 down-regulation in L5/6 IT neurons.
A narrow lysosomal catabolic signal accompanied the cortical response.
The postnatal sparse Tbr1 response did not recover the canonical embryonic Auts2/Grin2b/Reln/Fezf2/Sox5/Foxp2 laminar-fate program.
Measured TBR1-neighborhood perturbations did not phenocopy Tbr1, and active Grin perturbations diverged by layer and target genes.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not identify a robust Tbr1 phenocopy or anti-phenocopy in the model-visible universe.
Tbx19 CRISPR loss of function produced a pan-assayed neuronal null: all 23 measured brain groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The flat Tbx19 surface contrasts with the represented brain T-box factor Tbr1, which produced 28 downstream FDR<0.10 genes concentrated in cortical glutamatergic groups.
Unbiased whole-surface neighbors did not nominate a Tbx19 module: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score cosine was Abat at 0.030 and the strongest named-gene negative cosine was Pclo at -0.008.
The expected pituitary POMC and alternate-fate program was absent: Pomc, Pcsk1, Pcsk2, Cpe, Crh, Crhr1, Etv1, Neurod1, Nr5a1, Cga, Lhb and Tshb all had FDR 1.0 in every Tbx19 cell group tested.
Canonical pituitary-development comparators were also flat or singleton-only in the neuronal assay, while Tbr1 was the only measured T-box-family comparator with a multi-gene cortical response.
Tbx1 produced a single FDR-significant downstream hit, Polr2a down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Tbr1, but not Tbx1, induced a cortical postmitotic-neuron transcriptional profile under the same assay.
Most represented Tbx family members were flat or singleton responders and did not phenocopy Tbx1 or Tbr1.
The embryonic Tbx1-FGF/ERK program was absent after P16 neuronal Tbx1 perturbation.
The full Tbx1 DE surface had no robust genome-wide convergence or anti-convergence partner.
The 22q11.2 behavioral role of Tbx1 was not reproduced as a broad acute P16 NeuN+ neuronal transcriptome.
Tbx21 loss of function produced no robust transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured non-olfactory neuronal cell groups.

No T-bet type-1 immune module was recovered: expected effector genes such as Ifng, Il12rb2 and Cxcr3 were FDR=1.0 throughout the Tbx21 surface, and represented immune comparators Stat1, Stat4, Runx3 and Rorc were themselves broad nulls in matched neuronal groups.
The expected OB T-box relative Tbr1, unlike Tbx21, had 28 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in L5-6 IT, L4-5 IT, L2-3 PIR/AON/ENT, and NP-CT-L6b-OB glutamatergic groups.
Genome-wide score-neighbor analysis placed Tbx21 next to safe-target and near-null perturbations; the strongest positive cosine was only +0.0406 and the strongest negative was -0.0124.
Acute P16 Tbx22 loss produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The CPX-associated palatal osteogenic program expected from germline Tbx22 loss was absent from the neuronal snRNA-seq response.
Tbx22 did not converge with represented developmental T-box factors, while the matched neural T-box comparator Tbr1 showed detectable cortical/NP transcriptional effects.
The closest global Tbx22 rank-space neighbors were near zero and were rejected as biological modules.
Tbx2 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Canonical BMP-Tbx2-Shh/Fgf and Cdkn2a/Cdkn1a senescence readouts were also absent under Tbx2 perturbation.
The close Tbx2/Tbx3/Tbx4/Tbx5 subfamily and represented BMP/FGF receptor comparators were themselves flat or one-gene responders in the same neuronal DE universe.
Tbr1, another represented T-box transcription factor with postmitotic cortical biology, showed a real cortical glutamatergic response while Tbx2 remained flat in the same broad groups.
The global Tbx2 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor; the top correlations were near zero and were carried by flat comparator surfaces.
Tbx3 produced only one FDR<0.10 downstream call: Acbd6 was reduced in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
The expected hypothalamic melanocortin/KNDy neuropeptide program was not recovered after Tbx3 perturbation.
Tbx3 did not phenocopy represented T-box relatives; Tbr1, not Tbx3 or Tbx2-subfamily targets, gave the main cortical T-box response.
Tbx3 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor in the global perturbation universe.
Tbx4 produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic zero in this P16-to-P37/P44 mouse-brain CRISPR screen.
The canonical Tbx4-Fgf10/Shox2 limb-lung program was absent: Fgf10, Bmp4, Spry2, Etv5, Wnt2, Wnt2b, Shox2, Tbx2 and Fgfr2 all remained FDR=1.0 under Tbx4 perturbation.

Neither data-driven neighbors nor literature-obvious T-box/FGF relatives formed a meaningful Tbx4-like neuronal signature; the largest all-gene correlations were near zero and robust related-target DE was limited to one- or two-gene hits.
The neuronal null displaces TBX4 disease biology toward skeletal and pulmonary mesenchymal compartments rather than juvenile brain neurons.
Tbx5 loss produced a narrowly localized decrease of Cbl in 008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic neurons.
The 008 Cbl response was Tbx5-specific within the measured T-box relatives and had no robust data-driven neighbor across the screen.
Juvenile neuronal Tbx5 perturbation did not recover the canonical Holt-Oram cardiac-output or limb Wnt/Fgf programs.
The postnatal neuronal Tbx5 knockout surface was almost completely buffered at the soma-transcriptome level.

Postnatal Tbx6 loss produced a very small, CTX-CGE GABA-restricted signature: Atosa increased and Dynll2 decreased, both at FDR 0.0595, while the other 21 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
The CTX-CGE GABA signal is uncoupled from the canonical Tbx6-Mesp2/Notch/Sox2 somitogenesis circuit and was not reproduced by measured T-box, Notch, or FGF comparators in the same cell group.
The unbiased nearest-neighbor search yielded only near-zero whole-surface cosines, and Pitx3, Dlx6, Sp7, Ufc1, Uba5 and Cd81 all failed to reproduce the Atosa/Dynll2 pair in CTX-CGE GABA at FDR<0.10.
Tcf12 loss in the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal assay was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null, not a local effect hidden in one cell group.
The embryonic Tcf12-NeuroD1 cortical migration and dopaminergic programs were not reactivated or collapsed after postnatal Tcf12 perturbation.
Tcf4, but not its E-protein paralog Tcf12, produced a small Pvalb interneuron signature, demonstrating non-interchangeability of paralogs in this assay.

The neuronal null does not contradict dosage-sensitive craniosynostosis or Kallmann biology; it displaces those TCF12 phenotypes to embryonic suture, GnRH, and olfactory-axis contexts absent from the assay.
Data-driven nearest neighbors of the Tcf12 signature were noise-floor rather than mechanistic convergence partners.
Acute P16 Tcf20 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous nuclear transcriptome in any of 21 measured neuronal groups.
The stress-induced NRF2/SQSTM1 branch of SPBP biology was not engaged by Tcf20 loss in baseline neurons.
The MeCP2-TCF20/RAI1 chromatin axis did not collapse to a single matched signature in the postnatal screen.
Whole-universe Tcf20 signature neighbors were extremely weak and did not define a hidden transcriptomic module.
Other transcriptional or chromatin perturbations generated detectable FDR-level programs where Tcf20 did not.
Postnatal Tcf3 loss produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any measured NeuN+ neuronal group.
The direct class-I E-protein paralogs Tcf4 and Tcf12 did not converge with Tcf3 in the same neuronal assay.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search found only near-zero, safe-target-like Tcf3 signature neighbors.
The specific developmental markers expected from E2A neural commitment, ID feedback, proneural, MGE, or oligodendrocyte programs were not recovered.
Acute postnatal Tcf4 loss produced a responder surface restricted to 052 Pvalb Gaba: 1/23 measured cell groups crossed FDR<0.10, with Oprd1 and Tmem44 both down-regulated.
Oprd1 was the strongest biological effector in the Tcf4 PV response, falling by logFC -0.570 at FDR 0.00884 together with Tmem44.
The represented E-protein paralogs Tcf3 and Tcf12, and the represented class-II bHLH factors Atoh1, Neurod1, and Neurod2, did not phenocopy Tcf4 in Pvalb neurons.

The data-driven positive neighbors of the two-gene Tcf4 PV signature were Psmb4, Wac, Cltc, and Ctcf, whereas the nominal anti-neighbors Arx, Chd2, Kif1b, and Ski did not show FDR-supported opposite regulation of Oprd1/Tmem44.
Canonical or proposed TCF4 targets from developmental and excitability literature—Cntnap2, Nrxn1, Bmp7, Rimbp2, Kcnq1, and Scn10a—were absent from the Tcf4 FDR surface.

Tcf7l2 loss is sharply thalamic-selective in this P16 mosaic neuronal screen: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 140 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, 009 had only Hp1bp3, 20 measured groups had none, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.

In 151, the strongest Tcf7l2 program is a mostly down-regulated thalamic terminal excitability and synaptic/neuropeptide battery, including Ramp3, Kcnc2, Pcsk2, Grin2b, Gabbr2, Gabra4, Gabra1, Prkcd, Pcp4 and Cpe.
The 151 signature also contains a neuronal projection, adhesion and extracellular-matrix arm: Ntng1, Spon1, Slitrk3, Edil3, Mmp15, Cntn1, Cdh2 and Robo1 are down-regulated.
Ctnnb1 is the literature-obvious comparator that truly converges with Tcf7l2: in 151 it produced 476 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and shared 59 of the 140 Tcf7l2 genes, 53 in the same direction.

The expected thalamic/Wnt neighborhood is not interchangeable: Rora, Prox1, Gsk3b, Lrp6, Mef2a, Mef2c and Foxp2 were represented but showed small or mixed overlaps with the 151 Tcf7l2 signature, despite several of them responding in 151.

Most raw nearest neighbors were rejected after matched FDR testing: Pde4d, Msx2 and Dock3 correlated positively, and Gprc5b, Lrp4, Kcnc2, Gabra2 and Hnf1b negatively, over the restricted vector, but none yielded a downstream 151 or 009 FDR signature.
Hp1bp3 up-regulation is the only FDR<0.10 event outside 151, occurring as a single-gene 009 L2-3 IT PIR/AON/ENT Glut call.

The screen supports a disease-mechanism refinement: acute Tcf7l2 LoF in juvenile NeuN+ neurons perturbs a thalamic terminal state but does not create broad cortical, striatal or cerebellar transcriptional toxicity.
Sparse P16 Tead1 loss of function was FDR-flat across every measured neuronal class.
The expected YAP/TEAD and cortical Tead target genes were absent rather than oppositely regulated.
Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Tead1 convergence module.
Represented Hippo-adjacent and developmental crosstalk targets did not phenocopy Tead1, while Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 formed a separate thalamic Wnt module.
The neuronal Tead1 null argues against modeling TEAD1 eye disease or pan-TEAD drug action as simple acute Tead1 depletion in mature brain neurons.

Postnatal neuronal Tecr loss produced a strongly buffered transcriptome: all 22 measured groups had negative Tecr logFC, 14 had FDR<0.10 target-RNA depletion, yet only six non-self DEGs appeared in five telencephalic glutamatergic groups and none appeared in GABAergic, thalamic, midbrain, pineal, or cerebellar groups.
Four Tecr responder groups each up-regulated one regulatory or trafficking gene: Sgsm1 in L4/5 IT CTX, Cpsf6 in L2/3 IT CTX, Cbx3 in L2/3 PIR/AON/ENT, and Hic2 in MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic neurons.
L5 ET cortical glutamatergic neurons were the only group with a two-gene downstream response, jointly decreasing Ccng1 and Nae1.
Tecr targeting did not elicit transcriptional compensation in VLCFA-elongation/sphingolipid enzymes or a secondary UPR/ISR stress program.
The true ER elongation-cycle genes were absent as perturbation targets, and the represented lipid-enzyme comparators Acsl4 and Mecr did not phenocopy Tecr.
The data-driven signature-neighbor search found no robust convergent or inverse neighbor for Tecr.
Tek loss of function was transcriptomically silent at FDR<0.10 across all 23 assayed NeuN-enriched neuronal groups.
The nearest empirical Tek neighbors were weak restricted-signature matches rather than robust shared responders.
Represented endothelial and PI3K/Notch relatives failed to phenocopy Tek in neurons.
The screen is poorly matched to TEK-related venous-malformation biology.
Tenm3 is transcriptome-buffered after P16 CRISPR loss of function across the recovered neuronal brain: no measured cell group had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

The measurable Tenm/Lphn axis is null as a single-gene transcriptional module in this dataset: Tenm4 and Adgrl1-Adgrl3, including the Ten3 partner Lphn2/Adgrl2, also had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the 22 Tenm3-matched groups.
A response-agnostic nearest-neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Tenm3 signature neighbor; the largest full-surface correlation was only r=0.0295.

The absent Epha7/Ephb1/Zic2 response reframes Tenm3 biology here as developmental wiring or ocular morphogenesis displaced from a P16 whole-brain neuronal transcriptomic assay, not as a postmitotic stress or identity-collapse program.
Postnatal sparse Tenm4 loss produced a transcriptomic zero across every recovered neuronal class.
Agnostic cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Tenm4 signature neighbor.
The represented teneurin-latrophilin-FLRT relatives failed to phenocopy Tenm4 at the downstream transcriptome level.
The Tenm4 disease/myelination axis is displaced out of this NeuN+ neuronal transcriptomic assay.
Tfap4 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 23 measured postnatal NeuN+ neuronal cell groups.
The MYC/AP4-adjacent perturbations represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Tfap4 with a coherent postmitotic-neuron signature.
Canonical AP4 effector genes for p21/p16/CDK2, p53-DNA-damage/senescence, and colorectal EMT were queryable but did not become robust Tfap4-dependent DEGs.
Whole-universe nominal-score neighbor analysis found no meaningful Tfap4 signature neighbor.
Acute single-gene Tfcp2 loss produced no robust neuronal mRNA response in any measured cell group.
The flat Tfcp2 phenotype is mirrored by the closest represented CP2-family perturbations rather than by a strong Ubp1-like collapse.
The data-driven nearest-neighbor search produced only near-zero nominal cosines, so no mechanistic positive or negative signature neighbor is supported for Tfcp2.
Ranbp2, unlike Tfcp2, has hundreds of robust neuronal DE genes despite appearing as the second nominal positive neighbor of Tfcp2.
The juvenile neuronal loss-of-function surface does not support a simple TFCP2 haploinsufficiency-like Alzheimer mRNA program.
Tfdp1 produced a narrowly restricted up-response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Cntrob and Dcaf15 were the only two downstream genes reaching FDR<0.10.
The only robust Tfdp1 response was uncoupled from the canonical E2F/DP G1-S replication program.
Represented DP/E2F relatives did not phenocopy Tfdp1. Tfdp2, E2f1, and E2f5 had near-zero whole-surface correlations to Tfdp1 and no robust downstream genes in any group where each was measured.

Unbiased whole-surface neighbors were very weak, not coherent phenocopies. The strongest biological positive neighbor, Fbxo11, correlated only r=0.055 with Tfdp1; the strongest negative neighbor, Wdr26, correlated r=-0.033 and carried a much broader 151 TH signature not centered on Cntrob or Dcaf15.
Tfdp2 loss produced a pan-neuronal robust negative result: no recovered cell group contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The canonical E2F G1/S and DNA-replication output was absent after Tfdp2 perturbation.
The represented E2F/DP relatives were themselves buffered rather than exposing a hidden DP2-specific program.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no meaningful positive or negative Tfdp2 neighbor.
Acute P16 Tfg perturbation was a pan-measured neuronal downstream null: 21 recovered cell groups, 1,061 total perturbed nuclei, and no gene at FDR<0.10 outside the target transcript.
Tfg loss did not activate a UPR, ISR, or autophagy transcript program even though the same dataset detected Hspa5/Canx/Hyou1/Chac1 induction after Sec63 perturbation.

The directly represented COPII neighbors Sec23a and Sar1b were also transcriptionally flat, whereas Sec63 was not; the Tfg null therefore sits with proximal COPII-buffered targets rather than with every ER-localized perturbation.
Whole-surface signature comparison left Tfg without a meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor.
The neuronal Tfg CRISPR null is a loss-of-function result and should not be used to infer absence of biology for TFG-NTRK1 kinase-fusion alleles.

P16 mosaic Tfrc loss produced a punctate rather than global neuronal iron-starvation response: only five corrected downstream genes appeared across 21 measured neuronal groups, and each responder carried just one FDR<0.10 gene.
The clearest biologically interpretable responder was a small HIF/glycolytic fragment in thalamic glutamatergic neurons: Vegfa rose in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and Pfkp rose in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
CTX-CGE GABA nuclei up-regulated Atg13 as a single corrected hit after Tfrc perturbation.
Two FDR hits were isolated and noncanonical: Celf3 decreased only in 008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP Glut, and Col11a1 decreased only in 191 MB P MY GABA.
The literature-obvious iron/HIF comparators represented in the screen did not phenocopy Tfrc: Ireb2, Hif1a, Abcb7, and Nfs1 were all flat or nearly flat in matched neuronal groups.

The data-driven signature neighbors were weak restricted-signature calls, not robust shared biology: Chd2, Ndufb8, and Kif1a were the top positive neighbors, Ap1s2, Msi1, and Foxj3 the top negative neighbors, but none shared any of Tfrc's five corrected genes.

The screen is uninformative for the major TFRC blood-brain-barrier shuttle use case because the measured Tfrc surface consists of NeuN-enriched neuronal groups, with no endothelial, vascular, microglial, astrocytic, or oligodendrocyte compartment tested.
Tgfbr1 loss was a reproducible pan-neuronal basal-transcriptome negative: none of 22 measured neuronal groups contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The expected SMAD feedback and TGFβ target transcripts were absent from the Tgfbr1 surface.
Tgfbr1 sat inside a broader TGFβ/BMP receptor-SMAD module that was nearly silent in basal neuronal nuclei.
The data-driven Tgfbr1 nearest neighbors were correlations of noise, not a disguised biological module.
Smad7, Serpine1, Skil, and ID-family transcripts are poor basal neuronal engagement markers for this perturbation format.
Tgfbr2 produced a one-gene response restricted to 054 CNU-MGE GABA: Ssbp4 was up-regulated, while every other measured neuronal group had zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes.

The focal Ssbp4 induction did not look like canonical TGF-beta/TGFBR2-SMAD loss: sentinel SMAD-responsive genes were absent, Bmpr2 produced a separate Eif4a1 event, and Tgfbr1, Tgfbr3, Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4 perturbations did not induce Ssbp4 in the same CNU-MGE group.
Whole-signature neighbors of Tgfbr2 were essentially orthogonal to it; top positive and negative gene perturbations had Pearson |r| below 0.039 and no shared FDR<0.10 Ssbp4 call.

The broad neuronal null surface refines Tgfbr2 CNS genetics toward displaced contexts: embryonic axon/neurovascular signaling, dopaminergic arbor or synapse morphology, and glial-microglial homeostasis rather than a constitutive juvenile NeuN+ nuclear program.
Tgfbr3 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional zero: every one of the 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Canonical TGF-beta/BMP feedback genes were assayed but did not shift after Tgfbr3 perturbation.
Literature-obvious TGF-beta-superfamily receptors and SMADs also failed to phenocopy a broad neuronal program.
The top data-driven Tgfbr3 neighbors were essentially noise-near: Fbxo11 was the strongest positive neighbor at r=0.044, and Wdr26 was the strongest negative neighbor at r=-0.027.
Postnatal, postmitotic Tgif1 loss did not derepress canonical Tgif/Nodal, Shh/Gli3, Evi5l, or retinoid transcripts in any neuronal class.
The Tgif1 null is selective relative to the mSin3/CtBP corepressor axis: Sin3a produced thousands of DEGs while Tgif1 produced none.
Represented TGF/Nodal/activin and retinoid receptor-SMAD targets, and represented HPE/Shh-patterning targets, were also null or nearly single-gene responders.
Unbiased whole-signature neighbors did not reveal a hidden Tgif1 module: all positive and negative score correlations were near zero and their target surfaces were null or tiny.
Thap11 has an acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic role in 22 of 23 recovered classes, but the effect is strongly graded.
Prkn is a recurrent positive readout of Thap11 loss in mature neurons.
Thap11 loss depresses mitochondrial and cobalamin transcripts in only the strongest neuronal responders.
The Parkin rise is embedded in mixed, partly antagonistic autolysosomal and mitochondrial quality-control remodeling.
A noncanonical centrosome/cilium and endomembrane-trafficking module is the most repeated part of the Thap11 signature.
Amino-acid and ATF4-like stress transcripts are a thalamic branch, not a pan-neuronal consequence, of Thap11 loss.
Thap11 perturbation repeatedly downregulates selected mature-neuronal synaptic and excitability genes.
Ogt is the top measured signature neighbor of Thap11 and shares the recurrent downregulated core in a subset of groups.
THAP-family and chromatin relatives were not interchangeable with Thap11 in this neuronal assay.
Several high-ranked noncanonical neighbors were proteostasis or RNA-translation perturbations, but only Elp1/Elp2 survived as a localized coherent match.
Acute P16 Thap1 loss produced a sparse transcriptomic response confined to five of 23 measured neuronal groups.
The most recurrent Thap1 module was Prepl down, Cuedc2 down, and Fam117a up across noncortical responders.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a small mitochondrial/lysosomal branch marked by Tomm40l and Pet100 induction with Cln3 repression.
Yy1 was the top robust same-direction Thap1 signature neighbor in thalamic and midbrain/pons-medulla neurons.
Thap11, E2f1, and Ogt do not reproduce the Thap1 neuronal module despite their HCF/E2F relationship to THAP-family biology.
Thap1 did not down-regulate Psmb5 or trigger a proteasome/NFE2L1/UPR/ISR transcriptional response.
Tor1a, Rrm1, and Birc5 were not robustly altered in any Thap1 neuronal cell group.
Prepl is a reusable cross-perturbation effector rather than a Thap1-specific downstream node.

Acute Thoc1 loss produced a sharply selective neuronal response: 1331 of 1353 FDR-significant downstream rows came from 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.

The major responders carried a THO/TREX-compatible RNA-biogenesis program, with Sart1, Sf3a3, Dhx38, Exosc10, and Ncbp1 induced while mRNA-export or spliceosome genes including Nxf1, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, Srrm2, and Ddx17 were recurrently repressed.
Thoc1 responders up-regulated many chromatin and transcriptional regulators, including Smarcc2, Gtf2i, Gtf2f1, Med1, Ncor2, Ubtf, Dnmt1, Smarca2, Smarca4, and Kdm6b.

The broad Thoc1 signatures included neuronal membrane-traffic and cytoskeletal-transport genes: Anxa6, Whamm, Vps35l, Rab11fip4, Ap3d1, Tpcn1, Hook2, Kif1a, Map1b, and Stx1b were recurrently up, while Agrn was recurrently down.
The Thoc1 neuronal signature lacked the expected overt p53/apoptosis, DNA-damage, UPR, or integrated-stress transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.

Data-driven convergence was strongest with splicing/export/nuclear-pore perturbations, but the exact TREX accessory Ddx39b only gave a small, MB P MY GABA-restricted phenocopy: 21 of 21 shared 191 MB P MY GABA genes matched Thoc1 direction, whereas Ddx39b was flat in 066, 110, 151, and 155.

Setx, a represented R-loop-resolution target, had zero FDR-significant genes across the whole screen, and Sin3a only partially overlapped Thoc1, arguing against the measured Thoc1 signature being a generic R-loop axis.
Acute Thra loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut lowered Hr, the clearest recovered direct thyroid-hormone target, while Thra itself was also FDR-significantly lower in the same nuclei.
The Thra response surface was narrow: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a borderline one-gene 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut signature had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Thra loss lowered the neuronal surface/excitability genes Adgrb1 and Hcn2 together with Hr.
The noncanonical Thra thalamic edges, not Hr, drove the data-driven neighbor map: Elp1/Bmal1/Rora/Cic converged mainly through Adgrb1 or Hcn2, whereas Zbtb7a/Xrn1/Hnrnpu opposed Adgrb1 and/or Rogdi.
Represented thyroid-receptor family comparators did not phenocopy Thra: Thrb, Rxra and Rxrg were flat, and Rxrb had only one off-surface singleton outside the Thra responder groups.

The assay did not recover the expected broad neurodevelopmental TRα programs: Klf9, Dbp, Nrgn, Aldh1a1, Dio3, Shh, Pvalb and Crip2 never reached FDR<0.10 after Thra perturbation, and all GABAergic and cerebellar bins were downstream-null or weak.

Sparse postnatal Thrb loss was robustly silent across the sampled neuronal transcriptome: every one of the 21 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Thrb mRNA row itself was never significant after correction.

The literature-obvious TR network did not converge on Thrb: Thra produced only a five-gene response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Rxra and Rxrg were fully flat, and Rxrb, Ncoa1, and Ncoa3 each produced only one FDR<0.10 gene with no shared Thrb overlap.

Pre-literature all-gene neighbors confirmed that Thrb sits on a null-like background rather than in a coherent convergent module: its closest positive neighbors Glrb, Bckdhb, Ndufa9, and Ppp2r2b were also completely flat, whereas least-positive comparators such as Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced thousands of DE genes.

The P16 neuronal Thrb CRISPR surface did not recover HPT-axis, retinal-cone, cochlear, or dominant-negative RTHβ programs: Trh, Tshb, Opn1mw, Opn1sw, Tecta, Slc26a5, Hr, and Klf9 all remained at FDR=1 in the Thrb surface.
Tia1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally buffered in basal juvenile postmitotic neurons: only two downstream FDR hits appeared across 19 recovered cell groups.
The two positive Tia1 readouts were single-gene, cell-class-isolated increases of Dpm1 in Pvalb interneurons and Zyg11b in hindbrain GABA neurons.
Canonical TIA1 stress-granule, EIF2AK2/ISR-UPR, tau/RBP, and inflammatory sentinel transcripts were measured but absent from the FDR signature.

Represented ALS/RNA-granule comparators did not phenocopy Tia1: Tardbp and Matr3 were broad responders, Atxn2 and Ddx3x were restricted responders, and Eif2ak4 and Ubp1 were flat without reproducing Dpm1/Zyg11b.
A data-driven cross-target search failed to identify a strong Tia1 signature neighbor.
The P16 mosaic Tia1 LoF surface did not recapitulate ALS/FTD phase-transition or tauopathy expectations, supporting a context- and allele-specific view of TIA1 neurologic risk.
