Tiam1 was a complete FDR-flat perturbation in the recovered neuronal atlas: all 22 measured Tiam1 cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa was not tested.

Canonical NMDA-receptor/Tiam1 coupling did not translate into a Grin-like transcriptional phenotype: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced 238 FDR<0.10 downstream calls in matched cell groups, whereas Tiam1 produced none.

The expected Rac/EphB/PAK/WAVE neighborhood was also transcriptionally buffered: Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1-3, Kalrn, Cyfip1, Ephb1/2, Dock3, Limk1, and Tnik generated only four single-gene FDR hits across 251 matched target-cell surfaces and had near-zero correlations to Tiam1.

Pre-literature signature-neighbor analysis found no strong Tiam1 transcriptomic relatives: the top signed-score Pearson correlations were only +0.0346 to Zic1 and -0.0352 to Safe_target_15, and the top neighboring real-gene perturbations were themselves mostly null.
The absence of a postnatal transcriptional stress signature is not a safety or efficacy green light for Tiam1/Rac inhibition.
Timmdc1 perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered neuronal group.
Timmdc1 did not activate the Opa1-like mitochondrial ISR even in cell groups where that program is detectable in the same dataset.
direction_pattern: ISR absent after Timmdc1, up after Opa1

canonical_summary: Complex-I assembly and NDUF structural perturbations were broadly silent in the Timmdc1-matched neuronal panel.
Whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Timmdc1 convergence or anti-convergence neighbor.
Timp3 loss produced a single robust downstream transcript, Syp, and only in CTX-CGE GABA interneurons.
A restricted all-target scan put Timp3 beside Wac, direct Syp perturbation, and Psmc1 on the CTX-CGE Syp readout, with no FDR-supported opposite regulator.
Represented ADAM10/APP, VEGFR, TNF-receptor, and Notch targets did not phenocopy the Timp3 CTX-CGE Syp hit or reveal a hidden canonical pathway program.
The neuronal Timp3 surface is broadly buffered: 22 measured cell groups had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10, including the thalamic group where the Timp3 transcript itself dropped significantly.

Tlk2 loss after P16 was globally buffered rather than a broad neurodevelopmental transcriptomic perturbation: only 2 downstream FDR10 genes were found in 388,046 Tlk2 rows across all 23 neuronal groups.
The only robust downstream Tlk2 calls were two non-recurrent signaling-regulatory singletons: Cab39 down in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Ppp2r2d up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The predicted p53/replication-stress output of TLK loss was absent under Tlk2 even though the same transcripts are detectable elsewhere in the screen.

A full-universe signed-score search failed to find a convincing Tlk2-like perturbation module: the strongest positive and negative neighbors had near-zero cosine values and no FDR10 overlap with the Cab39/Ppp2r2d singletons.

The flat Tlk2 surface is gene-specific rather than a universal inability to see chromatin-gene effects: Chd8 and Chd4 produced 148 and 158 downstream FDR10 calls, respectively, in the same analysis universe while sharing neither Tlk2 singleton.
Tlr2 loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
Directly represented TLR, IL-1R and NF-kB pathway relatives did not converge with Tlr2 in the same neuronal DE surface.
The Tlr2 null cautions that healthy juvenile neuronal LoF is not a proxy for TLR2 modulation in glial or synucleinopathy-associated neuroinflammation.
Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors of the Tlr2 logFC profile were all near zero correlation and did not define a convergent module.
DG-containing mature glutamatergic groups did not reproduce the published Tlr2 neurogenesis phenotype.
Hypothalamic-enriched young neuronal groups were flat despite literature linking hypothalamic neuronal TLR2 to age-induced obesity.
Tlr3 loss produced one robust downstream call, Rgs4 up-regulation, and it was confined to 145 MH-LH TH Glut neurons.
Neuronal Tlr3 CRISPR uncoupled receptor loss from the expected TLR3-TRIF interferon/NF-kB transcriptional program.
Represented TLR-family and IFN-pathway relatives did not phenocopy Tlr3 and were themselves almost completely buffered in the same neuronal Perturb-seq universe.
The whole-transcriptome Tlr3 signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor across the model-visible target universe.
Acute Tlr4 CRISPR loss-of-function was a pan-neuronal baseline null: none of the 20 recovered NeuN-positive cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
The canonical TLR4->NF-kappaB/IRF output was absent, not merely hidden among unannotated genes.
Tlr4 did not phenocopy measurable TLR-family or NF-kappaB/IRF pathway relatives.
Unbiased signature-neighbor search placed Tlr4 at the noise floor rather than in a hidden weak module.
The dataset is a poor stand-alone efficacy model for TLR4-directed neuroinflammation drugs.
Tlr5 LoF generated a single FDR-supported downstream event, Mpp1 up-regulation, restricted to 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
Tlr5 LoF did not recover the flagellin/TLR5/MyD88/NF-κB inflammatory transcriptional program; Mpp1 was the only FDR<0.10 gene.
Represented TLR-family and NF-κB pathway targets were measured but did not converge with the Tlr5 Mpp1 signature.
The whole-surface pre-literature neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Tlr5 signature neighbor.
Tlr7 loss of function was transcriptionally silent in every measured neuronal cell group in the postnatal mosaic screen.
Neither the canonical TLR7 inflammatory program nor the reported neuronal Myd88-c-Fos-IL-6 axis was recovered as a corrected downstream program.
The represented Toll-like receptor neighborhood was also nearly flat and did not phenocopy Tlr7 in matched neuronal groups.
The data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful Tlr7 signature neighbors.
The screen argues against a direct basal neuronal transcriptomic liability of Tlr7 loss but cannot de-risk TLR7 modulation in microglia, peripheral immune cells, or ligand-rich inflammation.
Tlr8 loss produced a single robust downstream response, Cnpy3 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Literature-obvious TLR and NF-kB/IRF comparators did not phenocopy the Tlr8-Cnpy3 event in CNU-MGE GABA.
The Tlr8 signature was orphan-like in the model-visible DE universe; the best data-driven neighbors had near-zero cosines and were rejected.
Tlr8 loss did not evoke Tlr7 derepression, NF-kB/AP-1, interferon-stimulated, cytokine, or neuronal TLR-morphogenesis sentinel transcripts in the only responding group.
Tm2d1 loss produced a two-gene up-regulated cell-surface recognition signature in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic response was a single R3hdm2 up-regulation event, not a broad pathway activation.
Postnatal Tm2d1 perturbation failed to recover a canonical Notch output despite TM2D-family literature connecting these proteins to Notch and gamma-secretase biology.
Tm2d1 had no strong data-driven transcriptomic neighbor in the screen.
There was no transcriptional bounce-back of Tm2d2 or Tm2d3 in Tm2d1-perturbed neurons.
Juvenile Tm2d1 LoF is a poor phenocopy of the amyloid/TM2D3 risk biology that motivated the family.
Tmco1 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 20 recovered neuronal cell groups, spanning 338350 downstream gene tests overall.
Tmco1 loss did not induce an ER-stress, ERAD, or IRE1-XBP1 transcript program, even though Atp2a2 and Hspa5 perturbations recovered UPR-like signatures in matched neuronal groups.
The top unbiased Tmco1 signature neighbors were all noise-scale, with maximum absolute Pearson score correlation about 0.04 and a Safe_target among the nearest positives.
The embryonic FGF/ERK program linked to Tmco1 corpus-callosum rescue was not recovered in P16 NeuN+ neurons.
Tmem106b produced exactly one robust downstream call, a Cyfip2 decrease in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut nuclei.
Canonical lysosome, autophagy, TFEB/MiT and ISR/UPR marker genes were absent from the Tmem106b FDR surface.
Represented progranulin, MAP6, v-ATPase and mTOR/autophagy comparators failed to converge with the sole Tmem106b L5-ET Cyfip2 response.
The unbiased DE-score neighbor search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Tmem106b.
The juvenile NeuN+ null surface does not de-risk TMEM106B lowering in glia, myelin, disease models, specific D252N biology or aging.
Tmem126a produced a pan-tested neuronal transcriptional null: every measured cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 21 independent Wilcoxon surfaces.
The expected respiratory-chain and ATF4/mitochondrial-stress transcript programs were also absent after Tmem126a perturbation.
Opa1, another optic-atrophy mitochondrial target, induced a clear ASNS/DDIT3/CHAC1/MTHFD2-rich stress signature in matched groups where Tmem126a was silent.
The measured null argues that OPA7 cannot be modeled by acute Tmem126a loss in the sampled forebrain/midbrain/cerebellar NeuN+ nuclei alone.
Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no biologically compelling convergent or anticorrelated Tmem126a module.

Tmem163 had no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of 21 measured neuronal cell groups, even in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut where the Tmem163 mRNA itself was significantly depleted.
P2X receptor markers were transcriptionally uncoupled from Tmem163 loss: P2rx3 and P2rx4 were FDR=1.0 in every measured group.
The hypomyelinating-leukodystrophy mechanism is displaced away from sparse postmitotic neurons toward earlier oligodendrocyte/myelin and allele-specific biology.
Tmem163 had no material cross-perturbation neighbor, and the obvious ZnT, TRPML1, and P2X relatives were absent as perturbation targets.
The absent zinc/stress program was assay-detectable in principle: the same parquet called Mtf1, metallothioneins, ZnT sentinels, P2rx4, and UPR/autophagy sentinels after other perturbations.
Tmem165 was a pan-measured transcriptomic non-responder after P16 neuronal CRISPR: all 22 recovered neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Tmem165 loss did not recruit a detectable UPR/ERAD, Golgi-stress, or glycosylation-compensation transcript module.
The Golgi/CDG comparators represented in the parquet—Atp2c1, Cog4, Cog5, and Dpm1—were also null or near-null, with Atp2c1 showing zero downstream neuronal genes across all groups matched to Tmem165.
Core proteostasis, translation, and RNA-processing perturbations, not Golgi glycosylation genes, formed the least Tmem165-like real-gene signatures and carried thousands of DE genes.
The strongest positive transcriptome-wide neighbors of Tmem165 were all null or near-null perturbations, not Golgi manganese or glycosylation relatives.
Tmem63b loss produced a near-null, baseline-state neuronal transcriptome: only two singleton downstream genes across 22 recovered cell groups and no robust global cross-perturbation neighbor.
L5 extratelencephalic neurons carried a unique Caln1 up-regulation after Tmem63b perturbation.
CNU-HYa/HY GABA neurons showed a borderline-FDR Fdft1 up-regulation that points to, but does not complete, a sterol-biosynthesis compensation.
The represented TMEM63-family paralog Tmem63c did not phenocopy Tmem63b.
The flat loss-of-function surface is consistent with TMEM63B developmental-epileptic-encephalopathy variants not being modeled as simple postnatal haploinsufficiency.
Acute postmitotic Tmem63c loss produced a pan-neuronal FDR-null nuclear transcriptomic surface: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 measured cell groups.
The represented TMEM63 paralog Tmem63b did not converge with Tmem63c despite a stronger self-transcript decrease and two isolated downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

Canonical HSP and ER/mitochondrial-shaping comparators that were present in the parquet failed to align with Tmem63c; even Opa1, which produced 241 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, shared no robust same-direction genes with Tmem63c.
The data-driven Tmem63c signature-neighbor search found only negligible raw signed-score cosines, with safe-target controls interleaved among the closest neighbors.
Tnfrsf11a loss of function was transcriptionally silent across all 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups: every group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the 215 MB Dopa group was not tested.

A pre-specified RANK-output panel was absent rather than merely shifted below a pathway threshold: Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Fos, Jun, Nfatc1, osteoclast effector genes, Ptgs2/Ptger3, and inflammatory chemokines all had no FDR<0.10 response after Tnfrsf11a perturbation.

Directly measurable TNFR-superfamily and NF-kB-adjacent perturbations did not reveal a hidden RANK-like neuronal module: Cd40, Chuk, Nfkb1, Tnfrsf1a, Traf3, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9 were flat or near-flat, while Fas and Tnfrsf13c produced only one and four downstream hits, respectively.
Genome-scale score-vector comparison found no meaningful positive or inverse Tnfrsf11a signature neighbor: the strongest cosine was only 0.027 and the most negative was -0.0126.

Tnfrsf13c loss produced a context-specific negative for the core BAFF-R program in healthy juvenile NeuN+ neurons: only 4 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in 23 measured groups and a 19-gene BAFF/NF-kB/survival panel was FDR=1.0 throughout.
The only corrected Tnfrsf13c hits were isolated neuronal or membrane-trafficking genes in Sst GABA, MB Glut, and MB/P/MY GABA cells: Nav2 up, Smap2 up, Sez6l down, and Stxbp5 down.

The top FDR-supported positive sparse neighbor was the proteasome ATPase Psmc1, which matched both MB Glut Tnfrsf13c directions for Smap2 and Sez6l, while producing thousands of additional DE genes that Tnfrsf13c did not share.
Psmb4 was the only FDR-supported opposite neighbor, but the opposition was mixed: it drove Sez6l down like Tnfrsf13c in MB Glut and Stxbp5 up, opposite to Tnfrsf13c, in MB/P/MY GABA.
The BAFF-R pathway comparators that were actually represented, Traf3 and Nfkb1, had no corrected downstream signatures and did not reproduce the four Tnfrsf13c hits in matched responder groups.
Acute Tnfrsf1a loss of function was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null: every one of the 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
No basal TNF/NF-kB immediate program appeared after Tnfrsf1a perturbation, and measurable intracellular TNFR/NF-kB neighbors were likewise flat.
Tnfrsf1a had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the complete perturbation universe.
Simple sparse neuronal Tnfrsf1a loss did not create a TRAPS-like inflammatory gain-of-function signature.

Tnfrsf4 loss of function was transcriptomically inert across the recovered juvenile NeuN+ neuronal surface: 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, with 052 Pvalb Gaba only weak because its best non-target gene was Vps53 at FDR 0.1007.

The Tnfrsf4 perturbation did not recover the expected OX40/TRAF/NF-kappaB pro-survival or cytokine module: rows for Bcl2, Bcl2l1, Birc5, Aurkb, Nfkb1/Rel/Rela, Traf, Il12rb2/Ctla4/Foxp3, Ccl5, Ifng, Il6, and Il12 components were present but all had FDR=1.0.

Represented TNFR-family and NF-kappaB-neighbor perturbations were also essentially flat in the same neuronal groups: Cd40, Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf9, and Traf3 produced no matched FDR<0.10 genes, while Fas and Tnfrsf13c produced only one to four isolated genes.

Unbiased cross-target signature search found no meaningful convergence or opposition: the best whole-profile Pearson correlations to Tnfrsf4 were only +0.028 for Ufsp2, +0.027 for Sox11, +0.027 for Erbb3, -0.014 for Eef2, and -0.013 for Arid1b.

The neuronal null argues against a direct, cell-autonomous OX40 target in young homeostatic neurons and redirects OX40 perturbation studies toward activated T cells, APCs, microglia/macrophages, endothelial cells, and inflammatory ligand engagement.
Tnfrsf9 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 21 measured NeuN+ neuronal groups.
The canonical CD137-TRAF-NF-kB/MAPK/AP-1 transcriptional program was not recovered downstream of Tnfrsf9, and represented TNFR/NF-kB comparator perturbations were flat or sparse.
All-gene signature neighbors of Tnfrsf9 had near-zero correlations and no adjusted-gene overlap, so the target has no hidden convergent module in the model-visible screen.
A flat neuronal Tnfrsf9 LoF signature should not be read as evidence that CD137 agonism is CNS-inert.
P16 mosaic Tnik loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
Tnik did not phenocopy the CTNNB1-TCF7L2 transcriptional module that is visible in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The unbiased neighbor search found no meaningful positive or inverse Tnik signature partner.
The flat snRNA-seq result should not be interpreted as CNS safety for TNIK kinase inhibition.

Tnpo3 loss produced a sharply uneven total-mRNA response: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA carried most of the 1734 FDR<0.10 downstream gene-cell calls, whereas 11 measured groups had no robust downstream genes.
The most canonical Tnpo3 module was down-regulation of SR-splicing and RNA-processing transcripts, led by Srrm2, Srsf5, Srsf1, Srsf7, Srsf2, Akap8l, Clk1, and Cstf2.
Tpr, a nuclear-basket mRNA-export perturbation, was the strongest same-direction FDR-overlap neighbor of Tnpo3, sharing 610 same-direction and only 22 opposite-direction significant gene-cell pairs.
Spliceosome and RNA-processing perturbations converged with Tnpo3, but broader nuclear-transport perturbations represented in the library did not.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 unexpectedly resembled Tnpo3 more than most RNA-processing genes did.
Col20a1 was the broadest induced single transcript, significant in eight of ten responding cell groups.
Broad subcortical responders remodeled transcription and chromatin regulators in both directions: Tcea2 was strongly down, while genes such as Btaf1, Zfp655, Cdk13, Akirin2, and Aff4 were induced.
The largest 151/155/191 signatures included coordinated loss of neuronal receptor, ion-channel, adhesion, and synaptic transcripts including Grin1, Gria2, Kcnt1, Scn2b, Adam23, Lrrc7, and Syn1.
A recurrent Rap/Rho, cytoskeletal, ciliary, and trafficking down-branch featured Rap1gap, Arhgef25, Coro6, Ahi1, Ttc4, Ttc8, and Stx16.
Ccl25, Fpr2, Fasl, Mcl1, and Cdkn1a defined a stress/survival and immune-ligand induction module in the larger hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain responders.
A small mitochondrial and metabolic down-branch accompanied the RNA-processing signature, with Samm50 recurring from the 054 CNU-MGE GABA narrow response into 151, 155, and 191.
Neuronal Tnpo3 loss did not phenocopy represented limb-girdle-muscular-dystrophy or dystrophin-glycoprotein targets.
The negative-neighbor search did not yield a clean mirror image; Huwe1 was the strongest interpretable partial anti-neighbor but had only 42 opposite-direction significant intersections.
Tnrc6a loss produced a real but very sparse derepressive signature restricted to 155 MB Glut: Atp1a3 and Ptges2 were the only downstream genes below FDR 0.10.
The ranked Tnrc6a surface had no robust all-target signature neighbor: the best positive and negative Wilcoxon-score neighbors were low-cosine and shared zero FDR-level axes with Tnrc6a.
Other single miRISC core perturbations did not phenocopy Tnrc6a: Tnrc6b, Ago2 and Dicer1 were completely flat, Ago1 had only one unrelated DEG, and none reproduced Atp1a3 or Ptges2 in 155 MB Glut.

Directly adjacent decay and translation factors were active where Tnrc6a was sparse but did not share its FDR genes. Cnot1, Gigyf2 and Xrn1 each produced 155 MB Glut signatures, yet none altered both Atp1a3 and Ptges2 at FDR<0.10.

Acute Tnrc6a loss of function did not resemble a familial adult myoclonic epilepsy allele: cortical and cerebellar classes were null and the only response was sparse 155 MB Glut Atp1a3/Ptges2 up-regulation.
Acute single-gene Tnrc6b perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in every measured neuronal group: 20 of 20 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The represented miRNA-silencing relatives failed to form a Tnrc6b-like responder module: Ago2 and Dicer1 were fully flat, Ago1 and Tnrc6a yielded only 1-2 FDR genes, and Cnot1/Xrn1 responded sparsely in thalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar classes while Tnrc6b stayed flat.
Tnrc6b had no meaningful all-transcriptome neighbor: the top positive score cosine was 0.0313 and the top negative was -0.0249.
The Tnrc6b deficiency surface does not resemble a strong acute, cell-autonomous postnatal neuronal transcriptome despite human TNRC6B haploinsufficiency causing neurodevelopmental disease.

Tomm40 loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal FDR-null surface: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 23 measured cell groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where the Tomm40 transcript itself fell with logFC -0.923 and FDR 5.46e-07.
Canonical import-failure transcriptional programs were absent: Tomm40 perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 ISR/ATF, UPRmt-chaperone/protease, proteasome, or TOM-subunit compensation genes.

Tomm40 had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor: the best positive score cosine was only +0.0303 and the strongest non-safe negative was Mecp2 at -0.0142; the broader mitochondrial comparator Opa1 had 241 FDR<0.10 downstream genes where Tomm40 had none.
The juvenile neuronal coding-loss perturbation did not phenocopy the human TOMM40/APOE regulatory disease axis.
Tpi1 produced a single downstream RNA response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Ogt and Slc25a27 were both down-regulated; all other groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Ogt was the one Tpi1 downstream gene that converged with other perturbations: Gfpt1 and Psmb4 also down-regulated Ogt in the same 145 MH-LH TH Glut group.
Tpi1 did not activate the expected glycolytic-compensation, glyoxalase, ISR/UPR, or proteasome-bounce-back transcripts in the effect group or in two high-powered self-depleted groups.

The represented glycolytic comparators Hk1, Gpi1, Pfkm, and Eno1 were also mostly transcriptionally flat and did not phenocopy Tpi1 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, whereas Gfpt1 and Ogt were far broader responders.

The sparse P16 neuronal Tpi1 LoF signature is consistent with TPI disease requiring a deeper activity/stability threshold or structurally unstable missense proteins, not uniform mild catalytic reduction alone.
Slc25a27/Ucp4 down-regulation is an exploratory mitochondrial-coupling marker of the 145 MH-LH TH Glut Tpi1 response.
Whole-transcriptome Tpi1 signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated: even the highest absolute Pearson correlations were between -0.016 and 0.031 after self-gene removal.
Tpk1 loss of function was transcriptomically buffered across every recovered postnatal neuronal group: no group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Tpk1 did not converge with the measured PDH, OGDH, or BCKDH-axis perturbations, which themselves were almost flat in the Tpk1-matched neuronal groups.
An unbiased all-target signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Tpk1 neighbor; the strongest whole-profile score cosines were only +0.0365 and -0.0197.
The flat postnatal Tpk1 CRISPR signature is not evidence that neuronal TPK1 suppression is safe or that thiamine rescue is irrelevant.

Acute postmitotic Tpm1 loss was a near-pan-neuronal transcriptional null: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the Tpm1 self-transcript was FDR=1.000 in every cell group.
215 MB Dopa was the only Tpm1 responder, and its response consisted of a single down-regulated gene, Nfxl1.

The measured actin/tropomyosin comparators did not converge with Tpm1: Tpm3 had no downstream FDR-level genes, Actg1 and Actn4 had near-zero flattened correlations with Tpm1, and Tpm1 did not induce FDR-level Tpm2, Tpm4, Actg1 or Actn4 compensation.
Tpm1 had no meaningful whole-universe signature neighbor: the top positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations across other targets were all |r|<=0.026.
Tpm3 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq signature in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Tpm3 perturbation did not induce Tpm1, Tpm2, or Tpm4 mRNA compensation, and the measurable paralog Tpm1 was also flat in the same cell groups.
The top whole-surface positive and negative signature neighbors of Tpm3 were rejected because all Pearson correlations were near zero.

Tpr produced a strongly selective response: 12 of 21 measured groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, with 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut accounting for 5371 of 6852 total downstream significant calls.
Tpr perturbation recurrently altered nuclear transport and NXF1-adjacent export genes, with Ranbp6 and Xpo1 up and Nxf1 down across multiple cell groups.
RNA-processing factors were repeatedly down-regulated after Tpr perturbation, including Rnpc3, Srsf5, Srrm2, Ddx17, Cstf2, Pabpn1, and Nxf1.
Proteasome and UFMylation perturbations were the top positive cross-target neighbors of Tpr, led by Psmb4, Psmc1, Uba5, and Ufc1.
Tpr-responsive thalamic and midbrain neurons mounted ATF4/ER-stress and ubiquitin-system compensation, while the canonical MTOR-lysosome arm was narrow.
Zinc-finger, Mediator, and chromatin-remodeling genes rose recurrently after Tpr perturbation.
DNA-repair and genome-maintenance transcripts, including Lig4, Rev1, Smc6, Wapl, Mdm2, and Trp53, were induced in the Tpr response.
Large Tpr signatures included recurrent down-regulation of neuronal effector transcripts such as Agrn, Gria2, Stxbp1, Ptprs, Cyp46a1, Slc22a17, and Unc80.
Thoc1 partially phenocopied Tpr, but Ranbp2 and Mtor did not: Ranbp2 shared only 66 FDR-supported Tpr-coordinate genes and Mtor only 3.
The Mad1/Mad2 spindle-checkpoint program expected from TPR in mitotic cells was absent from all postmitotic neuronal Tpr signatures.
P16 Traf3 CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal FDR null: all 23 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the Traf3 self-transcript was nonsignificant in every group.

No interferon-stimulated, immediate NF-κB/MAPK, oxidative-stress, or apoptosis transcripts were recovered after Traf3 perturbation; the inspected expected genes were present in the DE table but had FDR=1 across all 23 groups.

The pre-literature all-gene Traf3 Wilcoxon-score vector had no strong positive or negative neighbor among 1,772 other targets; the largest absolute score-cosines were only +0.0335 and -0.0294 and both involved Safe_target perturbations covering only 4 to 5 cell groups.

Measured TNFR/TLR/NF-κB relatives did not phenocopy a Traf3 program: Cd40, Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Rel, Tlr2, Tlr4, and Tnfrsf1a each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in their own matched surfaces, while Tlr3 and Tnfrsf13c produced only 1 and 4 significant genes, respectively.

Trak1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally buffered across the juvenile postmitotic neuron panel: only Nop56 in Sst GABA and Synj1 in midbrain glutamatergic neurons reached FDR<0.10, and no ISR, UPR, autophagy, mitophagy, or mitochondrial-transport feedback panel was induced.
Sst GABA was the only forebrain inhibitory class with a robust Trak1 downstream hit, an isolated Nop56 increase.
Midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed a single robust Trak1 effect, up-regulation of Synj1.
Represented Miro/kinesin arm genes did not phenocopy Trak1: Rhot1, Kif5a, Kif5c, and Klc2 were fully transcriptionally flat, and Klc1 altered only two genes in unrelated classes.
Ogt and Opa1 produced broad transcriptional responses where Trak1 was nearly flat.
The unbiased score-neighbor search found no robust Trak1-like global module; the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were near zero and included safe-target-like null signatures.
Trappc10 perturbation produced a single FDR-supported downstream call: Jund was up in 155 MB Glut and no other gene in any measured group reached FDR<0.10.
The measured TRAPP relatives do not converge transcriptionally: Trappc6b had a different one-gene response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, whereas Trappc9 was flat.
Trappc10 perturbation did not activate a coordinated UPR/ISR, autophagy-lysosome, NF-kB, Rab1/Rab11, or TRAPP-subunit transcript program.
Trappc10 has no meaningful transcriptomic neighbor in the full perturbation universe; the strongest positive and negative z-score correlations were only r=0.0257 and r=-0.0196.
The lone robust Trappc6b downstream hit was Nsdhl up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Trappc6b perturbation did not trigger a detectable UPR, ISR, lysosomal, or autophagy transcriptional program in any recovered neuronal group.
Measured TRAPP II-specific targets Trappc9 and Trappc10 did not converge with Trappc6b in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
A restricted-signature cross-target search found only low-amplitude Trappc6b neighbors.
Acute postnatal Trappc9 perturbation produced no robust steady-state neuronal transcriptome in any recovered cell group.
Canonical NF-κB, Rab/TRAPP-autophagy, neurite, synaptic, dopamine and activity-regulated marker transcripts were measured but did not move after Trappc9 perturbation.
A transcriptome-wide neighbor search placed Trappc9 outside any strong model-visible positive or negative perturbation signature.
Measured TRAPPII, NF-κB and dopamine comparators did not reveal a shared Trappc9-like module, while Rab7 showed that trafficking perturbations can be transcriptionally visible in the same dataset.
Trim2 loss generated a real but two-gene nuclear RNA response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where App and Cntn1 were down-regulated.
The responder did not show the canonical neurofilament, ISR/UPR, autophagy-lysosome, or proteasome transcriptional programs expected if acute TRIM2 loss had produced a strong nuclear stress response.

Trim2 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor: the best positive non-self correlation was a Safe_target label and the most anti-correlated target, Wdr26, did not oppose App/Cntn1 in the responder.
Literature-obvious relatives and disease-family targets represented in the parquet did not phenocopy the Trim2 thalamic signature.
Acute Trim37 loss produced a real but extremely sparse neuronal transcriptome, restricted to two subcortical classes: Fbxo3/Senp5 down in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Sorcs2 up in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
The 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA response synchronized two post-translational regulators, Fbxo3 and Senp5, downward after knockout of the E3-ligase gene Trim37.
Sorcs2 was the only downstream transcript induced by Trim37 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut neurons.
Trim37 loss did not activate a canonical peroxisome, oxidative-stress, UPR/ISR, lysosome-proteasome, p53-apoptosis, centrosome, or cell-cycle transcriptional program in the neuronal nuclei assayed.
Represented peroxisomal relatives and a represented TRIM-family relative did not phenocopy Trim37: Pex14, Hsd17b4, Pex1, Agps, Trim2, and Atr were null or disjoint at the FDR level.
No robust cross-perturbation module converged on the Trim37 response: the best all-score neighbors had cosines below 0.031, and none reproduced the three FDR-significant Trim37 features.
Trip11 produced a pan-measured-neuron transcriptomic null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The Golgi-loss prediction was uncoupled from canonical nuclear stress output: Trip11 did not induce Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Herpud1, Asns, Chac1, Cars, or Slc1a4 in any measured neuronal group.

Trip11 sat in a broader buffered secretory-pathway region of the screen: represented Sec23a, Sar1b, Copa, Copg1, Stx5a, Cog4, and Cog5 perturbations were absent or nearly absent responders in the same neuronal groups.
Data-driven signature search found no meaningful Trip11 neighbor: the largest full-score Pearson correlation was only 0.038, and the strongest negative non-safe target was -0.024.

Acute Trmt1 perturbation was nearly flat at the nuclear-transcriptome level, with only 3 downstream FDR<0.10 gene hits across 22 measured cell groups and no FDR-significant Trmt1 self-transcript decrease.
The only three Trmt1 downstream genes were Coq2 up in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Slc9a8 down in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and Prkcsh up in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
The strongest data-driven Trmt1 score-vector neighbors were themselves weak and shared no exact FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell-group hits with Trmt1.
Elp1 and Elp2, but not Trmt1, induced a robust amino-acid/ATF4 integrated-stress module in the same dataset; Nsun2 and Alkbh8 were flat like Trmt1.
The postnatal Trmt1 null refines, rather than negates, recessive TRMT1 neurodevelopmental disease biology.
Acute Trp53 loss-of-function was transcriptionally silent across the measured juvenile postmitotic neuronal atlas: every one of the 23 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The p53-family paralogs did not reveal a hidden family-wide baseline neuronal module: Trp63 was flat in 22 groups and Trp73 yielded only one CB-GABA gene, with no overlap to Trp53 because Trp53 itself had no FDR<0.10 genes.

The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Trp53 convergence: the best positive and negative score-vector neighbors were Fntb and Akt3 with correlations close to zero, and return-to-data checks showed at most two isolated FDR<0.10 Fntb genes and no Akt3 downstream genes.

Represented p53-axis comparators also failed to produce a p53 target-gene program: Atr, E2f1, and Ep300 were flat, while Crebbp responded only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Trp53 itself had no downstream genes.
Trp63 is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null in this acute P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR loss-of-function screen.
Loss of Trp63 did not release a detectable p53/PUMA apoptotic, precursor-loss, or epithelial target program in any measured neuronal group.
The Trp63 null surface was not rescued by cross-perturbation similarity: the closest data-driven neighbors had only near-zero score correlations and p53-family paralogs did not phenocopy Trp63.
Acute Trp63 LoF in postmitotic neurons does not model the epithelial and dominant-variant axis of TP63-related human disease.
The only Trp73 responder was a one-gene 308 CB GABA signature: Klhl3 increased while every other measured cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
Trp73 loss did not induce a p53-family cell-cycle or apoptotic transcriptome in any captured neuronal class.
The p73-Foxj1 multiciliogenesis program was completely absent from Trp73-edited NeuN+ brain nuclei.
Textbook p73 comparators were measurable but also flat: Trp53, Trp63, E2f1, Bcl2, and the ciliary-factor proxy Rfx3 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in their assayed neuronal groups.
All-gene, data-driven Trp73 neighbors were rejected as biology: the nearest cosines were tiny, included Safe_target-labelled entries, and did not share Klhl3.
Trpa1 loss-of-function produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered central neuronal cell group.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of the Trpa1 signature were near zero and were rejected as biological convergence.
Canonical nociceptor relatives Trpv1, Trpm3, Ntrk1, and Ret were measured and failed to converge with Trpa1 in brain neurons.
The central-neuron Trpa1 null should not be read as evidence against peripheral TRPA1 analgesic or anti-inflammatory targeting.
P16 Trpm3 loss in postmitotic NeuN-enriched brain nuclei left an almost blank steady-state transcriptome: 1 FDR<0.10 downstream gene over 22 measured cell groups.
The sole Trpm3 FDR signal was Cpd down-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
Neither phenotype-first neighbors nor literature-obvious TRP/Ca2+ pathway relatives phenocopied Trpm3.
The sparse Trpm3 loss-of-function signature does not model the transcriptional consequences of human TRPM3 gain-of-function channelopathy.
Trpm7 produced a single robust downstream transcriptomic hit: Psmd12 was up-regulated only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
Psmd12-up is rare in the complete screen but recurs after direct proteasome perturbations, making the Trpm7 L4/5 hit a candidate proteasome-feedback marker rather than a random high-frequency DEG.
Neither unbiased neighbors nor literature-obvious TRP and magnesium-gene relatives converged on the Trpm7 responder gene.
Loss of Trpm7 in unstressed postmitotic neurons did not activate the expected synaptic-vesicle, glutamate-receptor, Mg2+/Ca2+, oxidative-stress, or injury transcriptional programs.
Trps1 loss produced a single FDR-level neuronal response, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
direction_pattern: Tnc and Atp6ap2 up; Pid1 down

canonical_summary: Tnc was the strongest Trps1-induced gene and recapitulates a known direction of Trps1 mutant derepression.
The Atp6ap2 arm of the Trps1 response is rare and opposite to canonical Wnt-effector perturbations.
direction_pattern: Trps1 increases Atp6ap2; Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 decrease Atp6ap2

canonical_summary: Sox9, classical GATA factors, and Ctbp1 do not robustly phenocopy Trps1 in the responding thalamic group.
Data-driven Trps1 signature neighbors are weak and non-canonical.

Trpv1 produced only two corrected downstream genes across 22 measured postnatal brain-neuron groups, and the expected immediate-early, nociceptor-neuropeptide, injury, heat-shock, and ER-stress marker set had zero FDR<0.10 changes.
The only corrected cortical response to Trpv1 loss was Gsk3a down-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The only corrected subcortical GABAergic response to Trpv1 loss was Cep120 induction in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Psmc1 was the top positive data-driven neighbor because it also up-regulated Cep120 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, but it produced 1,351 corrected genes in that group whereas Trpv1 produced only Cep120.
The represented thermoTRP/channel relatives Trpa1, Trpm3, and Trpm7, plus the endocannabinoid comparator Cnr1, did not phenocopy either corrected Trpv1 feature.
Basal brain snRNA after Trpv1 loss offers little support for using unstimulated resident-neuron transcription as a proximal biomarker of TRPV1 antagonism.

Postmitotic Tsc2 loss produced a selective nuclear response rather than a uniform mTORopathy signature: 636 downstream FDR<0.10 hits concentrated in nine measured groups and especially in caudal hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar neurons.
direction_pattern: upward caudal metabolic/lysosomal program with sparse synaptic down-regulation

canonical_summary: The strongest Tsc2 responders activated the mTORC1 metabolic/endomembrane output most clearly through sterol and lysosomal genes.
Tsc2 loss induced transcripts for PI3K/mTOR feedback and nutrient-sensing regulators, including Tsc1, Ddit4, Pten, Fnip1/Fnip2, Flcn, Rragb/Rragd, and Pik3r1/Pik3r3.
A subset of responders coupled the mTORC1 metabolic program to immediate-early, UPR/ISR-adjacent, and apoptotic transcripts, including Jun, Btg2, Ddit3, Ddit4, Bax, and Bbc3.

Tsc2 altered neuronal-communication genes in two separable ways: Syp/Clstn1/Sort1 and neurosecretory genes fell in L4-5, hypothalamic, and MB/P/MY responders, whereas CB GABA showed an up-shift of Shank3, Cacna1d, Slc24a3, Stxbp1, and Rph3a with adhesion genes moving in both directions.

Cross-perturbation analysis nominated a noncanonical Tsc2 neighborhood: Wdr26 was the top positive restricted-cosine neighbor, and Psmc1/Psmb4, Rab7, and Sin3a reproduced large same-direction subsets of the Tsc2 signature.

Measurable mTOR-pathway relatives separated by pathway position: Srebf2 loss strongly reversed the Tsc2 sterol branch, Depdc5 loss matched 11 thalamic genes, but Mtor, Rptor, Igf1r, Irs1, and Akt3 did not give a robust matched FDR overlap.
direction_pattern: Srebf2 opposite; Depdc5 partially same; core/upstream relatives mostly absent

canonical_summary: Tsc2 loss did not detectably induce a direct proteasome-subunit or ribosomal mRNA program despite the mTORC1 NRF1 proteasome branch described in other systems.
Acute Tsga10 loss did not trigger a robust postnatal neuronal transcriptional program in any measured cell group, including HIF, UPR or ISR sentinels.

Tsga10 had no meaningful convergent or opposing perturbation neighbor: the best global Wilcoxon-z correlations were only r=0.0308 to Arid1b and r=-0.0151 to the top negative non-safe gene Lrig2, and Hif1a/Arnt were also flat.
Tshr loss produced an extremely sparse, singleton response in three neuronal classes: Kcnj4 down in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Stxbp1 up in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and Arfgef3 down in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The Tshr DE surface did not recover the expected CREB, Wnt5a/β-catenin, immediate-early, neurogenesis, or thyroid-hormone receptor programs.
The glycoprotein-hormone receptor relatives Fshr and Lhcgr were fully flat, so Tshr's three singletons were not a receptor-family-wide transcriptional module.
Canonical Gs/adenylyl-cyclase/PKA/CREB perturbations in the same parquet did not converge with Tshr.
Tshr was a data-driven signature orphan: no other target reproduced any of its three robust gene×cell features at FDR<0.10.
Tshz2 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The literature-obvious paralog Tshz3 was nearly as flat as Tshz2, with only one marginal downstream hit across 22 measured groups.
Tshz2 did not activate the expected cortical projection-neuron gene program, while Tbr1 did respond in matched cortical groups.
The data-driven nearest-neighbor pass produced only sub-threshold, seven-gene matches and no robust Tshz2 signature neighbor.
Acute P16 mosaic Tshz3 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: 21 of 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and 308 CB GABA contributed a single borderline FDR hit.
The only robust downstream Tshz3 hit was a decrease of Atxn7l3 in 308 CB GABA.
The expected identity and corticostriatal synaptic programs were absent from the Tshz3 DE surface.
The data-driven positive and negative nearest neighbors, Crbn and Cog5, did not share an FDR-supported Tshz3 effector.
Tshz2 and selected synaptic/ASD perturbations failed to phenocopy the Tshz3 surface.
P16 mosaic Tspan7 CRISPR produced a broad drop in the target RNA but almost no secondary nuclear transcriptome: only 1 of 355074 downstream gene tests crossed FDR<0.10 in 21 measured cell groups.
The sole FDR<0.10 downstream event was Ss18l1 up-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
Canonical AMPAR/PICK1/integrin transcripts and immediate-early activity genes were unchanged after Tspan7 perturbation.
Represented AMPAR-subunit and pathway-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy the Tspan7 singleton signature.
The unbiased full-signature neighbor scan found no recurring perturbation module for Tspan7.
Acute postnatal Tspoap1 perturbation produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 23 measured neuronal cell groups, restricted to 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
The only CNU-MGE GABA hit was down-regulation of the RIM-BP paralog Rimbp2, not up-regulation of a compensatory RIM-BP backup program.
Tmem131l was the sole FDR<0.10 signal in CNU-HYa/HY GABA, making it a noncanonical marker of the hypothalamic GABA response to Tspoap1 perturbation.

Data-driven whole-transcriptome signature neighbors of Tspoap1 were extremely weak; top positive neighbors did not converge in the responder groups, while Wdr26 produced a broad divergent 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA response.
Represented active-zone genes did not phenocopy Tspoap1 in the two responder groups.
Tspoap1 did not induce a mitochondrial ISR, whereas Opa1 produced a strong Asns/Chac1/Ddit3-centered stress signature in the same GABA cell groups.

P16 mosaic Ttc19 loss was transcriptionally buffered in juvenile neurons: the screen recovered one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across all 23 measured cell groups, even though Ttc19 itself was detectably depleted in five groups.
The only non-self Ttc19 hit was a weak, cell-restricted decrease of the sorting receptor Sorl1 in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
Measured complex-III subunit perturbations did not phenocopy Ttc19: Uqcrb, Uqcrc2, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrh, and Uqcrq were almost flat and did not reproduce Sorl1 loss in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
A different mitochondrial perturbation, Opa1, produced a broad amino-acid/ATF4-like ISR across matched neurons, whereas Ttc19 did not.
Unbiased cross-perturbation mapping did not find a robust positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Ttc19.
Ttc21b produced a single robust downstream transcriptional event, down-regulation of Klf13, confined to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The canonical IFT-A/Hedgehog/ciliary-GPCR program was not transcriptionally engaged by Ttc21b in P16-perturbed postmitotic neurons.
A related transition-zone ciliopathy perturbation, B9d1, evoked a 25-gene 308 CB GABA response that Ttc21b did not share.
Across the full queryable perturbation universe, Ttc21b had only weak top-50-gene signature neighbors and no robust convergent or anticorrelated partner.

Acute postnatal Ttc8 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the neuronal taxonomy: all 22 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a negative Ttc8 self-transcript in every group.
Canonical neuronal ciliary-cargo and hypothalamic energy-balance transcripts were not remodeled by Ttc8 loss.
The literature-obvious ciliary comparators represented in the parquet also failed to converge with Ttc8 into a robust shared transcriptional module.
The data-driven Ttc8 signature neighbors were weak and non-recurrent.

The screen refines where BBS8 disease biology should be looked for: not as a broad resting neuronal mRNA program, but as ciliary localization in photoreceptors, olfactory sensory neurons, and specialized hypothalamic circuits.
Ttll5 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal class: no measured cell group contained even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10 despite 371,818 tested group-by-gene rows.

The TTLL5-RPGR disease axis is absent from the recovered brain DE surface: Ttll5 was flat in 22 groups and Rpgr, its canonical photoreceptor substrate, produced 0 FDR<0.10 genes across 21 represented groups.

Ttll5 did not engage the neuronal structural-tubulin transcriptional response seen after Tuba1a perturbation: Tuba1a up-regulated Tubb2a, Tubb3, Tuba4a, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5 in Pvalb and thalamic neurons, whereas Ttll5, Kif5a, Spast, and Map1b had no FDR<0.10 DEGs.

The alternative TTLL5/STAMP nuclear-receptor co-regulator axis did not covary with Ttll5: Nr3c1, Ncoa1, and Ar had only 5, 1, and 0 total FDR<0.10 genes, respectively, and none overlapped the empty Ttll5 signature.

The unbiased full-universe comparison found no meaningful Ttll5 co-perturbation neighbor: the strongest positive Pearson score correlation was only +0.0383 and the strongest negative correlation only -0.0194 among non-safe targets.
Tuba1a has a highly restricted downstream surface: 10 downstream FDR<0.10 cell-gene events in only 2 of 21 measured cell groups.
The real downstream program is dominated by up-regulation of other alpha/beta tubulin transcripts after Tuba1a loss.
The FDR<0.10 response lacks a broad stress, autophagy, redox, proteasome, or synaptic-collapse transcriptome; Copb1 is the only non-tubulin call and is a singleton.
Direct Tuba4a, Tubb4b, and Tubb5 perturbations do not phenocopy the Tuba1a multi-tubulin up-regulation module in the two responder groups.
Tbcd, Map1b, Kif5a, Spast, and Stmn2 did not reproduce the Tuba1a responder signature; Tbcd instead showed reciprocal alpha-tubulin induction.
Restricted-signature cross-perturbation ranked Cic and Depdc5 as positive tubulin-module neighbors and Atxn10, Gfpt1, and Thap11 as opposite-direction neighbors.
Postnatal Tuba1a LoF yields tubulin compensation, not an embryonic dominant-missense tubulinopathy program.

Acute Tuba4a loss yielded a near-null somatic transcriptome: only Mospd3 in Pvalb GABA and Mast1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons passed the downstream FDR<0.10 threshold across 371,818 tested gene-by-cell-group rows.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Tuba4a knockdown selectively up-regulated Mast1, a microtubule-associated serine/threonine kinase gene, with no broader FDR-level tubulin response.
In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Mospd3 was the only downstream transcript induced by Tuba4a perturbation.

The alpha-tubulin paralog Tuba1a induced an alpha/beta-tubulin compensation module in both Tuba4a responder groups, whereas Tuba4a, Tubb5, Tubb4b, Mapt, and Mast1 perturbations did not phenocopy that module.
A microtubule-transport perturbation, Dctn1, produced a broad sterol/lipid and neuronal response in the same analysis universe, while Tuba4a stayed two-gene-sparse.
The screen did not phenocopy the ALS/FTD-oriented TUBA4A literature as an acute, broad postmitotic neuronal injury transcriptome.
Tubb4b loss was transcriptomically buffered in every recovered neuronal cell group: 22/22 measured groups had zero non-self genes at FDR<0.10.
Tubb4b did not induce the beta/alpha-tubulin mRNA replacement program that is visible after Tuba1a perturbation in the same screen.

Literature-obvious microtubule relatives failed to phenocopy Tubb4b: Tubb5, Tuba1a, Tuba4a, Stmn2, Mapt, Map1b, Map6, Mapre2, Kif5a, Kif5c, and Dctn1 all had residual signature cosines between -0.00694 and 0.00591 versus Tubb4b.
The data-driven nearest neighbors of Tubb4b were all essentially zero-correlation hits; even the strongest positive and negative non-Safe neighbors had |cosine|≤0.01456.
Sparse postnatal Tubb4b loss in parenchymal brain neurons does not phenocopy TUBB4B sensorineural disease biology.
Tubb5 produced only three downstream FDR<0.10 single-gene effects: Repin1 up in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Chrd up in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and Tnrc18 down in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
A measured Tubb5 mRNA decrease was often uncoupled from any stable nuclear RNA program.
The α-tubulin Tuba1a, but not the β-tubulins Tubb5 or Tubb4b, elicited a tubulin-paralog RNA feedback signature.
The microtubule transport adaptor Dctn1 generated a broad sterol/lipid response that Tubb5 and most structural microtubule-neighbor perturbations lacked.
Data-driven signature search found no convincing Tubb5 phenocopy.
A P16 mosaic CRISPR loss-of-function of Tubb5 is a poor phenocopy of TUBB5 tubulinopathy mechanisms.
Twist2 produced no robust downstream single-nucleus RNA response in any of the 23 measured neuronal groups after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.
Canonical Twist2 output genes from dermal fibroblast, osteogenic, and NF-kappaB cytokine biology were completely uncoupled from the postmitotic neuronal Twist2 perturbation.

Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor Twist2 literature relatives phenocopied Twist2: residual screen-wide correlations were all tiny, Tcf3/Tcf12/Runx2 were flat, and Mef2c—not Twist2—was the related transcription factor with a clear neuronal response.

Txndc15 loss up-regulated a compact sterol/SREBP-like program only in 3/22 recovered cell groups, with the main six-gene response in 155 MB Glut and partial echoes in 191 MB P MY GABA and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
Txndc15 perturbation did not recover a canonical ciliary Hedgehog, ciliogenesis, or unfolded-protein-response mRNA program in any recovered cell group.
Srebf2 flipped the Txndc15 sterol feature set while Marchf6 converged on the same 155 MB Glut genes; Srebf1 and Hmgcr did not phenocopy.
Ciliary and Hedgehog pathway targets represented in the screen had 0/9 FDR-level overlaps with the Txndc15 downstream feature set.
A restricted data-first search placed Htt, Dctn1, and Mib1 as the strongest positive Txndc15 sterol neighbors and Uba5 and Phf12 as FDR-supported inverse neighbors.

U2af2 loss-of-function produced a broad whole-gene response mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with intermediate Pvalb and hypothalamic responses and many flat cortical/hippocampal groups.

Rsrp1 was the dominant recurrent U2af2 downstream marker, always down when significant; the same signature repeatedly decreased Srrm2, Luc7l2, Srsf5, Tial1, Atp11b, and Wsb1 and increased Map7d1, Nxf1, Xpot, and Cmtr1.
Broad U2af2 responders induced ubiquitin/ERAD/chaperone and vacuolar-trafficking genes, including Zfp598, Dnaja2, Dnajb5, Herpud1, Ubr4, Nprl2, Atp6v0b, Atp6v1h, Copb1, Vps35l, and Rab12.
The largest U2af2 signatures down-regulated mature neuronal and synaptic effector transcripts, notably Grin1, Gls, Slc17a6, Agrn, Cyp46a1, Vamp1, Stxbp1, Syt2, Kcnc1, and Kcnc2.
Unbiased signature search placed Psmc1, Psmb4, Prpf6, Cdc40, and Tpr as the top positive U2af2 neighbors.

Most matched RNA-processing comparators failed to converge with U2af2: Hnrnpc was slightly anti-correlated, Upf3b and Snrpb were effectively flat, Hnrnpa2b1 and Hnrnph2 had tiny signatures, and Ddx39b overlapped only 14 U2af2 pairs.
P16 U2af2 loss did not reproduce a Rbfox1 total-mRNA response but did depress Nova1, Srrm4, and synaptic-effector transcripts in selected mature neuronal groups.
Large downstream signatures occurred even though U2af2 self-mRNA was only modestly reduced and often FDR-flat.

Uba5 perturbation was not pan-neuronal: the high-amplitude response localized to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with only tiny tails in 066, 054, and 110.
Uba5 responders mounted a uniformly upward nuclear-encoded mitochondrial OXPHOS/import program.
Uba5 loss induced an autophagy/ubiquitin-like proteostasis rebound anchored by Sqstm1 and COP9/NEDD8/ubiquitin genes.
Translation initiation and elongation RNAs rose alongside the proteostasis response.
SR-splicing and nuclear RNA-processing genes were a recurrent downward arm of the Uba5 signature.
Uba5 down-regulated a sterol/reticulon/v-ATPase lysosomal arm while other stress modules went up.
The broad responders coupled organelle stress to synaptic and neurite transcript remodeling.
The stress arm was Ddit3/redox-biased and did not recover a full canonical ER-UPR transcriptional program.
Ufc1, the sole UFM1 E2, was the strongest same-direction Uba5 neighbor.
Ufsp2 loss did not invert Uba5 loss; the represented UFM1 deconjugase showed only a weak same-direction overlap.
The strongest data-driven non-UFMylation positive neighbors were Tpr, Tnpo3 and Elp1, linking Uba5 to RNA export/splicing and tRNA-modification stress.
Marchf6 and Mib1 were data-driven negative neighbors because they up-regulated the sterol genes that Uba5 suppressed.
Acute Ube2e2 perturbation was flat across all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and a non-significant Ube2e2 self-transcript in every group.
Ube2e2 did not phenocopy represented ubiquitin/proteostasis neighbors: Psmb4, Psmc1, Uba5, and Huwe1 were broad responders, but their correlations to Ube2e2 were r=-0.00035 to 0.0179.
Ube2e2 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce the measured UBE2E paralogs Ube2e1 or Ube2e3 in any measured neuronal group.
The neuronal Ube2e2 LoF null separates this target's β-cell gain-of-function diabetes axis from a postmitotic neuronal p21/Nedd4, UPR/ISR, heat-shock, or ISG transcriptional program.
Genome-wide score-vector comparison found no meaningful Ube2e2 signature neighbor: the largest positive Pearson r was 0.026 and the largest negative r was -0.0157.
Ube3a produced a broad weak/null basal snRNA-seq surface: 18 recovered neuronal groups, 713 total perturbed nuclei, measurable Ube3a transcript, but 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every group.

The established Arc/AMPAR and synaptic substrate axis was absent at FDR<0.10 on the RNA readout: Arc, Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Dlg4, Cbln1, Gabrb3, Hdac1, and Hdac2 were all FDR 1.0 across Ube3a-measured groups.

A matched HECT-family comparison showed strong divergence: Huwe1 produced 342 downstream DE genes in Ube3a-matched groups, whereas the UBE3A regulator Herc2 produced only 2 and Hecw2, Hectd4, and Herc1 were flat or nearly flat.

Measured Angelman/Dup15q and synaptic disease comparators did not expose a hidden Ube3a-like RNA module: Gabrb3 had 0 matched downstream genes, Snrpn 2, Gria2 1, Fmr1 1, Camk2a 4, Mtor 6, and Mecp2 33, with no shared-direction overlap with Ube3a because Ube3a itself had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.

The unbiased signature-neighbor analysis failed to identify a robust convergent or anti-convergent module: top positive and negative cosines computed on nominal Ube3a top features were only 0.1168 and -0.0857.
P16 Ubp1 loss-of-function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
The literature-obvious CP2/Grainyhead comparators Tfcp2 and Grhl2 did not reveal a shared postmitotic-neuronal module with Ubp1.
An unbiased all-target signature search found no meaningful Ubp1 convergence or anti-convergence.
Known UBP1/TFCP2-family target programs were absent from the postnatal neuronal Ubp1 surface.
Acute Ubr1 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 19 neuronal groups in which it was recovered.

Ubr1 was uncoupled from bulk proteasome-stress transcription: canonical ISR/UPR, heat-shock, p62/autophagy and immediate-early markers did not pass FDR, whereas core proteasome perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 produced thousands of DE genes in the same matched cell groups.
The Ubr1 null is consistent with UBR-family buffering, but the directly redundant N-recognins were not perturbation targets in this parquet.
The data-driven Ubr1 nearest-neighbor search did not nominate a robust biological module: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were only +0.038 and -0.033.
Uchl1 loss produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream change, Ctif down-regulation, only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Uchl1 did not activate the proteasome-bounce-back, UPR/ISR, or autophagy-lysosome transcriptional programs that are detectable in the same screen after stronger proteostasis lesions.
Measured deubiquitinase and proteostasis relatives did not phenocopy Uchl1; Bap1 and Usp48 responded in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Uchl1 was flat there.
The pre-literature, restricted-signature search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Uchl1.
The acute Uchl1 brain signature did not resemble Snca or Park7 perturbation and did not induce amyloid, tau, synuclein, or synaptic-stress marker transcription in the measured neuronal groups.
Ufc1 loss produced a real response in only five of 22 measured neuronal groups, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The same-sign Uba5-Ufc1 overlap ties the Ufc1 signature to UFMylation loss.
Uba5 was broader than Ufc1 across midbrain, hypothalamic, and pineal groups.
Ufc1 induced a Ddit3/CHOP-centered stress branch but not a full BiP/Xbp1 ER-UPR.
Proteasome, chaperone, and autophagy/lysosome genes rose after Ufc1 loss.
RNA-processing and splicing transcripts formed a recurring down-regulated arm of the Ufc1 signature.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coupled stress induction to down-regulation of synaptic and excitability genes.
Mitochondrial import, respiratory-chain, and CLPP genes were induced as a secondary Ufc1 branch.
The strongest Ufc1 responder up-regulated Ufm1 and Ufsp2 transcripts.
Immediate-early and MAPK-feedback genes rose only in the large 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
The screen did not contain a robust anti-Ufc1 signature.
Ufsp2 had a sparse, subcortically restricted response: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Uba5 and Ufc1 were the dominant positive signature neighbors of Ufsp2 and recapitulated its 151/155 responder genes in the same direction.

Ufsp2 converged with but did not phenocopy Uba5/Ufc1: conjugating-enzyme loss induced hundreds to thousands of genes and a stress program whereas Ufsp2 changed only 4 and 16 genes in the matched responders.
The significant Ufsp2 responder genes included a mitochondrial arm: Pink1 increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Cox5a, Ndufa2, Timm8b, and Timm13 increased in 155 MB Glut.
Ufsp2 responders showed a small neuronal membrane/cytoskeletal module with Tmsb4x and Cfl1 up and Sema6b, C1qtnf4, Atp6v0c, Syt11, and Tspan3 down.
Ufsp2 did not induce a canonical UPR/ISR/autophagy transcriptome, even in the two responder classes, despite Uba5 and Ufc1 showing that such genes were detectable in this dataset.
P16 Ulk4 loss produced an almost completely buffered postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: one downstream FDR<0.10 gene in 22 measured cell groups.
Ints10 was the sole Ulk4 downstream hit and was down-regulated only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
The only data-driven same-feature neighbor of Ulk4 was Psmb4, yet Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced broad proteasome-loss signatures while Ulk4 did not.
The Stk36/Hedgehog expectation was not recovered: Ulk4 did not move Gli1/Gli2/Ptch/Smo/Stk36 readouts, and Gli1, Gli2, Smo, Ptch1, and Ptch2 perturbations were flat in the Ulk4 responder group.
Ulk4 did not acutely erase GABAergic transmitter identity: Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Pvalb, Sst, Cck, and Npy were never significant after Ulk4 perturbation.
Autophagy-neighbor perturbations Rb1cc1 and Becn1 did not recapitulate the CNU-MGE Ulk4 signature.
Unc13a perturbation produced a single robust downstream call: Dpp6 was down in 053 Sst Gaba and no other Sst synaptic, Kv4/A-current, immediate-early, or stress marker reached FDR<0.10.

Unc13a did not phenocopy Stxbp1/Munc18-1 despite both proteins acting in synaptic vesicle priming: Stxbp1 produced 140 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 8 of 22 recovered groups, whereas Unc13a produced one downstream gene in 23 groups.

The neuronal Munc13 paralogs queried in the screen were not interchangeable with Unc13a at the DE level: Unc13b had only one downstream hit in one of 12 recovered groups, and Unc13c had none in 21 groups.
A data-driven whole-universe signature scan found only tiny positive and negative correlations to Unc13a, and the nearest neighbors did not share the 053 Sst Gaba Dpp6 hit.

This screen tests acute mouse coding loss of Unc13a, not the two main human disease modalities: dominant gain-of-function UNC13A variants and TDP-43-dependent human cryptic splicing that lowers UNC13A expression in ALS/FTD.
Unc13b has a single robust downstream hit, Cdc27 up-regulation, confined to 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
Unc13b loss did not induce a robust cell-autonomous activity, stress, autophagy, or synaptic-compensation RNA program in any measured group.
Unc13b and its represented Munc13 paralogs were transcriptionally buffered, whereas the related priming factor Stxbp1 produced broad readouts in overlapping groups.
Unc13b has no robust data-driven signature neighbor in the full perturbation universe.
The UNC13B epilepsy prior maps better to presynaptic and circuit physiology than to a sustained cell-autonomous snRNA signature after postnatal sparse loss.
P16 Unc13c perturbation produced no robust whole-transcriptome DE in any recovered neuronal group.
The Unc13c null is selective: Stxbp1, an interacting SNARE-assembly factor, caused 139 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in matched groups where Unc13c caused none.
The expected Munc13 paralogs Unc13a and Unc13b did not phenocopy Unc13c in the snRNA surface.
Unc13c had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.

Unc5c loss produced a pan-measured downstream null: 22 neuronal groups had 0 non-Unc5c genes at FDR<0.10, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut remained downstream-flat despite a significant Unc5c self-transcript decrease.

The literature-obvious netrin and APP comparators did not define a shared Unc5c-like module: Unc5d, Dcc, Dscam, and App each had 0 downstream genes across their measured surfaces, while Neo1 produced only 3 non-overlapping genes and was weakly anti-correlated with Unc5c.
Juvenile CRISPR loss of Unc5c did not elicit apoptosis, stress, or APP-like transcription in AD-vulnerable cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups or in any other measured group.

Unc5c is isolated in the measured perturbation manifold: its top positive full-score neighbor, Wdr26, reached only r=0.043 yet had 3128 robust downstream DE genes, and its strongest non-Safe negative neighbor, Fbxo11, had r=-0.0595 with a single FDR gene.

Unc5d loss after P16 produced a pan-neuronal whole-transcriptome null: every recovered cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, although weak negative Unc5d self shifts were present in most groups.
Unc5d had no meaningful perturbation-signature neighbors: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations across 1772 other target profiles were only 0.039997 and -0.047654.

Represented netrin/FLRT/latrophilin and broader axon-guidance comparators did not phenocopy Unc5d: Unc5c, Dcc, Dscam, Adgrl3, Robo1, Robo2, and Slit2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 calls, and all measured comparator correlations to Unc5d lay between -0.016929 and 0.019828.
The Unc5d zero surface included no detectable apoptosis, immediate-early, ISR, or UPR marker induction in any cell group.
Acute postmitotic Upf3b loss produced a caudal, Inpp5f-only FDR signature rather than a broad NMD-collapse transcriptome.
Hnrnpc, Tpr, and Xrn1 were the top same-direction perturbations at the six Upf3b Inpp5f response positions.
Camta1 and proteasome subunit perturbations drove the Upf3b marker Inpp5f in the opposite direction in the same caudal groups.
The assay did not recover the expected Atf4/Arhgap24 UPF3B-NMD response or a broad neural differentiation program.
Inpp5f is an exploratory acute Upf3b-response biomarker for caudal neuronal nuclei.
Uqcrb yielded a single corrected downstream event, Map7 down-regulation, restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
Canonical mitochondrial ISR, UPR, redox/HIF, autophagy/mitophagy, and OXPHOS transcriptional programs were absent after Uqcrb perturbation.
Represented complex-III relatives did not phenocopy Uqcrb, including in the 066 cell group where Uqcrb alone down-regulated Map7.
Uqcrb had no strong unbiased signature neighbor or antipode across the model-visible perturbation universe.
Uqcrc2 produced no robust downstream single-gene DE in any measured neuronal group; the only near-threshold trace was Cct8 up in 155 MB Glut at FDR 0.114.

Canonical mitochondrial-stress genes were absent: Atf4/Atf5, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Aldh1l2, Mthfd2, chaperones/proteases, redox genes, and mitophagy sentinels all had minimum FDR 1.0 after Uqcrc2 perturbation.
Represented complex-III relatives did not uncover a hidden Uqcrc2-like program: Uqcrb, Uqcrfs1, Uqcrh, Uqcrq, Cyc1, and Ttc19 each had 0-1 downstream genes in Uqcrc2-matched groups.
Opa1 perturbation activated the mitochondrial ATF4/ISR marker set in the same cell groups where Uqcrc2 was flat.
A whole-universe Wilcoxon-score search found no meaningful Uqcrc2 signature neighbor; the largest positive and negative cosines were only 0.0395 and -0.0320.
The Uqcrc2 null should not be read as evidence that complex-III deficiency is harmless in neurons or that UQCRC2 is irrelevant to brain disease.
Uqcrfs1 produced a singleton 155 MB Glut downstream signature, with Cfl1 down as the only non-target gene at FDR<0.10.
Uqcrfs1 did not induce a detectable mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, chaperone, protease, or mitochondrial-encoded ETC RNA program in any of the 23 measured cell groups.
Respiratory complex-III relatives and the UQCRFS1-turnover factor Ttc19 failed to phenocopy Uqcrfs1 across the measured neuronal surface.
The unbiased cross-perturbation signature search yielded only near-zero Uqcrfs1 neighbors and no robust anti-neighbor module.
Uqcrfs1-linked mitochondrial disease was not recapitulated as a broad juvenile neuronal stress transcriptome after P16 sparse LoF.
Uqcrh loss did not induce a detectable neuronal mitochondrial-stress or ATF4/ISR transcriptome in any recovered cell group.
Measured nuclear complex-III subunit perturbations phenocopied Uqcrh by being nearly transcriptionally flat.
The formal genome-wide Uqcrh signature neighbors had near-zero score cosines and did not define a real convergent or opposing module.
Uqcrq had exactly one robust downstream hit, a Gpr180 decrease restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Uqcrq perturbation did not activate a canonical mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, redox, hypoxia, mitophagy, or mitochondrial-biogenesis transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group.
Screened Complex III members failed to phenocopy the Uqcrq Gpr180 signal and were themselves almost flat.
Nrf1, a mitochondrial respiratory transcriptional regulator, produced a broad response that Uqcrq lacked in overlapping groups.
Uqcrq had only near-zero genome-wide signature neighbors, and the top positive or negative neighbors did not recover the Gpr180 effect.
The screen does not phenocopy severe recessive UQCRQ Complex III deficiency in juvenile recovered neurons.
Usf1 loss lowered the lysosomal glycogen hydrolase transcript Gaa only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons at FDR<0.10.
Single Usf1 perturbation was broadly buffered: lipid, sterol, USF-family, and ISR/UPR programs expected from canonical USF biology were not recovered at FDR<0.10.
Represented literature-obvious comparators did not phenocopy Usf1: Gtf2i and Srebf2 produced detectable but non-overlapping signatures, Myc was flat, and Usf2 itself was not a perturbation target.
Gaa is a recurrent, bidirectional perturbation-sensitive transcript in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
Acute Usp48 loss produced a robust downstream transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The 151 response is a compact Abhd12b/Cyp46a1/Msrb2/Bcan module rather than a canonical Hh, NF-kB, p53, UPR, ISR, or autophagy program.
Chd4 and Zmynd8, both chromatin/DNA-damage comparators represented in the screen, converge with the Usp48 thalamic signature more than the literature-obvious Hh or NF-kB targets do.
Represented Hedgehog and NF-kB effectors did not reproduce the Usp48 thalamic response, and expected Hh/NF-kB target panels were absent after Usp48 perturbation.
Uba5, Ctnnb1, Arid2, and Bptf are robust opposite-direction neighbors of Usp48 in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group.
Vamp1 loss in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut selectively decreased Atp6v0e, a V-ATPase V0-sector gene, without a broader FDR<0.10 transcriptional cascade.
Vamp1 loss in 145 MH-LH TH Glut selectively decreased Cacng7, a type-II TARP AMPA-receptor auxiliary subunit.

Where Vamp1 mRNA was significantly reduced, the perturbation stopped at the target transcript and did not induce a secondary SNARE, synaptotagmin, Munc13, synaptophysin, or Vamp2 transcriptional compensation program.
Stxbp1, a same-machinery Munc18-1 perturbation, produced a broader transcriptional surface than Vamp1 in matched central neurons.
Vamp1 lacked a strong positive or negative whole-transcriptome neighbor across 1772 other perturbations, including represented SNARE-adjacent genes.
The disease-relevant VAMP1 loss-of-function phenotype is displaced away from a juvenile central-neuron stress transcriptome.

Acute Vcp loss of function produced a sparse, cell-type-restricted transcriptomic phenotype: five FDR-significant downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, one in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and no robust downstream genes in the other 19 measured groups.

The thalamic Vcp response combines Slc38a2 and Rasgef1b up-regulation with lower Nsmf, Ptprs, and Plch2, consistent with a small amino-acid/adaptive-stress component plus repression of neuronal receptor, phosphatase, and phospholipase signaling genes.
direction_pattern: Slc38a2 and Rasgef1b up; Nsmf, Ptprs, Plch2 down

canonical_summary: In 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, the only robust downstream transcript was Gba, which decreased, implicating lysosomal glycosphingolipid catabolism as a narrow Vcp-sensitive output.

The top positive whole-transcriptome neighbors of Vcp in its responder groups were Uba5, Psmb4, Ufc1, Elp1, and Psmc1, and their significant genes recurred in the same direction with the thalamic Vcp signature.

In the same 151 thalamic group, pathway neighbors gave much larger expression programs than Vcp: Uba5, Psmb4, Ufc1, Elp1, Psmc1, Rab7, and Atp2a2 produced 284-3225 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, while Vcp produced only five.
Core p62/LC3 autophagy targets Sqstm1 and Map1lc3a failed to phenocopy Vcp even though VCP disease involves p62/LC3-positive autophagic pathology.
The data-driven search found no robust anti-neighbor for Vcp: the most negative whole-transcriptome correlations were only about -0.04 to -0.05 and lacked shared FDR-significant Vcp genes.
Vcp did not induce the canonical UPR, heat-shock, proteasome bounce-back, ERAD, p62/LC3, lysosomal-cathepsin, or TDP-43 transcripts at FDR<0.10 in any measured group.

Acute postmitotic neuronal Vdr loss produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 measured cell groups and did not alter tested vitamin-D, calcium-handling, RXR, or dopaminergic-development transcripts.
Vdr did not phenocopy RXR isotypes, NCOA coactivators, or same-superfamily nuclear receptors in the matched neuronal perturbation surface.
An unbiased restricted-signature search found no strong positive or negative Vdr neighbor across the model-visible perturbation universe.
Vezf1 loss produced a sparse postmitotic neuronal response: only 3 of 23 measured groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with the clearest signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Vezf1 perturbation down-regulated a compact Ca2+/Ras-PKC/Kv3 effector set and paired it with transcriptional and cytoskeletal changes.
Zcchc18 was the only recurrent Vezf1-dependent transcript outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, falling in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 155 MB Glut.
Prkcg and Kcnc1 behaved as Vezf1-responsive output transcripts, not as sufficient drivers of the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptome.
The Vezf1 neuronal signature was uncoupled from represented VEGF/endothelin vascular targets.
Cross-perturbation analysis rejected a strong Vezf1-like global neighbor and showed divergence from both data-driven and insulator-related comparators.
Acute P16 Vldlr loss produced no FDR-supported downstream nuclear transcriptome in any recovered juvenile neuronal class.
Measured Reelin-core perturbations and LDL-receptor-family comparators did not converge with the Vldlr null surface.
The unbiased Vldlr signature-neighbor search found no hidden transcriptional module.
The screen constrains VLDLR cerebellar-hypoplasia biology to developmental architecture rather than a maintained young-adult neuronal transcriptomic defect.
Acute Vps13a loss was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered juvenile neuronal panel.
Vps13a loss did not induce the expected autophagy, lysosomal, ISR/UPR, redox, BDNF, or synaptic receptor transcripts.
Endolysosomal and movement-disorder comparators responded where Vps13a stayed flat.
The represented VPS13 paralogs did not phenocopy an acute neuronal transcriptome either.
A whole-surface score search did not place Vps13a in a reproducible transcriptional perturbation module.
Vps13b was a strict whole-transcriptome null in all 20 recovered neuronal groups after P16 acute CRISPR perturbation.
The expected autophagy/lysosome mRNA program was absent after Vps13b perturbation, although lysosomal/autophagy perturbations can score in matched cell groups.
The represented VPS13 paralogs Vps13a and Vps13c were also flat and did not form a shared Vps13b-like signature.
An unbiased whole-surface signature scan found only near-zero positive and negative neighbors for Vps13b.
Direct Golgi/ERES VPS13B partners were absent as perturbation targets, and represented indirect Golgi/adaptor targets did not converge with Vps13b.
Vps13c loss was a pan-null downstream transcriptomic perturbation across all 22 recovered neuronal groups.
Vps13c did not induce a durable lysosome, autophagy, mitophagy, UPR/ISR, or IFN-STING RNA program in any measured group.
Rab7, Vps35, and Vps54 elicited endomembrane transcriptional responses where Vps13c stayed flat.
Vps13a and Vps13b did not phenocopy Vps13c or produce their own FDR<0.10 neuronal signatures.
The data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful Vps13c signature module.

Vps35 loss produced a sharply restricted transcriptional response: 30 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one Serac1 hit in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the other 20 measured groups.
The 151 TH Vps35 program hit receptor, excitability, calcium, and synaptic-neurite genes rather than a bulk lysosomal response.
Serac1 up-regulation was the only Vps35-dependent transcript in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
Rab7, the top whole-surface positive neighbor, partially reproduced the 151 TH Vps35 signature while adding a large adaptive lysosome/proteasome program that Vps35 lacked.
Vps35l/Retriever and Washc4 did not phenocopy Vps35 in the Vps35 responder groups.
The acute Vps35 loss signature did not recover the expected APP/BACE1/Sort1, autophagy-lysosome, mitochondrial MUL1/Mfn2, or LRRK2-Rab10 transcriptional programs.
Camta1 was the weak whole-surface negative neighbor and significantly opposed a subset of Vps35-up genes in 151 TH.
Acute Vps35l perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional program in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.

The Vps35l null did not collapse all endosomal trafficking biology: Rab7 and, more weakly, Vps35 produced FDR-level responses in the same thalamic group where Vps35l had 205 cells and zero downstream genes.
A model-wide signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Vps35l convergence or opposition: the best cosine was only 0.092 and the strongest anticorrelation was -0.047.

Vps41 produced a sparse, caudally biased transcriptional response: exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in each of 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 308 CB GABA, a weak sub-threshold trace in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other measured cortical, forebrain, thalamic, hypothalamic and interneuron groups.

The canonical part of the Vps41 response was a weak lysosomal compensation module: Mcoln1 was induced in 155 MB Glut and Dpp7 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and Rab7 perturbation independently induced the same two genes in the same cell groups.
direction_pattern: Mcoln1 and Dpp7 up after Vps41 and Rab7 perturbation

canonical_summary: 217 P MY Pineal Glut responded to Vps41 with an isolated, very large Idh1 induction rather than a corrected lysosomal-gene set.
308 CB GABA carried an isolated up-regulation of Timm17a, a mitochondrial inner-membrane import component, with no accompanying lysosomal FDR genes.

Cross-perturbation structure was Rab7-centered but shallow: Rab7 was the top positive score neighbor and the only comparator sharing Vps41 FDR genes, whereas Dctn1 was a broader sterol-biogenesis neighbor and Vps35, Vps53/Vps54, Vps13-family, Atg5, Becn1, Ctsb, Lamp2 and Tmem106b did not phenocopy Vps41.
direction_pattern: Rab7 partial convergence; other comparators rejected or divergent

canonical_summary: The expected TFEB/TFE3-autophagy transcriptional expansion after VPS41 inhibition was largely absent: Vps41 yielded only four FDR genes total and only two lysosomal/autophagy hits, Mcoln1 and Dpp7, across 22 measured groups.
Vps53 produced only three FDR<0.10 downstream calls across 21 measured neuronal groups, all up-regulated and confined to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
The strongest Vps53 responder was 191 MB P MY GABA, where Rhoq and Ddit3 were the only corrected downstream genes.
Vps53 up-regulated only Farp1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.

Vps54, the represented same-GARP-complex partner, had a 45-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Vps53 was weak in that thalamic group and Vps54 did not share Vps53's 005 or 191 responder genes.
