Vps53 did not activate a full UPR/ISR module, despite one Ddit3 hit in 191 MB P MY GABA and clear detectability of Ddit3/Chac1/Xbp1/Herpud1/Hspa5/Asns after Atp2a2 perturbation in the same dataset.

Other represented Golgi, endosome-to-TGN, and endolysosomal perturbations, including Tbc1d23, Stx16, Cog4, Cog5, Vps35, Vps35l, and Vps41, failed to converge on Vps53's Farp1/Rhoq/Ddit3 responder genes.
Acute Vps54 loss produced one FDR-scale neuronal response, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 45 downstream genes while 20 other measured cell groups had none.
The 151 Vps54 program is biased toward loss of mature neuronal signaling, peptide processing, and axon/neurite transcripts rather than induction of a canonical lysosomal rescue program.
Vps54 splits the 151 immediate-early axis: Egr1 is the strongest decreased gene whereas Jun is one of only eight up-regulated FDR genes.
Vps54 did not activate the UPR/ISR, proteasome, lysosomal hydrolase, or sphingolipid transcripts that a severe GARP trafficking collapse would be expected to secondarily expose to snRNA-seq.

The top data-driven positive neighbors of the Vps54 151 signature were Grin1, Pitpna, Atp6ap2, Vps53, and Rab7 by 45-gene cosine; Rab7, Grin1, Psmb4, Prpf6, and U2af2 shared many same-direction FDR genes on that restricted signature.
Rab7 most strongly shares the Vps54 151 down-shifted neuronal tail but extends to lysosomal, sterol, autophagy, PERK, and apoptosis genes that are absent after Vps54 perturbation.
The represented GARP/EARP subunit Vps53 continuously shadows the Vps54 45-gene vector but does not reach an FDR-scale Vps54 phenocopy.
Retromer/TGN-SNARE pathway neighbors Vps35, Stx16, and Stx5a failed to converge with Vps54 in the 151 signature even though Vps35 was itself active there.
The Vps54 151 transcriptome neither nominated sphingolipid-enzyme genes nor showed an opposite FDR-scale relationship to Sptlc2, Asah1, or Cert1 perturbations.
Vsx1 produced a tiny but FDR-controlled response restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA: Zc3h13 and Atp1b2 were both up-regulated, and no other measured cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.

The data-driven Vsx1 neighbors in 066 were single-anchor contrasts: Zbtb7a alone converged through Atp1b2 up-regulation, whereas Ogt, Hnrnpu, and Psmb4 opposed Vsx1 through Atp1b2 or Zc3h13 down-regulation embedded in broader signatures.
Vsx2 and other represented retinal/V2 transcription-factor relatives did not phenocopy the 066 Vsx1 signature; Vsx2 had 0 FDR genes in 066 and only one FDR gene across its whole 22-group surface.

The canonical Vsx1 loss programs were absent: retinal genes including Rcvrn, Neto1, Cabp5, Tacr3, Prkca, Grm6, Trpm1, and Vsx2 and embryonic V2 markers including Prox1, Insm1, Pax6, Lhx3, Lhx4, and Gata3 had 0 FDR<0.10 responses.
Vsx2 perturbation induced a singleton Il34 response in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
The Vsx2 perturbation was a near-null, cell-restricted singleton: 1 downstream gene in 1 of 22 measured cell groups, 21 null groups, and 215 MB Dopa missing.
Retinal/V2a transcription-factor relatives failed to phenocopy Vsx2 in the same measured brain groups.
Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Vsx2 neighbor: the top positive and negative real-gene correlations were only +0.0335 for Ndufb7 and -0.0186 for Npy5r.
The canonical retina program expected from Vsx2/Chx10 loss was absent from the measured brain-neuron surface.
Wac loss was transcriptionally active in 16 of 22 measured neuronal groups but was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba rather than in all Wac-expressing neurons.

The dominant Wac downstream direction was repression of neuronal and synaptic marker transcripts, recurring as Lgi3, Septin5, Ache, C1qtnf4, Eno2, Syp, and related receptor or transporter genes across cortical, thalamic, midbrain, GABAergic, and cerebellar responders.
Pvalb interneurons carried a coherent inhibitory/fast-spiking marker decrease after Wac loss, including Pvalb, Kcnab3, Gabrg2, Gabra1, Grin2d, and Syp down-regulation.
Large Wac responders induced RNA-processing, transcription, chromatin, and ubiquitin-conjugation factors, including Adarb1, Luc7l2, Msi2, Rbm4, Ube2b, Clk1, Srsf9, Wdr33, Cpsf6, Atrx, and Kmt2a.

The unbiased Wac signature neighbors were proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 and the chromatin corepressor Sin3a; they reproduced hundreds of Wac significant gene-by-cell features, mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

The expected mTORC1/autophagy arm of WAC biology was not recovered: core Map1lc3, Gabarap, Sqstm1, Ulk, Atg5/Becn1, Mtor, and Rptor transcripts were non-significant after Wac perturbation, and Mtor, Rptor, Atg5, and Becn1 perturbations were not Wac-like.
Zbtb7a and Uba5 were the top signed negative Wac neighbors, reversing many of the 151 TH Wac features such as Eno2, Ache, Vgf, Clk1, and Msi2.
Washc4 CRISPR produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any of the 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Expected WASH/Commander/Retromer, ER-stress, lysosomal-enzyme, and synaptic-module transcripts were not recovered after Washc4 perturbation.
Retromer Vps35, but not WASH-pathway Washc4 or Retriever Vps35l, produced a small thalamus-biased transcriptional response.
Washc4 had no meaningful data-driven positive or negative signature neighbors in the full perturbation universe.

Wdfy3 loss produced a sharply restricted postnatal neuronal response: 32 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only Stmn4 in 155 MB Glut, with the other 20 measured groups lacking robust downstream hits.

The main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program was a neuronal AP-1 / synaptic-vesicle / membrane downshift rather than a canonical autophagy transcriptome: Jun, Jund, Scg2, Chgb, Syt1, Syt11, Gpm6a, Tspan7, Kcnc2, and Kctd16 were all lower.
Stmn4 was the only Wdfy3 downstream gene recurrent across both detected responder groups, down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

Wdfy3 did not elicit the expected aggrephagy, mitophagy, lysosomal, or DVL3-Wnt transcriptional rebound, and targeted perturbations of Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Map1lc3a, Rb1cc1, Sqstm1, Htt, Vcp, Ctnnb1, and Lrp6 failed to phenocopy the Wdfy3 151/155 signature.

Dctn1 was the strongest FDR-supported positive neighbor of Wdfy3, matching 13 Wdfy3 features in the same direction across the thalamic and MB Glut responders, while adding a broad sterol/lipid response absent from Wdfy3.
Grin1 opposed rather than copied Wdfy3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 13 FDR<0.10 Wdfy3 features changing in the opposite direction under NMDAR loss.

Basal P16 Wdr26 loss generated a sharply non-cortical response: 7 of 21 measured cell groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, dominated by 308 CB GABA, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while 14 measured telencephalic/cortical groups had none.

A recurrent RNA-processing and nuclear-transport module is the most penetrant Wdr26 downstream signature: Srrm2 fell in every responder and Hnrnpu, Kpna1, Luc7l2, Ccnl2, Ddx24, Son, and Arglu1 were repeatedly lower.
Wdr26 converged with proteasome-subunit perturbations in diencephalic and midbrain responders: Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the top two same-direction FDR-overlap neighbors, especially in 066, 155, and 191.

Wdr26 loss reconfigured synaptic and ion-channel transcripts, from recurrent Kcna2, Scn1b, Atp1a3, Atp1b1, and Grin2b decreases to a broad cerebellar shift involving Cacna1g, Cacna1a, Grik1, Grid2, Grm7, Kcnt1, Grin2d, and Gria4.

A mitochondrial and amino-acid-metabolic arm was reduced after Wdr26 perturbation, with Nat8l down in four responders and Cyc1, Slc25a3, Samm50, Atp5d, Ndufb5, and Gls lower within the thalamic, midbrain, and pontomedullary signatures.
Col11a2 was one of the largest induced transcripts in Wdr26 responders, recurring in 110, 155, 191, and 308, accompanied by Ptprz1 induction and mixed Bcan and collagen-family changes.
Tsc2 was the top positive signed-score neighbor of Wdr26 and shared 133 same-direction versus 9 opposite robust Wdr26-signature features, with a purely same-direction 55-gene overlap in 308 CB GABA.

Canonical Wnt, MAPK/AP-1, and Gβγ/PI3K/Rac expectations were weakly and sparsely recovered: Axin2 was induced in 155 and 191 and Jun/Mapk genes appeared in 191 or 308, but represented pathway-node perturbations did not phenocopy Wdr26.
Ranbp2 was a cerebellar anti-neighbor: in 308 CB GABA it overlapped 153 Wdr26 significant genes and flipped the sign of 152 of them.

Wdr26 loss coupled its RNA/synaptic response to cytoskeletal and vesicle-trafficking remodeling, with recurrent Dync1h1, Actr1b, Hook2, Hap1, Pak3, Septin3, Stmn3/Stmn4, and cerebellar Kalrn/Arhgap26/Srgap2 changes.
Wdr37 loss was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The embryonic zebrafish cholesterol signal and the lymphocyte ER/oxidative-stress readout of Pacs1-Wdr37 disruption were absent after P16 Wdr37 CRISPR in neurons.
The WDR37-PACS1-PACS2 physical axis was jointly buffered in the acute neuronal CRISPR surface: Pacs2 was fully null and Pacs1 had only a single FDR<0.10 call.
The Wdr37 null was not a WD-repeat-family readout floor: Wdr26, another WD-repeat neurodevelopmental target, produced 3,128 corrected DEGs in matched groups where Wdr37 had none.
Whole-transcriptome signature-neighbor analysis found no coherent Wdr37 module: the strongest positive and negative score-vector cosines were only 0.035 and -0.029.
Acute P16 Wdr48 perturbation produced no adjusted downstream transcriptomic response in any of 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The USP1-UAF1 Fanconi/homologous-recombination branch did not appear as Fanconi, p53, or DNA-damage DE, and represented repair comparators Atr and Ddb2 were also null.
The USP46/AMPAR/GABA branch predicted from WDR48 biology was not recovered as Gria, Gabr, Gad, immediate-early, or UPR nuclear RNA changes.
Full-rank Wdr48 score-vector neighbors were near zero and failed as mechanistic comparators after direct DE-surface inspection.
Wdr48 did not produce a signature in the L5 ET cortical class despite WDR48/SPG60 being a corticospinal-motor-neuron disease candidate.
Acute Wnk1 loss-of-function was buffered at the steady-state mRNA level across every recovered neuronal cell group: 22 of 22 measured groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The represented WNK-SPAK-SLC12 pathway members did not recreate a common transcriptional module: Wnk3 had only three FDR<0.10 downstream genes in two groups, Stk39 had none in 21 recovered matched groups, and Slc12a2 had none in all 22 matched groups.

The all-target Wnk1 signature-neighbor search found no strong convergent or opposing partner: the best non-control positive cosine was 0.0439 and the most negative was -0.0222 over matched Wilcoxon-score vectors.

A postnatal central-neuron Wnk1 CRISPR loss-of-function null does not phenocopy the major WNK1 disease axes, which are kidney gain-of-WNK signaling in PHAII and HSN2 sensory-neuron or injury-evoked chloride signaling.
Wnk3 produced only 3 robust downstream DE genes in 2 of 22 measured cell groups: Stim1 down and Syt3 up in 052 Pvalb Gaba, and Ppp2cb down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The canonical WNK-SPAK/OSR1-CCC pathway was absent as a transcriptional program after Wnk3 perturbation, and Wnk1, Stk39, and Slc12a2 perturbations were themselves flat.
In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Wnk3 loss down-regulated Stim1 and up-regulated Syt3, suggesting a small calcium-store and synaptic-vesicle adjustment rather than direct CCC transcript regulation.
Wnk3 loss down-regulated the PP2A catalytic beta subunit gene Ppp2cb in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Sparse signature neighbors centered on one Wnk3 sentinel each: Ctnnb1 matched Ppp2cb down, whereas Uba5 and Elp1 up-regulated Ppp2cb and Psmb4, Psmc1, and Ranbp2 down-regulated Syt3.
Postnatal Wnk3 CRISPR did not trigger a broad transporter, stress, or synaptic-transcript collapse despite human WNK3 loss-of-function neurodevelopmental disease.
Acute Wrn loss produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
The Wrn rank signature had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor among the 1,772 other perturbations visible in the parquet.
A canonical DNA-damage/p53 secondary program expected after consequential WRN failure was absent.
Normal juvenile neurons did not show the lethality-like transcriptional collapse that makes WRN attractive in MSI-high cancers.
Wt1 was a uniform postnatal neuronal non-responder: none of 22 measured cell groups had even one downstream gene below FDR 0.10.
The embryonic WT1-TET2-EPO program was absent after postmitotic Wt1 perturbation.
Basal Wt1 loss did not reproduce the published hippocampal WT1 plasticity phenotype as an immediate-early or neurotrophic RNA program.
Neither unbiased neighbors nor WT1 literature comparators converged on the Wt1 null surface.
Wwox loss was a pan-null transcriptional perturbation in the recovered P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen: 22 measured cell groups and 371,818 target-gene tests yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
A whole-universe Wilcoxon-score neighbor scan found no real Wwox similarity module: the largest absolute Pearson correlation to any other target was only 0.054.
Represented WWOX-linked ERBB/NRG, GSK3β, SMAD and PPxY-interactor perturbations also failed to reveal a Wwox-like postnatal neuronal transcriptional axis.
The same screen could produce large signatures in Wwox-flat neuronal groups, as Wdr26 and Ranbp2 had hundreds-to-thousands of FDR<0.10 genes in subcortical and cerebellar classes where Wwox had zero.

The null P16 CRISPR surface should not be used as evidence against neuronal WWOX gene replacement; the literature rescue phenotype requires neuron-wide WWOX restoration in Wwox-null neonates and is read out by seizures, myelin and survival rather than by a sparse acute DE signature.
Acute Xiap loss-of-function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured survivor neuronal class.
The XIAP-NOD2/TNFR inflammatory signaling arm was not engaged in the neuron-enriched basal brain screen.
Xiap perturbation did not trigger a Birc2/Birc3 transcriptional IAP-paralog rebound in postmitotic neurons.
Whole-surface signature neighbors of Xiap were near-zero and rejected as a real convergent module after FDR-level comparator testing.
The Xiap null surface does not phenocopy injury-neuroprotection or SMAC-mimetic cancer contexts, because the screen lacked apoptotic challenge and showed no preterminal stress signature.
Xpo7 loss induced a single cerebellar-GABA hit, Vps41, without a broader HOPS or TFEB lysosomal module.
The Xpo7 perturbation did not recover Hedgehog/Gli derepression in any neuronal group.
Direct Vps35 and Ppm1g perturbations were transcriptionally separable from Xpo7 loss.
Ranbp2/Nup358 drove a broad neuronal transcriptome while Xpo7 stayed sparse.
The schizophrenia-linked Xpo7 prior did not appear as an acute, pan-neuronal SCHEMA-family transcriptional module.
Xpr1 loss produced a uniformly FDR-flat neuronal transcriptome in all 13 recovered cell groups, with no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 despite measurable Xpr1 rows and a median self logFC of -0.394.

The literature-obvious phosphate node was flat as a transcriptional module: Slc20a2, the PP-InsP/XPR1 regulator Ppip5k2, and the vascular PFBC comparator Pdgfrb all had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their represented neuronal surfaces and did not converge with Xpr1.

Transcriptome-wide neighbor search found no meaningful Xpr1 signature neighbor: the largest positive and negative score cosines were only 0.02577 for Pax4 and -0.02751 for Uba5, and the six retested biological neighbors either had no matched FDR signature or a strong Uba5/Ufc1 stress program lacking in Xpr1.

Xpr1-perturbed neurons did not activate phosphate-importer, mineralization, reactive-glial, lysosomal, UPR, ISR, or autophagy marker transcripts; Ddit3, Atf4, Hspa5, Sqstm1, Spp1, Runx2, Alpl, Col1a1, Gfap, Aif1, Lgals3, Lamp1, Lyz2, and Slc20a2 were all FDR=1 across the 13 Xpr1 cell groups.

Xrn1 produced real FDR<0.10 downstream responses only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with no robust downstream genes in 19 other measured groups and no rows in 215 MB Dopa or 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
The two Xrn1 signatures were nearly direction-balanced, not globally up-regulated: 151 had 15 up and 14 down genes, and 155 had 11 up and 10 down genes at FDR<0.10.
Xrn1 responders down-regulated lysosomal, V-ATPase, and ER-lumen genes, including Psap, Ap3m1, Atp6v0c, Hyou1, Hsp90b1, Atp6v0e2, Atp6v0a1, Cyp46a1, and Tmem59l.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut uniquely up-regulated an adhesion/synaptic/cAMP block containing Adgrb1, Rap1gap2, Ppp1r9b, Rims2, Adcy1, Agap3, Shank1, Nt5c2, Nsmf, and Hrh3.
155 MB Glut up-regulated RNA and chromatin regulators including Pnrc1, Dhx9, Dnmt3a, Brd2, Pura, Chd2, Myt1l, Apc2, and Maged1.
Tpr, Cdc40, U2af2, and Thoc1 were the robust positive cross-perturbation neighbors of Xrn1 across the 50 significant Xrn1 group-gene features.
Rab7 and Elp1 opposed rather than copied the Xrn1 signature, with zero same-direction shared FDR genes and 10 or 9 opposing Xrn1 group-gene calls, respectively.
Measured miRNA, CCR4-NOT, and NMD perturbations did not phenocopy Xrn1: Dicer1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b, Cnot1, and Upf3b were flat or weak and shared at most one Xrn1 FDR gene.
Xrn1 did not induce a canonical ISR, IFN, or autophagy-transcription program in its two responder groups.

The neuronal Xrn1 signature did not reproduce the interferon/PKR pharmacodynamic direction being explored for XRN1 cancer targeting and instead exposed a narrow neuronal endolysosomal/synaptic footprint.
Xylt1 loss produced a pan-neuronal null nuclear transcriptome rather than a stress, proteostasis, or synaptic transcriptional program.
Represented GAG-pathway perturbations did not form a shared Xylt1-like module.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search placed Xylt1 near the origin of the perturbation space.
The XYLT1 disease axis is displaced away from acute postmitotic neuronal gene regulation.

Yeats2 is transcriptome-flat across the juvenile postmitotic neuronal surface: no measured cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene, despite direct measurement of the Yeats2 transcript in every recovered group.
The direct ATAC/YEATS comparator layer was mostly not present in the perturbation panel, and the represented H3-acetylation neighbors did not phenocopy Yeats2.
The model-visible universe found no meaningful signed transcriptomic neighbor for Yeats2.
Loss-of-function signatures across represented FAME repeat-locus host genes do not converge on a Yeats2-like neuronal state.
Ylpm1 produced a small, cell-restricted gene-abundance response, with 20 downstream FDR<0.10 hits across only 4 of 20 measured groups and 16 of those hits in 155 MB Glut.
In 155 MB Glut, Ylpm1 loss lowered the SR splicing-factor transcripts Srsf6 and Srsf5 and raised Atxn2l.
Responder cells showed a small ubiquitin-ligase arm: Shprh, Dcaf11, and Ube2o were up in 155 MB Glut, and Fbxl17 was up in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
Inha was down in both 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, making it the only recurrent downstream Ylpm1 FDR<0.10 gene.
The postnatal neuronal Ylpm1 perturbation did not induce the Tert, shelterin, or cell-cycle program expected from proliferative YLPM1 models.

The strongest data-derived Ylpm1 relationships were non-obvious: full-profile neighbors were very weak, whereas a restricted FDR-coordinate comparison selected Tpr as the top convergent perturbation and Setd1a as the top anti-neighbor.
Canonical RNA-processing target perturbations were far broader than Ylpm1 and only partly overlapped its significant genes; Son did not phenocopy Ylpm1 in the matched groups.
Ylpm1 was significantly down at the transcript level in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
Yme1l1 loss did not create a robust cell-autonomous nuclear RNA signature in any recovered postmitotic brain neuron group.
The YME1L-to-OPA1 biochemical edge was not transcriptionally transmitted: Opa1 was a robust comparator responder in matched cells, but Yme1l1 had zero shared FDR genes.
Yme1l1 did not induce the Opa1-like ATF4/ISR amino-acid program that the same screen detected through Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Slc7a5, Cars, Mars1 and one-carbon genes after Opa1 perturbation.
Unbiased cross-perturbation search found no strong hidden Yme1l1 signature neighbor.
Acute P16 Ywhae perturbation produced a pan-measured downstream transcriptomic null: no cell group had any non-Ywhae gene below FDR 0.10.
The measured 14-3-3 paralogs Ywhag and Ywhaz also lacked a broad single-isoform downstream program, rather than converging with Ywhae on a shared neuronal RNA module.

Canonical YWHAE migration and morphology effectors were uncoupled from the P16 snRNA phenotype: Ndel1, Dcx, Pafah1b1, Ctnnd2, Rho-family, Limk1/Cfl1, Syp, and Snca transcripts all stayed at FDR 1.0 after Ywhae perturbation.

A data-driven whole-universe neighbor search did not reveal a hidden Ywhae-like module: the strongest non-safe positive cosines were only +0.031 and +0.030 and the strongest non-safe anticorrelations were about -0.016.

Measured RAF-family pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Ywhae: Braf had a small thalamic/hypothalamic Vgf-Ptpn5-Atp2a2-Unc13a response, whereas Raf1 and Ywhae were flat and both RAF cosines to Ywhae were near zero.
Ywhag loss produced a single near-threshold downstream transcriptomic event: Vgf upregulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
Ywhag perturbation did not elicit the canonical 14-3-3γ migration, cytoskeletal, GABA_A/NMDAR, BDNF-Syn1, immediate-early, or dopaminergic transcripts at FDR<0.10.
The represented 14-3-3 paralogs Ywhae and Ywhaz did not phenocopy the Ywhag/Vgf signature, and Ywhag loss did not transcriptionally induce other 14-3-3 family genes.
Global signed-score neighbors were weak; at the only Ywhag responder, Eef2 converged on Vgf up while Grin2b opposed it.
P16 mosaic CRISPR LoF flatness should not be used to deprioritize YWHAG disease biology or to certify 14-3-3γ inhibition as transcriptionally silent therapy.
Ywhaz loss produced a one-gene actin/synaptic-cytoskeletal signature, Pfn2 up-regulation, only in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
The assayed 14-3-3 paralogs did not phenocopy each other after P16 CRISPR: Ywhaz, Ywhag, and Ywhae were all nearly flat, and their lone hits were in different cortical IT groups.
Ywhaz did not induce the canonical apoptosis, FOXO/IEG, UPR/ISR, or autophagy/lysosome programs that might have been expected from a 14-3-3ζ signaling LoF.
No data-driven non-safe perturbation converged strongly with Ywhaz across the whole measured signature.
Yy1 loss produced a posteriorly enriched neuronal transcriptome rather than a pan-neuronal response.
A compact, recurrent YY1 core crossed many otherwise small responders.
Yy1 perturbation rewired Polycomb/chromatin transcripts with Pcgf2 down and Ring1 up instead of a uniform PRC shutdown.
YY1 loss repeatedly affected RNA-processing genes.
Posterior YY1 responders contained a vesicle and endolysosomal-trafficking arm.
Several broad responders down-regulated excitability and synaptic genes.
The postnatal Yy1 metabolic response did not recapitulate the embryonic ribosome/biosynthetic collapse.
Postmitotic Yy1 loss induced a small chromosomal/DNA-repair-like signal without a p53-Cdkn1a arrest signature.
Data-driven signature search placed Yy1 closest to BRD4/CHD8/PHF12/WAC/ADNP-class chromatin perturbations, not to a measured YY1 paralog or PRC core member.
Proteasome-subunit perturbations were the top broad, non-textbook positive sparse neighbors of Yy1.
SETD1A, ZBTB7A, THOC1 and SIN3A diverged from Yy1 despite hitting the same posterior groups.
ASH1L, EP300, KMT2A, CREBBP and CTCF did not phenocopy Yy1 in the same assay universe.
Zbtb10 CRISPR loss produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any recovered postmitotic neuronal class.
The cancer-derived ZBTB10/RINZF-Sp angiogenic/survival circuit was not derepressed in postnatal neurons.
The ZBTB-family comparison separates Zbtb10 from the broad Zbtb7a neuronal program and from smaller Zbtb18/Zbtb38 effects.
An unbiased score-vector search found no meaningful phenocopy or anti-phenocopy for Zbtb10.
Acute P16 Zbtb16 loss produced a genome-wide transcriptional zero across the recovered neuronal brain surface.
The embryonic deep-layer-corticogenesis and FGF-neural-progenitor program is not reactivated by Zbtb16 CRISPR in juvenile postmitotic forebrain neurons.
The adult PVH/ARC energy-deficit axis was not captured as a basal Zbtb16 transcriptional response in the hypothalamus-containing groups.
PLZF-linked Sin3/HDAC repression is not rate-limited by Zbtb16 in these postmitotic neurons.
BTB-ZF factors are not interchangeable in the neuronal screen: Zbtb7a was a broad responder, Zbtb18/Zbtb38 were weakly focal, and Zbtb16/Zbtb20/Zbtb10/Zbtb21 were flat.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no coherent positive or negative Zbtb16 module.
Zbtb18 loss induced a recurrent Pxdn-positive extracellular-matrix marker in only four of 22 measured cell groups.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut responder added Endou, Clstn2, and Man2a2 to the shared Pxdn response.
Postnatal Zbtb18 loss did not derepress the expected Pax6/Neurog2/Neurod1/Rnd2/Id cortical-neurogenesis program.
Zbtb7a, not the textbook Zbtb16/Zbtb20 family comparators, was the top same-direction Zbtb18 signature neighbor.
Rora and Ctnnb1 opposed separable branches of the 151 Zbtb18 signature, while Ehmt1 shared only Endou up-regulation.
Tbr1 stayed transcriptionally active in several postnatal cortical groups where Zbtb18 was flat.
Juvenile mosaic Zbtb18 LoF produced a sparse marker response rather than a transcriptomic model of ZBTB18-related malformation disease.

Sparse P16 Zbtb20 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every neuronal cell group recovered for this target: 22 measured groups and 371,796 downstream Wilcoxon tests produced zero genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected Zbtb20 CA1/isocortical repression module was absent: Cux1, Cux2, Fezf2, Foxp2, Mef2c, Rorb, Satb2, Sox5, Tbr1, Tle4 and Zfpm2, together with CA1 or gliogenic markers, had 0 of 396 Zbtb20 tests at FDR<0.10.

Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Zbtb20 neighbor: after group-by-gene standardization across the full parquet, the top cosine similarities were Snta1 0.018, Scamp5 0.016 and Gucy2e 0.016, and the most negative was Gabra3 -0.017.

The screen could detect related transcription-factor perturbations in the same matched cell groups, but they did not converge with Zbtb20: Zbtb7a produced 2,639 FDR<0.10 genes and Mef2c, Prox1 and Tbr1 produced 109, 64 and 28 respectively across the 22 Zbtb20-matched groups, whereas Zbtb20 produced zero.

The null surface is consistent with Primrose-syndrome biology being poorly modeled by simple postnatal neuronal LoF: the disease is linked to heterozygous ZBTB20 variants, many described as dominant-negative missense alleles, while the assay introduces sparse CRISPR LoF after neuronal specification.
Zbtb21 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq signature in any of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups.

CREB/CBP and cohesin/ZBTB comparators were not globally inert, so the Zbtb21 zero is pathway-selective rather than a universal failure of these cell groups to respond to transcriptional or chromatin regulators.
A prior-free full-universe neighbor search found no convincing positive or negative Zbtb21 signature neighbor.

P16 CRISPR loss of Zbtb38 produced a sparse postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: only 3 downstream FDR<0.10 genes distributed across 2 of 22 measured cell groups, with every self-transcript test at FDR=1.0.
The clearest responder was a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-signature containing Msra and Abhd12b.
008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut showed an isolated Rcn2 up-regulation.
Whole-surface score neighbors were essentially at the noise floor and did not share any responder genes in the two Zbtb38 effect groups.

Represented BTB-ZF family perturbations did not phenocopy Zbtb38; Zbtb7a was a broad neuronal responder yet had a whole-surface cosine of -0.0004 with Zbtb38 and no shared Rcn2/Msra/Abhd12b FDR genes.
The expected methyl-CpG/CtBP and embryonic Sox2/Nanog axes were uncoupled from the observed P16 neuronal Zbtb38 signature.

Zbtb7a loss was a broad but graded postmitotic neuronal perturbation: 22 of 23 measured groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, whereas 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the only FDR-level nonresponder.

The cancer-cell glycolysis target axis was recovered only partially: Pfkp and Slc2a3 were de-repressed in the strongest thalamic/Pvalb responders, with Eno2 recurrently up, but the full HK2/PKM-like Warburg cassette was not a pan-neuronal output.
Zbtb7a loss rewired endomembrane and lysosome-related transcripts, with Rab34/Cd63/Gaa/Ctsl/Gprasp1/2 recurrently up and Stx16/Ppip5k1/Gpr108/Tspan17/Tmem106c/P2rx4 recurrently down.

A synaptic and excitability layer accompanied the trafficking response: Cacng7, Syn1, Atp8a2, Dnm1, and Kcnab/Kcn channel genes fell in high responders, while Akap5, Nlgn2, Stx1a, and Ptprn rose in selected classes.
High Zbtb7a responders acquired a neurosecretory/peptidergic component, led by Vgf, Pnoc, Ptprn, and Stx1a in thalamic, Pvalb, MGE, CTX-CGE, and midbrain groups.

The nearest FDR-backed positive signatures were not ZBTB7A paralogs but UFMylation/proteostasis perturbations: Uba5 and Ufc1, with Tpr as another broad positive neighbor, shared hundreds of Zbtb7a-directional genes.
Canonical fetal-globin partners did not phenocopy Zbtb7a in neurons: Chd4 weakly overlapped in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Bcl11a, Bcl11b, Mbd2, and Gatad2b were essentially flat.

The postnatal neuronal response was uncoupled from the classic ARF/p53/MYC and HSP90-KLHL20 circuitry: Trp53, Cdkn2a, Myc, Hsp90ab1, Klhl20, Pparg, and Ppargc1a perturbations were flat or near-flat and did not reconstruct the Zbtb7a surface.

The top negative neighbors Chd8 and Yy1 inverted parts of the Zbtb7a signature, most visibly for Usp11, Wsb1, Rsrp1, and Ache, arguing that Zbtb7a is not a generic chromatin-factor loss-of-function response.
Zc3h14 loss produced a narrow, postmitotic steady-state RNA response in only five of 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
The two strongest responder glutamatergic groups changed RNA-maturation genes in the direction of a compact nuclear poly(A)/3′-processing feedback.
Zcchc18 was the recurrent positive marker of the Zc3h14 response.
The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response included a small endomembrane acidification/trafficking branch.
Zc3h14 decreased Agrn in midbrain glutamatergic neurons but did not reproduce a canonical Agrn-Lrp4-MuSK pathway signature.
Inha induction nominates a single-cell-state neuroendocrine/TGF-β-family output of Zc3h14 loss in 155 MB Glut.
Wdr26, not a canonical ZC3H14 partner, was the top positive data-driven neighbor and shared the midbrain Zcchc18/Pabpn1/Cstf2 module.
Zc3h14 did not phenocopy the measurable THO/TREX and cleavage-polyadenylation comparators.
Fragile-X/Ataxin-2 relatives measured in the screen were largely flat where Zc3h14 responded.
The apparent top negative neighbor, Flrt3, was rejected after full-surface follow-up.
Zdhhc17 induced a single robust downstream hit, Tubb3 down, only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
155 MB Glut showed significant Zdhhc17 self-transcript reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
Canonical HIP14 substrate and synaptic receptor mRNAs were absent from the Zdhhc17 FDR<0.10 surface.
Acute Htt and Zdhhc17 perturbations diverged: Htt produced sterol/lipid genes whereas Zdhhc17 produced Tubb3 only.
Dlg4/Psd95 was downstream-flat like Zdhhc17, whereas NMDAR-subunit perturbations generated measurable RNA responses.
The data-driven neighbor search found only near-zero positive neighbors and a broad Uba5 negative neighbor.
Zeb1 loss was almost silent in most postmitotic brain neurons but reproducibly activated a small thalamic/midbrain-enriched module.
The main Zeb1 transcriptomic output is de-repression of an epithelial junction, polarity and vesicle-trafficking cassette.
Ctbp1 perturbation partially phenocopied the Zeb1 module in the same thalamic groups.
The expected paralog and upstream EMT/TGF-beta pathway neighbors did not phenocopy Zeb1.
Postnatal Zeb1 loss did not induce the canonical embryonic neural-progenitor or full epithelial MET target set.
Whole-transcriptome global signature neighbors were numerically weak and were not accepted as biological phenocopies.
Zeb1 did not look like a generic neuronal stress, proteasome-bounce-back or synaptic-downregulation perturbation.
Zeb2 responded in only four of 22 measured neuronal groups, with 11 of the 15 total FDR<0.10 downstream entries concentrated in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
P16 Zeb2 loss in Pvalb neurons induced a mixed terminal-state signature rather than the embryonic Nkx2-1/Unc5b guidance program.
direction_pattern: Rasd2/Plcl1/Patj up; Dlx6/Dcx/Zfp536 down; embryonic guidance genes absent

canonical_summary: Patj was the only recurrent Zeb2-induced gene, rising in both L4/5 IT and Pvalb neurons and aligning with a ZEB-family polarity/junction module seen for Zeb1 and Ctbp1 in other groups.
direction_pattern: junction/polarity genes up after loss of ZEB-family repression

canonical_summary: The non-Pvalb responder groups contained only marker-sized signatures: Otof up and Phyhip down in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Slf2 up in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
direction_pattern: Otof and Slf2 up; Phyhip down

canonical_summary: Canonical ZEB/SMAD/NuRD relatives did not phenocopy the acute Zeb2 signature in matched responder groups.
The unbiased nearest-neighbor search found only near-zero full-surface correlations, and broad Eef2/Psmb4/Zbtb7a perturbations overlapped the Zeb2 hits only sparsely.
Expected Wnt/Sfrp1, Ntf3/Fgf9, Ninein, netrin-guidance, BMP/SMAD, and EMT genes were not recovered after postnatal Zeb2 perturbation.
Zeb2 was not tested in 215 MB Dopa, the group closest to the published dopaminergic axon-growth model, while Pvalb neurons were the strongest measured responders.
Zfat produced a two-gene downstream surface restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with Setd1a up in 151 and D6Wsu163e down in 155.
The only robust thalamic Zfat downstream gene was the H3K4 methyltransferase Setd1a, and Setd1a perturbation itself strongly affected the same thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
Brd4 and Setd1a perturbations generated broad signatures in the same responder bins in which Zfat generated only one gene per group.
CA1/DG and cerebellar GABA bins were null despite published Zfat reporter signal in CA1 pyramidal and Purkinje cells.
The Tal1/Lmo2/Gata1 blood-island program and the FoxO1/Akt/Brpf1 immune-survival program were not recovered after neuronal Zfat perturbation.
The top genome-wide Zfat signature neighbors had absolute cosine below 0.026 and did not reproduce the two Zfat downstream genes in matched responder groups.
Zfhx2 produced a single weak downstream hit, Nt5c3 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
The central Zfhx2 perturbation did not recover the DRG pain/neuropeptide genes Gal, Sst, Gfra3, and Ptgir, and represented pain comparators Gal, Ntrk1, Trpa1, and Trpv1 did not phenocopy it.
A model-wide Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found only near-zero Zfhx2 correlations, and the top apparent neighbor Hspa5 did not share the 009 Nt5c3 response.
Zfhx2 loss caused no detectable mRNA rebound of the related homeobox factors Zfhx3 or Zfhx4.
Zfp106 loss produced an isolated Palm up-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
The direct RNA-binding-network comparator Tardbp was active where Zfp106 was almost flat and shared no FDR<0.10 downstream feature with Zfp106.
Canonical ZFP106-null mitochondrial, Rtn4/Nogo, and RNA-splicing-factor total-expression programs were not recovered in the postnatal brain screen.
Zfp148 loss produced an FDR-significant transcriptome only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 14 downstream genes, and was flat in the other 20 measured neuronal groups.

The Zfp148 thalamic signature converged on an RNA-splicing/nuclear-speckle axis: Srrm2, Srsf9, and Luc7l2 were down, and the top same-direction restricted-signature neighbors were Rnpc3, Tnpo3, and U2af2 perturbations.
Zfp148 knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also down-regulated a neuronal adhesion, vesicle, and excitability module including Cacnb3, Slitrk5, Ptprn, Syngr3, Ly6h, Afdn, and Rasgrp2.

The canonical Zfp148-to-ARF/p53/cell-cycle program was absent: no assayed p53-response or proliferation transcript reached FDR<0.10 in any Zfp148 group, and Trp53 or Cdkn2a perturbation did not phenocopy Zfp148 in the thalamic responder.
Rora, Zbtb7a, and Huwe1 were the strongest restricted anti-neighbors of Zfp148 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, reversing pieces of the Ypel4/Ly6h/Rasgrp2/Ptprn/Luc7l2 signature.
Zfp160 acute loss of function produced no corrected downstream transcriptomic response in any of 18 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The IEC ZNF160-to-TLR4 repression axis was silent: Zfp160 perturbation did not up-regulate Tlr4 or TLR4/NF-kappaB effector transcripts, and Tlr4 itself was flat as a perturbation target.
Zfp160 did not phenocopy a core KRAB/KAP1 heterochromatin effector: Setdb1 had corrected DE in 9 of the 18 matched groups whereas Zfp160 had none.
A universe-wide Wilcoxon-score neighbor scan found no credible Zfp160 convergence module; the strongest positive and negative correlations were only |r|<=0.0264.
Zfp182 loss produced an almost completely buffered protein-coding snRNA-seq response across recovered postmitotic neuronal groups.
Wdr33 down-regulation is the sole Zfp182-associated FDR<0.10 event and is restricted to 191 MB P MY GABA.
The expected KRAB effector axis did not phenocopy Zfp182: Setdb1 and Chd4 were active elsewhere but shared no FDR<0.10 genes with Zfp182.
The full Zfp182 signature had no substantive data-driven neighbor in the screen.
No interferon, ISR/UPR, heat-shock, or AP-1 secondary stress program accompanied Zfp182 perturbation.
Zfp1 produced no downstream gene-level DE genes at FDR<0.10 in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups after P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR loss of function.

The represented KRAB/H3K9me3 effector Setdb1 diverged from Zfp1: Setdb1 perturbation yielded 45 FDR<0.10 genes in 9 of 22 measured groups, whereas the matched Zfp1 vector had zero FDR<0.10 genes and a Setdb1-Zfp1 score correlation of only 0.005.

A full transcriptome-by-cell-group similarity search found no meaningful Zfp1 neighbor: the strongest positive score correlation was Adam10 at r=0.0308 and the strongest negative was Wdr26 at r=-0.0130, with near-null Safe_target perturbations among the extremes.

Zfp236 loss produced a narrow postnatal neuronal transcriptome: 13 of 22 measured cell groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the only multi-dozen-gene response was 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Ogt was the dominant recurrent Zfp236-responsive transcript, decreasing in 12 of the 13 FDR-positive Zfp236 cell groups.
Eif4a2, a translation-initiation factor, was repeatedly decreased with Ogt and reached FDR<0.10 in nine Zfp236 cell groups.
Cpt1c down-regulation marked the ventral/hypothalamic-thalamic and midbrain branch of the Zfp236 signature.
The strongest thalamic/midbrain Zfp236 response added a chromatin/RNA-processing layer, including Kmt5b down in 151, 155, and 191 and Kdm5b up in 110 and 151.
The HBP enzyme Gfpt1 was the cleanest pathway neighbor of Zfp236: it shared eight same-direction restricted-signature hits and no opposite hits, driven by Ogt down in six matched groups.
Perturbing major downstream genes did not recreate the non-self Zfp236 signature: Ogt, Eif4a2, Cpt1c and Gdi1 targets had zero exact FDR<0.10 non-self overlaps with the 56-gene Zfp236 signature.
The KRAB/heterochromatin comparator Setdb1 and brain ZFP comparator Zfp536 did not phenocopy Zfp236 on its restricted signature.
The data-driven negative neighbors Ctcf, Elp1, and Setd1a drove several Zfp236-signature genes in the opposite direction, most clearly Ogt up where Zfp236 drove Ogt down.
Zfp266 perturbation produced a singleton Hmgcs1 increase in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
The B1-SINE / OSKM reprogramming program expected from Zfp266 loss was absent from postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
Setdb1 and Chd4 perturbations responded in matched neurons without converging on Zfp266.
The top full-score neighbors of Zfp266 had near-zero cosine similarity and no FDR overlap with its Hmgcs1 hit.
Zfp280c loss is transcriptionally buffered across postnatal neuronal nuclei, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 call among 355025 downstream tests across 21 measured groups.
Fam118a is a narrow, low-confidence candidate reporter for Zfp280c perturbation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
Zfp280c does not phenocopy CTCF/cohesin, SMCHD1, or ATR-family DDR comparators in this postmitotic-neuron assay.
Data-driven positive and negative neighbors of Zfp280c are extremely weak, so the one-gene Zfp280c response does not define a reusable cross-perturbation module.
Zfp280d loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 18 measured neuronal groups.
The data-driven Zfp280d score signature sits at the noise floor rather than in a strong convergent module.
Matched chromatin regulators Setdb1, Chd4, and Gatad2b generated selective neuronal DE surfaces that Zfp280d did not share.
The represented Zfp280-family/domain comparators, Zfp280c and Pogz, also failed to reveal an acute matched neuronal program.
Acute P16 Zfp292 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 recovered NeuN+ neuronal classes.
Full-surface Wilcoxon score comparison found no substantive Zfp292 signature neighbor; the strongest positive and negative gene-target correlations were Tsc2 at r=0.034 and Zfp266 at r=-0.019.

Rlf and Bptf, the represented literature-obvious Zfp292-related comparators, do not phenocopy Zfp292: Rlf had 3 significant genes, Bptf had 159, and both were uncorrelated with Zfp292 across matched groups.
Zfp322a loss of function produced an all-null downstream transcriptome in every recovered NeuN+ neuronal group.
The embryonic stem-cell Zfp322a program fails to fire after P16 perturbation in postmitotic neurons.
Literature-obvious Oct4/Sox2/Zfx/E2F/Myc-axis comparators do not converge with Zfp322a in the neuronal screen.
The unbiased signature-neighbor search nominated only extremely weak positive and negative neighbors, all of which were null or near-null on direct query.
The human ZNF322A/c-MYC cancer-stemness axis did not appear after Zfp322a loss in normal postmitotic mouse neurons.
Zfp341 loss of function was an all-group FDR-null perturbation in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons: every one of the 23 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The expected Zfp341-to-Stat3/Th17 transcriptional program was absent: Stat3, Stat1, Rorc, IL-6/IL-21/IL-23/IL-17 receptor genes, and sparse Il17a/Il17f rows never reached FDR<0.10 after Zfp341 perturbation, and matched STAT-family perturbations also failed to produce a neuronal downstream signature.

Whole-transcriptome signature search did not uncover a cryptic Zfp341-like neuronal module: the best positive score correlation was Grm7 at only r=0.0281 and the most negative was Crebbp at r=-0.0196.
Among Th17-obvious transcriptional comparators, Rora—but not Zfp341 or Rorc—showed a robust neuronal phenotype, with 363 of its 365 downstream genes concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Acute postnatal Zfp397-targeting CRISPR was transcriptionally silent in every recovered neuronal group: 22/23 groups were measured and none contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
Zfp397 lacked a robust transcriptomic neighbor: the strongest positive and negative score-cosine neighbors were all near zero.
Measured SCAN/zinc-finger relatives did not phenocopy Zfp397 as a coherent family module in this assay.
Acute postnatal Zfp423 loss produced real downstream signal in only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA, with 205 and 10 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, respectively.
The main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature rewired thalamic subtype and neurotransmission markers, with Ntsr1, Drd2 and Prkcd up and Grin2c, Grid2ip, Syt13 and Slc12a5 down.
Zfp423 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut bidirectionally changed cell-surface and extracellular-matrix genes.
A mixed ER and glycoprotein-processing module accompanied the 151 thalamic Zfp423 response.
Only a narrow ciliary or ciliopathy-adjacent signal was recovered: Dzip1 and Anks6 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Cfap100 increased in 308 CB GABA.
Zfp423 perturbation in 308 CB GABA yielded a 10-gene, mostly upregulated cerebellar GABA signature containing Rab37, Gusb, Cfap100, Rnd2 and Notum.
Known or obvious Zfp423 relatives did not phenocopy the matched Zfp423 response.
Uba5, Tpr and Sin3a were the strongest significant-overlap neighbors of the Zfp423 FDR signature, but they were much broader and only partially directional.
Zfp451 loss was buffered across the recovered P16-to-P37/44 neuronal panel: every measured group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected PML, TOP2, p53, ISR, and heat-shock secondary stress programs were absent after Zfp451 perturbation.
The ESC ZFP451-SATB2 differentiation axis did not reappear as a maintenance program in juvenile cortical-glutamatergic neurons.
The same screen separated Zfp451 from other SUMO E3 biology: Ranbp2 was an active neuronal perturbation, whereas Zfp451 and Nsmce2 were flat.
The cross-perturbation nearest-neighbor map provided no strong hidden Zfp451 module.
P16 neuronal Zfp462 loss did not reactivate the embryonic mesendoderm or Pbx1-Hoxb8 programs expected from early developmental Zfp462 loss.
The G9A/GLP partner Ehmt1 and the chromatin ATPase Chd4 produced thalamic and midbrain signatures that Zfp462 did not share.
Genome-wide signature-neighbor analysis found no meaningful Zfp462 convergence or anti-convergence module.
P16 CRISPR loss of Zfp521 produced a pan-flat postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: every measured group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

The close paralog Zfp423 did not phenocopy Zfp521. Zfp423 had 215 FDR<0.10 downstream genes, concentrated in thalamic and cerebellar groups, whereas Zfp521 had 0 and a Zfp423/Zfp521 score correlation of only 0.0278.
The ES-cell Zfp521-p300 neuroectodermal program was absent after P16 Zfp521 perturbation: Sox1, Sox2, Sox3, Pax6, Ebf1-3, and endogenous Zfp423 never passed FDR<0.10.
The LGE/striatal group did not recover a Zfp521-Ebf1 medium-spiny-neuron program; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA had 0 FDR<0.10 genes and D1/D2 marker genes were all FDR=1.0.
The germline-mutant DBH/noradrenaline axis was not reproduced: Dbh, Th, and Slc6a3 had 0 FDR<0.10 rows after Zfp521 perturbation.
Global score-neighbor analysis found no robust convergent perturbation for Zfp521: the largest positive score correlation was Pax2 at r=0.0317 and the most negative was Fgfr2 at r=-0.0194.
Zfp536 loss was almost fully buffered in P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neurons, with one robust downstream gene across all 23 recovered cell groups.
Fam171b was the sole FDR<0.10 Zfp536 hit and was selectively down in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Measured RA/CtBP and oligodendroglial-conversion comparators were flat or divergent and did not reproduce the Pvalb Fam171b response.
Unbiased restricted-signature neighbors of Zfp536 were weak, non-obvious, and did not form an FDR-level convergent module.
Postnatal neuronal Zfp609 loss produced a pan-null whole-transcriptome surface: every one of the 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The expected Zfp609-Nipbl cortical migration targets Sema3a, Nrp1, Plxnd1, and Gabbr2 were directly tested but were not significantly downregulated in any recovered group.
A global signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative neighbor for Zfp609; the closest named-gene Wilcoxon-score cosines were only +0.0278 to -0.0167.

Represented cohesin/CTCF comparators were not Zfp609 phenocopies: Smc1a and Stag2, two proteins recovered in Zfp609 pull-downs, produced convergent DE in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Zfp609 had zero significant genes there.
Zfp612 loss produced a host-gene response in only 2 of 23 measured neuronal groups: two genes in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and one gene in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Notum is the strongest Zfp612-responsive transcript: it increased about two-fold in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and no other gene in that cell group reached FDR<0.10.
Nrcam was the only down-regulated FDR<0.10 transcript after Zfp612 perturbation and the only adhesion/axon-guidance gene in the corrected signature.
Impact was selectively up-regulated with Nrcam down in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, without a canonical ER/ISR stress cassette.

The two real Zfp612 response groups did not show the canonical programs that would make the nulls a readout failure: broad KRAB/KAP1 target derepression, host innate immunity, cell-cycle entry, or a multi-gene ER/ISR signature.
Zfp612 did not phenocopy represented KRAB-associated chromatin effectors or broad zinc-finger comparators.

Unbiased whole-surface signature search also classified Zfp612 as almost neighborless: the largest non-self Wilcoxon-score cosine was 0.0345 and a safe-target signature was the nominal nearest neighbor.
Acute postnatal Zfp644 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in any of the 20 neuronal groups where the perturbation was recovered.
Loss of Zfp644 did not derepress the retinal/neural progenitor program that ZNF644-G9a biology predicts: Ccnd1, Vsx2, Pcna, and Mki67 were all FDR=1.0 in every measured group.
Zfp644 did not phenocopy the detectable Ehmt1 or Setdb1 H3K9-family perturbations in matched groups.
The data-driven Zfp644 vector had only noise-scale perturbation neighbors, and every top positive or negative gene comparator was rejected as a biological convergence.
Zfp654 loss produced no robust downstream DE in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
Residual cross-perturbation search placed Zfp654 next to weak Safe_target-like null surfaces, with no meaningful positive or negative neighbor.
The predicted STRING Zfp654 network was not resolved as a matched transcriptional module; only Tbc1d23 was testable and it was also flat.
Zfp664 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptomic response in any recovered postmitotic neuronal cell group.
The known hepatic Zfp664 loss program did not appear in neuronal nuclei.
Neither data-driven neighbors nor broad C2H2 zinc-finger comparator perturbations converged on a Zfp664 module.
Zfp692 produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group at P37-P44 after sparse P16 CRISPR loss of function.
The hepatic PCK1/AMPK arm and the nucleolar-40S/stress programs predicted from ZNF692 biochemistry were not present in Zfp692-perturbed neuronal nuclei.

Both unbiased neighbors and literature-obvious comparators rejected a coherent Zfp692-like module; the nearest cosine neighbors were null-like, and Tsc2, unlike Zfp692, gave a large measurable mTOR-axis response.

Zfp804a produced a robust all-null neuronal RNA phenotype: 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the two nearest misses were only weak subthreshold rows in 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
The pre-literature score-profile neighbor search nominated no credible convergent module for Zfp804a.
Reported ZNF804A transcriptional targets and synaptic/GABA sentinels were cleanly absent after Zfp804a perturbation.
Zfp804a did not converge with represented partner, RNA-processing, schizophrenia-target, or Glu/GABA perturbations that were visible elsewhere in the same screen.
The screen disfavors post-P16 pan-neuronal coding loss as a transcriptomic stand-in for fetal ZNF804A risk-variant biology.
GAD67/Glu-GABA and clozapine-responsive cKO biology did not leave an acute Gad1/Gad2/Dlg4 RNA biomarker in sparse Zfp804a-edited neurons.
Zfp846 loss elicited a single reproducible annotated-gene response: Ldhb up-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
The Zfp846 signature has no robust convergent or inverse neighbor in the screen-wide perturbation universe.
Zfp846 does not phenocopy the detectable SETDB1/KRAB-adjacent repressive program in postnatal neurons.
Zfp949 had a pan-measured downstream-null DE surface: every recovered neuronal group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The embryonic Nczf-to-Cdkn1b/p27 de-repression program did not fire in any recovered postnatal neuronal group.
Zfp949 was much flatter than KAP1-associated effector perturbations represented in the same groups: Chd4 and Setdb1 produced FDR-level signatures where Zfp949 and Zfp950 did not.
A whole-universe Wilcoxon-score neighbor scan found no meaningful positive or negative Zfp949 signature neighbor.
Zfp950 loss of function produced no robust gene-level transcriptional response in any recovered postmitotic neuronal group.
Zfp950 did not uncover a neuronal PDGF/MRTF effector module; Pdgfrb was also silent and Mrtfa was reduced to a single marginal FDR<0.10 gene.
Zfp950 did not phenocopy the gene-level response to Setdb1 despite its KRAB/C2H2 zinc-finger architecture.
The global Zfp950 signature has no meaningful positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
Zfp961 produced a real but extremely thin response confined to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, where Dctn2 increased and Strn4 decreased at FDR<0.10.
Canonical ZFP961 outputs from adipose PPARα biology, hepatic apoB/lipogenesis, and PBS-Lys/ERV repression were absent from the neuronal DE surface.

Literature-nominated relatives did not phenocopy Zfp961: Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, Ppargc1a, Rxra, Casz1, Mttp, Dnmt3a, and Lrif1 were flat, and Setdb1 responded in other neuronal groups without reproducing Dctn2 or Strn4 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
Unbiased signature comparison found no strong Zfp961 neighbor; the largest positive and negative full-surface cosines were only 0.0287 for Celsr2 and -0.0191 for Tpr.
The juvenile neuronal null does not de-risk ZFP961-directed metabolic interventions beyond the assayed axis.
Zfpm2 was a whole-surface postnatal neuronal transcriptomic null: every one of its 21 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
The juvenile Zfpm2 perturbation did not reopen the Fog2 corticothalamic/projection-neuron differentiation program in cortical glutamatergic bins.
Represented GATA and NuRD perturbations did not phenocopy Zfpm2 in the matched neuronal surface.
The nominal data-driven signature neighbors of Zfpm2 were rejected as meaningful convergences.
The neuronal null should not be used to deprioritize ZFPM2 for congenital diaphragm, gonad, or heart disease mechanisms.

Acute Zfx loss produced corrected transcriptional signal in only four of 22 measured neuronal groups, with its main response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and complete FDR-level silence across cortical and hippocampal groups.
The corrected Zfx signature was overwhelmingly down-regulated: 22 of 25 significant cell-group/gene events were decreases.
Cyp46a1 was the only corrected Zfx-dependent transcript in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and was decreased.

A small neuronal signaling/scaffold module recurred in subcortical responders: Arhgef25 was down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, and Begain was down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA alongside Npr2, Nalcn, Ssh3, Prrg3, and Cdh18 in the thalamic group.
Zfx loss decreased Inha in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA; the 191 signature also decreased Thpo.
The largest Zfx response, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, included centrosome/IFT/endosomal and metabolic tail genes rather than a canonical proteasome, ISR, UPR, or autophagy bounce-back.

The strongest same-direction data-driven neighbors were Tpr, Tnpo3, Brd4, Prpf6, and Psmc1, each sharing multiple Zfx-significant genes in the same direction but with hundreds to thousands more DEGs than Zfx.

Yy1, Sin3a, Tardbp, and U2af2 were the strongest corrected opposite-direction neighbors on the restricted Zfx gene set, inverting several 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut events such as Inha, Pcca, Zmynd11, Flvcr1, and Ssh3.

The postnatal neuronal Zfx response did not recover the canonical ESC self-renewal program: Tbx3, Tcl1, Myc, Sox2, Pou5f1, Nanog, and Zfp42 were not corrected downstream hits, and represented stemness-factor perturbations did not phenocopy Zfx.
Acute Zhx3 loss produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: every recovered cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and Zhx3 itself had FDR=1.0 in every group.
The fibroblast ZHX3-loss senescence module was not recovered in neurons: Cdkn2a, Il1a, and Il1b were present in all 20 Zhx3 DE tables but were FDR=1.0 everywhere.
The only assayed NF-Y subunit, Nfyc, did not phenocopy Zhx3: Nfyc had no FDR<0.10 genes in 19 of 20 matched groups and only four all-down genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

Zhx3 raw-vector nearest neighbors were null-like rather than pathway-informative: Ap3b1, Safe_target_52, and Washc4 were the top three Pearson neighbors, and each had 0 FDR<0.10 genes in its Zhx3-matched surface.

The Zhx3 null is not a global inability of this screen to detect neuronal stress: the least-concordant Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations produced 11089 and 13606 downstream FDR<0.10 calls, respectively, in Zhx3-matched groups.
A reported ZHX3 interactor, Atxn1, was divergent rather than convergent: Atxn1 had 262 downstream genes in Zhx3-matched groups, including 256 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Zhx3 had none.
Acute Zic1 loss produced a measurable but one-gene transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Slc29a1/ENT1 was the lone robust downstream RNA hit after Zic1 perturbation and was up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The expected cerebellar Shh/GCP proliferation and maturation programs were absent across the Zic1 DE surface.
Zic2, Zic3 and Zic4 did not phenocopy the Zic1 Slc29a1 response in the matched 151 thalamic group.
Measured Shh/Gli and ciliary pathway perturbations failed to converge with Zic1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Rora was the strongest 151 signature neighbor of Zic1 and independently up-regulated Slc29a1.
Zic2 perturbation produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream event: Rap1gap was weakly up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
The represented Zic paralogs did not phenocopy Zic2 in the P16 Perturb-seq surface.
Holoprosencephaly, Hedgehog/Gli, and EphB1 retinal-guidance comparators were sparse and nonconvergent with Zic2.
Canonical Wnt effector perturbations were strong in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but did not collapse onto the Zic2→Rap1gap signature.
Whole-surface neighbors place Zic2 in the near-null signature cloud rather than in a coherent positive or negative module.
Zic3 produced a sparse but real 308 CB GABA response consisting of Pkd2, Galnt16, and Tspyl1 up-regulation.
Acute Zic3 loss in P16 neurons did not recover the embryonic Nodal, Wnt, PCP, or neural-progenitor programs expected from Zic3 developmental literature.
Zic1, Zic2, and Zic4 did not phenocopy the Zic3 CB-GABA response despite being the closest represented Zic-family perturbations.
Wnt, Nodal/TGF-beta, Gli, and axial-patterning comparator perturbations separated from Zic3: they neither shared the CB-GABA triplet nor reproduced Zic3's flat thalamic profile.

Zic4 produced zero FDR<0.10 transcriptional responses across all 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal cell groups, and the cerebellar Shh-response genes expected from Zic1/Zic4 developmental literature were absent from the signature.
Measured Zic paralogs and Shh/Gli pathway comparators failed to converge with Zic4 in the matched P16 postmitotic DE surface.
The top data-driven signature neighbors of Zic4 were unrelated, extremely weak correlations rather than a coherent positive or inverse module.
Zkscan16 loss produced a two-gene, two-cell-class surface rather than a broad neuronal transcriptional program.

canonical_summary: The strongest Zkscan16-responsive transcript was Mkrn3, up-regulated only in 155 MB Glut.
Zkscan16 perturbation down-regulated the palmitoyltransferase Zdhhc17 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
The Mkrn3 and Zdhhc17 cell-type-specific events were unique to Zkscan16 at FDR<0.10 across the 1773-target universe.
Data-driven global signature neighbors of Zkscan16 were only weakly similar and did not reproduce its two significant features.
Screened KRAB/SCAN, SETDB1, and MeCP2 relatives did not phenocopy Zkscan16.
The ZNF483-P19 neuronal-differentiation phenotype was not recovered as a Mecp2 or neuronal-marker mRNA program after postnatal Zkscan16 loss.
Zkscan1 produced an all-null postnatal neuronal DE surface: every one of the 22 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
The GABA(A)-receptor subunit program nominated from brain eQTL work was not recovered: Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, and Gabrg2 were all FDR=1.0 in every recovered Zkscan1 cell group.

Represented SCAN-family perturbations did not phenocopy Zkscan1: Zkscan16 had only two FDR<0.10 genes and Zscan26 had none across the 22 matched groups, with full-score correlations to Zkscan1 of 0.0116 and 0.0192.

The closest full-rank data-driven neighbors were rejected: Msx2, Il6st, and Bcap31 were the top positive biological score neighbors and Fbxo11, Npy1r, and Timmdc1 the top negative neighbors, but all correlations were |r|<0.035 and each comparator was null or nearly null in matched groups.

Chromatin-repression machinery perturbations were active where Zkscan1 was silent: Chd4 and Setdb1 generated 158 and 45 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across matched groups, including a same-direction 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut module, but the shared genes were all FDR=1.0 after Zkscan1 perturbation.

Disease and cancer priors are displaced from this assay: ZKSCAN1 has been implicated in GABA(A) regulation, tumor migration/proliferation assays, and lower-confidence childhood speech-disorder networks, but P16 sparse neuronal coding loss showed no cell-autonomous GABA(A) or other FDR-defined transcriptome.
Zmym2 loss produced a sparse genic response that was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only two MB Glut hits and one P MY Pineal hit outside that thalamic class.
The real 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signal is a derepression-biased neuronal surface/signaling/excitability cassette rather than the embryonic germline-LINE cassette.
Outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zmym2 generated only FDR-borderline singleton loci rather than a coherent stress, UPR, proteostasis, or synaptic-collapse program.
Adnp and Chd4 partially converged with Zmym2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, sharing several same-direction genes while driving larger signatures.
The CoREST-associated comparator Phf21a did not phenocopy Zmym2; its only exact 151 overlap was Plppr3 in the opposite direction.
The top restricted-signature neighbors were mostly rank-level, not robust, phenocopies of Zmym2.
The expected embryonic germline-gene and young-LINE de-repression program was absent from the P16 neuronal DE surface.
P16 sparse CRISPR loss of Zmynd11 produced 0 non-self downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal groups.
The P16-to-young-adult null shifts the ZMYND11 disease hypothesis toward an earlier cortical progenitor/corticogenesis window rather than broad late pan-neuronal gene dysregulation.
Zmynd11 did not phenocopy a related 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut H3K36/PBP-reader module in which Zmynd8 and Nsd1 shared ten same-direction upregulated genes.
The whole-surface data-driven neighbor search yielded only near-zero correlations for Zmynd11.
The RBFOX2-linked splicing expectation was uncoupled from whole-gene abundance after postnatal Zmynd11 perturbation.
A postmitotic Zmynd11 gene-abundance signature is a poor standalone pharmacodynamic biomarker in this system.

Zmynd8 loss was strongly cell-type selective: 93 of 99 downstream FDR<0.10 genes were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas all non-151 effects were one to three genes and 17 measured groups had no FDR-significant downstream genes.

In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zmynd8 perturbation primarily de-repressed high-amplitude ectopic signaling and secreted genes, including Ptgds, Lhcgr, Capn3, P2rx7, Asb2, Cyp2j13, Atp2a1, Myo5c, and Zap70.
The 151 response had a negative synaptic/receptor arm: Gabbr2, Nrxn1, Grm1, Trim9, Lrrc7, Stxbp2, Zfp804a, Pcdh1, and Gabra1 were down-regulated while the ectopic enhancer-like arm was up-regulated.
Zmynd8 induced a redox/ER-calcium-adjacent module in 151, with Msra, Sil1, Atp2a1, Capn3, Aifm3, and Pycr1 up, but Hspa5, Atf4, Ddit3, Xbp1, Sqstm1, and core autophagy genes were not FDR-significant.
Kdm5c was the top measured positive neighbor of Zmynd8, and Nsd1 was second, linking the thalamic signature to the literature RACK7/KDM5C enhancer brake and to NSD1-dependent H3K36me2 biology.

The Zmynd8 phenotype was not a generic ZMYND-family or NuRD loss phenotype: Kdm5b and Zmynd11 had no downstream FDR genes, Gatad2b and Mbd2 did not overlap, and Chd4 produced a large but mixed 151 signature with both shared and opposite Zmynd8 features.
Data-driven negative neighbors Arid2 and Elp1, together with Sin3a and Brd4, flipped many of the same 151 genes that rose after Zmynd8 loss.
The non-151 FDR effects were sparse and upward, limited to Myo5c in 005, Zfp821 in 027, Spag5 in 145, and Spag5, Hexim2, and Pnck in 155.
Acute Zscan26 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups: every measured group had zero non-target genes at FDR<0.10.
155 MB Glut showed a bona fide Zscan26 self-transcript decrease, but that on-target effect did not propagate to any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
The c-fos/SRE immediate-early program predicted by the SRE-ZBP cloning literature was absent from the Zscan26 neuronal DE surface.
A phenotype-first whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful Zscan26 convergence: the best named positive and negative cosine neighbors were all close to zero.
Represented SCAN-domain relatives did not reveal a shared SCAN-family response: Zkscan1 was fully downstream-null and Zkscan16 produced only two isolated single-gene hits.
Acute P16 Zswim6 loss produced no adjusted downstream transcriptional response in any of the 20 recovered neuronal cell groups.
The CNU GABA groups closest to the LGE/striatal prior were still transcriptomically flat after Zswim6 perturbation.
Zswim6 did not phenocopy the represented repressive-chromatin/NDD comparators Sin3a or Mecp2.
Neuronal Zswim6 loss did not activate the Hedgehog/BMP developmental-signaling programs suggested by AFND and distant ZSWIM4-6 literature.
AMPAR-family perturbations and AMPAR target transcripts did not converge with Zswim6.
Full-surface data-driven Zswim6 neighbors had near-zero positive and negative correlations and minuscule adjusted DE surfaces.
